JDG 12:15 And Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and he was entombed in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the mountain of Amalek.
JDG 13:1 And the sons of Israel proceeded still to act wickedly before the LORD, and the LORD delivered them into the hand of the Philistines - forty years.
JDG 13:2 And there was one man from Zorah, from the tribe of Dan, and the name to him was Manoah; and his wife was sterile, and had not given birth.
JDG 13:3 And an angel of the LORD appeared to the woman, and said to her, Behold indeed, you are sterile, and have not borne; but you shall have one in the womb, and shall bear a son.
JDG 13:4 And now guard and do not drink wine and liquor, and do not eat any unclean thing!
JDG 13:5 For behold, you have one in the womb, and you shall bear a son, and an iron razor shall not ascend upon his head, for the boy will be a Nazarite to God from the womb; and he shall begin to deliver Israel from out of the hand of the Philistines.
JDG 13:6 And the woman went in, and spoke to her husband, saying, A man of God came to me, and his appearance was as the appearance of an angel of God - very prominent. And I did not ask him from what place he is, and his name he did not report to me.
JDG 13:7 And he said to me, Behold, you have one in the womb, and you shall give birth to a son. And now, do not drink wine and strong drink, and do not eat any uncleanness, for the boy will be a Nazarite of God from the womb, until the day of his death!
JDG 13:8 And Manoah besought of the LORD. And he said, Be to me, O LORD, the man of God whom you sent, let him come yet once more to us and enlighten us what we should do with the boy to be born!
JDG 13:9 And God heeded the voice of Manoah. And the angel of God came again to the woman, and she sat in the field, and Manoah her husband was not with her.
JDG 13:10 And the woman hastened, and ran, and reported to her husband, and said to him, Behold, the man has appeared to me, coming in this day to me.
JDG 13:11 And Manoah rose up and went after his wife. And he came to the man, and he said to him, Are you the man speaking to the woman? And the angel said, I am.
JDG 13:12 And Manoah said, Now, your word going through, what will be the distinguishing manner of the boy, and of his works?
JDG 13:13 And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, Of all which I spoke to the woman, let her guard!
JDG 13:14 From every thing which goes forth from out of the grapevine she shall not eat, and wine and liquor she shall not drink, and every thing unclean she shall not eat - all as much as I gave charge to her, let her guard!
JDG 13:15 And Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, We should indeed force you to stay, and shall prepare before you a kid of the goats.
JDG 13:16 And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, If she should hold me I will not eat from your breads. And if you should offer a whole burnt offering, you shall offer it to the LORD. For Manoah did not know that he was an angel of the LORD.
JDG 13:17 And Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, What is the name to you, that whenever your word should come to pass that we should glorify you?
JDG 13:18 And the angel of the LORD said to him, Why is this you ask of my name, for it is Wonderful?
JDG 13:19 And Manoah took the kid of the goats, and the sacrifice offering, and he offered upon the rock to the LORD, to the wonderful being. And Manoah and his wife were viewing.
JDG 13:20 And it happened in the flame ascending on top of the altar unto the heaven, that the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife were viewing, and they fell upon their face upon the ground.
JDG 13:21 And the angel of the LORD did not proceed any longer to appear to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that this was an angel of the LORD.
JDG 13:22 And Manoah said to his wife, To death we shall die, for we have looked at God.
JDG 13:23 And his wife said to him, If the LORD wanted to kill us, he would not have received from our hand a whole burnt offering and a sacrifice offering, and he would not have enlightened us all these things, even as this time, and he would not have made these things audible to us.
JDG 13:24 And the woman bore a son, and she called his name Samson. And the boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
JDG 13:25 And spirit of the LORD began to go forth with him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and between Eshtaol.
JDG 14:1 And Samson went down unto Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath from the daughters of the Philistines.
JDG 14:2 And he ascended, and reported to his father and to his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Timnath from the daughters of the Philistines. And now take her to me for wife!
JDG 14:3 And his father said to him, and his mother, Is there not a woman of the daughters of your brothers and among all my people, that you should go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said to his father, Take this one for me, for she pleases in my eyes!
JDG 14:4 And his father and his mother knew not that it is from the LORD, that he required recompense of the Philistines. And in that time the Philistines dominated the sons of Israel.
JDG 14:5 And Samson went down, and his father and his mother unto Timnath. And he came to the vineyards of Timnath. And behold, a cub of a lion was roaring in meeting him.
JDG 14:6 And spirit of the LORD straightened upon him, and he tore it apart as a kid of the goats, and nothing was in his hand. And he did not report to his father and to his mother what he did.
JDG 14:7 And they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was pleasing before Samson.
JDG 14:8 And he returned after some days to take her, and he turned aside to behold the carcass of the lion - and, behold, a swarm as of an apiary of bees was in the mouth of the lion, and honey.
JDG 14:9 And he took it into his mouth, and went forth going and eating. And he went to his father and to his mother, and he gave to them, and they ate - and he did not announce to them that he took the honey from the manner of the lion.
JDG 14:10 And his father went down to the woman. And Samson prepared there a banquet for seven days - for thus the young men did.
JDG 14:11 And it came to pass in their fearing him, that they posted in front to him thirty companions, and they were with him.
JDG 14:12 And Samson said to them, I will propound indeed to you a riddle; and if by reporting you should report it to me in the seven days of the banquet, and you should find the solution, I will give to you thirty pieces of fine linen, and thirty robes of clothes.
JDG 14:13 And if you should not be able to report the solution to me, then you shall give to me yourselves thirty pieces of fine linen, and thirty robes of clothes. And they said to him, Propound your riddle, and we shall hear it!
JDG 14:14 And he said to them, From the one eating came forth food, and from the strong came forth sweetness. And they were not able to explain the riddle for three days.
JDG 14:15 And it came to pass in the seventh day, and they spoke to the wife of Samson, saying, Deceive indeed your husband! And let him explain to you the riddle, lest at any time we should burn you and the house of your father by fire - or did you call us to make us poor?
JDG 14:16 And the wife of Samson wept to him, and said to him, You detest me, and do not love me, because the riddle which you propounded to the sons of my people, you did not explain even it to me. And Samson said to her, Behold, to my father and to my mother I did not report it, and should I report to you?
JDG 14:17 And she wept upon him for the seven days in which the banquet was to them. And it came to pass on the seventh day he explained to her, for she troubled him. And she reported to the sons of her people.
JDG 14:18 And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun going down, What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion? And Samson said to them, Unless you plowed by my heifer, you would not have found my riddle.
JDG 14:19 And spirit of the LORD straightened upon him, and he went down unto Ashkelon, and smote from there thirty men, and took their robes, and gave them to the ones explaining the riddle. And Samson was enraged in anger, and he ascended into the house of his father.
JDG 14:20 And the wife of Samson lived with his groomsman who was his companion.
JDG 15:1 And it came to pass after some days, at the days of the wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife, carrying a kid of the goats. And he said, I shall enter to my wife into the bedroom. But her father would not grant him to enter.
JDG 15:2 And her father said, In saying, I said that, By detesting you detested her; and I gave her to your companion. Behold is not her younger sister better than she? Let her be to you instead of her!
JDG 15:3 And Samson said to him, I am innocent this once concerning the Philistines, that I myself should do evils with you.
JDG 15:4 And Samson went and seized three hundred foxes, and took lamps, and tied them together tail to tail, and put one lamp between the two tails, and guided them.
JDG 15:5 And he kindled fire in the lamps, and he sent them out in the ears of wheat of the Philistines. And he burned the ears of wheat from the threshing-floor, and unto the straight standing ears of wheat, and unto the vineyard, and olive orchards.
JDG 15:6 And the Philistines said, Who did these things? And they said, Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife, and gave her to his male companion. And the Philistines ascended up, and burnt her and the house of her father by fire.
JDG 15:7 And Samson said to them, Since you should do thus, I shall not think well, but I will execute my vengeance against each one of you.
JDG 15:8 And he struck them shank unto thigh with a great beating. And he went down and sat at the hole in the rock of Etam.
JDG 15:9 And the Philistines ascended and camped in Judah, and cast forth about Lehi.
JDG 15:10 And every man of Judah said to them, Why have you ascended against us? And the Philistines said, We ascended to tie up Samson, and to do to him in which manner he did to us.
JDG 15:11 And three thousand men of Judah went down unto the hole in the rock of Etam, and said to Samson, Do you not behold that the Philistines dominate us? Then why did you do these things to us? And Samson said to them, In which manner they did to me, so I did to them.
JDG 15:12 And they said to him, We came down to tie you, to deliver you up into the hands of the Philistines. And Samson said to them, Swear to me by an oath to not kill me yourselves, that lest at any time you should meet up with me yourselves.
JDG 15:13 And they swore by an oath to him, saying, No; but only by a bond will we tie you, for we should deliver you up into their hands - but to death we will not kill you. And they tied him with two new ropes, and bore him from the rock.
JDG 15:14 And he came unto Jaw. And the Philistines shouted, and ran to meet him. And spirit of the LORD straightened upon him, and the ropes in his arms became as hemp when fire smells. And the bonds melted away from his arms.
JDG 15:15 And he found a jaw bone of a donkey having been tossed. And he stretched out his hand, and took it, and struck with it a thousand men.
JDG 15:16 And Samson said, By the jaw bone of a donkey, in wiping away, I wiped them away, for by the jaw bone of the donkey I struck a thousand men.
JDG 15:17 And it came to pass when he finished speaking, that he tossed the jaw bone from his hand, and called that place, Removal of the Jaw.
JDG 15:18 And he thirsted exceedingly, and yelled to the LORD, and said, You gave by the hand of your servant this great deliverance, and now shall I die in thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?
JDG 15:19 And God opened the gash, the one in Jaw, and there came forth from out of it waters. And he drank, and his spirit was restored, and he lived. Because of this its name is called, Spring of the Calling Upon, which is in Jaw until this day.
JDG 15:20 And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.
JDG 16:1 And Samson went into Gaza, and saw there a woman harlot, and entered to her.
JDG 16:2 And it was reported to the Gazites, saying, Samson comes here. And they encircled, and laid in wait for him the entire night at the gate of the city. And they were silent the entire night, saying, We should wait until light shows through at dawn, and we should kill him.
JDG 16:3 And Samson went to bed until midnight. And he rose up at half the night, and he took hold of the doors of the gate of the city, and the two doorposts, and carried them with the bar, and put them upon his shoulders, and bore them upon the top of the mountain which is at the face of Hebron.
JDG 16:4 And it came to pass after this, that he loved a woman by the rushing stream Sorek, and her name was Delilah.
JDG 16:5 And the satraps of the Philistines ascended to her, and said to her, Beguile him, and see by what means his great strength is, and by what means we shall be able to prevail against him, and tie him so as to humble him. And we will give to you by man a thousand and a hundred pieces of silver.
JDG 16:6 And Delilah said to Samson, Explain indeed to me! By what means your great strength is, and by what means you shall be tied so as to humble you?
JDG 16:7 And Samson said to her, If they should tie me with seven wet strings of a bow that are not ruined, then I will be weakened, and I will be as one of the men.
JDG 16:8 And the satraps of the Philistines brought to her seven wet strings of a bow not ruined. And she tied him with them.
JDG 16:9 And the ambush sat down for him in the storeroom. And she said to him, The Philistines are upon you, Samson. And he tore up the strings of the bow in which manner one pulls apart yarn of hemp in its smelling of fire - and his strength was not made known.
JDG 16:10 And Delilah said to Samson, Behold, you misled me, and you spoke to me by lying. Now then, report to me! By what you shall be tied?
JDG 16:11 And he said to her, If by binding, they should tie me by new ropes which were not used in their work, then I shall be weak, and I will be as one of the men.
JDG 16:12 And Delilah took new ropes, and tied him with them, and said to him, The Philistines are upon you, Samson. And the ambush sat in the storeroom. And he pulled them from his arms as thread.
JDG 16:13 And Delilah said to Samson, Until now you misled me, and spoke to me lying. Announce indeed to me! By what you shall be tied? And he said to her, If you should weave the seven strands of hair of my head with the warp, and hammer with the peg into the wall, then I will be weak as one of the men.
JDG 16:14 And it came to pass in his going to sleep, that Delilah took the seven strands of his head, and weaved them with the warp, and pinned them to the peg into the wall. And she said to him, The Philistines are upon you, Samson. And he was awakened from his sleep, and he pulled out the pegs in the woven work from out of the wall, and the warp; for he knew not his strength.
JDG 16:15 And Delilah said to him, How do you say, I love you, and your heart is not with me? This third time you misled me, and did not report to me by what means your great strength is.
JDG 16:16 And it came to pass when she worked him by her words the whole night, and troubled him, that he was faint-hearted unto death.
JDG 16:17 And he reported to her all the things from his heart. And said to her, A razor shall not ascend upon my head; for I am a Nazarite of God from out of the belly of my mother; and if I should be shaven, my strength shall leave from me, and I shall be weakened, and I will be as all the men.
JDG 16:18 And Delilah knew that he reported to her all his heart. And she sent and called the satraps of the Philistines, saying, Ascend this once, for he reported to me all his heart! And they ascended up to her - all the satraps of the Philistines, and they offered the silver in her hands.
JDG 16:19 And she rested him between her knees; And she called the barber, and he shaved the seven curls of his head; and it began to humble him, and his strength left from him.
JDG 16:20 And Delilah said, The Philistines are upon you, Samson. And he was awakened from out of his sleep. And he said, I shall go forth, and I shall do as continually before, and I shall brush myself off. And he did not know that the LORD left from him.
JDG 16:21 And the Philistines took hold of him, and gouged out his eyes, and carried him unto Gaza. And they bound him with shackles of brass; and he was grinding in the house of the prison.
JDG 16:22 And the hair of his head began to grow, as he was shaven.
JDG 16:23 And the rulers of the Philistines came together to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to be merry. And they said, Our god delivered into our hand Samson our enemy.
JDG 16:24 And the people saw him, and they praised their god, for they said, Our god delivered our enemy into our hands - the one making our land quite desolate, who multiplied our slain.
JDG 16:25 And it came to pass when their heart was feeling good, that they said, Call Samson from out of the house of the prison, and let him play before us! And they called Samson from out of the house of the jail, and they sported with him. And they stood him in between the two posts.
JDG 16:26 And Samson said to the young man leading him by the hand, Allow me! And I should handle the monumental pillars upon which the house stays upon them.
JDG 16:27 And the house was full of the men and women; and all the satraps of the Philistines were there. And upon the roof were about three thousand men and women, looking at and mocking Samson.
JDG 16:28 And Samson yelled to the LORD, and said, O LORD, O LORD, remember me, and strengthen me indeed besides! And this once, O God, and I will avenge one vengeance against the Philistines for my two eyes.
JDG 16:29 And Samson took hold of the two posts in the midst upon which the house stood, and he stayed against them, one at his right hand, and one at at his left.
JDG 16:30 And Samson said, Let my soul die with the Philistines. And he leaned in strength, and the house fell upon the satraps, and upon all the people in it. And the ones having died whom Samson put to death were in his death many over whom he put to death in his life.
JDG 16:31 And his brothers went down, and all the house of his father, and took him, and ascended, and entombed him between Zorah and between Esthaol in the burying-place of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.
JDG 17:1 And there was a man of mount Ephraim, and his name was Micah.
JDG 17:2 And he said to his mother, The thousand and hundred pieces of silver seized from you, and you adjured, and said it in my ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Being blessed is my son in the LORD.
JDG 17:3 And he gave back the thousand and hundred pieces of silver to his mother. And his mother said, By sanctification, I sanctified the silver to the LORD out of my hand alone, to make a carving and molten image - and now I will give it back to you.
JDG 17:4 And he gave back the silver to his mother. Then his mother took two hundred of the pieces of silver, and gave them to the smelterer. And he made it into a carving and molten image. And it was in the house of Micah.
JDG 17:5 And the house of Micah was to him a house of a god. And he made an ephod and teraphim, and filled up the hand of one of his sons, and he became to him for a priest.
JDG 17:6 In those days there was not a king in Israel - a man did upright in his own eyes.
JDG 17:7 And there was a young man from out of Beth-lehem Judah from the kin of Judah, and he was a Levite, and he sojourned there.
JDG 17:8 And the man went from the city of Beth-lehem Judah to sojourn where ever he should find. And he came unto mount Ephraim, and unto the house of Micah, making his way.
JDG 17:9 And Micah said to him, From what place come you? And he said to him, I am a Levite from Beth-lehem Judah, and I go to sojourn where ever I should find.
JDG 17:10 And Micah said to him, Sit down with me, and become to me as a father and as priest, and I will give to you ten silver pieces for days, and a pair of clothes, and the things for your means of life.
JDG 17:11 And the Levite went, and began to sojourn by the man. And the young man became to him as one of his sons.
JDG 17:12 And Micah filled up the hand of the Levite, and the young man became to him for a priest - and he was in the house of Micah.
JDG 17:13 And Micah said, Now I know that the LORD did good to me, for the Levite became to me for a priest.
JDG 18:1 In those days there was not a king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of Dan sought for itself an inheritance to dwell; for an inheritance did not fall in to it until that day in the midst of the tribes of Israel.
JDG 18:2 And the sons of Dan sent out from their peoples five men from their part, men of sons of power, from Zorah and Esthaol, to survey the land, and to track it. And they said to them, Go, and search out the land! And they came unto mount Ephraim, unto the house of Micah, and they rested there.
JDG 18:3 In their being by the house of Micah, that they knew the voice of the young man, the Levite, and they turned aside there. And they said to him, Who brought you here? And what do you do here? And what is it here?
JDG 18:4 And he said to them, Micah did so and so with me, and hired me, and I became to him for a priest.
JDG 18:5 And they said to him, Ask indeed to God, that we will know if our way greatly prospers which we go by it!
JDG 18:6 And the priest said to them, Go in peace before the LORD - your way by which you go by it!
JDG 18:7 And the five men went, and came into Laish. And they saw the people in it dwelling in hope as the amalgamation of the Sidonians, being tranquil in hope, and not being able to speak a word in the land, for they are far from Sidon, and there was not a word to them with Syria.
JDG 18:8 And the five men came to their brothers in Zorah and in Esthaol. And their brothers said to them, Why do you sit down?
JDG 18:9 And they said, Rise up! for we should ascend against them, for we saw the land, and behold, it is exceedingly good; and you are silent - you should not be reluctant to go, and to enter to inherit the land.
JDG 18:10 When ever you should enter, you shall come to a people being secure, and the land of broad space, for God delivered it over into your hand. A place where there is not any deficiency there of a thing as much as is on the earth.
JDG 18:11 And they departed from there, from the kin of Dan, from Zorah and from Esthaol - six hundred men being girded with weapons for battle.
JDG 18:12 And they ascended and camped in Kirjath-jearim, in Judah. On account of this that place was called, Camp of Dan until this day. Behold, it is behind Kirjath-jearim.
JDG 18:13 And they went from there unto mount Ephraim, and came unto the house of Micah.
JDG 18:14 And the five men going to survey the land of Laish responded, and said to their brothers, Did you know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a carved image, and a molten image? And now know what you shall do!
JDG 18:15 And they turned aside there, and entered into the house of the young man - the Levite, into the house of Micah, and asked him for peace.
JDG 18:16 And the six hundred men being girded with weapons for their warfare, being set up by the door of the gatehouse, were the ones from the sons of Dan.
JDG 18:17 Then the five men going to survey the land ascended; and coming there, they took the carved image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image. And the priest was set up by the door of the gatehouse, and the six hundred men were girded with weapons for warfare.
JDG 18:18 And when these entered into the house of Micah, and took the carved image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image; that the priest said to them, What do you do?
JDG 18:19 And they said to him, Be silent, place your hand over your mouth, and come with us, and you will be to us for a father and for a priest! Is it not better for you to be a priest of the house of one man, or for you to be priest of a tribe and kin in Israel?
JDG 18:20 And it was good to the heart of the priest. And he took the ephod, and the teraphim, and the carved image, and the molten image, and entered into the midst of the people.
JDG 18:21 And they turned and went forth, and put the children, and the property, and the load before them.
JDG 18:22 And they were far from the house of Micah, and behold, Micah and the men in the houses, near the house of Micah, cried out, and overtook the sons of Dan.
JDG 18:23 And they yelled to the sons of Dan. And the sons of Dan turned their faces, and said to Micah, What is it to you that you cry out?
JDG 18:24 And he said, The gods which I made you took, and the priest, and you departed. And what is there to me still? And what is this you say to me, Why is this that you cry out?
JDG 18:25 And the sons of Dan said to him, Your voice should not be heard with us, lest at any time men in severe pain of soul should encounter you, and you shall add your life, and the life of your household.
JDG 18:26 And the sons of Dan went on their way. And Micah saw that they are too mighty for him, and he turned aside and returned to his house.
JDG 18:27 And they took as much as Micah made, and the priest who was with him, and they went unto Laish, upon a people being tranquil, and being secure. And they struck them by the mouth of the broadsword, and the city they burned by fire.
JDG 18:28 And there is not the one for rescuing, for it is far from Sidon, and communication is not to them with man; and it is in the valley which is of the house of Rehob. And they built up the city, and dwelt in it.
JDG 18:29 And they called the name of the city Dan, according to the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel. And the name to the city formerly was Laish.
JDG 18:30 And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image. And Jonathan, son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the displacement of the land.
JDG 18:31 And they themselves stationed the carved image Micah made all the days - as many as the house of God was in Shiloh. And it came to pass in those days there was not a king in Israel.
JDG 19:1 And there was a man, a Levite, sojourning on the sides of mount Ephraim. And he took to himself a woman concubine from Beth-lehem Judah.
JDG 19:2 And his concubine provoked him to anger, and she went forth from him unto the house of her father in Beth-lehem Judah, and was there the days of four months.
JDG 19:3 And her husband rose up, and went after her, to speak unto her heart, to reconcile her; and his servant was with him, and a pair of beasts of burden. And he went unto the house of her father. And the father of the young woman beheld him, and was at hand for meeting him.
JDG 19:4 And his father-in-law brought him in - the father of the young woman. And he stayed with him three days. And they ate and drank and slept there.
JDG 19:5 And it came to pass on the fourth day, that they rose early in the morning, and he rose up to depart. And the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, Support your heart with a piece of bread, and after this go!
JDG 19:6 And he sat down, and both ate together, and drank. And the father of the young woman said to the man, For a beginning, lodge and do good to your heart!
JDG 19:7 And the man rose up to depart, and his father-in-law forced him, and he stayed and lodged there.
JDG 19:8 And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart. And the father of the young woman said, Support indeed your heart with bread, and soldier until the day should decline! And both ate and drank.
JDG 19:9 And the man rose up to go, he and his concubine, and his servant. And his father-in-law said to him, the father of the young woman, Behold, indeed the day is declined into evening, lodge here and do good to your heart, and rise early tomorrow unto your way, and you shall depart unto your tent!
JDG 19:10 And the man did not want to lodge. And he rose up and went forth, and came unto before Jebus, this is Jerusalem; and with him were a pair of beasts of burden being saddled, and his concubine with him.
JDG 19:11 And they were near Jebus, and the day declined exceedingly. And the servant said to his master, Come please, even we should turn aside into this city of the Jebusites, and lodge in it.
JDG 19:12 And his master said to him, In no way shall we turn aside into an alien city, in which there is not one from the sons of Israel; even we shall go by unto Gibeah.
JDG 19:13 And he said to his servant, Come, for we should approach one of the places, and we should lodge in Gibeah or in Ramah.
JDG 19:14 And they went by, and the sun went down on them being next to Gibeah, which is of Benjamin.
JDG 19:15 And they turned aside there to enter to rest up in Gibeah. And he entered and sat in the square of the city; and there is not a man bringing them into the house to rest up.
JDG 19:16 And behold, an old man entered from his works from out of the field at evening, and the man was from mount Ephraim; and he sojourned in Gibeah. And the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.
JDG 19:17 And he looked up with his eyes, and saw the journeying man in the square of the city. And the old man said, Where are you going, and from what place do you come?
JDG 19:18 And he said to him, We are passing over from Beth-lehem of Judah unto the side of mount Ephraim; And I am from there, and I went unto Beth-lehem of Judah, and I run to my house; but there is not a man bringing me into a house.
JDG 19:19 And indeed straw and fodder exists for our donkeys, and indeed bread and wine exists to me, and to the maidservant, and to the servant - to your servants there is not a deficiency of any thing.
JDG 19:20 And the old man said, Peace to you; only let any deficiency of yours be upon me, only you should not rest up in the square.
JDG 19:21 And he brought him into his house, and camped his beasts of burden. And they washed their feet, and ate and drank.
JDG 19:22 And they were doing their heart good; and, behold, the men of the city, sons of lawbreakers, encircled the house, and knocked upon the door, and said to the man, the master of the house, the old man, saying, Lead out the man entering into your house, that we should know him.
JDG 19:23 And the man came forth to them, the master of the house, and said to them, By no means, my brothers; you should not do evil indeed with this man entering into my house - you should not do this folly.
JDG 19:24 Behold, my daughter the virgin, and his concubine; but I will bring them, and you humble them, and do to them the good thing in your eyes - and to this man you should not do the thing of this folly.
JDG 19:25 And the men did not want to hear him. And the man took hold of his concubine, and led her to them outside; and they knew her, and sported with her the entire night until the morning. And they sent her at the same time the dawn ascended.
JDG 19:26 And the woman came in the morning, and fell by the door of the vestibule of the house of the man of whom her master was there, until of which time light shown through.
JDG 19:27 And her master rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and came forth to depart into his way. And behold, the woman, his concubine, was fallen by the door of the house, and her hands were upon the threshold.
JDG 19:28 And he said to her, Rise up, for we should go forth! And she answered not to him for she had died. And he lifted her upon the beast of burden, and the man rose up and went forth to his place.
JDG 19:29 And he entered into his house, and took the knife, and took hold of his concubine, and dismembered her according to her bones into twelve portions, and sent them unto all the tribes of Israel.
JDG 19:30 And it came to pass all the ones seeing said, Neither happened, nor was thus seen from the days of the ascending of the sons of Israel from out of the land of Egypt until this day. Appoint indeed to yourselves counsel concerning her, and speak!
JDG 20:1 And there came forth all the sons of Israel, and the congregation held an assembly as one man, from Dan and unto Beer-sheba, and the land of Gilead, before the LORD in Mizpeh.
JDG 20:2 And the region established all of the people in all the tribes of Israel in the assembly of the people of God - four hundred thousand men on foot unsheathing the broadsword.
JDG 20:3 (And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel ascended unto Mizpeh.) And the sons of Israel said, Tell where this evil took place?
JDG 20:4 And the man answered, the Levite, the husband of the woman having been murdered, and said, I came unto Gibeah of Benjamin, I and my concubine, to rest up.
JDG 20:5 And the men rose up against me, the ones of Gibeah, and they encircled upon me, upon the house at night, and wanted to kill me. And they humbled my concubine, and sported with her, and she died.
JDG 20:6 And I took hold of my concubine, and I dismembered her, and I sent out into every border of the inheritance of Israel - for they committed folly in Israel.
JDG 20:7 Behold, all you, the sons of Israel, make to yourselves an account and plan here!
JDG 20:8 And all the people rose up as one man, saying, We shall not enter - a man into his tent, and we shall not turn aside - a man to his house.
JDG 20:9 And now this is the thing which we shall do to Gibeah; we will ascend against it by lot.
JDG 20:10 And we shall take ten men out of a hundred for all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand men, and a thousand out of ten thousand men, to take a provision for the people, to complete the task to the ones in going unto Gibeah of Benjamin, against all the folly which they did in Israel.
JDG 20:11 And came together every man of Israel to the city, as one man coming.
JDG 20:12 And the tribes of Israel sent out men in all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What is this evil that took place among you?
JDG 20:13 And now, give over the impious men in Gibeah, the sons of Belial, and we shall kill them, and lift away evil from Israel. But the sons of Benjamin wanted not to hear the voice of their brothers of the sons of Israel.
JDG 20:14 And the sons of Benjamin came together from their cities to Gibeah, to go forth into battle array against the sons of Israel.
JDG 20:15 And the sons of Benjamin were numbered in that day from out of the cities - twenty five thousand men unsheathing the broadsword, apart from the ones dwelling in Gibeah.
JDG 20:16 These numbered seven hundred chosen men from all of the people, ambidextrous; all these were slingers casting stones accurate to the hair, and not missing entirely.
JDG 20:17 And every man of Israel were numbered separate from the sons of Benjamin - four hundred thousand men unsheathing the broadsword. All these were men warriors.
JDG 20:18 And they rose up and ascended unto Beth-el, and asked of God. And the sons of Israel said, Who shall ascend to us guiding to wage war with the sons of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall ascend guiding.
JDG 20:19 And the sons of Israel rose up in the morning, and camped at Gibeah.
JDG 20:20 And every man of Israel went forth for war against Benjamin. And the man of Israel deployed against them for war against Gibeah.
JDG 20:21 And came forth the sons of Benjamin from out of the city, and they utterly destroyed in Israel in that day two and twenty thousand men upon the ground.
JDG 20:22 And the people strengthened - the man of Israel. And they proceeded to deploy for war in the place in which he deployed there on the first day.
JDG 20:23 And the sons of Israel ascended up, and wept before the LORD until evening, and asked of the LORD, saying, Shall I proceed to draw near for war against the sons of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, Ascend against him!
JDG 20:24 And the sons of Israel came forward against the sons of Benjamin in the second day.
JDG 20:25 And Benjamin came forth to meet them from Gibeah on the second day. And they utterly destroyed yet of the people of Israel eighteen thousand men upon the ground, all these unsheathing the broadsword.
JDG 20:26 And all the sons of Israel ascended up, and all the people, and came unto Beth-el, and wept, and sat there before the LORD, and fasted in that day until evening. And they offered a whole burnt offering for deliverance before the LORD.
JDG 20:27 And the sons of Israel asked in the LORD, (and the ark of the covenant of the LORD was there in those days,
JDG 20:28 and Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days,) saying, Shall I proceed still to go forth for war against the sons of Benjamin my brother, or slacken? And the LORD said, Ascend, and tomorrow I will deliver him into your hand.
JDG 20:29 And the sons of Israel placed an ambush in Gibeah round about.
JDG 20:30 And the sons of Israel ascended against the sons of Benjamin on the third day. And they deployed against Gibeah as once before, and once before that.
JDG 20:31 And the sons of Benjamin came forth for meeting the people, and were drawn away from the city; and they began to strike of the people (slain as once before, and once before that) in the ways which there is one ascending to Beth-el, and one ascending to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men of Israel.
JDG 20:32 And the sons of Benjamin said, They stumble before us as before. And the sons of Israel said, We should flee, and pull them out from the city into the ways.
JDG 20:33 And every man of Israel rose up from his place, and deployed in Baal-tamar. And the ambush of Israel wrestled from out of its place from the descent of Gibeah.
JDG 20:34 And they arrived right opposite Gibeah - ten thousand chosen men from out of all Israel. And the battle weighed down, and they they knew not that hurt has been affixed upon them.
JDG 20:35 And the LORD put Benjamin to flight before Israel. And the sons of Israel utterly destroyed among Benjamin in that day twenty and five thousand and a hundred men - all these unsheathing the broadsword.
JDG 20:36 And the sons of Benjamin beheld that they were put to flight. And the man of Israel gave place to Benjamin, for they hoped upon the ambush which they arranged near Gibeah.
JDG 20:37 And the ambush advanced, and they poured out against Gibeah. And the ambush went, and they struck all the city by the mouth of the broadsword.
JDG 20:38 And the arranged order was with the man of Israel with the ambush, for them to offer a signal-fire of smoke from the city.
JDG 20:39 And the man of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin began to strike slain against the man of Israel about thirty men. For they said, Surely being put to flight he was put to flight before us as the battle before.
JDG 20:40 And the signal-fire began to ascend from the city as a column of smoke. And Benjamin looked behind him, and, behold, there ascended the consummation of the city unto the heaven.
JDG 20:41 And the man of Israel turned. And the man of Benjamin hastened, for he beheld that a bad thing has touched him.
JDG 20:42 And they leaned before the man of Israel in the way of the wilderness, and the battle fell upon them unawares. And the ones from the cities - they utterly destroyed them in their midst.
JDG 20:43 And they cut up Benjamin, and pursued him according to his feet, and trampled him unto opposite Gibeah towards the rising of the sun.
JDG 20:44 And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell - all these men of power.
JDG 20:45 And they turned aside and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon. And they gleaned him in the ways - five thousand men. And they cleaved after them unto Gidom, and struck of them two thousand men.
JDG 20:46 And it came to pass all the ones falling among Benjamin was twenty-five thousand men unsheathing the broadsword in that day - all these were men of power.
JDG 20:47 And they turned aside and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon - six hundred men; and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon four months.
JDG 20:48 And the man of Israel turned against the sons of Benjamin, and struck them by the mouth of the broadsword, from the next city by city city., unto beast, and unto all being found in the cities - and the cities being found they burned by fire.
JDG 21:1 And the man of Israel swore by an oath in Mizpeh, saying, Not a man from us shall give his daughter to Benjamin for a wife.
JDG 21:2 And all the people came unto Beth-el, and sat there until evening before God, and lifted their voice, and wept a great weeping.
JDG 21:3 And they said, Why, O LORD God of Israel, has this taken place in Israel, to overlook today in Israel one tribe?
JDG 21:4 And it happened in the next day that the people rose early, and built there an altar, and offered a whole burnt offering of deliverance.
JDG 21:5 And the sons of Israel said, Who is the one not ascending among the assembly from all of the tribes of Israel to the LORD? For there was a great oath concerning the one not ascending to the LORD in Mizpeh, saying, To death he shall die.
JDG 21:6 And the sons of Israel relented concerning their brother Benjamin, and said, one tribe from Israel is removed today.
JDG 21:7 What should we do to them, to the ones left behind - for wives; for we swore by an oath to the LORD to not give to them from our daughters for wives?
JDG 21:8 And they said, What one is there of the tribes of Israel which ascended not to the LORD in Mizpeh? And behold, not a man came to the camp from Jabesh Gilead to the assembly.
JDG 21:9 And the people were numbered, And behold, there is not there a man from the ones dwelling in Jabesh Gilead.
JDG 21:10 And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the sons of the force. And they gave charge to them, saying, Go and strike all the ones dwelling in Jabesh Gilead by the mouth of the broadsword, even the women and the people!
JDG 21:11 And this is the word which you shall do. Every male and every woman knowing the marriage-bed of a man you shall devote to consumption.
JDG 21:12 And they found of ones dwelling Jabesh Gilead four hundred young women virgins that knew not a man, in the marriage-bed of a man. And they led them into the camp in Shiloh which is in the land of Canaan.
JDG 21:13 And all the congregation sent and spoke to the sons of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon, and they called them for peace.
JDG 21:14 And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel in that time, and they gave to them the women who were of the women of Jabesh Gilead - and it pleased them thus.
JDG 21:15 And the people were comforted concerning Benjamin, for the LORD made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
JDG 21:16 And the elders of the congregation said, What shall we do to the remaining for wives, now that the woman was removed from Benjamin?
JDG 21:17 And he said, There must be an inheritance to the ones surviving - to Benjamin, that in no way a tribe should be wiped away from Israel.
JDG 21:18 For we are not able to give to them wives from our daughters, for the sons of Israel swore by an oath, saying, Accursed is the one giving a wife to Benjamin.
JDG 21:19 And they said, Behold, there is a holiday to the LORD in Shiloh from days to days, which is from the north of Beth-el, according to the rising of the sun, upon the corridor ascending from Beth-el unto Shechem, and from south of Lebonah.
JDG 21:20 And they gave charge to the sons of Benjamin, saying, Go forth and lie in wait at the vineyards!
JDG 21:21 And you shall look, and, behold, whenever the daughters of the ones dwelling in Shiloh should come forth joining in a dance with a company of dancers, that you shall come forth from the vineyards, and let a man seize by force to himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh! And you shall depart unto the land of Benjamin.
JDG 21:22 And it will be whenever their fathers or their brothers should come to quarrel with us, that we shall say to them, Show mercy on them! For a man did not take to himself a wife in the battle, for you did not give to them according to the time which you trespassed.
JDG 21:23 And the sons of Benjamin did thus, and took wives according to their number from the ones dancing whom they snatched. And they went and returned unto their inheritance, and built up the cities, and dwelt in them.
JDG 21:24 And the sons of Israel walked from there in that time, each man to his tribe, and to his kin; and each man went forth from there to his inheritance.
JDG 21:25 In those days there was not a king in Israel - man did the upright thing in his eyes.
RUT 1:1 And it came to pass in the days in the judging of the judges. And came to pass a famine in the land. And went forth a man from Beth-lehem of Judea to sojourn in the field of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
RUT 1:2 And the name to the man was Elimelech, and the name to his wife was Naomi, and the name to his two sons - Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from out of Beth-lehem of Judah. And they came into the country of Moab, and were there.
RUT 1:3 And Elimelech the husband of Naomi died; and she and her two sons were left.
RUT 1:4 And they took to themselves Moabite wives; the name to the one was Orpah, and the name to the second Ruth; and they dwelt there about ten years.
RUT 1:5 And also indeed both Mahlon and Chilion died; and the woman was left of her two sons, and of her husband.
RUT 1:6 And she rose up, and her two daughters-in-law, and they returned from out of the country of Moab; for they heard in the country of Moab that the LORD visited his people to give to them breads.
RUT 1:7 And she went forth from out of the place of which she was there, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went by journey to return to the land of Judah.
RUT 1:8 And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, Go, please, let each return to the house of her mother! May the LORD deal mercy with you, as you did with the ones having died, and with me.
RUT 1:9 May the LORD give to you, and you should find rest each in the house of her husband. And she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice and wept.
RUT 1:10 And they said to her, We shall return with you unto your people.
RUT 1:11 And Naomi said, Return, please, my daughters! Why do you go with me? Are there still to me sons in my belly, and will they be to you for husbands?
RUT 1:12 Return, please, my daughters! Go, please! For I grow old to not have a husband. For I said, Is it to me a reality for it to be to me a husband, and shall I give birth to sons?
RUT 1:13 Shall you wait for them until of which time they should become manly? Or, for them shall you hold up to not have a husband? No, my daughters. For it is made bitter to me exceedingly for you that the hand of the LORD came forth against me.
RUT 1:14 And they lifted up their voice, and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, and turned back to her people; but Ruth followed her.
RUT 1:15 And Naomi said to Ruth, Behold, your sister-in-law returned to her people, and to her gods; you also please turn back after your sister-in-law!
RUT 1:16 And Ruth said, Do not encounter to me to leave you, or to turn behind you! For you - where ever you should go, I shall go; and where ever you should lodge, I shall lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
RUT 1:17 And where ever you should die, I shall die, and there I shall be entombed. Thus the LORD do to me, and thus may he add more! For death only shall separate between me and you.
RUT 1:18 And Naomi seeing that she was determined to go with her, abated to speak to her any more.
RUT 1:19 And both went until their arriving in Beth-lehem. And it came to pass in their coming unto Beth-lehem, that all the city resounded concerning them, and they said, Is this Naomi?
RUT 1:20 And she said to them, Do not indeed call me Naomi! Call me, Bitter! for the worthy one embittered me exceedingly.
RUT 1:21 I went out full, and the LORD returned me empty. And why do you call me Naomi, and the LORD humbled me, and the worthy one afflicted me?
RUT 1:22 And Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, to return from the country of Moab. And they came unto Beth-lehem at the beginning of barley harvest.
RUT 2:1 And to Naomi was a man acquainted to her husband, and the man was mighty in strength of the kin of Elimelech; and the name to him was Boaz.
RUT 2:2 And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, I should go indeed into a field, and gather among the ears of wheat after of whom ever I should find favor in his eyes. And she said to her, Go, O daughter!
RUT 2:3 And she went. And having arrived, she collected together in the field after the ones harvesting. And she fell by chance in the portion of the field of Boaz, of the kin of Elimelech.
RUT 2:4 And, behold, Boaz came from Beth-lehem, and said to the ones harvesting, The LORD be with you. And they said to him, May the LORD bless you.
RUT 2:5 And Boaz said to his servant having been set over the ones harvesting, Whose young woman is this?
RUT 2:6 And the servant attending over the ones harvesting answered and said, She is the Moabitess servant returning with Naomi from out of the country of Moab.
RUT 2:7 And she said, I shall collect together please, and I will bring in the sheaves behind the ones harvesting. And she came and stood, from morning and until evening - she rested not in the field a little.
RUT 2:8 And Boaz said to Ruth, Did you not hear, O daughter? You should not go to collect into another field, and you should not go from here - you join up here with my young women!
RUT 2:9 And let your eyes be unto the field where ever mine should harvest, and you should go after them! Behold, I gave charge to the servants to not touch you. And when you shall thirst, then you shall go to the vessels, and you shall drink from where the servants should draw water.
RUT 2:10 And she fell upon her face, and did obeisance upon the ground, and said to him, Why is it that I found favor in your eyes to recognize me, and I am a stranger?
RUT 2:11 And Boaz answered, and said to her, By report it was reported to me all as much as you have done with your mother-in-law after the dying of your husband; and how you left behind your father, and your mother, and the land of your origin, and went to a people which you knew not yesterday and the third day before.
RUT 2:12 May the LORD repay your work, and may your wage be full from the LORD God of Israel, to whom you came to yield under his wings.
RUT 2:13 And she said, May I find favor in your eyes, O my master; for you comforted me, and because you spoke in your heart to your bondwoman; and behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants.
RUT 2:14 And Boaz said to her, Already it is the hour to eat; draw near here, for you shall eat of my breads, and dip your morsel in the vinegar! And Ruth sat by the side of the ones harvesting. And Boaz heaped up to her toasted grain, and she ate, and was filled, and left.
RUT 2:15 And she rose up to collect grain, and Boaz gave charge to his servants, saying, And indeed, let her collect in the midst of the sheaves, and do not shame her!
RUT 2:16 And indeed in setting aside, you set aside for her of the things being heaped up, and allow her, and she shall collect, and you shall not reproach her!
RUT 2:17 And she collected in the field until evening, and she beat with a rod what she collected up, and it was about an ephah of barley.
RUT 2:18 And she carried it, and entered into the city. And her mother-in-law saw what she collected - and Ruth brought forth to give to her what was left of what she was filled up with.
RUT 2:19 And her mother-in-law said to her, Where did you collect today? And where did you do it? May it be the one recognizing you be being blessed. And Ruth reported to her mother-in-law where she did it. And she said, The name of the man with whom I did this today is Boaz.
RUT 2:20 And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed is the LORD, for he abandoned not his mercy with the living and with the ones having died. And Naomi said to her, The man is near to us, of the ones acting as next of kin - he is of us.
RUT 2:21 And Ruth said to her mother-in-law, And also he said to me, You cleave with the young men of mine, until whenever they should finish all the harvest which belongs to me.
RUT 2:22 And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, It is good, O daughter, that you went forth with his young women, and they shall not meet with you in another field.
RUT 2:23 And Ruth cleaved to the young women of Boaz to collect until they completed the harvest of the barley, and the harvest of the wheat.
RUT 3:1 And she stayed with her mother-in-law. And Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, O daughter, In no way shall I seek to rest for you, that a good thing should happen to you.
RUT 3:2 And now is not Boaz acquainted to us, of whom you were with his young women? Behold, he winnows at the threshing-floor of the barley this night.
RUT 3:3 And you shall bathe, and anoint, and put your clothes upon yourself, and ascend unto the threshing-floor! You should not make yourself known to the man, until he finishes eating and drinking.
RUT 3:4 And it will be at his going to sleep, that you shall perceive the place where he sleeps there, and you shall go in and uncover the things by his feet, and you shall go to sleep - and he shall report to you what you shall do.
RUT 3:5 And Ruth said to her, All as much as you should tell to me I will do.
RUT 3:6 And she went down into the threshing-floor, and she did according to all as much as her mother-in-law gave charge to her.
RUT 3:7 And Boaz ate, and drank, and did good to his heart, and went to sleep in a portion of the pile. And she came in secret, and uncovered the things by his feet, and went to sleep.
RUT 3:8 And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was startled and disturbed - and behold, a woman slept at his feet.
RUT 3:9 And he said, Who are you? And she said, I am Ruth, your bondwoman - and you shall put your garment border upon your bondwoman, for you are a relative.

RUT 3:11 And now, O daughter, do not fear! All what ever you should say I will do for you. For all of the people of my tribe know that you are a woman of ability.
RUT 3:12 And now truly I am a relative. But indeed there is a relative in the land who is over me.
RUT 3:13 You lodge the night! and it will be in the morning, that if he should act as next of kin for you - good, let him act as next of kin! But if he should not want to act as next of kin for you, I shall act as next of kin for you. As the LORD lives, you go to sleep until morning!
RUT 3:14 And she went to sleep at his feet until morning. And she rose up before a man could recognize his neighbor. And Boaz said, Do not let it be known that a woman has come unto the threshing-floor!
RUT 3:15 And he said to her, Bring the apron upon you, and hold it! And she held it, and he measured six measures of barley, and placed them unto her. And she entered into the city.
RUT 3:16 And Ruth entered to her mother-in-law. And she said, What is it, O daughter? And she reported to her all as much as the man did for her.
RUT 3:17 And she said, These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said to me, You should not enter empty to your mother-in-law.
RUT 3:18 And she said, Sit down, O daughter, until you realize how not the matter shall fall! For not in any way should the man be still until whenever he should finish the matter today.
RUT 4:1 And Boaz ascended unto the gate, and sat there. And behold, the relative came near whom Boaz spoke of. And Boaz said to him, In turning aside, sit here in private! And he turned aside, and sat.
RUT 4:2 And Boaz took ten men from the elders of the city, and said, Sit here! And they sat.
RUT 4:3 And Boaz said to the one acting as next of kin, Concerning the portion of the field which is of our brother Elimelech, which he gave to Naomi, the one returning from out of the country of Moab,
RUT 4:4 that I said to myself, I will uncover your ear, saying, You acquire it before the ones sitting down, and before the elders of my people! If you are acting as next of kin, then act as next of kin! But if not acting as next of kin, announce it to me, and I shall know! For there is not one besides you to act as next of kin, and I am after you. And he said, I am. I shall act as next of kin.
RUT 4:5 And Boaz said, In the day you acquire the field from the hand of Naomi, also of Ruth the Moabitess, wife of the one having died, even she you must acquire, so as to raise up the name of the one having died, for his inheritance.
RUT 4:6 And the relative said, I shall not be able to act as next of kin myself, lest at any time I ruin my right of inheritance. You yourself act as next of kin for my inheritance, for I shall not be able to act as next of kin!
RUT 4:7 And this was the ordinance in former times in Israel for the right of inheritance, and for the equivalent, to establish every matter - a man untied his sandal, and he gave it to his neighbor acting as next of kin for his right of inheritance. And this was testimony in Israel.
RUT 4:8 And the relative said to Boaz, You acquire to yourself my right of inheritance! And he untied his sandal and gave it to him.
RUT 4:9 And Boaz said to the elders, and to all the people, You are witnesses today that I have acquired all the things of Elimelech, and all as much as exists to Chilion and to Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi.
RUT 4:10 And indeed, Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon I have acquired for myself for wife, to raise up the name of the one having died, for his inheritance, and the name of the one having died shall not be utterly destroyed from among his brothers, and from the gate of his place - you are witnesses today.
RUT 4:11 And all the people at the gate said, We are witnesses. And the elders said, May the LORD give your wife, the one entering into your house, to be as Rachel and as Leah, the ones who both built the house of Israel, and did powerfully in Ephratah, and it will be a name in Beth-lehem.
RUT 4:12 And may your house become as the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bore to Judah. Of your seed may the LORD give to you children of this maidservant.
RUT 4:13 And Boaz took Ruth, and she became to him for wife. And he entered to her. And the LORD gave to her conception, and she bore a son.
RUT 4:14 And the women said to Naomi, Blessed be the LORD who rested not to provide to you today a relative; and may he call out your name in Israel.
RUT 4:15 And he will be to you for restoring life, and to nourish your gray hair; for your daughter-in-law loving you bore him, which is good to you above seven sons.
RUT 4:16 And Naomi took the boy, and put him to her bosom, and became to him for a wet-nurse.
RUT 4:17 And the neighbor women called to him the name, saying, A son was birthed to Naomi. And they called his name Obed - this one is father of Jesse, father of David.
RUT 4:18 And these are the generations of Pharez - Pharez engendered Hezron,
RUT 4:19 and Hezron engendered Ram, and Ram engendered Amminadab,
RUT 4:20 and Aminadab engendered Nahshon, and Nahshon engendered Salmon,
RUT 4:21 and Salmon engendered Boaz, and Boaz engendered Obed,
RUT 4:22 and Obed engendered Jesse, and Jesse engendered David.
1SA 1:1 And there was one man from Ramathaim Zophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son Zuph, from mount Ephraim.
1SA 1:2 And to this one was two wives; the name to the one was Hannah, and the name to the second was Peninnah. And there was to Peninnah a child, and to Hannah there was not a child.
1SA 1:3 And that man ascended from days to days from out of his city of Ramathaim to do obeisance and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And was there Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, priests of the LORD.
1SA 1:4 And came to pass a day that Elkanah sacrificed, and he gave to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons, and to her daughters, portions.
1SA 1:5 And to Hannah he gave one portion, for there was not a child to her; except that Elkanah loved Hannah above Peninnah. But the LORD locked the matter concerning her womb.
1SA 1:6 And her rival provoked her to anger - even indeed a provocation to anger because of the treating her with contempt, for the LORD closed up the matters concerning her womb to not give to her a child.
1SA 1:7 Thus she did year by year in her ascending unto the house of the LORD; and she was depressed, and she wept, and did not eat.
1SA 1:8 And Elkanah her husband said to her, Hannah, what is it to you that you weep? And why do you not eat? And why does your heart beat you? Am I not good to you over ten children?
1SA 1:9 And Hannah rose up after their eating in Shiloh, and after drinking. And Eli the priest sat upon the chair at the doorposts of the temple of the LORD.
1SA 1:10 And she was in severe pain of soul, and she prayed to the LORD, and with weeping she wept.
1SA 1:11 And she vowed a vow, saying, O LORD of hosts, if looking you should look upon the humiliation of your bondwoman, and should remember me, and should not forget your bondwoman, and should give to your bondwoman seed of a male, then I will put him before you, dedicated until the day of his death. And an iron razor shall not ascend upon his head.
1SA 1:12 And it came to pass when she multiplied praying before the LORD, that Eli the priest watched her mouth.
1SA 1:13 And she spoke in her heart, and her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. And Eli considered her to be intoxicated.
1SA 1:14 And Eli said to her, Until when shall you be intoxicated? Remove your wine!
1SA 1:15 And Hannah answered, and said, No, O master, I am a woman with a hard day, and wine and strong drink I have not drunk, and I pour out my soul before the LORD.
1SA 1:16 You should not grant your bondwoman for a mischievous daughter. For from the amount of my meditation, and from the amount of my depression, I have been stretched out until the present.
1SA 1:17 And Eli answered, and said to her, Go in peace! The God of Israel will give to you all your request which you asked of him.
1SA 1:18 And she said, Your bondwoman found favor in your eyes. And the woman went her way, and ate with her husband, and drank, and her face was not downcast any longer.
1SA 1:19 And they rose early in the morning, and they did obeisance to the LORD, and went their way. And Elkanah entered unto his house in Ramah, and he knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her, and she conceived.
1SA 1:20 And it came to pass in the time of the days that Hannah bore a son, that she called his name Samuel, saying that, From the LORD almighty I asked him.
1SA 1:21 And the man Elkanah ascended, and all his house, to sacrifice in Shiloh, for the sacrifice of the days, and his vows.
1SA 1:22 And Hannah ascended not with him; for she said to her husband, I will wait until the ascending of the boy, whenever I should have weaned it, and he shall appear in front of the LORD, and shall settle there unto the eon.
1SA 1:23 And Elkanah her husband said to her, You do the good thing in your eyes; sit until whenever you should wean it! Only may the LORD establish the thing coming forth from out of your mouth. And the woman sat, and nursed her son until whenever she weaned him.
1SA 1:24 And she ascended with him unto Shiloh with a calf being three years old, and an ephah of fine flour, and a skin flask of wine. And she entered into the house of the LORD in Shiloh, and the boy with them.
1SA 1:25 And they led him before the LORD, and they slew the calf. And Hannah the mother of the boy brought it to Eli.
1SA 1:26 And she said, By me, O master, your soul should live; I am the woman standing before you with you while praying to the LORD.
1SA 1:27 Over this boy I prayed, and the LORD gave to me my request which I asked of him.
1SA 1:28 And I lend him to the LORD all the days which he should live for use by the LORD.
1SA 2:1 And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart is solidified in the LORD; my horn was raised high by my God; my mouth was widened over my enemies; for I was glad in your deliverance.
1SA 2:2 For there is not one holy as the LORD; and there is not a just one as our God; and there is not one holy besides you.
1SA 2:3 Do not boast, and do not speak high things in superiority! Let not come forth lofty language from out of your mouth! For the LORD is a God of knowledge, and God is preparing his practices.
1SA 2:4 The bow of the mighty is weakened, and the ones being weakened girded on power.
1SA 2:5 The ones full of breads are made less; and the ones hungering disregarded the land the hungering ceased.; for the sterile gave birth to seven, and the one with many in children weakened.
1SA 2:6 The LORD puts to death, and he brings forth alive; he leads them down into Hades, and he leads up.
1SA 2:7 The LORD makes poor, and he enriches; he humbles, and elevates.
1SA 2:8 He raises up from the earth the needy, and from the dung he raises the poor, to seat him with mighty ones of the people, and inheriting to them a throne of glory;
1SA 2:9 giving the thing vowed to the one vowing, and blessed the years of the just one; for not by strength is man able.
1SA 2:10 The LORD shall make his opponent weak. The LORD is holy. The LORD ascended into heavens, and he thundered. He shall judge the extremities of the earth being just. And he shall give strength to our kings, and will raise up high the horn of his anointed one.
1SA 2:11 And they went forth unto Ramah unto their house. And the boy was officiating to the LORD before the face of Eli the priest.
1SA 2:12 And the sons of Eli the priest were mischievous sons; not knowing the LORD.
1SA 2:13 And the ordinance of the priest of all the people of the one sacrificing was this - that the servant of the priest came when ever the meat boiled, and in his hand was a three-pronged meat hook.
1SA 2:14 And he stuck it into the great kettle, or into the brass caldron, or into the earthen pot; and all, what ever ascended on the meat hook the priest took to himself. According to thus they did to all Israel in Shiloh to the ones coming to sacrifice to the LORD.
1SA 2:15 And before the burning the fat, the servant of the priest would come, and said to the man sacrificing, Give meat to the priest to roast; for in no way shall I take meat from you cooked from out of the kettle.
1SA 2:16 And if the man who was sacrificing said, First let there be burnt as is fit for the fat, and then you shall take for yourself from all what your soul desires. Then he said, No, but now you shall give it; and if not, I will take it forcefully.
1SA 2:17 And the sin of the young men was great before the LORD, exceedingly; for they annulled the sacrifice of the LORD.
1SA 2:18 And Samuel was officiating in the presence of the LORD, a boy, being girded with a linen ephod.
1SA 2:19 And his mother made a small double garment for him, and brought to him from days unto days in her ascending with her husband, to sacrifice the sacrifice of the days.
1SA 2:20 And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, the LORD pay to you seed from out of this woman for the loan of which she treated to the LORD. And the man went forth to his place.
1SA 2:21 And the LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived again, and she bore yet three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel was magnified in the presence of the LORD.
1SA 2:22 And Eli was an old man, exceedingly. And he heard what his sons did to all the sons of Israel, and that his sons went to bed with the women standing by the doors of the tent of the testimony.
1SA 2:23 And he said to them, Why do you do according to these things, which I hear being spoken ill of you from the mouth of all the people of the LORD?
1SA 2:24 No, children, no; for it is not good, the hearing which I hear of the making the people to not serve to the LORD.
1SA 2:25 If by sinning a man should sin against a man, then they shall pray for him to the LORD. But if a man sins against the LORD, who shall pray for him? But they hearkened not to the voice of their father. For willing, the LORD preferred to utterly destroy them.
1SA 2:26 And the boy Samuel went on, and was magnified, and was in good standing with the LORD, and with men.
1SA 2:27 And the man of God came to Eli, and said to him, Thus says the LORD, In revealing, I revealed myself to the house of your father, of their being bondmen to the house of Pharaoh in the land of Egypt.
1SA 2:28 And I chose the house of your father from out of all the tribes of Israel to officiate as priest to me, to ascend unto my altar, and to burn incense, and to carry an ephod before me. And I gave to the house of your father all the things of the sacrifices of the fire of the sons of Israel for food.
1SA 2:29 Why have you looked upon my incense offering, and upon my sacrifice offering with an impudent eye, and glorified your sons above me, in their blessing themselves with the first-fruit of every sacrifice of Israel, prior of me?
1SA 2:30 On account of this, thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, I said, Your house, and the house of your father shall go through before me unto the eon. And now, says the LORD, not even one will be to me, for the ones glorifying me I will glorify, and the ones treating me with contempt shall be disgraced.
1SA 2:31 Behold, days come, and I shall utterly destroy your seed, and the seed of the house of your father.
1SA 2:32 And you shall look upon new fortifications upon all the things which Israel shall do good - and there will not be an old man in your house all the days.
1SA 2:33 And a man whom I should not utterly destroy among you from my altar, I will make his eyes to fail, and his life will flow down, and all the ones abounding of your house shall fall by the broadsword of men.
1SA 2:34 And this is to you the sign which shall come upon these your two sons - Hophni and Phinehas; in one day both shall die.
1SA 2:35 And I will raise up for myself a trustworthy priest who will do all the things in my heart and the things in my soul. And I will build to him a trustworthy house; and he shall go through before my anointed all the days.
1SA 2:36 And it will be everyone being left behind among your house shall come to do obeisance to him for an obolus of silver, and for one bread, saying, Throw me aside upon one of your priesthoods to eat bread!
1SA 3:1 And the boy Samuel was officiating to the LORD before Eli the priest. And the word of the LORD was esteemed in those days - there was not a vision for giving orders.
1SA 3:2 And it came to pass in that day, that Eli slept in his own place, and his eyes began to be darkened, and he was not able to see.
1SA 3:3 And the lamp of God was before its being extinguished, and Samuel slept in the temple of the LORD where the ark of God was.
1SA 3:4 And the LORD called, saying, Samuel, Samuel. And he said, Behold, it is I.
1SA 3:5 And he ran to Eli, and said, Behold, it is I; for you called me. And he said, I have not called you; return and sleep! And he returned and slept.
1SA 3:6 And the LORD added again to call Samuel. And he went to Eli the second time, and said, Behold, it is I; for you called me. And he said, I have not called you child, return and sleep!
1SA 3:7 And it was before Samuel knew God, and before the revealing the word of the LORD to him.
1SA 3:8 And the LORD added again to call Samuel a third time. And he rose up and went to Eli. And said, Behold, it is I; for you have called me. And Eli discerned that the LORD has called the boy.
1SA 3:9 And Eli said to Samuel, Return and sleep child! And it will be if he should call you, that you shall say, Speak, O LORD, for your bondman hears! And Samuel went, and went to bed in his place.
1SA 3:10 And the LORD came, and stood, and called him as once before, and once before that, Samuel, Samuel. And Samuel said, Speak, O LORD, for your bondman hears!
1SA 3:11 And the LORD said to Samuel, Behold, I perform my words in Israel, so that every one hearing them, it shall sound in both of his ears.
1SA 3:12 In that day I rouse up against Eli all as many things as I spoke against his house - I will begin, and I will complete.
1SA 3:13 And I have announced to him that I punish; even I, his house, unto the eon for the iniquities of his sons, in which he knew that his sons were speaking evil of God, and he did not admonish them.
1SA 3:14 And have I not thus sworn by an oath to the house of Eli, Shall the iniquity of the house of Eli be atoned by incense or by sacrifices into the eon?
1SA 3:15 And Samuel went to bed until morning. And he rose up early in the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel feared to report the vision to Eli.
1SA 3:16 And Eli said to Samuel, Samuel child. And he said, Behold, it is I.
1SA 3:17 And he said, What was the word being spoken to you? Do not indeed hide them from me! Thus God do to you, and thus add to it, if you should hide from me the word.
1SA 3:18 And Samuel reported to him all the words, and hid not from him. And Eli said, The LORD himself will do the good thing before him.
1SA 3:19 And Samuel was magnified, and the LORD was with him, and there fell not one from all of his words upon the ground.

1SA 4:1 And came to pass the word of Samuel to all Israel. And the Philistines gathered together for war against Israel; and Israel went forth to meet them for war. And they camped at Eben-ezer. And the Philistines camped in Aphek.
1SA 4:2 And the Philistines deployed for war against Israel. And the war leaned one way, and the men of Israel failed before the Philistines. And four thousand men were struck in the battle array in the field.
1SA 4:3 And the people came into the camp. And the elders of Israel said, Why is it so the LORD devastated us today before the Philistines? We should take to us the ark of the covenant of the LORD from out of Shiloh, and let it come forth in our midst, and it will deliver us from the hand of our enemies!
1SA 4:4 And the people sent unto Shiloh, and lifted from there the ark of covenant of the LORD of the forces, of which the cherubim sit upon. And both the sons of Eli were with the ark of the covenant of God - Hophni and Phinehas.
1SA 4:5 And it came to pass as the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, that all Israel shouted aloud with a great voice, and the earth resounded.
1SA 4:6 And the Philistines heard the sound of the cry. And they said, What is the sound of the cry - this great one in the camp of the Hebrews? And they knew that the ark of the LORD comes into the camp.
1SA 4:7 And the Philistines feared, and they said, This their God comes to them into the camp.
1SA 4:8 Woe to us, rescue us, O Master, today! For it happened not thus yesterday and third day before. Woe to us, who shall rescue us from out of the hand of these substantial gods? These are the gods striking Egypt in every calamity, and in the wilderness.
1SA 4:9 Fortify, and become as men, O Philistines, so that you should not serve to the Hebrews, as they served to us! And you shall be for men, and wage war against them!
1SA 4:10 And the Philistines waged war against them, and every man of Israel failed before the Philistines, and each fled unto his tent. And there came to pass an exceedingly great calamity; and there fell from Israel thirty thousand from the ranks.
1SA 4:11 And the ark of God was taken, and both the sons of Eli died - Hophni and Phinehas.
1SA 4:12 And there ran a man of Benjamin from out of the battle array, and came into Shiloh on that day, and his garments were torn up, and earth was upon his head.
1SA 4:13 And he came, and behold, Eli sat upon his chair by the gate watching the way, for his heart was receded on account of the ark of God. And the man entered into the city to report. And the whole city yelled out.
1SA 4:14 And Eli heard the sound of the yelling, and said, What is this sound of yelling? And the man hastening, entered and reported to Eli.
1SA 4:15 And Eli was a son ninety and eight years, and his eyes were weighed down, and he did not see.
1SA 4:16 And Eli said to the men standing around him, What is the report of this sound? And the man hastening, came forward to Eli, and said to him, I am the one having come from out of the camp, and I have fled from the battle array today. And Eli said, What is the thing taking place child?

1SA 4:18 And it happened as the ark of God was mentioned, that he fell from the chair backwardly, being next to the gate, and his back was broken, and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he judged Israel forty years.
1SA 4:19 And his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, having conceived to give birth, when she heard the message that the ark of God was taken, and that her father-in-law died, and her husband, that she wept and gave birth, for her birth pangs turned upon her.
1SA 4:20 And in the time she was going to die, that the women standing beside her said to her, Do not fear! For you have birthed a son. But she did not answer, and did not comprehend in her heart.

1SA 8:5 And they said to him, Behold, you grow old, and your sons go not in your way. And now place over us a king to adjudicate for us as all the nations!
1SA 8:6 And the matter was wicked in the eyes of Samuel, as they said, Give to us a king to adjudicate for us! And Samuel prayed to the LORD.
1SA 8:7 And the LORD said to Samuel, Hearken to the voice of the people as whatever they should speak to you. For it is not you they treat with contempt, but only me they treat with contempt, to not reign over them -
1SA 8:8 according to all the works which they did to me from which day I led them from Egypt, and until this day; even as they abandoned me, and served other gods, so they do also to you.
1SA 8:9 And now hearken to their voice! Only that in testifying you should testify to them, and you shall report to them the ordinance of the king, which shall reign over them.

1SA 8:16 And your bondmen, and your bondwomen, and your good herds, and your donkeys he shall take - and he will take a tenth for his works.
1SA 8:17 And he will take a tenth of your flocks. And you will be to him for bondmen.
