1SA 9:1 And there was a man from the sons of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Bechorath, son of Aphiah, son of a man of Benjamin, a mighty man in strength.
1SA 9:2 And to this one was a son, and his name was Saul, a huge goodly man. And there was not among the sons of Israel one good above him - he was head and shoulders and high above over all the land.
1SA 9:3 And the donkeys of Kish the father were lost of Saul. And Kish said to Saul his son, Take with yourself one of the servant-lads, and rise up, and go and seek the donkeys!
1SA 9:4 And they went through mount Ephraim, and went through the land of Shalitha, and did not find. And they went through the land of Shalim, and it was not. And they went through the land of Benjamin, and they did not find.
1SA 9:5 And of their coming unto Zuph, and Saul said to his servant-lad with him, Come, for we should return, lest my father sparing concerning the donkeys, should be thoughtful concerning us.
1SA 9:6 And the servant-lad said to him, Behold, indeed a man of God is in this city, and the man is honorable; all what ever he should speak, coming, it shall be at hand. And now, we should go there, so that he should report to us our way upon which we should go upon it.
1SA 9:7 And Saul said to his servant-lad with him, Yes, behold, we shall go. But what shall we carry in to the man of God, for the breads have failed from out of our containers, and there is not much with us to carry to the man of God that exists to us?
1SA 9:8 And the servant-lad proceeded to answer Saul, and said, Behold, there is found in my hand a fourth shekel of silver; and you shall give it to the man of God, and he shall report to us our way.
1SA 9:9 And before in Israel, thus said each man in their going to ask God, Come, and we should go to the seer. For the prophet was called by the people before, The Seer.
1SA 9:10 And Saul said to his servant-lad, Your word is good. Come, for we should go. And they went into the city of which was there the man of God.
1SA 9:11 And of their ascending the ascent of the city, and they found young women going forth to draw water. And they say to them, Is there here the seer?
1SA 9:12 And the young women answered them, and said, He is, behold, in front of you - hasten! For now he comes into the city, because of the day, for a sacrifice today for the people in Bama.
1SA 9:13 As soon as you enter into the city, thus you shall find him in the city, before his ascending unto Bama to eat. For in no way should the people eat until his entering, for this one blesses the sacrifice; and after these things the strangers eat. And now, ascend! For on account of the day you shall find him.
1SA 9:14 And they ascend into the city. And they were entering in the midst of the city, and behold, Samuel came forth for the meeting them, to ascend unto Bama.
1SA 9:15 And the LORD uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came to him, saying,
1SA 9:16 At this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him for ruler over my people Israel, and he shall deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I looked upon the humiliation of my people, for their yelling came to me.
1SA 9:17 And Samuel beheld Saul, and the LORD answered him, Behold, the man whom I said to you - this one shall rule over my people.
1SA 9:18 And Saul came to Samuel in the midst of the city, and he said, Report indeed to me, of what house is the seer?
1SA 9:19 And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am he. Ascend before me unto Bama, and eat with me today, and I will send you in the morning, and all the things in your heart I will report to you!
1SA 9:20 And concerning the donkeys being lost to you today for three days, you should not put your heart to them, for they are found. And what are the beautiful things of Israel? Is it not to you, and to all the house of your father?
1SA 9:21 And Saul answered and said, Am I not a man a son of a Benjamite, of the lesser chiefdom of the tribes of Israel? And my family least of all the families of Benjamin? And why have you spoken to me concerning this thing?
1SA 9:22 And Samuel took Saul and his servant-lad, and brought them into the lodging, and set for them a place among the foremost of the ones being called - about thirty men.
1SA 9:23 And Samuel said to the cook, Give to me the portion which I gave to you, which I told you to put it by you.
1SA 9:24 And the cook took the hind quarter, and the part upon it, and placed it before Saul. And Samuel said to Saul, Behold, the leftover; place it before you, and eat! For as a testimony it is placed for you over the people - pluck it off! And Saul ate with Samuel in that day.

1SA 25:37 And it came to pass in the morning as Nabal sobered up from the wine, his wife reported to him all these things. And his heart died in him, and he became as stone.
1SA 25:38 And it came to pass after about ten days, that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

And the evil of Nabal the LORD returned against his own head. And David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her to himself for a wife.

1SA 26:5 And David rose up in private, and went into the place where Saul was sleeping there. And David saw the place where Saul went to bed there. And Abner son of Ner his commander-in-chief was there. And Saul was sleeping in the royal chariot, and the people were camping round about him.

2SA 1:26 I ache over you, Jonathan, O my brother. You were beautiful to me, exceedingly; your affection to me caused wonder - above the affection of women.
2SA 1:27 O how the mighty ones fell, and the weapons of warfare perished.

2SA 2:14 And Abner said to Joab, Raise up indeed the servant-lads and let them play before us! And Joab said, Let them arise!
2SA 2:15 And they rose up and went by in number - twelve of the servants of Benjamin of Ishbosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
2SA 2:16 And they each held by their hand the head of his neighbor; and his knife was thrust into the side of his neighbor; and they fell down together. And they called that place, Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gibeon.
2SA 2:17 And the battle was hard so as to an exceeding degree in that day. And Abner and the men of Israel failed before the servants of David.
2SA 2:18 And there were there three sons of Zeruiah - Joab and Abishai and Asahel. And Asahel was light of his feet, as one doe of the ones in the field.
2SA 2:19 And Asahel pursued after Abner, and did not turn aside to go to the right nor to the left after Abner.
2SA 2:20 And Abner looked to his rear, and said, Are you Asahel himself? And he said, I am.
2SA 2:21 And Abner said to him, Turn aside to the right or to the left, and constrain to yourself one of the servant-lads, and take to yourself his full armor! And Asahel did not want to turn aside from being behind him.
2SA 2:22 And Abner added yet, saying to Asahel, Leave from me, that I should not strike you unto the ground! For how shall I lift my face to Joab your brother?
2SA 2:23 And he was not willing to leave. And Abner struck him with the rear of the spear upon his flank. And the spear went completely through out behind him; and he falls there and dies underneath him. And it came to pass every one coming unto the place where Asahel fell there and died, even stood still.
2SA 2:24 And Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner, and the sun went down. And they entered unto the hill of Ammah, according to the face of Giah, the wilderness way of Gibeon.
2SA 2:25 And the sons of Benjamin gathered together following after Abner, and came to meet as one, and stood upon the head of one hill.
2SA 2:26 And Abner called Joab, and said, Shall the broadsword devour in victory, or do you not know that it will be bitter at the last? And for how long shall you in no way speak to the people to return from following after their brothers?
2SA 2:27 And Joab said, As the LORD lives, that if you had not spoken, that then from the morning the people ascended even each after his brother.
2SA 2:28 And Joab trumped the trumpet, and all the people left, and did not pursue any longer after Israel, and proceeded not any longer to wage war.
2SA 2:29 And Abner and his men went forth at the descent of the sun, and went all that night, and passed over the Jordan, and went the entire extent, and came unto Camp.
2SA 2:30 And Joab returned from following behind Abner. And he gathered together all the people, and they numbered the servants of David having fallen - nineteen men and Asahel.
2SA 2:31 And the servants of David struck of the sons of Benjamin, of the men of Abner - three hundred and sixty men.
2SA 2:32 And they lifted up Asahel, and entombed him in the burying-place of his father in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men went the entire night, and light shined through to them in Hebron.
2SA 3:1 And there was war for a long time between the house of Saul, and between the house of David. And the house of David went and strengthened, and the house of Saul went and weakened.
2SA 3:2 And were born to David in Hebron six sons, and his first-born was was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
2SA 3:3 and his second was Chileab of Abigail the Carmelitess; and the third was Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
2SA 3:4 and the fourth was Adonijah son of Haggith; and the fifth was Shephatiah by Abital;
2SA 3:5 and the sixth was Ithream of Eglah wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.
2SA 3:6 And it came to pass in the war being between the house of Saul, and between the house of David, that Abner was holding rule over the house of Saul.
2SA 3:7 And to Saul was a concubine, and the name to her was Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. And Ishbosheth son of Saul said to Abner, Why is it that you enter to the concubine of my father?
2SA 3:8 And Abner was enraged exceedingly on account of this word by Ishbosheth. And Abner said to him, Am I a dog's head that I executed today mercy with the house of Saul your father, and with his brothers, and with his acquaintances, and did not desert to the house of David, that you seek anxiously about me concerning injustice to a woman today?
2SA 3:9 Thus may God do to Abner, and thus may he add to him, that as the LORD swore by an oath to David, that so I should do the same to him in this day,
2SA 3:10 to remove the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to raise up the throne of David over Israel, and over Judah, from Dan until Beer-sheba.
2SA 3:11 And Ishbosheth was not able still to answer Abner's utterance, because of fearing him.
2SA 3:12 And Abner sent messengers to David in Hebron, saying, You ordain a covenant with me! And behold, My hand is with you to return to you all Israel.
2SA 3:13 And David said, Well, I shall ordain with you a covenant, except one word I ask from you, saying, You shall not see my face if you do not lead Michal daughter of Saul, in your coming to behold my face.
2SA 3:14 And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth son of Saul, saying, Give back to me my wife Michal, which I took for a hundred foreskins of Philistines.
2SA 3:15 And Ishbosheth sent, and took her from her husband, from Phaltiel son of Laish.
2SA 3:16 And her husband went with her, going and weeping after her unto Behurim. And Abner said to him, Go return! And he returned.
2SA 3:17 And the word of Abner came to the elders of Israel, saying, Yesterday and the third day before you sought David to reign over you.
2SA 3:18 And now act! For the LORD spoke concerning David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will deliver my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines, and from the hand of all his enemies.
2SA 3:19 And Abner spoke in the ears of Benjamin. And Abner went to speak into the ears of David in Hebron, all as much as it pleased in the eyes of Israel, and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.
2SA 3:20 And Abner came to David in Hebron, and with him twenty men. And David made a banquet to Abner and the men with him.
2SA 3:21 And Abner said to David, I will arise indeed and shall go, and shall gather together all Israel to my master the king. And I will ordain with you a covenant, and you shall reign over all whom your soul desires. And David sent away Abner, and he went in peace.
2SA 3:22 And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from the expedition, and they brought many spoils with themselves. And Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he went in peace.
2SA 3:23 And Joab and all the military with him came. And they reported to Joab, saying, Abner son of Ner comes to David, and he has sent him, and he went forth in peace.
2SA 3:24 And Joab entered to the king, and said to him, What is this you did? Behold, Abner came to you, and why have you sent him away, and he has gone forth in peace?
2SA 3:25 Or do you not know the evil of Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your entering and your exiting, and to know all together as much as you do?
2SA 3:26 And Joab went from David, and sent messengers after Abner, and they returned him from the well of Sirah - and David knew not.
2SA 3:27 And Abner returned to Hebron, and Joab turned him from the side of the gate to speak to him laying in wait. And he struck him there in the flank, and he died for the blood of Asahel his brother.
2SA 3:28 And David heard about these things, and said, I am innocent, and my kingdom, before the LORD, and unto the eon of the blood of Abner son of Ner.
2SA 3:29 Let it arrive upon the head of Joab, and upon all the house of his father! And may there not cease to be from out of the house of Joab one having gonorrhea, and leprous, and holding a stave, and falling by the broadsword, and lacking breads.
2SA 3:30 For Joab and Abishai his brother observed Abner, because he killed Asahel their brother in Gibeon in the battle.
2SA 3:31 And David said to Joab, and to all the people with him, Tear your clothes, and gird on sackcloths, and lament before Abner! And king David went behind the bier.
2SA 3:32 And they entombed Abner in Hebron. And the king lifted his voice, and wept over the tomb of Abner; and all the people wept.
2SA 3:33 And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Shall Abner die according to the death of Nabal?
2SA 3:34 Your hands were not tied, nor your feet in shackles; you did not lead as Nabal - you fell in the presence of a son of injustice. And all the people were brought together to weep for him.
2SA 3:35 And all the people came to cause David to eat breads at the wake still being day. And David swore by an oath, saying, Thus may God do to me, and thus may he add yet more, that until the sun should go down, in no way shall I taste bread nor any thing.
2SA 3:36 And all the people knew. And it was pleasing before them - all as much as the king did in the presence of all the people.
2SA 3:37 And all the people and all Israel knew in that day, that the putting to death of Abner son of Ner happened not by the king.
2SA 3:38 And the king said to his servants, Do you not know that a leader and a great one has fallen in this day in Israel?
2SA 3:39 And that I am as a relative today, and one being placed for king. But these men, the sons of Zeruiah are hard for me. The LORD should recompense to the one doing the wicked things according to his evil.
2SA 4:1 And Ishbosheth son of Saul heard that Abner has died in Hebron. And his hands were faint, and all the men of Israel were disturbed.
2SA 4:2 And there were two men being leaders of the confederation to Ishbosheth son of Saul - the name to the one was Baanah, and the name of the second, Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from out of the sons of Benjamin. (For also Beeroth was considered among the sons of Benjamin.
2SA 4:3 And the Beerothites ran away unto Gittaim, and were there sojourning until this day.)
2SA 4:4 And to Jonathan, son of Saul, there was a son stricken in the feet - a son five years old. And this one was in the way in the coming of the message of Saul and Jonathan his son from out of Jezreel. And hearing, his wet-nurse lifted him, and fled. And it happened in her hastening and withdrawing, he fell and became lame. And the name to him was Mephibosheth.
2SA 4:5 And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite went out - Rechab and Baana, and entered in the sweltering heat of the day into the house of Ishbosheth - and he was asleep in the bed in the midday.
2SA 4:6 And behold, the doorkeeper of the house was cleansing wheat, and he slumbered and slept. And Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped notice.
2SA 4:7 And they entered into the house, and Ishbosheth was sleeping upon his bed in his bedroom. And they struck him, and put him to death, and removed his head, and took his head, and went forth in the way according to the west the entire night.
2SA 4:8 And they brought the head of Ishbosheth to David in Hebron. And they said to the king, Behold, the head of Ishbosheth son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life; and the LORD gave to our master the king punishment of his enemies, as this day, of Saul your enemy, and of his seed.
2SA 4:9 And David responded to Rechab and to Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, As the LORD lives, who ransomed my soul from all affliction;
2SA 4:10 that the one reporting to me that Saul has died, and he was as one announcing good news before me, but I constrained him, and killed him in Ziklag, in which he must have thought to be giving me good news;
2SA 4:11 and now, wicked men killed a just man in his house upon his bed; and now, I will require for his blood from out of your hand, and I will utterly destroy you from the earth.
2SA 4:12 And David gave charge to his servants, and they killed them, and lopped off their hands and their feet, and hung them upon the fountain in Hebron. And the head of Ishbosheth they entombed in the tomb of Abner son of Ner in Hebron.
2SA 5:1 And all the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron. And they say to him, Behold, we are of your bones and of your flesh.
2SA 5:2 And before yesterday and the third day before, when Saul was king over us, you were the one leading out and bringing in Israel. And the LORD said to you, You tend my people Israel, and you will be for leader over my people Israel.
2SA 5:3 And all the elders of Israel come to the king in Hebron. And king David ordained with them a covenant in Hebron, in the presence of the LORD. And they anoint David for king over all Israel.
2SA 5:4 David was a son thirty years in his reigning, and forty years he reigned.
2SA 5:5 Seven years and six months he reigned in Hebron over Judah. And thirty three years he reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.
2SA 5:6 And the king went forth, and all his men unto Jerusalem, to the Jebusite dwelling the land. And it was said to David, You shall not enter here. For the blind and the lame opposed, saying, David shall not enter here.
2SA 5:7 And David overtook the citadel of Zion, this is the city of David.
2SA 5:8 And David said in that day, Every one striking a Jebusite, let him touch by the dagger both the lame and the blind, and the ones detesting the soul of David! On account of this they shall say, Blind and lame shall not enter into the house of the LORD.
2SA 5:9 And David stayed in the citadel, and this was called the city of David. And David built the city round about from the Akra, and his house.
2SA 5:10 And David went going, and being magnified, and the LORD almighty was with him.
2SA 5:11 And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and wood of cedars, and fabricators of woods, and fabricators of stones - and they built a house for David.
2SA 5:12 And David knew that the LORD prepared him for king over Israel, and that his kingdom was lifted up on account of his people Israel.
2SA 5:13 And David took again wives and concubines from Jerusalem, after his coming from Hebron. And still more sons and daughters were born to David.
2SA 5:14 And these are the names of the ones being born of them in Jerusalem - Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
2SA 5:15 and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
2SA 5:16 and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet, and Elishua.
2SA 5:17 And the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over Israel. And all the Philistines ascended to seek David. And David heard, and went down unto the citadel.
2SA 5:18 And the Philistines came and met in battle in the Valley of the Titans.
2SA 5:19 And David asked of the LORD, saying, Shall I ascend against the Philistines? and, Will you deliver them into my hands? And the LORD said to David, Ascend! for in delivering I will deliver the Philistines into your hands.
2SA 5:20 And David came from the upper breaches, and smote them there. And David said, The LORD cut through my enemies before me, as he cuts through waters. On account of this the name of that place is called Upper Breaches.
2SA 5:21 And they left behind there their gods, and David took them and the men with him.
2SA 5:22 And the Philistines proceeded yet again to ascend, and met in battle in the valley of the Titans.
2SA 5:23 And David asked through the LORD. And the LORD said, Do not ascend to meet them! Turn from them, and you shall be at hand for them neighboring the Place of Weeping!
2SA 5:24 And it will be, in your hearing the sound of the rumbling from out of the Grove of the Weeping, then you shall go down to them; for then the LORD shall go forth in front of you, to strike in the battle of the Philistines.
2SA 5:25 And David did thus as the LORD gave charge to him; and struck the Philistines from Gibeon unto Gezer.
2SA 6:1 And David gathered again every young man of Israel - thirty thousand.
2SA 6:2 And David rose up and went, and all the people with him, and some of the rulers of Judah, to lead from there the ark of God, upon which the name of the LORD of the forces is called upon - the one sitting upon the cherubim upon it.
2SA 6:3 And they set the ark of God upon a new wagon, and lifted it from out of the house of Abinadab on the hill. And Uzzah and his brothers, the sons of Abinadab, led the wagon with the ark.
2SA 6:4 And his brothers went in front of the ark.
2SA 6:5 And David and all the sons of Israel played before the LORD with instruments in accord, and with odes, and with lutes, and with stringed instruments, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with pipes.
2SA 6:6 And they come unto the threshing-floor of Nachon. And Uzzah stretched out his hand to the ark of God to hold it. And he held it, for the calf distracted it.
2SA 6:7 And the LORD was enraged in anger with Uzzah; and God struck him there for the rashness; and he died there by the ark of the LORD before God.
2SA 6:8 And David was depressed because of which the LORD cut severance with Uzzah. And he called that place, Severance of Uzzah until this day.
2SA 6:9 And David feared the LORD in that day, saying, How shall the ark of God enter to me?
2SA 6:10 And David did not want to turn aside to himself the ark of the covenant of the LORD into the city of David. And David turned off with it into the house of Obed Edom the Gittite.
2SA 6:11 And the ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed Edom the Gittite three months. And the LORD blessed the entire house of Obed Edom and all the things of his.
2SA 6:12 And it was reported to king David, saying, The LORD blessed the house of Obed Edom, and all of his, because of the ark of God. And David went and led the ark of the LORD from out of the house of Obed Edom into the city of David with gladness.
2SA 6:13 And there were with him the ones lifting the ark of the LORD - seven companies of dancers, and a calf and lambs for sacrifice.
2SA 6:14 And David played music with instruments in accord in the presence of the LORD. And David was clothed in a special robe.
2SA 6:15 And David and all the house of Israel led the ark of the LORD with a cry, and with the sound of a trumpet.
2SA 6:16 And it happened of the ark coming unto the city of David, that Michal daughter of Saul looked through the window, and saw king David dancing and playing music before the LORD. And she treated him with contempt in her heart.
2SA 6:17 And they carried in the ark of the LORD, and put it aside in its place, in the middle of the tent which David pitched for it. And David offered whole burnt offerings before the LORD, and peace offerings.
2SA 6:18 And David completed offering the whole burnt offerings, and the peace offerings. And he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of the forces.
2SA 6:19 And he portioned to all the people among all the force of Israel, from man unto woman, to each a biscuit of bread, and broiled meat, and a pancake from the frying pan. And all the people went forth each to his house.
2SA 6:20 And David returned to bless his house. And Michal the daughter of Saul came forth to meet David, and said, How was the king of Israel glorified today, who was uncovered today in the eyes of the girls of his servants, as one uncovers by uncovering of the ones dancing.
2SA 6:21 And David said to Michal, In the presence of the LORD I will dance, who chose me over your father, and over all his house, to place me in the lead over his people Israel - and I shall play and dance in the presence of the LORD.
2SA 6:22 And I will be uncovered again thus, and I will be useless in your eyes, and with the girls of whom you said of me not being extolled.
2SA 6:23 And Michal daughter of Saul did not have a child unto the day of her dying.
2SA 7:1 And it came to pass when the king sat in his house, and the LORD rested him round about from all of his enemies;
2SA 7:2 that the king said to Nathan the prophet, Behold indeed, I dwell in a house of cedar, and the ark of God sits in the midst of the tent.
2SA 7:3 And Nathan said to the king, All as much as should be in your heart, proceed and do! For the LORD is with you.
2SA 7:4 And it came to pass in that night, and the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
2SA 7:5 Go and speak to my servant David! Thus says the LORD, You shall not build for me a house for me to dwell in.
2SA 7:6 For I have not dwelt in a house from which day I led the sons of Israel out of Egypt, until this day, for I was walking about in a lodging, in a tent.
2SA 7:7 In all the places which all Israel went by, have I in speaking spoke to one tribe of Israel, in which I gave charge to tend my people Israel, saying, Why do you not build for me a house of cedar?
2SA 7:8 And now thus you shall say to my servant David, Thus says the LORD almighty, I took you from out of the haven of the sheep, for you to be for leader over my people Israel.
2SA 7:9 And I was with you in all wheresoever you went, and I utterly destroyed all your enemies from your face, and I made to you a great name, according to the name of the great ones upon the earth.
2SA 7:10 And I will establish a place to my people Israel, and I will plant it, and they shall encamp by themselves, and shall not be anxious any longer. And the son of iniquity shall not proceed to humble them as from the beginning,
2SA 7:11 even from the days which I ordered judges over my people Israel, and will rest you from all your enemies. And the LORD will report to you that he shall build a house to you.
2SA 7:12 And it will be whenever your days should have been fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, that I shall raise up your seed after you, who will be from out of your belly, and I shall prepare his kingdom.
2SA 7:13 He shall build to me a house to my name, and I will erect his throne unto into the eon.
2SA 7:14 I will be to him for father, and he will be to me for son. And if his injustice should come, then I shall reprove him by a rod of men, and by blows of the sons of men.
2SA 7:15 But my mercy I will not remove from him, as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from your face.
2SA 7:16 And your house shall be trustworthy, and your kingdom unto the eon before me. And your throne will be erected into the eon.
2SA 7:17 According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so spoke Nathan to David.
2SA 7:18 And king David entered, and sat before the LORD, and said, Who am I, O my Lord, O LORD? And what is my house, that you love me for these things?
2SA 7:19 And it was reduced small before you, O my Lord, O LORD; and you spoke about the house of your servant for a far time. And is this the law of man, O my Lord, O LORD?
2SA 7:20 And what shall David add yet to speak to you? And now, you know your servant, O my Lord, O LORD.
2SA 7:21 Because of your word, and because of your servant, you have acted, and according to your heart, you have done all this greatness, to make known to your servant;
2SA 7:22 so as to magnify you, O my Lord, O LORD. For there is not one as you, and there is not a God besides you, among all in whom we heard with our ears.
2SA 7:23 And what other nation is as your people Israel in the earth, s God guided it to ransom to himself a people, to establish your name for the executing greatness and grandeur, for you to cast out from in front of your people, whom you ransomed to yourself from out of Egypt, even nations and tents?
2SA 7:24 And you prepared to yourself your people Israel to be for a people unto the eon. And you, O LORD, became to them for God.
2SA 7:25 And now, O my Lord, O LORD, the word which you spoke for your servant, and for his house, confirm it as trustworthy unto the eon, and as you spoke, do!
2SA 7:26 And now may your name be magnified until the eon, saying,
2SA 7:27 The LORD almighty - God over Israel. You uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, I will build to you a house. On account of this your servant found his own heart to pray to you this prayer.
2SA 7:28 And now, O my Lord, O LORD, you are God, and your words will be true, and you spoke these good things concerning your servant.
2SA 7:29 And now begin and bless the house of your servant, to be into the eon before you! For you, O my Lord, O LORD, spoke. And from your blessing the house of your servant shall be blessed into the eon.
