2SA 9:1 And David said, Is there anyone still left from the house of Saul, that I should perform with him an act of mercy because of Jonathan?
2SA 9:2 And from the house of Saul was a servant, and the name to him was Ziba. And they called him to David. And the king said to him, You are Ziba? And he said, Your servant.
2SA 9:3 And the king said, Is there left any man from out of the house of Saul, that I should perform with him an act of mercy of God? And Ziba said to the king, There still is a son to Jonathan being stricken of the feet.
2SA 9:4 And the king said to him, Where is this one? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, in the house of Machir, son of Ammiel, of Lo-debar.
2SA 9:5 And king David sent, and took him from out of the house of Machir, son of Ammiel, of Lo-debar.
2SA 9:6 And Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul comes to king David, and fell upon his face, and did obeisance to him. And David said to him, Mephibosheth! And he said, Behold, your servant.
2SA 9:7 And David said to him, Do not fear, for by dealing with you I shall execute with you an act of mercy because of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the fields of Saul, the father of your father; and you shall eat bread at my table always.
2SA 9:8 And he did obeisance to him, and said, Who am I your servant, that you looked upon the dying dog likened to me?
2SA 9:9 And the king called Ziba, the servant of Saul, and said to him, All as much as is to Saul, and his entire house, I have given to the son of your master.
2SA 9:10 And you shall work the land for him, and your sons, and your servants. And you shall carry in breads to the son of your master, and he shall eat. And Mephibosheth son of your master shall eat bread always at my table. And to Ziba were fifteen sons and twenty servants.
2SA 9:11 And Ziba said to the king, According to all as much as my master the king gives charge to his servant, so shall your servant do. And Mephibosheth ate at the table of David as one of the sons of the king.
2SA 9:12 And to Mephibosheth there was a small son, and the name to him was Micha. And all the household of the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
2SA 9:13 And Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem - for at the table of the king he ate always. And he was lame of both of his feet.
2SA 10:1 And it came to pass after these things, that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned instead of him.
2SA 10:2 And David said, I will perform an act of kindness with Hanun son of Nahash, in which manner his father performed an act of kindness with me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father. And the servants of David came into the land of the sons of Ammon.
2SA 10:3 And the rulers of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their master, Is it for David to glorify your father before you that he sent to you comforters? But is it not however that they should search the city, and spy it - for to survey it David sent his servants to you?
2SA 10:4 And Hanun took the servants of David, and shaved their beards, and cut off their uniforms in half unto their hips, and sent them out.
2SA 10:5 And it was reported to David concerning the men. And he sent to meet them, for the men were dishonored exceedingly. And the king said, Stay in Jericho until your beards rise, and you shall return.
2SA 10:6 And the sons of Ammon saw that the people of David were disgraced. And the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Syrian of Beth-rehob, and the Syrian of Zoba - twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah - a thousand men, and the one of Tob - twelve thousand men.
2SA 10:7 And David heard, and sent Joab, and all the force of the mighty ones.
2SA 10:8 And the sons of Ammon came forth, and deployed for war by the door of the gate. And the Syrian Zoba, and Rehob, and Ishtob, and Maacah were by themselves in the field.
2SA 10:9 And Joab beheld that it came to pass that the war was facing him from the face right opposite, and from the rear, that he chose from out of all the young men of Israel, and they deployed right opposite Syria.
2SA 10:10 And the rest of the people he put into the hand of Abishai his brother, and they deployed right opposite the sons of Ammon.
2SA 10:11 And he said, If Syria should strengthen over me, then you shall be to me for deliverance. And if the sons of Ammon should be strengthened over you, then I will come to deliver you.
2SA 10:12 Be manly! for we should be strengthened for our people, and for the cities of our God. And the LORD will do good in his eyes.
2SA 10:13 And Joab approached, and his people with him, for war against Syria. And they fled from his face.
2SA 10:14 And the sons of Ammon beheld that Syria has fled, and they fled from the face of Abishai, and entered into the city. And Joab returned from the sons of Ammon, and came unto Jerusalem.
2SA 10:15 And Syria beheld that it failed in front of Israel; and they gathered together at the same place.
2SA 10:16 And Hadarezer sent, and gathered together the Syrian from the other side of the river, and they came unto Helam. And Shobach the commander-in-chief of Hadarezer was in front of them.
2SA 10:17 And it was reported to David, and he gathered together all Israel, and passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. And Syria deployed before David, and waged war with him.
2SA 10:18 And Syria fled from the face of Israel; and David killed of the one from Syria - seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen. And Shobach his commander-in-chief he struck, and he died there.
2SA 10:19 And all the kings the servants of Hadarezer beheld that they failed in front of Israel. And they deserted after Israel, and served to them. And Syria feared to yet again deliver the sons of Ammon.
2SA 11:1 And it came to pass in the turning of the year into the time of the departure of the kings for battle, that David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they utterly destroyed the sons of Ammon, and besieged against Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
2SA 11:2 And it came to pass towards evening, and David rose up from his bed, and walked upon the roof of the house of the king. And he beheld from the roof a woman bathing; and the woman was good to the appearance - exceedingly.
2SA 11:3 And David sent and sought the woman. And they said, Is not this Bath-sheba, daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?
2SA 11:4 And David sent messengers, and took her. And he entered to her, and went to bed with her; and she was being set apart from her uncleanness. And she returned to her house.
2SA 11:5 And the woman conceived, and sent and reported to David, and said, I am one conceiving.
2SA 11:6 And David sent to Joab, saying, Send to me Uriah the Hittite! And Joab sent Uriah to David.
2SA 11:7 And Uriah came, and entered to him. And David asked for the peace of Joab, and for the peace of the people, and for the peace of the war.
2SA 11:8 And David said to Uriah, Go down to your house, even to wash your feet! And Uriah went forth from the house of the king, and there went forth after him a tribute from the king.
2SA 11:9 And Uriah went to bed by the door of the house of the king with all the servants of his master, and did not go down to his house.
2SA 11:10 And they reported to David, saying that, Uriah did not go down to his house. And David said to Uriah, Are you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?
2SA 11:11 And Uriah said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, dwell in tents; and my master Joab, and the man-servants of my master camp upon the face of the field; and shall I enter into my house to eat and to drink and to go to bed with my wife? By your life, and by the life of your soul, in no way shall I do this thing.
2SA 11:12 And David said to Uriah, Stay here also today, and tomorrow I will send you! And Uriah stayed in Jerusalem on that day, and the next day.
2SA 11:13 And David called him, and he ate before him, and drank - and he intoxicated him. And he went forth at evening to go to bed upon his bed with the servants of his master, but he did not go down unto his house.
2SA 11:14 And it became morning, and David wrote a scroll to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
2SA 11:15 And he wrote in the scroll, saying, Bring Uriah right opposite the battle of the fortified part, and turn away from behind him, so that he shall be struck and shall die!
2SA 11:16 And it came to pass in Joab's guarding at the city, that he put Uriah into the place where he knew that men of power were there.
2SA 11:17 And the men of the city came forth, and waged war against Joab. And there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and even Uriah the Hittite died also.
2SA 11:18 And Joab sent and reported to David all the matters of the battle.
2SA 11:19 And Joab gave charge to the messenger, saying, In your completing all the matters of the battle speaking to the king,
2SA 11:20 that it shall be if the rage of the king ascends, and he should say to you, Why is it that you approached to the city to wage war? Did you not know that they would shoot from on top the wall?
2SA 11:21 Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman toss a piece of millstone upon him from above the wall, and he died in Thebez? Why did you lead forward to the wall? And you shall say, And also your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.
2SA 11:22 And the messenger of Joab came to the king in Jerusalem, and reported to David all as much as Joab spoke.
2SA 11:23 And the messenger said to David that, The men strengthened against us, and came forth against us into the field, and we came unto them unto the door of the gate.
2SA 11:24 And the ones shooting shot unto your servants from the wall, and there died some from the servants of the king, and even your subject Uriah the Hittite has died.
2SA 11:25 And David said to the messenger, Thus you shall say to Joab, Do not let this matter be severe in your eyes, for perhaps indeed it is thus one way, and perhaps thus another way that the broadsword devours; strengthen your battle against the city, and raze it, and strengthen against it.
2SA 11:26 And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband has died, and she lamented over her husband.
2SA 11:27 And the time of mourning went by, and David sent and brought her into his house, and she became to him for a wife, and bore to him a son. And the matter which David did appeared wicked in the eyes of the LORD.
2SA 12:1 And the LORD sent Nathan the prophet to David. And he entered to him, and said to him, There were two men in one city - one rich and one needy.
2SA 12:2 And there was to the rich man flocks and herds - many, exceedingly.
2SA 12:3 And to the needy there was not anything, but only one small ewe-lamb which he acquired, and protected, and nourished it. And it matured with him, and with his sons at the same time. It ate from his bread, and drank from his cup, and slept in his bosom, and it was to him as a daughter.
2SA 12:4 And a traveller came to the rich man. And he spared to take from his flock, and from his herd, to prepare for the stranger coming to him. And he took the ewe-lamb of the needy man, and prepared it for the man coming to him.
2SA 12:5 And David was enraged in anger exceedingly against the man. And he said to Nathan, As the LORD lives, that man doing this is a son of death.
2SA 12:6 And for the ewe-lamb he shall pay four-fold, because he did this thing, and for which he did not spare.
2SA 12:7 And Nathan said to David, You are the man doing this thing. Thus says the LORD God of Israel, I anointed you for king over Israel, and I rescued you from out of the hand of Saul;
2SA 12:8 and I gave to you the house of your master, and the wives of your master into your bosom, and gave to you the house of Israel and Judah; and if it is little to you, I would have added to you as those.
2SA 12:9 Why is it that you treated as worthless the word of the LORD, to do the wicked thing in his eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck by the broadsword, and his wife you took to yourself for wife, and him you killed by the broadsword of the sons of Ammon.
2SA 12:10 And now, the broadsword shall not depart from your house unto the eon. Because of this - that you treated me with contempt, and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be to you for a wife.
2SA 12:11 Thus says the LORD, Behold, I shall awaken evils against you from out of your house, and I shall take your wives before your eyes, and I will give them to your neighbor, and he shall go to bed with your wives before this sun.
2SA 12:12 For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before this sun.
2SA 12:13 And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said to David, And the LORD cast aside your sin, and you shall not die.
2SA 12:14 Except that, in provoking to anger, you provoked to anger the enemies of the LORD in this thing, and indeed your son born to you - to death he will die.
2SA 12:15 And Nathan went forth to his house. And the LORD enfeebled the child which the wife of Uriah bore to David, and he was ill.
2SA 12:16 And David sought God for the boy. And David fasted with fasting, and entered and lodged upon the ground.
2SA 12:17 And the elders of his house rose up to him, to raise him from the ground; and he wanted not, and would not eat bread with them.
2SA 12:18 And it came to pass in the seventh day, and the boy died. And the servants of David feared to announce to him that, The boy has died. For they said, Behold, in the time the boy was still living, we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice. And how should we say to him that, The boy has died? for he shall do bad things.
2SA 12:19 And David perceived that his servants were whispering, and David comprehended that the boy has died. And David said to his servants, Has the boy died? And they said, He has died.
2SA 12:20 And David rose up from the ground, and bathed, and anointed himself, and changed his clothes. And he entered into the house of God, and did obeisance to him. And he entered unto his house, and asked for bread to eat. And they placed near to him bread, and he ate.
2SA 12:21 And his servants said to him, What is this thing which you do because of the boy? While still living you fasted, and wept, and were sleepless; and when the boy died, you rose up and ate bread and drank?
2SA 12:22 And David said, In the time the boy was still living, I fasted and wept. For I said, Who knows if the LORD will show mercy on me, and the boy shall live?
2SA 12:23 And now he has died, why this that I fast? I shall not be able to return him, yet I will go to him, but he shall not return to me.
2SA 12:24 And David comforted his wife Bath-sheba. And he entered to her, and went to bed with her. And she conceived, and gave birth to a son, and he called his name Solomon. And the LORD loved him.
2SA 12:25 And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, by the word of the LORD.
2SA 12:26 And Joab waged war with Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and overtook the city of the kingdom.
2SA 12:27 And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I waged war against Rabbah, and overtook the city of waters.
2SA 12:28 And now, gather together the rest of the people, and camp upon the city, and be the first to take it; that I should not be the first to take the city, and my name should be called upon it!
2SA 12:29 And David gathered together all the people, and went to Rabbah, and waged war against it, and overtook it.
2SA 12:30 And he took the crown of their king from his head, and its weight was a talent of gold, and of precious stone. And it was upon the head of David. And he brought forth exceedingly much spoils of the city.
2SA 12:31 And the people in it he led out and put to the saw, and to the threshing-machines of iron, and adz of iron, and led them through the brick-kiln. And thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David returned and all the people to Jerusalem.
2SA 13:1 And it happened after these things that there was to Absalom, son of David, a sister good to the sight - exceedingly. And her name was Tamar; and Amnon son of David loved her.
2SA 13:2 And Amnon was afflicted so as to be ill over Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin, and it was an enormous thing in the eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.
2SA 13:3 And there was a companion to Amnon, and his name was Jonadab, son of Shimeah the brother of David. And Jonadab was exceedingly practical.
2SA 13:4 And he said to him, What is it to you that thus you are weak morning by morning, O son of the king? Will you not report it to me? And Amnon said to him, Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom, I love.
2SA 13:5 And Jonadab said to him, Go to bed in your bed, and be as infirm! And your father will enter to see you. And you shall say to him, Let indeed Tamar my sister come and feed me! And let her make food before my eyes, so that I should see, and should eat from her hand!
2SA 13:6 And Amnon went to bed, and became as ill. And the king entered to see him. And Amnon said to the king, Let indeed Tamar my sister come to me! And let her bake two biscuits before my eyes, and I will eat from her hand!
2SA 13:7 And David sent for Tamar to the house, saying, Go indeed to the house of Amnon your brother, and make food for him!
2SA 13:8 And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother. And with him being in bed, that she took the dough and mixed it, and made biscuits before his eyes, and baked the biscuits.
2SA 13:9 And she took the frying pan, and emptied it before him; and he did not want to eat. And Amnon said, Lead out every man from about me! And they led out every man about him.
2SA 13:10 And Amnon said to Tamar, Carry in to me the food to the bedroom, and I shall eat from out of your hand! And Tamar took the biscuits which she made, and carried them to Amnon her brother, into the bedroom.
2SA 13:11 And she brought to him to eat, and he took hold of her, and said to her, Come go to bed with me, my sister!
2SA 13:12 And she said to him, No, O my brother, you should not abase me, for it shall not be done so in Israel - you should not do this folly.
2SA 13:13 And I, where shall I carry away my scorn? And you will be as one of the foolish in Israel. And now, speak indeed to the king! For in no way will he restrain me from you.
2SA 13:14 And Amnon did not want to hear her voice. And he powered over her, and abased her, and went to bed with her.
2SA 13:15 And Amnon detested her with an exceedingly great hatred; for so great was the hatred which he detested her, that it was above the love which he loved her. And Amnon said to her, Rise up and go!
2SA 13:16 And Tamar said to him that, Great is the last evil over the first which you do with me, to send me away. And Amnon wanted not to hearken to her voice.
2SA 13:17 And he called his servant set over his house, and said to him, Send indeed this one from me outside, and lock the door after her!
2SA 13:18 And upon her was an inner garment with long sleeves, for thus the daughters of the king dressed - the virgins, the ones with their outer garments. And his minister led her outside, and locked the door after her.
2SA 13:19 And Tamar took ashes, and put them upon her head. And the inner garment with long sleeves upon her she tore; and she put her hands upon her head, and went going and crying out.
2SA 13:20 And Absalom her brother said to her, Has Amnon your brother been with you? and now my sister be silent, for he is your brother! Do not put it to your heart to say anything! And Tamar sat expiring in the house of Absalom her brother.
2SA 13:21 And king David heard all these words, and was enraged exceedingly.
2SA 13:22 And Absalom did not speak with Amnon from bad or good; for Absalom detested Amnon, for which he abased Tamar his sister.
2SA 13:23 And it came to pass after two whole years of days, that they were shearing for Absalom in Baal-hazor by Ephraim. And Absalom called all the sons of the king.
2SA 13:24 And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold indeed, your servant shears. Let indeed the king go, and his servants with your servant.
2SA 13:25 And the king said to Absalom, No indeed, O my son, in no way should we all go ourselves, and in no way should we be burdensome upon you. And Absalom constrained him, and the king did not want to go, but he blessed him.
2SA 13:26 And Absalom said, And if not, let Amnon my brother go indeed with us! And the king said to him, Why should he go with you?
2SA 13:27 And Absalom constrained him, and he sent with him Amnon and all the sons of the king.
2SA 13:28 And Absalom gave charge to his servants, saying, Behold, when ever the heart of Amnon feels good with the wine, and I should say to you, Strike Amnon, and put him to death! you should not fear. For is it not I giving charge to you? Be manly, and become as sons of power!
2SA 13:29 And the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as he gave charge to them. And all the sons of the king rose up, and each mounted upon his mule, and fled.
2SA 13:30 And it came to pass of their being in the way, that the report came to David, saying, Absalom struck all the sons of the king, and did not leave behind of them not even one.
2SA 13:31 And the king rose up, and tore his clothes, and laid upon the ground. And all his servants standing around him tore their clothes.
2SA 13:32 And Jonadab son of Shimeah brother of David answered and said, Let not my master the king say that all the boys of the sons of the king he put to death! But only Amnon alone died, for by the mouth of Absalom it was situated to be from the day of which he abased Tamar his sister.
2SA 13:33 And now, let not my master the king put the matter upon his heart! saying that, All the sons of the king died - for only Amnon alone died.
2SA 13:34 And Absalom ran away. And the servant watchman lifted his eyes, and looked, and behold, there were many people going in the way behind him from out of the side of the mountain.
2SA 13:35 And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the sons of the king are at hand; according to the word of your servant, thus it has happened.
2SA 13:36 And it came to pass, when he completed speaking, that behold, the sons of the king came, and lifted up their voice and wept. And indeed the king and all his servants wept an exceedingly great weeping.
2SA 13:37 And Absalom ran away, and went to Talmai, son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And the king mourned over his son all the days.
2SA 13:38 And Absalom fled, and went forth unto Geshur, and was there three years.
2SA 13:39 And the spirit of king David abated to go forth unto Absalom - for he was comforted concerning Amnon, that he died.
2SA 14:1 And Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the heart of the king was towards Absalom.
2SA 14:2 And Joab sent to Tekoah, and took from there a wise woman, and said to her, You mourn indeed, and put on mournful garments, and do not anoint yourself with oil, and be as a woman mourning for many days for one having died!
2SA 14:3 And you shall come to the king, and you shall speak to him according to this thing. And Joab put the words into her mouth.
2SA 14:4 And the Tekoahite woman entered to the king, and fell upon her face to the ground, and did obeisance to him, and said, Deliver, O king, deliver!
2SA 14:5 And the king said to her, What to you is it? And she said, By all means I am a widow woman, and my husband died.
2SA 14:6 And indeed to your maidservant are two sons, and they both quarreled in the field, and there was not one for rescuing between them, and the one hit his one brother, and killed him.
2SA 14:7 And behold, the entire family rose up against your maidservant, and said, Give over the one hitting his brother, and we shall kill him, on account of the life of his brother whom he killed - and we shall take away the heir. And so they shall extinguish my spark of coal being left behind to me, so as to not establish to my husband a vestige and name upon the face of the earth.
2SA 14:8 And the king said to the woman, Go to your house being in health, and I will take charge concerning you!
2SA 14:9 And the Tekoahite woman said to the king, O my master, O king, upon me be the iniquity, and upon the house of my father; and the king and his throne be innocent!
2SA 14:10 And the king said, The one speaking to you a word, lead him to me, and in no way shall anyone proceed yet to touch you!
2SA 14:11 And the woman said, Let now the king remember indeed the LORD your God, in not multiplying a relative for blood utterly destroying, that in no way they should take away my son! And he said, As the LORD lives, there shall not fall of the hair of your son upon the ground.
2SA 14:12 And the woman said, Let your maidservant speak indeed to my master the king a thing! And he said, Speak!
2SA 14:13 And the woman said, Why have you imputed thus upon the people of God? Yes, by the king speaking this word it is as a trespass, for the king to not return the one being thrust away by him.
2SA 14:14 For to death we shall die, and are as the water being discharged upon the earth, not being gathered together; that God shall not take the life; yet he himself devises a device to not thrust away from him the one being thrusted away.
2SA 14:15 And now for which I came to speak to my master the king this word, for the people see me; and your maidservant will say, Let your maidservant speak indeed to my master the king; if by any means the king shall do the matter of his maidservant.
2SA 14:16 For the king shall hear to rescue his maidservant from out of the hand of the man seeking to take me away, and my son, from the inheritance of God.
2SA 14:17 And said your maidservant, Let be indeed the word of my master the king for an accepted sacrifice. For as a messenger of God, thus is my master the king, to hear the good and the bad - and the LORD your God will be with you.
2SA 14:18 And the king answered and said to the woman, You should not indeed hide from me the matter which ever I shall ask you. And the woman said, Let indeed my master the king speak!
2SA 14:19 And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab in all this with you? And the woman answered and said to the king, As your soul lives, O my master, O king, since there is no turning to the right or to the left of all which my master the king spoke; for your servant Joab himself gave charge to me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your maidservant.
2SA 14:20 So as for the face of this matter to come about, thus Joab your servant did this thing. And my master the king is wise as the wisdom of a messenger of God, to know all the things in the land.
2SA 14:21 And the king said to Joab, Behold indeed, I do to you according to this your word. Go return the young man Absalom!
2SA 14:22 And Joab fell upon his face upon the ground, and did obeisance, and blessed the king. And Joab said, Today your servant knows that he found favor in your eyes, O my master, O king, for my master the king did the matter for his servant.
2SA 14:23 And Joab rose up and went into Geshur, and led Absalom into Jerusalem.
2SA 14:24 And the king said, Let him return to his house, but let him not see my face! And Absalom returned to his house, but the face of the king he did not see.
2SA 14:25 And there was not a man as Absalom in all Israel as exceedingly praiseworthy. From the sole of his foot and unto the top of his head there was not a blemish on him.
2SA 14:26 And in his shearing of his head, (and it took place at the end of days unto days that he sheared it, for it became burdensome upon him, and thus was shearing it,) he set aside the hair of his head - two hundred shekels of the royal scale-weight.
2SA 14:27 And there was born to Absalom three sons and one daughter, and her name was Tamar - she was an exceedingly goodly woman.
2SA 14:28 And Absalom stayed in Jerusalem two years of days, and the face of the king he did not see.
2SA 14:29 And Absalom sent for Joab to send him to the king; and he did not want to come to him. And he sent again the second time to him, and he did not want to come.
2SA 14:30 And Absalom said to his servants, You know the portion in the field of Joab being next to mine, and to him is barley there; go and burn it by fire! And the servants of Absalom burned by fire the portion of the field of Joab.
2SA 14:31 And Joab rose up, and came to Absalom, to the house, and said to him, Why did your servants set on fire my field with fire?
2SA 14:32 And Absalom said to Joab, Behold, I sent to you, saying, Come here! And I will send you to the king, saying, Why did I come from out of Geshur? it was good for me to be there. And now, I shall see indeed the face of the king; and if there is iniquity in me then I shall be killed.
2SA 14:33 And Joab went to the king, and reported to him. And he called Absalom, and he entered to the king, and did obeisance to him, and fell upon his face upon the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
2SA 15:1 And it came to pass after these things, that Absalom prepared to himself chariots, and horsemen, and fifty men to run along in front of him.
2SA 15:2 And Absalom rose early, and stood at the way of the gate. And it came to pass, every man which had a case, and came to the king for a judgment, that Absalom called him, and said to him, From out of of what city are you? And he said, Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.
2SA 15:3 And Absalom said to him, Behold, your words are good and well-tempered; but there is not one hearing you from the king.
2SA 15:4 And Absalom said, Why shall he not place me for judge in the land, and every man shall come to me to whom ever might be a dispute, and a case, and I will do justice for him.
2SA 15:5 And it came to pass, when the man approached to do obeisance to him, that he stretched out his hand, and took hold of him, and kissed him.
2SA 15:6 And Absalom did according to this thing to all Israel, to the ones coming for a judgment to the king. And Absalom adopted the heart of the men of Israel.
2SA 15:7 And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said to his father, I will go indeed and pay my vows, which I vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.
2SA 15:8 For your servant vowed a vow in my living in Geshur in Syria, saying, If in returning the LORD shall return me to Jerusalem, then I will serve to the LORD.
2SA 15:9 And the king said to him, Proceed in peace! And rising up, he went unto Hebron.
2SA 15:10 And Absalom sent spies into all the tribes of Israel, saying, In your hearing the sound of the trumpet, that you shall say, Absalom reigns in Hebron.
2SA 15:11 And two hundred chosen men went with Absalom from out of Jerusalem; and they went in simplicity, and they did not know, not one thing.
2SA 15:12 And Absalom sent and called Ahithophel the Gilonite, counselor to David, from out of his city Giloh, during his sacrificing the sacrifices. And there was a strong confederation; and the people went and multiplied with Absalom.
2SA 15:13 And one came reporting to David, saying, The heart of the men of Israel is committed after Absalom.
2SA 15:14 And David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, Rise up, and we should flee, for there is not a deliverance for us from the face of Absalom! Hasten to go, that he should not hasten and overtake us, and thrust evil upon us, and should strike the city by the mouth of the broadsword!
2SA 15:15 And the servants of the king said to the king, According to all as much as seems good to our master the king, behold, we are your servants.
2SA 15:16 And the king went forth, and all his house on their feet. And the king left ten women of his concubines to guard the house.
2SA 15:17 And the king went forth, and all his people by foot, and set up in a house far away.
2SA 15:18 And all his servants passed by his hand; and every Cherethite, and every Pelethite, and all the Gittites - six hundred men having come from out of Gath, by foot, were passing in front of the king.
2SA 15:19 And the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why should you go even yourself with us? Return and live with the king! For you are an alien yourself, and because you are displaced from out of your place.
2SA 15:20 Since you came yesterday, then today shall I move you to go with us? and I shall go where ever I shall go. Go, and return your brothers with you; and the LORD shall execute with you an act of kindness and truth!
2SA 15:21 And Ittai answered the king, and said, As the LORD lives, and as my master the king lives, that unto the place where ever my master the king might be, and if unto death, or if unto life, that there your servant will be.
2SA 15:22 And David said to Ittai, Go, and pass over with me! And Ittai the Gittite went, and all the men with him, and all his servants.
2SA 15:23 And all the land wept with a great voice, and all the people passed through the rushing stream of the Kidron. And the king passed over the rushing stream Kidron, and all the people came unto the face of the way of the wilderness.
2SA 15:24 And behold, also indeed Zadok, and all the Levites were with him lifting the ark of the covenant of God. And they stationed the ark of God; and Abiathar ascended until all the people ceased going out of the city.
2SA 15:25 And the king said to Zadok, Return the ark of God unto the city! If I should find favor in the eyes of the LORD, and he returns me, then he shall show it to me, and its beauty.
2SA 15:26 And if he should say thus, I have not a want in you; behold, here am I, I let him do to me the pleasing thing before him.
2SA 15:27 And the king said to Zadok the priest, Behold, you return to the city in peace, and Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, the two sons of yours with you!
2SA 15:28 Behold, I wait for you in the wilderness of the desert until the coming of a word by you to report to me.
2SA 15:29 And Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem, and it stayed there.
2SA 15:30 And David ascended upon the ascent of the olive groves, ascending and weeping, and his head being covered over, and he went barefoot. And all the people with him - each man covered his head, and ascended - ascending and weeping.
2SA 15:31 And it was announced to David, saying, And Ahithophel is among the ones confederating with Absalom. And David said, O LORD my God, efface indeed the counsel of Ahithophel!
2SA 15:32 And David was coming unto Ros, where he did obeisance there to God. And behold, Hushai the chief friend of David was come for meeting him, tearing his inner garment, with earth upon his head.
2SA 15:33 And David said to him, If you should go through with me, then you will be unto me a load.
2SA 15:34 If you should return into the city, then you shall say to Absalom, I am your servant, O king; allow me to live! for I was a servant of your father then and just now, and now I am your servant. And by saying this efface to me the counsel of Ahithophel!
2SA 15:35 And behold, there are with you Zadok and Abiathar the priests. And it will be every word which ever you should hear from out of the house of the king, that you shall report it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
2SA 15:36 Behold, their two sons are with them there, Ahimaaz son of Zadok, and Jonathan son of Abiathar; and you shall send by their hand to me every word which ever you should hear.
2SA 15:37 And Hushai the friend of David entered into the city, and Absalom at present entered into Jerusalem.
2SA 16:1 And David went through a little way from Ros, and behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth arrived for meeting him, and a pair of donkeys being saddled, and upon them two hundred breads, and an ephah of dried grape clusters, and a hundred dried fruit clusters, and a skin flask of wine.
2SA 16:2 And the king said to Ziba, What are these to you? And Ziba said, The donkeys for the household of the king to mount, and the breads, and the dried fruit clusters, and dried grapes for food to the servants; and the wine to drink to the one faint in the wilderness.
2SA 16:3 And the king said, Where is the son of your master? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he sits in Jerusalem, for he said, Today the house of Israel shall return to me the kingdom of my father.
2SA 16:4 And the king said to Ziba, Behold, I give to you all as much as is Mephibosheth's. And Ziba said, I do obeisance, may I find favor in your eyes, O my master, O king.
2SA 16:5 And king David came until Bahurim, and behold, from there a man came forth from the family of the house of Saul, and the name to him was Shimei, son of Gera - he came forth coming and cursing,
2SA 16:6 and throwing stones at David, and at all the servants of king David, and all the people, and all the mighty ones of the right and of the left of the king.
2SA 16:7 And thus Shimei said in his cursing, Go forth, go forth, O man of the blood sheddings, and O man the lawbreaker!
2SA 16:8 The LORD returned upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, because you reigned instead of him; and the LORD gave the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. And behold, you are taken in your own evil, for you are a man of blood.
2SA 16:9 And Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, Why does this dying dog curse my master the king? Let me pass indeed, and I shall remove his head!
2SA 16:10 And the king said to Abishai, What is it to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah? Even allow him, and thus let him curse! For the LORD said to him to curse David. And who shall say to him, Why did you do thus?
2SA 16:11 And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, the one coming forth from out of my belly, seeks my life. And moreover, now the son of the Benjamite. Leave him to curse! for the LORD told him.
2SA 16:12 If by any means the LORD may behold in my humiliation, and shall return good to me for his curse this day - so be it!
2SA 16:13 And David went, and all his men in the way. And Shimei went according to the side of the mountain being next to him - he went, and cursed, and cast stones on him, and was strewing dust.
2SA 16:14 And the king went and all the people with him being faint, and they refreshed there.
2SA 16:15 And Absalom, and every man of Israel entered into Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
2SA 16:16 And it came to pass when Hushai the chief friend of David came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, Let live the king! Let live the king!
2SA 16:17 And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this your act of kindness with your companion? Why did you not go with your companion?
2SA 16:18 And Hushai said to Absalom, No; but after whoever the LORD chooses, and this people, and every man of Israel - I will be serving to him, and I shall sit down with him.
2SA 16:19 And secondly, to whom shall I serve? Should I not serve before his son? Just as I served before your father, so I will be before you.
2SA 16:20 And Absalom said to Ahithophel, Give counsel for yourselves what we should do.
2SA 16:21 And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Enter to the concubines of your father, which he left behind to guard his house! And all Israel shall hear that you disgraced your father; and the hands of all the ones with you shall grow in strength.
2SA 16:22 And they pitched the tent belonging to Absalom upon the roof. And Absalom entered to the concubines of his father, in the eyes of all Israel.
2SA 16:23 And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he consulted in the first days, was in which manner as if he should ask anything by the word of God - thus was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.
2SA 17:1 And Ahithophel said to Absalom, I shall choose indeed for myself twelve thousand men, and I shall rise up and pursue after David at night.
2SA 17:2 And I shall come upon him, and he will be tiring and loosening his hand, and I shall startle him; and all the people with him shall flee, and I shall strike the king alone.
2SA 17:3 And I shall return all the people to you, in which manner a bride returns to her husband. Besides you seek the life of one man, and all the people will be at peace.
2SA 17:4 And the word was pleasing in the eyes of Absalom, and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
2SA 17:5 And Absalom said, Call indeed Hushai the Archite, and I shall hear what is in his mouth, and indeed of him.
2SA 17:6 And Hushai entered to Absalom. And Absalom said to him, saying, According to this thing Ahithophel spoke. Shall we do according to his word? But if not; you speak!
2SA 17:7 And Hushai said to Absalom, It is not good, this counsel which Ahithophel counseled this one time.
2SA 17:8 And Hushai said, You know your father, and his men, that they are exceedingly mighty, and their soul is very bitter as a bear being made childless in the plain. And your father is a warrior man, and in no way shall he rest the people.
2SA 17:9 For behold, he now hides in one of the canyons, or in one of the places. And it will be when they fall upon them at the beginning, that one shall hear the hearing, and should say, There was a devastation among the people following after Absalom.
2SA 17:10 And indeed any son of power whose heart is as the heart of a lion, in melting away shall melt away; for all Israel knows that your father is mighty, and the sons of power are all with him.
2SA 17:11 Thus advising, I advised. And all Israel in gathering together shall gather together unto you, from Dan and unto Beer-sheba, as the sand upon the sea in multitude; and your presence shall be going in the midst of them.
2SA 17:12 And we shall come upon him in one of the places, which ever we should find him there, and shall camp upon him as falls the dew upon the ground. And we shall not leave behind in him, and of his men with him, even indeed one.
2SA 17:13 And, if he should gather into the city, then all Israel shall take lines against that city, and drag it apart unto the rushing stream - unto not leaving behind there neither a stone.
2SA 17:14 And Absalom said, and every man of Israel, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is good over the counsel of Ahithophel. And the LORD gave charge to efface the good counsel of Ahithophel, so that the LORD should bring the bad things upon Absalom.
2SA 17:15 And Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, So and so advised Ahithophel to Absalom, and to the elders of Israel, and so and so I advised.
2SA 17:16 And now send quickly and report to David! saying, You should not lodge the night according to the descent of the wilderness, but by passing over, pass over, so that the king should not be swallowed down, and all the people with him!
2SA 17:17 And Jonathan and Ahimaaz stopped at the spring of Rogel; and came forth the maidservant, and she reported to them. And they went and reported to king David, for they were not able to appear to enter into the city.
2SA 17:18 And a young man beheld them, and he reported to Absalom. And the two went quickly, and they entered into a house of a man in Bahurim, and unto his cistern in the courtyard, and went down there.
2SA 17:19 And a woman took and opened and spread out a covering over the mouth of the cistern. And she cooled dried clusters upon it, and they did not know the thing.
2SA 17:20 And the servants of Absalom came to the woman, into the house, and said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said to them, They went for a little water. And they sought and did not find them, and they returned unto Jerusalem.
2SA 17:21 And it came to pass, after their going forth, they ascended from out of the cistern, and went, and reported to king David. And they say to him, Rise up and pass over the water quickly! For thus Ahithophel has counseled against you.
2SA 17:22 And David rose up, and all the people with him, and passed over the Jordan until the light of the morning, until one was not unaware of who did not pass over the Jordan.
2SA 17:23 And Ahithophel knew that he had not taken his counsel. And he saddled his donkey, and rose up, and went forth to his house in his city. And he gave charge to his household, and he hung himself, and died. And they entombed him in the burying-place of his father.
2SA 17:24 And David went through unto Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.
2SA 17:25 And Absalom placed Amasa instead of Joab over the force. And Amasa was a son of a man, and the name to him was Ithra the Israelite, who entered to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
2SA 17:26 And Absalom camped, and all Israel, in the land of Gilead.
2SA 17:27 And it came to pass when David entered into Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
2SA 17:28 brought beds, and spreads, and kettles, and ceramic utensils, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and beans, and lentils and toasted grain,
2SA 17:29 and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese from oxen. And they brought near to David, and to the people with him to eat; for they said, The people are hungering, and fainting, and thirsting, in the wilderness.
2SA 18:1 And David numbered all the people with him, and placed over them commanders of thousands, and commanders of hundreds.
2SA 18:2 And David sent away the people, the third under the hand of Joab, and the third under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and the third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, In going forth, I shall go forth, even indeed I myself with you.
2SA 18:3 And the people said, You shall not go forth. For if we should flee into exile, they shall not put upon us to heart. And if half of us should die they shall not put upon us to heart. For you are as ten thousand of us. And now it is good that you will be with us in the city for our helper.
2SA 18:4 And the king said to them, The pleasing thing before you I will do. And the king stood by the side of the gate, and all the people went forth by hundreds and by thousands.
2SA 18:5 And the king gave charge to Joab and to Abishai and to Ittai, saying, Spare for me the young man Absalom! And all the people heard the king giving charge to all the rulers concerning Absalom.
2SA 18:6 And all the people went forth into the field for meeting Israel. And the battle happened in the grove of Ephraim.
2SA 18:7 And the people of Israel failed there before the children of David. And there became a great devastation in that day - twenty thousand men.
2SA 18:8 And it came to pass there the war dispersed over the face of all the land. And the forest was superabundant in devouring of the people above what the sword devoured among the people in that day.
2SA 18:9 And Absalom met before the servants of David. And Absalom was mounted upon the mule, and the mule was entering under the thicket of the great oak, and his head was twisted in the oak, and he hung between the heaven and between the earth, and the mule underneath him went on.
2SA 18:10 And one man saw it, and announced to Joab, and said, Behold, I have seen Absalom hanging in the oak.
2SA 18:11 And Joab said to the man announcing to him, And behold, you saw it? And why is it that you did not strike him there to the ground, and I would have given to you ten shekels of silver, and one sash?
2SA 18:12 And the man said to Joab, And if you rendered unto my hands a thousand shekels of silver, not in any way shall I put my hand against the son of the king. For in our ears the king gave charge to you, and to Abishai, and to Ittai, saying, Guard for me the young man Absalom,
2SA 18:13 to not do anything injust against his life! And all the matter will not be kept unaware from the king, and you shall set yourself right opposite me.
2SA 18:14 And Joab said, This I begin - not thus shall I remain before you. And Joab took three arrows in his hand, and he stuck them in the heart of Absalom while yet he was living, in the heart of the oak.
2SA 18:15 And there encircled ten young men lifting the weapons of Joab, and they struck Absalom, and killed him.
2SA 18:16 And Joab trumped with the trumpet, and the people returned to not pursue after Israel, for Joab spared the people.
2SA 18:17 And Joab took Absalom, and he tossed him into a great chasm in the grove, into the great pit, and set over him a heap of exceedingly great stones. And all Israel fled each to his tent.
2SA 18:18 And Absalom yet living took and set for himself a monument in the valley of the king. For he said, There is not to me a son who shall record my name. And he called the monument by his name. And he called it Hand of Absalom - until this day.
2SA 18:19 And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, Running indeed, I will announce good news to the king, that the LORD passed judgment to him on the hand of his enemies.
2SA 18:20 And Joab said to him, You are not a man of good news in this day, but you shall announce good news in another day. But in this day you shall not announce good news, for a son of the king has died.
2SA 18:21 And Joab said to Cushi, Go, announce to the king what you have seen! And Cushi did obeisance to Joab, and ran.
2SA 18:22 And Ahimaaz son of Zadok added still, and said to Joab, Also let it be that I run also indeed myself after Cushi! And Joab said, Why do you run, my son - there is not good news to you for benefit in going?
2SA 18:23 And Ahimaaz said, For what if I shall run? And Joab said to him, Run! And Ahimaaz ran by the way of Kechar, and he surpassed Cushi.
2SA 18:24 And David was sitting between the two gates, and the watchman went onto the roof of the gate house, unto the wall. And he lifted his eyes and saw, and behold, a man was running alone before him.
2SA 18:25 And the watchman yelled out, and reported to the king. And the king said, If he is alone good news is in his mouth. And he went along, coming and approaching.
2SA 18:26 And the watchman saw another man running. And the watchman yelled out at the gate, and said, Behold, another man is running alone. And the king said, Also this one is announcing good news.
2SA 18:27 And the watchman said, I see the racing of the first as the racing of Ahimaaz son of Zadok. And the king said, This is a good man, and indeed for good news he shall come.
2SA 18:28 And Ahimaaz yelled and said to the king, Peace. And he did obeisance to the king upon his face upon the ground. And he said, Blessed be the LORD your God, who shut up the men lifting their hand against my master the king.
2SA 18:29 And the king said, Is there peace to the young man Absalom? And Ahimaaz said, I saw the great multitude being gladdened in the sending Joab the servant of the king, and your servant, and I do not know what happened there.
2SA 18:30 And the king said, Turn aside and stand by here! And he turned aside and stood.
2SA 18:31 And behold, Cushi came. And Cushi said to the king, Let there be good news announced, O my master the king! For the LORD passed judgment for you today of the hand of all the ones rousing against you.
2SA 18:32 And the king said to Cushi, How is the peace to the young man Absalom? And Cushi said, Let be as that young man, the enemies of my master the king, and all as many as rise up against you for evils!
2SA 18:33 And the king was disturbed, and ascended into the upper room of the gate and wept. And so he said as he wept, O My son Absalom, O my son, O my son Absalom, what might my death give instead of you - I instead of you, Absalom, O my son, O my son.
2SA 19:1 And it was announced to Joab, saying, Behold, the king weeps and mourns over Absalom.
2SA 19:2 And the deliverance in that day became for mourning to all the people. For the people heard in that day, saying that, The king frets for his son.
2SA 19:3 And the people stole away in that day to enter into the city, as people steal away being shamed in their fleeing in the battle.
2SA 19:4 And the king hid his face, and the king cried out with a great voice, saying, O my son, Absalom, Absalom, O my son.
2SA 19:5 And Joab entered to the king into the house, and said, You disgraced today the faces of all your servants delivering your life today, and the life of your sons, and of your daughters, and the life of your wives, and the life of your concubines,

2SA 19:7 And now, arise, go forth and speak unto the heart of your servants! For by the LORD I swear by an oath, that unless you should go forth, in no way should a man remain with you this night. And realize this in yourself, that this evil will be upon you over all the evil coming upon you from your youth unto the present!

2SA 21:2 And the king called the Gibeonites, and spoke to them. And the Gibeonites were not of the sons of Israel, for they were of the remnants of the Amorites - but the sons of Israel swore an oath to them. But Saul sought to strike them in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah.
2SA 21:3 And David said to the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? And by what means shall I atone, and you shall bless the inheritance of the LORD?
2SA 21:4 And the Gibeonites said to him, There is not a problem with us over silver nor gold with Saul, and with his house; and there is not to us a man to put to death from out of all Israel.
2SA 21:5 And he said, What you say even I will do for you. And they said to the king, The man who finished us off entirely, and pursued us, who misled to utterly destroy us, we shall remove him, so that he is not established in any border of Israel.

And she did not allow the birds of the heaven to rest upon them by day, nor the wild beasts of the field by night.

2SA 22:1 And David spoke to the LORD the words of this ode in the day which the LORD rescued him from the hand of all his enemies, and from out of the hand of Saul.
2SA 22:2 And he said, The LORD - my rock, and my fortress, and the one rescuing me.
2SA 22:3 My God, my guard - I will be yielded upon him; my defender and horn of my deliverance; my shielder and my refuge; my deliverance from the unjust - you shall deliver me.
2SA 22:4 Praiseworthy - I shall call upon the LORD; and from my enemies I shall be delivered.
2SA 22:5 For conflicts of death compassed me, and the rushing streams of lawlessness made me distraught.
2SA 22:6 Cords of Hades encircled me, and shackles of death anticipated me.
2SA 22:7 In my affliction I shall call upon the LORD, and to my God I will yell. And he heard my voice from out of his temple, and my cry in his ears.
2SA 22:8 And the earth was shaken and disturbed; even the foundations of the heaven were disturbed and thrown into a spasm, for the LORD was enraged with them.
2SA 22:9 Smoke ascended in his wrath, and fire from out of his mouth devoured; coals were kindled by it.
2SA 22:10 And he leaned the heavens, and came down - and dimness was under his feet.
2SA 22:11 And he mounted upon cherubim, and was spread out; and was seen upon the wings of the winds.
2SA 22:12 And he placed darkness for his concealment. Round about him his tent was darkness of waters - thickened in clouds of air.
2SA 22:13 From the brightness before him coals of fire were kindled.
2SA 22:14 The LORD thundered from out of heaven, and the highest gave out his voice.
2SA 22:15 And he sent arrows, and dispersed them; and he flashed lightning, and startled them.
2SA 22:16 And the releases of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the inhabitable world were uncovered at the reproach of the LORD, by the breath of spirit of his rage.
2SA 22:17 He sent from the height, and took me; he drew me out of many waters.
2SA 22:18 He delivered me from the strength of my enemies, from the ones detesting me - for they were strong above me.
2SA 22:19 They anticipated me in a day of my affliction; and the LORD became my stay.
2SA 22:20 And he led me into an enlargement; and rescued me, for he thought to do well by me.
2SA 22:21 And the LORD recompensed unto me according to my righteousness. And according to the cleanliness of my hands he shall make recompense to me.
2SA 22:22 For I guarded the ways of the LORD, and was not impious before my God.
2SA 22:23 For all his judgments were in front of me, and his ordinances did not depart from me.
2SA 22:24 And I will be unblemished to him, and I shall keep guard from my lawlessness.
2SA 22:25 And the LORD shall recompense to me according to my righteousness, and according to the cleanliness of my hands before his eyes.
2SA 22:26 With the sacred you shall be sacred, and with the innocent you shall be innocent,
2SA 22:27 and with the chosen you shall be chosen, and with the crooked you shall be crooked.
2SA 22:28 And the poor people you shall preserve, and the eyes of the proud you shall humble.
2SA 22:29 For you shall light my lamp, O LORD; and the LORD shall shine forth in my darkness.
2SA 22:30 For in you I shall run lightly armed; and by my God I shall leap over a wall.
2SA 22:31 God - unblemished is his way; the saying of the LORD being set on fire; he is a defender to all the ones yielding upon him.
2SA 22:32 For who is God besides the LORD? And who is creator besides our God?
2SA 22:33 God - the one strengthening me is power; and he established my way as unblemished;
2SA 22:34 setting my feet as a stag, and standing me upon the heights;
2SA 22:35 teaching my hands for war, and breaking the bow of brass by my arms.
2SA 22:36 And you gave to me a shield of my deliverance; and obedience of you multiplied me.
2SA 22:37 And you widened my footsteps underneath me; and my legs shook not.
2SA 22:38 I will pursue my enemies, and I will remove them; and I shall not return until of which I shall finish them off.
2SA 22:39 And I will crush them, and they shall not rise up; and they shall fall under my feet.
2SA 22:40 And you shall gird on me power for war. You shall bend the ones rising up against me, underneath me.
2SA 22:41 And you gave my enemies to me - I trampled the back of the necks of ones detesting me.
2SA 22:42 They yelled out, and there was not one delivering; even to the LORD, and he did not take heed of them.
2SA 22:43 And I ground them as dust of the earth; I made them fine as the mud of the streets.
2SA 22:44 And you rescued me from disputes of people; you shall guard me as head of nations. A people whom not knowing, served to me.
2SA 22:45 With a hearing ear it obeyed me; alien sons lied to me;
2SA 22:46 alien sons shall reel - and they shall trip from their confinement.
2SA 22:47 As the LORD lives - for blessed be the one shaping me; and my God shall be raised up high - my deliverer.
2SA 22:48 The LORD is strong - the one giving acts of vengeance to me, and humbling peoples underneath me.
2SA 22:49 And he led me from my enemies; and from the ones rousing up against me you shall raise me up high. You shall rescue me from men of offences.
2SA 22:50 On account of this I will make acknowledgement to you, O LORD, among the nations, and I will strum to your name,
2SA 22:51 O one magnifying the deliverance of his king, and doing mercy to his anointed one, to David and to his seed unto the eon.

2SA 24:12 Go and speak to David! saying, Thus says the LORD, Three things I lift unto you - you choose for yourself one of them, and I will execute against you!
2SA 24:13 And Gad went to David, and announced, and said to him, Choose to yourself what is to be to you! Three years of famine in your land, or three months for you to flee before your enemies, and they will be pursuing you, or three days of plague to be in your land. Now then, know and perceive what I shall answer to the one sending me!
2SA 24:14 And David said to Gad, It is an exceedingly narrow choice to me - the three things. I shall fall into the hands of the LORD, for his compassions are exceedingly great, but into the hands of men in no way shall I fall.
2SA 24:15 And David chose for himself plague. And the LORD appointed plague in Israel from morning and unto the hour of dinner. And there died from out of the people from Dan and unto Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.

2SA 24:21 And Araunah said, For what reason comes my master the king to his servant? And David said, To acquire from you the threshing-floor, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the devastation upon the people should be constrained.

1KI 2:4 So that the LORD should establish his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, If your sons should guard their way, to go before me in truth, with their whole heart, and with their whole soul, (saying,) there shall not be lifted away to you a man from the throne of Israel.
1KI 2:5 And now you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two rulers of the forces of Israel, to Abner son of Ner, and to Amasa son of Jether, and he killed them, and ordered up the blood of war for peace, and put innocent blood on his belt on his loin, and on his sandal on his foot.

1KI 5:4 And now the LORD my God gave rest to me round about - there is not a plotter, and there is not a wicked meeting.
