2KI 15:17 In the thirtieth and ninth year of Azariah king of Judah Menahem son of Gadi reigned over Israel in Samaria ten years.
2KI 15:18 And he did the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD. He abstained not from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin.
2KI 15:19 In his days Pul king of the Assyrians ascended upon the land. And Menahem gave to Pul a thousand talents of silver for his hand to be with him to strengthen his kingdom in his hand.
2KI 15:20 And Menahem brought forth the silver for Israel, excised upon every mighty man in strength, to give to the king of the Assyrians - fifty shekels for the one man. And the king of the Assyrians returned, and did not station there in the land.
2KI 15:21 And the rest of the words of Menahem, and all as much as he did - behold are not these written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
2KI 15:22 And Menahem slept with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 15:23 In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekahiah son of Menahem reigned over Israel in Samaria two years.
2KI 15:24 And he did the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD. He abstained not from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.
2KI 15:25 And Pekah son of Remaliah his tribune confederated against him, and struck him in Samaria, before the house of the king, with Argob, and with Arieh, and with him fifty men from the sons of the Gileadites. And he killed him, and reigned instead of him.
2KI 15:26 And the rest of the words of Pekahiah, and all as much as he did - behold, these are written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Israel.
2KI 15:27 In the fiftieth and second year of Azariah king of Judah Pekah son of Remaliah reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty years.
2KI 15:28 And he did the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD. He abstained not from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.
2KI 15:29 In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians, and took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maachah, and Janoah, and Kenez, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and resettled them into Assyria.
2KI 15:30 And Hoshea son of Elah confederated a confederation against Pekah son of Remaliah, and struck him, and killed him, and reigned instead of him in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
2KI 15:31 And the rest of the words of Pekah, and all as much as he did - behold, these are written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Israel.
2KI 15:32 In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah reigned.
2KI 15:33 He was a son being twenty and five years old in his taking reign, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
2KI 15:34 And he did upright in the eyes of the LORD according to all as much as Uzziah his father did.
2KI 15:35 Only the high places he did not remove; and still the people sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the gate of the house of the LORD - the upper.
2KI 15:36 And the rest of the words of Jotham, and all as much as he did - behold are not these written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
2KI 15:37 In those days the LORD began to send against Judah Rezin king of Syria, and Pekah son of Remaliah.
2KI 15:38 And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they entombed him with his fathers in the city of David his forefather. And Ahaz his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 16:1 In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah reigned.
2KI 16:2 Ahaz was a son being twenty years old in his reigning, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem, and did not do the upright thing in the eyes of the LORD his God, as David his forefather.
2KI 16:3 And he went in the way of the kings of Israel, and indeed he led his son through fire, according to the abominations of the nations, which the LORD removed in front of the sons of Israel.
2KI 16:4 And he sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, and upon the hills, and underneath every tree of the woods.
2KI 16:5 Then Rezin king of Syria ascended, and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel to Jerusalem for war. And they made assault against Ahaz, and were not able to wage war successfully.
2KI 16:6 In that time Rezin king of Syria returned Elath to Syria, and cast out the Jews from Elath. And the Edomites came into Elath, and dwelt there until this day.
2KI 16:7 And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians, saying, I am your servant and your son. Ascend, and deliver me from out of the hand of the king of Syria, and from out of the hand of the king of Israel, of the ones rising up against me!
2KI 16:8 And Ahaz took the silver and the gold he found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD, and of the house of the king, and sent gifts to the king of the Assyrians.
2KI 16:9 And the king of the Assyrians heard him. And the king of the Assyrians ascended up against Damascus, and seized it, and resettled it, and killed Rezin.
2KI 16:10 And king Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians in Damascus, and saw the altar in Damascus. And king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the likeness of the altar, and the proportions of it, according to all its makings.
2KI 16:11 And Urijah the priest built the altar according to all as much as king Ahaz sent from Damascus. Thus Urijah the priest did until the coming of the king from Damascus.
2KI 16:12 And the king came from Damascus. And the king beheld the altar. And the king drew near to the altar, and ascended unto it.
2KI 16:13 And he offered his whole burnt offering, and his sacrifice offering, and offered a libation of his libation offering on it. And he poured upon it the blood of his peace offerings, upon the altar.
2KI 16:14 And the brass altar which was before the LORD he brought forward in front of the house of the LORD, from between the altar and from between the house of the LORD, and put it by the side of the altar according to the north.
2KI 16:15 And king Ahaz gave charge to Urijah the priest, saying, Upon the great altar offer the whole burnt offering, the early morning offering, and the the evening sacrifice offering, and the whole burnt offerings of the king, and his sacrifice offerings, and the whole burnt offering of all the people, and their sacrifice offerings, and their libation offerings! And all the blood of the whole burnt offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice offering you shall pour out upon it! And the altar of brass will be for me in the morning.
2KI 16:16 And Urijah the priest did according to all as much as Ahaz the king gave charge to him.
2KI 16:17 And king Ahaz cut down the joinery of the bases, and moved the bathing tub from them; and the sea he lowered from the oxen of brass underneath it, and put it upon a stone base.
2KI 16:18 And the foundation of the chair of the Sabbaths he built in the house of the LORD, and the entrance of the king outside, he turned in the house of the LORD from in front of the king of the Assyrians.
2KI 16:19 And the rest of the words of Ahaz, as much as he did - behold are not these written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
2KI 16:20 And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and he was entombed with his fathers in the city of David. And Hezekiah his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 17:1 In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah reigned in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
2KI 17:2 And he did the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD, only not as the kings of Israel who were before him.
2KI 17:3 Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians ascended against him; and Hoshea became a servant to him, and bore gifts to him.
2KI 17:4 And the king of the Assyrians found a plot by Hoshea; for Hoshea sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and did not bring gifts to the king of the Assyrians year by year. And the king of the Assyrians assaulted him, and tied him up in the house of the prison.
2KI 17:5 And the king of the Assyrians ascended unto all the land, and ascended unto Samaria, and assaulted it for three years.
2KI 17:6 In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of the Assyrians seized Samaria, and resettled Israel into Assyria, and settled them in Halah and in Habor, the rivers of Gozan, in the borders of the Medes.
2KI 17:7 And it came to pass that the sons of Israel sinned against the LORD their God, the one leading them from out of the land of Egypt, from beneath the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
2KI 17:8 And they went by the ordinances of the nations which the LORD removed in front of the sons of Israel, and the kings of Israel, as many as they did.
2KI 17:9 And the sons of Israel clothed words of wrongdoings against the LORD their God, and built to themselves high places in all their cities, from guard tower unto the fortified city.
2KI 17:10 And they set up to themselves stone monuments and sacred groves upon every high hill, and underneath every tree of the woods.
2KI 17:11 And they burned incense there in all the high places, as the nations which the LORD resettled from their face. And they made partners, and they graved images to provoke the LORD to anger.
2KI 17:12 And they served to the idols, which the LORD said to them, Do not do this thing!
2KI 17:13 And the LORD testified to Israel, and to Judah, by the hand of all his prophets, every one of them seers, saying, Turn from your wicked ways, and guard my commandments, and my ordinances, and every law which I gave charge to your fathers, as many as I sent to them by the hand of my servants the prophets!
2KI 17:14 And they hearkened not, and they hardened their back above the back of their fathers, that trusted not in the LORD their God;
2KI 17:15 even thrusting away his covenant, and the ordinances which he ordained with their fathers, and his testimonies, as many as he testified to them, and went after the vain things, and acted in folly, and followed after the nations surrounding them, which the LORD gave charge to them to not do according to these things.
2KI 17:16 And they abandoned the commandments of the LORD their God, and made to themselves molten castings of two heifers, and made a sacred grove, and did obeisance to all the military of the heaven, and served to Baal.
2KI 17:17 And they led their sons and their daughters through fire, and used oracles of divinations, and foretold. And they were sold to do the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.
2KI 17:18 And the LORD was enraged exceedingly with Israel. And he removed them from his face. He did not leave any behind except the tribe of Judah alone.
2KI 17:19 And indeed Judah did not guard the commandments of the LORD his God, and went by the ordinances of Israel, which they did. And they thrusted away the LORD.
2KI 17:20 And the LORD was enraged with all the seed of Israel, and he shook them off, and gave them into the hand of the ones tearing them in pieces, until of which time he threw them away from his face.
2KI 17:21 For furthermore Israel was torn from the house of David; and they gave reign to Jeroboam son of Nebat. And Jeroboam banished Israel from following the LORD, and led them into sin - a great sin.
2KI 17:22 And the sons of Israel went in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did - they abstained not from them;
2KI 17:23 until of which the LORD removed Israel from his face, as the LORD spoke by the hand of all his servants the prophets. And Israel was resettled from its land into Assyria until this day.
2KI 17:24 And the king of the Assyrians led from out of Babylon the one from out of Cuthah, and from out of Ava, and from out of Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria instead of the sons of Israel. And they inherited Samaria, and settled in its cities.
2KI 17:25 And it came to pass in the beginning of their place of sitting down, they did not fear the LORD. And the LORD sent among them the lions, and they were being killed by them.
2KI 17:26 And they said to the king of the Assyrians, saying, The nations which you resettled, and relocated in the cities of Samaria, know not the distinguishing manner of the God of the land. And he sent to them lions, and behold, they are killing them, in so far as they know not the distinguishing manner of the God of the land.
2KI 17:27 And the king of the Assyrians gave charge, saying, Lead away there one of the priests whom I resettled from Samaria, and let him go and dwell there! And he shall enlighten them on the distinguishing manner of the God of the land.
2KI 17:28 And they brought one of the priests whom they resettled from Samaria, and he settled in Beth-el. And he was enlightening them how they should fear the LORD.
2KI 17:29 And nation by nation were making their gods. And they put them in the houses of the high places, which the Samaritans made, nation by nation in their cities in which they dwelt.
2KI 17:30 And the men of Babylon made Succoth Benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,
2KI 17:31 and the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites incinerated their sons by fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, gods of the Sepharvaim.
2KI 17:32 And they were fearing the LORD, and they also made for themselves priests of the high places; and they offered for themselves in the houses of the high places.
2KI 17:33 They were fearing the LORD, and they served their gods, according to the distinguishing manner of the nations from where he resettled them from there.
2KI 17:34 Until this day they do according to their distinguishing manner. They are not fearing the LORD, and they do not do according to their ordinances, and according to their judgment, and according to the law, and according to the commandment which the LORD gave charge to the sons of Jacob, of whom he established his name Israel.
2KI 17:35 And the LORD ordained with them a covenant, and gave charge to them, saying, You shall not fear other gods, and you shall not do obeisance to them, and you shall not serve to them, and you shall not sacrifice to them.
2KI 17:36 For only to the LORD, who led you from out of the land of Egypt with great strength and with a high arm - him you shall fear, and to him you shall do obeisance, and to him you shall sacrifice.
2KI 17:37 And his ordinances, and the judgments, and the commandments, and the law which he wrote for you, you shall guard to do all the days; and you shall not fear other gods.
2KI 17:38 And the covenant which he ordained with you you shall not forget; and you shall not fear other gods.
2KI 17:39 For only the LORD your God - him you shall fear; and he will rescue you from the hand of all your enemies.
2KI 17:40 And they hearkened not, but only in their former ordinances they acted.
2KI 17:41 And these nations were fearing the LORD, and they served to their carvings - even indeed their sons, and the sons of their sons themselves do as did their fathers unto this day.
2KI 18:1 And it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah reigned.
2KI 18:2 He was a son being twenty and five years old in his taking reign, and twenty and nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Abi, daughter of Zachariah.
2KI 18:3 And he did the upright thing in the eyes of the LORD, according to all as much as David his forefather did.
2KI 18:4 He removed the high places, and broke the monuments, and cut down the sacred groves, and cut up the serpent of brass which Moses made; for unto those days the sons of Israel were burning incense to it. And he called it Nehushtan.
2KI 18:5 In the LORD God of Israel he hoped. There was not one likened to him after him among the kings of Judah, and among the ones taking place before him.
2KI 18:6 And he cleaved to the LORD. He did not leave from behind him, and he guarded his commandments, as many as the LORD gave charge to Moses.
2KI 18:7 And the LORD was with him - in all the things which he did he perceived. And he annulled allegiance to the king of the Assyrians, and did not serve to him.
2KI 18:8 He struck the Philistines unto Gaza, and unto its border, from the tower of the ones guarding, and unto the fortified city.
2KI 18:9 And it came to pass in the fourth year to king Hezekiah, this is the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, ascended Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians against Samaria, and assaulted it.
2KI 18:10 And he overtook it at the end of three years. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, this is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was seized.
2KI 18:11 And the king of the Assyrians resettled the Samarian into Assyria, and he put them in Halah and in Habor by the river Gozan, and in the borders of the Medes;
2KI 18:12 because they hearkened not to the voice of the LORD their God, and they violated his covenant, all as much as he gave charge to Moses the manservant of the LORD - and they hearkened not, and they did not do.
2KI 18:13 And in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah Sennacherib king of the Assyrians ascended against the fortified cities of Judah, and seized them.
2KI 18:14 And Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians to Lachish, saying, I have sinned; turn from me! What ever you should place upon me I will bear. And the king of the Assyrians placed a tribute upon Hezekiah king of Judah of three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
2KI 18:15 And Hezekiah gave all the silver he found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasuries of the house of the king.
2KI 18:16 In that time Hezekiah the king of Judah cut off the doors of the temple of the LORD, and the supports which Hezekiah the king of Judah gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.
2KI 18:17 And the king of the Assyrians sent Tartan, and Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a heavy force to Jerusalem. And they ascended, and came to Jerusalem. And they stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is in the way of the field of the fuller.
2KI 18:18 And they yelled to Hezekiah. And Eliakim son of Hilkiah the manager came to them, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the one taking record.
2KI 18:19 And Rabshakeh said to them, Say indeed to Hezekiah, Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians, What is this reliance which you yield on?
2KI 18:20 How then do words of the lips and counsel become the battle array for war? Now then, upon whom are you relying upon, that you annulled allegiance to me?
2KI 18:21 Behold, are you yourself relying upon this fractured rod of reed - upon Egypt? Thus if a man should stay upon it, it will enter into his hand, and puncture it. Thus is Pharoah king of Egypt to all the ones relying upon him.
2KI 18:22 And if you should say to me, Upon the LORD our God we rely on. Is it not he that Hezekiah removed his high places and his altars, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Before this altar you shall do obeisance in Jerusalem?
2KI 18:23 And now, mix in with my master the king of the Assyrians, and I will give to you two thousand horses - if you shall be able to put for yourself a rider upon them.
2KI 18:24 And how will you turn back the face of one toparch of the least of the servants of my master, and hope for yourself upon Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
2KI 18:25 And now, is it without the LORD that we ascended against this place to utterly destroy it? The LORD said to me, Ascend against this land, and utterly destroy it!
2KI 18:26 And Eliakim son of Hilkiah and Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, Speak indeed to your servants in Syrian! For we hear. And do not speak with us in Jewish to the ears of the people upon the wall!
2KI 18:27 And Rabshakeh said to them, Is it to your master, and to you my master sent me to speak these words? Is it not to the men sitting upon the wall, to eat their dung, and to drink their urine with you together?
2KI 18:28 And Rabshakeh stood and yelled with a great voice in Jewish, and spoke, and said, Hear the words of the king - of the great king of the Assyrians!
2KI 18:29 Thus says the king, Let not Hezekiah lift you! For in no way should he be able to rescue you from out of my hand.
2KI 18:30 And let not Hezekiah raise your hope unto the LORD! saying, In rescuing, the LORD will rescue us, and in no way shall this city be delivered into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
2KI 18:31 Do not listen to Hezekiah! For thus says the king of the Assyrians, Do for me a blessing, and come forth to me, and each shall eat of his grapevine, and each of his fig tree, and each shall drink water of his well;
2KI 18:32 until whenever I should come and should take you into a land as your land, a land of grain, and wine, and bread, and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, and you shall live, and not die! And do not listen to Hezekiah! For he deceives you, saying, The LORD shall deliver you.
2KI 18:33 Have by rescuing the gods of the nations rescued each his land from out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
2KI 18:34 Where is the god of Hamath, and Arphad? Where is the god of Sepharvaim - Hena, and Ivah? Did they deliver Samaria from out of my hand?
2KI 18:35 Who among all the gods of the lands is the one who rescued his land from out of my hand, that the LORD shall rescue Jerusalem from out of my hand?
2KI 18:36 And they kept silent, and did not answer him a word, because of the commandment of the king, saying, You shall not answer to him.
2KI 18:37 And Eliakim son of Hilkiah the manager entered, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the one recording, to Hezekiah tearing their garments, and announced to him the words of Rabshakeh.
2KI 19:1 And it came to pass as king Hezekiah heard, that he tore his garments, and put on sackcloth, and entered into the house of the LORD.
2KI 19:2 And he sent Eliakim the manager, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, having put on sackcloths, to Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet.
2KI 19:3 And they said to him, Thus says Hezekiah, A day of affliction, and of rebuke, and provocation to anger is this day; for the sons came unto birth pangs, and there is not strength to give birth.
2KI 19:4 If by any means the LORD your God shall hearken to all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of the Assyrians his master sent him to berate the living God, and to reprove by words which the LORD your God heard; that you shall take up a prayer for the remnant being found.
2KI 19:5 And the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
2KI 19:6 And Isaiah said to them, Thus you shall say to your master, Thus says the LORD, You should not fear from the words which you heard, which the servants of the king of the Assyrians blasphemed against me.
2KI 19:7 Behold, I give a spirit to him, and he shall hear a message, and shall return unto his land; and I will cast him down by the broadsword in his land.
2KI 19:8 And Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of the Assyrians waging war against Libnah; for he heard that he departed from Lachish.
2KI 19:9 And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of the Ethiopians, saying, Behold, he comes forth to wage war against you. And he returned, and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
2KI 19:10 Thus shall you say to Hezekiah king of Judah, Let not your God deceive you in whom you rely upon him, saying, In no way should Jerusalem be delivered up into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.
2KI 19:11 Behold, you heard all as much as the king of the Assyrians did in all the lands, as they utterly destroyed them - and how shall you be rescued?
2KI 19:12 Have the gods of the nations rescued which my fathers utterly destroyed - both Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden in Thelasar?
2KI 19:13 Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim - Hena and Ivah?
2KI 19:14 And Hezekiah took the scrolls from out of the hand of the messengers, and read them. And he ascended into the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah unrolled them before the LORD.
2KI 19:15 And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying, O Lord God of Israel, the one sitting upon the cherubim, you are God alone among all the kingdoms of the earth; you made the heaven and the earth.
2KI 19:16 Lean, O LORD, your ear, and hear! Open, O LORD, your eyes, and behold! And hear the words of Sennacherib, which he sent to berate the living God!
2KI 19:17 For truth, O LORD, the kings of the Assyrians made desolate the nations, and all their land,
2KI 19:18 and put their gods into the fire - for they are not gods, but only the works of the hands of men, wood and stone. And they destroyed them.
2KI 19:19 And now, O LORD our God, deliver us from out of his hand! And they shall know in all the kingdoms of the earth that you are the LORD God alone.
2KI 19:20 And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says the LORD God of Israel, I heard what you pray for to me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians.
2KI 19:21 This is the word which the LORD spoke against him; The virgin daughter of Zion treats you with contempt and sneers at you. The daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head over you.
2KI 19:22 Whom have you berated and blasphemed? And against whom have you raised up your voice, and lifted your eyes into the height? even against the holy one of Israel.
2KI 19:23 By the hand of your messengers you have berated the LORD, and said, By the multitude of my chariots I ascended into the height of the mountains, of the sides of Lebanon, and I felled the greatness of his cedar, his chosen cypresses, and I came in the midst of the grove of Carmel.
2KI 19:24 I cooled myself and drank alien waters. And I made quite desolate with the sole of my feet all the rivers of the citadel.
2KI 19:25 Heard you not that far off I made her? From ancient days I formed her, and now I brought her. And she became for haughtiness of fortified cities of combative resettlements.
2KI 19:26 And the ones dwelling in them weakened in the hand. They were alarmed and were disgraced. They became as grass of the field, and as the green pasturage; as tender shoots growing on roofs, and a trampling upon before standing.
2KI 19:27 And of your sitting-down, and of your exiting, and of your entering, and of your rage against me I knew.
2KI 19:28 On account of your being provoked to anger against me, that your indulgence ascended to my ears, and I shall put my hook in your nostrils, and bits in your lips, and I will return you in the way which you came by it.
2KI 19:29 And this is to you the sign. You shall eat this year the things grown by themselves, and in the second year the things rising up, and the third year you shall sow, and you shall reap, and you shall plant vineyards, and you shall eat their fruit.
2KI 19:30 And he shall add to the one being preserved of the house of Judah being left behind as a root below. And he shall produce fruit upward.
2KI 19:31 For from out of Jerusalem shall come forth a vestige, and the one rescuing from out of mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of the forces shall do this.
2KI 19:32 Therefore thus says the LORD to the king of the Assyrians, He shall not enter into this city, and he shall not shoot an arrow there, and he shall not anticipate it with a shield, nor shall he pour out dirt against it for a seige mound.
2KI 19:33 By the way in which he came by it, he shall return, and into this city he shall not enter, says the LORD.
2KI 19:34 And I shall shield over this city to deliver her because of myself, and because of David my servant.
2KI 19:35 And it came to pass at night, that there came forth an angel of the LORD, and struck among the camp of the Assyrians a hundred eighty-five thousand. And they rose early in the morning. And behold, all dead bodies.
2KI 19:36 And Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed and went and returned, and lived in Nineveh.
2KI 19:37 And it came to pass of his doing obeisance in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with a sword. And they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esar-haddon his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 20:1 In those days Hezekiah was infirm unto death. And Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet entered to him, and said to him, Thus says the LORD, Give charge concerning your house! For you die, and shall not live.
2KI 20:2 And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, and he prayed to the LORD, saying,
2KI 20:3 O LORD, remember indeed as much as I walked before you in truth, and in a perfect heart! And I did good in your eyes. And Hezekiah wept in a great weeping.
2KI 20:4 And Isaiah was in the courtyard between, and the saying of the LORD came to him, saying,
2KI 20:5 Return! And you shall say to Hezekiah, the one leading my people, Thus says the LORD, the God of David your forefather! I heard your prayer, and I beheld your tears. Behold, I shall heal you on the third day, and you shall ascend into the house of the LORD.
2KI 20:6 And I will add to your days fifteen years; and from the hand of the king of the Assyrians I will deliver you and this city; and I will shield over this city because of myself, and because of David my servant.
2KI 20:7 And Isaiah said, Let them take a dried cluster of figs, and place them upon the sore, and he shall be healed!
2KI 20:8 And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, What is the sign that the LORD shall heal me, and I shall ascend into the house of the LORD on the third day?
2KI 20:9 And Isaiah said, This to you is the sign by the LORD, that the LORD shall do the word which he spoke. Shall the shadow go ten stairs or shall it return ten stairs.
2KI 20:10 And Hezekiah said, It is a light thing for the shadow to lean ten stairs; not thus, but let the shadow return ten stairs to the rear.
2KI 20:11 And Isaiah the prophet yelled out to the LORD, and he returned the shadow on the stairs of Ahaz, in which it went down the ten stairs to the rear.
2KI 20:12 In that time Berodach Baladan the son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and gifts to Hezekiah, for he heard that Hezekiah was infirm.
2KI 20:13 And Hezekiah rejoiced over them. And he showed to them all the house of the spices - the silver, and the gold, the aromatics, and the good olive oil, and the house of his weapons, and all as much as was found in his treasuries. There was not a place which Hezekiah did not show to them in his house, and in all under his authority.
2KI 20:14 And Isaiah the prophet entered to Hezekiah the king, and said to him, What did these men say, and from what place came they to you? And Hezekiah said, From a land at a distance - they came to me from Babylon.
2KI 20:15 And he said, What did they behold in your house? And Hezekiah said, All as much is in my house they beheld. There was not anything in my house which I did not show to them, and in my treasuries.
2KI 20:16 And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the LORD!
2KI 20:17 Behold, days come, says the LORD, and there shall be taken away all the things in your house, and as much as your fathers treasured up until this day into Babylon. There shall not be left behind a thing, said the LORD.
2KI 20:18 And from your sons coming forth from you, whom you procreated, they shall take them, and they will be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon.
2KI 20:19 And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, The word of the LORD is good which he spoke, let there be peace and righteousness in my days!
2KI 20:20 And the rest of the words of Hezekiah, and all as much as he did, and all his dominations, and the fountain, and the aqueduct, and how he brought the water into the city - behold are not these written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
2KI 20:21 And Hezekiah slept with his fathers. And he was entombed in the city of David. And Manasseh his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 21:1 Manasseh was a son being twelve years old in his taking reign, and fifty and five years he reigned in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Hephzi-bah.
2KI 21:2 And he did the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD, and went according to the abominations of the nations, whom the LORD removed from in front of the sons of Israel.
2KI 21:3 And he returned and built the high places which Hezekiah his father tore down; and he reestablished an altar to Baal, and made the sacred groves as did Ahab king of Israel; and did obeisance to all the military of the heaven, and served to them.
2KI 21:4 And he built an altar in the house of the LORD, in which he said LORD, In Jerusalem I will establish my name.
2KI 21:5 And he built altars to all the military of the heaven in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD.
2KI 21:6 And he led his sons through fire, and prognosticated, and foretold, and appointed ones who deliver oracles, and diviners; to multiply to do the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.
2KI 21:7 And he put the carving of the sacred grove in the house, in which the LORD said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, in which I chose from out of all the tribes of Israel, that I will put my name there into the eon.
2KI 21:8 And I will not proceed to shake the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers; only if they should guard to do according to all which I gave charge to them - according to every law which Moses my servant gave charge to them.
2KI 21:9 And they hearkened not. And Manasseh misled them to do the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD above the nations which the LORD removed in front of the sons of Israel.
2KI 21:10 And the LORD spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,
2KI 21:11 On account of as much as Manasseh king of Judah did these wicked abominations, according to all as much as the Amorite did before him, and even indeed led Judah into sin by his idols.
2KI 21:12 Is it not so? Thus says the LORD God of Israel, Behold, I bring evils upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that all hearing, it shall sound in both of his ears.
2KI 21:13 And I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria, and the weight of the house of Ahab. And I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a writing tablet, and overturns it upon its face.
2KI 21:14 And I will wipe away the vestige of my inheritance, and I will deliver them into the hands of their enemies; and they will be for ravaging and for plunder by all their enemies;
2KI 21:15 because of as much as they did the wicked thing in my eyes, and were provoking me to anger from the day which I led their fathers from out of Egypt, and until this day.
2KI 21:16 And indeed Manasseh poured out exceedingly much innocent blood, until of which he filled Jerusalem of it mouth to mouth; outside of his sins which he led Judah into sin - to do the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD.
2KI 21:17 And the rest of the words of Manasseh, and all as much as he did, and his sin which he sinned - behold are not these written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
2KI 21:18 And Manasseh slept with his fathers. And they entombed him in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza. And Amon his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 21:19 Amon was a son being twenty and two years old in his taking reign. And two years he reigned in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz from out of Jotbah.
2KI 21:20 And he did the wicked thing in the eyes of the LORD, as Manasseh his father did.
2KI 21:21 And he went in every way in which his father went. And he slaved to the idols whom his father slaved, and did obeisance to them.
2KI 21:22 And he abandoned the LORD God of his fathers, and went not in the way of the LORD.
2KI 21:23 And the servants of Amon confederated against him, and they killed the king in his house.
2KI 21:24 And the people of the land struck the ones confederating against king Amon. And the people of the land gave reign to Josiah his son instead of him.
2KI 21:25 And the rest of the words of Amon, as much as he did - behold, are not these written upon the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
2KI 21:26 And they entombed him in his tomb, in the garden of Uzza. And Josiah his son reigned instead of him.
2KI 22:1 Josiah was a son being eight years old in his taking reign, and thirty and one year s he reigned in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah of Boscath.
2KI 22:2 And he did upright in the eyes of the LORD, and went in every way of David his forefather. He did not separate to the right nor left.

2KI 22:4 Ascend to Hilkiah the great priest, and set a seal upon the money being carried into the house of the LORD, which the ones guarding the money gathered together from the people!
2KI 22:5 And let them put it into the hand of the ones doing the works, of the ones being ordained in the house of the LORD! And he gave it to the ones doing the works in the house of the LORD, to strengthen the breach of the house -
2KI 22:6 to the fabricators, and to the builders, and to the stonemasons, and to acquire wood and quarried stones to fortify the breach of the house.
2KI 22:7 Only did not 1they 3call 5to account for the money being given to them, for they act in trust.
2KI 22:8 And Hilkiah the great priest said to Shaphan the scribe, I found a scroll of the law in the house of the LORD. And Hilkiah gave to Shaphan the scroll, and he read it.
2KI 22:9 And Shapan entered to king Josiah. And he turned to the king for a word, and said, Your servants cast the silver being found in the house of the LORD, and they put it in the hand of the ones doing the works being ordained in the house of the LORD.
2KI 22:10 And Shaphan the scribe reported to the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest gave to me a scroll. And Shaphan read it before the king.
2KI 22:11 And it came to pass, as the king heard the words of the scroll of the law, that he tore his garments.
2KI 22:12 And the king gave charge to Hilkiah the priest, and to Ahikam son of Shaphan, and to Achbor son of Michaiah, and to Shaphan the scribe, and to Asahiah the servant of the king, saying,
2KI 22:13 Go, seek after the LORD for me, and for all my people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this scroll being found! For great is the anger of the LORD burning away against us, for our fathers hearkened not of the words of this scroll, to do according to all the things being written concerning us.
2KI 22:14 And Hilkiah the priest went, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asahiah to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, the keeper of the cloaks. And she dwelt in Jerusalem in Masena. And they spoke to her.
2KI 22:15 And she said to them, Thus says the LORD the God of Israel, Speak to the man sending you to me,
2KI 22:16 Thus says the LORD, Behold, I bring bad things against this place, and against the ones dwelling in it - all the words of the scroll of which the king of Judah read;
2KI 22:17 because they abandoned me, and burned incense to other gods, that they should provoke me to anger in all the works of their hands; that my rage shall burn against this place, and shall not be extinguished.
2KI 22:18 And to the king of Judah sending you to inquire of the LORD, thus you shall say to him, Thus says the LORD God of Israel concerning the words which you heard;
2KI 22:19 for because your heart was tender, and you felt shame in front of me, as you hear as much as I spoke concerning this place, and concerning the ones dwelling it, to be for extinction and for a curse, and you tore your garments, and you wept before me - even indeed I heard, says the LORD.
2KI 22:20 Is it not so? Behold, I add you to your fathers, and you shall be brought into your tomb in peace. And your eyes shall not see all the bad things which I bring against this place. And they returned to the king the word.
2KI 23:1 And the king sent, and brought together to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
2KI 23:2 And the king ascended to the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah, and all the ones dwelling Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people from small and unto great. And he read in their ears all the words of the scroll of the covenant being found in the house of the LORD.
2KI 23:3 And the king stood near the column, and ordained the covenant before the LORD, to go after the LORD, and to guard his commandments, and his testimonies, and his orders with a whole heart, and with a whole life, to raise up the words of this covenant being written in this scroll. And he established all the people in the covenant.
2KI 23:4 And the king gave charge to Hilkiah the great priest, and to the priests being second, and to the ones guarding the doorpost, to bring out from the temple of the LORD all the items which they made to Baal, and to the sacred grove, and to all the military of the heaven. And he incinerated them outside Jerusalem in the plain of Kidron. And he took their dust into Beth-el.
2KI 23:5 And he incinerated the idolatrous priests, of whom the kings of Judah established to burn incense in the high places, and in the cities of Judah, and in the surroundings of Jerusalem, and the ones burning incense to Baal, and to the sun, and to the moon, and to the Mazuroth, and to all the military of the heaven.
2KI 23:6 And he brought forth the sacred grove carving from out of the house of the LORD outside of Jerusalem, unto the rushing stream Kidron, and incinerated it at the rushing stream Kidron, and ground it fine as dust. And he tossed its dust into the tombs of the sons of the people.
2KI 23:7 And he demolished the house of the male prostitutes in the house of the LORD, in which the women wove apparel there for the sacred grove.
2KI 23:8 And he brought in all the priests from out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests were burning incense there - from Geba and unto Beer-sheba, and demolished the high places by the door of the gate of Joshua ruler of the city, of the ones at the left sides of a man at the gate of the city.
2KI 23:9 Only the priests of the high places ascended not to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, for they ate unleavened breads in the midst of their brothers.
2KI 23:10 And he defiled Topheth, the one in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, for a man to not lead his son and his daughter in fire to Molech.
2KI 23:11 And he incinerated the horses which the kings of Judah presented to the sun, in the entrance of the house of the LORD, towards the treasury room of Nathan the eunuch of the king, of the one in the compound. And the chariot of the sun he incinerated by fire.
2KI 23:12 And the altars upon the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah made, and the altars which Manasseh made in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD, the king demolished, and tore down from there, and tossed their dust into the rushing stream Kidron.
2KI 23:13 And the house upon the face of Jerusalem from out of the right of the mount of Mosoath, which Solomon king of Israel built to Ashtoreth the loathsome thing of the Sidonians, and to Chemosh the loathsome thing of Moab, and to Molech the abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.
2KI 23:14 And he broke the monuments, and cut down the sacred groves, and filled their places of bones of men.
2KI 23:15 And indeed the high altar in Beth-el, which Jeroboam son of Nebat made, who led Israel into sin, also indeed he tore down that high altar, and broke its stones, and made them fine into dust, and incinerated the sacred grove.
2KI 23:16 And Josiah turned and saw the tombs of the ones being there in the mount. And he sent and took the bones from out of the tombs, and incinerated them upon the altar, and defiled it, according to the saying of the LORD which the man of God spoke when Jeroboam stood near the altar in the holiday. And turning Josiah lifted his eyes upon the burying-place of the man of God speaking these words.
2KI 23:17 And he said, What is that high rock which I see? And the men of the city said to him, The grave of the man of God coming from out of Judah, and calling these words which you did against the altar in Beth-el.
2KI 23:18 And he said, Let him alone! No one move his bones! And he preserved his bones, with the bones of the prophet having come from out of Samaria.
2KI 23:19 And indeed all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel made to provoke the LORD to anger, Josiah removed, and did to them according to all the works which he did in Beth-el.
2KI 23:20 And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places being there upon the altars, and incinerated the bones of the men upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

2KI 23:22 For there did not take place according to this passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, and in all the days of the kings of Israel, and of the kings of Judah,
2KI 23:23 for only in the eighteenth year of king Josiah this passover to the LORD took place in Jerusalem.
2KI 23:24 And indeed the soothsayers, and the diviners, and the teraphim, and the idols, and all the loathsome things taking place in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, king Josiah removed, that the words of the law should be established, of the ones being written upon the scroll which Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.
2KI 23:25 There was not a king before him likened to him, who turned towards the LORD with his entire heart, and with his entire life, and with his entire strength, according to all the law of Moses; and after him rose up not one like him.
2KI 23:26 Only the LORD did not turn from the great rage of his anger, of which his anger was enraged against Judah, against all the provocations to anger which Manasseh provoked him to anger.
2KI 23:27 And the LORD said, And indeed Judah I shall remove from my face, as I removed Israel, and I will thrust away this city which I chose - Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name will be there.

1CH 10:1 And the Philistines waged war against Israel; and every man of Israel fled from the face of the Philistines, and fell slain in mount Gilboa.
1CH 10:2 And the Philistines pursued after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines struck Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, sons of Saul.
1CH 10:3 And the battle pressed against Saul, and the bowmen found him with the bows, and he was in miseries and suffering pain from the bows.
1CH 10:4 And Saul said to the one carrying his weapons, Unsheathe your broadsword, and stab me with it! lest at any time these uncircumcised come and mock me. But the one carrying his weapons would not; for he feared exceedingly. And Saul took the broadsword, and fell upon it.
1CH 10:5 And the one carrying his weapons beheld that Saul died, and he fell also himself upon his broadsword and died.
1CH 10:6 And Saul died, and his three sons and all his house died in one accord.
1CH 10:7 And every man of Israel in the valley beheld that Israel fled, and that Saul died and his sons, and they left their cities and fled. And the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
1CH 10:8 And it came to pass in the next day, the Philistines came to despoil the slain, and they found Saul and his sons having fallen on mount Gilboa.
1CH 10:9 And they stripped him, and carried away his head, and his weapons. And the Philistines sent to the land round about to announce good news in the houses of their idols, and to their people.
1CH 10:10 And they put his weapons in the house of their god, and his head they pinned in the house of Dagon.
1CH 10:11 And all the ones dwelling in Jabesh Gilead heard all what the Philistines did to Saul and to his sons, and to Israel.
1CH 10:12 And every mighty man from out of Gilead rose up, and they came and took the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, and brought them into Jabesh, and entombed their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
1CH 10:13 And Saul died in his lawless deeds which he acted lawlessly against the LORD; against the word of the LORD, for he did not keep it, and because he asked to inquire by the one who delivers oracles.
1CH 10:14 And he inquired not in the LORD - and he killed him, and turned the kingdom to David son of Jesse.

1CH 11:18 And the three tore up the camp of the Philistines, and drew water from the well of Beth-lehem, which was at the gate, and took it, and came to David. And David wanted not to drink it. And he gave it as a libation to the LORD.
1CH 11:19 And he said, Kindness to me, O God, to do this thing. Shall I drink blood of these men with their lives? For with their lives they brought it, and I do not want to drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

1CH 20:2 And David took the crown of their king from his head, and found the weight of it to be a talent of gold, and on it a valuable stone. And it was upon the head of David. And he brought forth exceedingly much spoils from the city.
1CH 20:3 And the people in it he led out, and sawed through with saws, and with adz of iron, and with threshing machines. And thus David did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David returned and all his people unto Jerusalem.
1CH 20:4 And it came to pass after these things that there was still war in Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbechai the Hushathite struck Sippai of the sons of the giants, and abased him.
1CH 20:5 And came to pass yet again war with the Philistines. And Elhanan son of Jair struck Lahmi brother of Goliath the Gittite; and the wood of his spear was as the beam of a loom of one weaving.
1CH 20:6 And came to pass yet again a war in Gath. And there was an immense man, and his fingers and toes were six by six - twenty and four; and this one was a descendant of the giants.
1CH 20:7 And he berated Israel, and Jonathan the son of Shimea brother of David struck him.
1CH 20:8 These were born to Rapha in Gath; all four were giants; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
1CH 21:1 And Satan rose up against Israel, and stirred up David to count Israel.
1CH 21:2 And king David said to Joab, and to the rulers of the force, Go, count Israel from Beer-sheba unto Dan, and bring it to me, and I shall know their number!
1CH 21:3 And Joab said, May the LORD add unto his people as they are a hundred foldly, and the eyes of my master the king seeing it - are not, O my master, O king, all for bondservants to my master? and why does my master want this - so as to not become for a tresspass to Israel?
1CH 21:4 But the saying of the king prevailed over Joab. And Joab went forth, and went unto all Israel, and went up unto Jerusalem.
1CH 21:5 And Joab gave the number of the numbering of the people to David. And all Israel was a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand men unsheathing the broadsword. And of Judah - four hundred and seventy thousand men unsheathing the broadsword.
1CH 21:6 And Levi and Benjamin were not counted in the midst of them, for the word of the king was disgraceful to Joab.
1CH 21:7 And it was wicked before God concerning this thing, and he struck Israel.
1CH 21:8 And David said to God, I have sinned exceedingly, that I did this thing. And now, remove indeed the iniquity of your servant! for I acted in folly exceedingly.
1CH 21:9 And the LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,
1CH 21:10 Go and speak to David! saying, Thus says the LORD, Three things I will take up upon you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it unto you!
1CH 21:11 And Gad came to David, and said to him, Thus says the LORD, Choose for yourself!
1CH 21:12 Either three years of famine, or three months fleeing from the face of your enemies, with the sword of your enemies pursuing you; or three days of the broadsword of the LORD, and plague in the land, and the angel of the LORD utterly destroying among all the inheritance of Israel. And now, behold, what word should I answer to the one sending me?
1CH 21:13 And David said to Gad, It is narrow exceedingly. I shall fall indeed into the hands of the LORD, for his compassions are exceedingly great; but into the hands of men in no way should I fall.
1CH 21:14 And the LORD appointed plague in Israel. And there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.
1CH 21:15 And God sent an angel into Jerusalem to utterly destroy it. And as he was utterly destroying, the LORD beheld and repented concerning the evil, and said to the angel utterly destroying, Let it be enough to you! Spare your hand! And the angel of the LORD stood at the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
1CH 21:16 And David lifted up his eyes, and beheld the angel of the LORD standing between the earth and between the heaven, and his broadsword being unsheathed in his hand, being stretched out over Jerusalem. And David and the elders wearing sackcloths fell upon their face.
1CH 21:17 And David said to God, Did I not say to count among the people? Then I am the one sinning - in doing evil I did evil. And these sheep, what did they do, O LORD God? Let your hand come against me, and against the house of my father, and not against your people for destruction!
1CH 21:18 And the angel of the LORD told to Gad to say to David that he should ascend to establish an altar to the LORD at the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
1CH 21:19 And David ascended according to the word of Gad, which he spoke in the name of the LORD.
1CH 21:20 And Ornan turned, and beheld the king; and his four sons with him were being hidden. And Ornan was threshing wheat.
1CH 21:21 And David came to Ornan, and Ornan came forth from the threshing-floor. And Ornan looked up, and saw David, and did obeisance to David with the face upon the ground.
1CH 21:22 And David said to Ornan, Give to me the place of the threshing-floor, and I shall build upon it an altar to the LORD! Give it to me for its money's worth, and the calamity shall cease from among the people!
1CH 21:23 And Ornan said to David, Take it for yourself, and let my master the king do what is good before him! Behold, I have given the oxen for a whole burnt offering, and the plow for wood, and the grain for a sacrifice; the whole I have given.
1CH 21:24 And king David said to Ornan, Not so, but only by buying shall I buy of its money's worth; for in no way shall I take the things of yours to the LORD, to offer a whole burnt offering without charge to me to the LORD.
1CH 21:25 And David gave to Ornan for his place six hundred shekels of gold in scale-weight.
1CH 21:26 And David built there an altar to the LORD. And he offered whole burnt offerings, and a deliverance offering, and yelled to the LORD. And he heeded him by fire from out of the heaven on the altar of the whole burnt offering.
1CH 21:27 And the LORD spoke to the angel, and he put away his broadsword into its sheath.
1CH 21:28 In that time when David beheld that the LORD heeded him at the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite, then he sacrificed there.
1CH 21:29 And the tent of the LORD which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of the whole burnt offerings, in that time were in Bama in Gibeon.
1CH 21:30 And David was not able to go before it to seek God, for he hastened from the face of the broadsword of the angel of the LORD.
1CH 22:1 And David said, This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar for the whole burnt offering to Israel.
1CH 22:2 And David said to gather together all the foreigners in the land of Israel. And he placed quarriers to quarry planed stones to build a house to the LORD.
1CH 22:3 And much iron for the nails of the doorways, and of the gates, and of the hinges, David prepared; and brass in multitude - there was not a counting its weight.
1CH 22:4 And there was not a number for the wood of cedars; for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought wood of cedars in multitude to David.
1CH 22:5 And David said, Solomon my son is a tender boy, and the house to be built to the LORD must be to magnify upward, for a name and for glory in all the earth - I shall prepare for it. And David prepared for it in multitude before his decease.
1CH 22:6 And he called Solomon his son, and gave charge to him to build the house to the LORD God of Israel.
1CH 22:7 And David said, Solomon, my child, it was upon my soul to build a house to the name of the LORD my God.
1CH 22:8 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, You poured out blood in multitude, and you made great wars; you shall not build a house to my name, for you poured out much blood upon the earth before me.
1CH 22:9 Behold, a son is born to you, this one will be a man of rest; and I will rest him from all his enemies round about. For Solomon is his name, and peace and rest I shall appoint over Israel in his days.
1CH 22:10 This one shall build a house to my name; and this one shall be to me as a son, and I will be to him for father; and I will prepare the throne of his kingdom in Israel unto the eon.
1CH 22:11 And now, O my son, may the LORD be with you; and you shall prosper, and shall build a house to the LORD your God as he said concerning you.
1CH 22:12 Only may the LORD give to you wisdom and understanding, and strengthen you over Israel, to guard and to observe the law of the LORD your God.
1CH 22:13 Then the way shall prosper, if you should guard to observe the orders and the judgments which the LORD gave charge to Moses for Israel. Be manly and be strong! Fear not nor be timid!
1CH 22:14 And behold, I according to my poorness prepared for the house of the LORD - gold of a hundred thousand talents, and silver of a thousand thousand of talents, and brass, and iron of which there is not a counting the weight; for it is in multitude. And wood and stones I prepared; and you add unto these things!
1CH 22:15 And with you doing the works in multitude are craftsmen, quarriers of stones, and fabricators of wood, and every wise one for every work -
1CH 22:16 in gold, and silver, in brass, and in iron, in which there is not a number. Rise up, and act, and the LORD be with you!
1CH 22:17 And David gave charge to all the rulers of Israel to assist Solomon his son, saying,
1CH 22:18 Is not the LORD with you? And he will give you rest round about, for he delivered up into my hand the ones dwelling the land, and the land is submitted before the LORD, and before his people.
1CH 22:19 Now give your hearts and your souls to seek the LORD your God! And arise, and build the sanctuary to the LORD your God, to carry in the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and the holy items of God, into the house being built to the name of the LORD!
