And they put the holy ark in the house which Solomon son of David the king of Israel built. And the king said, It is not for you to lift anything upon your shoulders. Now then, you officiate to the LORD your God, and to his people Israel!
2CH 35:4 And be prepared according to the houses of your families, and according to your daily rotations, according to the writing of David king of Israel, and by the hand of Solomon his son!
2CH 35:5 And stand in the house according to the divisions of the houses of your families, of your brothers, the sons of the people, and the portion of the house of the family to the Levites!
2CH 35:6 And sacrifice the passover, and prepare the holy things for your brothers, to observe according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses!
2CH 35:7 And Josiah dedicated for the sons of the people - sheep, and lambs, and kids from the sons of the goats, all for the passover, to everyone being found - in number thirty thousand, and three thousand calves. These were of the substance of the king.
2CH 35:8 And his rulers dedicated to the people, and to the priests, and to the Levites; and Helkiah and Zechariah and Jeiel, the rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests for the passover - sheeps and lambs and kids - two thousand and six hundred, and three hundred calves.
2CH 35:9 And Conaniah, and Shemaiah, and Nethaneel his brother, and Hashabiah, and Jehiel, and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, dedicated for the Levites, for the passover - five thousand sheep, and five hundred calves.
2CH 35:10 And the ministration was set up, and the priests stood at their station, and the Levites in their divisions, according to the commandment of the king.
2CH 35:11 And they sacrificed the passover. And the priests poured the blood from out of their hand, and the Levites flayed.
2CH 35:12 And they prepared the whole burnt offering, to deliver them according to the division, according to the houses of the families to the sons of the people, to offer to the LORD, as it is written in the book of Moses. And so it was into the morning.
2CH 35:13 And they roasted the passover in fire according to the ordinance. And the holy pieces they boiled in the brass cauldrons, and in the kettles. And the way prospered, and they ran it to all the sons of the people.
2CH 35:14 And after this they prepared for themselves, and for the priests, (for the priests, the sons of Aaron, in offering of the whole burnt offerings and of the fat,) until night. And the Levites prepared for themselves, and for their brothers the sons of Aaron.
2CH 35:15 And the psalm singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station, according to the commands of David, Asaph, and Heman, and Jeduthun, of the prophets of the king; and the rulers, and the gatekeepers, gate by gate. It was not for them to move from their ministration, for their brothers the Levites prepared for them.
2CH 35:16 And all the ministration of the LORD was set up in that day, to observe the passover, and to offer the whole burnt offerings upon the altar of the LORD, according to the command of king Josiah.
2CH 35:17 And the sons of Israel being found present observed the passover at that time, and the holiday of the unleavened breads for seven days.
2CH 35:18 And there was not a passover likened to it in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; for all kings of Israel did not do the passover which Josiah did (and the priests, and the Levites, and all Judah and Israel being found, and the ones dwelling in Jerusalem) to the LORD.
2CH 35:19 In the eighteenth year of the kingdom of Josiah this passover was observed.
2CH 35:20 And after all these things which Josiah prepared for the house, Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt ascended up against the king of the Assyrians at the river Euphrates, to wage war against him at Carchemish. And king Josiah went to meet against him.
2CH 35:21 And he sent to him messengers, saying, What is it to me and to you, O king of Judah? I come not against you today to make war, but only against the place of my war; and God told me to hasten. You take heed of the God with me, lest he ruin you.
2CH 35:22 And Josiah did not turn his face from him, but he fortified himself to wage war against him. And he hearkened not concerning the words of Pharaoh Necho by the mouth of God. And he came to wage war in the plain of Megiddo.
2CH 35:23 And the bowmen shot unto king Josiah; and the king said to his servants, Lead me out, for I am in pain exceedingly!
2CH 35:24 And his servants led him from the chariot, and hauled him upon the second chariot which was his. And they led him to Jerusalem, and he died, and was entombed with his fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned over Josiah.
2CH 35:25 And Jeremiah lamented over Josiah. And all the rulers and the ones in control spoke a lamentation over Josiah spoken until today. And they appointed it for an order unto Israel. And behold, it is written in the lamentations.
2CH 35:26 And the rest of the words of Josiah and his hope were being written in the law of the LORD.
2CH 35:27 And his words, the first and the last, behold, they are written upon the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.
2CH 36:1 And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, and anointed him, and placed him as king instead of his father in Jerusalem.
2CH 36:2 Jehoahaz was a son being twenty and three years old in his taking reign, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem.
2CH 36:3 And the king of Egypt removed him to not give reign to him in Jerusalem; and put a tribute upon the land of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
2CH 36:4 And the king of Egypt placed Eliakim son of Josiah as king over Judah and Jerusalem, and converted his name to Jehoiakim. And Pharaoh Necho took Jehoahaz his brother, and brought him to Egypt.
2CH 36:5 Jehoiakim was a son being twenty and five years old in his taking reign, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem. And he acted wickedly before the LORD.
2CH 36:6 And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon ascended against him, and bound him in brass shackles, and took him into Babylon.
2CH 36:7 And part of the items of the house of the LORD he carried away unto Babylon, and put them in his temple in Babylon.
2CH 36:8 And the rest of the words of Jehoiakim, and all which he did, behold, these are written in the scroll of the words of the days of the kings of Israel and of Judah. And Jehoiachin his son reigned instead of him.
2CH 36:9 Jehoiachin was a son being eight years old in his taking reign, and three months and ten days he reigned in Jerusalem. And he acted wickedly before the LORD.
2CH 36:10 And at the turn of the year king Nebuchadnezzar sent and brougnt him unto Babylon, with the desirable items of the house of the LORD. And Zedekiah the brother of his father reigned over Judah and Jerusalem.
2CH 36:11 Zedekiah was a son being twenty one years old in his taking reign, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem.
2CH 36:12 And he did the wicked thing before the LORD his God. And he did not feel shame from in front of Jeremiah the prophet, and from the mouth of the LORD,
2CH 36:13 in the annulling the things with king Nebuchadnezzar, in which he bound him by an oath according to God. And he hardened his neck, and he strengthened his heart to not return to the LORD God of Israel.
2CH 36:14 And all the honorable men of Judah, and the priests, and the people of the land multiplied to disregard by disregardings according to the abominations of the nations; and they defiled the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
2CH 36:15 And the LORD God of their fathers sent out to them by the hand of his prophets, ones rising up early, even sending his messengers; for he was sparing his people, and his sanctuary.
2CH 36:16 And they were sneering at his messengers, and treating with contempt his words, and mocking among his prophets, until the rage of the LORD ascended among his people, until there was not a cure.
2CH 36:17 And he led against them the king of the Chaldeans. And he killed their young men by the broadsword in the house of his sanctuary, and spared not the young men; and their virgins he did not show mercy on, and their elders he took away - the whole he delivered up into their hands.
2CH 36:18 And all the items of the house of God, the great and the small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD, and all the treasures of the king, and of the great men - the whole he carried unto Babylon.
2CH 36:19 And he burnt the house of the LORD, and razed the wall of Jerusalem; and its palaces he burnt by fire, and every beautiful item he appointed for extinction.
2CH 36:20 And he resettled the remaining ones in Babylon; and they were to him and his sons for menservants until the kingdom of the Medes,
2CH 36:21 to fulfill the word of the LORD through the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land favorably receives its sabbaths - by observing the sabbath all the days of its desolation, to observe the sabbath in the fulfillment of seventy years.
2CH 36:22 In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, after the fulfillment of the saying of the LORD through the mouth of Jeremiah, the LORD awakened the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians. And he exhorted to proclaim in all his kingdom in written words, saying,
2CH 36:23 Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians, To all the kingdoms of the earth the LORD God of the heaven gave to me. And he gave charge to me to build to him a house in Jerusalem in Judea. Who is there of you from out of all his people? The LORD his God will be with him - let him ascend!

EZR 3:1 And the seventh month came, and the sons of Israel were in their cities, and the people were brought together as one man unto Jerusalem.
EZR 3:2 And Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brothers, and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer upon it whole burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses the man of God.
EZR 3:3 And they prepared the altar upon its preparation place; but terror was upon them because of the peoples of the lands. And they brougnt unto it the whole burnt offerings to the LORD in the morning and in the evening.
EZR 3:4 And they observed the holiday of the tents, according to the thing being written, and the whole burnt offerings day by day in number, according to the distinguishing manner, reckoning day by day for it.
EZR 3:5 And after this the perpetual whole burnt offering, and for the new moons, and for all holidays to the LORD were sanctified, and to every willing voluntary offering to the LORD.
EZR 3:6 On day one of the seventh month they began to offer whole burnt offerings to the LORD. But the house of the LORD was not laid of a foundation.
EZR 3:7 And they gave money to the quarriers, and to the fabricators; and food, and drink, and olive oil to the Sidonians, and to the Tyrians, to bring forth wood of cedars from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, by the grant of Cyrus king of the Persians, concerning this.
EZR 3:8 And in the second year of their coming into the house of the LORD God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel began, and with Jeshua the son of Jozadek, and the rest of their brothers, the priests, and the Levites, and all the ones coming from the captivity into Jerusalem; that they established the Levites from twenty years and up, to bring success upon the ones doing the works in the house of the LORD.
EZR 3:9 And Jeshua stood with his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, over the ones doing the works in the house of God; the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers the Levites.
EZR 3:10 And the ones building laid a foundation to build the house of the LORD, and the priests stood being robed with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD, by the hands of David king of Israel.
EZR 3:11 And they answered in praise and confession to the LORD, saying, That he is good, that into the eon is his mercy upon Israel. And all the people shouted a great voice, in the praising the LORD, at the groundwork of the house of the LORD.
EZR 3:12 And many from the priests, and the Levites, and rulers of the families, the elders who beheld the first house on its groundwork, and then this house, with their eyes, wept a great sound, and many with a shout with gladness to raise up high a sound.
EZR 3:13 And the people were not recognizing the sound of the cheering of gladness from the sound of the weeping of the people; for the people cried out with a great sound, and the voice was heard even from far off.
EZR 4:1 And the ones afflicting Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the resettlement were building a house to the LORD God of Israel.
EZR 4:2 And they approached to Zerubbabel, and to the rulers of the families, and said to them, We should build with you, for as you, we also inquire to your God; and to him we sacrifice from the days of Esar-haddon king of Assyria, the one bringing us here.
EZR 4:3 And Zerubbabel said to them, and Jeshua, and the rest of the rulers of the families of Israel, It is not for us and you to build a house to our God, for we ourselves together shall build to the LORD God of Israel, as Cyrus the king of the Persians gave charge to us.
EZR 4:4 And the people of the land were enfeebling the hands of the people of Judah, and impeded them to build.
EZR 4:5 And they were hiring against them counselors to efface their counsel all the days of Cyrus king of the Persians, and unto the kingdom of Darius the king of the Persians.
EZR 4:6 And in the kingdom of Ahasuerus, and in the beginning of his kingdom, they wrote a letter against the ones living in Judah and Jerusalem.
EZR 4:7 And in the days of Artaxerxes Mithridath wrote in peace, and Tabeel, with the rest of his fellow-servants, to Artaxerxes king of the Persians, saying, The tribute-gatherer wrote the writing in Syrian, and it was being translated.
EZR 4:8 Rehum the master, and Shimshai the scribe, wrote one letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king, saying,
EZR 4:9 Thus Rehum the master judges, and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of our fellow-servants, the Dinaites, Apharsathchites, Tarpelites, Apharsites, Archevites, Babylonians, Susanchites, Dehavites, Elamites,
EZR 4:10 and the rest of the nations whom the great and the esteemed Asnapper resettled, and settled them in the cities of Samaria, and the rest on the other side of the river.
EZR 4:11 This is the disposition of the letter which they sent to him - To Artaxerxes the king. By your servants the men on the other side of the river.
EZR 4:12 And now let it be made known to the king that the Jews ascending from you to us came into Jerusalem, the defecting and wicked city, which they are building; and the walls of it are being readied, and the foundations of it they elevated.
EZR 4:13 Now then let it be made known to the king, that, if that city should be rebuilt, and the walls of it should be readied, that tributes, toll, and custom they shall not give, and this does evil to kings!
EZR 4:14 And now we salted not as salt of the temple, and it is not allowed for us to behold an indecency concerning the king; on account of this we sent forth and made known to the king,
EZR 4:15 that it should be examined in the book of memoirs of your fathers. And you shall find in the book of the memorial, and shall know that that city is a defecting city, and one doing evil to kings; and in the midst of it from the time of the eon it is for places and flights for your runaway bondmen. On account of this this city was made desolate.
EZR 4:16 We make known then ourselves to the king, that if that city should be built, and its walls should be readied for these things, there shall not be to you a part on the other side of the river.
EZR 4:17 And this then is the word which the king sent to Rehum the master, and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their fellow-servants living in Samaria, and the rest on the other side of the river, saying, Peace. And says the king,
EZR 4:18 The tribute-gatherer whom you sent to us was called before me.
EZR 4:19 And by me was rendered a decree, and they examined and it was found that that city from days of the eon lifts itself up against kings, and defections and exiles take place in it.
EZR 4:20 And strong kings were over Jerusalem, prevailing over all of the other side of the river. And both tributes and tolls and customs were given to them.
EZR 4:21 And now establish a decree for those men to cease work, that that city shall not be built up any more!
EZR 4:22 So that of the decree you were guarding you not be remiss to do concerning this, lest at any time an extinction of power should be multiplied for an evil deed to happen to kings.
EZR 4:23 Then the tribute-gatherer of king Artaxerxes read in the presence of Rehum the master, and Shimshai the scribe, and his fellow-servants. And they went with diligence unto Jerusalem and to Judah, and caused them to cease work with horses and a force.
EZR 4:24 Then the work of the house of God was idle, in Jerusalem. And it was idle until the second year of the kingdom of Darius king of Persia.

EZR 5:3 At that same time there came upon them Tatnai chief ruler on the other side of the river, and Shethar-boznai, and their fellow-servants, and of such he said to them, Who ordained to you a decree to build this house, and to ready this expense?
EZR 5:4 Then they said to them, What are the names of the men building this city?
EZR 5:5 But the eyes of God became upon the captivity of Judah, and they did not cause them to cease work until the decree was carried to Darius. And then it was given to the tribute-gatherer concerning this.

EZR 5:7 They sent a word to him, and thus was written in it, To Darius the king, all peace.
EZR 5:8 Let it be known to the king! That we went into Judea, the place for the house of the great God, and it is being built with the choice stones, and timber is inserted in the walls, and that work is fittingly done, and the way is prospering in their hands.
EZR 5:9 Then we asked those elders, and thus we said to them, Who rendered to you a decree to build this house, and the bestowing of this expense to ready it?
EZR 5:10 And we asked of them their names to make known to you, so as to write to you the names of the men of their rulers.
EZR 5:11 And such a word they answered to us, saying to us, We are menservants of the God of the heaven and of the earth, and we are building the house which was built many years before this, and a great king of Israel built it, and readied it for themselves.
EZR 5:12 But from when our fathers provoked to anger the God of heaven, he gave them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, and this house he caused to rest, and the people he resettled in Babylon.
EZR 5:13 But in the first year of Cyrus the king of the Babylonians, Cyrus the king rendered a decree to build this house of God.
EZR 5:14 And the items of the house of God of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar brought forth from the house in Jerusalem, and carried them into the temple of the king in Babylon, Cyrus the king brought them forth from the temple in Babylon, and gave them to Sheshbazzar the treasurer - to the one over the treasury.
EZR 5:15 And he said to him, These items take, and go put them in the house in Jerusalem! And the house of God - let it be built in its place!
EZR 5:16 Then that Sheshbazzar came and put down the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem. And from then until now it is being built, and was not finished.
EZR 5:17 And now if for the king it seems good, let it be overseen in the house of the treasury of the king there in Babylon, so as you should know that if from king Cyrus a decree was rendered to build the house of God, that one in Jerusalem! And the king knowing concerning this, let him send forth a reply to us!
EZR 6:1 Then Darius the king rendered a decree, and examined in the libraries, of which the treasuries were situated there in Babylon.
EZR 6:2 And there was found in Achmetha the city, in the palace of the Mede city, one chapter of a scroll, and this was the record written in it.
EZR 6:3 In the first year of king Cyrus, Cyrus the king rendered a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem, saying, Let the house be built, and the place of which they sacrifice the sacrifices! And set the foundations, the height of sixty cubits, and the width of it sixty cubits,
EZR 6:4 and three layers of fortified stones, and one layer of new timbers! And the expense shall be granted out of the house of the king.
EZR 6:5 And the items of the house of God of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar brought forth from the house in Jerusalem, and carried into Babylon, even let them be given, and brought forth into the temple in Jerusalem, unto their place, and be put in the house of God!
EZR 6:6 Now then Tatnai, commandant of the other side of the river, Shethar-boznai, and his fellow-servants the Apharsachites on the other side of the river, be being far from there.
EZR 6:7 And now leave alone the work of the house of God, and the ones guiding of the Jews, and the elders of the Jews. Let them build that house of God upon its place!
EZR 6:8 And by me was rendered a decree to do through the elders of those Jews to build that house of God, even from the subsistence of the king, of the tributes on the other side of the river, that carefully an expense be given to those men to not cease work!
EZR 6:9 And what ever deficiency - both male offspring of oxen, and rams, and lambs for whole burnt offerings to the God of the heaven, and wheat, salt, wine, olive oil, according to the word of the priests in Jerusalem, let be given to them day by day unalterable what ever they should ask!
EZR 6:10 That there might be a pleasant aroma offering to the God of the heaven, and they might pray for the life of the king, and the ones of his sons.
EZR 6:11 And from me was rendered a decree, that every man who ever changes this word the timber of his house shall be demolished, and a stake being straight up he shall be pitched upon it, and his house will be for ravaging.
EZR 6:12 And the God of whom encamps with his name there, he shall eradicate every king and people who should stretch out his hand to change and remove from view the house of God, that one in Jerusalem. I Darius rendered the decree. Carefully let it become!
EZR 6:13 Then Tatnai, the chief ruler on the other side of the river, and Shethar-boznai, and his fellow-servants, in so far as Darius the king sent, thus they did carefully.
EZR 6:14 And the elders of the Jews built, and prospered at the prophecy of Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah son of Iddo. And they rebuilt, and made ready by the decree of the God of Israel, and by the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes kings of Persia.
EZR 6:15 And they finished this house by the third day of the month Adar, which is in the sixth year of the kingship of Darius the king.
EZR 6:16 And they made, (the sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites, and the rest of the sons of the resettlement), a holiday of rededication of the house of God with gladness.
EZR 6:17 And they offered for the holiday of rededication of this house of God; calves - a hundred; rams - two hundred; lambs - four hundred; winter yearlings of the goats for a sin offering for all Israel - twelve, for the number of the tribes of Israel.
EZR 6:18 And they established the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their distributions, for service of the house of God in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
EZR 6:19 And the sons of the resettlement observed the passover on the fourteenth of the first month.
EZR 6:20 For the priests and the Levites were purified - all were clean as one man. And they slew the passover for all the sons of the resettlement, and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
EZR 6:21 And the sons of Israel ate the passover - the ones coming forth from the resettlement, and every one separating of the uncleanness of the nations of the land that was theirs to inquire of the LORD God of Israel.
EZR 6:22 And they observed the holiday of the unleavened breads seven days with gladness. For the LORD gladdened them, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to fortify their hands in the works of the house of the God of Israel.
EZR 7:1 And after these things, in the kingdom of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, there ascended Ezra the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
EZR 7:2 son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
EZR 7:3 son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
EZR 7:4 son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
EZR 7:5 son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the foremost priest.
EZR 7:6 This Ezra ascended from out of Babylon; and he was a quick skilled scribe. in the law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel gave. And the king gave to him - for the hand of the LORD his God was upon him in all things which he sought.
EZR 7:7 And there ascended some from the sons of Israel, and from the priests, and from the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim, to Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
EZR 7:8 And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, this was the seventh year of the king.
EZR 7:9 For on day one of the first month he founded the expedition from Babylon, and during the first day of the fifth month he came into Jerusalem, for the hand of his God was good upon him.
EZR 7:10 For Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do, and to teach in Israel the orders and judgments.
EZR 7:11 And this is the copy of the edict which Artaxerxes the king gave to Ezra the priest, to the scribe, of the scroll of the words of the commandments of the LORD, and of his orders unto Israel.
EZR 7:12 Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Let the matter and the answer be initiated.
EZR 7:13 From me was rendered a decree that all the ones willing in my kingdom from the people of Israel, and priests, and Levites, to go to Jerusalem, with you let them go!
EZR 7:14 In so far as from in front of the king, and of his seven counselors, one should be sent to look about over Judea and Jerusalem, and in the law of their God in your hand;
EZR 7:15 to carry away even silver and gold for the house of the LORD, which the king and the counselors were willing to give to the God of Israel inhabiting in Jerusalem.
EZR 7:16 And all the silver and gold, whatever you should find in every place of Babylon, let it be offered with a voluntary offering of the people, and of the priests, willing to give for the house of God in Jerusalem.
EZR 7:17 And every one going you arrange this readily by this scroll - calves, rams, lambs, and their sacrifice offerings, and their libation offerings! And you shall offer them upon the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
EZR 7:18 And if anything should seem good with you and your brothers, with the rest of the silver and gold to do, as it pleases your God, you do it!
EZR 7:19 And the items given to you for the ministration of the house of God, you deliver before God in Jerusalem!
EZR 7:20 And for the rest of the need of the house of your God, what ever should be apparent to you to give, you shall give from the houses of the king's treasury.
EZR 7:21 I, Artaxerxes the king, established a decree to all the treasuries on the other side of the river, that all what ever he should ask of you (Ezra the priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven) readily, let it become so!
EZR 7:22 Unto a hundred talents of silver, and unto a hundred cors of wheat, and unto a hundred baths of wine, and unto a hundred baths of olive oil, and salt of which the amount is not on record.
EZR 7:23 All what is in the decree of the God of the heaven, let it become in the house of the God of the heaven! Take heed, lest any make an attempt against the house of the God of the heaven, lest at any time anger should happen upon the kingdom of the king, and his sons!
EZR 7:24 And to you, let it be made known in respect to all the priests, and to the Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and ministers of the house of God, that this tribute, and toll, and impost, you do not have authority to assign upon them!
EZR 7:25 And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of God, the wisdom in your hand, ordain scribes and judges, that they might judge all the people on the other side of the river, to all the ones knowing the laws of your God! And to the ones not knowing you shall make it known.
EZR 7:26 And all, who ever might not be observing the law of God, and the law of the king diligently, the judgment will be taken upon him, whether for death, whether to root him out, or to instruct, or to penalize the subsistance, or for prison to lock up.
EZR 7:27 Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers, who put it in the heart of the king thus, to glorify the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
EZR 7:28 And upon me mercy leaned in the eyes of the king, and his counselors, and all the rulers of the king of the mighty ones. And I was strengthened by the good hand of the LORD my God upon me, and I gathered from Israel rulers to ascend with me.

EZR 8:17 And I gave charge to them to Iddo the ruler of Casiphia of the place. And I put in their mouths words to speak to Iddo, and to their brothers of the Nethinim, of the ones with the money of the place Casiphia, to bring to us ministers and singers into the house of our God.
EZR 8:18 And they came to us as the good hand of our God was upon us, with a discerning man from the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi of Israel; and Sherebiah, and his sons, and his brothers - eighteen;
EZR 8:19 and Hashabiah, and Jeshaiah from the sons of Merari, his brothers and his sons - twenty.
EZR 8:20 And from the Nethinim, whom David appointed and the rulers for service of the Levites - two hundred twenty Nethinim. All these were named.
EZR 8:21 And I called there a fast at the river Ahava, to humble ourselves before our God, to seek by him a straight way for us, and for our children, and for all our property.
EZR 8:22 For I was ashamed to ask from the king for a force and horsemen to deliver us from the enemy in the way, for we said to the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all the ones seeking him for good; and his might and his rage is upon all the ones abandoning him.
EZR 8:23 And we fasted and sought from our God concerning this, and he heeded us.
EZR 8:24 And I separated twelve of the rulers of the priests; to Sherebiah, to Hashabiah, and with them from their brothers - ten.
EZR 8:25 And I set before them the silver, and the gold, and the items of the first-fruit of the house of our God which the king separated in dedication and his counselors, and his rulers, and all the ones being found of Israel.
EZR 8:26 And I set in their hands silver - six hundred fifty talents, and vessels made of silver - a hundred, and talents of gold - a hundred;
EZR 8:27 and twenty bowls of gold of a thousand drachmas, and vessels of brass, shining, good quality, diverse, desirable as gold.
EZR 8:28 And I said to them, You are holy to the LORD God; and the holy vessels, and the silver, and the gold are a voluntary offering to the LORD God of our fathers.
EZR 8:29 Be awake, and give heed! until you set them before the rulers of the priests and the Levites, and rulers of the families of Israel, in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD.
EZR 8:30 And the priests and the Levites took the weight of the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, to bring them into Jerusalem into the house of our God.
EZR 8:31 And we lifted away from the river Ahava on the twelfth of the first month, to come unto Jerusalem. And the hand of our God was upon us, and he rescued us from the hand of the enemy, and the warlike people along the way.
EZR 8:32 And we came into Jerusalem, and stayed there three days.
EZR 8:33 And on the fourth day we set the silver and the gold and the vessels in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest; and with him was Eleazar son of Phinehas; and with them was Jozabad son of Jeshua, and Noadiah son of Binnui - the Levites.

The whole amount was for whole burnt offerings to the LORD.

EZR 9:1 And as these things were finished, the rulers approached to me, saying, The people of Israel did not separate, and the priests and the Levites, from the peoples of the lands in their abominations - of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, and the Moserite, and the Amorite.
EZR 9:2 For they took of their daughters to themselves, and to their sons, and the holy seed mixed together among the peoples of the lands; even by the hand of the rulers and of the commandants in this breach-of-contract in rule.
EZR 9:3 And as I heard this word, I tore my garments and my undergarment, and was agitated, and plucked the hair of my head, and of my beard, and sat down for calming.
EZR 9:4 And there gathered to me everyone trembling at the word of the God of Israel concerning the breach-of-contract of the resettlement. And I was sitting calming myself until the evening sacrifice.
EZR 9:5 And during the evening sacrifice I rose up from my humiliation; and in my tearing my garments, and my undergarment, that I leaned upon my knees, and spread forth my hands to the LORD my God.
EZR 9:6 And I said, O LORD, I am ashamed and feel shame to raise up, O my God, my face to you; for our lawlessnesses multiplied over our head, and our trespasses are magnified unto the heaven.
EZR 9:7 From the days of our fathers we are in great trespass until this day. And in our lawless deeds we were delivered up, and our kings, and our priests, into the hand of the kings of the nations, by broadsword, and into captivity, and in seizure, and in shame of our face, as this day.
EZR 9:8 And now as the LORD our God was lenient to us a little, to leave us for deliverance, and to give to us reliance in the place of his sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes, and to give a little restoration to life in our servitude,
EZR 9:9 for we are servants, and in our servitude the LORD our God did not abandon us, and leaned mercy towards us before the kings of the Persians, to give us a restoring to life, for them to exalt the house of our God, and to reestablish its deserted places, and to give to us a fence in Judah and Jerusalem,
EZR 9:10 that now, what should we say, O our God, after this? For we abandoned your commandments,
EZR 9:11 which you gave to us by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying, The land into which you enter there to inherit it is a land in motion by the removal of the peoples of the lands of their abominations which they filled it from mouth to mouth gate to gate. in their uncleannesses.
EZR 9:12 And now, do not give your daughters to their sons, and of their daughters do not take to your sons; and do not require their peace and their good will into the eon, so as you should grow in strength, and should eat the good of the land, and allot it to your sons unto the eon!
EZR 9:13 And after all the things coming upon us by our actions in the wicked things, and by our great trespasses, (that you our God lightened our lawless deeds, and gave to us deliverance;)
EZR 9:14 for we turned to efface your commandments, and allied by marriage to the peoples of the these lands, you should not be provoked by us unto consumption, for their to not be one left over and preserved.
EZR 9:15 O LORD God of Israel, You are just, for we were left being preserved as in this day. Behold, we all are before you in our trespasses; for there is not a standing before you in this.
EZR 10:1 And as Ezra prayed. And as he confessed weeping and falling before the house of God, there came together to him from Israel an exceedingly vast assembly, of men and women and young people; for the people wept a great weeping.
EZR 10:2 And answered one Shechaniah son of Jehiel, from the sons of Elam, and said to Ezra, We broke contract with our God, and settled with alien wives from the peoples of the land; and now there is hope to Israel for this thing.
EZR 10:3 And now, we should ordain a covenant with our God to lead out all the wives and the ones being born from them, according to counsel of the LORD, and of the ones trembling in the commandments of our God; and let it be according to the law!
EZR 10:4 Rise up, for the matter concerns you, and we are with you - strengthen and do!
EZR 10:5 And Ezra rose up, and bound by an oath the rulers of the priests, and Levites, and all Israel, to do according to this word. And they swore by an oath.
EZR 10:6 And Ezra rose up from in front of the house of God, and went into the treasury of Johanan son of Eliashib, and lodged there, and did not eat bread, and did not drink water, for he mourned over the breach-of-contract by the resettlement.
EZR 10:7 And they carried about a report in Judah and in Jerusalem to all the sons of the resettlement, to gather together in Jerusalem, saying,

EZR 10:12 And answered all the assembly with a great voice, and said, According to your words which you said, thus we will do.
EZR 10:13 But the people are vast, and it is the time of winter, and there is not ability to stand outside, and the work is not for one day, nor two; for we multiplied the wrong in this matter.
EZR 10:14 Let indeed our rulers stand in every assembly, and to all the ones in our cities who settled with alien wives, let come at arranged times, and with them the elders city by city, and judges, to turn the anger of the rage of our God from us, on account of this matter!

NEH 1:1 The words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah. And it came to pass in the month of Chisleu, of the twentieth year, that I was in Susa Abira.
NEH 1:2 And there came Hanani one of my brothers, he and men of Judah. And I asked them concerning the Jews having survived, who were left behind from the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
NEH 1:3 And they said to me, The ones remaining behind surviving from the captivity there in the place are among great wickedness, and in scorning; and the walls of Jerusalem are being demolished, and its gates were burnt by fire.
NEH 1:4 And it came to pass, in my hearing these words, I sat and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
NEH 1:5 And I said, O indeed, O LORD God of the heaven, the strong and great and fearful one, guarding the covenant and the mercy to the ones loving him and guarding his commandments.
NEH 1:6 Let it be indeed your ear heeds, and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant which I pray before you today's day and night, for the sons of Israel your servants! And I declare openly concerning the sins of the sons of Israel, in which we sinned against you - both I and the house of my father sinned.
NEH 1:7 In parting, we parted from you, and guarded not the commandments, and the orders, and the judgments which you gave charge to Moses your servant.
NEH 1:8 Remember indeed, the word which you gave charge to Moses your servant! saying, If You should break contract, I will disperse you among the peoples.
NEH 1:9 But if you should return to me, and should guard my commandments, and observe them; and if your dispersion might be unto the tip of the heaven, from there I will gather them, and I will bring them into the place which I chose to encamp my name there.
NEH 1:10 And they are your children and your people, whom you ransomed by your great power, and by your fortified hand.
NEH 1:11 Indeed, O LORD, let be your ear heeding to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your children wanting to fear your name! And prosper the way indeed of your servant today, and give him for compassions before this man! And I was a wine server to the king.
NEH 2:1 And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that the wine was before him. And I took the wine, and gave it to the king, and there was not another before him.
NEH 2:2 And the king said to me, Why is your face in a sorry state, and you are not content? For is this not unless there is a sorrowful heart. And I was afraid exceedingly much.
NEH 2:3 And I said to the king, O king, Live into the eon! Why should not my face be sorry, for the city, the house of the sepulchres of my fathers was made desolate, and its gates were devoured by fire?
NEH 2:4 And the king said to me, For what is this you seek? And I prayed to the LORD God of heaven.
NEH 2:5 And I said to the king, If it be upon the king for good, and if your servant shall seem good before you, so as to send him to Judah, to the city of the sepulchres of my fathers, then I will rebuild it.
NEH 2:6 And the king said to me, and his concubine sitting next to him, For how long will you be going, and when will you return? And it was good before the king. And he sent me, and I gave to him a confirmation.
NEH 2:7 And I said to the king, If it be upon the king for good, let him give to me letters to the chief rulers on the other side of the river! So as to allow me to pass until I come unto Judah;
NEH 2:8 and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the garden, which is to the king, so as to give to me wood to roof the gates of the palace of the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house, for which I shall enter unto it. And the king gave to me by the good hand of God upon me.
NEH 2:9 And I came to the chief rulers on the other side of the river, and gave to them the letters of the king. And the king sent with me chiefs of the force, and horsemen.
NEH 2:10 And Sanballat the Horonite heard of it, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and it was a bad thing to them that it happened. And they were grieved that a man comes to seek good to the sons of Israel.
NEH 2:11 And I came unto Jerusalem, and I was there three days.
NEH 2:12 And I rose up at night, I and a few men with me. And I reported not to a man, for God put it into my heart to do this with Jerusalem. And there is not a beast with me, except the beast which I mounted upon it.
NEH 2:13 And I went forth through the gate of Gai at night to the mouth of the spring of the dragon, and to the dung gate. And I was studying the walls of Jerusalem having been torn down, and her gates having been consumed by fire.
NEH 2:14 And I went by the gate of the fountain, and into the pool of the king. And there was not a place for the beast underneath me to pass.
NEH 2:15 And I was ascending by the rushing stream at night, and was studying the wall, and was at the gate of the ravine, and I returned.
NEH 2:16 And the ones guarding did not know why I went, and what I was doing. And to the Jews, and to the priests, and to the important ones, and to the commandants, and to the rest of the ones doing the works until then, I reported not.
NEH 2:17 Then I said to them, You see this wickedness in which we are in it, how Jerusalem is desolate, and its gates were given to fire. Come, and let us build throughout the wall of Jerusalem, and we shall not be any longer for scorn!
NEH 2:18 And I reported to them the hand of God which is good upon me, and the words of the king which he spoke to me. And they said, Let us arise and build! And their hands were fortified for the good.
NEH 2:19 And Sanaballat the Horonite heard, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, and they laughed out loud at us, and disdained us. And they said, What is this thing which you are doing? or is it that you are defecting against the king?
NEH 2:20 And I returned to them a word, and said to them, The God of heaven, he shall prosper the way for us. And we his servants are pure, and we shall arise and build; and to you there is not a portion, nor judicial right, nor a memorial in Jerusalem.
NEH 3:1 And Eliashib the great priest rose up and his brothers the priests and constructed the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and set its doors; even unto the tower of the hundred they sanctified it, unto the tower of Hananeel.
NEH 3:2 And near his hands men of Jericho constructed. And near his hands Zaccur son of Imri constructed.
NEH 3:3 And the sons of Hassenaah constructed the fish gate - they roofed it, and set its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
NEH 3:4 And near their hands Maremoth took control, the son of Urijah, son of Kos. And near their hand Meshullam took control, son of Barechiah, son of Meshezabeel. And near their hand Zadok took control, son of Baana.
NEH 3:5 And near their hand the Tekoites took control; but their strong ones did not insert their neck into a service of their Lord.
NEH 3:6 And the gate of Jasanah Jehoiada son of Paseah repaired, and Meshullam son of Bosodeiah - they roofed it, and set its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
NEH 3:7 And near their hand Melatiah repaired, the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon, and of Mizpah, unto the throne of the ruler of the other side of the river.
NEH 3:8 And near their hand Uzziel repaired, son of Harhaiah of the refiners. And near his hand Hananiah repaired, son of the perfumers, and they established Jerusalem unto the broad wall.
NEH 3:9 And near their hand Rephaiah repaired, son of Hur, ruler of half of the place round about Jerusalem.
NEH 3:10 And near their hand Jedaiah repaired, son of Harumaph, even against his house. And near his hand Hattush repaired, son of Hashabniah.
NEH 3:11 And Malchijah son of Harim and Hashub son of Pahath-moab repaired a second measured section, even unto the tower of the furnaces.
NEH 3:12 And near his hand Shallum repaired, son of Halohesh, ruler of half the place round about Jerusalem, he and his daughters.
NEH 3:13 The gate of the ravine Hanun repaired, and the ones dwelling at Zanoah - they constructed it, and set its doors, and its bolts, and its bars, and a thousand cubits of the wall unto the dung gate.
NEH 3:14 And the dung gate Malchiah repaired, son of Rechab, ruler of a place round about the house of Beth-haccerem, he and his sons. And they sheltered it, and set its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
NEH 3:15 And the gate of the spring was safeguarded by Shallum son of Colhozeh, ruler of part of Mizpah; he built it, and roofed it, and set its doors, and its bars, and the wall of the pool of Siloah by the garden of the king, and unto the stairways going down from the city of David.
NEH 3:16 After him Nehemiah repaired, son of Azbuk, ruler of half the place round about Beth-zur, unto the garden of the burying-place of David, and unto the pool being built, and unto the house of the mighty ones.
NEH 3:17 After him the Levites repaired, Rehum son of Bani. Near his hand Hashabiah repaired, ruler of half the place round about Keilah, in the place round about him.
NEH 3:18 And after him their brothers repaired, Bavai son of Henadad, ruler of half the place round about Keilah.
NEH 3:19 And repaired near his hand Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, a second measured section right opposite the ascending unto the weapons site joining together at the corner.
NEH 3:20 After him Baruch repaired, son of Zabbai, a second measured section, from the corner unto the door of the house of Eliashib the great priest.
NEH 3:21 And after him Meramoth repaired, son of Uriah, son of Kos a second measured section, from the door of the house of Eliashib unto the completion of the house of Eliashib.
NEH 3:22 And after him the priests repaired, the men of Ekchechar.
NEH 3:23 And after him Benjamin repaired and Hashub over against their house. And after them Azariah repaired, son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, next to his house.
NEH 3:24 And after him Binnui repaired, son of Henadad, a second measured section, from the house of Azariah unto the corner, and unto the curve.
NEH 3:25 Palal, son of Uzai, was right opposite the corner, and the tower protruding from out of the house of the king, higher than the courtyard of the prison. And after him Pedaiah son of Parosh.
NEH 3:26 And the Nethinim were living in Ophel, unto before the garden of the water gate to the east, and the protruding tower.
NEH 3:27 And after him the Tekoites repaired a second measured section, right opposite the great protruding tower, and unto the wall of Ophel.
NEH 3:28 Upward of the gate of the horses the priests repaired, every man right opposite his own house.
NEH 3:29 And after him Zadok repaired, son of Immer, right opposite his own house. And after him Shemaiah repaired, son of Shechaniah, keeper of the east gate.
NEH 3:30 And after him Hananiah repaired, son of Shelemiah, and Hanun son of Zalaph the sixth son, a second measured section. And after him Meshullam repaired, son of Barechiah right opposite his treasury.
NEH 3:31 And after him Malchiah repaired, son of Sarefi, unto the house of the Nethinim, and of the traders, before the gate of Miphkad, and unto the ascending of the curve.
NEH 3:32 And between the ascending of the sheep gate the braziers and the traders repaired.
NEH 4:1 And it came to pass, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that it was evil to him, and he was angry very much, and was laughing out loud over the Jews.
NEH 4:2 And he spoke before his brothers and the force of the Samaritans, and said, What do these Judahmen do - the Jews? Shall we not abandon them? Is it to sacrifice? Is it that they will be able to? And today, will they repair the stones with the embankment rubbish for being burnt?
NEH 4:3 And Tobiah the Ammonite was next to him, and he said to them, And even if they shall build, shall not a fox ascend and demolish their wall of stones?
NEH 4:4 Hear, O our God! For we became for sneering. And return their scorning upon their head, and give them for sneering in a land of captivity!
NEH 4:5 And you should not cover over their lawlessness, and their sin - may it not be wiped away from your face. For they provoked you to anger before the ones building.
NEH 4:6 And we built the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half of it. And the heart of the people became so as to construct.
NEH 4:7 And it came to pass, as Sanballat heard, and Tobiah, and the Arabians, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites, and that the development of the walls of Jerusalem ascended, that they began to block up the gaps, that it appeared exceedingly wicked to them.
NEH 4:8 And they gathered all together to come and to deploy against Jerusalem, and to do it for a delusion.
NEH 4:9 And we prayed to our God, and set an advance guard against them day and night, from before them.
NEH 4:10 And Judah said, The strength of the enemies is broken, and the dust is vast, and we shall not be able to build on the wall.
NEH 4:11 And the ones afflicting us said, They shall not know, and shall not see, until whenever we should come into the midst of them, and should murder them, and should cause the work to cease.
NEH 4:12 And it came to pass, as the Jews living next to them came, that they said to us, They ascend from out of all the places that you returned from us.
NEH 4:13 And I stood men in the lowermost place from behind the wall, in the protected places. And I stood the people according to peoples, with their broadswords, and their wooden spears, and their bows.
NEH 4:14 And I beheld, and rose up, and spoke to the important ones, and to the commandants, and to the rest of the people, saying, You should not fear from their face. You should remember our great and fearful God, and deploy for your brothers, your sons, and your daughters, and your wives, and your residences!
NEH 4:15 And it came to pass when our enemies heard that it was made known to us, that God effaced their counsel, that we all returned to the wall, every man to his work.
NEH 4:16 And it came to pass from that day, that half of the ones being arrayed did the work, and half of them resisted with lances, and shields, and bows, and chest plates - and the rulers were behind the whole house of Judah.
NEH 4:17 The ones building on the wall, and the ones lifting things on their shoulders, did his work armed in one hand, and with one hand held the arrow.
NEH 4:18 And the builders - a man had his broadsword tied upon his loin, and they built. And the one trumpeting by the horn was next to me.
NEH 4:19 And I said to the important ones, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, The work is spacious and vast, and we are dispersed upon the wall with each man far from his brother.
NEH 4:20 In the place where ever you should hear the sound of the horn, gather together there to us, and our God shall wage war for us.
NEH 4:21 And we were doing the work, and the half of us were holding the lances from the ascending of the dawn until the coming out of the stars.
NEH 4:22 And in that time I said to the people, Each one with his young one shall lodge in the midst of Jerusalem, and let an advance guard be to us in the night, and let the day be for work!
NEH 4:23 And I was there, and my brothers, and the young men; and the men of the advance guard were behind me; and there was not of us a man being stripped of his own garments with a man and his weapons into the water.
NEH 5:1 And the cry of the people and their wives was great against their brothers of the Jews.
NEH 5:2 And there were some saying, With our sons and with our daughters we are many; and we shall take grain, and shall eat and shall live.
NEH 5:3 And there are some saying, Our fields, and our vineyards, and our houses we mortgaged, and we shall take grain and we shall eat.
NEH 5:4 And there are some saying, We borrowed money for tribute of the king of our fields, and our vineyards, and our houses.
NEH 5:5 And now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers; as their sons our sons; and behold, we are tyrannizing over our sons and our daughters selling them for bondmen, and there are some of our daughters being tyrannized already; and there is not power to redeem them by our hands, for our fields and our vineyards belong to the important ones.
NEH 5:6 And I fretted very much as I heard their cry and these words.
NEH 5:7 And my heart took counsel with me, and I did combat against the important ones, and the rulers. And I said to them, Shall a man exact from his brother what you do? And I put upon them a great assembly.
NEH 5:8 And I said to them, We have acquired our brothers of the Jews having been sold to the nations, by our voluntary offerings; and do you sell your brothers? Or shall they be sold to us? And they were quiet, and they did not find a word.
NEH 5:9 And I said, The matter is not good which you do. Should you not go forth thus in the fear of our God because of the scorn of the nations of our enemies?
NEH 5:10 And also I, and my brothers, and my acquaintances, put up for them money and grain - we abandoned indeed this exaction.
NEH 5:11 Return indeed, to them, even today, their fields, and their vineyards, and their olive groves, and their houses, and of the money for the grain, and bring forth to them the wine and the olive oil!
NEH 5:12 And they said, We will give it back, and we will not seek from them. We shall do thus as you say. And I called the priests, and bound them by an oath to do as this saying.
NEH 5:13 And I shook off my wrap, and said, Thus shall God shake off every man who does not stand by this word, from out of his house, and from out of his toil; and he will be thus shaken and empty. And all the assembly said, Amen, and praised the LORD. And the people did this thing.
NEH 5:14 And also from the day which he gave charge to me to be for their ruler in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year, and until the thirtieth and second year of Artaxerxes the king, twelve years, that even I and my brothers did not eat bread of my governing.
NEH 5:15 But the rulers before me oppressed upon the people, and took from them in breads and in wine, and last money of forty shekels. And also their servants dominated over the people. But I did not do so, because of the countenance of the fear of the LORD.
NEH 5:16 And in the work of the wall I repaired these things. I acquired not fields of land, and my servants and all the ones gathering were there for the work.
NEH 5:17 And the Jews, and the rulers were a hundred fifty men. And the ones coming to us from the nations round about us were at my table.
NEH 5:18 And there was coming in one day - one calf, and six choice sheep, and a winter yearling; there came to me also in the midst of ten days all wine in multitude. And with these I sought not bread of my governing, for the slavery was heavy upon this people.
NEH 5:19 Remember me, O God, for all good, as much as I did to this people!
NEH 6:1 And it came to pass as Sanballat heard, (and Tobiah, and Geshem the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies), that I built the wall, and that there was not a breach left in it; (and indeed until that time I did not set up the doors in the gates);
NEH 6:2 that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, Come, for we should come together in the towns in the plain of Ono! But they were considering to do harm against me.
NEH 6:3 And I sent messengers unto them, saying, The work is great that I do, and I am not able to go down, lest at any time the work should rest. When ever I shall perfect it, then I shall go down to you.
NEH 6:4 And they sent to me as this saying four returns; and I sent to them according to this word.
NEH 6:5 And Sanballat sent to me according to this word the fifth time by his servant, and a letter being open was in his hand.
NEH 6:6 And was written on it, Among the nations it was heard, and Geshem said, that you and the Jews are considering to defect. On account of this you are building the wall, and you should be to them for king.
NEH 6:7 And to these things you established to yourself prophets to proclaim for you in Jerusalem, saying, that you reigned in Judea. And now these words will be reported to the king. And now come, we should consult together.
NEH 6:8 And I sent to him, saying, It happened not as these words which you say, for you lie from the heart about them.
NEH 6:9 For all were throwing us into fear, saying, Their hands shall be made faint from this work, and it shall not be done. And now I strengthened my hands.
NEH 6:10 And I entered into the house of Shemaiah son of Dalaiah, son of Mehetabeel, and he was constrained. And he said, We should gather together in the house of God, in the midst of it, and we should lock its doors, for they are coming by night to murder you.
NEH 6:11 And I said, Who is the man such as I that shall flee? Or who such as I shall enter into the house and shall live?
NEH 6:12 I shall not enter. And I realized, and behold, God did not send him, for the prophesy was a word against me. And Tobiah and Sanballat hired him,
NEH 6:13 so that I should fear, and should do thus, and should sin, and that I should become to them for a bad name, so as to berate me.
NEH 6:14 Remember, O my God, Tobiah and Sanballat, according to these their actions, and Noadiah the prophet, and to the rest of the prophets, who were throwing me into fear!
NEH 6:15 And the wall was finished the fifth and twentieth of the month Elul, in fifty two days.
NEH 6:16 And it came to pass when all our enemies heard, that all the nations round about us feared, and an exceedingly great fear fell upon their eyes. And they knew that by God this work of ours was perfected.
NEH 6:17 And in those days letters went from many important men of Judah to Tobiah, and those of Tobiah came to them.
NEH 6:18 For many in Judah were bound by an oath to him, for he was son-in-law of Shechaniah son of Arah; and Johanan his son took the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah for wife.
NEH 6:19 And indeed the things being advantageous to him he spoke before me, and they were bringing my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to throw me into fear.
NEH 7:1 And it came to pass, when the wall was built, and I set the doors, and numbered the gatekeepers, and the singers, and the Levites,

NEH 7:3 that I said to them, The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until at the same time the sun rises; and while they are still vigilant let the doors be locked and be safeguarded! And you set advance guards of ones living in Jerusalem - a man at his own post, and a man before his own house!
NEH 7:4 And the city was spacious and great, and the people were few in it, and there were not houses having been built.
NEH 7:5 And God put it into my heart, and I gathered the important ones, and the rulers, and the people into groups. And I found a scroll of the group which ascended at first, and I found things being written in it.

NEH 8:1 And the seventh month arrived, and the sons of Israel were in their cities. And all the people gathered together as one man into the wide place in front of the water gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the scroll of the law of Moses, which the LORD gave charge to Israel.
NEH 8:2 And Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, from man unto woman, and all the ones perceiving to hear, on day one of the seventh month.
NEH 8:3 And he read in it before the square, before the gate of the waters, from the hour of the illuminating by the sun until the middle of the day, before men and women. And they were perceiving, even all the ears of the people, to the scroll of the law.
NEH 8:4 And Ezra the scribe stood upon the wooden rostrum he made for delivering a public address. And stood next to him, Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah at his right; and at the left, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, and Zechariah, and Meshullam.
NEH 8:5 And Ezra opened the scroll before all the people, for he was above the people. And it came to pass when he opened it, all the people stood.
NEH 8:6 And Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God. And all the people answered, and said, Amen, Amen, lifting up their hands. And they bowed and did obeisance to the LORD with their face upon the ground.
NEH 8:7 And Joshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah, Jamin, and Akkub, Shabbethai, and Hodijah, and Maaseiah, and Kelita, and Azariah, and Jozabad and Hanan, and Pelaiah, and the Levites, were bringing understanding to the people in the law. And the people were at its station.
NEH 8:8 And they read in the scroll of the law of God; and Ezra taught and gave orders in a higher knowledge of the LORD, and the people perceived in the reading.
NEH 8:9 And Nehemiah spoke, who is the Artasastha, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites bringing understanding to the people. And they said to all the people, It is a holy day to the LORD our God; do not mourn nor weep! for all the people wept as they heard the words of the law.
NEH 8:10 And he said to them, Go and eat fatnesses, and drink sweetnesses, and send portions to the ones not having! for the day is holy to the LORD our God. And do not faint! For the joy of the LORD, this is our strength.
NEH 8:11 And the Levites quelled all the people, saying, Keep silent, for the day is holy, and do not fall down!
NEH 8:12 And all the people went forth to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great gladness, for they perceived in the words which he made known to them.
NEH 8:13 And on the second day the rulers of the families gathered together with all the people, the priests, and the Levites, to Ezra the scribe, to attend to all the words of the law.
NEH 8:14 And they found written in the law which the LORD gave charge to Moses, that the sons of Israel should dwell in tents in the holiday in the seventh month,
NEH 8:15 and that they should signify with trumpets in all their cities, and in Jerusalem. And Ezra said, Go forth unto the mountain, and bring olive leaves, and leaves of cypress trees, and leaves of a myrtle tree, and leaves of palms, and leaves of the bushy tree, to make tents, according to the writing!
NEH 8:16 And the people went forth, and brought, and made themselves tents, each man upon his roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the squares of the gate of the waters, and in the squares of the gate of Ephraim.
NEH 8:17 And all the assembly of the ones returning from the captivity made tents, and stayed in tents. For the sons of Israel did not do thus from the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day. And there became a great gladness - exceedingly much.
NEH 8:18 And he read in the scroll of the law of God day by day - from the first day until the last day. And they observed the holiday seven days; and the eighth day was a holiday recess, according to the distinguishing manner.
NEH 9:1 And on the twentieth and fourth day of this month the sons of Israel gathered together for fasting, and with sackcloths, and ashes upon their head.
NEH 9:2 And the sons of Israel separated from every alien son, and stood and declared openly their sins, and the lawless deeds of their fathers.
NEH 9:3 And they stood in their position, and read in the scroll of the law of the LORD their God the fourth of the day; and were declaring openly to the LORD the fourth of the day, and doing obeisance to the LORD their God.
NEH 9:4 And Jeshua stood upon the ascent of the Levites, and the sons of Kadmiel, Secheniah son of Sherebiah, son of Chenani, and yelled with a great voice to the LORD their God.
NEH 9:5 And said the Levites, Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Sherebiah, Hodijah Shebaniah, Pethahiah, Rise up, bless the LORD our God from the eon and unto the eon! And they shall bless your glorious name, and shall raise it up high with all blessing and praise.
NEH 9:6 And Ezra said, You are he, the LORD alone. You made the heaven and the heaven of the heaven, and all their positions, the earth and all as much as is in it, the seas and all the things in them, and you restore to life all things; and to you the militaries of the heavens do obeisance.
NEH 9:7 You are, O LORD, the God. You chose Abram, and led him from the place of the Chaldeans, and placed unto him the name Abraham.
NEH 9:8 And you found his heart trustworthy before you, and ordained with him a covenant, so as to give to him the land of the Canaanites, and Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Jebusites, and Girgashites, and to give it to his seed. And you established your words, for you are just.
NEH 9:9 And you beheld the humiliation of our fathers in Egypt, and you heard their cry at the red sea.
NEH 9:10 And you gave signs and miracles in Egypt to Pharaoh, and among all his servants, and among all the people of his land. For you knew that they extolled themselves above them. And you made for yourself a name as it is this day.
NEH 9:11 And you tore up the sea before them, and they went in the midst of the sea in dryness; and the ones pursuing them you tossed into the bottom of the sea, as a stone in vehement water.
NEH 9:12 And in a column of cloud you guided them by day; and by a column of fire at night, to give light to them for the way in which they went by it.
NEH 9:13 And upon mount Sinai you went down, and spoke to them from out of heaven, and gave to them right judgments, and laws of truth, orders, and good commandments.
NEH 9:14 And your holy sabbath you made known to them - commandments, and orders, and law, you gave charge to them by the hand of Moses your servant.
NEH 9:15 And bread from heaven you gave to them for their provision, and water from out of the rock you brought forth to them for their thirst. And you spoke to them to enter to inherit the land into which you stretched out your hand to give to them.
NEH 9:16 But they and our fathers were prideful, and hardened their neck, and hearkened not unto your commandments.
NEH 9:17 And they shook their heads in dissent to listen, and did not remember your wonders which you performed among them. And they hardened their neck, and they granted a sovereign to return them to slavery in Egypt. But you, O God, in forgiving sins are merciful and pitying, lenient and full of mercy, and did not abandon them.
NEH 9:18 And still also they made for themselves a molten calf, and said, These are the gods leading us from Egypt. And they committed great provocations to anger.
NEH 9:19 And you in your great compassions did not abandon them in the wilderness. The column of cloud did not turn aside from them by day to guide them in the way; and the column of fire by night to give light to them in the way in which they went by it.
NEH 9:20 And your good spirit gave a bringing of understanding to them, and your manna you did not withhold from their mouth, and you gave water to them in their thirst.
NEH 9:21 And forty years you nourished them in the wilderness - not one thing lacked to them; their garments did not become old, and their sandals were not torn up.
NEH 9:22 And you gave them kingdoms, and you divided peoples to them. And they inherited the land of Sihon king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
NEH 9:23 And their sons you multiplied as the stars of the heaven, and brought them into the land which you spoke to their fathers, to enter and to inherit.
NEH 9:24 And their sons entered and inherited the land; and you obliterated before them the ones dwelling the land of the Canaanites, and gave them into their hands, even their kings, and the peoples of the land, to do to them as was pleasing before them.
NEH 9:25 And they overtook high cities, and a fertile land. And they inherited houses full of all good things, and pits for quarrying, vineyards, and olive groves, and every tree of eatable things in multitude. And they ate, and were filled up, and were fattened, and indulged in your great goodness.
NEH 9:26 And they changed and revolted from you. And they tossed your law behind their body, and they killed your prophets testifying to them to turn them towards you. And they made great provocations to anger.
NEH 9:27 And you gave them into the hand of ones afflicting them, and they afflicted them. And they yelled out to you in the time of their affliction, and you heard from out of your heaven, and in your great compassions you gave deliverers to them, and they delivered them from the hand of ones afflicting them.
NEH 9:28 And as they were caused to rest, they turned to act wickedly before you. And you abandoned them into the hands of their enemies, and they ruled among them. And again they yelled out to you, and you from out of heaven listened and rescued them by your abundant compassions.
NEH 9:29 And you attested to them, to turn them to your law. But they acted superior, and hearkened not of your commandments. And in your judgments they sinned, (which a man doing them shall live by them); and gave their back unto resisting persuasion, and hardened their neck, and hearkened not.
NEH 9:30 And you were long-suffering unto them many years, and drew out patience unto them many years, and attested to them by your spirit, by the hand of your prophets. But they did not give ear, and you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the land.
NEH 9:31 And you, in your abundant compassions, did not appoint them to consummation, and you did not abandon them; for you are strong, and merciful, and pitying.
NEH 9:32 And now, O our God, the strong, the great, the fortified, and fearsome, guarding your covenant, and your mercy, do not let your attention be lessened before you concerning all the trouble which found us, and our kings, and our rulers, and our priests, and our prophets, and our fathers, and among all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria, and until this day!
NEH 9:33 For you are just concerning all the things coming upon us; for truth you acted, but we were led into sin.
NEH 9:34 And our kings, and our rulers, and our priests, and our fathers, observed not your law, and heeded not your commandments and your testimonies which you testified to them.
NEH 9:35 And they in your kingdom, and in your abundant goodness which you gave to them, and in the spacious and lustrous land which you put before them, did not serve to you, and did not turn from their wicked practices.
NEH 9:36 Behold, we are today servants, and the land which you gave to our fathers, to eat the fruit of it, and the good things of it, even behold, we are servants upon it.
NEH 9:37 And its many fruits became to the kings which you put over us because of our sins; and they exercise authority over our bodies, and over our cattle, as is pleasing to them, and we are in great affliction.
NEH 9:38 And in all these things we are ordained a trust, and we write it; and our rulers put a seal upon it - our Levites, our priests.

NEH 10:28 And the rest of the people were the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and all the ones being parted from the peoples of the land to the law of God - their wives, their sons, their daughters, every one knowing and perceiving,
NEH 10:29 growing in strength with their brothers, and imprecating maledictions upon themselves, and entering into a curse, and into an oath, to go by the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, to guard and to observe all the commandments of the LORD our God, and his judgments and his orders;
NEH 10:30 and to not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and to not take their daughters for our sons.
NEH 10:31 And concerning the peoples of the land bringing things for purchase, and all things for sale during the sabbath day, to deliver up for sale - we shall not buy from them during the sabbath, nor during the holy days. And we shall ascend the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt of hand. we will obey the seventh year laws.
NEH 10:32 And we shall establish for us commandments to yield up for us a third of the double-drachma per year for the service of the house of our God;
NEH 10:33 for the breads in front, and the perpetual sacrifice offering, and for the perpetual whole burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the holidays, and for the holy things, and the things for a sin offering to atone for Israel, and for the works of the house of our God.
NEH 10:34 And we cast lots for the gifts of bearing wood (the priests, and the Levites, and the people), to bring into the house of our God, for houses of our families, at seasons, from times year by year, to burn upon the altar of the LORD our God, as is written in the law;
NEH 10:35 and to bring the first produce of our land, and the first produce of the fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house of the LORD;
NEH 10:36 and the first-born of our sons, and of our cattle, as is written in the law, and the first-born of our oxen, and of our flocks - to bring into the house of our God, for the priests officiating in the house of our God.
NEH 10:37 And the first-fruit of our grain, and our first-fruit offerings, and the fruit of every tree, of wine and olive oil, we shall bring to the priests, into the treasuries of the house of our God; and tenths of our land to the Levites, that they themselves, the Levites, are receiving a tenth in all the cities of our servitude.
NEH 10:38 And the priest the son of Aaron shall be with the Levites in the tenth of the Levites. And the Levites shall offer the tenth of the tenth for the house of our God, into a treasury of the house of the treasury.
NEH 10:39 For into the treasuries the sons of Israel and sons of the Levites shall carry in the first-fruits of the grain, and of the wine, and of the olive oil. And the holy vessels are there, and the priests, the ministers, and the gatekeepers, and the singers. And we shall not abandon the house of our God.

NEH 11:2 And the people blessed all the men willing to settle in Jerusalem.
