NEH 12:1 And these are the priests and the Levites ascending with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua; Saraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
NEH 12:2 Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
NEH 12:3 Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
NEH 12:4 Iddo, Ginnetho, Abijah,
NEH 12:5 Miamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
NEH 12:6 Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
NEH 12:7 Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the rulers of the priests, and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
NEH 12:8 And the Levites; Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Joiada, Mattaniah, which was over the acknowledgments, he and his brothers.
NEH 12:9 And Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, were over against them in the daily rotations.
NEH 12:10 And Jeshua engendered Joiakim, and Joiakim engendered Eliashib, and Eliashib engendered Joiada,
NEH 12:11 and Joiada engendered Jonathan, and Jonathan engendered Jaddua.
NEH 12:12 And in the days of Joiakim were the priests, and the rulers of the families - to Seraiah, Meraiah; to Jeremiah, Hananiah;
NEH 12:13 to Ezra, Meshullam; to Amariah, Jehohanan;
NEH 12:14 to Melicu, Jonathan; to Secheniah, Joseph;
NEH 12:15 to Harim, Adna; to Maraioth, Helkai;
NEH 12:16 to Iddo, Zechariah; to Ginnethon, Meshullam;
NEH 12:17 to Abijah, Zichri; to Miniamin, Moadiah; to Piltai;
NEH 12:18 to Bilgah, Shammua; to Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
NEH 12:19 to Joiarib, Mattenai; to Jedaiah, Uzzi;
NEH 12:20 to Sallai, Kallai; to Amok, Eber;
NEH 12:21 to Hilkiah, Hashabiah; to Jedaiah, Nethaneel.
NEH 12:22 The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Joa, and Johanan, and Jaddua were written down as rulers of the families; and the priests, in the kingdom of Darius the Persian.
NEH 12:23 And the sons of Levi, rulers of the families, were written down upon the scroll of the words of the days, even until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.
NEH 12:24 And the rulers of the Levites - Hashabiah, and Sherebiah, and Jeshua, and the sons of Kadmiel, and their brothers over against them, for praising and making acknowledgment, by the command of David the man of God, in daily rotation by daily rotation.
NEH 12:25 Mattaniah and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub, were guarding gatekeepers of the watch in my gathering the gatekeepers.
NEH 12:26 These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the ruler, and Ezra the priest and scribe.
NEH 12:27 And in the festival of dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites in their places, to bring them into Jerusalem, to observe the holiday of rededication with gladness, and in praise, and in odes, playing cymbals, and psalteries, and lutes.
NEH 12:28 And the sons of the singers gathered even from the place round about Jerusalem, and from the properties of the Netophathi,
NEH 12:29 and in Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth; for the singers built for themselves nearby properties surrounding Jerusalem.
NEH 12:30 And the priests and the Levites cleansed themselves, and they cleansed the people, and the gates, and the wall.
NEH 12:31 And they brought the rulers of Judah upon the wall, and I stationed two great companies for praise, and one went at the right of the wall of the gate of the dung;
NEH 12:32 and Hoshaiah and half of the rulers of Judah went behind them,
NEH 12:33 and Azariah, and Ezra, and Meshullam,
NEH 12:34 and Judah, and Benjamin, and Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
NEH 12:35 and some from the sons of the priests with trumpets - Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mathaniah, son of Michaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asap;
NEH 12:36 and his brothers, Shemaiah, and Azarael, Gilalai, Maai, Nethaneel, and Judah and Hanani, to praise by instruments in odes of David the man of God, and Ezra the scribe was in front of them.
NEH 12:37 At the gate of the spring, over by them, they ascended upon the stairways of the city of David, by ascending the wall on top of the house of David, and unto the water gate according to the east.
NEH 12:38 And for praise, the second group went forth to meet them. And I was behind them. And half of the people were above the wall, up above the tower of the furnaces, and unto the broad wall;
NEH 12:39 and up above the gate of Ephraim, and upon the gate of Eisiana, and upon the fish gate, and the tower of Hananeel, and from the tower of Meah, and unto the gate of the sheep; and they stopped upon the gate of the prison.
NEH 12:40 And the two groups stood for praise in the house of God, and I and the half of the commandants were with me.
NEH 12:41 And the priests; Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, Hananiah, were with trumpets;
NEH 12:42 and Maaseiah, and Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Melchijah, and Elam, and Ezer. And the singers were heard, and Jezrahiah the overseer.
NEH 12:43 And they sacrificed in that day great sacrifices, and were glad, for God gladdened them gladness with great. And their wives and their children were glad. And the gladness in Jerusalem was heard from far off.
NEH 12:44 And they ordained in that day men over the treasuries, for the treasures, for the first-fruits, and for the tenths, to gather in to them from the fields of the cities portions to the priests and to the Levites; for there was gladness in Judah, and upon the priests, and the Levites standing.
NEH 12:45 And they guarded the watch of their God, and the watches of the cleansing, even the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commands of David, and Solomon his son.
NEH 12:46 For in the days of David and Asaph from the beginning there was a first one of the singers, and a hymn and praise to God.
NEH 12:47 And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel, and in the days of Nehemiah, were giving portions for the singers and for the gatekeepers - an account of it day by day. And they sanctified them to the Levites; and the Levites sanctified them to the sons of Aaron.
NEH 13:1 In that day they read in the scroll of Moses into the ears of the people; and it was found written in it how that the Ammonite and Moabite should not enter into the assembly of God unto the eon,
NEH 13:2 for they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and water, and they hired against them Balaam to curse them. And our God turned the curse into a blessing.
NEH 13:3 And it came to pass as they heard the law, that they separated all the intermixed in Israel.
NEH 13:4 And before this, Eliashib the priest lived in the treasury of the house of our God, near Tobiah.
NEH 13:5 And he made for him a great treasury, and there they were formerly putting the sacrifice offering, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tenth of the grain, and of the wine, and of the olive oil, a commandment for giving to the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the first-fruits of the priests.
NEH 13:6 And during all this I was not in Jerusalem. For in the thirtieth and second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king, and after the end of the days I asked things of the king.
NEH 13:7 And I came into Jerusalem, and I perceived the wickedness which Eliashib did for Tobiah, to make for him a treasury in the courtyard of the house of God.
NEH 13:8 And it appeared exceedingly wicked to me, and I tossed all the items of the house of Tobiah outside of the treasury.
NEH 13:9 And I spoke, and they cleansed the treasuries; and I returned there the vessels of the house of God for the sacrifice offering and the frankincense.
NEH 13:10 And I knew that the portions of the Levites were not given them; and every man fled unto his own field - the Levites, and the singers, and ones doing the work.
NEH 13:11 And I quarreled with the commandants, and said, Why did it abandon the house of God? And I gathered them, and set them at their station.
NEH 13:12 And all Judah brought a tenth of the wheat, and of the wine, and of the olive oil, into the treasuries.
NEH 13:13 And I gave charge unto the hand of Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites; and near their hand was Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah. For they were considered trustworthy, as it was upon them to portion out to their brothers.
NEH 13:14 Remember me, O God, in this, that my acts of mercy should not be wiped away which I did in the house of the LORD my God, and in his watches!
NEH 13:15 In those days I beheld in Judah ones treading the wine vats on the sabbath, and bringing sheaves, and loading upon the donkeys - even wine, and the grape cluster, and figs, and every burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the day of the sabbath. And I attested to them in the day of their sale.
NEH 13:16 For even the ones of Tyre sold provision, and sat by it bringing fish, and selling every item for sale on the sabbath to the sons of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
NEH 13:17 And I quarreled with the free men of Judah, and said to them, What is this wicked matter which you do, and profane the day of the sabbath?
NEH 13:18 Did not your fathers do thus, and our God brought upon them and upon us all these evils, and upon this city? And you add to the anger upon Israel to profane the sabbath.
NEH 13:19 And it came to pass when the gates were stood in Jerusalem before the sabbath, that I spoke, and they locked the gates. And I spoke so as to not open them until after the sabbath. And I stood some of my young men at the gates, so as for others to not lift burdens on the day of the sabbath.
NEH 13:20 And all the traders lodged and did business outside of Jerusalem once or twice.
NEH 13:21 And I testified to them, and said to them, Why do you lodge before the wall? If you repeat it a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you. From that time they did not come on the sabbath.
NEH 13:22 And I spoke to the Levites who were being cleansed, and the ones coming guarding the gates to sanctify the day of the sabbath. For these things remember me, O my God, and spare me according to the magnitude of your mercy!
NEH 13:23 And in those days I saw the Jews who settled with wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and Moab.
NEH 13:24 And their sons were speaking half Ashdodish, and are not knowing to speak Jewish, but spoke according to the language of this people and that people.
NEH 13:25 And I quarreled with them, and cursed them, and struck some of their men, and plucked their hair, and bound them to an oath by God, You shall not give your daughters to their sons, and you shall not indeed take of their daughters for your sons, and to yourselves.
NEH 13:26 Did not Solomon king of Israel thus sin? And among many nations there was not a king likened to him, and he was one being loved by God, and God appointed him as king over all Israel, and in this the alien wives turned him aside.
NEH 13:27 So should we hearken of your doing this wickedness, to break contract with our God, and to settle with alien wives?
NEH 13:28 And from the sons of Joiada, Eliashib the great priest, in-law to Sanballat the Horonite - even I threw him from me.
NEH 13:29 Remember them, O my God, for they were against the right of inheritance of the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites!
NEH 13:30 And I cleansed them from all alien connection, and I set the daily rotations for the priests and for the Levites, every man according to his work;
NEH 13:31 and for the gift of the wood offerings in seasons, from times, and in the first produce. Remember me, O our God, for goodness!
EST 1:1 And it came to pass in the days of Artaxerxes - this Artaxerxes held a hundred twenty-seven regions from India.
EST 1:2 And in those days, when king Artaxerxes was enthroned in Shushan the city,
EST 1:3 in the third year of his reign, he made a banquet to his friends, and to the rest of the nations, and to the Persians and Medes, and honorable ones, and to the rulers of the satrapies.
EST 1:4 And after these things, after the showing to them the riches of his kingdom, and the glory of his gladness, even for a hundred eighty days,
EST 1:5 that when the days of the wedding feast were fulfilled, the king made a banquet for the nations found in the city, for six days, in the courtyard of the house of the king;
EST 1:6 being adorned in fine linen, and cotton being stretched upon lines of fine linen and of purple, upon cube studs of gold and silver, upon columns of Parian marble, and stones, with beds of gold and silver upon a stone pavement of emerald stone, and mother of pearl, and Parian marble stone, and transparent strewn beds being decorated variously,
EST 1:7 with cups of gold and silver, wine abundant and agreeable, which the king himself drank.
EST 1:8 But this banquet took place not according to the law being situated; but thus the king wanted, and he gave orders to the managers to do his will, and for the men.
EST 1:9 And Vashti the queen made a banquet for the women in the palace where king Artaxerxes was.
EST 1:10 And on the seventh day, the king being with pleasure, said to Mehuman, and Biztha, and Harbona, and Bigtha, and Abagtha, and Zethar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs of king Artaxerxes,
EST 1:11 to bring in the queen to him, to give her reign, and to put on her the diadem, and to show her to all the rulers, and to the nations of her beauty - for she was beautiful.
EST 1:12 And queen Vashti listened not to him to come with the eunuchs. And the king fretted, and was provoked to anger.
EST 1:13 And he said to his friends, Thus these things Vashti spoke, you deal then concerning this law and judgment!
EST 1:14 And came forward to him Carshena, and Shethar and Admatha, and Tarshish, and Meres and Marsena and Memucan - seven rulers of the Persians and Medes near the king, the ones foremost being seated near the king.
EST 1:15 And they reported to him according to the laws as what Vashti the queen must do, for she had not done the things having been assigned by the king through the eunuchs.
EST 1:16 And Memucan said to the king, and to the rulers, Not only queen Vashti wronged the king, but also all the rulers, and the leaders of the king,
EST 1:17 (for even he described to them the sayings of the queen, and how ever she contradicted to the king, as then she did contradict to king Artaxerxes),
EST 1:18 that today, the wives of the sovereigns, the rest of the rulers of the Persians and Medes, hearing the things having been said against the king by her, shall dare in like manner to dishonor their husbands.
EST 1:19 If then it seems good to the king, let him assign a royal decree, and let him write it according to the laws of the Medes and Persians, and not otherwise treat nor let the queen any longer enter to him. And let the king give her royalty to a woman better than her!
EST 1:20 And let the law by the king be heard, which ever he should make for his kingdom! And thus to all the wives - they shall invest honor to their own husbands, from poor unto rich.
EST 1:21 And the word pleased the king and the rulers. And the king did as Memucan said.
EST 1:22 And he sent letters into all the kingdom, according to place, according to their form of speech, so as to be fearing them in their households.
EST 2:1 And after these matters the king's rage was abated, and no longer was Vashti mentioned, remembering, as much as she spoke, and how he condemned her.
EST 2:2 And the servants of the king said, Let there be sought to the king young women uncorrupted, beautiful in appearance!
EST 2:3 And the king shall place magistrates in all the places of his kingdom; and let them choose young women, virgins, beautiful in appearance, to be brought to Shushan the city, into the chamber of the women! And let them be delivered to the eunuch of the king, to the keeper of the women! And let there be given a beauty treatment, and the remaining care!
EST 2:4 And the woman who ever should be pleasing to the king shall reign instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.
EST 2:5 And there was a man, a Jew, in Shushan the city, and his name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin;
EST 2:6 who was a captive from Jerusalem, which Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon captured.
EST 2:7 And there was to this man a child that he brought up, ( the daughter of the brother of his father), and her name was Esther. And at the changeover of her parents, he instructed her to himself for a wife. And the young woman was good in appearance.
EST 2:8 And when the king's order was heard, many young women were gathered together in Shushan the city, by the hand of Hegai, and Esther was led to Hegai, the keeper of the women.
EST 2:9 And the young woman pleased him, and she found favor before him. And he hastened to give her the beauty treatment, and her portion, and the seven young women being exhibited to her from the royal palace. And he treated her well, and her handmaidens in the chamber of the women.
EST 2:10 But Esther did not plainly show her race, nor her fatherland, for Mordecai gave charge to her not to report it.
EST 2:11 And each day Mordecai walked by the feminine courtyard, overseeing what would come to pass with Esther.
EST 2:12 For this was the time for a young woman to enter to the king, whenever she should have fulfilled twelve months, for thus are fulfilled the days of the treatment - six months with the aromatics, and with the beauty treatments for the women,
EST 2:13 and six months being anointed with myrrh oil, and then she enters to the king. And to whom ever he should tell, he delivers her to enter together with him, from the chamber of the women unto the palaces.
EST 2:14 In the evening she enters, and by day she runs to the second chamber of the women, where Hegai, the eunuch of the king, the keeper of the women is. And no longer does she enter to the king if she should not be called by name.
EST 2:15 And in the fulfilling the time, Esther, the daughter of Abihail, brother of the father of Mordecai, entered to the king. Not one thing she disregarded which the eunuch keeper of the women gave charge to her. For Esther was found in favor by all the ones seeing her.
EST 2:16 And Esther entered to Artaxerxes the king in the tenth month, which is Tebeth, in the seventh year of his kingship.
EST 2:17 And the king loved Esther passionately, and she found favor above all the virgins; and he placed upon her the feminine diadem.
EST 2:18 And the king made a banquet for all his friends, and the powerful ones, for seven days, and exalted the wedding feasts of Esther. And he made a release to the ones under his kingdom.
EST 2:19 But Mordecai attended to affairs in the courtyard.
EST 2:20 Now Esther did not plainly tell of her fatherland, for thus Mordecai gave charge to her, to fear God, and to observe his orders, as she was with him. And Esther did not change over her conduct.
EST 2:21 And the two eunuchs of the king fretted, and the chiefs of the body guards, for Mordecai advanced. And they sought to kill Artaxerxes the king.
EST 2:22 And the matter was made manifest to Mordecai, and he signaled it to Esther, and she revealed to the king the things of the plot.
EST 2:23 And the king examined the two eunuchs, and hanged them. And the king gave order to write for a memorial in the royal library about the good-will of Mordecai with commendation.
EST 3:1 After these things king Artaxerxes extolled Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and exalted him, and seated him first above all his friends.
EST 3:2 And all the ones in the courtyard did obeisance to him; for so the king assigned it to do. But Mordecai did not do obeisance to him.
EST 3:3 And the ones in the courtyard of the king said to Mordecai, O Mordecai, why do you disregard the things being said by the king?
EST 3:4 Accordingly each day they spoke to him, and he hearkened not to them. And they indicated to Haman that Mordecai was rebelling against the words of the king. And Mordecai indicated to them that he is a Jew.
EST 3:5 And Haman, realizing that Mordecai did not do obeisance to him, was enraged exceedingly.
EST 3:6 And he took counsel to remove all the Jews under the kingdom of Artaxerxes.
EST 3:7 And he made a referendum in the twelfth year of the kingdom of Artaxerxes, and cast lots day by day, and month by month, so as to destroy in one day the race of Mordecai. And the lot fell on the fourteenth of the month, which is Adar.
EST 3:8 And he spoke to king Artaxerxes, saying, There exists a nation having been disseminated among the nations in all your kingdom, but their laws are special from all the nations, and of the laws of the king they disregard; and it is not advantageous to the king to allow them.
EST 3:9 If it seems good to the king, let him decree to destroy them, and I will circumscribe for the treasury of the king ten thousand talents of silver.
EST 3:10 And the king removing the ring, gave it into the hands to Haman to set a seal according to the things being written against the Jews.
EST 3:11 And the king said to Haman, As for the silver, you have it! And to the nation - you treat it as you want!
EST 3:12 And the scribes were called by the king in the first month, the thirteenth day, and they wrote as Haman gave orders to the commandants, and to the rulers in every place from India unto Ethiopia, to a hundred twenty-seven places, to the rulers of the nations according to their form of speech, through Artaxerxes the king.
EST 3:13 And it was sent by couriers into the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to remove the race of the Jews on day one of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their possessions.

EST 3:15 And the thing was hastened, even in Shushan. And the king and Haman toasted, but the city was disturbed.
EST 4:1 But Mordecai realizing the end, tore his garments, and put on sackcloth, and strewed ashes. And rushing out through the square of the city, he yelled with a great voice, A nation having wronged no one is going to be taken away.
EST 4:2 And he came unto the gate of the king, and stood; for it was not allowed for him to enter into the courtyard having on sackcloth and ashes.
EST 4:3 And in every place where the letters were displayed there was a cry, and a beating of the breast, and great mourning among the Jews. And with sackcloth and ashes they made beds for themselves.
EST 4:4 And the handmaidens and the eunuchs of the queen entered, and announced to her. And she was disturbed hearing the thing taking place; and she sent to robe Mordecai, and to remove from him the sackcloth - but he yielded not.
EST 4:5 And then Esther called on Hatach, her eunuch, who stood beside her. And she sent to learn for herself from Mordecai the exact situation.
EST 4:7 And Mordecai indicated to him the thing taking place, and the promise which Haman promised to the king, for the treasury paying ten thousand talents that he should destroy the Jews.
EST 4:8 And the copy in Shushan, being displayed for purpose of destroying them, he gave to him, to show to Esther. And he told him to give charge to her to enter to ask pardon of the king, and to be found worthy by him for the people, remembering, said he, The days of your low estate, how you were maintained by my hand; for Haman the one being second to the king speaks against us for death. You call upon the LORD, and speak to the king concerning us, even to rescue us from out of death!
EST 4:9 And Hatach entering spoke to Esther all these words.
EST 4:10 And Esther said to Hatach, You go to Mordecai, and say!
EST 4:11 that, All the nations of the kingdom know that every man or woman who shall enter to the king, into the inner courtyard uncalled, that there is not deliverance to him, except to whomever the king stretches out the golden rod - this one shall be delivered. And I have not been called to enter to the king - they are these thirty days.
EST 4:12 And Hatach reported to Mordecai all the words of Esther.
EST 4:13 And Mordecai said to Hatach, Go and say to her! Esther, you should not say to yourself that you shall be delivered alone in the kingdom of all the Jews.
EST 4:14 So that if you should disregard at this time, from elsewhere help and protection will be to the Jews; but you and the house of your father will be destroyed; and who knows if it be for this occasion you reigned.
EST 4:15 And Esther sent the one having come to her to Mordecai, saying,
EST 4:16 In proceeding, you hold an assembly of the Jews in Shushan, and you all fast for me! And you should not eat nor drink for three days - night and day. And I and the handmaidens of mine shall go without food; and then I shall enter to the king contrary to the law, even if it is necessary for me to perish.
EST 4:17 And proceeding, Mordecai did as much as Esther gave charge to him.
EST 5:1 And it came to pass in the third day, Esther put on royal apparel, and stood in the courtyard of the house of the king, in the inner courtyard, right opposite the royal house of the king. And the king sat down on the throne of his own kingdom in the royal house, right opposite the door of the house.
EST 5:2 And as the king saw Esther the queen standing in the courtyard, that she found favor in his eyes. And the king stretching out to Esther the golden rod in his hand, that Esther approached, and touched the tip of the rod.
EST 5:3 And the king said, What do you want, Esther? and what is your request? the worth unto half of my kingdom will be to you.
EST 5:4 And Esther said, Today is a notable day for me. If then it seems good to the king, let both the king and Haman come to the banquet which I shall prepare today!
EST 5:5 And the king said, Hasten Haman, so that we should do the word of Esther! And they came both to the banquet which Esther made.
EST 5:6 And at the banquet the king said to Esther, What is it to you, queen Esther, and it will be to you as much as is worthy?
EST 5:7 And she said, The request of mine and my petition -
EST 5:8 if I found favor before the king, let the king and Haman come upon the morrow to the banquet which I shall prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do the same!
EST 5:9 And Haman went forth from the king overjoyed and being glad. But in Haman's seeing Mordecai the Jew in the courtyard, he was enraged exceedingly.
EST 5:10 And entering into his own place, he called his friends, and Zeresh his wife.
EST 5:11 And he showed to them his riches, and the glory which the king invested in him, and how he made him to be preeminent, and to take the lead of the kingdom.
EST 5:12 And Haman said, The queen has called not one with the king, not one to the banquet, but me; and for the morrow she has invited me.
EST 5:13 And these things do not please me, whenever I behold Mordecai the Jew in the courtyard.
EST 5:14 And Zeresh his wife said to him, and his friends, Fell to yourself a tree of fifty cubits, and at dawn speak to the king, and hang Mordecai upon the tree; and you enter into the banquet with the king, and be glad! And the saying pleased Haman, and the tree was prepared.

EST 6:2 And he found letters having been written concerning Mordecai, as was reported to the king concerning the two eunuchs of the king, during their watching and their seeking to put hands on Artaxerxes.
EST 6:3 And the king said, What glory or favor did we do for Mordecai? And the servants of the king said, We did not do for him one thing.
EST 6:4 And during the inquiring by the king concerning the good-will of Mordecai, behold, Haman was in the courtyard. And the king said, Who is in the courtyard? And he entered to speak to the king, to hang Mordecai upon the tree which he prepared.
EST 6:5 And the servants of the king said, Behold, Haman stands in the courtyard. And the king said, Call him!
EST 6:6 And the king said to Haman, What shall I do to the man whom I want to extol? And Haman said to himself, Who does the king want to extol unless me?
EST 6:7 And he said to the king, As for the man whom the king wants to extol,
EST 6:8 let the servants of the king bring fine linen apparel which the king puts on, and the horse upon which the king mounts,
EST 6:9 and give it to one of the friends of the king of the honorable ones, and robe the man whom the king loves, and mount him upon the horse, and let him proclaim through the square of the city! saying, So shall it be done to every man whom the king extols.
EST 6:10 And the king said to Haman, You spoke well, you do thus to Mordecai the Jew, the one attending in the courtyard, and do not let fall from you a word which you spoke!
EST 6:11 And Haman took the robe, and the horse, and he robed Mordecai, and mounted him upon the horse, and went through the square of the city, and proclaimed, saying, So it will be to every man the king wants to extol.
EST 6:12 And Mordecai returned to the courtyard. And Haman returned to his own place fretting with a down cast head.
EST 6:13 And Haman described the things coming to pass to him to Zeresh his wife, and to his friends. And the friends and wife said to him, Since Mordecai is of the race of the Jews, and you began to be humbled before him, in falling you shall fall, and in no way should you be able to defend against him, for the living God is with him.
EST 6:14 While they were yet speaking, the eunuchs came to hurry Haman unto the banquet which Esther prepared.
EST 7:1 And they entered, the king and Haman, to drink together with the queen.
EST 7:2 And the king said to Esther on the second day at the banquet, What is it queen Esther? and what is your request? and what is your petition? and it will be to you unto half of my kingdom!
EST 7:3 And answering she said, If I found favor before the king, let him give life to my request, and my people to my petition.
EST 7:4 For both I and my people were sold into destruction, and ravaging, and slavery; we, and both our children for menservants and maidservants, and I neglected to speak; for the slanderer is not worthy of the courtyard of the king.
EST 7:5 And the king said, Who is this who dared to do this thing?
EST 7:6 And Esther said, A man, an enemy, Haman, this wicked man. And Haman was disturbed before the king and the queen.
EST 7:7 And the king rose up from the party to go into the garden. And Haman appealed to the queen, for he saw himself being in evils.
EST 7:8 And the king returned from out of the garden; and Haman had fallen upon the bed petitioning the queen. And the king said, So as even with my wife you use force in my house. And Haman, hearing, was overawed in front of him.
EST 7:9 And Harbonah one of the eunuchs said to the king, Behold, Haman prepared even a tree for Mordecai, the one speaking for the king, and it was set straight up in the places of Haman - of fifty cubits. And the king said, Let him be crucified upon it!
EST 7:10 And Haman was hung upon the tree which he prepared for Mordecai. And then the king slackened from the rage.

EST 8:2 And the king took the ring which he removed from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther placed Mordecai over all the things of Haman.
EST 8:3 And proceeding, she spoke to the king, and fell upon his feet, and petitioned him to remove the evil of Haman, and as much as he did to the Jews.
EST 8:4 And the king stretched out to Esther the gold rod, and Esther arose to stand beside the king.
EST 8:5 And Esther said, If it seems good to you, and I found favor, let it be sent forth to return the letters being sent from Haman having been written to destroy the Jews who are in your kingdom.
EST 8:6 For how shall I be able to behold the ill treatment of my people? And how shall I be able to be delivered in the destruction of my fatherland?
EST 8:7 And the king said to Esther, If all the possessions of Haman I gave and granted to you, and he I hanged upon the tree for the hands he bore against the Jews, what yet do you anxiously seek?
EST 8:8 And you write in my name as it seems good to you, and set a seal with with my ring! For as much as is written of the king in giving an order, and the seal should be set by my ring, it is not to them to contradict.

And it was written to the Jews, as much as was given charge to the local managers, and to the rulers of the satrapies from India unto Ethiopia - a hundred twenty-seven satrapies, according to place by place, according to their form of speech.

EST 8:11 as he gave orders to them to deal with their laws in every city, both to help them, and to deal with their opponents, and with their adversaries, as they wanted,
EST 8:12 on one day in all the kingdom of Artaxerxes, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar.
EST 8:13 And the copies, let them be displayed clear to the eyes in all the kingdom, and for all the Jews to be prepared for this day, for them to wage war against their opponents.

EST 8:15 And Mordecai went forth robed in the royal apparel, and having a crown of gold, and a diadem of purple fine line. And the ones in Shushan beholding rejoiced.
EST 8:16 And to the Jews there became light and gladness.
EST 8:17 In each city and place, of which ever the public notice was displayed, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, with toasting and gladness. And many of the nations were circumcised, and were Jewish-like because of the fear of the Jews.

EST 9:3 For the rulers of the satraps, and the sovereigns, and the royal scribes esteemed the Jews; for the fear of Mordecai rested upon them.
EST 9:4 For the order of the king fell for him to be namedfamous. in all the kingdom.

EST 9:16 And the rest of the Jews in the kingdom gathered together and helped themselves, and gained rest from the warlike men; for they destroyed of them, seven ten thousands, and five thousand men on the thirteenth of Adar, but they plundered nothing.
EST 9:17 And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and celebrated it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
EST 9:18 And the Jews in Shushan the city gathered together also on the fourteenth and rested. But they celebrated even on the fifteenth with joy and gladness.
EST 9:19 Because of this then, the Jews, being disseminated in every place outside, celebrate on the fourteenth of Adar, a good day with gladness, each sending portions to the neighbor.
EST 9:20 And Mordecai wrote these words in a scroll, and sent them to the Jews, as many as were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes near and far,
EST 9:21 to establish these days as good days, and to celebrate both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar.
EST 9:22 For in these days the Jews gained rest from their enemies. And the month in which things turned for them, which was Adar, from mourning to joy, and from grief to good days, was to celebrate entirely for good days of wedding feasts and gladness, sending gift portions to their friends, and to the poor.

EST 9:24 of how Haman son of Hammedatha the Macedonian waged war against them; as he ordained a referendum and the lot, to obliterate them;
EST 9:25 and how he entered to the king, telling him to hang Mordecai. But as much as he attempted to bring bad things upon the Jews, upon himself it came to pass; and he was hanged, he and his children.

EST 9:28 And these days were celebrated for all time, and their memorial in no way should fail unto generations.

JOB 1:1 There was a certain man in the land of Uz, Job was the name to him; and that man was true, unblemished, a sincere man, and uprignt, and fearing God, at a distance from every wicked thing.
JOB 1:2 And there were to him seven sons and three daughters.
JOB 1:3 And his animals were - seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred teams of oxen, and five hundred grazing female donkeys, and for service exceedingly many. And there were great works attributed to him upon the land. And that man was great of the ones from the east sun.
JOB 1:4 And his sons going to one another prepared a banquet, each of his own day, taking along together also their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
JOB 1:5 And whenever they completed the days of the banquet, Job sent and purified them, rising up in the morning, and offering for them a sacrifice according to their number. For Job said, Lest at any time my sons sinned and raved against God with their heart. Thus then Job did all the days.
JOB 1:6 And it came to pass this day, and behold, the sons of God came to stand before the LORD, and the devil came in the midst of them.
JOB 1:7 And the LORD said to the devil, From what place have you come? And the devil answering to the LORD, said, Going around the earth, and walking about the place at hand under heaven.
JOB 1:8 And the LORD said to him, Have you been attentive then in your consideration to my attendant Job, that there is not one likened to him of the ones upon the earth, a blameless man, a man sincere and upright and fearing God, at a distance from every wicked thing?
JOB 1:9 And the devil answered, and said, Before the LORD, does Job freely fear God?
JOB 1:10 Have you not enclosed him, and the things inside his household, and the things outside? And all of the things being to him round about - the works of his hands you blessed, and you made his cattle many upon the earth.
JOB 1:11 But send your hand, and touch all which he has, and assuredly he will rave in your face against you.
JOB 1:12 Then the LORD said to the devil, Behold, all as much as is his I put into your hand; but he himself you shall not touch. And the devil went forth from the LORD.
JOB 1:13 And it was on this day the sons of Job and his daughters were drinking wine in the house of their elder brother.
JOB 1:14 And behold, a messenger came to Job, and said to him, The teams of oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were grazing next to them.
JOB 1:15 And Sabeans fell upon and captured them, and the servants they killed by swords. And I alone escaped, and I came to report to you.
JOB 1:16 Yet speaking this, there came another, and said to Job, Fire from God fell from out of the heaven and incinerated the sheep, and the shepherds were devoured up in like manner; and having escaped, I alone came to report to you.
JOB 1:17 While speaking this, there came another messenger, and said to Job, The Chaldeans put three companies, and encircled the camels, and captured them; and the servants they killed by swords; and I alone escaped, and I came to report to you.
JOB 1:18 While this one was speaking, another messenger came, saying to Job, Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking with their elder brother.
JOB 1:19 Suddenly a great wind came upon them from out of the wilderness, and it touched the four corners of their house, and the house fell upon your children, and they came to an end; and I alone escaped, and I came to report to you.
JOB 1:20 Thus rising up, Job tore up his garments, and sheared the hair of his head, and falling to the ground did obeisance.
JOB 1:21 And said, I myself came forth naked from out of my mother's belly, and naked I shall go forth there. The LORD gave, the LORD removed, as to the LORD it seemed good, so also it came to pass. May the name of the LORD be blessed.
JOB 1:22 In all these things coming to pass against him, in nothing Job sinned before the LORD, and he imputed not folly to God.
JOB 2:1 And it came to pass as this day occurred, and the sons of God came to stand before the LORD. And the devil came in the midst of them to stand before the LORD.
JOB 2:2 And the LORD said to the devil, From what place come you? Then the devil said before the LORD, Traveling over the place under heaven, and walking about the whole place at hand.
JOB 2:3 And the LORD said to the devil, Have you taken heed then to my attendant Job, that there is not according to him of the ones upon the earth, a man not wicked, true, blameless, godly, and at a distance from all evil? But still he has innocence, but you spoke to destroy his substance without cause.
JOB 2:4 But the devil undertaking, said to the LORD, Skin for skin, and all as much as exists to a man he will give for his life.
JOB 2:5 But not in fact - but you send your hand to touch his bones and his flesh, assuredly he will rave in your face.
JOB 2:6 And the LORD said to the devil, Behold, I deliver him to you, only you guard his life!
JOB 2:7 And the devil went forth from the LORD, and smote Job with a severe sore from feet unto head.
JOB 2:8 And he took to himself a potsherd so as to scrape the pus; and he sat down within the ashes.
JOB 2:9 And his wife said to him, Until how long will you persevere? But speak any word to God, and come to an end!
JOB 2:10 And he, looking to her, said, Why as one of the foolish women did you speak? If we looked for the good things from out of the hand of the LORD, shall we not endure the bad things? In all these things coming to pass to him, not one thing Job sinned with his lips before the LORD.
JOB 2:11 And his three friends hearing all the bad things coming upon him, came each from their own place to him. Eliphaz the Temanite - a king, Baldad the Shuhite - a sovereign, Zophar the Minaean - a king. And they came to him with one accord to comfort and visit him.
JOB 2:12 And seeing him at a distance, they did not recognize him. And yelling with a great voice, they wept, each tearing his own apparel, and strewing earth.
JOB 2:13 And they sat beside him seven days and seven nights, and not one of them spoke to him a word; for they saw the awful calamity being, and it was exceedingly great.
JOB 3:1 And after this Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day,
JOB 3:2 saying,
JOB 3:3 Maythe day in which I was born be destroyed, and the night in which they said, Behold, a male.
JOB 3:4 May that night be darkness, and may the LORD not search it out from above, nor may brightness come into it.
JOB 3:5 But may darkness and the shadow of death take it; may dimness come upon it; and may that day be disturbed.
JOB 3:6 And that night, may darkness have carried it away; may it not be for the days of the year, nor may it be counted for the days of the months.
JOB 3:7 But may that night be grief, and may gladness not come upon it, nor a cause for joy.
JOB 3:8 But may the one cursing that day curse it - the ones being about to awaken Leviathan.
JOB 3:9 May the stars of that night be enveloped in darkness, and not remain, and not come for illumination; and may the arising Hesperus not be seen.
JOB 3:10 For it did not close up the gates of my mother's womb, for it would have dismissed misery from my eyes.
JOB 3:11 For why in the belly did I not come to an end? but why came I forth from the womb, and was not straightway destroyed?
JOB 3:12 And why did the knees meet me? and why did I nurse on the breasts?
JOB 3:13 Now going to bed I should be stilled; and having slept, rested;
JOB 3:14 with the kings, counselors of the earth, who pranced with blades;
JOB 3:15 or with rulers, whose gold was abundant, who filled their houses with silver;
JOB 3:16 or as if a miscarriage going forth from out of a mother's womb, or as infants who beheld not light.
JOB 3:17 There the impious ones ceased the rage of anger; there the exhausted in the body are rested.
JOB 3:18 But with one accord the ones being boundprisoners. hear not the voice of the tribute-gatherer.
JOB 3:19 Small and great are there, even the attendant being in awe of his master.
JOB 3:20 For why has light been given to the ones in bitterness, and life to the souls in griefs?
JOB 3:21 The ones longing for death, and attain not; rooting it up as if for treasures;
JOB 3:22 and they become overjoyed if they should attain it. Death to a man is rest.
JOB 3:23 The way was not concealed, for God hemmed in against him.
JOB 3:24 For moaning comes to me before my grain, and shall be poured as waters roaring.
JOB 3:25 For the fear which I thought about, came to me; and which I had in awe, met with me.
JOB 3:26 Neither was I at peace, nor still, nor I rested; but wrath came to me.
JOB 4:1 And undertaking, Eliphaz the Temanite says,
JOB 4:2 If we take to speak to you, will you tire? But the strength of your words, who shall endure?
JOB 4:3 For since you admonished many, and comforted the hands of the weak,
JOB 4:4 and also raised up the ones being weak with words, and you invested courage to the ones powerless in knees,
JOB 4:5 but now misery comes upon you, and touched you; and now you are hurried.
JOB 4:6 Is it not that your fear is in folly, and your hope, and the evil of your way?
JOB 4:7 Do you remember then who being pure was destroyed? or when the true ones were destroyed entirely from the root?
JOB 4:8 As in which manner I beheld the ones plowing the unnatural places, then the ones sowing them shall harvest griefs for themselves.
JOB 4:9 By the order of the LORD they shall perish, and by the breath of his anger they shall be obliterated.
JOB 4:10 The strength of a lion, and a voice of a lioness, and a prancing of dragons shall be extinguished.
JOB 4:11 A small lion is destroyed by not having game, and cubs of lions forsook one another.
JOB 4:12 And to me it was spoken clandestinely in stealth; shall not my ear receive extraordinary things by him.
JOB 4:13 In amazement from my nightly vision falling fear upon men,
JOB 4:14 that a shuddering awe met with me, and trembling, and my bones shook greatly.
JOB 4:15 And a spirit came upon my face, and my hair and flesh shuddered.
JOB 4:16 I rose up, and knew not; I saw, and there was not an appearance before my eyes, but only a breeze, and I heard a voice, saying,
JOB 4:17 For what, Shall a mortal be pure before the LORD? or shall a man be blameless from his works?
JOB 4:18 If even his servants he trusts not, and even considers his angels as crooked in what he thinks about,
JOB 4:19 then the ones dwelling in houses of clay, of whom also they are from out of the same mortar - he smites them in the manner of a moth.
JOB 4:20 And from morning until evening they are no longer; by their not being able to help themselves they themselves perish.
JOB 4:21 You raised up together their vestige in them; they perished by their not having wisdom.
JOB 5:1 But call, if any one will hearken to you; or if you shall see any holy angels.
JOB 5:2 For even anger does away a foolish one, and zeal puts to death one having wandered.
JOB 5:3 And I have seen foolish ones laying root; and I cursed their attractiveness immediately.
JOB 5:4 May their sons be at a distance from safety, and be crushed at the doors of lesser men, and there shall not be one rescuing.
JOB 5:5 For those things which they harvested, one hungering shall eat; but they shall be carried to ones armed; may their strength be siphoned off.
JOB 5:6 For toil can not come forth from out of the earth, nor shall misery sprout up from out of mountains.
JOB 5:7 But a man is born to toil, and the young eagles to fly the high places;
JOB 5:8 but nevertheless, I shall beseech of the LORD, and I shall call upon the LORD the master of all;
JOB 5:9 the one doing great things, and untraceable; honorable things also, and extraordinary, which there is not a number;
JOB 5:10 the one giving rain upon the earth, sending water upon the place under heaven;
JOB 5:11 the one appointing the humble unto the height, and raising up the ones perishing;
JOB 5:12 effacing counsels of clever ones, that in no way should their hands perform true;
JOB 5:13 the one overtaking the wise ones with the intellect; and the counsel of the crafty ones he amazes.
JOB 5:14 By day darkness shall meet them, and at midday may they grope equally as at night.
JOB 5:15 And may they perish in war; and may the powerless come forth from out of the hand of the mighty one.
JOB 5:16 And may there be hope to the poor; but may the mouth of the unjust be obstructed.
JOB 5:17 And blessed be a man whom the LORD reproved, and does not refuse the admonition of the almighty.
JOB 5:18 For he causes one to ache, and again he restores; he smites, and his hands heal.
JOB 5:19 Six times he rescues you from out of your distresses; and in the seventh time in no way will he touch you for bad.
JOB 5:20 In famine he will rescue you from out of death; and in war he will untie you from out of the hand of iron.
JOB 5:21 He shall hide you from the whip of the tongue; and in no way shall you be fearful from the coming evils.
JOB 5:22 The unjust and lawless you shall ridicule; and from wild beasts in no way shall you be fearful.
JOB 5:23 For the beasts of the wild shall make peace with you.
JOB 5:24 Then you shall know that your house shall be at peace; and he shall visit your beauty, and in no way should it have sinned.
JOB 5:25 And you shall know that your seed shall be many, and your progeny will be as the abundant herbage of the field.
JOB 5:26 And you shall come unto the grave as grain in season, according to the time of harvesting; or as a heap of the threshing-floor according to the hour of its being collected.
JOB 5:27 Behold, these things thus we tracked out, these things are what we have heard; but you, know in yourself if you acted in anything!
JOB 6:1 And undertaking, Job says,
JOB 6:2 For if anyone stationing weight would set my wrath, and lift my griefs onto a yoke balance scale, they woud be in one accord.
JOB 6:3 For indeed of the sand of the coast it will be heavier - upon this my sayings were trampled.
JOB 6:4 For arrows of the worthy one are in my body, which their rage drinks up my blood. Whenever I begin to speak, they sting me.
JOB 6:5 For what - will the wild donkey ineffectually cry out if he is not seeking grain? and shall then the voice of the ox tear loose at the stable while having foods?
JOB 6:6 Shall bread be eaten without salt? and is there taste in empty words?
JOB 6:7 For my soul is not able to cease; for groaning I see my grain as the scent of a lion.
JOB 6:8 For if only he might give, and my requests might come; and that the LORD might grant my hope.
JOB 6:9 Beginning, let the LORD pierce; but let me not be done away with unto the end!
JOB 6:10 But may my city be the grave, upon which I leaped upon the walls; upon it I shall not spare; for I lied not about the holy sayings of my God.
JOB 6:11 For what is my strength that I remain? or what is my time that my soul endures?
JOB 6:12 Is my strength the strength of stones? or are my flesh members of brass?
JOB 6:13 or not upon him to yield? But help was departed from me;
JOB 6:14 mercy is forbidden me; and the visit of the LORD overlooked me.
JOB 6:15 My brothers looked not at me; they went by me as if a rushing stream dissipating or as if a wave.
JOB 6:16 The ones who revered me, now fall upon me; as if snow or ice banked up,
JOB 6:17 and as the melting away by the coming of heat, it was not recognized of where it was.
JOB 6:18 So I also was left by all; and I am destroyed, and I became homeless.
JOB 6:19 Behold the ways of the Temanites - O ones seeing clearly the short cuts of the Sabaeans.
JOB 6:20 And the ones in cities shall owe for shame, and the things relied upon there.
JOB 6:21 But nevertheless, even you mounted against me mercilessly; so that beholding my wound, you are fearful.
JOB 6:22 For what - did I ask anything of you, or do I want strength from you,
JOB 6:23 so as to deliver me from enemies, or to rescue me from out of the hand of mighty ones?
JOB 6:24 Teach me, and I will be silent! If in anything I have wandered, expound to me!
JOB 6:25 But as it seems, the words of a true man are vile; for I do not ask strength from you.
JOB 6:26 Nor will your reproof cause me to cease my words; for neither your utterance of a word will I endure.
JOB 6:27 Besides that, you fall upon an orphan, and you assail against your friend.
JOB 6:28 But now, having looked into your faces, I will not lie.
JOB 6:29 Sit indeed, and may there not be anything unjust, and again come together with the just one!
JOB 6:30 For there is not an unjust thing on my tongue; or, does not my throat meditate on understanding?
JOB 7:1 In either way is not the existence of man upon the earth a trial, and his life as the daily hireling,
JOB 7:2 or as an attendant in awe of his master, and attaining for shade, or as if a hireling awaiting his wage?
JOB 7:3 So I also waited months in vain; and nights of griefs are given to me.
JOB 7:4 When I should go to bed, I say, When will it be the day? And whenever I rise up, again I say, When will it be evening? And I am full of griefs, from evening unto morning.
JOB 7:5 And my body is befouled in rottenness of worms, and I melt away as clods of earth from scraping pus.
JOB 7:6 And my existence is lighter than speech, and has perished in vain hope.
JOB 7:7 Remember then that my breath is life; and no longer shall my eye return back to behold good.
JOB 7:8 The eye of the one seeing me shall not look round about; your eyes are on me, and I am not.
JOB 7:9 I am as a cloud being cleared away from the heaven; for if a man should go down into Hades, no longer in any way should he ascend;
JOB 7:10 and neither in any way shall he return unto his own house, nor shall his place in any way recognize him any more.
JOB 7:11 Nevertheless then, nor will I spare my mouth; I will speak being in distress of my spirit; I will open the bitterness of my soul being held in.
JOB 7:12 Is it that I am a sea or a dragon, that you delegated a guard over me?
JOB 7:13 I said that, My bed shall comfort me, and I shall offer to myself my own word in my bed.
JOB 7:14 You frighten me with dreams; and with visions you strike terror in me.
JOB 7:15 You will dismiss my soul from my spirit, and my bones from death.
JOB 7:16 For I shall not live into the eon, that I should patiently wait. Depart from me, for my livelihood is empty!
JOB 7:17 For what is man that you magnified him? or that you heed the mind in him?
JOB 7:18 or will you make him a visit until the morning? and shall you judge him for rest?
JOB 7:19 For how long do you not allow me, nor let me go, until whenever I should swallow down my spittle in grief?
JOB 7:20 If I sinned, how am I able to act out against you, O one having knowledge of the mind of men? Why did you establish me as your accuser, and I am a load unto you?
JOB 7:21 And why did you not appoint of my lawlessness to forgetfulness, and for a cleansing of my sin? But now into the earth I shall go forth, and I am no longer for rising early.
JOB 8:1 And undertaking, Baldad the Shuhite, says,
JOB 8:2 Till when shall you speak these things by a talkative spirit of your mouth?
JOB 8:3 Will the LORD transgress judging? or the one making all things disturb the just one?
JOB 8:4 If your sons sin before him, he sent them away in hand because of their lawlessness.
JOB 8:5 But you, rise early to the LORD almighty, beseeching him!
JOB 8:6 If you are pure and true, he will heed your supplication, and he will restore to you the habitation of righteousness.
JOB 8:7 It will be then that as your first shall be little, yet your last will be an untold amount.
JOB 8:8 For ask the first generation, and trace according to the race of the fathers!
JOB 8:9 For we are of yesterday, and have not known; for our existence upon the earth is a shadow.
JOB 8:10 Shall these not teach you, and announce to you, and from out of the heart lead forth sayings?
JOB 8:11 Does papyrus flourish without water? or shall the flowering rush rise up high without drinking?
JOB 8:12 Yet being upon the root, and in no way harvested, shall it not be dried before the drinking of all pasturage?
JOB 8:13 So therefore will it be for the last of all the ones forgetting the LORD; for the hope of an impious one shall perish.
JOB 8:14 For his house will be uninhabited, and his tent will turn out to be as for a spider's web.
JOB 8:15 If one should overlook his house, in no way shall it stand; even grasping it, in no way shall it remain.
JOB 8:16 For it is wet under the sun, and his tender branch shall come forth out of his rottenness.
JOB 8:17 Upon a gathering of stones he goes to bed, and in the midst of gravel he shall live.
JOB 8:18 And if the place should swallow him, it shall lie to him, saying, Have you not seen such a thing?
JOB 8:19 For the undoing of an impious one is such, and from out of the earth another shall sprout up.
JOB 8:20 For the LORD in no way will undo the guileless, and every gift of an impious one he will not receive.
JOB 8:21 But the mouth of true ones he will fill with laughter, and their lips with acknowledgment.
JOB 8:22 But their enemies shall put on shame; and the habitation of an impious one will not be.
JOB 9:1 And undertaking, Job says,
JOB 9:2 In truth I know that it is so; for how shall there be a just mortal before the LORD?
JOB 9:3 For if he should want to enter into judgment with him, in no way shall God obey him, so that he shall not contradict with one word of his from out of a thousand.
JOB 9:4 For he is wise in thought, fortified also, and great. Who being hard before him even made peace?
JOB 9:5 The mountains of old even do not know the one eradicating them in anger;
JOB 9:6 the one shaking the thing under heaven from its foundations, and the columns of it shake;
JOB 9:7 the one speaking to the sun, and it does not rise; and accordingly he seals up the stars;
JOB 9:8 the one stretching the heaven alone, and walking upon the sea as upon a floor;
JOB 9:9 the one making Pleiades and Hesperus and Arcturus, and the chambers of the south;
JOB 9:10 the one doing great and untraceable things; honorable also, and extraordinary things which there is not a number.
JOB 9:11 If he should pass over me, in no way shall I behold it; and if he should go by me, neither thus I knew it.
JOB 9:12 If he dismisses, who returns? or who shall say to him, What did you do?
JOB 9:13 God will not turn away the anger, but under him the sea-monsters under heaven were bent.
JOB 9:14 But then should he obey me, or shall he litigate my things?
JOB 9:15 For even if I should be just, he shall not listen to me. His equity I will beseech.
JOB 9:16 And if I should call, and he should hearken, I do not trust that he has listened to my voice.
JOB 9:17 He should not obliterate me by dimness; but many of my bruises he has made without cause.
JOB 9:18 For he allows me not to breathe, and he filled me with bitterness.
JOB 9:19 For indeed by strength he prevails. Who then shall oppose his judgment?
JOB 9:20 For if I might be just, my mouth will be impious; and though I might be blameless, I shall turn out perverse.
JOB 9:21 For whether I was impious, I do not know in the soul; besides, life is removed from me.
JOB 9:22 Therefore I said, he destroys the great and mighty one in wrath.
JOB 9:23 For the vile ones are extraordinary in death, but the just ones are ridiculed,
JOB 9:24 for they are delivered into the hands of an impious one; he covers up the faces of her judges; but if not he, who is it?
JOB 9:25 But my existence is lighter than a runner; my days ran away, and they knew it not.
JOB 9:26 Or also is there a trace of ships in the way? or a trace of an eagle flying seeking prey?
JOB 9:27 For if also I said, I shall forget about speaking, I will stoop down my countenance and I will moan.
JOB 9:28 I shake in all my limbs, for I know that you will not let me be innocent.
JOB 9:29 But since I am impious, for why is this I labor in vain?
JOB 9:30 For if I should wash myself off with snow, and should clear away my hands clean,
JOB 9:31 fittingly in my filth you dipped me, and my apparel abhorred me.
JOB 9:32 For you are not a man like me, with whom I can judge by comparison, that we should come with one accord for judgment.
JOB 9:33 If indeed our mediator was present, and the one reproving, and the one hearing between both,
JOB 9:34 let him dismiss the rod from me, and let not the fear of him whirl about;
JOB 9:35 and in no way shall I fear, but I will speak; for I am not thus conscious of guilt.
JOB 10:1 Being weary in my soul, in moaning I will let loose upon myself my sayings; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul, being constrained.
JOB 10:2 And I will say to the LORD, Teach me not to be impious! And why have you so judged me?
JOB 10:3 Or is it good to you that I should transgress? that I should forbid the works of your hands? and did you heed the counsel of impious ones?
JOB 10:4 Or as a mortal sees - do you look? or as a man sees - shall you see?
JOB 10:5 Or your existence - is it mankind? or your years - a man's?
JOB 10:6 For you searched out my lawlessnesses, and you traced my sins.
JOB 10:7 For you know that I did not act impious; but who is the one rescuing from out of your hands?
JOB 10:8 Your hands shaped me and made me; after these things in turning you smote me.
JOB 10:9 Remember that you shaped me of clay, and unto the earth again you return me.
JOB 10:10 Or did you not extract me as milk, and curdled me equal to cheese?
JOB 10:11 But skin and meat you put on me, and with bones and nerves you entwined me.
JOB 10:12 And life and mercy you put upon me, and of your overseeing you guarded my spirit.
JOB 10:13 Having these things in yourself, I know that you are able to do all things; and not one thing is impossible with you.
JOB 10:14 For if I should sin, you guard me; but from lawlessness you have not appointed me innocent.
JOB 10:15 For if I should be impious, alas. But if I might be just, I am not able to lift up the head, for I am full of dishonor.
JOB 10:16 For I am caught as a lion for slaughter; and again in turning you destroy me awfully;
JOB 10:17 renewing upon me my chastisement; and you dealt with me in great anger, and brought trials against me.
JOB 10:18 Why then in the belly did you lead me out, and I did not die, that an eye did not see me,
JOB 10:19 and that I became as if one not being? For why was I not dismissed from the womb unto the tomb?
JOB 10:20 Or is not the time of my existence little? Allow me to rest a little,
JOB 10:21 before my going from where I shall not return, unto a land dark and dim;
JOB 10:22 unto a land of eternal darkness, where there is not brightness, nor seeing the life of mortals!
JOB 11:1 And undertaking, Sophar the Minean says,
JOB 11:2 The one saying many things also shall listen in turn; or does the well-spoken imagine himself to be just? Blessed be the one born of woman short-lived.
JOB 11:3 Become not many in words; for there is not one judging you by comparison.
JOB 11:4 For do not say that, I am pure in the works, and blameless before him.
JOB 11:5 But how ever is the LORD to speak to you, and open his lips with you;
JOB 11:6 then he shall announce to you the power of wisdom, that it will be double to the things of yours. And then you shall know that what is worthy to you resulted from the LORD whom you have sinned.
JOB 11:7 Or will you find the trace of the LORD? or, did you arrive unto the latter end which the almighty prepared?
JOB 11:8 Heaven is high; and what will you do? and of the things deeper in Hades; what do you know?
JOB 11:9 or longer than the measure of the earth, or the breadth of the sea.
JOB 11:10 And if he shall eradicate all things, who will say to him, What did you do?
JOB 11:11 For he knows the works of the lawless; and beholding he shall not overlook the things out of place.
JOB 11:12 But man otherwise shall be over-confident with words; but a mortal born of a woman is equal to a recluse donkey.
JOB 11:13 For if you established your heart clean, and turned up and opened your hands to him;
JOB 11:14 if there is any lawless thing in your hands, cause it to be at a distance! and let not injustice lodge in your habitation!
JOB 11:15 For thus your face shall illuminate as if pure water; and you shall strip off filth, and in no way shall you be fearful.
JOB 11:16 And you shall forget trouble as a wave going by; and you shall not be terrified.
JOB 11:17 And your vow will be as Hesperus; and from midday life shall arise to you.
JOB 11:18 And you shall be complying, for it is hope to you; and from anxiety and bewilderment peace shall appear to you.
JOB 11:19 For you shall be tranquil, and there will not be one waging war against you; and turning, many will beseech you.
JOB 11:20 But deliverance shall leave them, for their hope is destruction; and the eyes of impious ones shall melt away.
JOB 12:1 And undertaking, Job says,
JOB 12:2 So then you are men; then wisdom comes to an end with you?
JOB 12:3 There is also to me indeed a heart like yours.
JOB 12:4 For a just man, and blameless, was born for an object for taunts.
JOB 12:5 For at an appointed time man had been prepared to fall under others; also for his house to be pillaged by lawless ones. But let not however any one being wicked rely on to be considered innocent -
JOB 12:6 as many as provoke the LORD to anger, as if there will not also be their chastisement.
JOB 12:7 But indeed ask the four-footed beasts, if they should speak to you; or birds of the heaven, if they were able to report to you!
JOB 12:8 And let the earth tell in detail, if it should expound to you; and the fishes of the sea shall describe to you!
JOB 12:9 Who knew not among all these that the hand of the LORD made these?
JOB 12:10 Except in his hand is the life of all of the living, and the breath of every man.
JOB 12:11 For the ear indeed scrutinizes words, and the throat tastes grains.
JOB 12:12 In a long time is wisdom; and in a long existence is higher knowledge.
JOB 12:13 By him is wisdom and power; with him counsel and understanding.
JOB 12:14 If he should throw down, who shall build up? If he locks against man, who opens?
JOB 12:15 If he should restrain the water, he shall dry the earth; and if he should slacken, he destroys it by eradication.
JOB 12:16 By him is might and strength; in him is higher knowledge and understanding;
JOB 12:17 leading counselors as captives, and judges of the earth he amazes;
JOB 12:18 sitting kings upon thrones, and ties a belt on their loins;
JOB 12:19 sending priests as captives, and the mighty ones of the earth he eradicates;
JOB 12:20 reconciling lips of the trustworthy, and the understanding of the elders he knew;
JOB 12:21 pouring out dishonor upon rulers, but the humble he healed;
JOB 12:22 uncovering the deeps from out of darkness, and he leads the shadow of death into light;
JOB 12:23 wandering nations, and destroying them; prostrating nations, and directing them;
JOB 12:24 reconciling hearts of rulers of the earth, but wandering them in a way which they knew not.
JOB 12:25 May they handle darkness, and not light; may they be wandering as if one being intoxicated.
JOB 13:1 Behold, my eye has seen these things, and my ear has heard.
JOB 13:2 And I know as much as even you know; and I am not more senseless than you.
JOB 13:3 But nevertheless, I will speak to the LORD; and I will reprove before him, if he should be willing.
JOB 13:4 But you are unjust physicians, and are all bad healers.
JOB 13:5 But it may be good for you to be silent, and it shall turn out to you for wisdom.
JOB 13:6 Hear the reproof of my mouth, and heed the judgment of my lips!
JOB 13:7 Is it not against the LORD you speak, and before him you utter a sound of deceit?
JOB 13:8 Or will you keep back? But you yourselves have become judges!
JOB 13:9 Is it good if he should track you? for as if the ones doing all things shall you be added to him?
JOB 13:10 In not one thing less shall he reprove you; but if also you shall secretly wonder at persons,
JOB 13:11 is it not in his awfulness that he shall whirl you, and fear of him shall fall upon you?
JOB 13:12 But your prancing shall turn out equal to ashes, and the body to clay.
JOB 13:13 Be silent, that I shall speak, and rest my rage!
JOB 13:14 Taking my flesh in my teeth, even I shall put my life in my hand.
