PRO 22:10 Cast out from the sanhedrin the mischievous one, and altercation shall go out together with him! For whenever he sits in the sanhedrin he dishonors all.
PRO 22:11 The LORD loves sacred hearts; and all unblemished ones are acceptable to him in their ways. A king tends with his lips.
PRO 22:12 But the eyes of the LORD carefully keep good sense; but he treats as worthless the words of a lawbreaker.
PRO 22:13 The lazy one makes an excuse and says, There is a lion in the streets, and in the squares are murderers.
PRO 22:14 The mouth of a lawbreaker is a deep cesspool; and the one being detested by the LORD shall fall into it.
PRO 22:15 Thoughtlessness lights up the heart of a young person; but the rod and instruction will drive it far from him.
PRO 22:16 The one extorting the needy produces many evils for himself; and gives to the rich to make it less.
PRO 22:17 Set aside your ear to the words of the wise, and hear my words! And set your heart that you should know!
PRO 22:18 for they are good, and if you put them in your heart, they shall gladden you at the same time upon your lips;
PRO 22:19 that your hope should be upon the LORD, and he shall make known to you his way;
PRO 22:20 but also you register them to yourself, even thrice for counsel and knowledge!
PRO 22:21 I teach you then a true word, and knowledge good to hearken to; for you to answer words of truth to the ones propounding things to you.
PRO 22:22 Do not repel the needy, for he is poor! And you shall not dishonor the weak at the gates.
PRO 22:23 For the LORD will arbitrate his cause, and you shall rescue your soul against reprisal.
PRO 22:24 Be not a companion to a man inclined to rage! and a friend prone to anger do not lodge with!
PRO 22:25 lest at any time you should learn of his ways, and should receive nooses for your soul.
PRO 22:26 Do not give yourself for surety, shaming the face!
PRO 22:27 For if you should not have from any place to pay, they shall take the bedding under your sides.
PRO 22:28 Do not remove the everlasting boundaries which your fathers set!
PRO 22:29 An observant man, and one sharp in his works must stand beside kings, and should not stand beside dull men.
PRO 23:1 If you should sit to have supper at the table of a monarch, intelligibly comprehend the things being placed near to you!
PRO 23:2 And give attention to your hand, beholding that it is a must for you to make preparations for such things! But if you are insatiable,
PRO 23:3 do not desire his food! for these have a false life.
PRO 23:4 Do not reach forth, being needy, to the rich; but in your insight be at a distance!
PRO 23:5 If you set your eye upon him, he shall not at all appear; for there are carefully prepared for him wings as of an eagle, and he returns to the house being set for him.
PRO 23:6 Do not dine with a bewitching man, nor desire his foods;
PRO 23:7 for in which manner as if any may swallow down a hair, thus he eats and drinks; nor should you bring him to yourself, nor you should eat your morsel with him,
PRO 23:8 for he will vomit it forth, and lay waste your good words.
PRO 23:9 Do not speak into the ears of a foolish one, lest at any time he sneer at discerning your words!
PRO 23:10 You should not transpose the everlasting boundaries; and to the possession of orphans you should not enter to take;
PRO 23:11 for the one ransoming them is the LORD; he is strong, and he arbitrates their case with you.
PRO 23:12 Give your heart for instruction, and prepare your ears for words of good sense!
PRO 23:13 You should not be at a distance to correct the simple; for if you strike him with a rod, in no way should he die;
PRO 23:14 forasmuch as you struck him with a rod, then you rescued his soul from death.
PRO 23:15 O son, if you should make your heart wise, you shall gladden also my heart;
PRO 23:16 and the words of your lips shall spend time with my lips, if they should be straight.
PRO 23:17 Let not your heart be jealous of sinners, but be in the fear of the LORD the whole day!
PRO 23:18 For if you should give heed to these things there will be a progeny for you, and your hope will not leave.
PRO 23:19 Hear, O son, and be wise, and straighten out the reflections of your heart!
PRO 23:20 Do not be a winebibber, nor stretch out couplings, nor purchasings of meats!
PRO 23:21 For every intoxicated one and whoremonger shall be poor; and every sleepy one shall put on torn and ragged garments.
PRO 23:22 Hear, O son, the father engendering you, and do not disdain that your mother has grown old!
PRO 23:23 Acquire truth! and you should not thrust away wisdom and instruction and understanding.
PRO 23:24 A just father nourishes well; and his soul is gladdened by a wise son.
PRO 23:25 Let your father and mother be glad over you; and let the one who gave birth to you rejoice!
PRO 23:26 Give to me, O son, your heart, and let your eyes give heed to my ways!
PRO 23:27 For a strange house is a cask having been drilled; and a strange well is narrow.
PRO 23:28 For this one suddenly shall perish, and every lawbreaker shall be consumed.
PRO 23:29 To whom is there woe? to whom a tumult? to whom litigations? to whom rancor and intrigue? to whom breaks without cause? to whom dark colored eyes?
PRO 23:30 Is it not the ones lingering in wines? Is it not the ones prowling where parties happen? Do not be intoxicated by wine, but consort with just men, and consort in the promenades!
PRO 23:31 For if in the bowls and the cups you should give your eyes, afterwards you shall walk more naked than a pestle.
PRO 23:32 But at last it will be as if being struck by a serpent he stretches out, and as if by a horned serpent the poison diffuses throughout him.
PRO 23:33 Whenever your eyes behold the strange woman, your mouth then speaks perverse things;
PRO 23:34 and you shall recline as if in the heart of the sea; and as a navigator in a great swell;
PRO 23:35 and you shall say, They beat me, and I pained not; and, They mocked me, but I knew not. When will it be dawn, that coming I shall seek after one who shall go together with me to drink?
PRO 24:1 O son, you should not be jealous of evil men, nor should you desire to be with them.
PRO 24:2 For their heart meditates on lying, and their lips speak of miseries.
PRO 24:3 A house is built with wisdom, and erected with skillfulness.
PRO 24:4 With good sense the storerooms are filled up of all valuable and good wealth.
PRO 24:5 A wise one is better than a strong man; a man of intelligence than one having a great farm.
PRO 24:6 War takes place with guidance, but help comes with the heart of a counselor.
PRO 24:7 Wisdom and good insight are in the gates of the wise. The wise do not turn aside from the law of the LORD, but consider things in the sanhedrins; but the uninstructed ones meet with death,
PRO 24:9 but a foolish one dies in sins. Uncleanness to a pestilent man -
PRO 24:10 he shall be contaminated in the evil day, and in the day of affliction, until whenever he should cease.
PRO 24:11 Rescue the ones being led for death, and buy off the ones for slaying! You should not spare.
PRO 24:12 But if you should say, I do not know this; know that the LORD knows the heart of all - even the one shaping the breath in all, he knows all. He is the one who renders to each according to his works.
PRO 24:13 Eat honey, O son, for the honeycomb is good, that your throat should be sweetened!
PRO 24:14 For thus you shall perceive wisdom in your soul; for if you should find it, your decease will be good, and hope shall not forsake you.
PRO 24:15 You should not lead an impious one to a pasture of the just ones; nor should you be deceived in filling the belly.
PRO 24:16 For seven times the just one shall fall, and rise up; but the impious ones will weaken in evils.
PRO 24:17 If your enemy should fall, you should not rejoice over him; and in his fall be not lifted up!
PRO 24:18 For the LORD shall see, and it will not be pleasing to him; and he will return his rage unto him.
PRO 24:19 Do not rejoice over ones doing evil, nor be jealous of sinners!
PRO 24:20 For not in any way shall there be a progeny of wicked ones; but the torch of the impious ones shall be extinguished.
PRO 24:21 Fear God, O son, and the king! And to neither one of them should you resist persuasion.
PRO 24:22 For suddenly they will pay the impious ones; and the punishment of both, who shall know?
PRO 24:23 But these things I say to you, to the wise, to realize that to stand in awe of a person in a judgment is not good.
PRO 24:24 The one having said, The impious one is a just one, will be accursed among the peoples, and detested among the nations.
PRO 24:25 But the ones reproving him shall appear the best; and a good blessing shall come upon them;
PRO 24:26 but lips shall kiss the ones answering with good words.
PRO 24:27 Prepare your works for the departure, and make preparations for the field, and go after me, and you shall rebuild your house!
PRO 24:28 Do not be a lying witness against your fellow-countryman, nor open wide with your lips!
PRO 24:29 You should not say, In which manner he treated me, I shall treat him; and I shall pay him who wronged me.
PRO 24:30 A foolish man is as a farm, and a man lacking of sense is as a vineyard;
PRO 24:31 if you should let it go barren, then it shall become entirely overgrown, and failing takes place, and his fences of stones shall be razed.
PRO 24:32 Afterwards I changed my mind; I looked to choose instruction.
PRO 24:33 I slumber a little; and I sleep soundly a little, and I fold my hands to my breasts a little.
PRO 24:34 But if you should do this, poverty shall come before you, and lack as a good runner.
PRO 25:1 These are the impartial parables of Solomon, which the friends of Hezekiah the king of Judea wrote out.
PRO 25:2 The glory of God hides a matter; but the glory of a king esteems things.
PRO 25:3 Heaven is high, and the earth is deep; but the heart of a king is unascertained.
PRO 25:4 Beat unproven silver, and it shall be cleansed clean all together!
PRO 25:5 Slay the impious ones from the presence of a king, and you shall set up his throne in righteousness!
PRO 25:6 Do not act ostentatiously in the presence of a king, nor stand in places of mighty ones!
PRO 25:7 For better the saying to you, Ascend to me! than to humble you in the presence of a mighty one. What you beheld with your eyes, speak!
PRO 25:8 Do not fall into a fight quickly, lest you should change your mind at the last! When ever a friend should berate you,
PRO 25:9 withdraw to the rear - do not disdain him;
PRO 25:10 lest indeed the friend should berate you, and your fight and hatred do not go away, but will be to you equal of death! Favor and friendship frees, which you give heed to yourself, that you should not be reviled! But keep your ways conciliatory!
PRO 25:11 As a golden apple in a pendant of sardius, so is it to speak a wise word.
PRO 25:12 In an ear-ring of gold, a very costly sardius is bound set.; so a wise word to a heedful ear.
PRO 25:13 As a delivery of snow in the harvest for sweltering heat, so a trustworthy messenger benefits the ones sending him; for the souls of the ones dealing with him derive benefit.
PRO 25:14 As winds, and clouds, and rains are apparent, so the men boasting over false portions.
PRO 25:15 Success comes to kings by long-suffering, and a soft tongue breaks bones.
PRO 25:16 In finding honey, eat what is enough, lest at any time being overfilled, you should vomit forth!
PRO 25:17 Sparingly bring your foot to your own friend, lest at any time he be filled of you, and should detest you!
PRO 25:18 As a club, and a sword, and a pointed bow, so also the man bearing false witness against his friend.
PRO 25:19 An evil way and the foot of a lawbreaker shall be destroyed in an evil day.
PRO 25:20 As vinegar draws hurtful, so passion falling on a body distresses the heart. As a moth in a garment, and a worm in wood, so distress of a man hurts the heart.
PRO 25:21 If your enemy hungers, nourish him! If he thirsts, give him to drink!
PRO 25:22 For doing this you shall heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD will recompense to you good things.
PRO 25:23 The north wind arouses clouds; and the face of an impudent tongue aggravates.
PRO 25:24 Better to live upon the corner of a roof, than with a reviling wife in a common house.
PRO 25:25 As cold water is kind to a thirsting soul, so a good message from a land far off.
PRO 25:26 As if any one may shut up a spring, and may lay waste an exiting of water; so it is unbecoming for a just one to fall before an impious one.
PRO 25:27 To eat much honey is not good; but it behooves to esteem honorable words.
PRO 25:28 As a city with walls having been thrown down and unwalled, so a man who acts in anything not with counsel.
PRO 26:1 As dew in harvest, and as rain in summer, so honor is not to a foolish one.
PRO 26:2 As birds and sparrows spread out to fly, so a vain oath shall not come unto one thing.
PRO 26:3 As a whip to a horse, and a spur to a donkey, so a rod to a lawbreaking nation.
PRO 26:4 Do not give an answer to a foolish one according to that one's folly, lest you should become likened to him!
PRO 26:5 But answer to a foolish one to the folly of that one, lest he should appear wise unto himself!
PRO 26:6 The one sending a word through a foolish messenger shall cause scorn by his own ways.
PRO 26:7 Remove the goings of legs, and proverbs from out of the mouth of foolish ones.
PRO 26:8 One who binds up a stone in a sling, is likened to giving glory to a foolish one.
PRO 26:9 Thorn-bushes germinate in the hand of the intoxicated, and servitude in the hand of the foolish ones.
PRO 26:10 All the flesh of foolish ones is tossed much by a storm, for their ecstasy is destroyed.
PRO 26:11 As a dog whenever it comes upon its own vomit, and becomes detested, so a foolish one returning to his own evil, unto his own sin.
PRO 26:12 I beheld a man seeming to be wise unto himself, however a foolish one had more hope rather than he.
PRO 26:13 The lazy one says when being sent into the way, A lion is in the ways, and in the squares are murderers.
PRO 26:14 As a door turns upon the hinge, so the lazy one turns upon his bed.
PRO 26:15 The lazy one hiding the hand in his bosom shall not be able to bring it unto the mouth.
PRO 26:16 The lazy one appears wiser to himself in fulfilling transmitting a message.
PRO 26:17 As the one holding the tail of a dog, so the one setting himself over a stranger's case.
PRO 26:18 As the ones needing healing propound words unto men, and the first one meeting the word shall be tripped up.
PRO 26:19 Thus are all the ones lying in wait for their own friends;, and whenever they should be caught in the act, they say that, In playing I acted.
PRO 26:20 With much wood fire flourishes; but where there is not a man at variance with others a fight is stilled.
PRO 26:21 A grate for coals, and wood for a fire; and a reviling man for a disturbance to a fight.
PRO 26:22 Words of mischievous ones are soft, but these beat into the inner chambers of the intestines.
PRO 26:23 Silver given with treachery is as a potsherd esteemed. Smooth lips cover a distressed heart.
PRO 26:24 An enemy weeping assents to all things with his lips, but in the heart he contrives treachery.
PRO 26:25 If the enemy should beseech you with a great voice, do not yield to him; for there are seven wickednesses in his heart.
PRO 26:26 The one hiding his hatred stands together with treachery, and he conceals the things of his own well-known sins in the sanhedrin.
PRO 26:27 The one digging a pit for his neighbor shall fall into it; and the one rolling a stone, rolls it upon himself.
PRO 26:28 A lying tongue detests truth; and an open-mouthed mouth makes commotion.
PRO 27:1 Do not boast the things for tomorrow; for you know not what the coming day shall give birth to!
PRO 27:2 Let the one near laud you, and not your mouth; a stranger, and not your lips!
PRO 27:3 A stone is heavy, and sand hard to bear; but anger of a foolish one is heavier than both.
PRO 27:4 Rage is unmerciful, and anger is sharp; but no one stands before jealousy.
PRO 27:5 Revealing reproofs is better than hiding friendship.
PRO 27:6 More worthy of trust are wounds of a friend, than voluntary kisses of an enemy.
PRO 27:7 A soul being in fullness mocks honeycombs; but a soul lacking, even the bitter things appear sweet.
PRO 27:8 As a bird whenever it flies down from out of its own nest; so a man is enslaved whenever he estranges himself from out of his own places.
PRO 27:9 Perfumes, and wines, and incenses make the heart happy; but the soul breaks down by adverse incidents.
PRO 27:10 Your friend or paternal friend you should not abandon; but to the house of your brother you should not enter in adversity; better a friend near, than a brother living far.
PRO 27:11 Become wise, O son, that the heart should gladden me, and turn reviling words from you!
PRO 27:12 A clever man, of evils coming along, conceals himself; but foolish ones coming along, shall pay a penalty.
PRO 27:13 Remove his garment, for an insulting man passed by, one who lays waste a stranger's goods!
PRO 27:14 Who ever shall bless a friend in the morning with a great voice, shall not seem to differ from one cursing.
PRO 27:15 Drops of rain on a day of winter shall cast a man from out of his house; likewise also a reviling wife drives a man from out of his own house.
PRO 27:16 The north wind is hard, but is called by name fittingly.
PRO 27:17 Iron sharpens iron; and a man sharpens the face of his companion.
PRO 27:18 The one who plants a fig-tree shall eat the fruits of it; and the one who guards his own master shall be esteemed.
PRO 27:19 As faces are not likened to other faces, so not even are the hearts likened to other men's.
PRO 27:20 Hades and destruction are not filled up; likewise also the eyes of the insatiable man. One fixing the eye is an abomination to the LORD, and the uninstructed ones are immoderate in tongue.
PRO 27:21 Proving silver and gold is through burning by fire; but a man is tried by the mouth of ones lauding him.
PRO 27:22 If you whip a foolish one in the midst of a sanhedrin, dishonoring him, in no way shall his folly be removed.
PRO 27:23 Knowingly, you shall recognize things concerning the lives of your flock, and you shall set your heart over your herds.
PRO 27:24 For might and strength to a man are not into the eon; nor does he deliver it up from generation to generation.
PRO 27:25 Care for the green things in the field, and you shall shear the herbage! And gather together grass of the mountainous area,
PRO 27:26 that you should have sheep's wool for clothes! Esteem a field, that there might be lambs to you!
PRO 27:27 O son, you have strong sayings from me for your life, and for the life of your attendants.
PRO 28:1 An impious one flees with no one pursuing; but a just one is secure as a lion.
PRO 28:2 Because of the sins of impious ones, litigations arise; but a clever man extinguishes them.
PRO 28:3 A vigorous man with impious deeds extorts the poor as a fierce and unprofitable rain.
PRO 28:4 Thus the ones abandoning the law laud impiety; but the ones loving the law put a wall around themselves.
PRO 28:5 Evil men do not comprehend equity; but the ones seeking the LORD perceive in all.
PRO 28:6 Better a poor man going in truth, than a rich liar.
PRO 28:7 A discerning son keeps the law; but the one who tends carnality dishonors his father.
PRO 28:8 The one multiplying his wealth with interest and usury, gathers it to the one showing mercy on the poor.
PRO 28:9 The one turning aside his ear to not hear the law, even he abhors his own prayer.
PRO 28:10 The one who wanders upright men in an evil way, shall himself fall into corruption; and the lawless ones shall go through good things, and they shall not enter to them.
PRO 28:11 A rich man is wise to himself; but an intelligent needy man shall condemn him.
PRO 28:12 Through the help of the just ones, much glory comes to pass; but in the places of the impious ones, men are being captured.
PRO 28:13 The one covering over his impiety, his way shall not be prospered; but the one describing and reproving shall be loved.
PRO 28:14 Blessed is a man who is struck with awe of all things through veneration; but the hard of heart shall fall into evils.
PRO 28:15 A lion hungering, and a wolf thirsting, is the one who is sovereign of a destitute nation being poor.
PRO 28:16 A king lacking revenue is a great extortioner; but the one detesting injustice shall live a long time.
PRO 28:17 The one guaranteeing a loan of a man under accusation of murder will be an exile, and not in safety.
PRO 28:18 The one going justly is helped; but the one going by crooked ways shall be entangled.
PRO 28:19 The one working his own land shall be filled of breads; but the one pursuing ease shall be filled with poverty.
PRO 28:20 A man worthy of trust in many things shall be blessed; but the evil one shall not be unpunished.
PRO 28:21 The one who does not feel respect for persons of the just ones is not good; such a one will deliver over a man for a morsel of bread.
PRO 28:22 A bewitching man hastens to be rich, and does not know that a merciful man will prevail over him.
PRO 28:23 The one reproving a man's ways shall have favors, rather than the flatterer with the tongue.
PRO 28:24 The one who throws off his father or mother, and assumes he does not sin - this one is partner of an impious man.
PRO 28:25 An insatiable man judges in vain; but the one yielding upon the LORD will be in care.
PRO 28:26 One who yields to a rash heart, such a one is a foolish one; but one who goes in wisdom shall be delivered.
PRO 28:27 The one who gives to the poor shall not be in want; but the one who turns his eye will be in much perplexity.
PRO 28:28 In the places of the impious ones the just ones moan; but in the destruction of those the just ones shall be multiplied.
PRO 29:1 Better a man of reproofs, than a man hard-necked; for suddenly there is not a healing blazing up for him.
PRO 29:2 In the lauding of the just ones peoples will be glad; but men moan over the rules of the impious ones.
PRO 29:3 A man fond of wisdom gladdens his father; but the one tending harlots destroys wealth.
PRO 29:4 A just king establishes regions; but a lawbreaking man razes them.
PRO 29:5 The one who makes preparations with a net against the person of his own friend puts it around his own feet.
PRO 29:6 A great snare is set against a man sinning; but a just one will be in joy and in gladness.
PRO 29:7 A just one has knowledge to judge for the destitute; but the impious one does not comprehend knowledge; and to the poor there does not exist the mind of an arbitrator.
PRO 29:8 Mischievous men burn away a city; but the wise turn away anger.
PRO 29:9 A wise man judges nations; but a heedless man, in provoking to anger, ridicules and is not struck with awe.
PRO 29:10 Men being partners of blood shall detest the sacred; but the upright will seek after his soul.
PRO 29:11 The foolish one brings forth his entire rage; but a wise one stores up in part.
PRO 29:12 A king hearkening in an unjust matter makes all the ones under him lawbreakers.
PRO 29:13 A money-lender and debtor, when one another come together the LORD commits to oversee both.
PRO 29:14 A king judging the poor in truth; his throne shall be established for a good testimony.
PRO 29:15 Strokes and reproofs give wisdom; but a child wandering shames his parents.
PRO 29:16 Of impious ones being many, many sins take place; but the just ones - of the falling of those fear takes place.
PRO 29:17 Correct your son, and he will cause you rest; and he will give a decoration to your soul.
PRO 29:18 In no way should there exist an expositor to a lawbreaking nation; but the one keeping the law is most blessed.
PRO 29:19 A recalcitrant domestic servant will not be corrected by words; for even if he comprehends he will not obey.
PRO 29:20 If you should behold a man hasty in words, know that the foolish one has hope rather than he!
PRO 29:21 The one who lives wastefully from child hood will be a domestic servant; and at the end will grieve over himself.
PRO 29:22 A man inclined to rage digs up altercation; and a man prone to anger gouges up sin.
PRO 29:23 Insolence abases a man; but the LORD establishes the humble-minded in glory.
PRO 29:24 The one who shares with a thief detests his own soul. And if an oath having been set before ones hearing, but they should not announce it,
PRO 29:25 they, fearing and shaming men, shall be tripped up; but the one yielding upon the LORD shall be glad. Impiety in man makes a man trip; but the one yielding unto the master shall be preserved.
PRO 29:26 Many attend to the persons of leaders; but by the LORD the just thing happens to a man.
PRO 29:27 A just man is an abomination to an unjust man; and an abomination to the lawless one is a straight way.
PRO 30:1 Thus speaks the man to the ones trusting in God. And now I will cease,
PRO 30:2 for I am all together most foolish of men, and the intelligence of man is not in me.
PRO 30:3 God has taught me wisdom, and I know the knowledge of the holies.
PRO 30:4 Who ascended into the heaven, and came down? Who brought together the winds in his bosom? Who bundled up waters in his cloak? Who holds all the extremities of the earth? What name is given to him? Or what name to his children that you should know?
PRO 30:5 For all the words of God are purified. And he himself shields the ones venerating him.
PRO 30:6 You should not add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you should become a liar.
PRO 30:7 Two things I ask from you; you should not remove favor from me before my dying;
PRO 30:8 appoint the vain and false word far from me; and riches and poverty you should not give to me; but order up to me the things necessary, and the things to be self-sufficient;
PRO 30:9 that I should not become false in being filled up, and should say, Who sees me? Or to be in need that I shall steal, and I shall swear an oath by the name of God.
PRO 30:10 You should not deliver a bondservant into the hands of a master, lest at any time he should curse you, and you should be obliterated.
PRO 30:11 A bad progeny curses a father, and blesses not the mother.
PRO 30:12 A bad progeny judges himself as just, and washes not his going out.
PRO 30:13 A bad progeny has lofty eyes, and with his eyelids he lifts himself up.
PRO 30:14 A bad progeny has swords for teeth, and the molars as pruning knives, so as to consume the weak from the earth, and the needy of them from among men.
PRO 30:15 There were three daughters to the leech being loved in affection. These three fulfilled her not, and to the fourth it was not sufficient to say, Enough -
PRO 30:16 Hades, and passion of a woman, and earth not filled with water; and water and fire in no way shall say, It suffices.
PRO 30:17 The eye ridiculing a father, and dishonoring the old age of a mother - let the crows from the ravines cut it out, and may the young of the eagles devour it.
PRO 30:18 And there are three things impossible for me to comprehend, and the fourth I do not know -
PRO 30:19 the traces of a flying eagle, and the ways of a serpent upon a rock, and the paths of a ship passing through the sea, and the ways of a man in youth.
PRO 30:20 Such is the way of an adulterous wife. Whenever she should act in washing herself, she says not to have acted out of place.
PRO 30:21 By three things the earth is shaken, and the fourth it is not able to bear -
PRO 30:22 if a domestic servant should reign, and a foolish one should be filled of food,
PRO 30:23 and a female domestic servant, if she is cast out by her own lady, and a hateful wife if she should attain a good man.
PRO 30:24 And there are four lesser things upon the earth, and these are wiser of the wise ones -
PRO 30:25 the ants in whom there is no strength, and they prepare nourishment in summer.
PRO 30:26 And the rabbits - a nation not being strong, the ones making their own houses in the rocks.
PRO 30:27 The locust is independent, but she marches orderly from one word of command.
PRO 30:28 And the newt, with its hands sticking, and being easily caught, it dwells in the fortresses of kings.
PRO 30:29 And there are three which go prosperously, and the fourth which passes over well -
PRO 30:30 a lion cub is stronger than the beasts, which does not turn away, nor is struck with awe of any beast;
PRO 30:31 and a rooster walking about among females confidently; and a he-goat taking the lead of a flock of goats; and a king delivering a public address to a nation.
PRO 30:32 If you should let go of yourself in gladness, and should stretch out your hand for a fight, you shall be dishonored.
PRO 30:33 Extract milk, and there will be butter; but if you should pressure the nostrils there shall come forth blood; and if you should drag out words, there shall come forth litigations and fights.
PRO 31:1 My words have been spoken by God; the divine answer by a king whom his mother instructed.
PRO 31:2 What, O child, will you give heed to? What sayings of God, O first-born, to you I speak, O son? What, O child of my belly? What, O child of my vows?
PRO 31:3 You should not give your wealth to women, nor your mind and livelihood for an afterthought. Do all things with counsel! Drink wine with counsel!
PRO 31:4 The mighty ones are inclined to rage; let them not drink wine,
PRO 31:5 lest drinking they should forget wisdom, and in no way are able rightly to judge the weak!
PRO 31:6 Give intoxication to the ones in distresses, and wine to drink to the ones in griefs,
PRO 31:7 that they should forget their poverty, and of the miseries they should not be remembered any longer!
PRO 31:8 O Son, open your mouth with the word of God, and judge all fairly!
PRO 31:9 Open your mouth, and judge justly, and litigate for the needy and weak!
PRO 31:10 Who shall find a vigorous wife? For such is more esteemed than very costly stones.
PRO 31:11 The heart of her husband takes courage over her. Such a one will not be distressed by the lack of good spoils.
PRO 31:12 For she exerts energy to her husband for good, and not bad, for all the livelihood.
PRO 31:13 She makes her hands useful furling wool and flax.
PRO 31:14 She became as a ship trading far off; she gathers together her wealth.
PRO 31:15 And she rises up at nights, and appoints foods to the household, and works to the female attendants.
PRO 31:16 In viewing a farm, she buys; and from the fruits of her hands she plants a possession.
PRO 31:17 Girding up her loin strongly, she establishes her arms for work.
PRO 31:18 She tastes that it is good to work; and her lamp is not extinguished all the night.
PRO 31:19 She stretches out her cubits unto the things being advantageous; and the things of her hands she sticks to the spindle.
PRO 31:20 And she opens wide her hands to the needy, and her wrist she stretches out to the poor.
PRO 31:21 Her husband does not take thought of the things in the house whenever he passes time somewhere; for all the ones of hers are being clothed.
PRO 31:22 A double goat's hair coat she made for her husband; and from out of linen and purple material garments for herself.
PRO 31:23 And her husband is admired at the gate when ever he should sit in the sanhedrin with the aged of the land.
PRO 31:24 She makes fine linen, and gives back loincloths to the Canaanites.
PRO 31:25 She puts on strength and beauty, and is glad in the last days.
PRO 31:26 And of her mouth she opens wisely and lawfully; and her charity is in her tongue.
PRO 31:27 The pastimes to her house are roofed, and the grain of laziness she eats not.
PRO 31:28 She raises up her children, and they grow rich; and her husband praises her.
PRO 31:29 Many daughters acquired riches; many acted with ability; but you have precedence - you are elevated above all.
PRO 31:30 Allurement is false, and vain beauty is not in you. For a discerning woman is blessed; and let her praise the fear of the LORD!
PRO 31:31 Give to her from the fruits of her lips, and let her husband be praised at the gates!
ECC 1:1 The sayings of an ecclesiastic, son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem.
ECC 1:2 Folly of follies, said the ecclesiastic, folly of follies - all things are folly.
ECC 1:3 What is abundance to man in all his trouble in which he is troubled under the sun?
ECC 1:4 A generation goes, and a generation comes; and the earth is established into the eon.
ECC 1:5 And the sun rises, and the sun goes down, and it draws unto its place.
ECC 1:6 In its rising it goes forth to the south, and it circles to the north; the wind circles going circling, and at its circuits the wind returns.
ECC 1:7 All the rushing streams go into the sea; and the sea is not filled up. To the place where the rushing streams went, there they shall return to go again.
ECC 1:8 All the wearied words a man shall not be able to speak, and the eye shall not be filled up to see, and the ear shall not be filled of hearing.
ECC 1:9 What is the thing taking place but the same thing as shall be taking place. And what is the thing being but the same thing as shall be done; and there is not anything newly made under the sun.
ECC 1:10 Who shall speak and shall say? Behold, this is new! Already it has happened in the eons to the ones having taken place from before us.
ECC 1:11 There is not a remembrance to the first things; and indeed to the last things being there will not be a remembrance of them, with the ones being born at the latter end.
ECC 1:12 I an ecclesiastic became king over Israel in Jerusalem.
ECC 1:13 And I gave my heart to inquire and to survey by wisdom concerning all things happening under the heaven. For God gave a wicked distraction to the sons of men to be distracting to him.
ECC 1:14 I beheld all the actions being done under the sun; and behold, all was folly and a resolve of spirit.
ECC 1:15 The thing being perverted is not able to be embellished. And deficiency is not able to be counted.
ECC 1:16 I spoke in my heart to say, Behold, I was magnified, and was added wisdom over all who came before me in Jerusalem. And I give my heart to know wisdom and knowledge.
ECC 1:17 And my heart beheld much wisdom and knowledge, parables, and higher knowledge. For I knew even indeed this is resolve of spirit.
ECC 1:18 For in abundance of wisdom is abundance of knowledge; and the one adding knowledge shall add pain.
ECC 2:1 I said in my heart, Come now indeed, I will test you with gladness, and therefore know good! And behold, also even this is folly.
ECC 2:2 To laughter, I said, Deviation. and to gladness, Why do you do this?
ECC 2:3 And I surveyed if my heart would draw my flesh with wine, and my heart guided me in wisdom; and to hold upon gladness, until of which I should see what kind was the good to the sons of men, which they shall do under the sun with their numbered days of life.
ECC 2:4 I magnified my action; I built to myself houses; I planted my vineyards.
ECC 2:5 I made to myself gardens and parks, and I planted in them a tree for every fruit.
ECC 2:6 I made to myself pools of waters to water by them the grove bursting forth trees.
ECC 2:7 I acquired menservants and maidservants. and native-born servants were born to me; and indeed a possession of a great herd and flock became to me above all the ones being before me in Jerusalem.
ECC 2:8 I brought together to myself also indeed silver, and indeed gold, and prized possessions of kings and of the places. I prepared to myself male singers and female singers, and amusements of the sons of man; and male wine servers and female wine servers.
ECC 2:9 And I became magnified, and proceeded in wisdom past all the ones being before me in Jerusalem; and indeed my wisdom was established to me.
ECC 2:10 And all whatever my eyes asked for was not at a distance from them. I did not detain my heart from any gladness; for my heart was gladdened in all my effort. And this was my portion of all my effort.
ECC 2:11 And I looked upon all my actions which I did by my hands, and on the effort in which I made an effort to do. And behold, all things were folly and a resolve of spirit, and there is not an advantage under the sun.
ECC 2:12 And I looked around to behold wisdom, and deviation, and folly. For what can man, who will come after counsel, do with the things as much as they did with it?
ECC 2:13 And I beheld that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, as the advantage of the light over the darkness.
ECC 2:14 The wise one - his eyes are in his head; but the foolish one goes in darkness. And I knew, even indeed I, that one event shall meet with all them.
ECC 2:15 And I said in my heart, As the event of the foolish one is, even indeed to me it shall meet up with me; and why have I discerned wisdom? And this extra I said in my heart, for a foolish one from out of abundance speaks, for even indeed this is folly.
ECC 2:16 For there is not a remembrance of the wise one with the foolish one in the eon; in so far as already the coming days all things are forgotten - even how the wise one shall die with the foolish one.
ECC 2:17 And I was detested with life; for evil was upon me - the action of doing a thing under the sun. For all is folly and a resolve of spirit.
ECC 2:18 And I detested all my effort which I made an effort under the sun. For I must leave it to the man coming after me.
ECC 2:19 And who knows if he will be a wise one or a foolish one? And if he exercises authority in all my effort in which I made an effort in, and in which I gained discernment under the sun - even indeed this is folly.
ECC 2:20 And I turned to dismiss my heart upon all effort in which I made an effort under the sun.
ECC 2:21 For there is a man that made his effort in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in courage; and a man which did not make an effort - in him he will give to him his portion. And indeed this is folly and great wickedness.
ECC 2:22 What happens to the man in all his effort, and in resolve of his heart in which he makes an effort under the sun?
ECC 2:23 For in all his days are pains and rage of his distraction; and indeed in night his heart does not go to bed. And indeed this is folly.
ECC 2:24 There is not a good thing to man unless to eat and to drink, and to show his soul good in his effort. And indeed this I knew, that it is from the hand of God.
ECC 2:25 For who shall eat, and who shall drink besides him?
ECC 2:26 For God gave to the good man before his face, wisdom, and knowledge, and gladness. And to the one sinning he gave distraction, to be added and to bring together so as to give what he has to the good man before the face of God. For even indeed this is folly and resolve of spirit.
ECC 3:1 To all there is the time and season to every thing under the heaven.
ECC 3:2 A season to give birth, and a season to die; a season to plant, and a season to pluck out the thing being planted;
ECC 3:3 a season to kill, and a season to heal; a season to demolish, and a season to build;
ECC 3:4 a season to weep, and a season to laugh; a season to lament, and a season to dance;
ECC 3:5 a season to throw stones, and a season to gather stones; a season to embrace, and a season to be far from embrace;
ECC 3:6 a season to seek, and a season to lose; a season to keep, and a season to cast out;
ECC 3:7 a season to tear, and a season to sew; a season to be quiet, and a season to speak;
ECC 3:8 a season to be fond of, and a season to detest; a season of war, and a season of peace.
ECC 3:9 What advantage of the one doing things in which he makes an effort?
ECC 3:10 I saw with the distraction which God gave to the sons of men to be distracting to him -
ECC 3:11 all which he made is good in his season; and indeed with the eon he gave in their heart, so that man should not find the action which God did from beginning till end.
ECC 3:12 I knew that there is not good in them, except to be glad and to do good in his life.
ECC 3:13 And indeed, every man who shall eat and shall drink, and should behold good in all his effort - it is a gift of God.
ECC 3:14 I knew that, all things as many as God did, they shall be into the eon. Unto them it is not to add, and from them it is not to remove. And God did, that they should fear from in front of him.
ECC 3:15 The thing becoming, already is; and as much as there is to be, already has become; and God shall seek the thing pursuing.
ECC 3:16 And still I beheld under the sun the place of judgment, that there the impious one was; and the place of the just ones, that there the pious one was.
ECC 3:17 I said in my heart, With the just one and with the impious one, God will judge. For there is a season to every thing, and for every action there.
ECC 3:18 I said in my heart, concerning the speech of the sons of man, that God will examine them, and to show that they are beasts.
ECC 3:19 And indeed to them the event of the sons of man, and the event of the beast is one event to them. As the death of this one, so also the death of this other one; and one breath to all. And what abounded the man more than the cattle? Nothing - for all the things are folly.
ECC 3:20 All things go to one place; all things came from the dust, and all things return to the dust.
ECC 3:21 And who has known the spirit of the sons of man, if it ascends itself upward? and the spirit of the beast, if it goes down itself below into the earth?
ECC 3:22 And I saw that there is not a good thing, except where a man shall be glad in his actions; for it is his portion. For who will lead him to see in what ever should take place after him?
ECC 4:1 And I turned and beheld all the extortions happening under the sun. And behold, the tear of the ones being extorted, and there is not one comforting them. And by the hand of ones extorting them was strength, and there is not one comforting them.
ECC 4:2 And I praised all of the ones having died of the ones already dying more than the living, as many as live until the present.
ECC 4:3 And better is he than these two, which not yet was born, which knew not all the evil action being done under the sun.
ECC 4:4 And I beheld all the effort, and all courage of action; for the same zeal of man is from his companion. And indeed this is folly and resolve of spirit.
ECC 4:5 The foolish one embraces his hands, and eats his own flesh.
ECC 4:6 Better a handful full of rest, than two handfuls full of trouble and resolve of spirit.
ECC 4:7 And I turned, and I saw folly under the sun.
ECC 4:8 There is one alone, and there is not a second; (and indeed, there is not son nor indeed brother to him; and there is not a limit to all his effort;) and indeed his eye is not satisfied of riches; and saying, Why do I make an effort, and deprive my soul of goodness? And indeed, this is folly and an evil distraction.
ECC 4:9 Better the two than the one, in which there is to them a good wage in their effort;
ECC 4:10 for if they should fall, the one shall raise his partner. But woe to him, to the one, whenever he should fall, and there should not be a second one to raise him.
ECC 4:11 And if two should go to bed, and heat themselves - then the one, how shall he heat himself?
ECC 4:12 And if one prevails against the one, the two shall stand against him. And the three-stranded cord shall not quickly be ripped apart.
ECC 4:13 Better a needy and wise child, than an older and foolish king who does not know to take heed any longer.
ECC 4:14 For from out of the house of the prisoners he shall come forth to reign, while even indeed one in his kingdom was needy.
ECC 4:15 I beheld all of the living walking under the sun, with the young of the second generation who shall stand in place of him.
ECC 4:16 There is not a limit to all the people, even to all as many as were before them; and indeed, the last shall not be glad in him. For even indeed this is folly and resolve of spirit.
ECC 5:1 Guard your foot whenever you should go into the house of God, and are near to hear! Let your sacrifice be above the gift of the foolish ones, for they are not knowing of the doing bad.
ECC 5:2 Do not hasten with your mouth, and let not your heart hasten to bring forth a word before the presence of God! For God is in the heaven upward, and you are upon the earth - upon this let your words be few!
ECC 5:3 For a dream comes through in a multitude of testing; and the voice of a foolish one in a multitude of words.
ECC 5:4 As when you vow a vow to God, you should not pass time to render it, for his will is not in foolish vows. You then, as much as you should have vowed, render!
ECC 5:5 Better for you to not make a vow, than for you to make a vow and not repay.
ECC 5:6 You should not give your mouth to lead your flesh into sin; and you should not say before the presence of God that, It is in ignorance; lest God should be provoked to anger at your voice, and should utterly destroy the things made by your hands.
ECC 5:7 For in a multitude of dreams, and follies, and many words - that with God you should fear.
ECC 5:8 If you should see extortion of the needy and seizure by lawsuit and judicial right in a place, you should not wonder over the thing; for a high one shall guard above a high one, and high ones over them.
ECC 5:9 And the abundance of the earth is for all; even a king needs the working of a field.
ECC 5:10 The one loving silver shall not be filled of silver; nor one who loved their offspring in their abundance. And indeed this is folly.
ECC 5:11 In a multitude of goodness the ones eating of it are multiplied. And what courageous thing is it to the one having it, but the sum of the seeing it with his eyes?
ECC 5:12 Sleep is sweet for the servant, if he shall eat little or if much. And to the one being filled to be rich there is not an allowing him to sleep.
ECC 5:13 There is a sickness which I beheld under the sun - riches being kept by him, for his hurt.
ECC 5:14 And those riches shall be destroyed in an evil distraction; and he engenders a son, and is there not anything in his hand.
ECC 5:15 As he came forth from the womb of his mother naked, he shall return to go as he comes, and nothing shall he take in his effort, that it should go with him in his hand.
ECC 5:16 And indeed this is an evil sickness; for as he came, so also he shall go forth. And what is his advantage in which he makes an effort into the wind?
ECC 5:17 And indeed all his days are in darkness, and in mourning, and much rage, and sickness, and bitter anger.
ECC 5:18 Behold, I saw good - that which is good to eat and to drink; and to see goodness in all his effort in what ever he should make an effort in under the sun, in the number of days of his life which God gave to him; for it is his portion.
ECC 5:19 And indeed, every man to whom God gave to him riches and possessions, and gave authority to him to eat from it, and to take his portion, and to be glad in his effort - this is a gift of God.
ECC 5:20 For not much will he remember the days of his life, for God distracts him in the gladness of his heart.
ECC 6:1 There is a wickedness which I beheld under the sun, and it is abundant with men.
ECC 6:2 A man to whom God shall give to him wealth, and possessions, and glory, and there is not a lacking to his soul from all things which he shall desire; but God shall not give authority to him to eat from it; for a man, a stranger, shall eat it. And this is folly and an evil sickness.
ECC 6:3 If a man should engender a hundred, and shall live many years, and however abundant will be the days of his years, that his soul shall not be filled up from goodness, and indeed a burial did not take place to him. I said, Better for him the miscarriage.
ECC 6:4 For in folly he came, and in darkness he goes, and in darkness his name shall be covered.
ECC 6:5 And indeed he knew not the sun, and this one knows not rest over this other one.
ECC 6:6 And if he lived a thousand years of returns, and he knew not goodness, is it not unto one place all shall go?
ECC 6:7 Every effort of man is for his mouth, and indeed the soul shall not be filled.
ECC 6:8 For what advantage to the wise one over the foolish one, for the needy knows to go in front of life?
ECC 6:9 Better vision of eyes, than going in life; for indeed this is folly and resolve of spirit.
ECC 6:10 If anything became, already its name has been called; and it is known what man is, and he is not able to judge against the one stronger than he.
ECC 6:11 For there are many matters multiplying folly.
ECC 6:12 What extra is to man? For who knows what is good to man in life, during the number of the life of the days of his folly? And he spent them as a shadow; for who shall report to man what will be after him under the sun?
ECC 7:1 A good name is above good oil, and the day of death above the day of birth.
ECC 7:2 It is good to go into a house of mourning, than than to go into a house of a banquet; in so far as this is the end of every man; and the living man will give good to his heart.
ECC 7:3 Better is rage than laughter, for by hurt of countenance the heart will be made better.
ECC 7:4 The heart of the wise ones is in the house of mourning; and the heart of the foolish ones is in the house of gladness.
ECC 7:5 It is good to hear the reproach of a wise one, than for a man to hear songs of foolish ones.
ECC 7:6 As the sound of the thorn-bushes burning under the kettle, so the laughter of the foolish ones; and indeed this is folly.
ECC 7:7 For extortion drives the wise one mad, and destroys the magnanimity of his heart.
ECC 7:8 Better the last of matters than its beginning; better the lenient than high spirit.
ECC 7:9 You should not hasten in your spirit to be enraged, for rage shall rest in the bosom of foolish ones.
ECC 7:10 You should not say, What happened that the former days were good over these - for you asked not in wisdom concerning this.
ECC 7:11 Wisdom is good with an allotment, and abundance to the ones viewing the sun.
ECC 7:12 For wisdom in its shadow is as the shadow of silver; and the advantage of the knowledge of wisdom will restore to life the one having it.
ECC 7:13 Behold the actions of God! For who shall be able to adorn what ever God should turn from him?
ECC 7:14 In the day of goodness live in good, and look out in the day of evil! Behold, and indeed with this God caused harmony with these concerning speech, that man should not find anything after him!
ECC 7:15 All things I beheld in days of my folly. There is a just one being destroyed in his just actions, and there is an impious one abiding in his evil actions.
ECC 7:16 Do not become super just, nor discern extra, lest at any time you should be overwhelmed!
ECC 7:17 You should not be super impious, and do not become hard, that you should not die in your time!
ECC 7:18 It is good for you to hold to in this; and indeed from this you should not defile your hand. For to the ones fearing God all things shall go forth.
ECC 7:19 Wisdom will give help to the wise one over ten exercising authority being in the city.
ECC 7:20 For there is not a just man on the earth who shall do good and shall not sin.
ECC 7:21 And indeed unto all the words which they shall speak, you should not put them to your heart, so that you should not hear your servant cursing you;
ECC 7:22 for very often he will act wickedly against you, and returning many times he shall inflict your heart - same as also indeed you cursed others.
ECC 7:23 All these things I tested in wisdom. I said, I shall be discerning, but it was far from me.
ECC 7:24 Far above what was, and a deep depth - who shall find it?
ECC 7:25 I and my heart circled about to know, and to survey, and to seek wisdom, and the reckoning of things, and to know an impious one's folly, and rioting, and deviation.
ECC 7:26 And I find her more bitter than death - with the woman in which her heart is snares and dragnets, and a bond in her hands. He that is good before the face of God shall be delivered from her; and the one sinning will be seized with her.
ECC 7:27 Behold, this I found, said the ecclesiastic, ( counting one by one, to find a device,)
ECC 7:28 which my soul anxiously sought, and did not find; even one man from out of a thousand did I find, and a woman among all these I did not find.
ECC 7:29 Except behold, this I found, that God dealt with the upright man! But they sought many devices, so who knows wise things, and who knows the loosening of a saying?
ECC 8:1 A man's wisdom will lighten his countenance; and an impudent man - his countenance will be detested.
ECC 8:2 Watch the mouth of a king, and concerning the word of the oath of God!
ECC 8:3 You should not hurriedly go from his face. You should not stand in an evil matter, for what ever he wants, he does.
ECC 8:4 As a king exercising authority, and who shall say to him, What do you do?
ECC 8:5 The one keeping the commandment shall not know an evil matter. And the heart of a wise one knows the time of judgment.
ECC 8:6 For every thing there is a season and judgment, for knowledge of man is vast unto him.
ECC 8:7 For there is not one knowing what the being is; for as it will be, who shall announce to him?
ECC 8:8 There is not a man exercising authority over spirit to restrain with the spirit; and there is not one exercising authority in the day of death; and there is not a discharge in the day of battle; and impiety shall not preserve the thing for it.
ECC 8:9 And all this I beheld, and gave my heart to every action which I had done under the sun; the things, as much as a man exercises authority to a man to inflict evil on him.
ECC 8:10 And then I beheld the impious ones being brought into the tombs, and from out of the holy place; and they went and were praised in the city, because they did thus. And indeed this is folly.
ECC 8:11 Because there is not a speedily existing objection for the ones doing the evil thing quickly, therefore by this the heart of the sons of man have full assurance in themselves to do evil.
ECC 8:12 The one who sinned did evil from then, and of their duration. (For also even I know that there is good to the ones fearing God, so that they should fear from in front of him.)
ECC 8:13 But it will not be good to the impious one, and he shall not prolong his days which are as a shadow; for he is not fearing from before God.
ECC 8:14 There is a folly which is done upon the earth - that there are the just ones that attain unto them, as the action of the impious ones; and there are the impious ones that attain to them, as the action of the just ones. I said that, Indeed also this is folly.
ECC 8:15 And I praised with the gladness, because there is not a good thing to man under the sun, were it not to eat, and to drink, and to be glad. And it will adhere to him in his effort all the days of his life, as God gave to him under the sun.
ECC 8:16 Whereupon I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to behold the distraction being done upon the earth. For also at day and at night a person is not seeing sleep with his eyes.
ECC 8:17 And I beheld all the actions of God, that man shall not be able to find anything with the action being done under the sun. As long as man should make an effort to seek, even he shall not find. And indeed, as long as the wise one should speak to know, he shall not be able to find. For all this I gave to my heart, and my heart beheld all this.
ECC 9:1 As the just ones, and the wise ones, even their works are in the hand of God. Indeed even love, indeed even hatred, there is not a man knowing all the things before them.
ECC 9:2 Folly is in all things; there is one event to the just one, and one to the impious one; to the good and to the bad; and to the clean and to the unclean; and to the one sacrificing and to the one not sacrificing; as is the good, as is the one sinning; as the one swearing by an oath, as is the one fearing the oath.
ECC 9:3 This evil is in all being done under the sun, that there is one event to all. And indeed, the heart of the sons of man are filled with evil, and madness in their heart during their life; and after them they go to the dead.
ECC 9:4 For someone who participates with all the living there is hope; for the living dog himself is good over the dead lion.
ECC 9:5 For the living shall know that they shall die; but the dead are not knowing anything; and there is not a wage to them any longer; for their remembrance was forgotten.
ECC 9:6 And indeed their love, and indeed their hatred, and indeed their zeal, already perished; and there is not a portion to them any longer into the eon, in all things being done under the sun.
ECC 9:7 Come, eat with gladness of your bread, and drink your wine with a good heart! For already God thought well of your actions.
ECC 9:8 In every time let your garments be white, and let not oil be lacking upon your head!
ECC 9:9 And behold life with the wife which you loved all the days of the life of your folly, the ones being given to you under the sun, all the days of the life of your folly! For it is your portion in your life, and in your effort wherein you made an effort under the sun.
ECC 9:10 All as much as your hand should find to do, you do as is in your power; for there is not an action, nor a device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Hades, of where you should go there.
ECC 9:11 I turned, and I beheld under the sun, that not to the light of foot is the race; and not to the mighty ones is the battle; and indeed not to the wise ones is the bread; and indeed not to the discerning ones is the riches; and indeed not to the ones knowing favor; for a season and a meeting shall meet with them all.
ECC 9:12 And indeed man does not know his season. As fishes being hunted with a hurtful casting-net, and as birds being hunted with a snare - as them the sons of man shall be ensnared in an evil season, whenever it should fall upon them suddenly.
ECC 9:13 And indeed this I beheld - wisdom under the sun, and it is great to me.
ECC 9:14 If there were a small city, and the men in it few; and there should come against it a great king, and shall encircle it, and shall build against it great siege mounds;
ECC 9:15 and that there should be found in it a needy wise man; and he himself shall deliver the city in his wisdom - but man remembered not with that needy man.
ECC 9:16 And I said, Wisdom is good over power. But the wisdom of the needy man is being treated with contempt, and his words are not being listened to.
ECC 9:17 Words of wise ones being at rest are heard above a cry of ones being in authority in follies.
ECC 9:18 Wisdom is good over weapons of war; but one sinning shall destroy much goodness.
ECC 10:1 A fly put to death will rot a concoction of luscious oil; A little wisdom is valuable over great glory of folly.
ECC 10:2 The heart of a wise one is at his right hand; and the heart of a foolish one is at his left.
ECC 10:3 And indeed whenever a foolish one goes in the way of his heart, he will fail, and all which he considers is folly.
ECC 10:4 If spirit of the one exercising authority should ascend against you, you should not leave your place; for a cure will put to rest great sins.
ECC 10:5 There is a wickedness which I beheld under the sun, as an unintentional act came forth from the person of one exercising authority.
ECC 10:6 The foolish one was put in great heights, and the rich shall settle in low.
ECC 10:7 I beheld servants upon horses, and rulers going as servants upon the ground.
ECC 10:8 The one digging a cesspool shall fall into it; and the one demolishing a fence boundary, a serpent shall bite him.
ECC 10:9 One lifting away stones shall work hard among them; one splitting wood shall be exposed to danger in them.
ECC 10:10 If an iron implement should fall off, and he disturbed countenance, then power and abundance shall strengthen to the man of which is wisdom.
ECC 10:11 Surely the serpent should bite with not an enchanter whispering, and there is not an advantage to the one charming.
ECC 10:12 The words of a wise mouth carry favor, but the lips of a foolish one shall sink him;
ECC 10:13 beginning with words of his mouth in folly, and the end of his mouth wicked madness.
ECC 10:14 And the foolish one multiplies words. Man knows not what the thing becoming is, and what the thing being is, while after him who shall announce to him?
ECC 10:15 The effort of the foolish ones shall trouble them, as one who knows not how to go into a city.
ECC 10:16 Woe to you, O city, of which your king is younger, and your rulers eat in the morning.
ECC 10:17 Blessed is your land of which your king is a son of free nobles, and your rulers at a proper time shall eat in force, and shall not be ashamed.
ECC 10:18 By slothful neglect a building will be lowered; and in idleness of hands the house will drip.
ECC 10:19 For laughter they make bread, and wine, and olive oil, for the living to be glad; and of money all will heed.
ECC 10:20 And indeed in your conscience you should not curse a king; and in the closets of your bedrooms you should not curse a rich man; for a winged creature of the heaven shall carry your voice, and the one having the wings shall report your word.
ECC 11:1 Send your bread upon the face of the water! for in a multitude of days you will find it.
ECC 11:2 Give a portion to seven, even indeed to eight! for you know not what evil there will be upon the earth.
ECC 11:3 If the clouds should be filled of rain, then they pour out upon the earth. And if a tree should fall towards the south, and if towards the north, then in a place where the tree shall fall - there it shall be.
ECC 11:4 Giving heed to the wind he sows not; and looking into the clouds he harvests not,
ECC 11:5 being among the ones in whom there is not a knowing what the way of the wind is, even as the bones in the womb of one being with child, so you shall not know the actions of God, as much as he shall do in all things.
ECC 11:6 At morning sow your seed, and at evening do not relieve your hand! For you know not what will line up - this here, or, this there. And if the two are together - good things.
ECC 11:7 Moreover the light is sweet, and it is good to the eyes to see with the sun,
ECC 11:8 for even if a man shall live many years, in all them he shall be glad, and the days of darkness shall be remembered, for they will be many. All coming is folly.
ECC 11:9 Be glad, O young man, in your youth! And let your heart do you good in the days of your youth! And walk in the ways of your heart unblemished, and in the vision of your eyes! And know that in all these God shall lead you in equity!
ECC 11:10 And leave rage from your heart, and pass off wickedness from your flesh! for youth and thoughtlessness are folly.
ECC 12:1 And remember the one creating you in the days of your youth, until whenever the days of evil should not come, and years should arrive, in which you shall say, There is not in me a want for them;
ECC 12:2 until of which the sun and the light are not darkened, nor the moon and the stars; nor the clouds return after the rain;
ECC 12:3 in a day in which ever the keepers of the house should be shaken, and men of power should be turned aside, and the grinding women are idle because they are made few, and the women looking out of the openings shall darken;
ECC 12:4 and they shall lock the doors in the market in weakness of the sound of the woman grinding, and one shall rise up to the sound of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song shall be humbled;
ECC 12:5 and indeed from the height they shall see, even stupefactions in the way; and the almond shall bloom, and the locust shall thicken, and the caper shall be dispersed; because man went to his eternal house; and the ones beating their chests in mourning circled in the market;
ECC 12:6 until whenever the line of silver should be prostrated, and the flower ornament of gold should be broken, and the water-pitcher should be broken at the spring, and the wheel should have rolled unto the pit,
ECC 12:7 and the dust shall return upon the earth as it was, and the spirit should return to the God who gave it.
ECC 12:8 Folly of follies, said the ecclesiastic, all things are folly.
ECC 12:9 And it was extra that the ecclesiastic became wise, and taught knowledge with man, and that he shall trace composed parables.
ECC 12:10 The ecclesiastic sought much to find a wanting of words, and writing of uprightness of words of truth.
ECC 12:11 The words of the wise ones are as the oxgoads, and as nails firmly planted; ones which by agreement were given from one shepherd.
ECC 12:12 And O my son guard extra by them! To make many scrolls there is not a limit; and much meditation is weariness of flesh.
ECC 12:13 The end of the whole matter, hear! Fear God, and keep his commandments! for this is all to man.
ECC 12:14 For all action God shall lead into judgment, with all being looked over, if good and if evil.

ISA 1:1 The vision which Isaiah son of Amoz beheld, which he beheld against Judea, and against Jerusalem, during the kingdom of Uzziah, and Jotham, and Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
ISA 1:2 Hear, O heaven, and give ear O earth! for the LORD spoke, saying, I have engendered sons, and raised them, but they disregarded me.
ISA 1:3 The ox knows the one acquiring it, and the donkey knows the stable of its master; but Israel does not know me, and my people perceived not.
ISA 1:4 Woe, O sinful nation; people full of sins; an evil seed; lawless sons. You abandoned the LORD, and provoked to anger the holy one of Israel; they were separated into the rear.
ISA 1:5 Why still should you be struck, proceeding in lawlessness? The whole head is in misery, and the whole heart is in distress.
ISA 1:6 From feet unto head there is not a wholeness in it. Neither wound, nor stripe, nor inflamed wound are healed; there is not a dressing to place upon it, nor oil, nor bandages.
ISA 1:7 Your land is desolate; your cities scorched; your place before you - strangers devour it, and it is made desolate, being eradicated by alien peoples.
ISA 1:8 The daughter of Zion shall be abandoned as a tent in a vineyard, and as a vacant storehouse in a cucumber garden, as a city being assaulted.
ISA 1:9 And unless the LORD of hosts left us a seed, we would have become as Sodom, and likened as Gomorrah.
ISA 1:10 Hear the word of the LORD, O rulers of Sodom! Take heed to the law of our God, O people of Gomorrah!
ISA 1:11 What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me? says the LORD. I am full of whole burnt offerings of rams, and fat of lambs; and I do not want blood of bulls and he-goats.
ISA 1:12 And neither should you come to appear to me; for who required these from out of your hands? You shall not proceed to tread my courtyard.
ISA 1:13 If you should bring fine flour, it is in vain; incense is an abomination to me; I endure not your new moons and the sabbaths and the great day.
ISA 1:14 Your fasting, and idleness, and your new moons, and your holidays my soul detests. You became to me as a glut; no longer shall I spare your sins.
ISA 1:15 Whenever you should stretch out your hands, I shall turn my eyes from you. And if you should multiply your supplication, I will not listen to you; for your hands are full of blood.
ISA 1:16 Bathe yourself! Become clean! Remove the wickednesses from your souls before my eyes! Cease from your wickednesses!
ISA 1:17 Learn to do good! Inquire of equity! Rescue the one wronged! Judge for the orphan! and do justice for the widow!
ISA 1:18 And come, we should plead, says the LORD. And if your sins should be as crimson, I shall whiten as snow; and if they should be as scarlet, I shall whiten as wool.
ISA 1:19 And if you should want, and if you should listen to me, you shall eat the good things of the earth.
ISA 1:20 But if you should not want, nor should you listen to me, a sword shall devour you. For the mouth of the LORD spoke these things.
ISA 1:21 O how the trustworthy city Zion became a harlot full of judgment, in which righteousness slept in it, but now murderers.
ISA 1:22 Your silver is debased, your peddlers mingle the wine with water.
ISA 1:23 Your rulers resist persuasion; they are partners of thieves, loving bribes, pursuing recompense, not arbitrating for orphans, and not heeding equity of widows.
ISA 1:24 On account of this, thus says the master, the LORD of hosts, Woe the ones being strong of Israel, for I will not cease my rage among the contrary ones, and I will execute judgment of my enemies.
ISA 1:25 And I will bring my hand against you, and I will purify you to cleanness. But the ones resisting persuasion I will destroy, and I will remove all lawless ones from you.
ISA 1:26 And all the proud I will abase; and I will stand your judges as formerly, and your counselors as at the beginning. And after these things you shall be called, City of Righteousness, the trustworthy mother-city Zion.
ISA 1:27 For with judgment her captivity shall be delivered, even with charity.
ISA 1:28 And the lawless ones and the sinners shall be broken together, and the ones abandoning the LORD shall be finished off entirely.
ISA 1:29 For they shall be ashamed of their idols which they preferred, and shall be ashamed over the gardens which they desired.
ISA 1:30 For they will be as a terebinth tree throwing off its leaves, and as a park not having water.
ISA 1:31 And their strength will be as stubble of hemp, and their works as sparks, and the lawless ones and the sinners shall be incinerated together, and there will not be one extinguishing.
ISA 2:1 The word coming to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judea, and concerning Jerusalem.
ISA 2:2 For it will be in the last days the mountain of the LORD will be apparent, and the house of God will be upon the uppermost part of the mountains, and it shall be raised up high above the hills; and all the nations shall come unto it.
ISA 2:3 And many nations shall go, and shall say, Come, for we should ascend unto the mountain of the LORD, and unto the house of the God of Jacob; and he will announce to us his way, and we shall go in it. For from out of Zion shall come forth law, and the word of the LORD from out of Jerusalem.
ISA 2:4 And he shall judge in the midst of the nations; and shall completely refute many people. And they shall cut down their swords into plows, and their pikes into sickles. And a nation shall not take a sword against a nation, and in no way should they learn yet to wage war.
ISA 2:5 And now, O house of Jacob, come and we should go to the light of the LORD.
ISA 2:6 For he forsook his people, the house of Jacob; for their place was filled up as from the beginning of ones prognosticating, as that of the Philistines; and many Philistine children were born to them.
ISA 2:7 For they filled up their place with silver and gold, and there was not a limit to the number of their treasures; and they filled up the land with horses, and there was not a limit to the number of their chariots.
ISA 2:8 And they filled up the land of abominations of the works of their hands, and did obeisance to the ones which they made by their fingers.
ISA 2:9 And people bowed, and each man was abased; and in no way will I spare them.
ISA 2:10 And now, enter to the rock, and hide in the earth from in front of the fear of the LORD, and from the glory of his strength, whenever he should rise up to devastate the earth!
ISA 2:11 For the eyes of the LORD are high, but man low; and the height of men shall be abased, and the LORD alone shall be raised up high in that day.
ISA 2:12 For the day of the LORD of hosts is upon every one insulting and proud, and upon every one high and elevated, and they shall be abased;
ISA 2:13 and upon every cedar of Lebanon, of the ones high and elevated, and upon every acorn tree of Bashan,
ISA 2:14 and upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill,
ISA 2:15 and upon every high tower, and upon every high wall,
ISA 2:16 and upon every boat of the sea, and upon every spectacle of boats of beauty.
ISA 2:17 And every man shall be abased, and the haughtiness of men shall fall. And the LORD alone shall be raised up high in that day.
ISA 2:18 And they shall hide all the things made by hand,
ISA 2:19 carrying them into the caves, and into the fissures of the rocks, and into the burrows of the earth, from in front of the fear of the LORD, and from the glory of his strength, whenever he should rise up to devastate the earth.
ISA 2:20 For in that day a man will cast out his abominations made of silver and gold, which they made to do obeisance to the vain things, and to the bats,
ISA 2:21 to enter into the burrows of the solid rock, and the fissures of the rocks, from in front of the fear of the LORD, and from the glory of his strength, whenever he should rise up to devastate the earth.
ISA 2:22 Cease yourself from the man breathing by his nostril! For by what is he considered?
ISA 3:1 Behold indeed, the master, the LORD of hosts, shall remove from Jerusalem and from Judea the prevailing man, and the prevailing woman, the strength of bread, and the strength of water,
ISA 3:2 the giant, and the one prevailing, and a man warrior, and magistrate, and prophet, and thinker, and old man,
ISA 3:3 and commander of fifty, and wonderful counselor, and wise architect, and discerning listener.
ISA 3:4 And I will set young men as their rulers, and mockers will lord over them.
ISA 3:5 And the people will be downcast, man against man, even a man will be against his neighbor; the boy will strike against the old man, and the one without honor against the important.
ISA 3:6 For a man shall take hold of his brother, or a member of the family of his father, saying, You have a garment, you become our chief, and let my food needs be under you!
ISA 3:7 And answering in that day, he will say, I will not be your chief, for there is not bread in my house, nor a garment; I will not be a chief of this people.
ISA 3:8 For Jerusalem is forsaken, and Judea is cast down, and their tongues speak with lawlessness the things against the LORD, resisting persuasion.
ISA 3:9 For now their glory was abased, and the shame of their face withstood them; and they announced their sin as Sodom, and revealed it. Woe to their soul, for they consulted wicked counsel against themselves,
ISA 3:10 having said, We should bind the just one, for he is inconvenient to us. Therefore the produce of their works they shall eat.
ISA 3:11 Woe to the lawless one - evils according to the works of his hands shall come to pass against him.
ISA 3:12 O my people, your exactors glean you, and the ones exacting lord over you. O my people, the ones declaring you blessed mislead you, and they disturb the roads of your feet.
ISA 3:13 But now the LORD will place in judgment, and will stand his people in judgment.
ISA 3:14 The LORD himself shall come for judgment with the elders of the people, and with his rulers. But you, why did you set on fire my vineyard, and the seizure of the poor is in your houses?
