MAT 25:38 And when did we behold you a stranger, and brought you in? or naked, and we clothed you?
MAT 25:39 And when did we behold you sick or in prison, and we came to you?
MAT 25:40 And answering the king shall say to them, Amen I say to you, In as much as you did to one of these the least of my brothers you did to me.
MAT 25:41 Then he will say also to the ones on his left, Go from me, O ones being cursed into the eternal fire having been prepared for the devil and his angels!
MAT 25:42 For I hungered, and you did not give to me to eat; I thirsted, and you did not give me a drink;
MAT 25:43 I was a stranger, and you did not bring me in; naked, and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.

MAT 25:45 Then he will answer to them, saying, Amen I say to you, If as much as you did not do to one of the least of these, not even to me did you do.
MAT 25:46 And these shall go forth unto eternal punishment; but the just ones unto life eternal.
MAT 26:1 And it came to pass when Jesus finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
MAT 26:2 You know that after two days the passover takes place, and the son of man is delivered up for crucifying.
MAT 26:3 Then gathered together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, into the courtyard of the chief priest, being called Caiaphas.
MAT 26:4 And they were advising that they should seize Jesus by treachery, and should kill him.
MAT 26:5 But they said, Not during the holiday, that a tumult should not take place among the people.
MAT 26:6 And Jesus being in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
MAT 26:7 there came forward to him a woman having an alabaster flask of a perfumed liquid of a heavy price, and she poured it down upon his head as he reclined.
MAT 26:8 And his disciples seeing it, were indignant, saying, For what reason is this loss?
MAT 26:9 For this perfumed liquid would be able to be sold for much, and to be given to the poor.
MAT 26:10 But knowing, Jesus said to them, Why do you make troubles to the woman? for she worked a good work for me.
MAT 26:11 For at all times you have the poor with yourselves; but me you do not at all times have.
MAT 26:12 For this woman laying this perfumed liquid upon my body, did so to embalm me.
MAT 26:13 Amen I say to you, Where ever this good news should be proclaimed in the entire world, there shall be spoken also what this woman did for a memorial of her.
MAT 26:14 Then one of the twelve having gone, the one being called Judas Iscariot, to the chief priest,
MAT 26:15 said, What do you want to give me, and I will deliver him up to you? And they established to him thirty silver pieces.
MAT 26:16 And from then he sought an opportune time that he should deliver him up.
MAT 26:17 And on the first day of the unleavened breads the disciples came forward to Jesus, saying to him, Where do you want we should prepare for you to eat the passover?
MAT 26:18 And he said, Go into the city, to a certain person, and say to him! The teacher says, My time is near; with you I will observe the passover with my disciples.
MAT 26:19 And the disciples did as Jesus gave orders to them; and they prepared the passover.
MAT 26:20 And evening becoming, he reclined with the twelve.
MAT 26:21 And of their eating, he said, Amen I say to you, That one of you shall deliver me up.
MAT 26:22 And fretting exceedingly, they began to say to him, each of them, By no means I am he, O Lord?
MAT 26:23 And he responding said, The one dipping the hand with me in the saucer will deliver me up.
MAT 26:24 Indeed the son of man goes away as it has been written concerning him; but woe to that man by whom the son of man is delivered up. It was good to him if that man was not born.
MAT 26:25 And responding, Judas the one delivering him up, said, Not I am he, Rabbi? He says to him, You said it.
MAT 26:26 And during their eating, Jesus having taken the bread, and having blessed, broke it and gave it to the disciples. And he said, Take, eat, this is my body!
MAT 26:27 And having taken the cup, and giving thanks, he gave to them, saying, You drink of it all!
MAT 26:28 For this is my blood of the new covenant for many, being poured out for a release of sins.
MAT 26:29 And I say to you, that in no way shall I drink from now on from this offspring of the grapevine, until that day whenever I should drink it with you new in the kingdom my father.
MAT 26:30 And having sung praise, they went forth unto the mount of the olives.
MAT 26:31 Then Jesus says to them, All you will be stumbled in me in this night. For it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will disperse.
MAT 26:32 And after my rising, I will go before you into Galilee.
MAT 26:33 And responding Peter said to him, If even all were to stumble in you, I at no time shall be made to stumble.
MAT 26:34 Jesus said to him, Amen I say to you, That in this night, before a rooster calls out, three times you shall totally reject me.
MAT 26:35 Peter says to him, And if it should be necessary for me to die with you, in no way shall I totally reject you. In like manner also all the disciples spoke.
MAT 26:36 Then Jesus comes with them unto a place being called, Gethsemane, and says to the disciples, Sit here, until of which going forth I should pray there!
MAT 26:37 And taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to fret and be anxious.
MAT 26:38 Then he says to them, My soul is dejected unto death; remain here, and be vigilant with me!
MAT 26:39 And having gone forth a little, he fell upon his face, praying, and saying, O my father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me - except not as I want, but as you want!
MAT 26:40 And he comes to the disciples, and finds them sleeping. And he says to Peter, So were you not able to be vigilant one hour with me?
MAT 26:41 Be vigilant, and pray, that you should not enter into a test! Indeed the spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak.
MAT 26:42 Again, a second time, having gone forth he prayed, saying, O my father, if it is not possible for this cup to pass from me, except that I drink it, let your will take place!
MAT 26:43 And having come he finds them again sleeping; for their eyes were weighed down.
MAT 26:44 And allowing them, going forth again, he prayed a third time, the same word having said,
MAT 26:45 Then he comes to his disciples, and says to them, Sleep the remaining, and rest! Behold, the hour approaches, and the son of man is delivered up into the hands of sinners.
MAT 26:46 Arise, we lead on! Behold, the one delivering me up approaches.
MAT 26:47 And yet while he was speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and wood spears, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
MAT 26:48 And the one delivering him up gave to them a sign, saying, Whom ever I should kiss, it is he; seize him!
MAT 26:49 And immediately having come forward to Jesus, he said, Hail, rabbi! And he kissed him.
MAT 26:50 And Jesus said to him, Companion, for what reason are you at hand? Then having come forward, they put hands upon Jesus, and seized him.
MAT 26:51 And behold, one of the ones with Jesus, stretching out the hand, drew up his sword, and striking the manservant of the chief priest, he removed his ear.
MAT 26:52 Then Jesus says to him, Return your sword unto its place! for all the ones taking the sword shall die by a sword.
MAT 26:53 Or do you think that I am not able just now to call for the aid of my father? Even he will stand by me more than twelve legions of angels.
MAT 26:54 How then should the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must take place?
MAT 26:55 In that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, As against a robber do you come forth with swords and wood spears to seize me? Daily with you I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me.
MAT 26:56 But this all happened, that the scriptures of the prophets should be fulfilled. Then all the disciples leaving him, fled.
MAT 26:57 And the ones seizing Jesus took him away to Caiaphas the chief priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
MAT 26:58 And Peter followed him from far off unto the courtyard of the chief priest, and entering inside, he sat down with the officers, to see the conclusion.
MAT 26:59 And the chief priests, and the elders, and the entire sanhedrin, sought false witness against Jesus, so that they should kill him;
MAT 26:60 and they did not find reason; and many false witnesses having come forward did not find reason. But afterwards two false witnesses having come forward,
MAT 26:61 they said, This one said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and in three days to rebuild it.
MAT 26:62 And having risen up, the chief priest said to him, Nothing you answer? What do these bear witness against you?
MAT 26:63 But Jesus kept silent. And responding the chief priest said to him, I adjure you according to the living God, that to us you should say if you are the Christ, the son of God.
MAT 26:64 Jesus says to him, You said it. Furthermore I say to you, From now you shall see the son of man sitting down at the right hand of the power, and coming upon the clouds of the heaven.
MAT 26:65 Then the chief priest tore his garments, saying that, He blasphemed - what still need do we have of witnesses? See! Now you heard his blasphemy.
MAT 26:66 What do you think? And they responding said, He is liable of death.
MAT 26:67 Then they spat in his face, and buffeted him; and some slapped,
MAT 26:68 saying, Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one hitting you?
MAT 26:69 And Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. And came forward to him one maidservant, saying, Even you were with Jesus the Galilean.
MAT 26:70 But he denied before all, saying, I do not know what you say.
MAT 26:71 And him coming forth into the vestibule, another beheld him. And he says to them there, Even this one was with Jesus the Nazarene.
MAT 26:72 And again he denied with an oath, that, I do not know the man.
MAT 26:73 And after a little while the ones standing having come forward said to Peter, Truly even you are of them; for even your speech makes you manifest.
MAT 26:74 Then he began to bind by a curse, and swear by an oath that, I have not known the man. And immediately a rooster called out.
MAT 26:75 And Peter remembered the saying of Jesus, having said to him that, Before a rooster calls out, three times you shall totally reject me. And having gone forth outside, he wept bitterly.
MAT 27:1 And morning having become, all the chief priests took council, and the elders of the people against Jesus so as to put him to death.
MAT 27:2 And having bound him, they took, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate the governor.
MAT 27:3 Then Judas the one delivering him up beholding that he was condemned, changed his mind, so as to return the thirty silver pieces to the chief priests and to the elders,
MAT 27:4 saying, I sinned, having delivered up innocent blood. But they said, What is that to us? You shall see to that.
MAT 27:5 And having tossed the silver pieces in the temple, he withdrew, and having gone forth he hung himself.
MAT 27:6 But the chief priests having taken the silver pieces, said, It is not allowed to throw them into the offering when it is the value for blood.
MAT 27:7 And taking council, they bought with them the field of the potter for a burial ground for strangers.
MAT 27:8 Therefore that field is called, Field of blood, until today.
MAT 27:9 Then was fulfilled the thing having been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying, And I took the thirty silver pieces, the value of the one being valued, who was valued by the sons of Israel.
MAT 27:10 And they gave them for the field of the potter, as the Lord gave orders to me.
MAT 27:11 And Jesus stood before the governor. And the governor asked him, saying, Are you the king of the Jews? And Jesus said to him, You say it.
MAT 27:12 And in the charging him by the chief priests and the elders, he answered nothing.
MAT 27:13 Then Pilate says to him, Do you not hear how much they witness against you?
MAT 27:14 And he answered not to him - to not even one word, so that the governor marveled exceedingly.
MAT 27:15 And according to the holiday the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the multitude, whom they wanted.
MAT 27:16 And they had then a notorious prisoner, being called Barabbas.
MAT 27:17 Then of their being gathered together, Pilate said to them, Whom do you want I release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus the one being called Christ.
MAT 27:18 For he knew that on account of envy they delivered him up.
MAT 27:19 And of his sitting down upon the rostrum, his wife sent to him, saying, Let there be nothing between you and that just one; for I suffered much today by a dream concerning him.
MAT 27:20 But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes that they should ask for Barabbas, and Jesus should perish.
MAT 27:21 And responding the governor said to them, Who do you want from the two I should release to you? And they said, Barabbas.
MAT 27:22 Pilate says to them, What then shall I do with Jesus the one being called Christ? all say to him, Let him be crucified!
MAT 27:23 And the governor said, For what evil did he do? And they extremely more cried out, saying, Let him be crucified!
MAT 27:24 And Pilate seeing that in nothing he derived benefit, but rather it became a tumult, having taken water, he washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just one; you shall see to it.
MAT 27:25 And responding all the people said, His blood is upon us and upon our children.
MAT 27:26 Then he released to them Barabbas. And scourging Jesus, he delivered him up that he should be crucified.
MAT 27:27 Then the soldiers of the governor, having taken with them Jesus to the praetorium, gathered against him the entire cohort.
MAT 27:28 And stripping him, they put on him a scarlet military cloak.
MAT 27:29 And having plaited a crown of thorns, they placed it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand. And kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying, Hail, king of the Jews!
MAT 27:30 And having spit on him, they took the reed, and beat upon his head.
MAT 27:31 And when they mocked him, they took the military cloak off him, and they put on 3him 1his garments, and took him to be crucified.
MAT 27:32 And going forth, they found a Cyrenaean man, by name Simon; this one they conscripted that he should bear his cross.
MAT 27:33 And having come unto a place being called Golgotha, which is being called, place of the skull,
MAT 27:34 they gave to him vinegar to drink, with bile being mixed; and having tasted, he did not want to drink.
MAT 27:35 And having crucified him, they divided his garments, casting a lot; that should be fulfilled the thing having been spoken by the prophet, They divided my garments among themselves, and over my clothes they cast a lot.
MAT 27:36 And sitting down they kept him there.
MAT 27:37 And they placed above his head his accusation being written - This is Jesus the king of the Jews.
MAT 27:38 Then were crucified with him two robbers, one at his right, and one at his left.
MAT 27:39 And the ones coming near blasphemed him, shaking their heads,
MAT 27:40 and saying, O one destroying the temple, and in three days rebuilding it, deliver yourself! If you are the son of God, come down from the cross!
MAT 27:41 And in like manner also the chief priests mocking, with the scribes and elders, said,
MAT 27:42 Others he delivered, himself he is not able to deliver. If he is king of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe upon him!
MAT 27:43 He relied upon God; let him rescue him now, if he wants him; for he said that, I am son of God!
MAT 27:44 And the same way also the robbers being crucified along with him berated him.
MAT 27:45 And from the sixth hour darkness came upon all the land until the ninth hour.
MAT 27:46 And around the ninth hour Jesus yelled out with a great voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lima sabacthani; that is, My God, My God, why have you abandoned me?
MAT 27:47 And some of the ones standing there having heard, said that, This one calls Elijah.
MAT 27:48 And immediately one of them running, and taking a sponge, filling also of vinegar, and putting it on a reed, gave him to drink.
MAT 27:49 And the rest said, Let go, we should see if Elijah comes delivering him!
MAT 27:50 And Jesus, again having cried out with a great voice, let go the spirit.
MAT 27:51 And behold, the veil of the temple was split into two from above unto below; and the earth was shaken, and the rocks split;
MAT 27:52 and the tombs were opened; and many bodies of the holy ones sleeping arose.
MAT 27:53 And having come forth from out of the tombs, after his rising up, they entered into the holy city, and were revealed to many.
MAT 27:54 And the centurion, and the ones with him, keeping guard over Jesus, having beheld the earthquake, and the things happening, feared exceedingly, saying, Truly this was son of God.
MAT 27:55 And were there many women from far off viewing, who followed Jesus from Galilee, serving to him;
MAT 27:56 among whom was Mary the Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
MAT 27:57 And evening having become, there came a rich man from Arimathea, by name Joseph, who also himself was discipled by Jesus.
MAT 27:58 This one having come forward to Pilate, asked the body of Jesus. Then Pilate bid to give the body.
MAT 27:59 And having taken the body, Joseph swathed it with pure fine linen.
MAT 27:60 And he placed it in his new sepulchre, which he quarried in the rock. And having rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, he went forth.
MAT 27:61 And was there, Mary the Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting down before the tomb.
MAT 27:62 And the next day, which is after the preparation, were gathered together the chief priests and the Pharisees to Pilate,
MAT 27:63 saying, O master, we remember that, that deluded one said, while still living, After three days I arise.
MAT 27:64 Bid then to safeguard the tomb until the third day! lest at any time his disciples coming at night should steal it, and should say to the people, He is risen from the dead; and will be the last delusion worse than the first.
MAT 27:65 And Pilate said to them, You have a custodial guard, Go away! You safeguard as you know!
MAT 27:66 And the ones having gone safeguarded the tomb, setting a seal upon the stone by the custodial guard.
MAT 28:1 And late of sabbaths, in the evening on day one of sabbaths, came Mary the Magdalene, and the other Mary to view the tomb.
MAT 28:2 And behold, a great earthquake took place; for an angel of the Lord having come down from out of heaven, having come forward, rolled the stone from the door, and was sitting down upon it.
MAT 28:3 And his shape was as lightning, and his garment white as snow.
MAT 28:4 And from the fear of him the ones keeping guard shook, and became as dead.
MAT 28:5 And responding the angel said to the women, You fear not! For I know that you seek Jesus the one having been crucified.
MAT 28:6 He is not here; for he is risen as he said. Come, behold the place where the Lord was situated!
MAT 28:7 And quickly going, say to his disciples that he is risen from the the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee! There you shall see him. Behold, I told to you.
MAT 28:8 And having gone forth quickly from the sepulchre, with fear and great joy; they ran to report to his disciples.
MAT 28:9 And as they were going to report to his disciples, that behold, Jesus met them, saying, Hail! And they having come forward held his feet, and did obeisance to him.
MAT 28:10 Then Jesus says to them, Fear not! Go! Report to my brothers that they should go forth into Galilee, and there they shall see me!
MAT 28:11 And of their going, behold, some of the custodial guard having come into the city reported to the chief priests all the things happening.
MAT 28:12 And having gathered together with the elders, and council having taken, they gave the soldiers enough silver,
MAT 28:13 saying, Say that! His disciples having come by night stole him of us being asleep.
MAT 28:14 And if this should be heard by the governor, we shall persuade him, and we will make you free from care.
MAT 28:15 And they, having taken the money, did as they were taught. And was spread abroad this word by the Jews until today.
MAT 28:16 But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, unto the mountain where Jesus ordered them.
MAT 28:17 And seeing him, they did obeisance to him; but some hesitated.
MAT 28:18 And having come forward, Jesus spoke to them, saying, All authority was given to me in heaven and upon earth.
MAT 28:19 Going then, disciple all the nations, immersing them in the name of the father, and of the son, and of the holy spirit!
MAT 28:20 Teaching them to give heed to all as much as I gave charge to you. And behold, I am with you all the days until the completion of the eon. Amen.
MAR 1:1 The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, son of God.
MAR 1:2 As it has been written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall carefully prepare your way before you.
MAR 1:3 A voice yelling in the wilderness, Prepare the way of the Lord! Make straight his roads!
MAR 1:4 John came immersing in the wilderness, and proclaiming an immersion of repentance for a release of sins.
MAR 1:5 And all the Judean went forth region to him, and the ones of Jerusalem. And all were immersed in the Jordan river by him, acknowledging their sins.
MAR 1:6 And John was clothed with hair of a camel, and a belt made of skin around his loin, and eating locusts and wild honey.
MAR 1:7 And he proclaimed, saying, There comes the one stronger than me after me, of whom I am not fit, having bowed down, to untie the strap of his sandals.
MAR 1:8 I indeed immerse you in water; but he shall immerse you in holy spirit.
MAR 1:9 And it came to pass in those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was immersed by John into the Jordan.
MAR 1:10 And immediately, ascending from the water, he beheld the splitting of the heavens, and the spirit as a dove coming down upon him.
MAR 1:11 And a voice came from out of the heavens, saying, You are my son the beloved, in whom I take pleasure.
MAR 1:12 And straightway the spirit cast him into the wilderness.
MAR 1:13 And he was there in the wilderness forty days being tempted by Satanthe adversary.. And he was with the wild beasts; and the angels served to him.
MAR 1:14 And after the delivering up John, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God,
MAR 1:15 and saying that, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God approaches; repent and believe in the good news!
MAR 1:16 And walking by the sea of Galilee, he beheld Simon and Andrew his brother casting a casting-net in the sea; for they were fishermen.
MAR 1:17 And Jesus said to them, Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
MAR 1:18 And immediately, leaving their nets, they followed him.
MAR 1:19 And having advanced from there a little, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, and them in the boat readying the nets.
MAR 1:20 And immediately he called them. And having left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hirelings they went forth after him.
MAR 1:21 And they entered into Capernaum. And immediately on the sabbaths, having entered into the synagogue, he taught.
MAR 1:22 And they were overwhelmed by his teaching; for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
MAR 1:23 And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he shouted aloud,
MAR 1:24 saying, Alas, what is it to us and to you, Jesus, O Nazarene? are you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are, the holy one of God.
MAR 1:25 And Jesus gave reproach to him, saying, Be halted, and come forth from out of him!
MAR 1:26 And the unclean spirit having thrown him into a spasm, and having cried out with a great voice, came forth from out of him.
MAR 1:27 And all were distraught, so as to debate among themselves, saying, What is this? What new teaching is this? that with authority even to the unclean spirits he gives orders, and they obey him.
MAR 1:28 And went forth the report of him straightway into all the place round about Galilee.
MAR 1:29 And immediately, having gone forth from out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
MAR 1:30 And the mother-in-law of Simon was reclining in a fever. And immediately they speak to him concerning her.
MAR 1:31 And having come forward he raised her, holding her hand; and immediately the fever left her, and she served to them.
MAR 1:32 And evening having become, when the sun went down, they brought to him all the ones badly having it, and the ones being demon-possessed.
MAR 1:33 And the entire city being assembled was at the door.
MAR 1:34 And he cured many badly having it of various diseases, and he cast out many demons; and did not allow the demons to speak, for they knew him.
MAR 1:35 And having risen up exceedingly in the morning by night he departed, and went forth unto a desolate place, and there prayed.
MAR 1:36 And Simon and the ones with him pursued him.
MAR 1:37 And having found him, they say to him that, All seek you.
MAR 1:38 And he says to them, We should lead on unto the places having small cities, that even there I should proclaim; for I have come forth for this.
MAR 1:39 And he was proclaiming in their synagogues in all Galilee, and casting out the demons.
MAR 1:40 And a leper comes to him, enjoining him, and kneeling down to him, and saying to him that, If you should want, you are able to cleanse me.
MAR 1:41 And Jesus, being moved with compassion, stretched out his hand, and touched him, and says to him, I want; be cleansed!
MAR 1:42 And having spoken, immediately the leprosy went forth from him, and he was cleansed.
MAR 1:43 And having given strict charge to him, immediately he cast him away.
MAR 1:44 And he says to him, See that you should say not one thing to anyone. But go show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses assigned for a testimony to them!
MAR 1:45 But having gone forth, he began to proclaim much, and to spread abroad the matter, so that no longer was he able to enter openly into a city, but was outside in deserted places. And they came to him from every place.
MAR 2:1 And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was heard that he is in the house.
MAR 2:2 And immediately were gathered together many, so that they no longer had space, nor the places by the door. And he spoke to them the word.
MAR 2:3 And they come to him bringing a paralytic, being lifted by four men.
MAR 2:4 And not being able to draw near to him on account of the multitude, they unroofed the roof where he was. And having gouged it out, they let down the litter upon which the paralytic reclined.
MAR 2:5 And Jesus beholding their belief says to the paralytic, Son, your sins have been forgiven you.
MAR 2:6 And some of the scribes were there sitting down, and reasoning in their hearts,
MAR 2:7 Why does this one thus speak blasphemies? Who is able to forgive sins except one - God?
MAR 2:8 And immediately, Jesus recognizing in his spirit that so they reasoned within themselves, he said to them, Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
MAR 2:9 What is easier to say to the paralytic? The sins have been forgiven you; or to say, Arise, and lift your litter, and walk!
MAR 2:10 But that you should know that the son of man has authority to forgive sins upon the earth, he says to the paralytic,
MAR 2:11 To you I say, Arise, and lift your litter, and go unto your house!
MAR 2:12 And he arose immediately, and having lifted the litter, he went forth before all; so that all were amazed and glorified God, saying that, At no time we beheld thus.
MAR 2:13 And he went forth again by the sea; and all the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
MAR 2:14 And passing by, he beheld Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting down at the tax collector's station. And he says to him, Follow me! And having risen up he followed him.
MAR 2:15 And it came to pass in his reclining in his house, also many tax collectors and sinners reclined together with Jesus and his disciples; for there were many, and they followed him.
MAR 2:16 And the scribes and the Pharisees beholding him eating with the tax collectors and sinners, said to his disciples, Why is it that with the tax collectors and sinners he eats and drinks?
MAR 2:17 And Jesus having heard, he says to them, Not a need have the ones being strong of a physician, but the ones badly having it. I came not to call the just ones, but sinners to repentance.
MAR 2:18 And the disciples of John and the ones of the Pharisees were fasting. And they come and say to him, Why do the disciples of John and the ones of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?
MAR 2:19 And Jesus said to them, Are the sons of the able bridal chamber, in which the groom is with them, to fast? as much time as they themselves have with the groom, they are not able to fast.
MAR 2:20 But will come days whenever the groom should depart from them, and then they shall fast in those days.
MAR 2:21 And no one sews a piece of cloth of an unshrunk rag upon an old garment; otherwise its fullness lifts the new from the old, and the split becomes worse.
MAR 2:22 And no one casts new wine into old leather wine bags; otherwise the new wine tears the leather wine bags, and the wine pours out, and the leather wine bags are destroyed; but new wine is to be put into new leather wine bags.
MAR 2:23 And it came to pass for him to pass on the sabbaths through the wheat fields. And his disciples began to make their way while plucking the ears of wheat.
MAR 2:24 And the Pharisees said to him, See! Why do they do on the sabbaths which is not allowed?
MAR 2:25 And he said to them, At no time did you read what David did, when he had need, and he hungered, himself, and the ones with him?
MAR 2:26 How he entered into the house of God unto Abiathar the chief priest, and ate the breads of the place setting,, which is not allowed to eat, unless to the priests, and gave even to the ones being with him?
MAR 2:27 And he said to them, The sabbath on account of man exists, not man on account of the sabbath.
MAR 2:28 So that the son of man is lord also of the sabbath.
MAR 3:1 And he entered again into the synagogue; and a man was there having the hand being withered.
MAR 3:2 And they closely watched him, if on the sabbaths he will cure him, that they should charge him.
MAR 3:3 And he says to the man having the hand being withered, Arise into the middle!
MAR 3:4 And he says to them, Is it allowed on the sabbaths to do good, or to do evil? to preserve a life or to kill? And they kept silent.
MAR 3:5 And having looked round about them with anger, being grieved over the callousness of their heart, he says to the man, Stretch out your hand! And he stretched it out. And his hand was restored in health as the other.
MAR 3:6 And having gone forth, the Pharisees immediately with the Herodians took council against him, how they should destroy him.
MAR 3:7 And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea. And a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judea,
MAR 3:8 and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and on the other side of the Jordan. And the ones around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, having heard as much as he was doing, came to him.
MAR 3:9 And he spoke to his disciples, that a small boat should attend constantly to him because of the multitude, that they should not squeeze him.
MAR 3:10 For many he cured; so as to fall upon him, that as many as had scourges should touch him.
MAR 3:11 And the unclean spirits, whenever they viewed him, fell at him, and cried out, saying that, You are the son of God.
MAR 3:12 And he reproached them much that they should not make him apparent.
MAR 3:13 And he ascends into the mountain, and calls on whom he wants. And they went forth to him.
MAR 3:14 And he appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he should send them to proclaim,
MAR 3:15 and to have authority to cure the diseases, and to cast out the demons.
MAR 3:16 And he placed upon Simon the name Peter.
MAR 3:17 And to James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James he placed upon them the names Boanerges, which is, sons of thunder.
MAR 3:18 And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
MAR 3:19 and Judas Iscariot, who also delivered him up. And they come to a house.
MAR 3:20 And there comes together again a multitude so that they are not able neither to eat bread.
MAR 3:21 And hearing, the ones of his come forth to seize him; for they said that, He is startled.
MAR 3:22 And the scribes from Jerusalem having come down, said that, He has Beelzeboul, and that by the ruler of the demons he cast out the demons.
MAR 3:23 And having called them, in parables he spoke to them, How is Satan able to cast out Satan?
MAR 3:24 And if a kingdom should be parted out against itself, that kingdom is not able to stand.
MAR 3:25 And if a house should be parted out gainst itself, that house is not able to stand.
MAR 3:26 And if Satan rose up against himself, and has been parted out, he is not able to stand, but has an end.
MAR 3:27 No one is able to plunder the items of the strong man by entering into his house, if not first he should tie up the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
MAR 3:28 Amen I say to you that, All sins shall be forgiven to the sons of men, and blasphemies as many as they should have blasphemed.
MAR 3:29 But who ever should blaspheme against the holy spirit has not a release into the eon, but is liable to eternal judgment.
MAR 3:30 For they said, He has an unclean spirit.
MAR 3:31 Then come the brothers and his mother. And standing outside they sent to him, calling him.
MAR 3:32 And the multitude sat around him, and said to him, Behold, your mother and your brothers outside seek you.
MAR 3:33 And he answered to them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brothers?
MAR 3:34 And having looked round about on the ones sitting around him, he says, See - my mother and my brothers!
MAR 3:35 For who ever should do the will of God, this one is my brother and sister and mother.
MAR 4:1 And again he began to teach by the sea. And there was gathered together to him a great multitude, so that he, having stepped into the boat, sat down in the sea; and all the multitude by the sea were upon the ground.
MAR 4:2 And he taught them in parables many things, and said to them in his teaching,
MAR 4:3 Hearken! Behold, went forth the one sowing to sow.
MAR 4:4 And it came to pass in the sowing, some seed fell by the way, and the birds of the heaven came and devoured it.
MAR 4:5 And other fell upon the rocky place, where it did not have much earth; and immediately it rose up, because of the not having a depth of earth.
MAR 4:6 And the sun having arisen, it was scorched; and because of the not having root, it was dried up.
MAR 4:7 And other fell into the thorns, and the thorns ascended, and choked it, and it did not give fruit.
MAR 4:8 And other fell into the good earth, and gave fruit ascending and growing; and one bore thirty, and one sixty, and one a hundred.
MAR 4:9 And he said to them, The one having ears to hear, let him hear!
MAR 4:10 And when he was alone, they asked him, (the ones around him with the twelve,) the parable.
MAR 4:11 And he said to them, To you has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those outside, all things happen in parables.
MAR 4:12 That in seeing they should see, and not know; and in hearing they should hear, and not perceive; lest at any time they should turn, and their sins should be forgiven them.
MAR 4:13 And he says to them, Do you not perceive this parable - then how shall you perceive all the parables?
MAR 4:14 The one sowing sows the word.
MAR 4:15 And these are the ones by the way, where the word is sown. And whenever they hear, immediately comes Satan, and takes away the word being sown in their hearts.
MAR 4:16 And these are in like manner the ones upon the rocky places being sown; the ones, whenever they should hear the word, immediately with joy receive it;
MAR 4:17 and they do not have root in themselves, but are temporary. So then when affliction happens or persecution because of the word, immediately they are caused to stumble.
MAR 4:18 And these are the ones among the thorns being sown; the ones having heard the word,
MAR 4:19 and the anxieties of this eon, and the deception of the riches, and on account of the remaining desires entering in, choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
MAR 4:20 And these are the ones having been sown upon the good earth; the ones who hear the word, and welcome it, and bear fruit, one thirty, and one sixty, and one a hundred.
MAR 4:21 And he said to them, Does the lamp come out that it should be put under the bushel, or under the bed? Is it not that it should be placed upon the lamp-stand?
MAR 4:22 For not is anything hidden which should not be made manifest; nor becomes concealed, but that it should come into the open.
MAR 4:23 If any has ears to hear let him hear!
MAR 4:24 And he said to them, Take heed what you hear! In what measure you measure, it shall be measured to you. And to the ones hearing it shall be added to you.
MAR 4:25 For who ever has, it shall be given to him; and the one who does not have, even what he has shall be taken from him.
MAR 4:26 And he said, Thus is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast the seed upon the ground;
MAR 4:27 and should sleep, and should arise night and day, and the seed should burst forth, and should lengthen as he knows not.
MAR 4:28 For by itself the earth bears fruit; first the blade, then an ear of wheat, then the full grain in the ear of wheat.
MAR 4:29 And whenever the fruit should be delivered up, immediately he sends the sickle, for the harvest stands by.
MAR 4:30 And he said, To what should we liken the kingdom of God? or by what kind of parable shall we compare it?
MAR 4:31 As a kernel of mustard, which, whenever it should be sown upon the ground, is lesser than all the seeds of the ones upon the earth.
MAR 4:32 And whenever it should be sown, it ascends, and becomes greater than all the vegetations, and produces great branches; so as to enable the birds of the heaven to encamp under its shade.
MAR 4:33 And with such many parables he spoke to them the word, as they were able to hear.
MAR 4:34 And without parables he did not speak to them. But in private he explained all to his disciples.
MAR 4:35 And he says to them in that day, Evening becoming, we should go through unto the other side.
MAR 4:36 And letting go the multitude, they take him with themselves, as he was in the boat. But also other small boats were with him.
MAR 4:37 And there comes a tempest of a great wind, and the waves put upon into the boat, so that it already was filling.
MAR 4:38 And he was himself at the stern upon the pillow sleeping. And they awaken him, and say to him, Teacher, is it not a care to you that we perish?
MAR 4:39 And having awakened, he gave reproach to the wind, and said to the sea, Be silent! Be halted! And the wind abated, and there became a great calm.
MAR 4:40 And he said to them, Why are you so timid? how do you not have belief?
MAR 4:41 And they feared a great fear, and they said to one another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
MAR 5:1 And they came unto the other side of the sea, into the place of the Gadarenes.
MAR 5:2 And on his having come forth from out of the boat, immediately there met him from out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
MAR 5:3 who had his dwelling in the tombs; and neither with chains, no one was able to bind him;
MAR 5:4 for the reason he often with shackles and chains had been bound, and the chains had been pulled apart by him, and the shackles had been broken; and no one was strong enough to tame him.
MAR 5:5 And always, night and day, in the mountains, and in the tombs, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
MAR 5:6 And beholding Jesus from far off, he ran and did obeisance to him.
MAR 5:7 And having cried out with a great voice, he said, What is it to me and to you, Jesus, O son of the highest God? I adjure you by God, that you should not torment me.
MAR 5:8 For he said to him, Come forth, O unclean spirit, from out of the man!
MAR 5:9 And he asked him, What is your name? And he answered, saying, Legion, is my name; for we are many.
MAR 5:10 And he appealed to him much that he should not send them outside the place.
MAR 5:11 And was there by the mountains a great herd of swine grazing.
MAR 5:12 And all the demons appealed to him, saying, Send us forth into the swine! that into them we should enter.
MAR 5:13 And Jesus committed them immediately. And having come forth, the unclean spirits entered into the swine. And the herd advanced down the precipice into the sea, (and there were about two thousand;) and they drowned in the sea.
MAR 5:14 And the ones grazing the swine fled, and announced in the city, and in the fields. And they came forth to behold what it is taking place.
MAR 5:15 And they came to Jesus, and viewing the demon-possessed sitting down, and being dressed, and being of a sound mind, (the one having the legion;) and they feared.
MAR 5:16 And the ones beholding described to them how it happened to the one being demon-possessed, and concerning the swine.
MAR 5:17 And they began to appeal to him to go forth from their borders.
MAR 5:18 And of his stepping into the boat, the one having been demon-possessed appealed to him that he might be with him.
MAR 5:19 But Jesus would not allow him, but says to him, Go unto your house, to your own, and announce to them as much as the Lord did to you, and showed mercy on you!
MAR 5:20 And he went forth, and began to proclaim in the Decapolis as much as Jesus did for him. And all marveled.
MAR 5:21 And Jesus having passed through in the boat again unto the other side, there was gathered together a great multitude unto him; and he was by the sea.
MAR 5:22 And behold, there comes one of the chiefs of the synagogue, by name Jairus; and beholding him, he falls to his feet,
MAR 5:23 and appeals to him much, saying that, My young daughter is next to the last; that having come, you should place upon her your hands, so that she should be delivered; and she should live.
MAR 5:24 And he went forth with him; and a great multitude followed him, and squeezed together on him.
MAR 5:25 And a certain woman, being with a flow of blood twelve years,
MAR 5:26 and suffering much under many physicians, and having spent the things of hers - all, and not deriving benefit, but rather having come to the worse,
MAR 5:27 having heard concerning Jesus, having come among the multitude behind, touched his cloak.
MAR 5:28 For she said that, If only I should touch his garments, I shall be delivered.
MAR 5:29 And immediately the spring of her blood was dried; and she knew in the body that she was healed from the scourge.
MAR 5:30 And immediately Jesus realizing in himself the power went forth from out of him, having turned among the multitude, said, Who touched my garments?
MAR 5:31 And his disciples said to him, You see the multitude squeezing you, and you say, Who touched me?
MAR 5:32 And he looked round about to behold the one doing this.
MAR 5:33 And the woman being fearful and trembling, knowing what has happened to her, came and fell at him, and told him all the truth.
MAR 5:34 And he said to her, O daughter, the belief of yours has delivered you; go in peace, and be in health from your scourge!
MAR 5:35 While he was speaking, they came from the chief of the synagogue, saying that, Your daughter died; why yet inconvenience the teacher?
MAR 5:36 But Jesus immediately having heard the word being spoken, says to the chief of the synagogue, Do not fear, only believe!
MAR 5:37 And he did not allow anyone to follow together with him, except Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
MAR 5:38 And he comes unto the house of the chief of the synagogue, and views a tumult, and weeping, and much shouting.
MAR 5:39 And having entered, he says to them, Why make a disruption and weep? the child has not died, but sleeps.
MAR 5:40 And they ridiculed him. But casting out all, he takes to himself the father of the child, and the mother, and the ones with him, and he enters where the child was reclining.
MAR 5:41 And holding the hand of the child, he says to her, Talitha cumi! which is being translated, Young woman, to you I say, Arise!
MAR 5:42 And immediately the young woman arose, and walked; for she was twelve years old. And they were amazed with great astonishment.
MAR 5:43 And he warned them much that no one should know this; and he said to give to her to eat.
MAR 6:1 And he came forth from there, and went into his fatherland; and his disciples follow him.
MAR 6:2 And the sabbath taking place, he began to teach in the synagogue. And many hearing were overwhelmed, saying, From where did this one receive these things? and what wisdom having been given to him, that even such power takes place through his hands?
MAR 6:3 Is this not the son of the fabricator, the son of Mary, and brother of James, and Joses, and Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were stumbled in him.
MAR 6:4 And Jesus said to them that, A prophet is not without honor, except in his fatherland, and among the relatives, and in his own house.
MAR 6:5 And he was not able to do there not even one powerful work, except to a few ill ones having placed the hands upon, he cured.
MAR 6:6 And he marveled because of their unbelief. And he led about the towns round about, teaching.
MAR 6:7 And he calls on the twelve, and begins to send them two by two; and gave to them authority of the unclean spirits.
MAR 6:8 And he made exhortation to them that they should carry nothing in the way, except a rod only - no provision bag, no bread, no brass coin in the belt;
MAR 6:9 but sandals being tied on; and not putting on two inner garments.
MAR 6:10 And he said to them, Where ever you should enter into a house, there abide until whenever you should come forth from there!
MAR 6:11 And as many as should not receive you, nor should hear you, in going forth from there, shake off the dust underneath your feet for a testimony to them! Amen I say to you, More endurable will it be for Sodom or Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than that city.
MAR 6:12 And having come forth, they proclaimed that they should repent.
MAR 6:13 And they cast out many demons, and anointed many ill ones with oilolive oil., and they cured.
MAR 6:14 And king Herod heard; (for his name became open;) and said that, John, the one immersing, is arisen from the dead, and because of this the works of power operate in him.
MAR 6:15 Others said that, He is Elijah. And others said that, He is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.
MAR 6:16 And having heard, Herod said that, John whom I beheaded; this is he, he arose from the dead.
MAR 6:17 For he, Herod, having sent, seized John, and bound him in the prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother; for he married her.
MAR 6:18 For John said to Herod that, It is not allowed to you to have the wife of your brother.
MAR 6:19 But Herodias held it against him, and wanted to kill him; and was not able.
MAR 6:20 For Herod feared John, knowing him as a just and holy man, and he preserved him; and having heard of him, he did many things, and with pleasure heard him.
MAR 6:21 And an opportune day having become, when Herod made a supper for his birthday to his great men, and to the commanders of thousands, and to the first ones of Galilee;
MAR 6:22 and her daughter having entered, (the one of Herodias,) and was dancing, and was pleasing to Herod and to the ones reclining together with him, the king said to the young woman, Ask me what ever you should want, and I will give it to you!
MAR 6:23 And he swore by an oath to her that, What ever you should ask me, I will give it to you, unto half of my kingdom.
MAR 6:24 And she having gone forth, said to her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the baptist.
MAR 6:25 And having entered immediately with haste to the king, she asked, saying, I want that you give to me immediately upon a platter the head of John the baptist.
MAR 6:26 And the king being dejected because of the oaths, and of the ones reclining together with him, did not want to disregard her.
MAR 6:27 And the king immediately having sent a guard, gave orders for his head to be brought. And having gone forth he beheaded him in the prison,
MAR 6:28 and brought his head upon a platter, and gave it to the young woman. And the young woman gave it to her mother.
MAR 6:29 And having heard, his disciples came and lifted his corpse, and put it in the tomb.
MAR 6:30 And the apostles gathered together to Jesus, and they reported to him all, even as much as they did, and as much as they taught.
MAR 6:31 And he said to them, You come by yourselves in private unto a desolate place, and rest a little! for the ones coming and the ones going were many, and not even did they have an opportune time to eat.
MAR 6:32 And he went forth unto a desolate place in the boat in private.
MAR 6:33 And they beheld them going away, and many recognized him, and they ran together there on foot from all of the cities, and went forth and came together to him.
MAR 6:34 And having come forth, Jesus beheld a great multitude, and was moved with compassion over them, for they were as sheep not having a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
MAR 6:35 And already the hour having been great, his disciples having come forward to him, say that, It is a desolate place, and already it is a great hour.
MAR 6:36 Dismiss them! that having gone forth into the fields round about, and towns, they should buy to themselves breads; for they do not have anything they shall eat.
MAR 6:37 And he, answering, said to them, You give to them yourselves something to eat! And they say to him, Having gone forth should we buy two hundred denarii of breads, and should we give to them to eat?
MAR 6:38 And he says to them, How many breads do you have? Go and see! And having known, they say, Five and two fishes.
MAR 6:39 And he gave orders to them to lie all down, parties by parties, upon the green grass.
MAR 6:40 And they reclined, plot by plot, by hundred, and by fifty.
MAR 6:41 And having taken the five breads and the two fishes, having looked up into the heaven, he blessed, and broke off in pieces of the breads, and gave to his disciples, that they should place near to them; and the two fishes he portioned to all.
MAR 6:42 And all ate, and were filled.
MAR 6:43 And they took up twelve hampers full of pieces, and of the fishes.
MAR 6:44 And the ones having eaten of the breads were about five thousand men.
MAR 6:45 And immediately he compelled his disciples to step into the boat, and to lead to the other side to Bethsaida, until he should dismiss the multitude.
MAR 6:46 And having dismissed them, he went forth into the mountain to pray.
MAR 6:47 And evening having become, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone upon the land.
MAR 6:48 And he beheld them being tormented in the rowing; for the wind was opposite them. And around the fourth watch of the night he comes to them, walking upon the sea. And he wanted to go by them.
MAR 6:49 And they, beholding him walking upon the sea, thought it to be a phantom, and shouted aloud.
MAR 6:50 For all beheld him, and were disturbed. And immediately he spoke with them, and says to them, Take courage! I am he; fear not!
MAR 6:51 And he ascended to them into the boat; and the wind abated. And exceedingly beyond extra they were amazed and marveled among themselves,
MAR 6:52 for they perceived not concerning the breads; for their heart was calloused.
MAR 6:53 And having passed through, they came unto the land of Gennesaret, and were moored.
MAR 6:54 And on their coming forth from out of the boat, immediately having recognized him,
MAR 6:55 all running round about that place, began to carry round about upon the litters the ones having it badly, where they were hearing that - He is there.
MAR 6:56 And where ever he entered, into towns, or cities, or fields, they put the ones being invalid in the markets, and appealed to him that if only they could just touch the decorative hem of his cloak. And as many as touched him were delivered.
MAR 7:1 And the Pharisees gathered together to him, and some of the scribes, having come from Jerusalem.
MAR 7:2 And seeing certain ones of his disciples with common hands, (that is to say unwashed,) eating bread, they complained.
MAR 7:3 For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, unless they washed the hands with a fist, they do not eat, holding the tradition of the elders.
MAR 7:4 And coming from markets, if they should not immerse, they do not eat. And many other things there are which they take on themselves to hold - immersion of cups, and quart pitchers, and brass kettles, and dinner beds.
MAR 7:5 Thereupon the Pharisees and the scribes asked him, Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but with unwashed hands they eat the bread?
MAR 7:6 And he answering said to them that, Well Isaiah prophesied concerning you the hypocrites, as it has been written, This people esteem me with the lip, but their heart is far off at a distance from me.
MAR 7:7 And in vain they worship me, teaching as instructions the precepts of men.
MAR 7:8 For leaving the commandment of God you hold the tradition of men - immersions of quart pitchers and cups; and many other similar such things you do.
MAR 7:9 And he said to them, Well you annul the commandment of God, that you give heed to your tradition.
MAR 7:10 For Moses said, Esteem your father and your mother! and, Let the one speaking evil of father or mother come to an end in death!
MAR 7:11 But you say, If a man should say to a father or to a mother, It is corban, (which is a gift offering,) what ever of me you should derive benefit,
MAR 7:12 that no longer you allow him to do anything to his father or to his mother;
MAR 7:13 thereby voiding the word of God by your tradition, which you delivered. And many similar such things you do.
MAR 7:14 And having called all the multitude, he said to them, Hear me all, and perceive!
MAR 7:15 There is nothing from outside of man entering into him which is able to make him unclean; but the things going forth from him, those are the things making the man unclean.
MAR 7:16 If any has ears to hear let him hear!
MAR 7:17 And when he entered into a house from the multitude, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
MAR 7:18 And he says to them, Thus also you are senseless? Do you not comprehend that everything from outside entering into the man is not able to make him unclean.
MAR 7:19 For it enters not into his heart, but into the belly; and into the bowel it goes forth, cleansing all the foods.
MAR 7:20 And he said that, The thing going forth from out of the man, that defiles the man.
MAR 7:21 For from inside, from out of the heart of men evil thoughts go forth - adulteries, harlotries, murders,
MAR 7:22 frauds, desires for wealth, wickednesses, treachery, lewdness, a wicked eye, blasphemy, pride, folly.
MAR 7:23 All these evils from inside go forth, and defile the man.
MAR 7:24 And from there, having risen up, he went forth into the boundaries of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into the house, wanting no one to know; but he was not able to be unaware.
MAR 7:25 For a woman having heard about him, of which her young daughter had an unclean spirit, having come, fell at his feet.
MAR 7:26 And the woman was a Greek, Syro-phoenician by race; and she asked him that he should cast out the demon from her daughter.
MAR 7:27 And Jesus said to her, Allow the children first to be filled! For it is not good to take the bread of the children, and to throw it to the little dogs.
MAR 7:28 And she answered and says to him, Yes, O Lord, but even the little dogs underneath 7the 8table 1eat 2from 3the 4crumbs 5of the 6children.
MAR 7:29 And he said to her, On account of this word, go! the demon has come forth from out of your daughter.
MAR 7:30 And having gone forth unto her house, she found the demon having gone forth, and the daughter being laid upon the bed.
MAR 7:31 And again, having come forth from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, he came to the sea Galilee, in the midst of the borders of Decapolis.
MAR 7:32 And they bring to him a deaf-mute stammering; and they appeal to him that he should place his hand upon him.
MAR 7:33 And taking him away from the multitude in private, he put his fingers into his ears, and having spit, touched his tongue.
MAR 7:34 And having looked up into the heaven, he moaned, and says to him, Ephphatha, which is, Be opened wide!
MAR 7:35 And immediately were opened wide his hearing faculties, and the bond of his tongue was untied, and he spoke rightly.
MAR 7:36 And he warned them that they should speak to no one. But as much as he warned them, rather more extra they proclaimed.
MAR 7:37 And more exceedingly they were overwhelmed, saying, He has done all things well; both the deaf he makes to hear, and the speechless to speak.
MAR 8:1 In those days, a very great multitude being, and not having anything to eat, Jesus, having called his disciples, says to them,
MAR 8:2 I am moved with compassion over the multitude, for already three days they remain with me, and have not anything to eat.
MAR 8:3 And if I should release them hungry from fasting unto their house, they shall be fainting in the way; for some of them have come from far off.
MAR 8:4 And his disciples answered to him, saying, From what place shall any of these here be able to fill of bread at a desolate place?
MAR 8:5 And he asked them, How many breads have you? And they said, Seven.
MAR 8:6 And he gave exhortation to the multitude to recline upon the ground. And having taken the seven breads, having given thanks, he broke, and gave to his disciples, that they should place them near. And they placed them near to the multitude.
MAR 8:7 And they had a few small fishes. And having blessed, he said to place them near also.
MAR 8:8 And they ate, and were filled. And they lifted up an abundance of pieces - seven small baskets.
MAR 8:9 And the ones eating were about four thousand. And he dismissed them.
MAR 8:10 And immediately having stepped into the boat with his disciples, he came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
MAR 8:11 And the Pharisees came forth, and began to debate with him, seeking from him a sign from the heaven, testing him.
MAR 8:12 And having groaned in his spirit, he says, Why does this generation seek anxiously a sign? amen I say to you, Shall a sign be given to this generation?
MAR 8:13 And having left them, again having stepped into the boat, he went forth unto the other side.
MAR 8:14 And they forgot to take breads, and except for one bread, they did not have any with themselves in the boat.
MAR 8:15 And he warned them saying, See! Take heed of the yeast of the Pharisees, and of the yeast of Herod!
MAR 8:16 And they reasoned with one another, saying that, We do not have breads.
MAR 8:17 And knowing, Jesus says to them, Why do you reason that you do not have breads? Not yet do you comprehend, nor perceive? Do you still have your heart being calloused?
MAR 8:18 Having eyes, do you not see? and ears having, do you not hear? and do you not remember?
MAR 8:19 When the five breads I broke for the five thousand, how many hampers full of pieces did you lift? They say to him, Twelve.
MAR 8:20 And when the seven for the four thousand, how many small baskets full of pieces did you lift? And they said, Seven.
MAR 8:21 And he said to them, How do you not perceive?
MAR 8:22 And he comes into Bethsaida; and they bring to him a blind man, and appeal to him that he should touch him.
MAR 8:23 And taking hold of the hand of the blind man, he led him outside of the town; and having spit into his eyes, having placed his hands to him, he asks him if he sees anything.
MAR 8:24 And having looked up, he said, I see the men as trees, walking.
MAR 8:25 Then again he placed the hands upon his eyes, and he made him to look up. And he was restored, and looked clearly on all.
MAR 8:26 And he sent him unto his house, saying, Neither into the town should you enter, nor should you speak to any in the town.
MAR 8:27 And Jesus went forth, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea of Philippi. And in the way he asks his disciples, saying to them, Whom do men say me to be?
MAR 8:28 And they answered, John the Baptist. And others, Elijah; and others, One of the prophets.
MAR 8:29 And he says to them, And you, whom do you say me to be? And answering, Peter says to him, You are the Christ.
MAR 8:30 And he gave reproach to them that to no one they should tell concerning him.
MAR 8:31 And he began to teach them that it is necessary for the son of man to suffer many things, and to be rejected by the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and to be killed, and after three days to rise up.
MAR 8:32 And in an open manner he spoke the matter. And Peter taking him to himself, began to reproach him.
MAR 8:33 And he turned, and beholding his disciples, he reproached Peter, saying, Go behind me, satanadversary.! For you do not think the things of God, but the things of men.
MAR 8:34 And having called the multitude with his disciples, he said to them, Whoever wants to come after me, let him totally reject himself, and lift his cross, and follow me!
MAR 8:35 For who ever should want to preserve his life shall lose it; and who ever should lose his life, because of me and of the good news, this one will preserve it.
MAR 8:36 For what will it benefit a man, if he should gain the whole world, and suffer loss of his soul?
MAR 8:37 Or what shall a man give as a bargain for his soul?
MAR 8:38 For who ever should be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; even the son of man shall be ashamed of him, whenever he should come in the glory of his father with the holy angels.
MAR 9:1 And he said to them, Amen I say to you that, There are some of the ones here standing, who in no way shall taste of death, until whenever they should behold the kingdom of God coming in power.
MAR 9:2 And after six days Jesus took to himself Peter, and James, and John. And he brought them into a high mountain in private alone. And he was transformed in front of them.
MAR 9:3 And his garments became shining, exceedingly white as snow; such as a fuller upon the earth is not able to whiten.
MAR 9:4 And appeared unto them Elijah with Moses; and they were conversing together with Jesus.
MAR 9:5 And responding Peter says to Jesus, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and we should make three tents; to you one, and Moses one, and Elijah one.
MAR 9:6 For he knew not what he shall speak; for they were frightened.
MAR 9:7 And there became a cloud overshadowing them. And came a voice from out of the cloud, saying, This is my son the beloved; hear him!
MAR 9:8 And suddenly having looked round about, no longer they beheld anyone, but Jesus alone with themselves.
MAR 9:9 And of their going down from the mountain, he gave warning to them that to no one should they describe what they saw, except whenever the son of man should be raised up from the dead.
MAR 9:10 And the matter they kept to themselves, debating what is the thing - to rise up from the dead?
MAR 9:11 And they asked him, saying that, The scribes say that it is necessary for Elijah to come first.
MAR 9:12 And he answering said to them, Elijah indeed having come first restores all things; and how it has been written about the son of man, that many things he should suffer, and should be treated with contempt.
MAR 9:13 And I say to you that, Even Elijah has come, and they did to him as much as they wanted, as it was written of him.
MAR 9:14 And having come to the disciples, he beheld a great multitude around them, and scribes debating with them.
MAR 9:15 And immediately all the multitude beholding him were astonished, and were running up to greet him.
MAR 9:16 And he asked the scribes, What do you debate with them?
MAR 9:17 And answering one from out of the multitude said, Teacher, I brought my son to you, having a speechless spirit;
MAR 9:18 and where ever he should be overtaken it tears him; and he foams, and grinds his teeth, and he withers. And I spoke to your disciples that they should cast it out; and they prevailed not.
MAR 9:19 And answering to him, he says, O unbelieving generation, for how long will I be to you? for how long shall I endure you? bring him to me!
MAR 9:20 And they brought him to him. And beholding him, immediately the spirit threw him into a spasm; and having fallen upon the ground, he rolled foaming.
MAR 9:21 And he asked his father, How long a time is it that this has happened to him? And he said, From childhood.
MAR 9:22 And often it threw him both into the fire, and into waters, that it should destroy him. But if any way you are able, help us, be moved with compassion upon us!
MAR 9:23 And Jesus said to him, The thing, if you are able to believe - all things are possible to the one believing.
MAR 9:24 And immediately the father of the child crying out with tears, said, I believe, O Lord, help my unbelief!
MAR 9:25 And Jesus beholding that the multitude ran together, he reproached the unclean spirit, saying to it, O spirit speechless and mute; I give orders to you - Come forth out of him, and no longer should you enter into him!
MAR 9:26 And having cried out, and greatly throwing him into a spasm, it came forth. And he became as dead, so as for many to say that he died.
MAR 9:27 And Jesus, having held him by the hand, raised him. And he rose up.
MAR 9:28 And in his entering into the house, his disciples responded to him in private, saying that, We were not able to cast it out.
MAR 9:29 And he said to them, This kind by nothing is able to come forth, except by prayer and fasting.
MAR 9:30 And from there having gone forth, they passed through Galilee; and he did not want that any should know.
MAR 9:31 For he taught his disciples, and said to them that, The son of man is delivered up into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and having been killed, the third day he shall rise up.
MAR 9:32 But they knew not the saying, and feared to ask him.
MAR 9:33 And he came into Capernaum, and being in the house he asked them, What were you reasoning in the way among yourselves?
MAR 9:34 And they were silent; for with one another they were reasoning in the way, who was greater.
MAR 9:35 And sitting down, he called the twelve, and says to them, If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.
MAR 9:36 And having taken a child, he set it in the midst of them. And having embraced it, he said to them,
MAR 9:37 Who ever should receive one of such children in my name, receives me. And who ever should receive me, receives not me, but the one having sent me.
MAR 9:38 And John responded to him, saying, Teacher, we beheld a certain one casting out demons in your name, who does not follow us; and we restrained him, for he does not follow us.
MAR 9:39 And Jesus said, Do not restrain him! for there is no none who shall do a work of power in my name, and be able to quickly speak evil of me.
MAR 9:40 For he who is not against us is for us.
MAR 9:41 For who ever should give you a drink of a cup of water in my name, for you are of Christ, amen I say to you, in no way should he lose his wage.
MAR 9:42 And whoever should cause to stumble one of the little ones trusting in me, it is good to him rather if a mill stone encompass around his neck, and to be thrown into the sea.
MAR 9:43 And if your hand should cause you to stumble, cut it off! it is good to you to enter crippled into life, rather than having two hands to go forth into Gehenna, into the inextinguishable fire;
MAR 9:44 where their worm does not come to an end, and the fire is not extinguished.
MAR 9:45 And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off! it is good to you to enter into life lame, rather than having two feet to be thrown into Gehenna, into the inextinguishable fire;
MAR 9:46 where their worm does not come to an end, and the fire is not extinguished.
MAR 9:47 And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out! it is good to you to enter one-eyed into the kingdom of God, rather than having two eyes to be thrown into Gehenna of fire;
MAR 9:48 where their worm does not come to an end, and the fire is not extinguished.
MAR 9:49 For all shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.
MAR 9:50 The salt is good; but if the salt becomes insipid, by what means shall you season? Have salt in yourselves, and make peace with one another!
MAR 10:1 And from there rising up, he comes unto the borders of Judea by the other side of the Jordan. And multitudes went again to him; and, as he was accustomed, again he taught them.
MAR 10:2 And coming forward Pharisees asked him, Is it allowed for a man to dismiss a wife? testing him.
MAR 10:3 And answering he said to them, What did Moses give charge to you?
MAR 10:4 And they said, Moses committed to one's care to write a scroll of divorce, and to dismiss.
MAR 10:5 And answering Jesus said to them, Because of the hardness of your heart he wrote to you this commandment.
MAR 10:6 But from the beginning of creation God made them male and female.
MAR 10:7 Because of this a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be cleaved to his wife;
MAR 10:8 and the two will be for one flesh. So that no longer are they two, but one flesh.
MAR 10:9 What then God yoked together, let not man separate!
MAR 10:10 And in the house again his disciples asked him concerning the same.
MAR 10:11 And he says to them, Who ever should dismiss his wife, and should marry another, commits adultery against her.
MAR 10:12 And if a wife should dismiss her husband, and should marry another, she commits adultery.
MAR 10:13 And they brought to him children, that he should touch them. But the disciples gave reproach to the ones bringing them.
MAR 10:14 And having beheld, Jesus was indignant, and said to them, Allow the children to come to me, and do not restrain them! for of the ones such is the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:15 Amen I say to you, Who ever should not receive the kingdom of God as a child, in no way shall he enter into it.
MAR 10:16 And having embraced them, having put his hands upon them, he blessed them.
MAR 10:17 And in his going forth into the way, one running up, and kneeling at him, asked him, Good teacher, what shall I do that I should inherit eternal life?
MAR 10:18 And Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? no one is good except one, God.
MAR 10:19 The commandments you know, Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not witness falsely. Do not wrong. Esteem your father and mother!
MAR 10:20 And he answering said to him, Teacher, these things all I kept from my youth.
MAR 10:21 And Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, One thing to you is lacking. Go, as much as you have sell, and give to the poor! and you shall have treasure in heaven. And come follow me, taking up the cross!
MAR 10:22 But he being gloomy over the word went forth fretting; for he was holding many possessions.
MAR 10:23 And looking round about, Jesus says to his disciples, How with difficulty the ones having things shall enter into the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:24 And the disciples were distraught at his words. And Jesus again responding says to them, Sons, how difficult it is for the ones yielding upon things to enter into the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:25 It is easier for a camel to enter through the hole made by an awl, than a rich person to enter into the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:26 And they were extremely overwhelmed, saying to themselves, And who is able to be delivered?
MAR 10:27 And looking at them Jesus says, With men impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.
MAR 10:28 And Peter began to say to him, Behold, we left all, and followed you.
MAR 10:29 And answering Jesus said, Amen I say to you, There is no one who left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, because of me, and the good news,
MAR 10:30 that should not receive a hundred fold now in this time - houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and fields, with persecutions; and in the coming eon life eternal.
MAR 10:31 But many first will be last; and the last first.
MAR 10:32 And they were in the way ascending into Jerusalem; and Jesus was leading before them. And they were distraught; and following, they were afraid. And having taken to himself again the twelve, he began to speak to them the things about to come to pass to him, saying,
MAR 10:33 For behold, we ascend into Jerusalem; and the son of man shall be delivered up to the chief priests, and to the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and will deliver him up to the nations.
MAR 10:34 And they shall mock him, and shall whip him, and shall spit on him, and shall kill him; and in the third day he will rise up.
MAR 10:35 And going to him, James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were saying, Teacher, we want that what ever we should ask you should do for us.
MAR 10:36 And he said to them, What do you want me to do for you?
MAR 10:37 And they said to him, Give to us that one at your right, and one at your left, should sit in your glory.
MAR 10:38 And Jesus said to them, You know not what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup which I drink? and the immersion which I am immersed, to be immersed?
MAR 10:39 And they said to him, We are able. But Jesus said to them, The cup indeed which I drink, you shall drink; and the immersion which I am immersed, you shall be immersed.
MAR 10:40 But the sitting at my right and at my left is not mine to give; but to ones whom it has been prepared.
MAR 10:41 And hearing, the ten began to be indignant on account of James and John.
MAR 10:42 But Jesus having called them, says to them, You know that the ones seeming to rule the nations dominate them; and their great ones exercise authority over them.
MAR 10:43 But thus not will it be with you. But who ever should want to become great among you, shall be your servant.
MAR 10:44 And who ever of you should want to become first, shall be servant of all.
MAR 10:45 For even the son of man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
MAR 10:46 And they come unto Jericho. And of his exiting from Jericho and his disciples and a fit multitude, a son of Timaeus - Bar Timaeus the blind man was sat down by the way begging.
MAR 10:47 And having heard that it is Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out, and to say, The son of David, Jesus, show mercy on me!
MAR 10:48 And many reproached him that he should keep silent. But the more rather he cried out, O son of David, show mercy on me!
MAR 10:49 And Jesus stopping, spoke for him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying to him, Take courage! Arise! he calls you.
MAR 10:50 And throwing off his cloak, having risen up, he came to Jesus.
MAR 10:51 And responding Jesus says to him, What do you want I should do unto you? And the blind man said to him, Rabboni, that I should gain sight.
MAR 10:52 And Jesus said to him, Go! the belief of yours has delivered you. And immediately he gained sight, and followed Jesus in the way.
MAR 11:1 And when they approached unto Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, to the mount olives, he sends two of his disciples.
MAR 11:2 And he says to them, Go into the town in front of you! and immediately entering into it, you will find a foal being tied, upon which not one of men has sat; having untied it, lead it!
MAR 11:3 And if anyone should say to you, Why do you do this? say that, His master has need; and immediately he will send it here.
MAR 11:4 And they went forth, and found the foal being tied at the door outside upon the plaza; and they untied him.
MAR 11:5 And some of the ones standing there said to them, What do you do, untying the foal?
MAR 11:6 And they spoke to them as Jesus gave charge; and they allowed them.
MAR 11:7 And they led the foal to Jesus. And they put upon him their cloaks. And he sat upon him.
MAR 11:8 And many spread out their cloaks in the way. And others beat boughs from out of the trees, and spread them out in the way.
MAR 11:9 And the ones leading before, and the ones following, cried out, saying, Hosanna; being blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord.
MAR 11:10 Being blessed is the coming kingdom in the name of the Lord, of the one of our father David. Hosanna in the highest.
MAR 11:11 And Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and into the temple. And having looked round about all, the hour being already late, he went forth into Bethany with the twelve.
MAR 11:12 And in the next day, of their coming forth from Bethany, he hungered.
MAR 11:13 And beholding a fig-tree far off having leaves, he went to see if he shall find anything on it. And having come upon it, he found nothing except leaves; for it was not the season of figs.
MAR 11:14 And responding Jesus said to it, No longer from you into the eon may not one fruit be to eat. And his disciples heard.
MAR 11:15 And they come into Jerusalem. And Jesus having entered into the temple, began to cast out the ones selling and buying in the temple, and the tables of the money-changers and the chairs of the ones selling the doves he overturned;
MAR 11:16 and he did not allow that any carry vessels through the temple.
MAR 11:17 And he taught, saying to them, Has it not been written that, My house shall be called a house of prayer by all the nations? but you made it a cave of robbers.
MAR 11:18 And the scribes and the chief priests heard, and sought how they should destroy him; for they feared him, for all the multitude were overwhelmed by his teaching.
MAR 11:19 And when evening became, he went forth outside the city.
MAR 11:20 And in the morning, coming near, they beheld the fig-tree being dried up from the roots.
MAR 11:21 And calling to mind, Peter says to him, Rabbi, see! the fig-tree which you cursed is dried up.
MAR 11:22 And responding Jesus says to them, Have belief of God!
MAR 11:23 For amen I say to you that, Who ever should say to this mountain, Be lifted, and be thrown into the sea; and should not examine in his heart, but should trust that what he says takes place; it will be to him what ever he should say!
MAR 11:24 On account of this I say to you, All as much as you ask praying, trust that you receive, and it will be to you!
MAR 11:25 And whenever you stand firmly praying, forgive! if you have anything against anyone. That also your father in the heavens should forgive you your transgressions.
MAR 11:26 But if you do not forgive, not even your father in the heavens shall forgive your transgressions.
MAR 11:27 And they come again into Jerusalem. And in the temple of his walking, there comes to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders.
MAR 11:28 And they say to him, By what authority do you do these things? and who gave to you this authority that you should do these things?
MAR 11:29 And Jesus answering said to them, And I shall ask you one matter, and you answer me! and I will tell to you by what authority I do these things.
MAR 11:30 The immersion of John, was it from heaven, or from men? You answer me!
