MAR 11:31 And they considered it among themselves, saying, If we should say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did you not believe him?
MAR 11:32 But if we should say, From men; they feared the people; for all held that John really was a prophet.
MAR 11:33 And answering they say to Jesus, We do not know. And Jesus answering says to them, Nor I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
MAR 12:1 And he began to speak to them in parables. A man planted a vineyard, and placed around it a barrier, and dug a wine-vat, and built a tower, and handed it over to growers, and traveled abroad.
MAR 12:2 And he sent to the growers a servant at the season, that he should receive from the growers of the fruit of the vineyard.
MAR 12:3 But they, having taken, flayed him, and sent him away empty.
MAR 12:4 And again he sent to them another servant; and that one, having stoned, they smote on the head, and sent away being disgraced.
MAR 12:5 And again another he sent; and that one they killed, and many others - some flaying, and some killing.
MAR 12:6 Still then having one son, his beloved, he sent him also to them last, saying that, They will show respect for my son.
MAR 12:7 But those growers said to themselves that, This is the heir; come, we should kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
MAR 12:8 And taking him, they killed him, and cast him outside the vineyard.
MAR 12:9 What then shall he do - the master of the vineyard? He will come and destroy the growers, and will give the vineyard to others.
MAR 12:10 Nor did you read this scripture? The stone which the ones building rejected, this is become for head of the corner.
MAR 12:11 By the Lord this happened, and it is wonderful in our eyes.
MAR 12:12 And they sought to seize him, but feared the multitude; for they knew that he spoke the parable against them. And leaving him, they went forth.
MAR 12:13 And they sent to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they should catch him in a matter.
MAR 12:14 And they having come, say to him, Teacher, we know that you are true, and there is not a care to you concerning anyone. For you see not to the person of men, but in truth the way of God you teach - is it allowed to give tribute to Caesar, or not?
MAR 12:15 Should we give, or should we not give? And he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, Why do you test me? Bring to me a denarius, that I should see it!
MAR 12:16 And they brought it. And he says to them, Whose image is this, and the inscription? And they said to him, Caesar.
MAR 12:17 And answering, Jesus said to them, Render the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God. And they marveled at him.
MAR 12:18 And Sadducees came to him who say a resurrection not to be; and they asked him, saying,
MAR 12:19 Teacher, Moses wrote to us, that if any brother should die, and should leave behind a wife, and she should not leave children, that his brother should take his wife, and should raise up seed to his brother.
MAR 12:20 There were seven brothers. And the first took a wife, and dying did not leave seed.
MAR 12:21 And the second took her, and he died, and not even he left seed. And the third likewise.
MAR 12:22 And the seven took her, and left not a seed. Last of all the wife died also.
MAR 12:23 In then the resurrection, whenever they shall arise, which of them shall she be wife? for the seven had her for a wife.
MAR 12:24 And answering Jesus said to them, On account of this do you not err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God?
MAR 12:25 For whenever they rise up from the dead, neither they marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as angels in the heavens.
MAR 12:26 But concerning the dead, that they arise; did you not read in the book of Moses, about the bush as God spoke to him? saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
MAR 12:27 He is not the God of the dead, but God of the living. You then greatly erred.
MAR 12:28 And one of the scribes having come forward, having heard them debating, knowing that he answered well to them, asked him, Which is foremost commandment of all?
MAR 12:29 And Jesus answered to him that, Foremost of all of the commandments, Hear, O Israel! The Lord our God is one Lord.
MAR 12:30 And You shall love the Lord your God from all your heart, and from all your soul, and from all your thought, and from all your strength. This is the foremost commandment.
MAR 12:31 And the second is likened to this, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Another commandment is not greater than these.
MAR 12:32 And the scribe said to him, Well, teacher, in truth you spoke; that there is one God; and there is not another besides him.
MAR 12:33 And to love him from the entire heart, and from the entire understanding, and from the entire soul, and from the entire strength, and to love the neighbor as himself, is more than all the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifice offerings.
MAR 12:34 And Jesus beholding him, that prudently he answered, said to him, You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one any longer dared to question him.
MAR 12:35 And responding Jesus said, of teaching in the temple, How say the scribes that the Christ is son of David?
MAR 12:36 For David himself said by holy spirit, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit down at my right until whenever I should make your enemies a footstool for your feet!
MAR 12:37 David then himself calls him Lord; then from where is he his son? And the great multitude heard him with pleasure.
MAR 12:38 And he said to them in his teaching, Take heed of the scribes, the ones wanting to walk in robes, and greetings in the markets,
MAR 12:39 and first seats in the synagogues, and first place at the suppers;
MAR 12:40 the ones devouring the houses of the widows, and making an excuse for praying long; these shall receive more extra judgment!
MAR 12:41 And Jesus having sat down over against the treasury, viewed how the multitude cast money into the treasury. And many rich cast much.
MAR 12:42 And one poor widow having come, threw two leptas, which is a quadrans.
MAR 12:43 And having called his disciples, he says to them, Amen I say to you that, This poor widow cast more than all of the ones casting into the treasury.
MAR 12:44 For all from out of their abundance cast; but this woman from her deficiency cast all as much as she had, her entire livelihood.
MAR 13:1 And as he was going forth from out of the temple, one of his disciples says to him, Teacher, behold what stones and what constructions!
MAR 13:2 And Jesus responding said to him, You see these great constructions? in no way shall there be left stone upon stone which shall not be broken up.
MAR 13:3 And as he was sitting in the mount of olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him in private,
MAR 13:4 Tell to us when these things will be, and what the sign is whenever all these things are about to be completed!
MAR 13:5 And Jesus answering them began to say, Take heed that not anyone should mislead you!
MAR 13:6 For many shall come in my name, saying that, I am he; and shall mislead many.
MAR 13:7 But whenever you should hear of wars and reports of wars, be not alarmed! for it is necessary to take place; but not yet is the end.
MAR 13:8 For shall rise up nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there shall be earthquakes in different places, and there shall be famines and disturbances; these are the beginnings of pangs.
MAR 13:9 And you take heed yourselves! for they shall deliver you up unto sanhedrins; and in synagogues you shall be flayed; and before governors and kings you shall be stood because of me, for a testimony to them.
MAR 13:10 And unto all the nations the good news must first be proclaimed.
MAR 13:11 And whenever they should lead you, being delivered up, do not be anxious beforehand what you should speak, nor meditate upon! But what ever should be given to you in that hour, this speak! for you are not the ones speaking, but the holy spirit.
MAR 13:12 And brother shall deliver up brother unto death, and a father a child; and children shall rise up against parents, and shall put them to death.
MAR 13:13 And you shall be a thing being detested by all on account of my name. But the one remaining unto the end, this one shall be delivered.
MAR 13:14 And whenever you should behold the abomination of the desolation, the thing having been spoken by Daniel the prophet, standing where it must not, (let the one reading comprehend!) then let the ones in Judea flee into the mountains!
MAR 13:15 And the one upon the roof, let him go not down into the house, nor enter to take anything from out of his house!
MAR 13:16 And the one being in the field, let him not turn back to take his cloak!
MAR 13:17 And woe to the ones having one in the womb, and to the ones nursing in those days.
MAR 13:18 And pray that your flight might not be in the winter!
MAR 13:19 For those days will be an affliction, such as has not taken place with this kind from the beginning of the creation which God created until the present, and in no way shall be.
MAR 13:20 And unless the Lord cut short the days, not would any flesh have escaped; but on account of the chosen ones, whom he chose, he cut short the days.
MAR 13:21 And then if any should say to you, behold, here is the Christ; or, Behold, there - do not believe it!
MAR 13:22 For shall arise false christs and false prophets, and shall give signs and miracles, to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
MAR 13:23 But you take heed! Behold, I have described beforehand to you all things.
MAR 13:24 And in those days, after that affliction, the sun shall be made dark, and the moon shall not give her brightness,
MAR 13:25 and the stars of the heaven will be falling off, and the powers in the heavens shall be shaken.
MAR 13:26 And then they shall see the son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
MAR 13:27 And then he shall send his angels, and they will assemble his chosen ones from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth unto the uttermost part of heaven.
MAR 13:28 But from the fig-tree learn the parable! Whenever already her tender branches come to pass, and she should spring forth the leaves, know that summer is near!
MAR 13:29 So also you, whenever you should see these taking place, know that it is near at the doors!
MAR 13:30 Amen I say to you that, In no way should this generation pass by, until of which all these should take place.
MAR 13:31 The heaven and the earth shall pass away; but my words in no way shall pass away.
MAR 13:32 But concerning that day and of the hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the son - only the father.
MAR 13:33 Take heed, be awake and pray! For you know not when the time is.
MAR 13:34 It is as a man going abroad, leaving his house, and giving to his servants the authority, and to each one his work, and gave charge to the doorkeeper that he should be vigilant.
MAR 13:35 Be vigilant then! for you know not when the master of the house comes - at evening, or at midnight, or at the crowing of a rooster, or in the morning.
MAR 13:36 Lest coming suddenly he should find you sleeping.
MAR 13:37 And what shall I say to you - to all I say, Be vigilant!
MAR 14:1 And it was the passover, and the holiday of the unleavened breads after two days. And the chief priests and the scribes sought how they should kill him by treachery seizing him.
MAR 14:2 And they said, Not during the holiday, lest at any time there shall be a tumult of the people.
MAR 14:3 And he being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, in his reclining, came a woman having an alabaster jar of perfumed liquid spikenard of great cost. And having broken the alabaster jar, she poured out on his head.
MAR 14:4 And there were some being indignant within themselves, and saying, For why has this loss of perfumed liquid taken place?
MAR 14:5 For it was possible to sell this above three hundred denarii, and to be given to the poor; and they strictly charged her.
MAR 14:6 And Jesus said, Let her go! Why do you make troubles for her? she worked a good work for me.
MAR 14:7 For at all times you have the poor among yourselves, and whenever you want you are able to do good for them; but you do not have me at all times.
MAR 14:8 What she has, she did; she first took to perfume my body for the entombing.
MAR 14:9 Amen I say to you, Where ever this good news should be proclaimed in the entire world, even what this woman did shall be spoken for her memorial.
MAR 14:10 And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went forth to the chief priests, that he should deliver him up to them.
MAR 14:11 And they hearing, rejoiced. And they promised to give money to him. And he sought how opportunely he should deliver him up.
MAR 14:12 And on the first day of the unleavened breads, when they sacrifice the passover, his disciples say to him, Where do you want, that going forth, we shall prepare that you should eat the passover?
MAR 14:13 And he sends two of his disciples, and says to them, Go into the city, and a man will meet you bearing a clay vessel of water - you follow him!
MAR 14:14 And where ever he should enter, say to the master of the house that, The teacher says, Where is the lodging where I should eat the passover with my disciples?
MAR 14:15 And he will show to you a great upper room being spread out prepared; there prepare for us!
MAR 14:16 And his disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found it as he said to them. And they prepared the passover.
MAR 14:17 And evening having become, he comes with the twelve.
MAR 14:18 And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, Amen I say to you that, One of you shall deliver me up - the one eating with me.
MAR 14:19 And they began to grieve, and to say to him one by one, No, how I? and another, No, how I?
MAR 14:20 And answering he said to them, One from out of the twelve dipping with me into the saucer.
MAR 14:21 Indeed the son of man goes away, as it has been written concerning him. But woe to that man by whom the son of man is delivered up; it was good to him if that man was not born.
MAR 14:22 And as they were eating, Jesus having taken the bread, having blessed, broke, and gave to them. And he said, Take! Eat! This is my body.
MAR 14:23 And having taken the cup, having given thanks, he gave to them; and all drank of it.
MAR 14:24 And he said to them, This is my blood of the new covenant, being poured out for many.
MAR 14:25 Amen I say to you that, No longer in any way shall I drink of the offspring of the grapevine, until that day whenever I should drink it new in the kingdom of God.
MAR 14:26 And having sung praise, they came forth unto the mount of olives.
MAR 14:27 And Jesus says to them that, All shall be stumbled in me in this night. For it has been written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be dispersed.
MAR 14:28 But after my arising, I will lead before you into Galilee.
MAR 14:29 And Peter said to him, Even if all shall be stumbled, yet not I.
MAR 14:30 And Jesus says to him, Amen I say to you that, Today in this night, before twice the rooster calls out loud, three times you shall totally reject me.
MAR 14:31 And he all the extra said, Rather if it should be necessary for me to die together with you, in no way shall I totally reject you. And likewise also all spoke.
MAR 14:32 And they came unto a place of which the name is Gethsemane. And he says to his disciples, Sit here while I pray!
MAR 14:33 And taking Peter and James and John with himself, that he began to be astonished and anxious.
MAR 14:34 And he says to them, My soul is dejected unto death. Abide here and be vigilant!
MAR 14:35 And having gone forth a little, he fell upon the ground, and prayed that, if it is possible the hour might pass from him.
MAR 14:36 And he said, Abba father, all things are possible with you; carry away this cup from me! But not what I want, but what you want.
MAR 14:37 And he comes and finds them sleeping. And he says to Peter, Simon, do you sleep? Were you not able one hour to be vigilant?
MAR 14:38 Be vigilant and pray, that you should not enter into a test! Indeed the spirit is eager, but the flesh weak.
MAR 14:39 And again having gone forth he prayed, having said the same word.
MAR 14:40 And having returned, he found them again sleeping, for their eyes were being weighed down, and they did not know what they should answer to him.
MAR 14:41 And he comes the third time, and says to them, Sleep the remaining, and rest! Be at a distance! the hour came. Behold, the son of man is delivered up into the hands of sinners.
MAR 14:42 Arise! we should lead on. Behold, the one delivering me up approaches.
MAR 14:43 And immediately while he was speaking, Judas comes, being one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and wood spears, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
MAR 14:44 And the one delivering him up had given an agreed upon sign to them, saying, Whom ever I should kiss, it is he - seize him, and take him away safely!
MAR 14:45 And having come, immediately having come forward to him, he says to him, Rabbi, rabbi - Hail rabbi!; and kissed him.
MAR 14:46 And they put upon him their hands, and seized him.
MAR 14:47 But a certain one of the ones standing by, having unsheathed the sword, hit the servant of the chief priest, and removed his ear.
MAR 14:48 And responding Jesus said to them, As unto a robber do you come forth with swords and wood spears to seize me?
MAR 14:49 By day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me. But it is that the scriptures should be fulfilled.
MAR 14:50 And leaving him, all fled.
MAR 14:51 And one certain young man follows him, having put on a fine linen garment upon his naked body; and the young men seized him.
MAR 14:52 But leaving behind the fine linen garment, he fled naked from them.
MAR 14:53 And they took Jesus to the chief priest. And all the chief priests gather to him and the elders and the scribes.
MAR 14:54 And Peter from far off followed him, even inside into the courtyard of the chief priest. And he was sitting together with the officers, and being heated by the light.
MAR 14:55 And the chief priests and the entire sanhedrin sought testimony against Jesus to put him to death; and they did not find.
MAR 14:56 For many witnessed falsely against him, and the testimonies were not equal.
MAR 14:57 And certain ones having risen up, witnessed falsely against him, saying that,
MAR 14:58 We heard him saying that, I shall break up this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.
MAR 14:59 And not even thus was their testimony equal.
MAR 14:60 And the chief priest having risen up into the midst, questioned Jesus, saying, Do you not answer one thing? what is it these are bearing witness against you?
MAR 14:61 And he kept silent, and not one thing did he answer. Again the chief priest questioned him, and says to him, Are you the Christ, the son of the blessed?
MAR 14:62 And Jesus said, I am, and you shall see the son of man sitting on the right of the power, and coming with the clouds of the heaven.
MAR 14:63 And the chief priest, having torn his inner garments, says, What yet need do we have of witnesses?
MAR 14:64 You heard the blasphemy. What does it appear to you? And they all condemned him to be liable of death.
MAR 14:65 And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say to him, Prophesy! And the officers threw slaps at him.
MAR 14:66 And Peter being in the courtyard below, there comes one of the maidservants of the chief priest.
MAR 14:67 And beholding Peter heating himself, having looked at him, she says, Even you were with Jesus the one of Nazareth.
MAR 14:68 But he denied, saying, I have not known him, nor have knowledge of what you say. And he went forth outside into the porch of the courtyard; and a rooster called out.
MAR 14:69 And the maidservant beholding him, again began to say to the ones standing by that, This one is of them.
MAR 14:70 And he again denied. And after a little time, again the ones standing by said to Peter, Truly you are of them, for even you are a Galilean, and your speech coincides.
MAR 14:71 And he began to devote to consumption and to swear by an oath that, I have not known this man of whom you speak.
MAR 14:72 And a second time a rooster called out. And Peter called to mind the saying which Jesus said to him that, Before a rooster calls out twice, you shall totally reject me three times. And giving it attention he wept.
MAR 15:1 And immediately in the morning, a council having been appointed, the chief priests with the elders and the scribes and the entire sanhedrin, having bound Jesus, carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
MAR 15:2 And Pilate questioned him, Are you the king of the Jews? And answering he said to him, You say it.
MAR 15:3 And the chief priests charged him much; but he answered not one thing.
MAR 15:4 And Pilate again questioned him, saying, Do you not answer one thing? See how much they bear witness against you!
MAR 15:5 But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate marveled.
MAR 15:6 And according to the holiday he loosed to them one prisoner, whomsoever they asked.
MAR 15:7 And there was the one being called Barabbas, being bound with the joint-conspirators, who with the faction committed murder.
MAR 15:8 And yelling out, the multitude began to ask him to do as continually he did to them.
MAR 15:9 And Pilate answered them, saying, Do you want that I should release to you the king of the Jews?
MAR 15:10 For he knew that through envy the chief priests delivered him up.
MAR 15:11 But the chief priests incited the multitude, that rather he should release Barabbas to them.
MAR 15:12 And Pilate, responding again said to them, What then do you want I shall do to whom you call King of the Jews?
MAR 15:13 And again they cried out, Crucify him!
MAR 15:14 And Pilate said to them, For what evil did he? But they more exceedingly cried out, Crucify him!
MAR 15:15 And Pilate, wanting to do the fit thing for the multitude, released to them Barabbas, and delivered up Jesus, having been scourged, that he should be crucified.
MAR 15:16 And the soldiers took him away inside the courtyard, which is the praetorium; and they called together all the cohort.
MAR 15:17 And they clothed him in purple, and having plaited a thorny crown they put it on him.
MAR 15:18 And they began to salute him, Hail, O king of the Jews!
MAR 15:19 And they beat him on the head with a reed, and spat on him, and setting the knees did obeisance to him.
MAR 15:20 And when they mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put on him his own garments, and led him out that they should crucify him.
MAR 15:21 And they conscripted one passing by, (a certain Simon a Cyrenian, coming from the field, the father of Alexander and Rufus,) that he should carry his cross.
MAR 15:22 And they brought him unto Golgotha, a place which is being translated, Place of a Skull.
MAR 15:23 And they gave to him myrrh mixed with wine to drink; but he did not take.
MAR 15:24 And having crucified him, they divided his garments, casting a lot over them, who should take what.
MAR 15:25 And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
MAR 15:26 And there was the inscription of his accusation being inscribed, The king of the Jews.
MAR 15:27 And with him they crucified two robbers, one at his right, and one at his left.
MAR 15:28 And the scripture was fulfilled saying, And he was imputed with lawless ones.
MAR 15:29 And the ones coming near blasphemed him, shaking their heads, and saying, Ah, the one breaking up the temple, and in three days rebuilding it,
MAR 15:30 deliver yourself, and come down from the cross!
MAR 15:31 And in like manner the chief priests mocking among one another with the scribes saying, Others he delivered; himself he is not able to deliver;
MAR 15:32 the Christ, the king of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, that we should know and should believe. And the ones being crucified along with him berated him.
MAR 15:33 And having become the sixth hour, darkness took place upon the entire land until the ninth hour.
MAR 15:34 And in the ninth hour Jesus yelled out a great voice, saying, Eloi, eloi, lima. sabacthani? which is being translated, My God, my God, for why did you abandon me?
MAR 15:35 And some of the ones standing by, having heard, said, Behold, he calls Elijah.
MAR 15:36 And one having run then filled the sponge with vinegar; and having put it on also a reed, gave him to drink, saying, Allow it! We should see if Elijah comes to lower him.
MAR 15:37 And Jesus letting go with a great voice, expired.
MAR 15:38 And the veil of the temple split in two from above unto below.
MAR 15:39 And beholding, the centurion standing by opposite him, that thus having cried out he expired, said, Truly this man was son of God.
MAR 15:40 And there were also women from far off viewing; among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the one of James the less and Joses mother, and Salome;
MAR 15:41 (the ones who also when he was in Galilee followed him, and served to him;) and many others - the ones going up with him unto Jerusalem.
MAR 15:42 And already evening having become, (since it was the preparation which is before the sabbath,)
MAR 15:43 there came Joseph, the one from Arimathea, a decent counselor, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, having dared entered to Pilate, and asked the body of Jesus.
MAR 15:44 And Pilate marveled that already he has died. And having called the centurion, he questioned him if he died earlier.
MAR 15:45 And having known from the centurion, he presented the body to Joseph.
MAR 15:46 And having bought fine linen, and having lowered him, he wrapped him in the fine linen, and laid him down in a tomb which was quarried from out of rock, and rolled a stone upon the door of the tomb.
MAR 15:47 And Mary Magdalene and Mary of Joses viewed where he was placed.
MAR 16:1 And the elapsing of the sabbath, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the one of James, and Salome, bought aromatics, that having come they should anoint him.
MAR 16:2 And exceedingly in the morning of day one of the sabbaths, they come unto the tomb at the rising of the sun.
MAR 16:3 And they said among themselves, Who shall roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?
MAR 16:4 And having looked up, they viewed that the stone was rolled away - for it was exceedingly great.
MAR 16:5 And having entered into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting down on the right, being clothed in white apparel; and they were astonished.
MAR 16:6 And he says to them, Do not be astonished! You seek Jesus the Nazarene, the one having been crucified; he was arisen, he is not here; see the place where they put him!
MAR 16:7 But go, say to his disciples and to Peter that he goes before you unto Galilee! There you shall see him, as he said to you.
MAR 16:8 And having come forth quickly, they fled from the tomb; and trembling and a change of state took hold of them; and they told no one not one thing; for they were afraid.
MAR 16:9 And having risen in the morning on the first day of the sabbath, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
MAR 16:10 That one having gone reported to the ones having been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
MAR 16:11 And those, having heard that he lives, and was seen by her, disbelieved.
MAR 16:12 And after these things with two of them walking, he was made manifest in another appearance, in their going into the field.
MAR 16:13 And those having gone forth reported to the rest - and those neither believed.
MAR 16:14 Afterwards with them reclining, he was made manifest to them to the eleven. And he berated their unbelief and hardness of heart, that to the ones seeing him being arisen they did not believe.
MAR 16:15 And he said to them, Having gone into the world all together, proclaim the good news to all in the creation!
MAR 16:16 The one believing and being immersed shall be delivered; but the one disbelieving shall be condemned.
MAR 16:17 And signs to these believing shall follow closely - in my name they shall cast out demons; they shall speak new languages;
MAR 16:18 they shall take away serpents; and if anything deadly they shall drink, in no way shall it hurt them; they shall place hands upon ill ones, and they shall suffice well.
MAR 16:19 So then the Lord, after speaking with them, was taken up into the heaven, and sat at the right of God.
MAR 16:20 And those having gone forth proclaimed everywhere of the Lord, and were working together firming the word by the signs following after. Amen.
LUK 1:1 Seeing that many attempted to arrange a narrative concerning the things having a full assurance among us,

LUK 1:3 it seemed good that I also, having followed closely from the beginning in all things exactly, write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
LUK 1:4 that you should realize concerning the certainty of which matters you were instructed.
LUK 1:5 It came to pass in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, with a certain priest, by name Zacharias, of the daily rotations of Abia; and his wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
LUK 1:6 And they were both just before God, going in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
LUK 1:7 And there was not a child to them, in so far as Elizabeth was sterile, and both were advancing in their days.

LUK 1:11 And appeared to him an angel of the Lord standing at the right of the altar of the incense.
LUK 1:12 And Zacharias was disturbed seeing him, and fear fell upon him.

LUK 3:1 And in the fifteenth year of the governing of Tiberius Caesar, and the governing of Pontius Pilate of the Jews, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother being tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis the region, and Lysanias being tetrarch of Abilene,

LUK 3:3 And he went into all the place round about the Jordan, proclaiming an immersion of repentance for a release of sins;
LUK 3:4 as it has been written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, saying, A voice yelling in the wilderness, Prepare the way of the Lord! Make straight his roads!
LUK 3:5 Every ravine shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be lowered; and the crooked will be for straight, and the rough for smooth ways;
LUK 3:6 and all flesh shall see the deliverance of God.
LUK 3:7 He said then to the multitudes coming forth to be immersed by him, Offspring of vipers, who indicated to you to flee from the wrath about to be?
LUK 3:8 Do then fruits worthy of repentance! For you should not begin to say among yourselves, We have father Abraham; for I say to you that, God is able from out of these stones to raise children to Abraham.

LUK 4:1 And Jesus full of holy spirit returned from the Jordan, and was led by the spirit into the wilderness,

LUK 4:3 And the devil said to him, If you are Son of God, tell to this stone that it become bread!

LUK 4:8 And answering to him, Jesus said, Go behind me Satan! for it has been written, You shall do obeisance to the Lord your God, and to him alone shall you serve.

LUK 4:11 and upon hands they shall lift you, lest at any time your foot should stumble against a stone.
LUK 4:12 And answering Jesus said to him that, It has been said, Do not put to test the Lord your God!

LUK 4:24 And he said, Amen I say to you that, Not one prophet is accepted in his fatherland.

LUK 4:26 and to not one of them was Elijah sent, except unto Sarepta of Sidon, to a widow woman.

LUK 4:28 And they were all filled with rage in the synagogue, hearing these things.
LUK 4:29 And having risen up, they cast him outside the city, and led him unto a brow of the mountain upon which their city had been built, so as to fling him downwards.
LUK 4:30 But he, going through the midst of them, went away.
LUK 4:31 And he went down unto Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the sabbaths.
LUK 4:32 And they were overwhelmed at his teaching; for his word was with authority.

LUK 4:35 And Jesus reproached him, saying, Be halted, and come forth from him! And the demon having tossed him into the midst, came forth from him, in nothing having hurt him.
LUK 4:36 And there became a stupefaction upon all, and they conversed together with one another, saying, What word is this that with authority and power he gives orders to the unclean spirits, and they come forth?
LUK 4:37 And the sound concerning him went forth unto every place round about.
LUK 4:38 And rising up from out of the synagogue, he entered into the house of Simon. And the mother-in-law of Simon was constrained by a great fever; and they asked him concerning her.
LUK 4:39 And standing above her, he reproached the fever, and it left her. And immediately rising up she served to them.
LUK 4:40 And at the going down of the sun, all as many as had ones being weak by various diseases led them to him; and having placed the hands upon each one of them, he cured them.
LUK 4:41 And there came forth also demons from many, crying out and saying that, You are the Christ the son of God. And reproaching he did not allow them to speak; for they knew him to be the Christ.
LUK 4:42 And becoming day, having come forth, he went into a desolate place. And the multitudes sought him, and came unto him, and constrained him to not go from them.
LUK 4:43 And he said to them that, Also to the other cities it is necessary for me to announce good news - the kingdom of God; for in this I have been sent.
LUK 4:44 And he was proclaiming in the synagogues of Galilee.
LUK 5:1 And it came to pass in the time the multitude pressed upon him to hear the word of God, and he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret,
LUK 5:2 and saw two boats standing by the lake. And the fishermen having disembarked from them were washing the nets.
LUK 5:3 And having stepped into one of the boats, which was Simon's, he asked him to turn back a little from the land. And having sat down he taught the multitudes from out of the boat.
LUK 5:4 And as he ceased speaking, he said to Simon, Turn back into the depth, and let down your nets for a catch!
LUK 5:5 And responding Simon said to him, Master, through the entire night having tired, we took nothing; but on your word I will let down the net.
LUK 5:6 And this having done, they closed up a multitude of great fishes; and their net was being torn.
LUK 5:7 And they nodded to their partners in the other boat, to come seize them. And they came, and filled both the boats, so as to submerge them.

LUK 5:20 And beholding their belief, he said to him, O man, your sins are forgiven to you.

LUK 5:23 What is easier to say? Your sins are forgiven to you; or to say, Arise and walk!

LUK 5:27 And after these things he went forth, and saw a tax collector, by name Levi, sitting down at the tax collector's station. And he said to him, Follow me!
LUK 5:28 And leaving behind all, having risen, he followed him.
LUK 5:29 And Levi made a great banquet for him in his house. And there was a great multitude of tax collectors, and others who were with them reclining.
LUK 5:30 And their scribes and the Pharisees grumbled against his disciples, saying, Why with the tax collectors and sinners does he eat and drink?
LUK 5:31 And answering Jesus said to them, No need do the ones being in health have of a physician; but the ones having illnesses.

LUK 5:35 But there will come days, that whenever the groom departs from them, then they shall fast in those days.

LUK 5:37 And no one casts new wine into old leather wine bags; otherwise, the new wine shall tear the leather wine bags, and it will be poured out, and the leather wine bags will be destroyed.
LUK 5:38 But new wine is put into new leather wine bags; and both are preserved together.
LUK 5:39 And no one having drunk old wine immediately wants new; for he says, The old is better.

LUK 6:43 For there is not a good tree producing rotten fruit; nor a rotten tree producing good fruit.
LUK 6:44 For each tree from out of its own fruit is known. For not from thorn-bushes do they collect figs, nor from a bush do they gather the vintage grape.

LUK 12:10 And every one who shall say a word against the son of man, it shall be forgiven him. But to the one blaspheming against the holy spirit, it will not be forgiven.
LUK 12:11 And whenever they should bring you unto the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, be not anxious how or what you should plead or what you should say!
LUK 12:12 For the holy spirit shall teach you in the same hour what is necessary to say.
LUK 12:13 And said a certain one to him from out of the multitude, Teacher, tell to my brother to portion with me the inheritance.
LUK 12:14 And he said to him, Man, who ordained me magistrate or apportioner for you?
LUK 12:15 And he said to them, See, and guard from the desire for wealth! for not to anyone is his life in the abundance of his possessions.
LUK 12:16 And he spoke a parable to them, saying, The place of a certain rich man bore well.
LUK 12:17 And he reasoned in himself, saying, What shall I do, for I do not have a place where to gather up my fruits?
LUK 12:18 And he said, This I will do. I will demolish my storehouses, and I will build greater; and I will gather there all my produce and my good things.
LUK 12:19 And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have many good things laid up for many years - rest, eat, drink, be glad!
LUK 12:20 But God said to him, Foolish one, this night your soul will be exacted from you; and what you prepare, to whom will it be?
LUK 12:21 Thus the one treasuring up for himself, and not being rich unto God.
LUK 12:22 And he said to his disciples, Because of this I say to you, Let not your life be anxious in what you should eat; nor the body in what you should put on!
LUK 12:23 Life is more than nourishment, and the body more than the garment.
LUK 12:24 Contemplate the crows! For they sow not, nor reap; (the ones which there is not a storeroom nor storehouse;) and God maintains them. How much more you differ from the birds?
LUK 12:25 But who of you being anxious is able to add unto his stature one cubit?
LUK 12:26 If then neither the least thing you are able, why concerning the rest are you anxious?
LUK 12:27 Contemplate the lilies how they grow! it labors not, nor spins. But I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed as one of these.
LUK 12:28 But if the grass in the field, being today, and tomorrow is being thrown into the oven, (the one God so clothes); how much more you, O ones of little belief?
LUK 12:29 And you, do not seek what you should eat, or what you should drink, and do not be raised up high!
LUK 12:30 For these things all the nations of the world seek anxiously; but your father knows that you need these.
LUK 12:31 Furthermore seek the kingdom of God! and all these shall be added to you.
LUK 12:32 Fear not small flock! For your father thinks well to give to you the kingdom.
LUK 12:33 Sell your possessions, and give charity! Make to yourselves bags not growing old! a treasure unceasing in the heavens, where thief shall not approach, nor moth ruin!
LUK 12:34 For where your treasure is, there also your heart will be.
LUK 12:35 Let your loins be girded, and the lamps burning!
LUK 12:36 And you be likened to men waiting for their Lord, as to when he disengages from the wedding feasts; that having come and having knocked, immediately they should open to him.
LUK 12:37 Blessed are those servants, whom the Lord coming shall find being vigilant. Amen I say to you, that he will gird himself, and lay them down, and going by will serve to them.
LUK 12:38 And if he should come in the second watch, or he should come in the third watch, and should find them thus, blessed are those servants.
LUK 12:39 But know this! That if the master of the house knew what hour the thief comes, he would have been vigilant, and would not have let his house be dug through.
LUK 12:40 And you then be prepared! For the hour you think not - the son of man comes.
LUK 12:41 And Peter said to him, O Lord, do you speak this parable to us, or also to all?
LUK 12:42 And the Lord said, Who then is the trustworthy and practical manager, whom the master places over his attendants, to give in time the measure of grain?
LUK 12:43 Blessed is that servant, whom his master having come finds him doing thus.
LUK 12:44 Truly I say to you, that over all his possessions he will place him.
LUK 12:45 But if that servant should say in his heart, My master passes time to come; and should begin to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be intoxicated;
LUK 12:46 the master of that servant shall come in a day in which he does not expect, and in an hour in which he knows not, and will cut him in pieces, and his portion will be put with the unbelieving.
LUK 12:47 And that servant, which having known the will of his master, and not having prepared, nor doing according to his will, shall be flayed much.
LUK 12:48 But the one not having known, but doing things worthy of strokes, shall be flayed little. And to every one whom much was given, much shall be sought from him. And to whom they placed near much, more extra shall they ask him.
LUK 12:49 I came to throw fire onto the earth; and what will I, if already it be lighted?
LUK 12:50 But an immersion I have to be immersed; and how constrained I am until of which it should be finished?
LUK 12:51 Do you think that I came to execute peace on the earth? No, I say to you, but only division.
LUK 12:52 For there will be from now on five in one house being divided - three against two, and two against three.
LUK 12:53 Father shall be divided against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against mother; mother-in-law against the daughter-in-law, and she, the daughter-in-law, against her mother-in-law.
LUK 12:54 And he said also to the multitudes, Whenever you should behold the cloud arising from the west, immediately you say, A heavy shower comes; and it happens thus.
LUK 12:55 And whenever a south wind is being blown, you say that, It will be a burning wind; and it happens.
LUK 12:56 Hypocrites, the surface of the heaven and of the earth you know to distinguish; but this time, how do you not distinguish?
LUK 12:57 And why even of yourselves do you not judge the just thing?
LUK 12:58 For as you go with your opponent unto the ruler in the way, make an effort to be dismissed from him; lest at any time he should drag you to the judge, and the judge should deliver you up to the exactor, and the exactor should throw you into prison.
LUK 12:59 I say to you, In no way shall you come forth from there, until of which even the last lepton you should repay.
LUK 13:1 And certain ones were at hand at the same time reporting to him concerning the Galileans, of whom the blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices.

LUK 13:3 No, I say to you. But if you should not repent, you shall all perish likewise.
LUK 13:4 Or those ten and eight upon whom fell the tower in Siloam, and it killed them. Do you think that these were debtors beyond all men dwelling in Jerusalem?
LUK 13:5 No, I say to you. But if you should not repent, you shall all perish in like manner.
LUK 13:6 And he spoke this parable. A certain one had a fig-tree in his vineyard being planted; and he came seeking fruit on it, and found not.
LUK 13:7 And he said to the vine dresser, Behold, three years I come seeking fruit on this fig-tree, and I found not. Cut it down! Why even render the land useless?
LUK 13:8 But answering, he says to him, O master, leave it even this year, until whenever I shall dig around it, and throw manure.
LUK 13:9 And if then it should produce fruit, good. But if not you can cut it down for the about to be.

LUK 13:13 And he placed hands upon her. And immediately she was erected, and glorified God.
LUK 13:14 But responding the chief of the synagogue being indignant, that Jesus cured on the sabbath, said to the multitude, Six days there are in which it behooves to work. During these then in coming you be cured, and not in the day of the sabbath!
LUK 13:15 And the Lord responded then to him, and said, Hypocrite, each of you in the sabbath, does he not untie his ox or donkey from the stable, and having taking it away waters it?
LUK 13:16 And this one, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound, behold, ten and eight years, must not she be untied from this bond on the day of the sabbath?
LUK 13:17 And of his saying these things, all the ones being adverse to him were put to shame. And all the multitude rejoiced over all the noble things being done by him.
LUK 13:18 And he said, To what is the kingdom of God likened? and to what shall I liken it?
LUK 13:19 It is likened to a kernel of mustard, which a man having taken threw into his own garden; and it grew, and became into a great tree; and the birds of the heaven encamped in the branches of it.
LUK 13:20 And again he said, To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
LUK 13:21 It is likened to leaven, which having taken a woman hid in three seahs of flour, until of which all was leavened.
LUK 13:22 And he traveled by cities and towns, teaching, and making a coursing unto Jerusalem.
LUK 13:23 And said a certain one to him, O Lord, are there few being delivered? And he said to them,
LUK 13:24 Struggle to enter through the narrow gate! for many, I say to you, will seek to enter, and will not be able.
LUK 13:25 From of which ever time the master of the house should arise, and should lock the door, and you should begin outside to stand, and to knock on the door, saying, O lord, O lord, open to us! And answering, he shall say to you, I do not know you - from what place you are.
LUK 13:26 Then you will begin to say, We ate in your presence, and we drank, and in our squares you taught.
LUK 13:27 And he shall say, I say to you, I do not know you, from what place you are; depart from me all workers of iniquity!
LUK 13:28 There there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth, whenever you should see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you being cast forth outside.
LUK 13:29 And they shall come from east and west, and north and south, and shall lie down in the kingdom of God.
LUK 13:30 And behold, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.

LUK 13:35 Behold, your house is left to you desolate. And I say to you that, In no way shall you behold me, until whenever it should come when you should say, Being blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord.
LUK 14:1 And it came to pass in his coming into a certain house of the rulers of the Pharisees on a sabbath to eat bread, that they were closely watching him.

LUK 14:4 But they were still. And taking hold, he healed him, and dismissed him.

LUK 14:6 And they were not able to answer to him as to these things.
LUK 14:7 And he spoke to the ones being invited a parable, giving heed how they chose the first places; saying to them,
LUK 14:8 Whenever you should be invited by anyone to wedding feasts, you should not lie down to eat in the first place; lest at any time a more important one than you might be invited by him;
LUK 14:9 and having come, the one having invited you and him shall say to you, Give place to this one! And then you begin with shame to take the last place.
LUK 14:10 But whenever you should be invited, having gone, recline in the last place; that whenever the one having invited you should come, he should say to you, O friend, ascend higher! Then there will be glory to you in the presence of the ones reclining together with you.
LUK 14:11 For every one exalting himself shall be humbled; and the one humbling himself shall be exalted.

LUK 14:13 But whenever you make a banquet, call the poor, maimed, lame, blind!
LUK 14:14 And blessed you will be; for they do not have anything to recompense to you. For it shall be recompensed to you in the resurrection of the just ones.
LUK 14:15 And having heard, a certain one of the ones reclining together with these, said to him, Blessed is the one who shall eat dinner in the kingdom of God.
LUK 14:16 And he said to him, A certain man made a great supper, and invited many.

LUK 14:19 And another said, I bought five teams of oxen, and I go to try them. I ask you, Have me pardoned!
LUK 14:20 And another said, I married a wife, and on account of this I am not able to come.
LUK 14:21 And that servant having come, reported to his master these things. Then being provoked to anger the master of the house said to his servant, Go forth quickly into the squares and streets of the city, and the poor and maimed and lame and blind bring here!
LUK 14:22 And the servant said, O master, it has taken place as you ordered, and still there is place.
LUK 14:23 And the master said to the servant, Go forth into the ways and fences, and compel them to enter, that my house should be filled!
LUK 14:24 For I say to you that, Not one of those men having been invited shall taste of my supper.

LUK 14:27 And whosoever does not bear his cross, and come after me, is not able to be my disciple.
LUK 14:28 For who of you, wanting to build a tower, not having first sat down to tally the expense, sees if he has the things for completion?
LUK 14:29 That lest at any time having set its foundation, and not being able to complete it, all the ones viewing should begin to mock him,
LUK 14:30 saying that, This man began to build, and was not able to complete.
LUK 14:31 Or what king, going to engage with another king in war, does not sit first to consult if he is able with ten thousand to meet the one with twenty thousand coming against him?
LUK 14:32 But if not, still of his being at a distance, having sent an embassy, he asks the terms for peace.
LUK 14:33 So then, every one of you who does not send away to all the things he himself possesses, is not able to be my disciple.

LUK 14:35 Neither for earth, nor for manure is it fit - they throw it outside. The one having ears to hear let him hear!

LUK 18:4 And he did not want to for a time; but afterwards he said to himself, If even God I do not fear, and man I do not respect;
LUK 18:5 yet because this widow makes trouble to me, I shall avenge her, that it should not come to pass bruising me in the end.
LUK 18:6 And the Lord said, Hear what the unrighteous judge says.
LUK 18:7 But God, shall he in no way execute vengeance for his chosen yelling to him day and night, and is lenient unto them?
LUK 18:8 I say to you that he shall execute his vengeance quickly. Furthermore, the son of man having come then, shall he find belief upon the earth?
LUK 18:9 And he spoke also to some, (the ones relying upon themselves that they are just ones, and treating with contempt the rest,) this parable.
LUK 18:10 Two men ascended unto the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a tax collector.
LUK 18:11 The Pharisee standing prayed these things to himself, God, I give thanks to you, that I am not as the rest of the men, predacious, unjust, adulterers, or even as this tax collector.
LUK 18:12 I fast twice a sabbath, I tithe all as much as I acquire.
LUK 18:13 And the tax collector far off standing, wanted not even to lift up his eyes unto the heaven, but beat onto his breast, saying, God deal kindly with me the sinner.
LUK 18:14 I say to you, this one went down justified unto his house rather than that one. For every one exalting himself shall be humbled; and the one humbling himself shall be exalted.
LUK 18:15 And they brought to him also the babes, that he should touch them. But seeing, the disciples reproached them.
LUK 18:16 But Jesus, having called on them, said, Allow the children to come to me, and do not restrain them! for of such is the kingdom of God.
LUK 18:17 Amen I say to you, Who ever should not receive the kingdom of God as a child in no way shall enter into it.
LUK 18:18 And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good teacher, what having done shall I do to inherit eternal life?
LUK 18:19 And Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? No one is good except one - God.
LUK 18:20 The commandments you know, Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not witness falsely, esteem your father and your mother!
LUK 18:21 And he said, These all I kept from my youth.
LUK 18:22 And having heard these things, Jesus said to him, Still one thing to you is missing. All, as much as you have, sell and distribute to the poor! and you shall have treasure in heaven. And come, follow me!
LUK 18:23 But hearing these things, he became dejected; for he was rich, exceedingly.
LUK 18:24 And Jesus beholding him being dejected, said, How with difficulty the ones having things shall enter into the kingdom of God.
LUK 18:25 For it is easier for a camel to enter through the hole from an awl, than a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
LUK 18:26 And the ones hearing said, And who is able to be delivered?
LUK 18:27 And he said, The impossible things by men are possible with God.
LUK 18:28 And Peter said, Behold, we left all, and we followed you.
LUK 18:29 And he said to them, Amen I say to you, That there is no one who left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children, because of the kingdom of God,
LUK 18:30 who in no way should recover much more in this time, and in the coming eon life eternal.
LUK 18:31 And having taken to himself the twelve, he said to them, Behold, we ascend unto Jerusalem, and all the things being written by the prophets about the son of man shall be finished.
LUK 18:32 For he shall be delivered to the nations, and will be mocked, and will be insulted, and will be spit upon.
LUK 18:33 And having been whipped, they shall kill him. And the third day he will rise up.
LUK 18:34 And they perceived nothing of these things. For this thing was being hidden from them, and they did not know the things being said.
LUK 18:35 And it came to pass in his approaching unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way begging.
LUK 18:36 And hearing the multitude traveling about, he inquired about what this may be.
LUK 18:37 And they reported to him that Jesus the Nazarene is going by.
LUK 18:38 And he yelled out, saying, Jesus, O son of David, show mercy on me!
LUK 18:39 And the ones going before reproached him, that he should keep silent. But he more rather cried out, O son of David, show mercy on me!
LUK 18:40 And having stopped, Jesus urged for him to be brought to him. And at his having approached, he asked him,
LUK 18:41 saying, What do you want I should do? And he said, O Lord, that I should gain sight.
LUK 18:42 And Jesus said to him, Gain sight! The belief of yours has delivered you.
LUK 18:43 And immediately he gained sight, and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, having beheld, gave praise to God.
LUK 19:1 And having entered he went through Jericho.
LUK 19:2 And behold, there was a man by name being called Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector, and this one was rich.
LUK 19:3 And he was seeking to see who Jesus is. And he was not able because of the multitude, for his stature was small.
LUK 19:4 And having run in front, he ascended up a wild fig-tree, that he should behold him; for by that place he was about to go.
LUK 19:5 And as he came unto the place, having looked up, Jesus beheld him, and said to him, Zacchaeus, making haste, come down! For today it is necessary for me to remain in your house.
LUK 19:6 And making haste, he came down, and welcomed him rejoicing.
LUK 19:7 And having seen, all complained, saying that, With a sinful man he enters to rest up.
LUK 19:8 But standing, Zacchaeus said to the Lord, Behold, the half of my possessions, O Lord, I give to the poor; and if to any what I extorted, I will give back quadruple.
LUK 19:9 And Jesus said to him that, Today deliverance took place in this house in so far as he also is a son of Abraham.
LUK 19:10 For the son of man came to seek and to deliver the one being lost.
LUK 19:11 And in their hearing these things, adding he spoke a parable, on account of his being near Jerusalem, and their thinking that immediately the kingdom of God was about to appear.
LUK 19:12 He said then, A certain well-born man went unto a place afar to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
LUK 19:13 And having called ten of his servants, he gave to them ten minas, and said to them, Be engaged in matters until I return.
LUK 19:14 And his citizens detested him, and sent an embassy after him, saying, We do not want this one to reign over us.
LUK 19:15 And it came to pass in his returning back, having received the kingdom, that he spoke for these servants to be called to him, to whom he gave the money, that he should know what business each did.
LUK 19:16 And came the first saying, O master, your minas gained an additional ten minas.
LUK 19:17 And he said to him, Good, O good servant. For in the least you were trustworthy, let there be for you having authority above ten cities!
LUK 19:18 And the second came, saying, O master, Your mina made five minas.
LUK 19:19 And he said also to this one, And you become above five cities.
LUK 19:20 And another came, saying, O master, behold, your mina, which I have is being reserved in a scarf.
LUK 19:21 For I feared you, for you are a stern man - you take up what you rendered not, and you harvest what you sowed not.
LUK 19:22 And he says to him, From out of your mouth I will judge you, O wicked servant. You knew that I am a stern man, taking up what I rendered not, and harvesting what I sowed not.
LUK 19:23 And therefore why did you not give my money unto the money lenders table, and I having come would have exacted it with interest?
LUK 19:24 And to the ones standing by, he said, Take from him the mina, and give it to the one having ten minas!
LUK 19:25 And they said to him, O master, he has ten minas.
LUK 19:26 For I say to you that, To every one having, it shall be given; but of the one not having, even what he has shall be taken from him.
LUK 19:27 Furthermore, my enemies, those of the ones not wanting me to reign over them, lead them here and butcher them in front of me!
LUK 19:28 And having said these things, he went ahead, ascending unto Jerusalem.
LUK 19:29 And it came to pass as he approached unto Bethphage and Bethany, to the mountain being called Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
LUK 19:30 having said, Go unto the opposite town; in which entering you will find a foal being tied, upon which no one of men at any time sat. Having untied him, lead him!
LUK 19:31 And if anyone asks you, On account of why do you untie? Thus shall you say to him that, His master has need.
LUK 19:32 And going forth, the ones having been sent found it as he said to them.
LUK 19:33 And of their untying the foal, his masters said to them, Why do you untie the foal?
LUK 19:34 And they said, His master has need.
LUK 19:35 And they led him to Jesus. And having cast their own garments upon the foal, they conducted Jesus.
LUK 19:36 And of his going, they spread their garments in the way.
LUK 19:37 And of his approaching already to the descent of the ount of Olives, all the multitude of the disciples began rejoicing to praise God with a great voice for all which they beheld of works of power;
LUK 19:38 saying, Blessed be the coming king in the name of the Lord. Reace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
LUK 19:39 And some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, Teacher, reproach your disciples!
LUK 19:40 And responding he said to them, I say to you that, If these should keep silent, the stones will have been crying out.
LUK 19:41 And as he approached beholding the city, he wept over it,
LUK 19:42 saying that, If you knew, even you, also indeed in this your day, the things for your peace - but now it was hidden from your eyes.
LUK 19:43 For days shall come upon you, that your enemies shall put a siege mound around you, and shall surround you, and shall constrain you from all sides,
LUK 19:44 and shall dash you and your children with you; and shall not leave among you a stone upon a stone; because you knew not the time of your visitation.
LUK 19:45 And entering into the temple, he began to cast out the ones selling, and buying in it;
LUK 19:46 saying to them, It has been written, My house is a house of prayer. But you made it a cave of robbers.
LUK 19:47 And he was teaching by day in the temple. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy him, and the foremost of the people.
LUK 19:48 And they did not find what they should do. For the people all depended on hearing him.
LUK 20:1 And it came to pass, in one of those days, of his teaching the people in the temple, and announcing good news, the chief priests and the scribes stood by with the elders,
LUK 20:2 and spoke to him, saying, Tell us! By what kind of authority do you do these things? or who is the one having given to you this authority?
LUK 20:3 And answering he said to them, And I will ask you one word, and you tell to me!
LUK 20:4 The immersion of John, was it from heaven, or from men?
LUK 20:5 And they reckoned to themselves, saying that, If we should say, From heaven; he shall say, Therefore why then did you not believe in him?
LUK 20:6 And if we should say, From men; all the people will completely stone us; for they are persuaded John to be a prophet.
LUK 20:7 And they answered, We do not know from where.
LUK 20:8 And Jesus said to them, Nor do I say to you by what authority I do these things.
LUK 20:9 And he began to speak to the people this parable, A certain man planted a vineyard, and handed it over to growers, and traveled abroad a fit amount of time.
LUK 20:10 And in the season he sent to the growers a servant, that from the fruit of the vineyard they might give to him. But the growers having flayed him, sent him away empty.
LUK 20:11 And he proceeded to send forth another servant. But they having flayed that one also, and dishonoring him, sent him away empty.
LUK 20:12 And he proceeded to send forth a third. But they also having wounded this one, cast him out.
LUK 20:13 And the master of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send forth my son, the beloved - perhaps beholding this one they will show respect.
LUK 20:14 But beholding him, the growers reasoned to themselves, saying, This is the heir. Come, we should kill him, that the inheritance becomes ours.
LUK 20:15 And having cast him outside the vineyard, they killed him. What then shall the master of the vineyard do to them?
LUK 20:16 He shall come and shall destroy those growers, and will give the vineyard to others. And having heard, they said, May it not be.
LUK 20:17 And looking to them, he said, What then is this having been written, The stone which the ones building rejected, this is become for head of the corner?
LUK 20:18 Every one falling upon that stone, shall be fractured in pieces; but whom ever it should fall upon, it will winnow him.
LUK 20:19 And the chief priests and the scribes sought to put hands upon him in that same hour; and they feared. For they knew that he spoke this parable against them.
LUK 20:20 And closely watching, they sent ones lying in wait, pretending themselves to be just ones, that they should take hold of his word, for the delivering him up to the sovereignty and to the authority of the governor.
LUK 20:21 And they questioned him, saying, Teacher, we know that rightly you speak and teach, and do not take face, but in truth you teach the way of God.
LUK 20:22 Is it allowed for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?
LUK 20:23 But contemplating their cunning, he said to them, Why do you test me?
LUK 20:24 Display to me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have? And answering they said, Caesar.
LUK 20:25 And he said to them, Give back therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God.
LUK 20:26 And they were not able to take hold of his saying before the people. And marveling over his answer, they were quiet.
LUK 20:27 But coming forward, a certain one of the Sadducees, the ones disputing a resurrection, claiming it not to be; asked him,
LUK 20:28 saying, Teacher, Moses wrote to us, If anyone's brother should die having a wife, and he should die childless, that his brother should take the wife, and should raise up seed to his brother.
LUK 20:29 There were then seven brothers; and the first having taken a wife died childless.
LUK 20:30 And the second took the wife, and he died childless.
LUK 20:31 And the third took her, and likewise also the seven. And they did not leave children, and they died.
LUK 20:32 And afterwards all died and the woman.
LUK 20:33 In then the resurrection, which of them does she become wife? for the seven had her as wife.
LUK 20:34 And answering Jesus said to them, The sons of this age marry, and give in marriage.
LUK 20:35 But the ones being deemed worthy to attain of that eon, and of the resurrection of the ones from the dead, neither marry nor give in marriage.
LUK 20:36 For neither are they able to die any longer. For they are like angels, and they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
LUK 20:37 But that the dead be raised, even Moses indicated at the bush, as he says, The Lord God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
LUK 20:38 But God is not of the dead, but the living; for all live to him.
LUK 20:39 And answering some of the scribes said, Teacher, well you spoke.
LUK 20:40 And no longer they dared to ask him anything.
LUK 20:41 And he said to them, How do they say the Christ to be the son of David?
LUK 20:42 And he, David says in the book of Psalms, The Lord - the Greek proper name of Diety said. to my Lord, Sit down at my right,
LUK 20:43 until whenever I put your enemies as a footstool for your feet.
LUK 20:44 David then calls him Lord, so how is he his son?
LUK 20:45 And all the people hearing, he said to his disciples,
LUK 20:46 Take heed of the scribes wanting to walk in robes, and being fond of greetings in the markets, and first seats in the synagogues, and first place in the suppers;
LUK 20:47 who devour the houses of the widows, and for an excuse they pray long. These shall receive extra judgment.
LUK 21:1 And looking up, he beheld the rich throwing their gifts into the treasury.
LUK 21:2 And he beheld a certain destitute widow throwing there two leptas.
LUK 21:3 And he said, Truly I say to you that this poor widow threw in more than all.
LUK 21:4 For all these from out of their abundance threw in the gifts for God. But she from out of her deficiency threw all the livelihood which she had.
LUK 21:5 And as some were speaking concerning the temple, that with goodly stones and consecrated offerings it was adorned, he said,
LUK 21:6 These things which you view - there shall come days in which a stone shall not be left upon a stone, which shall not be broken up.
LUK 21:7 And they asked him, saying, Teacher, when then will these things be? and what is the sign whenever these things are about to take place?
LUK 21:8 And he said, Take heed that you should not be misled! For many shall come in my name, saying that, I am he; and the time approaches. You should not then go after them.
LUK 21:9 And whenever you should hear of wars and commotions, you should not be terrified; for it is necessary these things take place first. But not immediately is the end.
LUK 21:10 Then he said to them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
LUK 21:11 Also great earthquakes in places, and there shall be famines and pestilences; also fearful things, and there will be great signs from heaven.
LUK 21:12 But before these things all together, they shall put their hands upon you, and shall persecute you, delivering you up unto synagogues, and prisons, leading you unto kings and governors because of my name.
LUK 21:13 But it shall result to you for a testimony.
LUK 21:14 Then you put it into your hearts, not to meditate beforehand to make a defense!
LUK 21:15 For I shall give to you a mouth and wisdom, in which all the ones being adverse to you will not be able to contradict nor oppose.
LUK 21:16 But you will be delivered up even by parents, and brothers, and relatives, and friends; and they shall put to death some of you.
LUK 21:17 And you will be detested by all on account of my name.
LUK 21:18 But a hair from your head in no way shall perish.
LUK 21:19 By your endurance acquire your life!
LUK 21:20 And whenever you should behold Jerusalem being encircled by encamped armies, then know that her desolation approaches.
LUK 21:21 Then the ones in Judea let flee into the mountains! And the ones in the midst of her let withdraw! And let the ones in the regions not enter into her!
LUK 21:22 For these are days of avenging to fulfill all the things having been written.
LUK 21:23 But woe to the ones having one in the womb, and to the ones nursing in those days. For there will be great distress upon the land, and wrath among this people.
LUK 21:24 And they shall fall by the mouth of the sword, and shall be taken captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be for treading by nations until the times of the nations shall be fulfilled.
LUK 21:25 And there shall be signs in the sun, and moon, and stars; and upon the earth conflict of nations, in perplexity of resounding sea and tossing about;
LUK 21:26 men fainting from fear, and expectation of the things coming to the inhabitable world. For the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
LUK 21:27 And then they shall see the son of man coming in a cloud with power and much glory.
LUK 21:28 But at the beginning of these things coming to pass, let your heads be raised and lifted up; for your release by ransom approaches!
LUK 21:29 And he spoke a parable to them, Look at the fig-tree, and all the trees!
LUK 21:30 Whenever they should burgeon already, seeing it yourselves, you know that already the summer is near!
LUK 21:31 Thus also you, whenever you should see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near!
LUK 21:32 Amen I say to you that, In no way shall this generation pass away, until whenever all shall take place.
LUK 21:33 The heaven and the earth shall pass away; but my words in no way shall pass away.
LUK 21:34 But take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts should be weighed down in dizziness, and intoxication, and anxieties of life, and that day suddenly should stand upon you!
LUK 21:35 For as a snare it shall come upon all the ones being settled upon the face of all the earth.
LUK 21:36 Be awake then at every season! beseeching, that you should be deemed worthy to flee from all the things being about to take place, and to stand before the son of man.

LUK 23:4 And Pilate said to the chief priests and the multitudes, Not one fault do I find in this man.
LUK 23:5 And they grew more urgent and violent, saying that, He incites the people, teaching throughout entire Judea, beginning from Galilee unto here.
LUK 23:6 And Pilate having heard Galilee, asked if the man is a Galilean.
LUK 23:7 And having realized that he is under the authority of Herod, he sent him to Herod, he being also in Jerusalem in these days.
LUK 23:8 And Herod beholding Jesus, rejoiced exceedingly. For he was wanting for a fit time to behold him, because of the hearing many things concerning him; and he hoped to behold any sign by him taking place.
LUK 23:9 And he asked him with a fit amount of words; but he answered to him nothing.
LUK 23:10 And standing by were the chief priests and the scribes intensely charging him.
LUK 23:11 And Herod with his military having treated him with contempt, and having mocked him, having put around him bright attire, sent him back to Pilate.
LUK 23:12 And they became friends, both Pilate and Herod, in this day with one another. For beforehand they were being at enmity between themselves.
LUK 23:13 And Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
LUK 23:14 said to them, You brought to me this man as perverting the people. And behold, I, before you having questioned him, find nothing in this man for a fault of which to lay charge against him.
LUK 23:15 And not even Herod. For I sent you to him; and behold, nothing worthy of death is being acted by him.
LUK 23:16 Correcting him then, I will release him.
LUK 23:17 (And by necessity he had to release to them each holiday one person.)
LUK 23:18 But they shouted aloud all at once, saying, Take this one, but release to us Barabbas.
LUK 23:19 (Who was on account of a certain insurrection having taken place in the city, and for murder, thrown into prison.)
LUK 23:20 Then again, Pilate called out to them, wanting to release Jesus.
LUK 23:21 But they were sounding out, saying, Crucify! Crucify him!
LUK 23:22 And the third time he said to them, For what evil did this one do? No fault for death do I find in him. Correcting him then, I will release him.
LUK 23:23 And they pressed with great voices, asking for him to be crucified. And their voices prevailed and of the chief priests.
LUK 23:24 And Pilate adjudged their request to take place.
LUK 23:25 And he released to them the one through insurrection and murder being thrown into the prison, whom they asked for; but Jesus he delivered up to their will.
LUK 23:26 And as they led him away, having taken hold of Simon, a certain Cyrenian, coming from the field, they placed upon him the cross, to bear it behind Jesus.
LUK 23:27 And were following him a great multitude of the people, and women, which also were beating their chest and wailing over him.
LUK 23:28 And having turned to them, Jesus said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me! Furthermore, weep for yourselves, and for your children!
LUK 23:29 For behold, days come in which they shall say, Blessed are the sterile, and bellies which bore not, and breasts which nursed not.
LUK 23:30 Then they shall begin to say to the mountains, Fall upon us! And to the hills, Cover us!
LUK 23:31 For if in the wet wood these things they do, what should happen in the dry?
LUK 23:32 And they led also other two evildoers with him to be done away with.
LUK 23:33 And when they went forth unto the place being called Skull, there they crucified him, and the evildoers, one on the right, and one on the left.
LUK 23:34 And Jesus said, O Father, forgive them! for they do not know what they do. And dividing his garments they cast a lot.
LUK 23:35 And the people stood viewing. And deriding also were the rulers with them, saying, Others he delivered; let him deliver himself, if this is the Christ, the one chosen of God!
LUK 23:36 And the soldiers also mocked at him, coming forward, and bringing vinegar to him,
LUK 23:37 and saying, If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!
LUK 23:38 And there was also an inscription being depicted above him in letters in Greek, and Roman, and Hebrew - This is the king of the Jews.
LUK 23:39 And one of the hanging evildoers blasphemed him, saying, If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!
LUK 23:40 And responding the other reproached him, saying, Not even do you fear God, for you are under the same judgment?
LUK 23:41 And we indeed justly; for worthy of what we acted, we receive; but this one did not act out of place.
LUK 23:42 And he said to Jesus, Remember me, O Lord, whenever you should come in to your kingdom.
LUK 23:43 And Jesus said to him, Amen I say to you, Today with me you will be in paradise.
LUK 23:44 And it was about the sixth hour, and darkness came upon the entire land until the ninth hour.
LUK 23:45 And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was split in the middle.
LUK 23:46 And calling out with a great voice, Jesus said, Father, into your hands I place my spirit. And these things having said, he expired.
LUK 23:47 And the centurion beholding the thing taking place, glorified God, saying, Really, this man was just.
LUK 23:48 And all the multitudes coming together upon this sight, viewing the things having taken place, were beating themselves on the breast returning.
LUK 23:49 And all the ones who knew him stood afar off, even the women following him from Galilee, seeing these things.
LUK 23:50 And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a counselor, being a good man, and just,
LUK 23:51 (this one was not assenting together with the counsel and their action,) from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who even was waiting also himself the kingdom of God.
LUK 23:52 This one came forward to Pilate, to ask the body of Jesus.
LUK 23:53 And having lowered it, he swathed it in fine linen, and put it in a tomb of dressed stone, of which not was not yet any one being laid.
LUK 23:54 And it was preparation day, and sabbath evening coming on.
LUK 23:55 But following closely after also were women, (the ones who were gathered together to him from out of Galilee,) for seeing the sepulchre, and how his body was placed.
LUK 23:56 And having returned, they prepared aromatics and perfumed liquids; and on the sabbath they were tranquil according to the commandment.
LUK 24:1 And day one of the sabbaths, at deep dawn, they came unto the tomb, bringing aromatics which they prepared, and some others with them.
LUK 24:2 And they found the stone having been rolled away from the sepulcher.
LUK 24:3 And having entered, they found not the body of the Lord Jesus.
LUK 24:4 And it came to pass, in their being perplexed on account of this, that behold, two men stood by them in attire flashing lightning.
LUK 24:5 And of their being thrown into fear, and leaning the face unto the ground, they said to them, Why do you seek the living with the dead?
LUK 24:6 He is not here, but arisen. Remember as he spoke to you still being in Galilee!
LUK 24:7 Saying that, It is necessary the son of man to be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and to be crucified, and on the third day to rise up.
LUK 24:8 And they remembered his sayings.
LUK 24:9 And they returned from the sepulchre, to report all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.
LUK 24:10 And they were the Magdalene - Mary, and Joanna, and Mary of James, and the rest with them who spoke to the apostles these things.
LUK 24:11 And their words appeared before them as nonsense, and they disbelieved them.
LUK 24:12 But Peter, having risen up, ran unto the sepulchre; and having leaned over, he sees the linen bands being situated alone; and he went forth to his own place wondering at the thing having taken place.
LUK 24:13 And behold, two of them were going on the same day unto a town at a distance of sixty stadiums from Jerusalem - the name is Emmaus.
LUK 24:14 And they were consorting with one another concerning all these things coming to pass.
LUK 24:15 And it happened during their consorting and debating, that Jesus himself having approached, went with them.
LUK 24:16 And their eyes were kept to not recognize him.
LUK 24:17 And he said to them, What words are these which you argue with one another while walking, and are looking downcast?
LUK 24:18 And answering, the one whose name was Cleopas, said to him, You alone sojourn in Jerusalem, and know not the things taking place in it in these days?
LUK 24:19 And he said to them, What kind? And they said to him, The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet, mighty in work and word before God and all the people.
LUK 24:20 And how that the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up unto the judgment of death, and they crucified him.
LUK 24:21 But we were hoping that he is the one about to ransom Israel. But indeed with all these things, today leads in this third day, from which time these things took place.
LUK 24:22 But also certain women from us amazed us, happening early unto the sepulchre;
LUK 24:23 and not having found his body, they came saying also to have seen an apparition of angels, who say him to be living.
