JOH 14:22 Judas says to him (not Iscariot,) O Lord, what has taken place that to us you are about to reveal yourself, and not to the world?
JOH 14:23 Jesus answered and said to him, If anyone loves me, he will give heed to my word; and my father will love him, and to him we will come, and will make an abode with him.
JOH 14:24 The one not loving me does not give heed to my words. And the word which you hear is not mine, but the father having sent me.
JOH 14:25 These things I have spoken to you, abiding with you.
JOH 14:26 But the comforter, the holy spirit, whom the father will send in my name, that one will teach you all things, and will remind you all things which I said to you.
JOH 14:27 Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you - not as the world gives, give I to you. Let not your heart be disturbed, nor be timid!
JOH 14:28 You heard that I said to you, I go away, and I come to you. If you loved me, you would have rejoiced, that I said, I go to the father; for my father is greater than me.
JOH 14:29 And now I have told it to you before it takes place, that whenever it happens, you should believe.
JOH 14:30 No longer will I speak many things with you. For the one of the world comes - the ruler; and with me he has not one thing.
JOH 14:31 But that the world should know that I love the father; and as the father gave charge to me, so I do. Arise, we should lead on from here.
JOH 15:1 I am the true grapevine, and my father is the grower.
JOH 15:2 Every vine branch in me not bearing fruit, he takes it. And every branch bearing fruit, he cleanses it, that it should bear more fruit.
JOH 15:3 Already you are clean through the word which I have spoken to you.
JOH 15:4 Abide in me, and I in you! As the vine branch is not able to bear fruit of itself, unless it should abide in the grapevine; so not even you, unless you should abide in me.
JOH 15:5 I am the grapevine, you are the vine branches. The one abiding in me, and I in him, this one bears much fruit; for apart from me you are not able to do anything.
JOH 15:6 Unless one should abide in me, he is thrown outside as the vine branch, and withers; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
JOH 15:7 If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, whatever you should want, ask, and it shall be to you!
JOH 15:8 In this my father is glorified, that you should bear much fruit; and you should become disciples to me.
JOH 15:9 As the father loved me, I also loved you. Abide in the love - in the one mine!
JOH 15:10 If you should keep my commandments, you shall abide in my love; as I have kept the commandments of my father, and I abide in the love of his.
JOH 15:11 These things I have spoken to you, that my joy should abide in you, and your joy should be full.
JOH 15:12 This is my commandment, That you love one another, as I loved you!
JOH 15:13 Greater love than this no one has, that one should place his life for his friends.
JOH 15:14 You are my friends, if you should do as much as I give charge to you.
JOH 15:15 No longer do I call you servants; for the servant knows not what his master does. But I have called you friends; for all things which I heard from my father I made known to you.
JOH 15:16 You chose me not, but I chose you, and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and your fruit should abide; that whatever you should ask the father in my name, he should give to you.
JOH 15:17 These things I give charge to you, that you should love one another.
JOH 15:18 If the world detests you, know that it detested me first before you!
JOH 15:19 If you were of the world, the world would be fond of its own. But because you are not of the world, but I chose you from out of the world - on account of this the world detests you.
JOH 15:20 Remember the word which I said to you! A servant is not greater than his master. If me they persecuted, also you they shall persecute. If they give heed to my word, then they will give heed to yours.
JOH 15:21 But all these things they shall do to you because of my name, for they know not the one having sent me.
JOH 15:22 Unless I came and spoke to them, they had not had sin; but now they have not an excuse concerning their sin.
JOH 15:23 The one detesting me, even detests my father.
JOH 15:24 If I did not the works among them which no other has done, they had not had sin. But now even they have seen and have detested even me and my father.
JOH 15:25 But that the word should be fulfilled, the one having been written in their law that, They detested me without a charge.
JOH 15:26 But whenever the comforter should come, whom I send to you from the father, the spirit of the truth, who from the father goes forth, that one will witness concerning me;
JOH 15:27 and you also witness, for you were with me from the beginning.
JOH 16:1 These things I have spoken to you, that you should not be caused to stumble.
JOH 16:2 Out of the synagogue they shall put you. And, there comes an hour, that every one killing you thinks he offers service to God.
JOH 16:3 And these things they shall do, for they know not the father, nor me.
JOH 16:4 But these things I have spoken to you, that whenever the hour should come, you should remember them, that I spoke to you. But these things I said not to you at the beginning, for I was with you.
JOH 16:5 But now I go away to the one having sent me; and not one of you asks me, Where do you go?
JOH 16:6 But because these things I have spoken to you, distress has filled your heart.
JOH 16:7 But I speak to you the truth; it is advantageous to you that I go forth. For if I should not go forth, the comforter shall not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
JOH 16:8 And having come, that one will reprove the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment.
JOH 16:9 Concerning sin then, that they believe not in me.
JOH 16:10 And concerning righteousness, that to my father I go away, and no longer you view me.
JOH 16:11 And concerning judgment, for the ruler of this world has been judged.
JOH 16:12 Still many things I have to say to you, but you are not able to bear them just now.
JOH 16:13 But whenever that one should come, the spirit of the truth, he will guide you into all the truth. For he shall not speak from himself; but as much as whatever he should hear, he shall speak; and the things coming he shall announce to you.
JOH 16:14 That one will glorify me. For of mine he shall take, and shall announce to you.
JOH 16:15 All as much as the father has is mine. On account of this I said that, Of mine he takes, and shall announce to you.
JOH 16:16 A little while, and you shall not view me. And again a little while and you shall see me, for I go away to the father.
JOH 16:17 Said then some of his disciples to one another, What is this which he says to us, A little while, and you will not view me. And again a little while, and you shall see me; and, For I go away to the father?
JOH 16:18 They said then, What is this which he says, the, Little while? We do not know what he speaks.
JOH 16:19 Jesus knew then that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, Concerning this do you seek with one another, that I said, A little while, and you shall not view me. And again a little while, and you shall see me?
JOH 16:20 Amen, amen, I say to you that, You will weep and wail, but the world will rejoice. And you will be distressed, but your distress will become for joy.
JOH 16:21 The woman whenever she should give birth has distress, for her hour came. But whenever she should bear the child, no longer does she remember the affliction, on account of the joy that a man was born into the world.
JOH 16:22 And you then indeed now have distress. But again I shall see you, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no one shall take from you.
JOH 16:23 And in that day you shall not ask me any thing. Amen, amen, I say to you that, Whatever as much as you should ask the father in my name, he will give to you.
JOH 16:24 Until now you asked not any thing in my name. Ask and you shall receive, that your joy should be filled!
JOH 16:25 I have spoken these things in proverbs to you. But comes the hour when no longer in proverbs shall I speak to you, but I will announce to you concerning the father in an open manner.
JOH 16:26 In that day you shall ask in my name. And I say not to you, that I will ask the father concerning you.
JOH 16:27 For the father himself is fond of you, for you are fond of me, and have believed that I have come forth from God;
JOH 16:28 I came forth from the father, and I have come into the world. Again I leave the world, and I go to the father.
JOH 16:29 His disciples say to him, See, now in an open manner you speak, and not one proverb do you say!
JOH 16:30 Now we know that you know all things, and you have not a need that anyone should ask you. In this we believe that you came forth from God.
JOH 16:31 Jesus responded to them, Now you believe?
JOH 16:32 Behold, there comes an hour, and now has come, that you will be dispersed each unto his own place, and you shall leave me alone. And I am not alone, for the father is with me.
JOH 16:33 These things I have spoken to you, that in me you should have peace. In the world you shall have tribulation. But be of courage! I have overcome the world.
JOH 17:1 These things Jesus spoke, and lifted up his eyes unto the heaven, and said, O father, the hour has come; glorify your son, that also your son should glorify you!
JOH 17:2 As you gave to him authority over all flesh, that all whom you have given to him, he gives to them life eternal.
JOH 17:3 And this is the eternal life, that they should know you the only True God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent.
JOH 17:4 I glorified you upon the earth. I perfected the work which you have given to me that I should do.
JOH 17:5 And now you glorify me, O father, with the glory of yourself which I had with you before the world being in existence!
JOH 17:6 I made manifest your name to the men whom you have given to me from out of the world. They were yours, and you have given them to me; and your word they have given heed.
JOH 17:7 Now they have known that all things, as many as you have given to me, are from you.
JOH 17:8 For the words which you have given to me, I have given to them; and they received, and they know truly that from you I came forth, and they believed that you sent me.
JOH 17:9 I ask concerning them. Not concerning the world do I ask, but concerning whom you have given to me; for they are yours.
JOH 17:10 And the ones mine are all yours, and the ones yours mine; and I have been glorified in them.
JOH 17:11 And no longer am I in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to you. O holy father, keep them in your name - whom you have given to me, that they might be one, as we!
JOH 17:12 When I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I guarded whom you have given to me, and not one of them perished, except the son of destruction; that the scripture should be fulfilled.
JOH 17:13 And now I come to you; and these things I speak in the world, that they should have my joy having been filled in them.
JOH 17:14 I have given to them your word; and the world detested them, for they are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
JOH 17:15 I ask not that you should take them from out of the world, but that you should keep them from the evil.
JOH 17:16 They are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
JOH 17:17 Sanctify them in your truth! Your word is truth.
JOH 17:18 As you sent me into the world, I also send them into the world.
JOH 17:19 And for them I sanctify myself, that also they might be ones having been sanctified in truth.
JOH 17:20 And I ask not for these only, but also for the ones believing in me through their word;
JOH 17:21 that all might be one; as you, O father, are in me, and I in you, that also they in us might be one; that the world should believe that you sent me.
JOH 17:22 And I have given to them the glory which you have given to me; that they should be one, as we are one.
JOH 17:23 I in them, and you in me, that they should be perfected into one; and that the world should know that you sent me, and loved them, as you loved me.
JOH 17:24 O father, whom you have given to me, I want that where I am, also those should be with me; that they should view my glory, which you gave to me. For you loved me before the founding of the world.
JOH 17:25 O just father, even the world knew you not. But I knew you, and these knew that you sent me.
JOH 17:26 And I made known to them your name, and I will make it known. That the love which you loved me should be in them, and I in them.
JOH 18:1 These things having said, Jesus came forth with his disciples on the other side of the rushing stream of the Kidron, where there was a garden into which he and his disciples entered.
JOH 18:2 And Judas the one delivering him up also knew the place. For often Jesus gathered together there with his disciples.
JOH 18:3 Then Judas, taking the cohort and officers of the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with torches and lamps and weapons.
JOH 18:4 Jesus then knowing all things coming upon him, having come forth, said to them, Whom do you seek?
JOH 18:5 They answered to him, Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus says to them, I am he. And standing by also was Judas, the one delivering him up, with them.
JOH 18:6 When then he said to them that, I am he, they went rearwards, and fell on the ground.
JOH 18:7 Again then he asked them, Whom do you seek? And they said, Jesus the Nazarene.
JOH 18:8 Jesus answered, I said to you that I am he. If then you seek me, let these go!
JOH 18:9 That the word which he said should be fulfilled, that, Of whom you have given to me perished not of them not one.
JOH 18:10 Simon Peter then having a sword drew it, and hit the servant of the chief priest, and cut off his right ear. And the name to the servant was Malchus.
JOH 18:11 then Jesus said to Peter, Put your sword into its holder! The cup which the father has given to me, should I in no way drink it?
JOH 18:12 Then the cohort and the commander and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus, and bound him.
JOH 18:13 And they took him away to Annas first; for he was father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was chief priest that year.
JOH 18:14 And it was Caiaphas advising the Jews, saying that, It is advantageous for one man to perish for the people.
JOH 18:15 And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and another disciple. And that disciple was known to the chief priest, and entered together with Jesus into the courtyard of the chief priest.
JOH 18:16 And Peter stood by the door outside. The other disciple came forth then, who was known to the chief priest, and spoke with the doorkeeper, and she brought in Peter.
JOH 18:17 Says then the maidservant doorkeeper to Peter, Are you not also one of the disciples of this man? That one says, I am not.
JOH 18:18 And the servants and the officers were standing, having made a charcoal bed; for it was chilly. And they were heating themselves. And Peter was standing with them, and heating himself.
JOH 18:19 Then the chief priest asked Jesus concerning his disciples, and concerning his teaching.
JOH 18:20 Jesus answered to him, I in an open manner spoke to the world; I at all times taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, where at all times the Jews come together; and in secret I spoke nothing.
JOH 18:21 Why do you ask? Ask the ones hearing what I spoke to them! Behold, these know what I said!
JOH 18:22 And in his having said these things, one of the officers standing by gave a slap to Jesus, having said, Thus you answer to the chief priest?
JOH 18:23 Jesus responded to him, If ill I have spoken, testify concerning the bad; but if well, why do you flay at me?
JOH 18:24 And Annas sent him being bound to Caiaphas the chief priest.
JOH 18:25 And Simon Peter was standing and heating himself. Then one said to him, are you not also one of his disciples? That one denied, and said, I am not.
JOH 18:26 Says one of the servants of the chief priest, being a relative of whom Peter cut off the ear, Did I not see you in the garden with him?
JOH 18:27 Then again Peter denied. And immediately a rooster called out.
JOH 18:28 Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas unto the praetorium. And it was morning; and they did not enter into the praetorium, that they should not be defiled; but that they should eat the passover.
JOH 18:29 Then came forth Pilate to them, and said, What charge do you bring against this man?
JOH 18:30 They answered and said to him, If this one was not doing evil, we would not have delivered him up to you.
JOH 18:31 Then said Pilate to them, You take him, and according to your law judge him! Then the Jews said to him, To us it is not allowed to kill anyone.
JOH 18:32 That the word of Jesus should be fulfilled which he spoke signifying by what death he was about to die.
JOH 18:33 Pilate entered then into the praetorium again, and called Jesus, and said to him, Are you the king of the Jews?
JOH 18:34 Jesus answered to him, From yourself do you say this, or others spoke to you concerning me?
JOH 18:35 Pilate answered, Much less, am I a Jew? Your nation and the chief priests delivered you to me. What did you do?
JOH 18:36 Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom was of this world, my officers would have been struggling that I should not be delivered up to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here.
JOH 18:37 Then said Pilate to him, Then you are a king? Jesus answered, You say it, for I am a king. I have been born for this, and for this I have come into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Every one being of the truth hears my voice.
JOH 18:38 Pilate says to him, What is truth? And this having said, again he came forth to the Jews, and says to them, I find not one fault in him.
JOH 18:39 But it is a custom with you that I should loosen one to you at the passover. Do you want then I should loose to you the king of the Jews?
JOH 18:40 They cried out then again, all saying, Not this one, but Barabbas. And Barabbas was a robber.
JOH 19:1 Then therefore Pilate took Jesus, and whipped him.
JOH 19:2 And the soldiers, having plaited a crown of thorns, placed it upon his head, and a cloak of purple they put around him,
JOH 19:3 and said, Hail, the king of the Jews! And they gave him slaps.
JOH 19:4 Pilate came forth then again outside, and says to them, See! I bring him to you outside, that you should know that in him not one fault I find.
JOH 19:5 Jesus then came forth outside, wearing the thorny crown, and the purple cloak. And he says to them, Behold the man!
JOH 19:6 When then the chief priests and the officers beheld him, they cried out saying, Crucify, crucify him! Pilate says to them, Take him yourselves, and crucify, for I do not find fault in him.
JOH 19:7 The Jews answered him, We have a law, and according to our law he ought to die, for he made himself a son of God.
JOH 19:8 Then when Pilate heard this word, more he feared.
JOH 19:9 And he entered into the praetorium again, and says to Jesus, From what place are you? But Jesus gave not an answer to him.
JOH 19:10 Then says Pilate to him, To me you speak not? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you, and I have authority to release you?
JOH 19:11 Jesus answered, You have not an authority in anything against me, except what was given to you from above. On account of this, the one delivering me up to you has the greater sin.
JOH 19:12 From this Pilate sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying, If this one you should release, you are not a friend of Caesar. Every one making himself king, speaks against Caesar.
JOH 19:13 Then Pilate hearing this word, brought Jesus outside, and sat upon the rostrum in the place being called Lithostratus, but in Hebrew Gabbatha.
JOH 19:14 And it was preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour. And he says to the Jews, Behold your king!
JOH 19:15 And they cried out, Take him, take him! Crucify him! Pilate says to them, Shall I crucify your king? The chief priests answered, We have not a king except Caesar.
JOH 19:16 Then therefore he delivered him up to them that he should be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him.
JOH 19:17 And bearing his cross, he came forth unto the place being called of the Skull, which is called in Hebrew, Golgotha;
JOH 19:18 where they crucified him, and with him two others, one here on this side and one h ere on that side, and Jesus in the middle.
JOH 19:19 And Pilate wrote also a title, and put it upon the cross. And was written, Jesus the Nazarene the King of the Jews.
JOH 19:20 This title then many of the Jews read, for the place was near the city where Jesus was crucified. And it was written in Hebrew, in Greek, in Roman.
JOH 19:21 then the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews! but that that one said, I am king of the Jews.
JOH 19:22 Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.
JOH 19:23 Then the soldiers, when they crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts - to each soldier a part, and the inner garment. But the inner garment was seamless, from the top woven through entire.
JOH 19:24 They said then to one another, We should not split it, but obtain by lot for it, whose it shall be; that the scripture should be fulfilled, the one saying, They divided into parts my garments among themselves, and over my clothes they cast a lot. Then indeed the soldiers did these things.
JOH 19:25 And stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and the sister of his mother, Mary the one of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
JOH 19:26 Jesus then seeing the mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he says to his mother, O woman, See your son!
JOH 19:27 Then he says to the disciple, Behold, your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her for his own.
JOH 19:28 After this, Jesus knowing that all things already have been finished, that the scripture should be perfected, says, I thirst.
JOH 19:29 A utensil then was situated full of vinegar; and the ones having filled a sponge with vinegar, and putting on hyssop, brought it near his mouth.
JOH 19:30 When therefore Jesus took the vinegar, he said, It has been finished. And having leaned the head, he delivered up the spirit.
JOH 19:31 Then the Jews (that the bodies should not remain upon the cross during the sabbath, since it was preparation, for that was a great day of the sabbath) asked Pilate that their legs should be broken, and they should be taken away.
JOH 19:32 Then came the soldiers. And the first one they broke the legs, and the other being crucified along with him.
JOH 19:33 But having come unto Jesus, when they saw him already having died, they did not break his legs.
JOH 19:34 But one of the soldiers with a lance pierced his side, and immediately came forth blood and water.
JOH 19:35 And the one seeing bears witness, and his testimony is true. And that one knows that he speaks true, that you should believe.
JOH 19:36 For these things took place, that the scripture should be fulfilled, Not a bone of his shall be broken.
JOH 19:37 And again another scripture says, They shall look on whom they pierced.
JOH 19:38 And after these things Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate, (being a disciple of Jesus, but being hidden for the fear of the Jews,) that he should take the body of Jesus. And Pilate committed it to his care. Then he came, and took the body of Jesus.
JOH 19:39 And came also Nicodemus, (the one coming to Jesus by night at first,) bearing a mixture of myrrh and aloe, about a hundred liters.
JOH 19:40 They then took the body of Jesus, and tied it with small pieces of cloth with the aromatics, as is custom with the Jews to embalm.
JOH 19:41 And a garden was in the place where he was crucified; and in the garden a new sepulchre, in which not yet was anyone placed.
JOH 19:42 There then, (because of the preparation of the Jews, for the sepulchre was near,) they placed Jesus.
JOH 20:1 But on day one of the sabbaths, Mary the Magdalene comes in the morning, still being darkness, unto the sepulchre, and sees the stone having been lifted from the sepulchre.
JOH 20:2 She runs then, and comes to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus is fond of, and says to them, They took the Lord from out of the sepulchre, and we knew not where they put him.
JOH 20:3 Peter went forth then, and the other disciple, and they came unto the sepulchre.
JOH 20:4 And the two ran together; and the other disciple ran in front more quickly than Peter, and came first unto the sepulchre.
JOH 20:5 And leaning over, he sees the linen bands lying; however he enters not.
JOH 20:6 Then Simon Peter comes following him, and he entered into the sepulchre, and views the linen bands lying.
JOH 20:7 And the scarf which was upon his head is not lying with the linen bands, but separate from them, being swathed in one place.
JOH 20:8 Then therefore entered also the other disciple, the one having come first unto the sepulchre. And he saw, and believed.
JOH 20:9 For not yet they knew the scripture that it is necessary for him to rise up from the dead.
JOH 20:10 Then the disciples went forth again to their own.
JOH 20:11 But Mary stood at the sepulchre weeping outside. As then she wept, she leaned over into the sepulchre,
JOH 20:12 and views two angels in white, one being seated at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus has been laid.
JOH 20:13 And they say to her, those ones, O woman, why do you weep? She says to them that, They took my Lord, and I know not where they placed him.
JOH 20:14 And these things having said, she turns to the rear, and she views Jesus standing, and knows not that it is Jesus.
JOH 20:15 Jesus says to her, O woman, Why do you weep? Whom do you seek? That on, thinking that he is the gardener, says to him, O master, if you bore him, tell me where you put him, and I will take him.
JOH 20:16 Jesus says to her, Mary. Turning, that one says to him, Rabboni; which is to say, Teacher.
JOH 20:17 Jesus says to her, Do not touch me! for not yet have I ascended to my father. But go to my brothers, and say to them! I ascend to my father, and your father; and my God, and your God.
JOH 20:18 Then Mary Magdalene comes reporting to the disciples that she has seen the Lord, and these things he said to her.
JOH 20:19 It being then late in that day, in the day one of the sabbaths, and the doors being locked where the disciples were being gathered together because of the fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and says to them, Peace to you.
JOH 20:20 And this having said, he showed to them his hands and the side. The disciples rejoiced then seeing the Lord.
JOH 20:21 Jesus said then to them again, Peace to you. As the father sent me, I also send you.
JOH 20:22 And this having said, he breathed onto, and says to them, Receive holy spirit.
JOH 20:23 Of whomsoever sins you should forgive, they are forgiven to them; of whomsoever you should hold, they are held.
JOH 20:24 But Thomas, one of the twelve, the one being called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
JOH 20:25 The other disciples said then to him, We have seen the Lord. And he said to them, Unless I should see in his hands the impression of the nails, and should put my finger into the impression of the nails, and should put my hand into his side, in no way shall I believe.
JOH 20:26 And after eight days again his disciples were inside, and Thomas was with them. Then comes Jesus, of the doors having been locked, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace to you.
JOH 20:27 So then he says to Thomas, Bring your finger here, and behold my hands; and bring your hand, and put it into my side; and be not unbelieving, but believing!
JOH 20:28 And Thomas responded and said to him, My Lord and my God.
JOH 20:29 Jesus says to him, Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are the ones not seeing, and having believed.
JOH 20:30 Indeed many then even other signs Jesus did in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this scroll.
JOH 20:31 But these things have been written that you should believe that Jesus is the Christ, the son of God; and that believing you should have life in his name.
JOH 21:1 After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and he manifested thus.
JOH 21:2 There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas, the one being called Didymus, and Nathanael, the one from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples.
JOH 21:3 Simon Peter says to them, I go to fish. They say to him, We also go with you. And they went forth, ascending into the boat straightly. And in that night they laid hold of nothing.
JOH 21:4 And morning already coming to pass, Jesus stood on the shore. However the disciples knew not that it is Jesus.
JOH 21:5 Jesus then says to them, Sons do you have anything for eating? They answered to him, No.
JOH 21:6 And he said to them, Cast unto the right parts of the boat with the net, and you shall find. They cast then, and no longer were they able to draw because of the multitude of the fishes.
JOH 21:7 Says then that disciple whom Jesus loved to Peter, It is the Lord. Then Simon Peter having heard that it is the Lord, girded up the outer garment, (for he was naked,) and threw himself into the sea.
JOH 21:8 And the other disciples came in the boat; (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits,) dragging along the net of the fishes.
JOH 21:9 Then as they disembarked onto the land, they see a charcoal bed being situated, and fish resting upon it, and bread.
JOH 21:10 Jesus says to them, bring of the little fish which you laid hold of just now.
JOH 21:11 Simon Peter ascended, and drew the net upon the land full of great fishes, a hundred and fifty-three. And being so great the net was not split.
JOH 21:12 Jesus says to them, Come dine! But no one dared of the disciples to diligently inquire of him, Who are you? knowing that it is the Lord.
JOH 21:13 Then comes Jesus, and takes the bread, and gives to them, and the little fish in like manner.
JOH 21:14 This is already the third time Jesus was manifested to his disciples, having been raised from the dead.
JOH 21:15 When therefore they dined, Jesus says to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these? He says to him, Yes, O Lord; you know that I am fond of you. He says to him, Graze my little lambs!
JOH 21:16 He says to him again a second time, Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me? He says to him, Yes, O Lord; you know that I am fond of you. He says to him, Tend my sheep!
JOH 21:17 He says to him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, are you fond of me? Peter fretted that he said to him the third time, Are you fond of me? And he said to him, O Lord, you know all things; you know that I am fond of you. Jesus says to him, Graze my sheep!
JOH 21:18 Amen, amen, I say to you, When you were younger, you tied up yourself, and walked where you wanted; but whenever you shall grow old, you shall stretch out your hands, and another will tie you up, and shall bring you where you want not.
JOH 21:19 And this he said, signifying by what death he shall glorify God. And this having said, he says to him, You follow me!
JOH 21:20 And Peter turning, sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following; who also reclined at the supper upon his breast, and said, O Lord, who is the one delivering you up?
JOH 21:21 Seeing this one, Peter says to Jesus, O Lord, But what about this one?
JOH 21:22 Jesus says to him, If I want him to remain until I come, what is it to you? You follow me!
JOH 21:23 Then this word went forth unto the brothers, that that disciple does not die. But Jesus said not to him that he does not die; but, If I want him to remain until I come, what is it to you?
JOH 21:24 This is the disciple witnessing concerning these things, and writing these things. And we know that his witness is true.
JOH 21:25 And there are also many other things, as much as Jesus did, which if they should be written one by one, I imagine not even the world itself to have space for the scrolls being written. Amen.
ACT 1:1 Indeed the first matter I made concerning all the things, O Theophilus, which Jesus began to both do and to teach,
ACT 1:2 until which day, giving charge to the apostles through holy spirit whom he chose, he was taken up.
ACT 1:3 To whom also he rendered himself living after his suffering with many evidences, during forty days being seen by them, and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of God.
ACT 1:4 And being assembled together, he exhorted them to not separate from Jerusalem, but to remain about for the promise of the father, Which he said, you heard of me.
ACT 1:5 For John indeed immersed in water; but you shall be immersed in holy spirit not after these many days.
ACT 1:6 They indeed then having come together, they asked him, saying, O Lord, is it in this time you restore the kingdom to Israel?
ACT 1:7 And he said to them, It is not for you to know times or seasons which the father put in his own authority.
ACT 1:8 But you shall receive power of the holy spirit coming upon you. And you will be to me witnesses in both Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and unto the end of the earth.
ACT 1:9 And having said these things, of their looking, he was lifted up; and a cloud undertook him from their eyes.
ACT 1:10 And as they were gazing into the heaven at his going, and behold, two men stood by them in white attire,
ACT 1:11 ones who also said, Men, Galileans, why do you stand looking into the heaven? This Jesus being taken up from you into the heaven, so shall come in which manner you saw him going into the heaven.
ACT 1:12 Then they returned unto Jerusalem from the mount being called Olive Grove, which is near Jerusalem, sufficing for a sabbath journey.
ACT 1:13 And when they entered, they ascended unto the upper room, where were staying both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot, and Jude of James.
ACT 1:14 These all were attending constantly with one accord in the prayer and in the supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
ACT 1:15 And in those days, Peter having risen up in the midst of the disciples, said, (and was the multitude of names together about a hundred twenty,)
ACT 1:16 Men, brothers, it was necessary to fulfill this scripture, which the holy spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, the one becoming a guide to the ones seizing Jesus.
ACT 1:17 For he was counted with us, and obtained a lot of this service.
ACT 1:18 This one indeed then acquired a place from the wage of iniquity; and being fallen headlong, he split open in the middle, and all his intestines poured out.
ACT 1:19 And it became known to all the ones dwelling in Jerusalem, so as to call that place, in their own dialect, Akeldama; that is, Place of Blood.
ACT 1:20 For it has been written in the book of Psalms, Let his property become desolate, and let there not be one dwelling in it! and, May another receive his overseeing.
ACT 1:21 It is necessary then of the men coming together with us during all the time in which the Lord Jesus entered and went forth among us,
ACT 1:22 beginning from the immersion of John, until the day of which he was taken up from us, for one of these to become a witness with us of his resurrection.
ACT 1:23 And they established two, Joseph (being called Barsabas, who was called by name Justus,) and Matthias.
ACT 1:24 And praying, they said, You, O Lord, are a knower of hearts of all, make manifest whom you chose of these - the one of the two,
ACT 1:25 to receive the lot of this service and commission, from of which Judas violated to go unto his own place!
ACT 1:26 And they gave their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was alloted with the eleven apostles.
ACT 2:1 And in the filling up the days of Pentecost, they were all together with one accord in the same place.
ACT 2:2 And came suddenly from out of the heaven a sound as if of a violent breath being brought, and it filled the whole house of which they were settled.
ACT 2:3 And there appeared to them divided tongues as of fire, and it sat upon each one of them.
ACT 2:4 And they were filled all together of holy spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the spirit gave to them to be declared.
ACT 2:5 And there were Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, reverent men from every nation of the ones under the heaven.
ACT 2:6 And the report of this having taken place, the multitude came together and were confounded, for they heard each one of them speaking in his own dialect.
ACT 2:7 And they were amazed and marvelled, saying to one another, Behold are these not all which are speaking Galileans?
ACT 2:8 And how hear we each in our own dialect, in which we were born?
ACT 2:9 Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the ones inhabiting Mesopotamia, and Judea, and Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
ACT 2:10 both Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and the Romans emigrating here, both Jews and converts,
ACT 2:11 Cretans and Arabians - we hear them speaking in our own languages the magnificent things of God.
ACT 2:12 And all were amazed and perplexed, saying the other to another, What ever would this be?
ACT 2:13 But others taunting said that, They are stuffed with sweet new wine.
ACT 2:14 And Peter standing with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and declared to them, Men, Jews, and all the ones dwelling in Jerusalem, let this be made known to you, and give ear to my words!
ACT 2:15 For these are not intoxicated as you undertake, for it is the third hour of the day.
ACT 2:16 But this is the thing being spoken by the prophet Joel;
ACT 2:17 And it will be in the last days, says God, I will pour out from my spirit upon all flesh. And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.
ACT 2:18 And indeed upon my menservants and upon my maidservants in those days I will pour out from my spirit; and they shall prophesy.
ACT 2:19 And I will execute miracles in the heaven upward, and signs upon the earth below; blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke.
ACT 2:20 The sun shall be converted into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the coming - the great and apparent day of the Lord.
ACT 2:21 And it shall be all, who ever should call upon the name of the Lord shall be delivered.
ACT 2:22 Men, Israelites, hear these words! Jesus the Nazarene, a man from God exhibited unto you powers and miracles and signs, which God did through him in your midst, as even you yourselves know.
ACT 2:23 This one delivered up by the confirmed counsel and foreknowledge of God; having taken, you did away with by lawless hands staking him up.
ACT 2:24 Whom God raised up, having loosed the pangs of death. In so far as it was not possible for him to be held by it.
ACT 2:25 For David says concerning him, I foresaw the Lord before me continually, for he is at my right hand, that I shall not be shaken.
ACT 2:26 On account of this my heart was made merry, and my tongue exulted; but still also my flesh shall encamp in hope.
ACT 2:27 For you shall not abandon my soul into Hades, nor shall you give your sacred one to see corruption.
ACT 2:28 You made known to me the ways of life; you shall fill me with gladness with your countenance.
ACT 2:29 Men, brothers, it is allowed to speak with an open manner to you concerning the patriarch David, that both he came to an end and was entombed, and his tomb is among us as far as this day.
ACT 2:30 A prophet then being, and knowing that God swore to him an oath, (of the fruit of his loin, the one according to the flesh,) to raise up the Christ, to sit upon his throne;
ACT 2:31 looking out ahead he spoke concerning the resurrection of the Christ, That his soul was not left in Hades, nor his flesh saw corruption.
ACT 2:32 This Jesus God raised up, of which all we are witnesses.
ACT 2:33 By the right hand then of God having been raised up high, and the promise of the holy spirit having received by the father, he poured out this which you now see and hear.
ACT 2:34 For David did not ascend into the heavens. For he says himself, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit down at my right,
ACT 2:35 until whenever I should establish your enemies as a footstool of your feet.
ACT 2:36 With certainty then let all the house of Israel know, that God made him both Lord and Christ - this Jesus whom you crucified!
ACT 2:37 And having heard, they were vexed in the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, What shall we do men, brothers?
ACT 2:38 And Peter said to them, Repent, and each of you be immersed in the name of Jesus Christ for a release of sins, and you shall receive the present of the holy spirit!
ACT 2:39 For to you is the promise, and to your children, and to all the ones far away, as many as should call on the Lord our God.
ACT 2:40 And with many more other words he testified and appealed, saying, Be delivered from this crooked generation.
ACT 2:41 The ones indeed then gladly receiving his word were immersed. And about three thousand souls were added in that day.
ACT 2:42 And they were attending constantly in the teaching of the apostles, and in the fellowship, and in the breaking of bread, and in the prayers.
ACT 2:43 And fear came to every soul. And many miracles and signs took place through the apostles.
ACT 2:44 But all the ones believing were together, and had all in common.
ACT 2:45 And the possessions and the things of substance they sold, and parted them to all in so far as anyone had need.
ACT 2:46 And by day attending constantly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread in their houses, they shared provision with exultation and simplicity of heart,
ACT 2:47 praising God, and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added the ones being delivered daily to the assembly.
ACT 3:1 And together Peter and John ascended unto the temple at the hour of prayer - the ninth.
ACT 3:2 And a certain man being lame from his mother's belly was borne, whom they put daily at the door of the temple being called Beautiful, to ask charity from the ones entering into the temple.
ACT 3:3 Who seeing Peter and John being about to enter into the temple, asked charity.
ACT 3:4 And Peter gazing at him with John, said, Look at us!
ACT 3:5 And he waited for them, expecting to receive something from them.
ACT 3:6 But Peter said, Silver and gold does not exist to me; but what I have this I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth arise and walk!
ACT 3:7 And laying hold of him by the right hand, he raised him. And immediately his bases and ankles were solidified.
ACT 3:8 And leaping up, he stood and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
ACT 3:9 And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
ACT 3:10 And they recognized him, that this one was the one sitting down for charity at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. And they were filled with stupefaction and astonishment over the thing having happened to him.
ACT 3:11 And of the lame man who was healed holding Peter and John, all the people ran together to them unto the stoa being called Solomon's, utterly astonished.
ACT 3:12 And seeing, Peter responded to the people, Men, Israelites, why do you marvel at this? or why gaze upon us as if it was by our own power or piety making him to walk?
ACT 3:13 The God of Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his servant Jesus; whom you delivered up, and denied him in front of Pilate, having adjudged to release that one.
ACT 3:14 But you denied the holy and just one, and asked for a man, a murderer to be granted to you;
ACT 3:15 and the chief of life you killed, whom God raised from the dead; of which we are witnesses.
ACT 3:16 And by the belief of his name, this one whom you view and know, he made solid by his name; and the belief which is through him he gave to him this wholeness before all of you.
ACT 3:17 And now, brothers, I know that according to ignorance you acted, as also your rulers.
ACT 3:18 But what God preannounced through the mouth of all his prophets, for the Christ to suffer, he fulfilled thus.
ACT 3:19 Repent then, and turn, for the wiping away of your sins! so that times of respite should come from the presence of the Lord;
ACT 3:20 and he should send the one who was publicly proclaimed to you - Jesus Christ;
ACT 3:21 whom heaven must indeed receive till times of restoration of all things, of which God spoke through the mouth of all his holy prophets from the eon.
ACT 3:22 For Moses indeed said to the fathers that, The Lord your God shall raise up a prophet unto you from your brothers, as me; him you shall hear according to all as much as he should speak to you.
ACT 3:23 And it shall be every soul, which ever should not hearken to that prophet, shall be utterly destroyed from the people.
ACT 3:24 And indeed all the prophets from Samuel and of the ones in order, as many as spoke, also announced these days.
ACT 3:25 You are sons of the prophets, and of the covenant of which God ordained to our fathers, saying to Abraham, And in your seed shall be blessed all the families of the earth.
ACT 3:26 To you first God, having raised up his servant Jesus, sent him blessing you, in the turning each from your wickednesses.
ACT 4:1 And of their speaking to the people, the priests stood by them, and the commandant of the temple, and the Sadducees,
ACT 4:2 being worked up because of their teaching the people, and announcing in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.
ACT 4:3 And they put upon them hands, and put them in keep until the morrow; for it was evening already.
ACT 4:4 But many of the ones hearing the word believed; and the number of the men was about five thousand.
ACT 4:5 And it came to pass on the morrow, their rulers gathered together, and elders, and scribes in Jerusalem,
ACT 4:6 and Annas the chief priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the family of the chief priest.
ACT 4:7 And having stood them in the midst, they inquired, By what power, or in whose name do you this?
ACT 4:8 Then Peter, filled of holy spirit, said to them, Rulers of the people, and elders of Israel.
ACT 4:9 If we today are questioned about a good work of the infirm man, by how this one was delivered;
ACT 4:10 let it be made known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by this one this man stands before you in health.
ACT 4:11 This one is the stone being treated with contempt by you the ones building, the one becoming for head of the corner.
ACT 4:12 And there is not deliverance in no one other. For neither is there another name under the heaven being given to men by which we must be delivered.
ACT 4:13 And viewing the open manner of Peter and John, and perceiving that they are illiterate men and common people, they marvelled; and they recognized them, that they were with Jesus.
ACT 4:14 But seeing the man with them standing having been cured, they had nothing to contradict.
ACT 4:15 And having bid them to go forth outside the sanhedrin, they engaged with one another,
ACT 4:16 saying, What shall we do to these men? For indeed a known sign having taken place through them is apparent to all the ones dwelling in Jerusalem; and we are not able to deny it.
ACT 4:17 But that it should not be spread unto more among the people, we should threaten them with intimidation to no longer speak in this name to anyone of men.
ACT 4:18 And having called them, they summoned them to not utter a sound altogether nor to teach in the name of Jesus.
ACT 4:19 But Peter and John answering to them said, If it is just before God to hearken to you rather than God, you judge!
ACT 4:20 For we are not able what we know and hear to not speak.
ACT 4:21 And the one adding threats released them, finding nothing how they shall punish them, on account of the people. For all glorified God over the thing having taken place.
ACT 4:22 For the man was more than forty years old upon which had taken place this sign of healing.
ACT 4:23 And having been released, they came to their own, and reported as much as the chief priests and the elders said to them.
ACT 4:24 And having heard, with one accord they lifted a voice to God, and said, O master, you are God, the one making the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all the things in them.
ACT 4:25 The one having spoken through the mouth of David your servant, saying, Why do nations neigh, and peoples meditate upon vain things?
ACT 4:26 The kings of the earth stood, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord, and against his Christ.
ACT 4:27 For they gathered together in truth against the holy one, your servant Jesus, whom you anointed - both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with nations, and peoples of Israel,
ACT 4:28 to do as much as your hand and your counsel predefined to take place.
ACT 4:29 And at present, O Lord, look upon their intimidations! and grant to your servants with every open manner to speak your word!
ACT 4:30 in the stretching out of your hand for healing; and signs and miracles to take place through the name of your holy servant Jesus.
ACT 4:31 And in their beseeching the place in which they were being gathered together was shaken; and they were all filled of holy spirit, and they spoke the word of God with confidence.
ACT 4:32 And the multitude of the ones believing was of one heart and soul. And not even one said anything existing to him to be his own; but all things were in common to them.
ACT 4:33 And with great power the apostles rendered testimony of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus; and great favor was upon all of them.
ACT 4:34 For neither anyone lacking existed among them. For as many as were owners of places or houses existing to them, by selling they brought the value of the things being sold,
ACT 4:35 and put them by the feet of the apostles. And it was distributed to each in so far as any should have need.
ACT 4:36 And Joses, the one being called Barnabas by the apostles, (which is, being translated, Son of Comfort,) a Levite, a Cypriot by race,
ACT 4:37 having sold a field existing to him, brought the thing, and put it by the feet of the apostles.
ACT 5:1 And a certain man, Ananias by name, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession.
ACT 5:2 And he pilfered from the value. And his wife being fully conscious of it, and having brought a certain part, put it by the feet of the apostles.
ACT 5:3 And Peter said, Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart for you to lie against the holy spirit, and to pilfer from the value of the place?
ACT 5:4 Remaining in your possession did it not remain? and for selling it existed in your authority? Why is it that you put this thing in your heart? You lied not to men, but to God.
ACT 5:5 And Ananias hearing these words, falling down, expired. And there became great fear upon all the ones hearing these things.
ACT 5:6 And having risen up, the younger men wrapped him, and having brought him forth, entombed him.
ACT 5:7 And it came to pass about three hours interval, and his wife, not knowing what happened, entered.
ACT 5:8 And Peter responded to her, Tell me if you rendered so much for the place? And she said, Yes, for so much.
ACT 5:9 And Peter said to her, Why is it that you joined in one accord to test the spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of the ones burying your husband are at the door, and shall bring you forth.
ACT 5:10 And she fell immediately by his feet, and expired. And the young men having entered, found her dead, and, having brought her forth they entombed her by her husband.
ACT 5:11 And there became great fear upon the entire assembly, and upon all the ones hearing these things.
ACT 5:12 And by the hands of the apostles there took place signs and miracles among the people - many; (and they were with one accord all together in the stoa of Solomon;
ACT 5:13 but of the rest no one dared join them; but the people magnified them;
ACT 5:14 and more were added believing in the Lord - multitudes of men and also of women.)
ACT 5:15 so as in the squares to bring forth the weak, and to put them upon beds and litters, that at the coming of Peter even the shadow should overshadow some one of them.
ACT 5:16 And came together also the multitudes of the cities all around into Jerusalem, bringing the weak, and ones being mobbed by unclean spirits; who were cured all together.
ACT 5:17 And having risen up, the chief priest and all the ones with him, ( which is the sect of the Sadducees,) were filled of zeal.
ACT 5:18 And they put their hands upon the apostles, and put them in a public keep.
ACT 5:19 But an angel of the Lord by night opened the doors of the prison, and leading them out said,
ACT 5:20 Go, and standing, speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life!
ACT 5:21 And having heard, they entered at the dawn into the temple, and were teaching. But having come, the chief priest and the ones with him, called together the sanhedrin, and all the council of elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the jail for them to be brought.
ACT 5:22 And the officers having come, did not find them in the prison. And having returned, they reported,
ACT 5:23 saying that, Indeed the jail we found locked with all security, and the keepers standing before the doors; but having opened we found no one inside.
ACT 5:24 And as they heard these words, both the priest and the commandant of the temple and the chief priests were perplexed concerning them, whatever this might be.
ACT 5:25 And having come, a certain one reported to them, saying that, Behold, the men whom you put in the prison are in the temple standing and teaching the people.
ACT 5:26 Then the commandant having gone forth with the officers led them, not with force; for they feared the people, that they should not be stoned.
ACT 5:27 And having brought them, they stood them in the sanhedrin. And the chief priest asked them,
ACT 5:28 saying, Was it not with an exhortation we exhorted to you to not teach in this name? And behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to bring upon us the blood of this man.
ACT 5:29 And answering Peter and the apostles said, It is necessary to yield obedience to God rather than men.
ACT 5:30 The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you laid hands upon having hanged upon a treetimber..
ACT 5:31 This one God, chief and deliverer, exalted by his right hand, to give repentance to Israel and release of sins.
ACT 5:32 And we are his witnesses of these things; but also the holy spirit, which God gave to the ones yielding obedience to him.
ACT 5:33 And the ones hearing were sawed through, and consulted to do away with them.
ACT 5:34 And having risen up, a certain one in the sanhedrin, a Pharisee, by name Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, esteemed by all the people, urged the apostles to be made to go outside a little while.
ACT 5:35 And he said to them, Men, Israelites, take heed to yourselves over these men what you are about to act!
ACT 5:36 For before these days Theudas rose up, naming himself to be somebody, in whom a number of men leaned towards, about four hundred, who were done away with. And all, as many as were persuaded by him, were parted, and came to nothing.
ACT 5:37 After this Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census, and separated a fit amount of people to go after him. And that one perished; and all, as many as were persuaded by him, were dispersed.
ACT 5:38 And at present I say to you, Abstain from these men, and allow them! for if this counsel should be of men, then this work will be broken up.
ACT 5:39 But if it is of God, you will not be able to break it up; lest at any time even you be found fighters against God.
ACT 5:40 And they were persuaded by him. And having called the apostles, having flayed them, they exhorted them to not speak in the name of Jesus, and they released them.
ACT 5:41 Indeed then they went rejoicing from in front of the sanhedrin, that they were deemed worthy for the name of Jesus to be dishonored.
ACT 5:42 And every day in the temple, and by house, they ceased not teaching and announcing good news of Jesus the Christ.
ACT 6:1 And in these days, of the multiplying of the disciples, there took place a grumbling of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, that their widows were overlooked in the daily service.
ACT 6:2 And the twelve having called the multitude of the disciples, said, It is not pleasing for us leaving behind the word of God, to serve tables.
ACT 6:3 Number brothers then, men from among you being witnesses - seven men, full of holy spirit and wisdom, whom we will place over this need!
ACT 6:4 But we in the prayer and in the service of the word will attend constantly.
ACT 6:5 And the word was pleasing before all the multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of belief and holy spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a convert of Antioch,
ACT 6:6 whom they stood before the apostles. And having prayed, they placed hands on them.
ACT 6:7 And the word of God grew; and the number of the disciples was multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly; also a great multitude of the priests hearkened to the belief.
ACT 6:8 And Stephen, full of belief and power, did miracles and great signs among the people.
ACT 6:9 And rose up certain ones from the synagogue being called, Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of the ones from Cilicia, and Asia, debating with Stephen.
ACT 6:10 And they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the spirit which he spoke.
ACT 6:11 Then they suborned men, saying that, We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God.
ACT 6:12 And they agitated together the people, and the elders, and the scribes; and attending to it, they seized him, and brought him to the sanhedrin.
ACT 6:13 And they set false witnesses, saying, This man does not cease speaking blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law.
ACT 6:14 For we have heard him saying, that this Jesus the Nazarene shall destroy this place, and shall change the customs which Moses delivered up to us.
ACT 6:15 And having gazed onto him, all the ones being seated in the sanhedrin beheld his face as the face of an angel.
ACT 7:1 And the chief priest said, Do then these things so hold to?
ACT 7:2 And he said, Men, brothers, and fathers, hearken! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham, being in Mesopotamia before his dwelling in Haran.
ACT 7:3 And he said to him, Go forth from out of your land, and from your kin, and come into a land which I will show to you!
ACT 7:4 Then having gone forth from the land of the Chaldeans, he dwelt in Haran. And from there, after the dying of his father, he displaced him into this land, into which you now dwell.
ACT 7:5 And he did not give to him an inheritance in it, nor a foot stool. And he promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him - there not being a child to him.
ACT 7:6 And God thus spoke, that his seed will be a sojourner in an alien land; and they shall enslave it, and inflict evil for four hundred years.
ACT 7:7 And the nation which ever shall enslave them I shall judge, said God. And after these things they shall come forth, and shall serve to me in this place.
ACT 7:8 And he gave to him a covenant of circumcision. And thus he engendered Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac engendered Jacob; and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
ACT 7:9 And the patriarchs, envying Joseph, rendered him into Egypt. And God was with him,
ACT 7:10 and delivered him from out of all his afflictions, and gave to him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he placed him as leader over Egypt and his whole house.
ACT 7:11 And there came a famine upon the entire land of Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction. And our fathers did not find fodder.
ACT 7:12 And Jacob hearing of their being grain in Egypt, sent forth our fathers a first time.
ACT 7:13 And in the second time Joseph made himself known to his brothers; and the family of Joseph became apparent to Pharaoh.
ACT 7:14 And Joseph having sent, called back his father Jacob, and all his kin, in total seventy five souls.
ACT 7:15 And Jacob went down unto Egypt, and he and our fathers came to an end.
ACT 7:16 And they were transferred unto Shechem, and were put in the tomb which Abraham purchased for a value of silver from the sons of Emmor of Shechem.
ACT 7:17 And as the time approached of the promise of which God swore by an oath to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
ACT 7:18 until of which there rose up another king who knew not Joseph.
ACT 7:19 This one having dealt subtly with our race, inflicted evil upon our fathers, to make them expose their babies, so that they should not be brought forth alive.
ACT 7:20 In which time Moses was born, and was fair to God, who was reared three months in the house of his father.
ACT 7:21 And he being exposed, the daughter of Pharaoh took him up, and she reared him herself for a son.
ACT 7:22 And Moses was instructed in all wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in works.
ACT 7:23 And as forty years of time was filled up to him, it ascended unto his heart to visit his brothers of the sons of Israel.
ACT 7:24 And beholding a certain one being wronged, he defended and executed vengeance for the one being harassed, having struck the Egyptian.
ACT 7:25 And he thought his brothers would perceive that God is giving deliverance to them through his hand; but they perceived not.
ACT 7:26 And the following day he appeared to ones doing combat, and he forced them to peace, having said, Men, you are brothers, why wrong one another?
ACT 7:27 But the one wronging the neighbor, thrust him away, having said, Who placed you ruler and magistrate over us?
ACT 7:28 Do you want to do away with me, in which manner you did away with the Egyptian yesterday?
ACT 7:29 And Moses fled at this word, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, of which place he engendered two sons.
ACT 7:30 And forty years being fulfilled, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire of a bush.
ACT 7:31 And Moses beholding, marvelled at the vision. And of his coming forward to study it, there came the voice of the Lord to him, saying,
ACT 7:32 I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses having become trembling, dared not to study it.
ACT 7:33 And the Lord said to him, Untie the sandal of your feet; for the place in which you stand is holy ground!
ACT 7:34 In beholding, I saw the ill-treatment of my people in Egypt, and I heard their moaning, and I came down to rescue them. And now come, I shall send you to Egypt.
ACT 7:35 This Moses whom they denied, having said, Who placed you ruler and magistrate? This one God sent as ruler and ransomer by the hand of an angel appearing to him in the bush.
ACT 7:36 This one led them out, having done miracles and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.
ACT 7:37 This is the Moses having said to the sons of Israel, The lord our God shall raise up a prophet to you from out of your brothers as me.
ACT 7:38 This is the one being among the assembly in the wilderness with the angel speaking to him on mount Sinai, and of the ones of our fathers; who received living oracles to give to us.
ACT 7:39 To whom our fathers wanted not to become subjects, but thrust him away, and turned their hearts unto Egypt,
ACT 7:40 having said to Aaron, Make us gods who shall go before us; for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we know not what has happened to him.
ACT 7:41 And they made a calf image in those days, and led up a sacrifice to the idol, and made merry in the works of their hands.
ACT 7:42 And God turned and delivered them up to serve the military of the heaven; as it has been written in the book of the prophets, Did you not offer to me victims for slaughter and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
ACT 7:43 And you take up the tent of Molech, and the star of your god Remphan, the models of which you made to do obeisance to them; and I will displace you beyond Babylon.
ACT 7:44 The tent of testimony was with our fathers in the wilderness, as set in order by the one speaking to Moses, to make it according to the model which he had seen.
ACT 7:45 Which also our fathers relieving brought in after Joshua in the taking possession of the nations, whom God pushed out from in front of our fathers, until the days of David;
ACT 7:46 who found favor before God, and asked to find a tent for the God of Jacob.
ACT 7:47 But Solomon built to him a house.
ACT 7:48 But the highest does not dwell in temples made by hands; as the prophet says,
ACT 7:49 The heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What house will you build to me? says the Lord, or what place for my rest?
ACT 7:50 Did not my hand make all these things?
ACT 7:51 O hard-necked and uncircumcised in the heart and in the ears, you continually rush headlong against the holy spirit. As your fathers, so also you.
ACT 7:52 Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed the ones preannouncing concerning the advent of the just one; of whom you now have become betrayers and murderers.
ACT 7:53 Who received the law by disposition of angels, and kept not.
ACT 7:54 And hearing these things, they were sawed through in their hearts, and gnashed their teeth against him.
ACT 7:55 And being full of holy spirit, having gazed into the heaven, he beheld the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right of God.
ACT 7:56 And he said, Behold, I view the heavens being opened, and the son of man standing at the right of God.
ACT 7:57 And crying out with a great voice, they held their ears, and advanced with one accord against him.
ACT 7:58 And having cast him outside the city, they stoned him. And the witnesses put aside their garments by the feet of a young man, being called Saul.
ACT 7:59 And they stoned Stephen, the one calling upon and saying, O Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!
ACT 7:60 And having placed the knees, he cried out a great voice, O Lord, you should not set this sin to them. And this having said, he went to sleep.
ACT 8:1 And Saul was assenting with his removal. And came to pass in that day a great persecution against the assembly in Jerusalem; and all were dispersed throughout the places of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
ACT 8:2 And reverent men collected up Stephen, and were making a great beating of the breast over him.
ACT 8:3 But Saul laid waste the assembly entering by houses; dragging both men and women, he delivered them up into prison.
ACT 8:4 The ones then being scattered went through announcing good news - the word.
ACT 8:5 And Philip going down unto a city of Samaria, proclaimed to them the Christ.
ACT 8:6 And the multitudes took heed to the things being said by Philip with one accord, in their hearing and seeing the signs which he did.
ACT 8:7 For many of the ones having unclean spirits, the unclean spirits came forth yelling with a great voice; and many having been disabled and lame were cured.
ACT 8:8 And came to pass a great joy in that city.
ACT 8:9 And a certain man, by name Simon, beforehand in the city was practicing magic, and amazing the nation of Samaria, saying himself to be some great one.
ACT 8:10 To whom all gave heed from small unto great, saying, This one is the power of the great God.
ACT 8:11 And they were giving heed to him, on account of the spending a fit amount of time with the magic to amaze them.
ACT 8:12 And when they believed, with Philip announcing good news - the things concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were immersed, both men and women.
ACT 8:13 And Simon even himself believed. And having been immersed, he was constantly attending to Philip. And viewing works of power and signs being done, he was amazed.
ACT 8:14 And the apostles in Jerusalem having heard that Samaria received the word of God, sent to them Peter and John.
ACT 8:15 Who having gone down prayed concerning them, that they should receive holy spirit.
ACT 8:16 For not yet was it falling upon any one of them; but only being immersed in the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 8:17 Then they placed hands upon them, and they received holy spirit.
ACT 8:18 And Simon seeing that through the laying on of the hands of the apostles the holy spirit was given, he brought to them things,
ACT 8:19 saying, Give to me also this authority, that whom ever I should place the hands should receive holy spirit.
ACT 8:20 And Peter said to him, May your money be with you unto destruction, for you thought the gift of God is to be acquired by things.
ACT 8:21 There is not a portion to you nor lot in this matter; for your heart is not straight before God.
ACT 8:22 Repent then from this your evil, and beseech God, if then the thought of your heart shall be forgiven you!
ACT 8:23 For in bile of bitterness, and bond of unrighteousness I see you being.
ACT 8:24 And responding Simon said, You beseech for me to the Lord, so that nothing should come upon me of which you have said!
ACT 8:25 They indeed then, testifying and having spoken the word of the Lord, returned unto Jerusalem, and in many towns of the Samaritans they announced good news.
ACT 8:26 And an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Rise up, and go according to the south unto the way going down from Jerusalem unto Gaza - this is wilderness!
ACT 8:27 And having risen up he went. And behold, there was an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a mighty one of Candace the queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, who had come to do obeisance in Jerusalem.
ACT 8:28 And he was returning, and sitting upon his chariot. And he read the prophet Isaiah.
ACT 8:29 And the spirit said to Philip, Draw near and join to this chariot.
ACT 8:30 And running up, Philip heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said, Then indeed you know what you read?
ACT 8:31 And he said, For how might I be able, unless someone should guide me? And he appealed to Philip having ascended to sit with him.
ACT 8:32 And the section of the scripture which he read was this, As a sheep unto slaughter he was led; and as a lamb before the one shearing it is voiceless, so he opens not his mouth.
ACT 8:33 In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. And who shall describe his generation, for his life is taken from the earth?
ACT 8:34 And the eunuch responding to Philip, said, I beseech you, concerning whom does this prophet speak? concerning himself, or concerning some other?
ACT 8:35 And Philip having opened his mouth, and having begun from this scripture, announced good news to him - Jesus.
ACT 8:36 And as they were going along the way, they came upon some water. And the eunuch says, Behold, water; what prevents me to be immersed?
ACT 8:37 And Philip said, If you believe of your entire heart, it is allowed. And responding he said, I believe Jesus Christ to be the son of God.
ACT 8:38 And he urged the chariot to stop. And both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he immersed him.
ACT 8:39 And when they ascended from out of the water, spirit of the Lord seized Philip by force, and the eunuch saw him not any longer; for he went his way rejoicing.
ACT 8:40 And Philip was found in Azotus. And going through, he announced good news to all the cities until he came unto Caesarea.
ACT 9:1 And Saul still breathing intimidation and carnage against the disciples of the Lord, having come forward to the chief priest,
ACT 9:2 asked from him letters for Damascus to the synagogues, so that if any should be found being of the way, both men and women, having bound them he should lead them unto Jerusalem.
ACT 9:3 And in the going, it happened as he approached to Damascus. And suddenly flashed about him light from the heaven.
ACT 9:4 And having fallen upon the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
ACT 9:5 And he said, Who are you, O Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus, whom you persecute. It is hard to you to kick against spurs.
ACT 9:6 And trembling and distraught, he said, O Lord, what do you want me to do? And the Lord said to him, But rise up and enter into the city, and it will be told to you what you must do!
ACT 9:7 But the men journeying with him stood dumb, hearing indeed the voice, but viewing no one.
ACT 9:8 And Saul rose from the ground; and his eyes having been opened, he saw no one. And leading him by the hand, they brought him unto Damascus.
ACT 9:9 And he was three days not seeing, and he ate not nor drank.
ACT 9:10 And there was a certain disciple in Damascus, by name Ananias. And the Lord said to him in a vision, Ananias! And he said, Behold, it is I, O Lord.
ACT 9:11 And the Lord said to him, Rise up, go unto the street called, Straight, and seek in the house of Judas for one named Saul of Tarsus! for behold he prays,
ACT 9:12 and saw in a vision a man, by name Ananias entering and placing upon him a hand, so that he should gain sight.
ACT 9:13 And Ananias responded, O Lord, I have heard from many concerning this man, how many evils he did to your holy ones in Jerusalem.
ACT 9:14 And here he has authority by the chief priests to bind all the ones calling upon your name.
ACT 9:15 And the Lord said to him, Go! For this one is a utensil of choice to me, to bear my name before nations, and kings, and the sons of Israel.
ACT 9:16 For I will show plainly to him how much he must suffer for my name.
ACT 9:17 And Ananias went forth, and entered into the house; and having placed hands upon him, he said, O brother Saul, the Lord has sent me, the one appearing to you in the way by which you came, that you should gain sight, and should be filled of holy spirit.
ACT 9:18 And immediately there fell away from his eyes as it were scales. And he gained sight, and having risen up, he was immersed.
ACT 9:19 And taking nourishment, he strengthed. And Saul existed with the disciples in Damascus some days.
ACT 9:20 And immediately in the synagogues he was proclaiming the Christ, that this one is the son of God.
ACT 9:21 And all the ones hearing were amazed, and said; Is not this the one ravaging in Jerusalem the ones calling upon this name, and for this has come here, that he should lead them bound unto the chief priests?
ACT 9:22 And Saul the more was empowered, and confounded the Jews dwelling in Damascus, instructing that this is the Christ.
ACT 9:23 Now when a fit amount of days were fulfilled, the Jews advised to do away with him.
ACT 9:24 And their plot was made known to Saul. And they were closely watching the gates both day and night so as to do away with him.
ACT 9:25 And the disciples taking him by night, lowered him through the wall, letting him down in a small basket.
ACT 9:26 And Saul having arrived in Jerusalem, attempted to join the disciples. And all were afraid of him, not believing that he is a disciple.
ACT 9:27 But Barnabas, having taken him, brought him to the apostles, and described to them how in the way he saw the Lord, and that he spoke to him, and how in Damascus he spoke openly in the name of Jesus.
ACT 9:28 And he was with them entering into Jerusalem,
ACT 9:29 and speaking openly in the name of the Lord Jesus. And he spoke and debated with the Hellenists; but they attempted to do away with him.
ACT 9:30 And knowing, the brothers led him down unto Caesarea, and they sent him to Tarsus.
ACT 9:31 Indeed then the assemblies according to the whole of Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up and going in the fear of the Lord; and in the comfort of the holy spirit they were multiplied.
ACT 9:32 And it came to pass, Peter going through all places, went down also to the holy ones dwelling in Lydda.
ACT 9:33 And he found there a certain man, Aeneas by name, who was for eight years reclining upon a litter, who was disabled.
ACT 9:34 And Peter said to him, Aeneas, Jesus the Christ heals you. Rise up, and make your own bed! And immediately he rose up.
ACT 9:35 And all the ones dwelling Lydda and Saron saw him, who turned unto the Lord.
ACT 9:36 And in Joppa there was a certain disciple, by name Tabitha, which being interpreted is called Dorcas. She was full of good works and charity which she did.
ACT 9:37 And it came to pass in those days, she having weakened, died. And having bathed her, they put her in an upper room.
ACT 9:38 And Lydda being near Joppa, the disciples having heard that Peter is in it, sent two men to him, appealing to not be reluctant to go unto them.
ACT 9:39 And having risen up Peter came together with them. Whom having arrived, they led up to the upper room. And there stood beside him all the widows weeping, and displaying inner garments and cloaks, as many as Dorcas made while being with them.
ACT 9:40 And Peter having put all outside, having placed his knees, he prayed. And having turned to the body, he said, Tabitha, rise up! And she opened her eyes. And seeing Peter, she sat erect.
ACT 9:41 And having given to her his hand, he raised her up. And having called the holy ones and the widows, he presented her living.
ACT 9:42 And it became known throughout the whole of Joppa; and many believed upon the Lord.
ACT 9:43 And it came to pass that he abided a fit amount of days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.
ACT 10:1 And a certain man was there in Caesarea, by name Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort being called, Italic;
ACT 10:2 pious and fearing God with all his house, both performing much charity to the people, and beseeching God always.
ACT 10:3 He beheld in a vision openly about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God entering to him, and having said to him, Cornelius.
ACT 10:4 And gazing upon him, and becoming thrown into fear, he said, What is it, O Lord? And he said to him, Your prayers and your charity ascended for a memorial before God.
ACT 10:5 And now send forth men unto Joppa, and fetch Simon, who is called Peter.
ACT 10:6 This one lodges with a certain Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea. This one shall tell to you what is necessary for you to do.
ACT 10:7 And when the angel speaking to Cornelius departed, having called two of his servants, and a pious soldier of the ones attending constantly to him;
ACT 10:8 and having described to them all things, he sent them unto Joppa.
ACT 10:9 And the next day, as those are journeying, and approaching the city, Peter ascended upon the roof to pray around the sixth hour.
ACT 10:10 And he became hungry, and wanted to taste. And as those were making preparations, there fell upon him a change of state.
ACT 10:11 And he viewed the heaven being opened, and there descending unto him a certain item as a great piece of cloth, the four corners being tied, and being lowered unto the earth;
ACT 10:12 in which were all the four-footed creatures of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the reptiles, and the birds of the heaven.
ACT 10:13 And there came a voice to him, Rise up, Peter; sacrifice and eat!
ACT 10:14 And Peter said, By no means, O Lord; for at no time ate I anything common or unclean.
ACT 10:15 And a voice again a second time came to him, What God cleansed, you are not to make unclean!
ACT 10:16 And this happened unto three times. And again the item was taken up into the heaven.
ACT 10:17 And as Peter was perplexed within himself what ever the vision may be which he beheld, that behold, the men being sent from Cornelius having inquired about the house of Simon, stood at the vestibule.
