ACT 10:18 And calling out they inquired, Does Simon, the one being called Peter, lodge here?
ACT 10:19 And Peter pondering over the vision, the spirit said to him, Behold, three men seek you;
ACT 10:20 and having risen up, go down, and go with them, examining nothing! for I have sent them.
ACT 10:21 And Peter having gone down to the men, said, Behold, I am whom you seek. What is the reason for which you are at hand?
ACT 10:22 And they said, Cornelius a centurion, a just man, and one fearing God, and borne witness by the entire nation of the Jews, received a divine message by a holy angel to fetch you unto his house, and to hear words from you.
ACT 10:23 Then having invited them, he lodged them. And the next day Peter went forth with them, and certain ones of the brothers from Joppa went together with him.
ACT 10:24 And the next day they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his relatives and important friends.
ACT 10:25 And as it came to pass at Peter entering, having met him, Cornelius, having fallen at the feet, did obeisance.
ACT 10:26 But Peter raised him, saying, Rise up! I also myself am a man.
ACT 10:27 And accompanying him, he entered and found many were come together.
ACT 10:28 And he said to them, You know that it is unlawful for a man, a Jew, to join or approach a philistine. And God showed to me not to call a man common or unclean.
ACT 10:29 Therefore also indisputably I came, having been fetched. I inquire then to what matter you fetched me?
ACT 10:30 And Cornelius said, From four days ago until this hour I was fasting, and the ninth hour praying in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright attire.
ACT 10:31 And he says, Cornelius, your prayer was listened to, and your gifts of charity were remembered before God.
ACT 10:32 Send forth then unto Joppa, and call for Simon, who is called Peter! This one lodges in the house of Simon a tanner by the sea, who, having come, shall speak to you.
ACT 10:33 Immediately then I sent to you; and you did well having come. Now then, all we before God are at hand to hear all the things assigned to you by God.
ACT 10:34 And Peter having opened his mouth, said, In truth I am overtaken that God is not one who discriminates;
ACT 10:35 but in every nation fearing him, and practicing righteousness, it is acceptable to him.
ACT 10:36 The word which he sent to the sons of Israel, announcing good news, peace through Jesus Christ - this one is Lord of all.
ACT 10:37 You know the thing taking place in all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the immersion which John proclaimed;
ACT 10:38 Jesus, the one from Nazareth, how God anointed him in holy spirit and power; who went through benefiting and healing all the ones being overpowered by the devil; for God was with him.
ACT 10:39 And we are witnesses of all which he did both in the region of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom they did away with by hanging upon a tree.

ACT 10:46 For they heard them speaking languages, and magnifying God. Then Peter responded,
ACT 10:47 Shall water be able to be restrained to anyone of these to not be immersed, who received the holy spirit as also we?

ACT 12:1 And at that time Herod the king put upon the hands to afflict some of the ones of the assembly.
ACT 12:2 And he did away with James the brother of John by the sword.
ACT 12:3 And having seen that it is pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to seize also Peter, (and they were the days of the unleavened breads;)
ACT 12:4 whom also having laid hold of, he put into prison, having delivered him up to four parties of four soldiers to guard him, wanting after the passover to lead him to the people.
ACT 12:5 Then indeed Peter was given heed to in the prison. And there was intense prayer taking place by the assembly unto God for him.
ACT 12:6 And when Herod was about to lead him before them in that night, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, being bound with two chains; and guards before the door kept the prison.
ACT 12:7 And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by, and a light radiated in the building. And having struck the side of Peter, he roused him, saying, Rise up quickly! And the chains fell off of him from his hands.
ACT 12:8 And the angel said to him, Gird yourself and tie on your sandals! And he did so. And he says to him, Put on your cloak, and follow me!
ACT 12:9 And going forth, he followed him. And he knew not that it was true - the thing taking place by the angel; but he thought he was seeing a vision.
ACT 12:10 And having gone through a first guard and a second, they came unto the gate of iron, bearing into the city; which by itself opened to them. And having come forth, they went by one street; and immediately the angel separated from him.
ACT 12:11 And Peter having come to himself, said, Now I know truly that the Lord sent his angel, and rescued me from the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
ACT 12:12 And being fully conscious, he came unto the house of Mary the mother of John, of the one being called Mark; where there were a fit amount being gathered together and praying.
ACT 12:13 And Peter having knocked at the door of the vestibule, there came forward a maidservant to listen, by name Rhoda.
ACT 12:14 And having recognized the voice of Peter, from the joy she did not open the vestibule, but having ran in, reported Peter to be standing before the vestibule.
ACT 12:15 But the ones by her said, You are maniacal. But she contended obstinately thus to have been. And they said, It is his angel.
ACT 12:16 But Peter continued knocking. And having opened, they beheld him, and were amazed.
ACT 12:17 And having waved to them with the hand to be quiet, he described to them how the Lord led him from out of the prison. And he said, Report to James and to the brothers these things! And having come forth he went to another place.
ACT 12:18 And day having come, there was not a little disturbance among the soldiers, to what then became of Peter.
ACT 12:19 And Herod seeking him anxiously, and not finding, having questioned the guards, urged them to be taken away. And having gone down from Judea to Caesarea, he spent time.
ACT 12:20 And Herod was violently incensed with the Tyrians and Sidonians. But with one accord they were at hand with him, and having persuaded Blastus the one over the bedroom of the king, they asked peace; because their place was maintained by the royalty.
ACT 12:21 And Herod appointed a day, having put on royal attire, and having sat upon the rostrum, delivered a public address to them.
ACT 12:22 And the people sounded out, saying The voice of a god, and not a man.
ACT 12:23 And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he gave not the glory to God. And becoming worm-eaten, he expired.
ACT 12:24 But the word of God grew and multiplied.
ACT 12:25 And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, having fulfilled the service, having taken along also John, the one called Mark.
ACT 13:1 And there were some in Antioch, according to the assembly being there, prophets and teachers - both Barnabas, and Simeon being called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen, a companion of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
ACT 13:2 And of their officiating to the Lord, and fasting, the holy spirit said, Separate indeed to me Barnabas and Saul for the work which I have called them.
ACT 13:3 Then fasting and praying, and placing the hands upon them, they dismissed them.
ACT 13:4 These indeed then having been sent by the holy spirit, went down unto Seleucia; and from there they sailed away unto Cyprus.
ACT 13:5 And having come unto Salamis, they announced the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; and they also had John as an assistant.
ACT 13:6 And having gone through the island as far as Paphos, they found a certain magus, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus;
ACT 13:7 who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a discerning man. This one calling on Barnabas and Saul, sought anxiously to hear the word of God.
ACT 13:8 But Elymas the magus opposed them (for so is translated his name) seeking to turn aside the proconsul from the belief.
ACT 13:9 And Saul, the one also called Paul, being filled of holy spirit, and having gazed at him,
ACT 13:10 said, O one full of all treachery and all villainy, O son of the devil, O enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease turning aside the straight ways of the Lord?
ACT 13:11 And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time. And immediately there fell upon him a mistiness and darkness; and leading about he sought ones to guide him by hand.
ACT 13:12 Then the proconsul beholding the thing having taken place, believed, being overwhelmed over the teaching of the Lord.
ACT 13:13 And the ones around Paul having embarked from Paphos, they came unto Perga of Pamphylia. And John retreating from them, returned unto Jerusalem.
ACT 13:14 And they, having gone through from Perga, came into Antioch of Pisidia. And having entered into the synagogue on the day of the sabbath, they sat.
ACT 13:15 And after the reading of the law and of the prophets, the chiefs of the synagogue sent to them, saying, Men, brothers, if there is a word in you of comfort to the people, speak!
ACT 13:16 And Paul having risen up, and waving the hand, said, Men, Israelites, and ones fearing God, hearken!
ACT 13:17 The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people in the sojourn in the land of Egypt, and with a high arm led them out of it.
ACT 13:18 And about forty years time he bore with them in the wilderness.
ACT 13:19 And having demolished seven nations in the land of Canaan, he divided to them their land by lot.
ACT 13:20 And after these things, about four hundred and fifty years, he gave judges, until Samuel the prophet.
ACT 13:21 And from there they asked for a king. And God gave to them Saul son of Kis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin - for forty years.
ACT 13:22 And having removed him, he raised up to them David for king; to whom also having borne witness he said, I found David the one of Jesse, a man according to my heart, who shall do all my wants.
ACT 13:23 God from the seed of this one, according to the promise, raised up deliverance to Israel - a deliverer, Jesus.
ACT 13:24 Which John having publicly proclaimed before the presence of his entrance an immersion for repentance to all the people of Israel.
ACT 13:25 And as John was fulfilling the race, he said, Who do you suspect me to be? I am not he. But behold, comes after me, of whom I am not worthy to untie the sandal of his feet.
ACT 13:26 Men, brothers, sons of the race of Abraham, and the ones among you fearing God, to you the word of this deliverance was sent.
ACT 13:27 For the ones dwelling in Jerusalem, and their rulers, not having known this one, nor the voices of the prophets being read on every sabbath, they fulfilled them having judged him.
ACT 13:28 And not one reason for death having found, they asked Pilate to do away with him.
ACT 13:29 And as they finished all the things being written concerning him, lowering him from the tree, they put him into a tomb.
ACT 13:30 But God raised him from the dead -
ACT 13:31 who appeared for many days to the ones having gone up with him from Galilee unto Jerusalem, who are witnesses of him to the people.
ACT 13:32 And we announce you good news - the promise to the fathers taking place,
ACT 13:33 that this thing God has fulfilled to us their children, having raised up Jesus; and as in the second Psalm it has been written, You are my son, I today have engendered you.
ACT 13:34 And that he raised him from the dead, no longer to be about to return unto corruption, thus he has spoken that, I will give to you the trustworthy sacred things of David.
ACT 13:35 Wherefore also in another he says, You shall not give your sacred one to see corruption.
ACT 13:36 For David indeed having assisted his own generation by the counsel of God, went to sleep, and was added to his fathers, and saw corruption.
ACT 13:37 But the one whom God raised, did not see corruption.
ACT 13:38 Let it be made known then to you men, brothers, that through this one a release of sins is announced to you.
ACT 13:39 And from all things of which you were not able in the law of Moses to be justified, in this one every one believing is justified.
ACT 13:40 Take heed then, that it should not come upon you - the thing being spoken by the prophets,
ACT 13:41 Behold, O despisers, and wonder, and vanish! For a work I work during your days, which in no way should you believe if one should tell you in detail.
ACT 13:42 And exiting from out of the synagogue of the Jews, the nations appealed to them in the time between the sabbath to speak to them these things.
ACT 13:43 And the synagogue being dismissed, many of the Jews and worshiping converts followed Paul and Barnabas, who speaking, persuaded them to continue in the favor of God.
ACT 13:44 And on the coming sabbath, nearly all the city gathered to hear the word of God.
ACT 13:45 But the Jews beholding the multitudes, were filled with jealousy, and spoke against the things being spoken by Paul, disputing and blaspheming.
ACT 13:46 But speaking openly, Paul and Barnabas said, To you it was important first for the word of God to be spoken. But since you thrust it away, and do not judge yourselves worthy of eternal life, behold, we turn unto the nations.
ACT 13:47 For thus the Lord has given charge to us, saying, I have put you for a light of nations, for you to be for deliverance unto the end of the earth.
ACT 13:48 And hearing, the nations rejoiced, and glorified the word of the Lord. And as many as were being arranged for life eternal believed.
ACT 13:49 And the word of the Lord was carried through the entire region.
ACT 13:50 But the Jews instigated the worshiping women, and the decent and the foremost men of the city, and roused up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them from their borders.
ACT 13:51 And they having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, came unto Iconium.
ACT 13:52 And the disciples were filled with joy and holy spirit.
ACT 14:1 And it came to pass in Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and spoke thus so as for a great multitude of both Jews and Hellenists to believe.
ACT 14:2 But the Jews resisting persuasion, roused up and afflicted the souls of the ones of nations against the brothers.
ACT 14:3 Then they spent a fit time speaking openly in the Lord, in the bearing witness to the word of his favor, granting signs and miracles to take place through their hands.
ACT 14:4 And the multitude of the city was split; and some were with the Jews, and some with the apostles.
ACT 14:5 And as there became a movement by the nations, and also of Jews with their rulers, to insult and to stone them,
ACT 14:6 being fully conscious, they took refuge in the cities of Lycaonia - Lystra and Derbe, and the place round about.
ACT 14:7 And there they were announcing good news.
ACT 14:8 And a certain man in Lystra, disabled in the feet, sat; one being lame from the belly of his mother, who at no time walked.
ACT 14:9 This one heard Paul speaking; who having gazed upon him, and seeing that he had belief to be delivered,
ACT 14:10 said with a great voice, Rise upon your feet straight! And he leaped up and walked.
ACT 14:11 And the multitudes beholding what Paul did, lifted up their voice in Lycaonian, saying, The gods having become like men are come down to us.
ACT 14:12 And they called Barnabas - Dia, and Paul - Hermes, since he was the one leading by word.
ACT 14:13 And the priest of Dia, being before their city, having brought bulls and garlands unto the vestibules, with the multitudes, wanted to sacrifice.
ACT 14:14 And having heard, the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having torn their garments, rushed into the multitude, crying,
ACT 14:15 and saying, Men, why do you do these things? Even we are men having the same passions as you, announcing good news - for you to turn from these vanities unto the living God, who made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all the things in them;
ACT 14:16 who in the generations passing by allowed all the nations to go by their ways.
ACT 14:17 Though indeed not without his own witness did he allow it, but was doing good from heaven to you - giving rains, and seasons bearing fruit, filling up provision and gladness of our hearts.
ACT 14:18 And saying these things, the multitudes hardly ceased to not sacrifice to them.
ACT 14:19 And Jews came from Antioch and Iconium. And having persuaded the multitudes, and having stoned Paul, they dragged him outside the city thinking him to have died.
ACT 14:20 But the disciples having encircled him, having risen up, he entered into the city. And the next day he went forth with Barnabas unto Derbe.
ACT 14:21 And having announced good news in that city, and having discipled a fit amount, they returned unto Lystra, and Iconium, and Antioch,
ACT 14:22 staying up the souls of the disciples, appealing to them to adhere to the belief, and saying that, By many afflictions we must enter into the kingdom of God.
ACT 14:23 And having hand picked for them elders in every assembly, having prayed with fastings, they placed them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
ACT 14:24 And having gone through Pisidia, they came unto Pamphylia.
ACT 14:25 And having spoken the word in Perga, they went down unto Attalia.
ACT 14:26 And from there they sailed away unto Antioch, from where they were delivered up to the favor of God for the work which they fulfilled.
ACT 14:27 And having arrived, and having gathered together the assembly, they announced as much as God did with them, and that he opened to the nations a door of belief.
ACT 14:28 And they spent time there, not a little, with the disciples.
ACT 15:1 And certain ones having come down from Judea taught the brothers, saying that, If you should not be circumcised in the custom of Moses, you are not able to be delivered.
ACT 15:2 A faction then having taken place, and not a small inquiry with Paul and Barnabas with them, they ordered Paul and Barnabas to ascend, and certain others of them, to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem concerning this matter.
ACT 15:3 They then indeed having been sent forward by the assembly, went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling in detail the turning of the nations. And they caused great joy to all the brothers.
ACT 15:4 And having come unto Jerusalem, they were gladly received by the assembly, and of the apostles and the elders, and they announced as much as God did with them.
ACT 15:5 And there rose up some of the ones from the sect of the believing Pharisees, saying that, It is necessary to circumcise them, also to exhort them to give heed to the law of Moses.
ACT 15:6 And there were gathered together the apostles and the elders to know concerning this matter.
ACT 15:7 And much debating having taken place, Peter having risen up, said to them, Men, brothers, you know that from days of old God among us chose by my mouth for the nations to hear the word of the good news, and to believe.
ACT 15:8 And the knower of hearts - God, he bore witness to them, giving to them the holy spirit as also to us;
ACT 15:9 and in nothing discriminating between us and even them, by the belief having cleansed their hearts.
ACT 15:10 Now then why test God, to place a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
ACT 15:11 But by the favor of the Lord Jesus Christ we believe to be delivered in which manner as those.
ACT 15:12 And all the multitude was quiet, and they heard Barnabas and Paul describing as much as God did by signs and miracles among the nations through them.
ACT 15:13 And after their quieting, James responded saying, Men, brothers, hear me!
ACT 15:14 Simeon described as how first God visited to take from out of nations a people for his name.
ACT 15:15 And with this the words of the prophets agreed; as it has been written,
ACT 15:16 After these things I will return, and will rebuild the tent of David, the one fallen; and the things having been razed of it I will rebuild, and I will re-erect it.
ACT 15:17 So that the remnants of men shall seek after the Lord, and all the nations upon which my name has been called upon by them, says the Lord - the one doing all these things.
ACT 15:18 To God all his works are known from the eon.
ACT 15:19 Therefore I judge to not cause trouble to the ones from the nations turning towards God;
ACT 15:20 but write to them to be at a distance from the pollution of idols, and harlotry, and the thing strangled, and blood.
ACT 15:21 For Moses, from generations of old has the ones in every city proclaiming him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath.
ACT 15:22 Then it seemed good to the apostles and to the elders, with the entire assembly, to send forth chosen men of them unto Antioch with Paul and Barnabas - Judas the one called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers,
ACT 15:23 having written by their hand thus; The apostles, and the elders, and the brothers, to the ones in Antioch, and Syria, and Cilicia. To the brothers of the nations, rejoice!
ACT 15:24 Since we heard that some from us having come forth disturbed you in words, subverting your souls, saying to be circumcised and to give heed to the law - to whom we did not give orders.
ACT 15:25 It seemed good to us, taking place with one accord, choosing men to send to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
ACT 15:26 men delivering up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT 15:27 We have sent then Judas and Silas, and they by word are reporting the same things.
ACT 15:28 For it seemed good to the holy spirit, and to us, to place upon you no more load except these things of necessity;
ACT 15:29 to be at a distance of things sacrificed to idols, and of blood, and of what is strangled, and of harlotry; of which keeping yourselves you do good. Stay firm!
ACT 15:30 The ones indeed then being dismissed, came unto Antioch. And having gathered together the multitude, they gave over the letter.
ACT 15:31 And having read, they rejoiced over the exhortation.
ACT 15:32 And Judas and Silas, also themselves being prophets, through much communication, exhorted the brothers, and stayed them.
ACT 15:33 And having spent time, they were dismissed with peace from the brothers to the apostles.
ACT 15:34 And it seemed good to Silas to remain himself.
ACT 15:35 And Paul and Barnabas spent time in Antioch, teaching and announcing good news - the word of the Lord with also many others.
ACT 15:36 And after some days Paul said to Barnabas, Returning, we should indeed visit our brothers in every city in which we announced the word of the Lord, to see how they suffice.
ACT 15:37 And Barnabas planned to take along John, the one being called Mark.
ACT 15:38 But Paul thought it worthy that the one separating from them from Pamphylia, and not coming together with them for the work, to not take this one along.
ACT 15:39 There took place then a fit of temper so that they separated from one another. And Barnabas having taken Mark with himself, sailed across unto Cyprus;
ACT 15:40 and Paul having chosen Silas, went forth, having been delivered up to the favor of God by the brothers.
ACT 15:41 And he went through Syria and Cilicia, staying up the assemblies.
ACT 16:1 And he arrived at Derbe and Lystra. And behold, a certain disciple was there, by name Timothy, son of a certain believing Jewish woman, but the father was a Greek,
ACT 16:2 who was borne witness to by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.
ACT 16:3 Paul wanted this one to go forth with him. And having taken he circumcised him on account of the Jews being in those places, for they all knew his father, that he was a Greek.
ACT 16:4 And as they traveled the cities, they delivered up to them the decrees being adjudged to keep, by the apostles and the elders in Jerusalem.
ACT 16:5 Then indeed the assemblies were solidified in the belief, and abounded in number by day.
ACT 16:6 And having gone through the Phrygian, and the Galacian region, they were restrained by the holy spirit to speak the word in Asia.
ACT 16:7 Having come down to Mysia, they attempted to go towards Bithynia. And the spirit did not allow them.
ACT 16:8 And going by Mysia, they went down unto Troas.
ACT 16:9 And a vision by the night appeared to Paul; a certain man of Macedonia was standing, appealing to him, and saying, Having passed over into Macedonia, help us!
ACT 16:10 And as he beheld the vision, immediately we sought to go forth into Macedonia, being instructed that the Lord called on us to announce good news to them.
ACT 16:11 Having embarked then from Troas, we ran direct unto Samothrace, and the following day to Neapolis;
ACT 16:12 and from there to Philippi, which is a foremost city of the portion of Macedonia - a colony. And we were in this city spending time some days.
ACT 16:13 And on the day of the sabbaths we went forth outside the city by a river, of which we thought prayer to be; and having sat down we spoke to the women having gathered together.
ACT 16:14 And a certain woman, by name Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God, was listening; of whom the Lord opened wide her heart to take heed to the things being spoken by Paul.
ACT 16:15 And as she was being immersed, and her house, she appealed, saying, If you adjudge me to be trustworthy to the Lord, having entered into my house, abide! And she pressured us.
ACT 16:16 And it came to pass of our going unto prayer, a certain maidservant having a spirit of python met us, which furnished much work to her masters divining oracles.
ACT 16:17 She having followed closely after Paul and us, cried out saying, These men are servants of God the highest, who shall announce to us the way of deliverance.
ACT 16:18 And this she did for many days. And Paul being worked up, and having turned, said to the spirit, I summon to you in the name of Jesus Christ to come forth from her. And it came forth the same hour.
ACT 16:19 And her masters seeing that the hope of their work went forth, having taken hold of Paul and Silas, drew them into the market unto the rulers.
ACT 16:20 And leading them forward to the commandants, they said, These men disturb our city, being Jews,
ACT 16:21 and announce customs which are not allowed for us to welcome, nor to do, being Romans.
ACT 16:22 And rose up together the multitude against them. And the commandants having torn off their garments, bid to beat them with a rod.
ACT 16:23 And having placed upon them many strokes, they threw them into prison, exhorting the jailer to keep them safely.
ACT 16:24 Who having received such exhortation, cast them in the inner prison, and safeguarded their feet in the wood stocks.
ACT 16:25 And towards midnight, Paul and Silas were praying, singing praise to God; and the prisoners heeded them.
ACT 16:26 And suddenly a great earthquake took place, so as to shake the foundations of the jail. And immediately all the doors were opened, and all the bonds were unfastened.
ACT 16:27 And the jailer being awakened out of sleep, and beholding the doors of the prison being open, unsheathed his sword, being about to do away with himself, thinking the prisoners to have fled.
ACT 16:28 And Paul spoke out with a great voice, saying, You should not exact hurt on yourself; for we are all together here.
ACT 16:29 And asking for lights, he rushed in, and being trembling, fell before Paul and Silas.
ACT 16:30 And having led them outside, he said, Masters, what is necessary for me to do that I should be delivered?
ACT 16:31 And they said, Believe upon the Lord Jesus Christ, and you shall be delivered, you and your house.
ACT 16:32 And they spoke to him the word of the Lord, and to all the ones in his house.
ACT 16:33 And having taken them in that hour of the night, he bathed them from the strokes; and he was immersed, and all his family, immediately.
ACT 16:34 And having led them into his house, he placed a table, and exulted with his whole family, having believed in God.
ACT 16:35 And day having come the commandants of the lictors sent, saying, Release those men!
ACT 16:36 And the jailer reported these words to Paul, that, The commandants have sent that you be released. Now then having gone forth, go in peace!
ACT 16:37 But Paul said to them, Having flayed us in public, uncondemned men, being Romans, they cast us into prison; and now in private they cast us out? For no, but having come let them lead us out themselves!
ACT 16:38 And the lictors announced to the commandants these words. And they feared, having heard that they are Romans.
ACT 16:39 And having come, they appealed to them, and having led them out, asked them to go forth out of the city.
ACT 16:40 And having gone forth from out of the prison, they entered to Lydia. And having seen the brothers, they comforted them, and they went forth.
ACT 17:1 And having traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came unto Thessalonica, where there was the synagogue of the Jews.
ACT 17:2 And according to the thing accustomed to Paul, he entered to them, and for three sabbaths reasoned with them from the scriptures,
ACT 17:3 opening and pointing out, that it was a must for the Christ to suffer, and to be raised up from the dead; and that this one is the Christ - Jesus, whom I announce to you.
ACT 17:4 And some of them yielded and associated with Paul and Silas; both of the worshiping Greeks a great multitude, and of the foremost women not a few.
ACT 17:5 And having taken up with the Jews resisting persuasion of the advocates, certain wicked men, and having raised a mob, made a disruption in the city. And having stood by the house of Jason, they sought to lead them unto the people.
ACT 17:6 But not having found them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers unto the rulers of the city, yelling that, The ones overthrowing the inhabitable world are these, and they are at hand here;
ACT 17:7 whom Jason has welcomed. And these all act contrary of the decrees of Caesar, saying another to be king - Jesus.
ACT 17:8 And the multitude and the rulers of the city were disturbed hearing these things.
ACT 17:9 And having taken a fit security from Jason, and the rest, they released them.
ACT 17:10 And the brothers immediately by the night sent forth both Paul and Silas unto Berea. Who, being come, went into the synagogue of the Jews.
ACT 17:11 And these were more well-born - of the others. of the ones in Thessalonica, who received the word with all eagerness, by the day examining the scriptures, if these held such things.
ACT 17:12 Many indeed then from them believed; and of the decent Greek women, and men, there were not a few.
ACT 17:13 But when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that also in Berea the word of God was announced by Paul, they came also shaking up the multitudes.
ACT 17:14 And immediately then the brothers sent Paul to go as by the sea. But both Silas and Timothy remained behind there.
ACT 17:15 And the ones standing by Paul led him unto Athens. And receiving a command to Silas and Timothy, that as quickly as possible they should come to him, they exited.
ACT 17:16 But in Athens, Paul looking out for them, was provoked in his spirit, in his viewing the city being full of idols.
ACT 17:17 He reasoned indeed then in the synagogue with the Jews, and the ones worshiping, and in the market every day with the ones coming by.
ACT 17:18 And some of the Epicureans, and of the Stoics, philosophers, engaged with him. And some said, What ever does this seed picker want to say? And some said, He seems to be an announcer of strange demons - because he announced good news of Jesus and the resurrection to them.
ACT 17:19 And taking hold of him, they led him unto the Areopagus, saying, Are we able to know what this new teaching being spoken by you is?
ACT 17:20 For some things being strange you insert into our hearing. We want then to know what ever these things will to be.
ACT 17:21 ( And all Athenians, and the emigrating strangers, spend their opportune time in nothing else than to tell and to hear something newer.)
ACT 17:22 And Paul having stood in the middle of the Areopagus, said, Men, Athenians, I view you in all things as ones reverent of gods.
ACT 17:23 For going through, and contemplating your objects of worship, I found also a shrine in which had been inscribed, To an unknown God. Whom then not knowing you are pious towards, this one I announce to you.
ACT 17:24 The God making the world and all the things in it, this one being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in handmade temples;
ACT 17:25 nor by the hands of men attending is there any feeling any want, himself giving to all life and breath, and all things;
ACT 17:26 and made of one blood every nation of men to dwell upon all the face of the earth, (having confirmed beforehand times and the boundaries of their dwelling,)
ACT 17:27 to seek the Lord, if then perhaps they might grope after him, and might find him, though indeed he being not far from each one of us.
ACT 17:28 For in him we live, and move, and are; as also some of the poets among you have said, For of him we are also a family.
ACT 17:29 Being a family then of God, we ought not to think gold, or silver, or stone, (an imprint of a craft, and thinking of man,) to be like the divine?
ACT 17:30 Indeed then the times of ignorance God having overlooked; at present exhorts all men everywhere to repent.
ACT 17:31 For he set a day, in which he is about to judge the world in righteousness by a man in whom he confirmed; having furnished belief to all, having raised him from the dead.
ACT 17:32 And hearing a resurrection of the dead, some taunted; and some said, We will hear you again concerning this.
ACT 17:33 And thus Paul came forth from out of the midst of them.
ACT 17:34 But some men cleaving to him believed. Among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman, by name Damaris, and others with them.
ACT 18:1 And after these things Paul having separated from Athens, came unto Corinth.
ACT 18:2 And having found a certain Jew, by name Aquila, of Pontus by race, recently come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife; (because Claudius ordered all the Jews to separate from Rome;) he came forward to them.
ACT 18:3 And because of being the same trade, he stayed with them, and worked; for they were tentmakers in the craft.
ACT 18:4 And he reasoned in the synagogue according to every sabbath, to persuade both Jews and Greeks.
ACT 18:5 And when both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was constrained in the spirit, testifying the Christ to the Jews - Jesus.
ACT 18:6 And they being rebellious and blaspheming, having shaken off his garments, said to them, Your blood be upon your head; I am clean. From now on I shall go unto the nations.
ACT 18:7 And having crossed over from there, he came unto the house of a certain one, by name Justus, who worshiped God, of whose house was adjoining the synagogue.
ACT 18:8 But Crispus, the chief of the synagogue trusted in the Lord with his entire house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were immersed.
ACT 18:9 And the Lord said by a vision at night to Paul, Fear not, but speak, and do not keep silent!
ACT 18:10 For I am with you, and no one shall attack you to inflict evil on you; for there are many people with me in this city.
ACT 18:11 And he stayed a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
ACT 18:12 And Gallio being proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up against Paul with one accord, and led him unto the rostrum,
ACT 18:13 saying that, By this law he dissuades men to worship God.
ACT 18:14 And Paul being about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If indeed then it was some offence or evil villainy, O Jews, on this account I would have endured you;
ACT 18:15 but if the matter is concerning a word and names and a law of yours, you shall see to it yourselves; for I do not want to be a judge of these things.
ACT 18:16 And he drove them away from the rostrum.
ACT 18:17 And all the Greeks taking hold of Sosthenes, the chief of the synagogue, beat him in front of the rostrum. And to Gallio he cared not one thing of these.
ACT 18:18 But Paul, yet having remained a fit amount of days, having dismissed the brothers, sailed across unto Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea - for he had a vow.
ACT 18:19 And he arrived in Ephesus, and those he left behind there. But he himself having entered into the synagogue, reasoned with the Jews.
ACT 18:20 And being asked of them for more time to stay with them, he did not nod assent;
ACT 18:21 but sent them away, having said, It is necessary for me assuredly with the coming holiday to observe it in Jerusalem; but again I will return to you, God willing. And he embarked from Ephesus.
ACT 18:22 And having gone down unto Caesarea, having ascended, and having greeted the assembly, he went down to Antioch.
ACT 18:23 And having spent some time, he went forth, going through the Galatian and Phrygian region in order, staying up all the disciples.
ACT 18:24 And a certain Jew, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by race, a learned man, arrived in Ephesus, being mighty in the scriptures.
ACT 18:25 This one was being instructed in the way of the Lord; and bubbling in the spirit, he spoke and he taught exactly the things concerning the Lord, having knowledge of only the immersion of John.
ACT 18:26 This one also began to speak openly in the synagogue. And Aquila and Priscilla having heard him, took him to themselves, and more exactly expounded to him the way of God.
ACT 18:27 And he wanting to go through into Achaia, the brothers encouraging wrote to the disciples to gladly receive him; who having arrived engaged much with the ones believing through favor.
ACT 18:28 For intensely with the Jews he thoroughly confuted in public, displaying through the scriptures Jesus to be the Christ.
ACT 19:1 And it came to pass, in the fact of Apollos being in Corinth, Paul having gone through the remote parts, came unto Ephesus. And having found certain disciples,
ACT 19:2 he said to them, Did you receive holy spirit having believed? And they said to him, Not even if there is holy spirit have we heard.
ACT 19:3 And he said to them, By what then were you immersed? And they said, By the immersion of John.
ACT 19:4 And Paul said, John indeed immersed with an immersion of repentance, saying to the people, that they should believe on the one coming after him, that is to say in Jesus the Christ.
ACT 19:5 And having heard, they were immersed in the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 19:6 And Paul having put hands upon them, the holy spirit came upon them, both speaking languages and prophesying.
ACT 19:7 And all the men were about twelve.
ACT 19:8 And having entered into the synagogue, he spoke openly for three months, reasoning and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
ACT 19:9 But when some were hardened, and resisted persuasion, speaking evil of the way before the multitude, having left from them, he separated the disciples, by day reasoning in the school of a certain Tyrannus.
ACT 19:10 And this took place for two years, so that all the ones dwelling Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
ACT 19:11 And works of power, not happening by chance, God did through the hands of Paul;
ACT 19:12 so that even unto the ones being invalid scarfs or aprons from his flesh were borne, and the diseases were rid from them, and the evil spirits went forth from them.
ACT 19:13 But certain ones of the traveling Jewish exorcists attempted to name the name of the Lord Jesus against the ones having evil spirits, saying, We bind you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims!
ACT 19:14 And there were certain ones, seven sons of Sceva a Jew a chief priest, doing this.
ACT 19:15 And responding the evil spirit said, Jesus I know, and Paul I have knowledge of; but you, who are you?
ACT 19:16 And the man springing upon them, in whom was the evil spirit, and having dominated them, prevailed against them, so that naked and wounded they fled from out of that house.
ACT 19:17 And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, dwelling in Ephesus. And fear fell upon all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
ACT 19:18 And many of the ones believing came, acknowledging and announcing their actions.
ACT 19:19 And a fit amount of the ones practicing useless works found it advantageous to incinerate the books before all. And they joined in tallying their value, and found it to be five myriads of silver.
ACT 19:20 Thus with might the word of the Lord grew and strengthened.
ACT 19:21 And when these things were fulfilled, Paul set in the spirit, having gone through Macedonia and Achaia, to go unto Jerusalem, having said that, After my being there, it is necessary for me also to see Rome.
ACT 19:22 And having sent unto Macedonia two of the ones serving to him, Timothy and Erastus, he waited for a time in Asia.
ACT 19:23 And came to pass according to that time not a little disturbance concerning the way.
ACT 19:24 For Demetrius, a certain one by name, a silversmith, making temples of silver of Artemis, furnished to the craftsmen not a little work;
ACT 19:25 whom gathering together, and the ones concerning such workers, said, Men, you know that from out of this work is our means.
ACT 19:26 And you view and hear, that not only Ephesus, but nearly all Asia, this Paul, having persuaded, changed over a fit multitude, saying that the things being made by hands are not gods.
ACT 19:27 And not only this, it exposes danger to us, lest the part come into disrepute, but also the temple of the great goddess Artemis is considered as nothing, and her magnificence also is about to be lowered, which all Asia and the habitable world worship.
ACT 19:28 And having heard, and having become full of rage, they cried out, saying, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.
ACT 19:29 And the entire city was filled of confusion. And they advanced with one accord unto the theater, having seized by force Gaius and Aristarcus, Macedonian traveling companions of Paul.
ACT 19:30 And Paul wanting to enter unto the people, the disciples did not allow him.
ACT 19:31 And certain ones also of the Asiarchs, being friends with him, sending to him, appealed for him to not put himself in the theater.
ACT 19:32 Others therefore one thing and some another were crying out; for the assembly was in tumult; and most did not know for what reason they had come together.
ACT 19:33 And from the multitude they forced Alexander, of the Jews burgeoning him forth. But Alexander, having waved his hand, wanted to make a defense to the people.
ACT 19:34 And recognizing that he is a Jew, there became one voice from all, for about two hours crying out, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.
ACT 19:35 And the scribe having restrained the multitude, says, Men, Ephesians, for what man is there who does not know the city of the Ephesians being a devotee of the great goddess Artemis, even of the one sent by Zeus?
ACT 19:36 Indisputable then these things being, it is necessary for you to be restrained, and in nothing to act precipitously.
ACT 19:37 For you brought these men, who are neither sacrilegious, nor blasphemous of your god.
ACT 19:38 If indeed then Demetrius, and the craftsmen with him have a matter against anyone, let advocates be led, and there are procounsuls - let them accuse one another!
ACT 19:39 But if anything concerning other matters you anxiously seek, it shall be explained in the lawful assembly.
ACT 19:40 For also we are exposed to danger to be accused of insurrection concerning today, with no one reason existing concerning which we shall be able to render a word for this tumult.
ACT 19:41 And these things having said, he dismissed the assembly.
ACT 20:1 And after the tumult ceased, Paul having called the disciples, and saluting, went forth to go into Macedonia.
ACT 20:2 And having gone through those parts, and comforting them by much communication, he came unto Greece.
ACT 20:3 And having spent three months, with a plot having been made against him by the Jews, being about to embark unto Syria, he became of the opinion to return through Macedonia.
ACT 20:4 And there accompanied him as far as Asia Sopator a Berean; and of Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
ACT 20:5 These having gone forward waited for us in Troas.
ACT 20:6 And we sailed across, after the days of the unleavened breads, from Philippi, and came to them in Troas unto five days; where we spent seven days.
ACT 20:7 And on day one of the sabbaths, the disciples having been gathered to break bread, Paul reasoned with them, being about to exit the next day; and he extended the word until midnight.
ACT 20:8 And there were a fit amount of lamps in the upper room, where we were gathered together.
ACT 20:9 And there was sitting down a certain young one, by name Eutychus, by the window, being sunk in a deep sleep. And with Paul reasoning for a long time, having sunken from the sleep, he fell from the third level to below, and was lifted up dead.
ACT 20:10 And having descended, Paul fell upon him, and having wrapped around him, said, Do not make a disruption, for his life is in him.
ACT 20:11 And having ascended, and having broken bread, and having tasted, and for a fit time consorting until daylight, thus he went forth.
ACT 20:12 And they brought the child alive, and were comforted not moderately.
ACT 20:13 And we having gone forth unto the boat, embarked unto Assos, from there being about to take up Paul. For so it was having been set in order, himself being about to go on foot.
ACT 20:14 And when he united with us at Assos, having taken him in, we came unto Mitylene.
ACT 20:15 And from there sailing away, on the following day we arrived towards Chios; and in the other day we set aside unto Samos, and abided in Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
ACT 20:16 For Paul decided to sail by Ephesus, so that it should not happen for him to spend time in Asia. For he hastened, if it was possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
ACT 20:17 And from Miletus, having sent to Ephesus, he called for the elders of the assembly.
ACT 20:18 And when they were come to him, he said to them, You know, from the first day of which I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,
ACT 20:19 serving to the Lord with all humility, and many tears, and tests, of the ones coming to pass to me in the plots of the Jews;
ACT 20:20 how I kept back nothing of the things advantageous unto you, so as to not announce it to you, and to teach you in public, and by houses,
ACT 20:21 testifying both to Jews, and Greeks, the thing for God - repentance and belief in our Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT 20:22 And now, behold, I being bound in the spirit go unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things in it meeting up with me.
ACT 20:23 Except that the holy spirit in every city testifies, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.
ACT 20:24 But I make account of nothing, nor do I hold my life esteemed to myself, as to finish my race with joy, and the service which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the good news of the favor of God.
ACT 20:25 And now, behold, I know that no longer shall you all see my face, among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom of God.
ACT 20:26 Therefore I testify to you in today's day, that I am clean from the blood of all.
ACT 20:27 For I did not keep back to announce to you all the counsel of God.
ACT 20:28 Take heed then to yourselves, and to all the flock, in which the holy spirit placed you as overseers, to tend the assembly of God, which he procured through his own blood!
ACT 20:29 For I know this, that grievous wolves shall enter after my departure unto you, not sparing the flock.
ACT 20:30 And from out of your own selves shall rise up men speaking things being perverted, to draw away the disciples after them.
ACT 20:31 Therefore be vigilant! Remembering that for a space of three years, night and day, I ceased not with tears admonishing each one.
ACT 20:32 And at present I point you out, brothers, to God, and to the word of his favor, to the thing being able to build up, and to give to you an inheritance among all the ones having been sanctified.
ACT 20:33 I desired of no one silver or gold or clothes.
ACT 20:34 You know yourselves, that my needs, and the ones being with me, these hands assisted.
ACT 20:35 All things I plainly showed to you, that so tiring it is necessary to assist the ones being weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
ACT 20:36 And these things having said, having set his knees with them all, he prayed.
ACT 20:37 And there became a fit amount of weeping by all. And falling upon the neck of Paul they kissed him,
ACT 20:38 being grieved especially over the word which he had said, that no longer are they about to view his face. And they sent him unto the boat.
ACT 21:1 And when it came to pass, we embarked, having drawn away from them, having run direct, we came unto Cos, and the next day unto Rhodes, and from there unto Patara.
ACT 21:2 And having found a boat passing through unto Phoenicia, having set foot on it, we embarked.
ACT 21:3 And Cyprus having appeared, and having left it on the left, we sailed unto Syria, and led down unto Tyre; for at that place the boat was unloading the cargo.
ACT 21:4 And having discovered the disciples, (we remained there seven days,) who said to Paul through the spirit, to not ascend unto Jerusalem.
ACT 21:5 But when it happened we accomplished the days, having gone forth we went, with all the women and children escorting us, as far as outside the city. And setting the knees upon the shore, we prayed.
ACT 21:6 And having saluted one another, we mounted into the boat; and those returned to their own.
ACT 21:7 And we having concluded the voyage from Tyre, arrived at Ptolemais. And having saluted the brothers, we abode one day with them.
ACT 21:8 And the next day, the ones around Paul having gone forth, they came unto Caesarea. And having entered into the house of Philip the Evangelist, being from out of the seven, we stayed with him.
ACT 21:9 And to this man were four virgin daughters, who prophesied.
ACT 21:10 And of our remaining many days, there came down a certain one from Judea, a prophet, by name Agabus.
ACT 21:11 And having come to us, and having taken the belt of Paul, and having bound his hands and feet, he said, Thus says the holy spirit, The man of which is this belt, so shall the Jews in Jerusalem bind, and shall deliver him up into the hands of the nations.
ACT 21:12 And when we heard these things, both we and the ones of that place appealed for him to not ascend unto Jerusalem.
ACT 21:13 And Paul responded, Why do you cause weeping and breaking of my heart? for I not only to be bound, but also readily hold to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 21:14 And he not being persuaded, we were still, having said, The will of the Lord, let it be!
ACT 21:15 And after these days, having packed up, we ascended unto Jerusalem.
ACT 21:16 And came together also some of the disciples from Caesarea with us, bringing the one with whom we should lodge, a certain Mnason a Cypriot, a disciple of old.
ACT 21:17 And of our being in Jerusalem, the brothers gladly received us.
ACT 21:18 And the following day Paul enters with us to James; and all the elders arrived.
ACT 21:19 And having greeted them, he described according to each one what God did among the nations through his service.
ACT 21:20 And they having heard, glorified the Lord, and said to him, You view, O brother, how many myriads of believing Jews there are, and all being zealous of the law.
ACT 21:21 And they instruct concerning you that you teach all the Jews among the nations defection from Moses, saying not to circumcise their children, nor to walk in the customs.
ACT 21:22 What then is it? Assuredly it is necessary for a multitude to come together, for they shall hear that you have come.
ACT 21:23 This then do what we tell you! There are with us four men having a vow upon themselves;
ACT 21:24 taking these, be purified with them, and spend for them, that they may shave the head! And all should know that of which they have been instructed concerning you is nothing; but you conform to keeping the law even yourself.
ACT 21:25 But concerning the ones believing of the nations, we wrote, judging them to give heed to no such thing, except to keep themselves from both that sacrificed to idols, and the blood, and what is strangled, and harlotry.
ACT 21:26 Then Paul, having taken the men the next day, with them having been purified, he entered into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of the purification, while the offering was offered for each one of them.
ACT 21:27 And when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia, having seen him in the temple, caused a tumult with all the multitude, and put hands upon him,
ACT 21:28 crying out, Men, Israelites, help! This is the man teaching all everywhere against the people and the law and this place. Still indeed even Greeks he brings into the temple, and makes this holy place unclean.
ACT 21:29 (For they were seeing Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, whom they thought that Paul brought into the temple.)
ACT 21:30 And the entire city was shaken indeed, and there became a stampede of people. And having taken hold of Paul, they drew him outside of the temple, and immediately locked the doors.
ACT 21:31 And seeking to kill him, a report ascended to the commander of the cohort, that all Jerusalem was in tumult.
ACT 21:32 Who immediately, having taken soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them. And the ones beholding the commander and the soldiers, ceased beating Paul.
ACT 21:33 And having approached, the commander took hold of him, and bid him to be tied with two chains, and to inquire about who he may be, and what he is doing.
ACT 21:34 And others to another were yelling in the multitude. And not being able to know safely because of the tumult, he bid them to lead him unto the camp.
ACT 21:35 And when he was at the stairs, it happened that he was borne by the soldiers because of the force of the multitude.
ACT 21:36 For the multitude of the people followed, crying out, Take him away!
ACT 21:37 And being about to be brought into the camp, Paul says to the commander, Is it allowed for me to speak to you? And he said, You know Greek?
ACT 21:38 Are you not then the Egyptian, who before these days overthrew, and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Sicari?
ACT 21:39 And Paul said, I a man indeed, am a Jew of Tarsus of Cilicia, a citizen of not an unmarked city; and I beseech you, commit it to my care to speak to the people.
ACT 21:40 And he having permitted, Paul standing upon the stairs, waved his hand to the people. And with a great quietness having taken place, he called out in the Hebrew dialect, saying,
ACT 22:1 Men, brothers, and fathers, hear my defense to you now!
ACT 22:2 And hearing that in the Hebrew dialect he called out to them, the more they made rest.
ACT 22:3 And he says, I indeed am a man, a Jew, being born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but being reared in this city by the feet of Gamaliel, being instructed according to the exactness of the paternal law, being zealous of God, as all you are today;
ACT 22:4 one who persecuted this way unto death, binding and delivering up unto prisons both men and women.
ACT 22:5 As also the chief priest bears witness to me, and all the council of elders; by whom also letters having received, I went to the brothers in Damascus, for leading also the ones at that place being bound unto Jerusalem, that they should be punished.
ACT 22:6 And it happened to me going and approaching to Damascus around midday, suddenly from out of the heaven flashed about a light, a fit amount around me.
ACT 22:7 And I fell onto the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
ACT 22:8 And I answered, Who are you, O Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you persecute.
ACT 22:9 And the ones being with me indeed saw a light, and became thrown into fear; but they heard not the voice of the one speaking to me.
ACT 22:10 And I said, What shall I do, O Lord? And the Lord said to me, Having risen up, go unto Damascus, and there it shall be told to you concerning all of which is arranged to you to do!
ACT 22:11 And as I looked not upon anything because of the glory of that light, being led by the hand by the ones being with me, I came unto Damascus.
ACT 22:12 And a certain Ananias, a pious man according to the law, borne witness to by all the Jews dwelling in Damascus,
ACT 22:13 having come to me, and having stood by, said to me, O brother Saul, look up! And I the same hour looked up on him.
ACT 22:14 And he said, The God of our fathers handpicked you to know his will, and to behold the just one, and to hear the voice from out of his mouth.
ACT 22:15 For you will be a witness to him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
ACT 22:16 And now, why be about to delay.? Having arisen, be immersed, and wash off your sins, calling upon the name of the Lord.
ACT 22:17 And it happened to me in returning unto Jerusalem, and my praying in the temple, there took place in me a change of state;
ACT 22:18 and beholding him saying to me, Hasten, and go forth quickly from Jerusalem! for they will not welcome your testimony concerning me.
ACT 22:19 And I said, O Lord, they know that I was casting into prison and flaying against the synagogues believing upon you.
ACT 22:20 And when the blood of Stephen your witness was poured out, also I myself was standing by, and assenting with his removal, guarding the garments of the ones doing away with him.
ACT 22:21 And he said to me, Go! For I shall send you unto nations far off!
ACT 22:22 And they heard him until this word, and they lifted up their voice, saying, Take such a one from the earth! for it is not fit for him to live.
ACT 22:23 And of their crying out, and tossing their garments, and throwing dust into the air,
ACT 22:24 the commander bid him to be led unto the camp, having said, Investigate him with whips! that we should know for what reason thus they sounded out against him.
ACT 22:25 And as they stretched him forward with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing, Is it allowed to you to crack the whip on a Roman man and uncondemned?
ACT 22:26 And hearing, the centurion came forward to report to the commander, saying, Look to what you are about to do! for this man is a Roman.
ACT 22:27 And having come forward, the commander said to him, Tell me if you are a Roman? And he said, Yes.
ACT 22:28 And the commander responded, I by a great sum acquired this citizenship. And Paul said, But I even was born to it.
ACT 22:29 Then immediately the ones being about to investigate him abstained from him. And the commander also feared, realizing that he is a Roman, and that he was tied up by him.
ACT 22:30 And the next day, wanting to know safely why he is charged by the Jews, he loosed him from the bonds, and bid the chief priests to come and all their sanhedrin; and leading down Paul, he stood him among them.
ACT 23:1 And Paul gazing upon the sanhedrin, said, Men, brothers, I in all good conscience have conducted myself in public to God as far as this day.
ACT 23:2 But the chief priest Ananias gave orders to the ones standing beside him to strike his mouth.
ACT 23:3 Then Paul said to him, God is about to beat you, O wall being whitewashed. And you, do you sit down judging me according to the law, and acting unlawfully you bid me to be struck?
ACT 23:4 And the ones standing beside said, The chief priest of God you revile?
ACT 23:5 And Paul said, I knew not brothers that he is chief priest; for it has been written, You shall not speak ill of a ruler of your people.
ACT 23:6 And Paul having known that the one part is of Sadducees, and the other of Pharisees, cried out in the sanhedrin, Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of a Pharisee; concerning hope and a resurrection of the dead I am judged.
ACT 23:7 And this he having said, there became a faction between the Pharisees and the Sadducees. And the multitude was split.
ACT 23:8 For the Sadducees indeed say to not be a resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees acknowledge both.
ACT 23:9 And there became a great cry. And having risen up, the scribes of the part of the Pharisees disputed violently, saying, Nothing bad do we find in this man. But if also a spirit spoke to him, or an angel, we should not fight against God.
ACT 23:10 And there being a great faction, the commander being cautious, lest Paul be pulled apart by them, bid the military to go down, and to seize him from out of the midst of them, and to lead him unto the camp.
ACT 23:11 And the following night, standing by him, the Lord said, Take courage, Paul! for as you testified the things concerning me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome.
ACT 23:12 And becoming day, some of the Jews having made a confederacy, devoted themselves, saying to neither eat nor drink until they should kill Paul.
ACT 23:13 And the ones making this conspiracy were more than forty;
ACT 23:14 who having come forward to the chief priests and to the elders, said, We devoted ourselves to consumption, to not taste one thing until of which we should kill Paul.
ACT 23:15 Now then you reveal yourselves to the commander with the sanhedrin, so that tomorrow he should lead him to you, as being about to determine more exactly the things concerning him. And we, before his approaching, are prepared to do away with him.
ACT 23:16 And the son of the sister of Paul having heard the ambush, having come and entered into the camp, reported it to Paul.
ACT 23:17 And Paul having called one of the centurions, said, Take this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him!
ACT 23:18 Then indeed having taken him, he brought him to the commander, and says, The prisoner Paul having called me, asked me to lead this young man to you, having something to say to you.
ACT 23:19 And the commander having taken hold of his hand, and having withdrawn in private, inquired, What is it which you have to report to me?
ACT 23:20 And he said that, The Jews agreed to ask you that tomorrow you should lead Paul unto the sanhedrin, as being about something to more exactly ascertain concerning him.
ACT 23:21 You then should not be persuaded by them; for they lie in wait for him, more than forty men of them, who devoted themselves unto consumption, to neither eat nor drink until of which they should do away with him. And now they are ready, waiting a promise from you.
ACT 23:22 Then the commander dismissed the young man, exhorting, saying, Divulge to no one that these things were revealed to me.
ACT 23:23 And having called on two certain centurions, he said, Prepare two hundred soldiers, that they should go unto Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, from the third hour of the night;
ACT 23:24 and present beasts, that Paul setting upon one, they should deliver him to Felix the governor;
ACT 23:25 having a letter written containing this impression.
ACT 23:26 Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix, Hail!
ACT 23:27 This man having been seized by the Jews, and being about to be done away with by them; attending with the military, I rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman.
ACT 23:28 And wanting to know the reason for which they accused him, I led him down unto their sanhedrin.
ACT 23:29 Whom I found to be accused concerning matters of their law, but having not one indictment worthy of death or bonds.
ACT 23:30 And having been indicated to me of a plot against the man, being about to be by the Jews, immediately I sent forth to you, exhorting also the accusers to say the things against him unto you. Be in health!
ACT 23:31 The soldiers then, according to the thing being set in order for them, having taken Paul, led him through the night unto Antipatris.
ACT 23:32 And the next day they allowed the horsemen to go with him, and they returned unto the camp.
ACT 23:33 Who, having entered into Caesarea, and having delivered the letter to the governor, presented also Paul to him.
ACT 23:34 And the governor having read it, and having asked of what jurisdiction he is, and having ascertained that he is from Cilicia;
ACT 23:35 said I will hold a hearing for you,, whenever also your accusers should come. And he bid him to be kept in the praetorium of Herod.
ACT 24:1 And after five days there came down the chief priest Ananias with the elders, and a rhetorician, a certain Tertullus, who revealed themselves to the governor against Paul.
ACT 24:2 And having been called, Tertullus himself began to charge, saying, Great peace is happening through you, and great feats are happening to this nation because of your forethought;
ACT 24:3 both totally and everywhere we receive it gladly, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
ACT 24:4 But so that I should not hinder upon you much more, I appeal for you to hear us so suddenly in your clemency.
ACT 24:5 For having found this man mischievous, and moving insurrection among all the Jews in the habitable world, and front rank of the sect of the Nazarenes;
ACT 24:6 who also attempted to profane the temple, whom also we seized, and according to our law we wanted to judge.
ACT 24:7 But Lysias the commander having come by with a great force took him from out of our hands,
ACT 24:8 bidding his accusers to come; from whom you will be able, he having questioned concerning all these things, to realize what we accuse him.
ACT 24:9 And also the Jews joined in making an attack, maintaining these things thus to suffice.
ACT 24:10 And Paul responded, of the governor nodding to him to speak, saying, For many years you being judge to this nation, knowing this, more cheerfully the things concerning myself I make a defense.
ACT 24:11 You being able to know that there were not more than twelve days to me from which I ascended to do obeisance into Jerusalem.
ACT 24:12 And neither in the temple did they find me with anyone reasoning, or causing a conspiracy of a multitude, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city;
ACT 24:13 nor are they able to render proof concerning which now they charge me.
ACT 24:14 But I acknowledge this to you, that according to the way, which they call a sect, so I serve to the paternal God, believing in all things according to the law and to the things having been written in the prophets;
ACT 24:15 having a hope in God, which also they themselves wait for - a resurrection about to be of the dead, both of just ones and unjust ones.
ACT 24:16 And in this I discipline myself, not causing anyone to stumble, having a conscience towards God and men continually.
ACT 24:17 And after more years I came offering charity to my nation, and offerings.
ACT 24:18 In which they found me purified in the temple, not with a multitude, nor with a tumult. But certain Jews from Asia,
ACT 24:19 whom must be at hand before you, and to charge, if anything they may have against me;
ACT 24:20 and let these themselves speak! if they found anything in me for an offence, with my standing before the sanhedrin;
ACT 24:21 other than concerning this one voice which I cried out standing among them, that, Concerning a resurrection of the dead I am judged today by you.
ACT 24:22 And hearing these things, Felix postponed them, more exactly knowing the things concerning the way, having said, Whenever Lysias the commander should come down, I will determine the things as to you.
ACT 24:23 And having given orders to the centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have relaxation, and for no one to restrain the ones of his own to assist or to come forward to him.
ACT 24:24 And after some days, Felix having come with Drusilla his wife, being Jewish, he fetched Paul, and he heard him concerning the belief in Christ.
ACT 24:25 And of his reasoning concerning righteousness, and self-control, and the judgment about to be, Felix becoming thrown into fear responded, For now it suffices, go! But a time for sharing I will call you back.
ACT 24:26 But at the same time also hoping that things shall be given to him by Paul, so that he should loose him; therefore also more frequently fetching him, he consorted with him.
ACT 24:27 And a space of two years having been fulfilled, Felix received as a successor, Porcius Festus. And wanting favors to be laid away with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.
ACT 25:1 Then Festus, having set foot in the jurisdiction after three days, ascended unto Jerusalem from Caesarea.
ACT 25:2 And the chief priest revealed to him, and the foremost men of the Jews, the things against Paul, that they appealed to him,
ACT 25:3 asking a favor against him, that he should fetch him unto Jerusalem, while making an ambush to do away with him along the way.
ACT 25:4 Then Festus responded for Paul to be kept in Caesarea, but he himself was about to quickly go forth.
ACT 25:5 The ones then mighty among you, says he, having gone down, if anything is out of place in this man, let them accuse him!
ACT 25:6 And having spent time among them more than ten days, having gone down unto Caesarea, the next day having sat upon the rostrum, he bid Paul to be led in.
ACT 25:7 And he being come, there stood around the Jews having come down from Jerusalem, with many and grievous accusations bringing against Paul, which they were not able to exhibit;
ACT 25:8 while of his pleading, saying that, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar in anything I sinned.
ACT 25:9 And Festus, wanting to lay down favor with the Jews, responding to Paul, said, Are you willing to ascend unto Jerusalem to be judged by me there concerning these things?
ACT 25:10 And Paul said, Unto the rostrum of Caesar I am standing, of which it is necessary for me to be judged. To Jews I did no wrong, as also you well realize.
ACT 25:11 For if indeed I do wrong, and have acted in anything worthy of death, I do not ask pardon to die; but if there is nothing of which they charge me, no one can grant me to them. To Caesar I call upon.
ACT 25:12 Then Festus conversing together with the council responded, To Caesar you have called upon, unto Caesar you shall go.
ACT 25:13 And some days having elapsed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, saluting Festus.
ACT 25:14 And when they spent many days there, Festus the king presented the things relating to Paul, saying, There is a certain man being left by Felix - a prisoner.
ACT 25:15 Concerning whom, on my being in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews revealed, asking for punishment against him.
ACT 25:16 To whom I answered that, It is not a custom with Romans to grant any man for destruction, before the one being accused may have the accusers face to face, and may receive a place of defense concerning the indictment.
ACT 25:17 Then they having come here, not making delay, in the next day having seated at the rostrum, I bid the man to be led in.
ACT 25:18 Concerning whom, the accusers standing up, brought no accusation which I suspected.
ACT 25:19 But certain matters concerning their own reverence of God they had against him, and concerning a certain Jesus having died, whom Paul maintained to be alive.
ACT 25:20 And I being perplexed concerning this inquiry, said, Shall he be willing to go unto Jerusalem, and there to be judged concerning these things?
ACT 25:21 But Paul, having called upon himself to be kept for the inquiry of Augustus, I bid to keep him until of which I should send him forth to Caesar.
ACT 25:22 And Agrippa said to Festus, I wanted also myself to hear the man. And the morrow, he says, you shall hear him.
ACT 25:23 Then in the next day Agrippa and Bernice having come with much visible display, and having entered into the auditorium, with both the commanders, and men of prominence being of the city, and Festus having bid, Paul was led in.
ACT 25:24 And Festus says, O king Agrippa, and all the men being present with us, you view this one concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews interceded with me in both Jerusalem and here, yelling aloud he must not live any longer.
ACT 25:25 And I having perceived he to have done nothing worthy of death, and this one also himself having called upon Augustus, I judged to send him.
ACT 25:26 Concerning of which I have not anything safe to write to my lord. Therefore I led him unto you, and especially unto you, O king Agrippa, so that the examination having taken place, I should have something to write.
ACT 25:27 For it seems illogical to me to send forth a prisoner, and not signifying the accusations against him.
ACT 26:1 And Agrippa said to Paul, It is permitted for you to speak for yourself. Then Paul made a defense, having stretched out the hand.
ACT 26:2 Concerning all of which I am accused by the Jews, O king Agrippa, I esteem myself blessed being about to make a defense unto you today.
ACT 26:3 Especially you being a diviner of all the things among the Jews of both customs and matters. Therefore I beseech you leniently to hear me.
ACT 26:4 Indeed then the mode of my life from youth, the thing from the beginning happening among my nation in Jerusalem, all the Jews understand;
ACT 26:5 foreknowing me from the beginning, (if they should want to witness,) that according to the exactest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
ACT 26:6 And now for the hope of the promise being by God to the fathers I stand being judged.
ACT 26:7 In which our twelve tribes, serving with intensity night and day, hope to arrive. Concerning which hope I am accused, O king Agrippa, by the Jews.
ACT 26:8 Why is it judged unbelievable by you, if God raises the dead?
ACT 26:9 I indeed then thought to myself that it was necessary in many things to act opposite towards the name of Jesus the Nazarene.
ACT 26:10 Which also I did in Jerusalem. And many of the holy ones I imprisoned in prisons, receiving authority from the chief priests; and for doing away with them I brought down a vote.
ACT 26:11 And in all the synagogues often punishing them, I compelled them to blaspheme; and extremely raging against them, I persecuted them even as unto the outer cities.
ACT 26:12 In which also going unto Damascus with authority and delegated power by the chief priests,
ACT 26:13 in the middle of the day in the way, I beheld, O king, from heaven above, light the brightness of the sun shining about me, and the ones going with me.
ACT 26:14 And all of us having fallen down onto the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me, and saying in the Hebrew dialect, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? it is hard for you to kick against spurs.
ACT 26:15 And I said, Who are you, O Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom you persecute.
ACT 26:16 But rise up, and stand upon your feet! for in this I appeared to you, to handpick you as an assistant and witness both of what you beheld, and of what I shall make known to you;
ACT 26:17 taking you out from the people, and of the nations, unto whom now I shall send you,
ACT 26:18 to open their eyes, to turn them from darkness unto light, and the authority of Satan unto God, for them to receive a release of sins, and a lot among the ones having been sanctified by the belief in me.
ACT 26:19 From where, O king Agrippa, not to be resisting persuasion to the heavenly apparition;
ACT 26:20 but to the ones in Damascus first, and Jerusalem, and in all the region of Judea, and to the nations, I reported to repent and to turn unto God, doing works worthy of repentance.
ACT 26:21 Because of these things the Jews having seized me in the temple, attempted to lay hands upon me.
ACT 26:22 Having attained aid then from God, unto this day, I have stood testifying both to small and great, saying nothing outside of what both the prophets and Moses said was about to happen -
ACT 26:23 whether the Christ is susceptible of suffering; whether he first through resurrection of the dead is about to announce light to the people, and to the nations.
ACT 26:24 And having made his defense with these things, Festus with a great voice said, You are maniacal, Paul; many letters dizzies you into a frenzy.
ACT 26:25 But I am not maniacal, he says, most excellent Festus; but truth and discreetness of words I declare.
ACT 26:26 For concerning these things the king knows, to whom also openly speaking I speak. For I am not persuaded in any way for him to be unaware in any of these things. For not in a corner is this being done.
ACT 26:27 You believe, O king Agrippa, the prophets? I know that you believe.
ACT 26:28 And Agrippa said to Paul, By little you persuade me to become a Christian.
ACT 26:29 And Paul said, I would make a vow even to God, both in a little and in much, not only you, but also all the ones hearing me today to become such as to like what even I am, except these bonds.
ACT 26:30 And these things him having said, the king rose up, and the governor, and also Bernice, and the ones sitting together with them.
ACT 26:31 And having withdrawn they spoke with one another, saying that, Nothing worthy of death or bonds this man does.
ACT 26:32 And Agrippa said to Festus, This man was able to be loosed if he had not called upon Caesar.
ACT 27:1 And when it was decided for us to sail away unto Italy, they delivered up both Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion, by name Julius, of the cohort of Augustus.
ACT 27:2 And having set foot in a boat of Adramyttium, being about to sail the places along Asia, we embarked; with Aristarchus a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
ACT 27:3 And in the other day we led down unto Sidon. And Julius kindly treating Paul, permitted him going to his friends to attain care.
ACT 27:4 And from there embarking, we sailed under Cyprus, because of the winds being adverse.
ACT 27:5 And the open sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia having sailed, we went down unto Myra of Lycia.
ACT 27:6 And there, the centurion having found a boat of Alexandria sailing to Italy, boarded us onto it.
ACT 27:7 And in a fit amount of days sailing slowly, and hardly coming near Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under Crete, near Salmone.
ACT 27:8 And hardly sailing along it, we came to a certain place being called, Good Harbors; which was near a city of Lasea.
ACT 27:9 And a fit amount of time having elapsed, and being already a dangerous voyage, because also the fasting already went by, Paul earnestly advised,
ACT 27:10 saying to them, Men, I contemplate that with damage and much loss, not only of the load of cargo and of the boat, but also the voyage is about to be of our lives.
ACT 27:11 But the centurion was persuaded by the navigator and the shipmaster, rather than the things being said by Paul.
ACT 27:12 And the existing harbor being unsuitable for wintering, the more they made counsel to embark from there, if by any means they might be able, arriving at Phoenix, to pass the winter, which is a harbor of Crete, looking towards the southwest and towards the northwest.
ACT 27:13 And blowing gently south, thinking the purpose to have been reached, having lifted off they sailed close by Crete.
ACT 27:14 But not long after a stormy wind shot by it, being called Euroclydon.
ACT 27:15 And the boat being seized with force, and not able to tack into the wind, giving up we bore off.
ACT 27:16 And running under some small island being called Clauda, we were hardly able to take control of the skiff;
