ACT 27:17 which having taken up, they employed helps, undergirding the boat; and fearing lest they should fall off into the Syrtis Gulf, letting down the rigging, thus they were borne along.
ACT 27:18 And vehemently with our being tossed by the storm, on the next day an expulsion of cargo was made;
ACT 27:19 and the third day with our own hands we tossed out the rigging of the boat.
ACT 27:20 And neither sun nor stars were appearing for many more days, and not a small distress was pressed upon us, and all remaining hope was removed for us to be preserved.
ACT 27:21 And a long lack of food existing, then Paul standing in their midst said, Indeed it behooved you, O men, having yielded obedience to me, to not have embarked from Crete, so as to gain this damage and the loss.
ACT 27:22 And at present I earnestly advise you be cheerful! for not one life will be cast off of you, except the boat.
ACT 27:23 For there stood beside me in this night an angel of God, of whom I am, and in whom I serve,
ACT 27:24 saying, Fear not, Paul, Caesar you must stand before, and behold, God has granted to you all the ones sailing with you.
ACT 27:25 Therefore be cheerful, men! for I believe in God, that so it will be in which manner it has been spoken to me.
ACT 27:26 But onto a certain island we must fall.
ACT 27:27 And when the fourteenth night came to pass, we being carried about in the Adriatic, towards the middle of the night the seamen suspected some region neared them.
ACT 27:28 And having sounded, they found it twenty fathoms; and a short time having elapsed, and again having sounded, they found it fifteen fathoms.
ACT 27:29 And fearing perhaps they should fall into rough places, they tossed four anchors from out of the stern, vowing day to come.
ACT 27:30 And the seamen seeking to flee from the boat, and having let down the skiff into the sea, with an excuse as to be about to stretch out the anchors from the prow,
ACT 27:31 Paul said to the centurion, and to the soldiers, If these do not stay in the boat, you will not be able to be preserved.
ACT 27:32 Then the soldiers cut off the lines of the skiff, and allowed it to fall off.
ACT 27:33 And until day was about to come, Paul appealed for all to share in nourishment, saying, Today is the fourteenth day you continue expecting without eating, having taken nothing to yourselves.
ACT 27:34 Therefore I appeal to you to take nourishment; for this exists for your deliverance; for not one hair of yours shall fall from your head.
ACT 27:35 And having said these things, and having taken bread, he gave thanks to God before all. And having broken he began to eat.
ACT 27:36 And all having become cheerful, also they took nourishment.
ACT 27:37 And we were in the boat, all two hundred seventy six souls.
ACT 27:38 And being satisfied with nourishment, they lightened the boat, casting out the grain into the sea.
ACT 27:39 And when it became day, they did not recognize the land. But they contemplated a certain bay having a shore, on which they consulted if they are able to thrust the boat.
ACT 27:40 And having removed the anchors, they gave up unto the sea; together unfastening the tillers of the rudder, and having lifted up the mainsail to the blow, they held for the shore.
ACT 27:41 And having fallen into a place between two seas, they ran the ship aground. And the prow having stuck, remained unshaken, but the stern was loose by the force of the waves.
ACT 27:42 And the soldiers plan was that they should kill the prisoners, lest any swimming, should have escaped.
ACT 27:43 But the centurion wanting to save Paul, restrained them of their will. And he bid the ones able to swim, having thrown themselves off first, to exit unto the land;
ACT 27:44 and the rest, some indeed upon planks, and others upon some of the things from the boat. And so it came to pass all came through safe unto the land.
ACT 28:1 And having come through safe, then they knew that the island is called Malta.
ACT 28:2 And the barbarians furnished not the happen by chance humane treatment to us; for having lit a bonfire, they took all of us unto themselves, because of the rain attending, and because of the chilliness.
ACT 28:3 And Paul bundled up a multitude of sticks, and having placed them on the bonfire, a viper having gone completely through from the heat, clinched onto his hand.
ACT 28:4 And when the barbarians beheld the beast hanging from his hand, they said to one another, Assuredly this man is a murderer, whom having been delivered from the sea, Dice allowed not to live.
ACT 28:5 He indeed then, having brushed off the beast into the fire, suffered no hurt.
ACT 28:6 And the ones expecting him to be about to become inflamed, or to fall down suddenly dead, and for a long time of their expecting, and viewing that nothing out of place was happening to him, changing their minds, said him to be a god.
ACT 28:7 And in the parts around that place existed a place belonging to the foremost man of the island, by name Publius; who having received us, three days obligingly lodged us.
ACT 28:8 And it happened the father of Publius reclined constrained with fevers and dysentery; to whom Paul having entered, and having prayed, having placed the hands on him, healed him.
ACT 28:9 This then having taken place, also the rest, (the ones having sicknesses in the island,) came forward, and were cured.
ACT 28:10 Who also with much honor esteemed us; and embarking, placed the things for our need.
ACT 28:11 And after three months we embarked in a boat, (having passed the winter in the island,) an Alexandrian marked by the ensign Dioscuri.
ACT 28:12 And leading down unto Syracuse, we remained three days.
ACT 28:13 From where having gone around we arrived at Rhegium. And after one day a south wind ensued; on the second day we came into Puteoli.
ACT 28:14 Of which having found brothers, we were appealed upon by them to remain seven days. And thus to Rome we came.
ACT 28:15 And from there, the brothers having heard the things concerning us, came forth to meet us as far as Appii Forum, and Three Taverns. Whom Paul seeing, having given thanks to God, took courage.
ACT 28:16 And when we came unto Rome, the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the commander of the camp. But to Paul was committed to remain by himself with the soldier guarding him.
ACT 28:17 And it came to pass after three days, Paul calling together the ones being foremost of the Jews, and they having come together, he said to them, Men, brothers, I having done nothing against the people or the paternal customs, was delivered up a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans;
ACT 28:18 who, having questioned me, wanted to loose me, on account of the not one reason for death being in me.
ACT 28:19 But the Jews disputing, I was compelled to call upon Caesar; not as having anything to accuse my nation.
ACT 28:20 For this reason then I appealed to you, to see, and to speak to you; for on account of the hope of Israel I am encompassed with this chain.
ACT 28:21 And they said to him, We received neither letters concerning you from Judea, nor having come has any one of the brothers reported or spoke anything bad concerning you.
ACT 28:22 But we deem it worthy to hear from you what you think; for indeed concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.
ACT 28:23 And arranging for him a day, there came to him many more unto his guest room; to whom he expounded, testifying the kingdom of God, and persuading them the things concerning Jesus, from both the law of Moses, and of the prophets, from morning until evening.
ACT 28:24 And some indeed were persuaded to the things being said, and some disbelieved.
ACT 28:25 And being disharmonious with one another, they retired at Paul having spoken one discourse, that, Well the holy spirit spoke through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
ACT 28:26 saying, Go to this people, and say! In hearing you shall hear, and in no way should you perceive; and seeing you shall see, and in no way should you know.
ACT 28:27 For the heart of this people was thickened, and they heard heavily with the ears, and they closed the eyelids of their eyes; lest at any time they should see with the eyes, and should hear with the ears, and with the heart should perceive, and should turn, and I should heal them.
ACT 28:28 Let it be known then to you, that to the nations the deliverance of God was sent, and they will hearken!
ACT 28:29 And these things he having said, the Jews went forth having much debating among themselves.
ACT 28:30 And Paul stayed a whole space of two years in his own hired house, and gladly received all the ones entering to him,
ACT 28:31 proclaiming the kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, unrestrainedly.
ROM 1:1 Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, a chosen apostle, being separated for the good news of God,
ROM 1:2 (which he preannounced through his prophets in holy scriptures,)
ROM 1:3 concerning his son, (the one born of the seed of David according to flesh;
ROM 1:4 the one being confirmed son of God in power, according to spirit of holiness, by a resurrection of the dead,) Jesus Christ our Lord;
ROM 1:5 through whom we received favor and a commission, for obedience of belief among all the nations, for his name;
ROM 1:6 among whom are also you, chosen of Jesus Christ.
ROM 1:7 To all the ones being in Rome, beloved of God, chosen holy ones. Favor to you, and peace from God our Father, and Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 1:8 First indeed, I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that the belief of yours is announced in the entire world.
ROM 1:9 For God is my witness, in whom I serve in my spirit in the good news of his son, how continually I make mention of you at all times at my prayers;
ROM 1:10 beseeching, (if by any means already at some time or other I shall prosper in the will of God,) to come to you.
ROM 1:11 For I long to see you, that some spiritual favor I should share with you for your support.
ROM 1:12 And this, it is to be comforted together with you through the belief that is in one another - both yours and mine.
ROM 1:13 But I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, for often I purposed to come to you, and was restrained as far as the coming, that I should have some fruit also among you, as also among the rest of the nations.
ROM 1:14 Both to Greeks and barbarians; both to wise ones and unthinking - I am a debtor.
ROM 1:15 So as to me to be eager also to announce good news to you the ones in Rome.
ROM 1:16 For not am I ashamed of the good news of the Christ; for it is power of God for deliverance to every one believing; both to the Jew first, and to the Greek.
ROM 1:17 For righteousness of God is revealed in it from out of belief for belief; as has been written, But the just one shall live from out of belief.
ROM 1:18 For anger of God is uncovered from heaven upon all impiety and unrighteousness of men, constraining the truth in unrighteousness.
ROM 1:19 For the thing made known of God is apparent among them; for God made it apparent to them.
ROM 1:20 For his unseen attributes, from the creation of the world, to the actions being comprehended, are looked at - both his everlasting power and divinity; for them to be inexcusable.
ROM 1:21 For having known God, they glorified him not as God, or gave thanks; but acted in folly in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
ROM 1:22 Maintaining to be wise ones, they became moronish,
ROM 1:23 and they bartered the glory of the incorruptible God for a representation of an image of corruptible man, and birds, and four-footed creatures, and reptiles.
ROM 1:24 Therefore also God delivered them up in the desires of their hearts, unto uncleanness, to dishonor their bodies among themselves.
ROM 1:25 The ones who changed over the truth of God into the lie, and worshiped and served to the created thing over the one having created it, who is blessed into the eons. Amen.
ROM 1:26 On account of this God delivered them up unto passions of dishonor. For both their females changed over the physical use unto the one against nature.
ROM 1:27 And indeed in like manner the males, leaving the physical use of the female, burned away in their lust for one another - males in males manufacturing indecency, and accepting in themselves the compensation which was a necessity of their delusion.
ROM 1:28 And as they tried not to hold God in full knowledge, God delivered them up unto a debased mind, to do the things not fitting;
ROM 1:29 being filled with all unrighteousness, harlotry, wickedness, desire for wealth, evil, full of envy, murder, strife, treachery, depraved morals, whisperers,
ROM 1:30 speaking vulgarities, hating God, insulting, proud, ostentatious, devisers of evils, to parents resisting persuasion,
ROM 1:31 senseless, contract-breakers, unaffectionate, hostile, unmerciful.
ROM 1:32 The ones who recognizing the ordinance of God, (that the ones acting such are worthy of death,) not only do the same, but also are assenting with the ones acting such.
ROM 2:1 Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, every one judging. For in which way you judge the other, yourself you condemn; for you do the same things, O one judging.
ROM 2:2 For we know that the judgment of God is according to truth upon the ones doing such things.
ROM 2:3 But do you think this, O man, (the one judging the ones doing such things, and yourself doing them,) that you shall flee from the judgment of God?
ROM 2:4 Or the riches of his graciousness and the forbearance and the leniency do you disdain; not knowing that the graciousness of God leads you to repentance?
ROM 2:5 But according to your hardness and impenitent heart you treasure up to yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
ROM 2:6 who will recompense each according to his works.
ROM 2:7 To the ones with endurance of good work, seeking anxiously glory and honor and incorruptibility - life eternal.
ROM 2:8 And to the ones of contention and resisting persuasion, indeed to the truth, and being yielded to iniquity - rage and wrath,
ROM 2:9 affliction and straits, upon every soul of man manufacturing the evil thing - both of Jew first, and Greek;
ROM 2:10 but glory, and honor, and peace to all working the good - both to the Jew first, and Greek.
ROM 2:11 For there is not a discrimination by God.
ROM 2:12 For as many as lawlessly sinned, lawlessly also they shall perish. And as many as in law sinned, by law they shall be judged;
ROM 2:13 ( for the listeners of the law are not just ones with God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.
ROM 2:14 For whenever nations not having law by nature should do the things of the law, these, not having law are to themselves law -
ROM 2:15 ones who demonstrate the work of the law written in their hearts, of their conscience bearing witness with and between one another, with devices charging or also making a defense;)
ROM 2:16 in a day when God judges the hidden things of men, (according to my good news,) through Jesus Christ.
ROM 2:17 Behold! you are named a Jew, and rest upon the law, and boast in God,
ROM 2:18 and you know the will, and you distinguish the differences, being instructed out of the law;
ROM 2:19 also persuading yourself to be a guide of the blind, a light of the ones in darkness,
ROM 2:20 a corrector of foolish ones, a teacher of infants, having the appearance of the knowledge and of the truth in the law.
ROM 2:21 The one then teaching another - do you not teach yourself? The one proclaiming, not to steal - do you steal?
ROM 2:22 The one saying, do not commit adultery - do you commit adultery? The one abhorring the idols - do you commit sacrilege?
ROM 2:23 The one who boasts in the law - through the violation of the law do you dishonor God?
ROM 2:24 For the name of God is blasphemed through you among the nations, as it has been written.
ROM 2:25 For indeed circumcision derives benefit if you should practice the law. But if you should be a violator of the law, your circumcision becomes uncircumcision.
ROM 2:26 If then the uncircumcised keep the ordinances of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be considered for circumcision?
ROM 2:27 And the one by nature uncircumcised fulfilling the law shall judge you, the one with contract and circumcision, but a violator of the law.
ROM 2:28 For not the one in the open is a Jew, nor the thing in the open in flesh circumcision.
ROM 2:29 But the one in the hiding is a Jew, and circumcision is in the heart, in spirit, not by contract; of whom the high praise is not of men, but of God.
ROM 3:1 Then what is the extra thing of the Jew, or what is the benefit of the circumcision?
ROM 3:2 Much in every manner. For indeed first that they were trusted with the oracles of God.
ROM 3:3 For what if some disbelieved? does their unbelief cease to work the belief of God?
ROM 3:4 May it not be. But let God be true, and every man a liar; as it has been written that, You should be justified in your words, and should overcome in your being judged.
ROM 3:5 But if our unrighteousness commends God's righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unjust, the one bearing upon the anger? (according to man I speak.)
ROM 3:6 May it not be; since how shall God judge the world?
ROM 3:7 For if the truth of God abounded in my untruth to his glory; why yet also I as a sinner am judged?
ROM 3:8 And not, as we are blasphemed, and as some say we say, that, We should do the bad things that the good things should come - their judgment is just.
ROM 3:9 What then, Do we have an advantage? Assuredly not. For we showed before both Jews and Greeks, all to be under sin;
ROM 3:10 as it has been written, There is not a just one, not even one.
ROM 3:11 There is not the one perceiving, there is not the one seeking after God.
ROM 3:12 All have turned aside, together they became useless; there is not one having graciousness; there is not even one.
ROM 3:13 Their throat having been opened is a tomb. With their tongues they use deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips;
ROM 3:14 whose mouth is full of curse and bitterness.
ROM 3:15 Keen are their feet to pour out blood;
ROM 3:16 destruction and misery are in their ways;
ROM 3:17 and the way of peace they knew not.
ROM 3:18 There is not a fear of God before their eyes.
ROM 3:19 And we know that as much as the law says, it speaks to the ones in the law; that every mouth should be shut, and all the world should be subject to trial to God.
ROM 3:20 For by works of law all flesh shall not be justified before him. For through law is full knowledge of sin.
ROM 3:21 But now righteousness of God has been made apparent separate of law, being witnessed by the law and the prophets -
ROM 3:22 even righteousness of God through belief of Jesus Christ unto all and for all the ones trusting; for there is not a difference.
ROM 3:23 For all sinned and lack the glory of God;
ROM 3:24 being justified without charge by his favor, through the release by ransom by Christ Jesus.
ROM 3:25 Whom God set forth as an atonement-seat, through the belief in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness through the letting pass the preceding sins;
ROM 3:26 in the forbearance of God, for a demonstration of his righteousness in the present time; for his being just and justifying the one of belief of Jesus.
ROM 3:27 Where then is the boasting? It was excluded. Through what kind of law? of the works? No, but through a law of belief.
ROM 3:28 We consider then a man to be justified by belief, separate from works of law.
ROM 3:29 Or is God only of Jews? But is he not also of nations? Yes, also of nations.
ROM 3:30 Since indeed there is one God who shall justify the circumcision of belief and uncircumcision through the belief,
ROM 3:31 then do we render law useless through the belief? May it not be. But we establish law.
ROM 4:1 What then shall we say Abraham our father has found according to flesh?
ROM 4:2 For if Abraham was justified of works, he has boasting, but not towards God.
ROM 4:3 For what does the scripture say? But Abraham trusted in God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness.
ROM 4:4 And to the one working, the wage is not considered according to favor, but according to the debt.
ROM 4:5 But to the one not working, but trusts upon the one justifying the impious one, his trust is imputed for righteousness.
ROM 4:6 Just as also David says about the blessing of the man to whom God imputes righteousness separate from works, saying,
ROM 4:7 Blessed are whom the lawless deeds were forgiven, and whom the sins were covered over.
ROM 4:8 Blessed is a man in whom in no way the Lord should impute sin.
ROM 4:9 Is this blessing then upon the circumcision only, or also upon the uncircumcision? For we say that belief was imputed to Abraham for righteousness.
ROM 4:10 How then was it imputed? being in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
ROM 4:11 And he received the sign of circumcision - a seal of the righteousness of the belief while being in the uncircumcision; for him to be father of all of the ones trusting through uncircumcision, for the righteousness to be imputed also to them.
ROM 4:12 And father of circumcision to the ones not of circumcision only, but also to the ones conforming to the tracks of the belief - to the ones in the uncircumcision of our father Abraham.
ROM 4:13 For not through law was the promise to Abraham or to his seed, for him to be heir of the world, but through righteousness of belief.
ROM 4:14 For if the ones from the law be heirs, the belief is empty, and the promise ceases to work.
ROM 4:15 For the law manufactures wrath. For where there is not law, not even is there a violation.
ROM 4:16 On account of this it is of belief, that according to favor, for the promise to be firm to all the seed - not to the one of the law only, but also to the one of belief of Abraham; who is father of all of us,
ROM 4:17 (as it has been written that, I have established you father of many nations, ) in front of which he trusted God restoring the dead to life, and calling the ones not being, as being;
ROM 4:18 who against hope trusted upon hope, for him to become father of many nations, according to the thing being said, So shall your seed be.
ROM 4:19 And not being weak in belief, he contemplated not his own body already deadened, being somewhere about a hundred years old, and the deadening of the womb of Sarah.
ROM 4:20 And at the promise of God he did not examine by unbelief, but was empowered in belief, giving glory to God;
ROM 4:21 and having full assurance that what he has promised, he is able also to do.
ROM 4:22 Therefore also it was imputed to him for righteousness.
ROM 4:23 But it was not written on account of him only, that it was imputed to him;
ROM 4:24 but also on account of us, to whom it was about to be imputed, to the ones trusting upon the one having raised Jesus our Lord from the dead;
ROM 4:25 who was delivered up on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification.
ROM 5:1 Having been justified then of belief, we have peace towards God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 5:2 Through whom also we have access by the belief into this favor in which we stand, and boast upon hope of the glory of God.
ROM 5:3 And not only that, but also we boast in the afflictions; knowing that the affliction manufactures endurance;
ROM 5:4 and the endurance - proof; and the proof - hope;
ROM 5:5 and the hope does not shame; for the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through holy spirit having been given to us.
ROM 5:6 For still while we were weak Christ died in due time for the impious ones.
ROM 5:7 For hardly for a just one shall one die; for over the good one perhaps someone even dares to die;
ROM 5:8 but God commends his own love for us, that yet we being sinners, Christ died for us.
ROM 5:9 Much more then, having been justified now in his blood, we shall be delivered by him from the wrath.
ROM 5:10 For if, being enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be delivered by his life.
ROM 5:11 And not only that, but also boasting in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom now we received the reconciliation.
ROM 5:12 On account of this, as if through one man sin entered into the world, and through sin - death; and thus to all men death went through, because by which reason all sinned.
ROM 5:13 For until law sin was in the world - but sin not charged, (not being a law.)
ROM 5:14 But death reigned from Adam until Moses, reigning even upon the ones not having sinned in the likeness of the violation of Adam, who is a model of the one being about to come.
ROM 5:15 But shall not as the transgression, so also be the favor? For if in the transgression of the one the many died, to many more the favor of God, (and the gift by favor in the favor of the one man Jesus Christ to many,) abounded.
ROM 5:16 And not as by one man having sinned the gift. For indeed the judgment of one was unto condemnation, but the favor from out of many transgressions was unto justice.
ROM 5:17 For if in the transgression of the one man death reigned through the one man; how much more the ones receiving the abundance of the favor and the gift of righteousness shall reign in life through the one man Jesus Christ.
ROM 5:18 It is so then as through one transgression it was unto all men for condemnation; so also through one right action it was unto all men for justification of life.
ROM 5:19 For as by the disobedience of the one man many were established as sinners; so also by the obedience of the one man many shall be established as just ones.
ROM 5:20 But law entered privately, that transgression should be superabundant. But where sin was superabundant, favor superabounded.
ROM 5:21 That as sin reigned in death, so also the favor should reign through righteousness to life eternal through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM 6:1 What then shall we say? Shall we remain in sin that favor should be superabundant?
ROM 6:2 May it not be. We who died to sin, how shall we still live in it?
ROM 6:3 Or do you not know that as many as we were immersed unto Christ Jesus, unto his death we were immersed?
ROM 6:4 We were buried together then with him through the immersion into death. That as Christ arose from the dead by the glory of the father, so also we in newness of life should walk.
ROM 6:5 For if we have become planted together in the likeness of his death, so also of his resurrection we shall be.
ROM 6:6 Knowing this, that our old man was crucified along with him, that the body of sin should cease work, that we no longer are to be a slave to sin.
ROM 6:7 For the one having died has been justified from sin.
ROM 6:8 And if we died with Christ, we trust that also we shall live together with him.
ROM 6:9 Knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, no longer dies; death no longer dominates him.
ROM 6:10 For the fact he died - he died to sin once for all. But the fact he lives - he lives to God.
ROM 6:11 So also you consider yourselves to be dead indeed to sin, but being alive to God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM 6:12 Then let not sin reign in your mortal body, for the obeying it in its desires!
ROM 6:13 Nor present your members as weapons of iniquity to sin! But render yourselves to God, as one living from out of the dead, and your members as weapons of righteousness to God!
ROM 6:14 For sin shall not dominate you. For you are not under law, but under favor.
ROM 6:15 What then, should we sin that we are not under law, but under favor? May it not be.
ROM 6:16 Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves servants to obedience, you are servants to whom you obey; either sin unto death, or obedience unto righteousness?
ROM 6:17 But favor to God, for you were slaves of sin, but you obeyed from the heart in which model of teaching you were delivered by.
ROM 6:18 And having been set free from sin, you were enslaved to righteousness.
ROM 6:19 Humanly I speak, on account of the weakness of your flesh. For as you rendered your members subservient to uncleanness and to lawlessness unto lawlessness; so now render your members subservient to righteousness unto sanctification!
ROM 6:20 For when you were servants of sin, you were free in righteousness.
ROM 6:21 What fruit therefore had you then, in the things in which now you are ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
ROM 6:22 But now, having been set free from sin, and having been enslaved to God, you have your fruit unto sanctification, and the end - life eternal.
ROM 6:23 For the rations of sin is death; but the favor of God is life eternal in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM 7:1 Or do you not know, brothers, (for to the ones knowing law I speak,) that the law dominates the man over as much time as he lives?
ROM 7:2 For the married woman is tied by law to the living husband; but if the husband should die, she is cleared from the law of the husband.
ROM 7:3 Surely then with the husband living, she shall be treated as an adulteress, if she becomes to another man. But if the husband should die, she is free from the law; for her to not be an adulteress, having become to another man.
ROM 7:4 So that, my brothers, also you were put to death to the law through the body of the Christ; for you to become to another, to the one being arisen from the dead, that we should bear fruit to God.
ROM 7:5 For when we were in the flesh, the passions of the sins through the law exerted energy in our members for the bearing fruit to death.
ROM 7:6 But now we were cleared from the law, having died by which we were held; so as for us to serve in newness of spirit, and not oldness of contract.
ROM 7:7 What then shall we say? Is the law sin? May it not be. But sin I knew not, except through the law. For also I knew not lust, except the law said, You shall not lust.
ROM 7:8 But sin taking an opportunity through the commandment, manufactured every lust in me. For separate from the law sin was dead.
ROM 7:9 And I was alive separate from the law at some time or other; but the commandment having come, sin was revived, and I died.
ROM 7:10 And the commandment for life was found by me, for this to be to death.
ROM 7:11 For sin having taken opportunity through the commandment, cheated me, and through it killed me.
ROM 7:12 So that the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.
ROM 7:13 The thing then good - has it become death to me? May it not be. But sin, that it should appear sin, through the good in me manufacturing death; that sin should become excessively sinful through the commandment.
ROM 7:14 For we know that the law is spiritual. But I am fleshly, having been sold under sin.
ROM 7:15 For what I manufacture, I do not know. For not what I want to do, this I practice. And what I detest, this I do.
ROM 7:16 But if what I do not want to do, this I do, then I assent to the law that it is good.
ROM 7:17 But now, no longer I manufacture it, but it is sin living in me.
ROM 7:18 For I know that there does not live in me (that is to say, in my flesh,) good. For the will is present with me, but the manufacturing the good I do not find.
ROM 7:19 For I do not do the good which I want to do, but the evil which I do not want to do, this I practice.
ROM 7:20 But if what I do not want to do, this I do; no longer I manufacture it, but it is sin living in me.
ROM 7:21 I find then the law wanting in me to do the good, that with me the evil is present.
ROM 7:22 For I delight in the law of God according to the inside man.
ROM 7:23 But I see another law in my members, undertaking an expedition against the law of my mind, and captivating me to the law of sin being in my members.
ROM 7:24 O miserable man am I. Who shall rescue me from this body of death?
ROM 7:25 I give thanks to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. It is so, then. I myself indeed to the mind serve the law of God, but to the flesh the law of sin.
ROM 8:1 In nothing then is there now condemnation to the ones in Christ Jesus, not walking according to the flesh, but according to spirit.
ROM 8:2 For the law of the spirit of the life in Christ Jesus freed me from the law of sin and of death.
ROM 8:3 For the powerlessness of the law, in which it was weak through the flesh, God sent forth his own son in the likeness of flesh of sin, and concerning sin condemned sin in the flesh.
ROM 8:4 That the ordinance of the law should be fulfilled in us, to the ones not walking according to flesh, but according to spirit.
ROM 8:5 For the ones being according to flesh think the things of the flesh; but the ones according to spirit think the things of the spirit.
ROM 8:6 For the thought of the flesh is death, but the thought of the spirit is life and peace.
ROM 8:7 For the thought of the flesh is hatred to God; for to the law of God it submits not, for neither is it able;
ROM 8:8 and the ones being in flesh are not able to please God.
ROM 8:9 But you are not in flesh, but in spirit, if indeed spirit of God lives in you. But if anyone does not have spirit of Christ, this one is not of him.
ROM 8:10 But if Christ is in you, indeed the body is dead on account of sin, but the spirit is life through righteousness.
ROM 8:11 And if the spirit of the one raising Jesus from the dead lives in you, the one having raised the Christ from the dead shall restore to life also your mortal bodies on account of his spirit dwelling in you.
ROM 8:12 It is so then, brothers, we are not debtors to the flesh, to live according to flesh.
ROM 8:13 For if you live according to flesh you are about to die. But if in spirit you put to death the actions of the body you shall live.
ROM 8:14 For as many as are led in spirit of God, these are sons of God.
ROM 8:15 For you received not a spirit of slavery again unto fear; but you received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry out, Abba, Father.
ROM 8:16 The spirit itself bears witness together to our spirit, that we are children of God.
ROM 8:17 And if children, also heirs; heirs indeed of God, but joint-heirs of Christ; if indeed we suffer together, that also we should be glorified together.
ROM 8:18 For I consider that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared to the glory about to be uncovered unto us.
ROM 8:19 For the earnest expectation of the creation awaits the uncovering of the sons of God.
ROM 8:20 For to vanity the creation was submitted, not willingly, but through the one submitting upon hope;
ROM 8:21 that even the creation itself shall be freed from the slavery of corruption, unto the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
ROM 8:22 For we know that all creation groans together and suffers distress together as far as the present.
ROM 8:23 And not only that, but also ourselves, having the first-fruit of the spirit, even we ourselves moan in ourselves, awaiting adoption - the release by ransom of our body.
ROM 8:24 For in the hope we were delivered. But hope being seen is not hope. For what anyone sees, why also does he hope?
ROM 8:25 But if we hope for what we see not, we await by endurance.
ROM 8:26 And likewise also the spirit aids in our weaknesses. For the thing - what we pray for according to necessity, we know not. But the spirit itself intercedes for us with unutterable moanings.
ROM 8:27 But the one searching the hearts knows what the thought of the spirit is, for according to God it intercedes for the holy ones.
ROM 8:28 But we know that to the ones loving God all things work together for good, to the ones being called according to purpose.
ROM 8:29 For of whom he foreknew, also he predefined conformable to the image of his son, for him to be first-born among many brothers.
ROM 8:30 But the ones whom he predefined, these also he called. And whom he called, these also he justified. And whom he justified, these also he glorified.
ROM 8:31 What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
ROM 8:32 The one who indeed spared not his own son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also grant all things to us with him?
ROM 8:33 Who accuses against the chosen of God? God is the one justifying.
ROM 8:34 Who is the one condemning? Christ is the one having died, and more, also being arisen, who also is at the right of God, who also intercedes for us.
ROM 8:35 Who shall separate us from the love of the Christ? affliction, or straits, or persecution, or hunger, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
ROM 8:36 As it has been written that, Because of you we are put to death the entire day; we are considered as sheep for slaughter.
ROM 8:37 But in all these things we are completely victorious through the one having loved us.
ROM 8:38 For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor sovereignties, nor powers, nor things present, nor things about to be,
ROM 8:39 nor height, nor depth, nor any other creation, shall be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.

ROM 10:2 For I bear witness to them that they have zeal of God, but not according to full knowledge.
ROM 10:3 For being ignorant of the thing of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they submitted not to the righteousness of God.
ROM 10:4 For Christ is the end for righteousness of the law to every one believing.
ROM 10:5 For Moses writes about the righteousness of the law, that, The man observing them shall live by them.
ROM 10:6 But of the righteousness of belief thus he says, You should not say in your heart, Who shall ascend unto the heaven? that is to say, to lead Christ down;
ROM 10:7 or, Who shall go down into the abyss? that is to say, to lead Christ from the dead.
ROM 10:8 But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart; (that is to say, the word of the belief which we proclaim;)

ROM 10:10 For the heart believes unto righteousness; and the mouth acknowledges to deliverance.

ROM 11:21 For if God spared not the branches according to nature, perhaps not even you he shall spare.

ROM 11:24 For if you, were cut off from the wild olive tree according to nature, and contrary to nature were engrafted into the fruitful olive tree; how much more these according to nature, shall be engrafted into their own olive tree?
ROM 11:25 For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, that you should not be intelligent in yourselves, that callousness has happened in part to Israel until of which the fullness of the nations should enter in.

ROM 11:31 so also these now resisted persuasion to your mercy, that also they should be shown mercy.
ROM 11:32 For God closed up all of the ones in disobedience, that all of the ones he should show mercy.

ROM 12:1 Then I exhort you, brothers, by the compassions of God, to present your bodies living sacrifices, holy, well-pleasing to God, the rational service of yours.
ROM 12:2 And be not conformed to this eon; but be transformed in the renewal of your mind, in the trying of yourselves in what is the good and well-pleasing and perfect will of God!
ROM 12:3 For I say, by the favor being given to me, to every one being among you, to not be high-minded above what you must think; but to think to be of a sound mind, to each as God portioned a measure of belief.
ROM 12:4 For just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same action;
ROM 12:5 thus we the many are one body in Christ, and each one members of one another.
ROM 12:6 But having diverse favors according to the favor being given to us; whether prophecy, let it be according to the ratio of the belief;
ROM 12:7 whether service - in the service; whether the teaching - in the instruction;
ROM 12:8 whether the comforting - in the comfort; the sharing - in simplicity; the being in charge - with diligence; the showing of mercy - with happiness;
ROM 12:9 the love - unpretentious; abhorring the evil - cleaving to the good;
ROM 12:10 in the brotherly affection - having a strong natural affection for one another; in the honor - giving preference for one another;
ROM 12:11 in the diligence - not lazy; in the spirit - bubbling; to the Lord - serving;
ROM 12:12 in the hope - rejoicing; in the affliction - enduring; in the prayer - constantly attending to;
ROM 12:13 in the needs of the holy ones - participating in; the hospitality - pursuing.
ROM 12:14 Bless the ones persecuting you! Bless and do not curse!
ROM 12:15 Rejoice with ones rejoicing, and weep with ones weeping!
ROM 12:16 Be thinking the same to one another; not the high thinking, but associating with the lowly. Do not become intelligent for yourselves!
ROM 12:17 To no one rendering bad for bad. Thinking beforehand good things before all men.
ROM 12:18 If possible, as to yourselves, being at peace with all men;
ROM 12:19 not by yourselves avenging, beloved, but give place to wrath! For it has been written, Vengeance is mine; I will recompense, says the Lord.
ROM 12:20 If then your enemy should hunger, feed him! If he should thirst, give him a drink! For this doing you shall heap coals of fire upon his head.
ROM 12:21 Be not overcome by the evil, but overcome the evil by the good!
ROM 13:1 Every soul be submitted to authorities being superior! For there is not an authority unless from God. And the ones being authorities are ordered by God.
ROM 13:2 So that the one rebelling against the authority, opposes in the disposition of God; and the ones opposing, shall receive judgment to themselves.
ROM 13:3 For the rulers are not a fear of the ones of good works, but of the ones of evils. But you should not want to be fearful of the authority - by the doing good even you shall have high praise from it.
ROM 13:4 For it is a servant of God to you for good. But if you should do evil, fear! For it does not wear the sword in vain. For it is a servant of God, punishing for wrath to the one doing evil.
ROM 13:5 Therefore it is a necessity to be submitted, not only because of the wrath, but also because of the conscience.
ROM 13:6 For on account of this also fulfill paying the tribute! For they are ministers of God in this same thing attending to constantly.
ROM 13:7 Render then to all the debts! To the one for the tribute - the tribute; to the one for the tax - the tax; to the one commanding fear - the fear; to the one commanding honor - the honor.
ROM 13:8 To no one owe anything, unless it be loving one another. For the one loving the other has fulfilled the law.
ROM 13:9 For the commandment, You shall not commit adultery; you shall not murder; you shall not steal; you shall not lust; and if any other commandment, in this the word is recapitulated in the saying, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
ROM 13:10 Love to the neighbor works not evil, love then is the fullness of the law.
ROM 13:11 Also this, knowing the time, that the hour we already arise from out of sleep. For now deliverance is nearer us than when we believed.
ROM 13:12 The night progressed, and the day approaches. We should put aside then the works of darkness, and put on the weapons of the light.
ROM 13:13 As we should walk decently by day; not in debaucheries and in intoxications, not in beds and in lewdnesses, not in strife and in jealousy.
ROM 13:14 But clothe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not have forethought for desire of the flesh.
ROM 14:1 But the one being weak in belief take to yourselves, not for distinction of arguings!
ROM 14:2 Indeed one trusts to eat all things. And the one being weak eats vegetables.
ROM 14:3 The one eating, treat not with contempt the one not eating! And the one not eating, judge not the one eating! For God received him to himself.
ROM 14:4 Who are you, the one judging a stranger's servant? To his own master he stands or falls. But he shall be established, for God is able to establish him.
ROM 14:5 The one who indeed judges a day over a day, and the one who judges every day alike - let each have full assurance in his own mind!
ROM 14:6 The one regarding the day, regards it to the Lord; and the one not regarding the day, regards it not to the Lord. The one eating, eats to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one not eating, eats not to the Lord, and he gives thanks to God.
ROM 14:7 For not one of us lives to himself, and no one dies to himself.
ROM 14:8 For if both we should live, we should live to the Lord; and if we should die, we should die to the Lord. If both then we should live, and if we should die, we are of the Lord.
ROM 14:9 For, for this Christ both died, and rose up, and lived, that both the dead and living he should lord over.
ROM 14:10 But you, why do you judge your brother? Or also why do you treat with contempt your brother? For all of us shall stand before the rostrum of the Christ.
ROM 14:11 For it has been written, As I live, says the Lord, that to me every knee shall bend, and every tongue shall make acknowledgment to God.
ROM 14:12 So then each of us concerning himself shall give account to God.
ROM 14:13 No longer then should we judge one another. But this judge rather - the not putting an occasion of stumbling to the brother or an obstacle!
ROM 14:14 I know, and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is profane of itself. Except to the one considering anything to be profane - to that one it is profane.
ROM 14:15 But if your brother frets on account of food, no longer do you walk according to love. Do not destroy that one by your food, for whom Christ died!
ROM 14:16 Let then your good not be blasphemed!
ROM 14:17 For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in holy spirit.
ROM 14:18 For the one serving the Christ in these things is well-pleasing to God, and approved by men.
ROM 14:19 So then, the things of peace we should pursue, and the things of the edifying the thing for one another.
ROM 14:20 Do not destroy the work of God because of food. All things indeed are pure, but it is evil to the man who eats by an occasion of stumbling someone.
ROM 14:21 It is good to not eat meats, nor to drink wine, nor anything in which your brother stumbles against, or be caused to stumble, or is weak.
ROM 14:22 You have belief? According to yourself have it before God! Blessed is the one not judging himself in what he distinguishes.
ROM 14:23 But the one scrutinizing, if he should eat, has been condemned, for it is not of belief; and everything which is not of belief is sin.
ROM 15:1 But we the ones able ought to bear the weaknesses of the powerless, and not to please just ourselves.
ROM 15:2 For let each of us please his neighbor for good and for edifying!
ROM 15:3 For even the Christ pleased not himself. But as it has been written, The scornings of the ones berating you fell upon me.
ROM 15:4 For as much as was written beforehand, was written beforehand for our instruction, that through the endurance and on account of the comfort of the scriptures we should have hope.
ROM 15:5 And the God of patience and comfort - may he give to you the same regard with one another according to Christ Jesus.
ROM 15:6 That with one accord in one mouth you should glorify the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 15:7 Therefore take to yourself one another, as also the Christ took you to himself for the glory of God!
ROM 15:8 But I say, Christ Jesus has become a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, for the firming the promises of the fathers;
ROM 15:9 and the nations for mercy to glorify God, as it has been written, saying, Because of this I will make acknowledgment to you among the nations, and to your name I will strum.
ROM 15:10 And again it says, Be glad, O nations, with his people!
ROM 15:11 And again, Praise the Lord, all nations! And praise him all peoples!
ROM 15:12 And again Isaiah says, There will be the root of Jesse, and the one rising up to rule nations - upon him nations shall hope.
ROM 15:13 And the God of hope - may he fill you with all joy and peace in trusting, for you abounding in the hope, in power of holy spirit.
ROM 15:14 But I am persuaded, my brothers, even I myself, concerning you, that you also are full of goodness, being filled with all knowledge, being able even to admonish others.
ROM 15:15 But more daring I wrote to you, brothers, in part, as reminding you, through the favor being given to me by God,
ROM 15:16 for me to be a minister of Jesus Christ to the nations, administering in sacred service the good news of God, that the offering of the nations should be well-received, having been sanctified in holy spirit.
ROM 15:17 I have then a boasting in Christ Jesus - the things about God.
ROM 15:18 For I dare not to speak anything which Christ did not manufacture through me for the obedience of the nations - by word and work,
ROM 15:19 in the power of signs and miracles, in the power of spirit of God; so as for me from Jerusalem and round about unto Illyricum to accomplish the good news of the Christ.
ROM 15:20 And so, striving earnestly to announce good news, where Christ was not named, that I should not build upon another's foundation;
ROM 15:21 but as it has been written, To the ones to whom it was not announced concerning him, they shall see; and the ones who have not heard, they shall perceive.
ROM 15:22 Therefore also I was hindered the many times to come to you.
ROM 15:23 But now no longer having a place in these regions, and having a longing to come to you for many years,
ROM 15:24 whenever I should go into Spain, I will come to you. For I hope traveling by to see you, and by you to be sent forward there, if I should first be filled up in part by you.
ROM 15:25 But now I go unto Jerusalem serving to the holy ones.
ROM 15:26 For Macedonia and Achaia think well to make a certain fellowship contribution unto the poor of the holy ones in Jerusalem.
ROM 15:27 For they take pleasure in it, and they are their debtors. For if to the nations they participated in their spiritual things, they ought also in the fleshly things minister to them.
ROM 15:28 This then completing, and having sealed to them this fruit, I will go forth by you into Spain.
ROM 15:29 And I know that coming to you, I shall come in fullness of blessing of the good news of the Christ.
ROM 15:30 But I appeal to you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the love of the spirit, to be companion at arms with me in the prayers for me to God;
ROM 15:31 that I should be rescued from the ones resisting persuasion among the Jews; and that my service for Jerusalem, should be well-received by the holy ones;
ROM 15:32 that in joy I should come to you by the will of God, that I should be refreshed together with you.
ROM 15:33 And the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
ROM 16:1 But I commend to you Phoebe our sister, being a servant of the assembly in Cenchrea;
ROM 16:2 that you should favorably receive her in the Lord, worthily of the holy ones, and you should stand beside her in what ever thing she should need of you. For also she was a patroness of many, and of me myself.
ROM 16:3 Greet Priscilla and Aquila my fellow-workers in Christ Jesus,
ROM 16:4 (who placed their own neck for my life. To whom not I only give thanks, but also all the assemblies of the nations;)
ROM 16:5 and the assembly at their house! Greet Epaenetus my beloved, who is a first-fruit of Achaia for Christ!
ROM 16:6 Greet Mary, who tired much for us!
ROM 16:7 Greet Andronicus and Junias, my relatives, and my fellow-captives, who are notable among the apostles, who also were before me in Christ!
ROM 16:8 Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord!
ROM 16:9 Greet Urbanus, our fellow-worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved!
ROM 16:10 Greet Apelles the one approved in Christ! Greet the ones of the household of Aristobulus!
ROM 16:11 Greet Herodion my relative! Greet the ones of the ones of Narcissus being in the Lord!
ROM 16:12 Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, the ones tiring by labor in the Lord! Greet Persis the beloved, who by much labor tired in the Lord!
ROM 16:13 Greet Rufus the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine!
ROM 16:14 Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers with them!
ROM 16:15 Greet Philologus and Julias, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and the ones with them - all holy ones!
ROM 16:16 Greet one another with a holy kiss! The assemblies of Christ greet you.
ROM 16:17 And I appeal to you, brothers, to watch the ones making the discords and the obstacles by the teaching which you learned; and turn aside from them.
ROM 16:18 For the ones such serve not to our Lord Jesus Christ, but in their own belly; and by flattery and blessing they cheat the hearts of the guileless.
ROM 16:19 For the obedience of yours reached unto all. I rejoice then over you. But I want you to be wise ones indeed unto the good, but unmixed unto evil.
ROM 16:20 But the God of peace will destroy Satan under your feet quickly. The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
ROM 16:21 Timothy my fellow-worker greets you, and Luke, and Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
ROM 16:22 I Tertius greet you, the one writing the letter, in the Lord.
ROM 16:23 Gaius greets you, my host, and of the entire assembly. Erastus the manager of the city greets you, and Quartus the brother.
ROM 16:24 The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
ROM 16:25 And to the one able to support you according to my good news, and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to an uncovering of the mystery, in times eternal having been quiet,
ROM 16:26 but made apparent now, and through the prophetic scriptures, according to the command of the eternal God, for obedience of belief, having been made known unto all the nations -
ROM 16:27 the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory into the eons. Amen.
1CO 1:1 Paul, a chosen apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
1CO 1:2 to the assembly of God being in Corinth, having been sanctified in Christ Jesus, chosen holy ones, with all the ones calling upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours.
1CO 1:3 Favor to you, and peace from God our father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO 1:4 I give thanks to my God at all times for you, for the favor of God being given to you in Christ Jesus;
1CO 1:5 that in everything you were enriched in him, in all word and in all knowledge;
1CO 1:6 as the testimony of the Christ was firmed up in you;
1CO 1:7 so that you be not lacking in not one favor; awaiting the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ;
1CO 1:8 who also will firm up you unto the end, without reproach in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO 1:9 Trustworthy is God through whom you were called into a fellowship of his son Jesus Christ our Lord.
1CO 1:10 And I appeal to you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you should all say the same thing, and there should be no splits among you; but that you should be readying yourselves with the same mind, and with the same opinion.
1CO 1:11 For it was made manifest to me concerning you, my brothers, by the ones of Chloe, that there are strifes among you.
1CO 1:12 And I say this, that each of you says, I indeed am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas, and I of Christ.
1CO 1:13 Has the Christ been portioned? Was Paul crucified for you? Or in the name of Paul were you immersed?
1CO 1:14 I give thanks to God that not one of you I immersed, except Crispus and Gaius;
1CO 1:15 that not any should say that in my name he was immersed.
1CO 1:16 And I immersed also the house of Stephanas. The rest I know not if any other I immersed.
1CO 1:17 For Christ did not send me to immerse, but to announce good news. Not in wisdom of word, lest the cross of the Christ should be an empty work.
1CO 1:18 For the word of the cross to the ones indeed perishing is moronishness; but to the ones being preserved, to us it is the power of God.
1CO 1:19 For it has been written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise ones; and the understanding of the experts I will disregard.
1CO 1:20 Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this eon? Did not God make moronish the wisdom of this world?
1CO 1:21 For since in the wisdom of God the world did not know God through wisdom, God thought well through the moronishness of the proclamation to deliver the ones believing.
1CO 1:22 Since both Jews ask for a sign, and Greeks seek by wisdom.
1CO 1:23 But we proclaim Christ being crucified, to Jews indeed an obstacle, and to Greeks moronishness;
1CO 1:24 but to these the chosen, both Jews and Greeks, Christ - God's power and God's wisdom.
1CO 1:25 For the moronish of God is wiser than the wisdom of men; and the weakness of God is stronger than the strength of men.
1CO 1:26 For you see your calling, brothers, that there are not many wise ones according to flesh, not many mighty, not many well-born.
1CO 1:27 But the moronish of the world God chose, that the wise ones should be disgraced; and the weak of the world God chose, that the strong should be disgraced;
1CO 1:28 and the ignoble of the world, and the ones being treated with contempt God chose; and the things not being, that the things being he should render useless.
1CO 1:29 So that all flesh should not boast before him.
1CO 1:30 But you are of him in Christ Jesus, who became wisdom to us from God, both righteousness, and sanctification, and release by ransom.
1CO 1:31 That, as it has been written, The one boasting, let him boast in the Lord!
1CO 2:1 And I having come to you, brothers, came not according to superiority of word or wisdom, announcing to you the testimony of God.
1CO 2:2 For I decided not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and this one being crucified.
1CO 2:3 And I in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling was with you.
1CO 2:4 And my word, and my proclaiming was not in persuasive human words of wisdom, but in a demonstration of spirit and power.
1CO 2:5 That the belief of yours should not be in wisdom of men, but in power of God.
1CO 2:6 But we speak wisdom among the ones completed; but wisdom not of this eon, nor of the rulers of this eon, of the ones being rendered useless.
1CO 2:7 But we speak wisdom of God in a mystery being concealed, which God predefined before the eons for our glory.
1CO 2:8 Which not one of the rulers of this eon has known. For if they knew, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
1CO 2:9 But as it has been written, That which eye saw not, and ear heard not, and into the heart of man ascended not, which God prepared to the ones loving him.
1CO 2:10 But to us God revealed by his spirit. For the spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
1CO 2:11 For who of men knows the things of the man, except the spirit of the man in him? So also the things of God no one knows, except the spirit of God.
1CO 2:12 But we received not the spirit of the world, but the spirit from God; that we should know the things being granted to us by God.
1CO 2:13 Which also we speak, not in words instructed by human wisdom, but by words instructed of holy spirit - spiritual things being interpreted in spiritual ways.
1CO 2:14 But the physical man does not receive the things of the spirit of God; for they are moronishness to him, and he is not able to know them, for they are examined spiritually.
1CO 2:15 But the spiritual one examines indeed all things, but he is examined by no one.
1CO 2:16 For who knew the mind of the Lord? Who instructs him? But we have the mind of Christ.
1CO 3:1 And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual ones, but as fleshly ones, as infants in Christ.
1CO 3:2 I gave you milk to drink, and not food; for not yet were you able, and neither yet now are you able.
1CO 3:3 For you are still fleshly ones. For where among you are jealousy, and strife, and discord; are you not fleshly ones, and walk according to man?
1CO 3:4 For whenever one should say, I indeed am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are you not fleshly ones?
1CO 3:5 Who then is Paul, and who Apollos, but only servants through whom you believed, and to each as the Lord gave?
1CO 3:6 I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave growth.
1CO 3:7 So that neither the one planting is anything, nor the one watering; but the one giving growth is God.
1CO 3:8 And the one planting and the one watering are one; and each shall receive his own wage according to his own toil.
1CO 3:9 For we are fellow-workers of God; of God's farm. You are God's construction.
1CO 3:10 According to the favor of God being given to me, as a wise architect, I set the foundation, and another builds. But let each take heed how he builds!
1CO 3:11 For another foundation no one is able to set except the one being laid, which is Jesus Christ.
1CO 3:12 And if anyone builds upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass, stubble;
1CO 3:13 the work of each shall become apparent. For the day will manifest it, for by fire it is revealed; and of each work the fire shall prove what it is like.
1CO 3:14 If anyone's work abides which he built upon, he shall receive a wage.
1CO 3:15 If anyone's work shall be incinerated, he shall suffer loss. But he shall be delivered; but thus as through fire.
1CO 3:16 Know you not that you are a temple of God, and the spirit of God lives in you?
1CO 3:17 If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God shall corrupt this one; for the temple of God is holy, which you are.
1CO 3:18 Let no one cheat himself! If anyone thinks himself to be wise among you in this eon, let him become moronish, that he should become wise!
1CO 3:19 For the wisdom of this world is moronishness with God. For it has been written, He is the one grabbing the wise ones in their cleverness.
1CO 3:20 And again, The Lord knows the devices of the wise ones, that they are vain.
1CO 3:21 So that let no one boast among men! For all things are yours.
1CO 3:22 Whether Paul, whether Apollos, whether Cephas, whether the world, whether life, whether death, whether things present, whether things about to be - all are yours;
1CO 3:23 but you are of Christ, and Christ of God.
1CO 4:1 So let a man consider us as assistants of Christ, and managers of the mysteries of God!
1CO 4:2 But remaining, it is sought in the managers that one should be found trustworthy.
1CO 4:3 But to me it is a least thing that I should be examined by you, or by a human's day. But, not even myself do I examine.
1CO 4:4 For nothing by myself am I fully conscious; but not in this have I been justified. But the one examining me is the Lord.
1CO 4:5 So that judge not anything before its time! until whenever the Lord should come, who both will give light to the hidden things of the darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts. And then the high praise shall be to each from God.
1CO 4:6 And these things, brothers, I changed appearance to myself and to Apollos on account of you; that in us you should learn not to think above what has been written, that not one over one you be inflated against the other.
1CO 4:7 For who scrutinizes you? and what do you have which you have not received? and if also you received, why do you boast, as not having received?
1CO 4:8 Are you already satisfied? are you already enriched? do you reign apart from us? And I ought indeed that you reigned, that also we with you should have reigned together.
1CO 4:9 For I think that God exhibited us apostles last, as condemned to death. For we became a theater to the world, and to angels, and to men.
1CO 4:10 We are moronish on account of Christ, but you are skilled in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honorable, but we are without honor.
1CO 4:11 As far as the present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and unsettled;
1CO 4:12 and we tire working with our own hands. Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we endure;
1CO 4:13 being blasphemed, we appeal; as the rubbish of the world, we were of all the sweepings until now.
1CO 4:14 Not shaming you do I write these things, but as my beloved children I admonish.
1CO 4:15 For if you should have ten thousand instructors in Christ, but not many fathers. For in Christ Jesus through the good news I engendered you.
1CO 4:16 I appeal to you then, become imitators of me!
1CO 4:17 On account of this I send to you Timothy, who is my beloved child, and trustworthy in the Lord, who shall remind you of my ways in Christ, as everywhere in every assembly I teach.
1CO 4:18 And as to my not coming to you, some were inflated.
1CO 4:19 But I shall come quickly to you, if the Lord should want, and I will know, not the word of the ones being inflated, but the power.
1CO 4:20 For not is the kingdom of God in word, but in power.
1CO 4:21 What do you want? Should I come with a rod to you, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?
1CO 5:1 Harlotry is wholly heard among you, and such harlotry which not even among the nations is named, so as for one to have his father's wife.
1CO 5:2 And you, are you being inflated, and not rather mourned, that the one having done this work should be removed from your midst.
1CO 5:3 For indeed I (as being absent in the body, but being at hand in the spirit,) already have judged as one being at hand, concerning the one thus manufacturing this,
1CO 5:4 in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, having brought together you and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1CO 5:5 to deliver up such to Satan for ruin of the flesh, that the spirit should be delivered in the day of the Lord Jesus.
1CO 5:6 Your boasting is not good. Know you not that a little yeast leavens the entire batch?
1CO 5:7 Clear out then the old yeast, that you should be a new batch - as you are unleavened breads! For indeed Christ our passover was sacrificed for us.
1CO 5:8 So that we should solemnize a holiday, not with old yeast, nor with yeast of evil and wickedness; but with unleavened breads of honesty and truth.
1CO 5:9 I wrote to you in the letter not to intermingle with fornicators.
1CO 5:10 But not assuredly with the fornicators of this world, or with the hoarders of wealth, or predacious, or idolaters; since you ought then to come forth from out of the world.
1CO 5:11 But now I wrote to you to not intermingle (if any brother being named, be a fornicator, or a hoarder of wealth, or an idolater, or a reviler, or an intoxicated person, or predacious) with the one such - nor to eat with.
1CO 5:12 For what is it to me and the ones outside to judge, shall you not judge the ones inside?
1CO 5:13 But the ones outside God judges. And you shall lift away the wicked one from you of them.
1CO 6:1 Dare any one of you, having a thing against the other, plead before the unjust, and not before the holy ones?
1CO 6:2 Know you not that the holy ones shall judge the world? And if by you the world is judged, are you unworthy of the judgment seat of the least?
1CO 6:3 Know you not that we shall judge angels? How much more indeed of the cares of life?
1CO 6:4 If you have then the judgment seat as to the cares of life of the ones being treated with contempt, then do you sit of these in the assembly?
1CO 6:5 To make you ashamed I speak. So is there not one among you being a wise one, nor one who is able to litigate between his brother?
1CO 6:6 But brother against brother goes to law, and this before unbelievers.
1CO 6:7 Already indeed then utterly there is failure among you, for you have lawsuits with yourselves. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be deprived?
1CO 6:8 But you do wrong, and deprive - and these things of brothers.
1CO 6:9 Or know you not that the unjust shall not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be misled. Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor soft, nor homosexuals,
1CO 6:10 nor thieves, nor hoarders of wealth, nor intoxicated ones, not revilers, not predacious, shall inherit the kingdom of God.
1CO 6:11 And some of you were these. But you were washed off, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the spirit of our God.
1CO 6:12 All things to me are allowed, but not all advantageous. All things to me are allowed, but I shall not be brought under the authority by any.
1CO 6:13 The foods are for the belly, and the belly for the foods; but God will render useless both this body and these foods. But the body is not for harlotry, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.
1CO 6:14 And God raised up also the Lord, and will awaken us through his power.
1CO 6:15 Know you not that your bodies are members of Christ? Having taken then the members of the Christ, shall I make them members of a harlot? May it not be.
1CO 6:16 Or, know you not that the one cleaving to the harlot, is one body? For he says the two shall be for one flesh.
1CO 6:17 But the one cleaving to the Lord is one spirit.
1CO 6:18 Flee harlotry! Every sin which ever a man should commit is outside of the body, but the one committing harlotry sins against his own body.
1CO 6:19 Or, know you not that your body is a temple of the holy spirit in you, which you have from God, and you are not your own?
1CO 6:20 For you were bought of value. Glorify God indeed in your body, and in your spirit, which is the one of God!
1CO 7:1 But concerning what you wrote to me. It is good for a man to not touch a woman.
1CO 7:2 But because of the harlotries, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband!
1CO 7:3 Let the husband render to the wife the good-will owed; and in like manner also the wife to the husband!
1CO 7:4 The wife does not exercise authority of her own body, but the husband. And in like manner also the husband does not exercise authority of his own body, but the wife.
1CO 7:5 Do not deprive one another, except for harmony's sake for a time, that you should relax in the fasting, and in the prayer! And again at the same time you should come together, that Satan should not test you because of your intemperance.
1CO 7:6 But this I say according to allowance, not according to command.
1CO 7:7 For I want all men to be as even myself. But each has his own favor from God - one so, and another so.
1CO 7:8 But I say to the unmarried and to the widows, it is good for them if they remain as even I.
1CO 7:9 But if they control not, let them marry! For it is better to marry than to be set on fire.
1CO 7:10 And to the ones being married I exhort, not I, but the Lord - a wife to not separate from a husband.
1CO 7:11 But if even she should separate, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to the husband! And a man's wife is not to be let go.
1CO 7:12 And to the rest I say, not the Lord. If any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she assents to live with him, he is not to leave her!
1CO 7:13 And a woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he assents to live with her, she is not to leave him!
1CO 7:14 For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband. Since then your children are unclean - but now are holy.
1CO 7:15 But if the unbeliever separates, let him be separated! The brother is not enslaved, or the sister in such cases. But in peace God has called us.
1CO 7:16 For what do you know, O wife, if you shall deliver the husband? Or what do you know, O husband, if you shall deliver the wife?
1CO 7:17 Except to each as God portioned - so let each walk as the Lord called! And so in all the assemblies I set an order.
1CO 7:18 Who is called while being circumcised, let him not become uncircumcised! Who is called in uncircumcision, let him not be circumcised!
1CO 7:19 Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping the commandments of God is.
1CO 7:20 Each in the calling in which he was called - in this let him abide!
1CO 7:21 A slave being called - let it not be a care. But if even you are able to be free, rather use it!
1CO 7:22 For the slave being called in the Lord is the Lord's freedman. In like manner also the free one being called, is Christ's slave.
1CO 7:23 Of value you were bought; do not become slaves of men!
1CO 7:24 Each in which he was called, brothers, in this abide with God!
1CO 7:25 And concerning the virgins I do not have a command of the Lord. But an opinion I give as one being shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.
1CO 7:26 I think then this existing is good because of the present necessity, that it is good for a man so to be.
1CO 7:27 Have you been tied to a wife, do not seek a loosening! Have you been untied from a wife, do not seek a wife!
1CO 7:28 But if also you should marry, you sinned not; and if the virgin should have married she sinned not. But affliction in the flesh such shall have. But I spare you.
1CO 7:29 But this I say, brothers, the remaining time is wrapping up, that also the ones having wives, should be as not having.
1CO 7:30 And the ones weeping, as not weeping; and the ones rejoicing, as not rejoicing; and the ones buying, as not holding possessions;
1CO 7:31 and the ones dealing in this world, as not abusing it. For the condition of this world passes by.
1CO 7:32 But I want you to be free from care. The unmarried is anxious for the things of the Lord, how he is pleasing to the Lord.
1CO 7:33 But the one married is anxious for the things of the world - how he pleases the wife.
1CO 7:34 The wife and the virgin are assigned a part even. The unmarried is anxious for the things of the Lord, that she might be holy, both in body and in spirit. But she having married is anxious for the things of the world, how she shall please the husband.
1CO 7:35 But this for your own advantage I speak, not that I should put a noose around you, but be undisturbed to the decent and well-occupied thing to the Lord.
1CO 7:36 But if anyone thinks to be disgraced over his virgin, if she should be advanced in years, and so it ought to be what he wants to do, he sins not - let them marry!
1CO 7:37 But the one who stands settled in the heart, not having necessity, but has authority concerning his own will, and this he has judged in his heart to give heed to his own virgin, well he does.
1CO 7:38 So that also the one giving in marriage does well; and the one not giving in marriage does better.
1CO 7:39 A wife is tied by law for as long a time as her husband lives; but if her husband should sleep, she is free to whom she wants to marry; only in the Lord.
1CO 7:40 But more blessed is she if so she should remain, according to my opinion. But I think I also have spirit of God.
1CO 8:1 And concerning the things sacrificed to idols - we know that we have all knowledge. Knowledge inflates, but love builds.
1CO 8:2 But if anyone thinks to know anything, nothing yet he knows as necessary to know.
1CO 8:3 But if anyone loves God, this one is known by him.
1CO 8:4 Concerning the food then of the ones sacrificing to idols - we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God except one.
1CO 8:5 For even if indeed there are ones being called gods, whether in heaven, whether upon the earth, (as there are many gods, and many lords,)
1CO 8:6 but to us there is one God - the father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord - Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him.
1CO 8:7 But knowledge is not in all. But some in the conscience of the idol, until just now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to idols; and their conscience being weak is tainted.
1CO 8:8 But a food does not stand us before God. For neither if we eat do we abound; nor if we do not eat do we lack.
1CO 8:9 But take heed, lest perhaps this your authority becomes an occasion for stumbling to the ones being weak!
1CO 8:10 For if any should behold you, the one having knowledge, reclining in the temple of an idol, shall not his conscience being weak be built up for eating the things sacrificed to idols?
1CO 8:11 And the brother being weak shall perish over your knowledge, for whom Christ died.
1CO 8:12 And thus sinning against the brothers, and striking their conscience which is weakened, you sin against Christ.
1CO 8:13 Therefore if a food causes my brother to stumble, in no way shall I eat meats into the eon, that I should not cause my brother to stumble.
1CO 9:1 Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
1CO 9:2 If to others I am not an apostle, but indeed I am to you; for you are the seal of my commission in the Lord.
1CO 9:3 My defense to the ones questioning me is this,
1CO 9:4 Do we not have authority to eat and to drink?
1CO 9:5 Do we not have authority to lead about a sister a wife, as also the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
1CO 9:6 Or only I and Barnabas have not authority to not work?
1CO 9:7 Who soldiers by his own rations at any time? who plants a vineyard, and from the fruit of it does not eat? or who tends a flock, and from the milk of the flock does not eat?
1CO 9:8 Is it according to a man these things I speak? or does not also the law say these things?
1CO 9:9 For in the law of Moses it has been written, You shall not muzzle an ox threshing. Is not the ox a care to God?
1CO 9:10 Or because of us assuredly it says? For because of us it was written that, The one plowing ought to plow in hope, and the one threshing in hope is to partake of the thing of his hope.
1CO 9:11 If we sowed the spiritual things to you, is it a great thing if we harvest your fleshly things?
1CO 9:12 If others partake of the authority over you, should not we more? But we did not use this authority; but all things we hold off, that we should not give any hindrance to the good news of the Christ.
1CO 9:13 Know you not that the ones working at the temple shall eat the consecrated things? and the ones taking care of the altar receive a portion of the altar?
1CO 9:14 So also the Lord set in order to the ones announcing the good news, to live from the announcing of the good news.
1CO 9:15 But I used none of these things. But I wrote not these things, that thus it should happen with me. For it is good for me rather to die, than that anyone should nullify my boasting.
1CO 9:16 For if I announce good news, there is not a boasting to me; for a necessity is pressed upon me; but it is woe to me if I should not announce good news.
1CO 9:17 For if I willingly do this, I have a wage; but if unwillingly, I am entrusted with a management.
1CO 9:18 What then to me is the wage? That announcing good news freely I should establish the good news of the Christ, for the not abusing my authority in the good news.
1CO 9:19 For being free from all, I enslaved myself to all, that the many more I should gain.
1CO 9:20 And I became to the Jews as a Jew, that I should gain the Jews; to the ones under law, as myself under law, that the ones under law I should gain;
1CO 9:21 to the lawless ones, as a lawless one, (not being lawless to God, but lawful to Christ,) that I should gain the lawless ones.
1CO 9:22 I became to the weak as weak, that the weak I should gain. To all these I have become all things, that assuredly some I should deliver.
1CO 9:23 But this I do on account of the good news, that I should become a fellow-partaker with him.
1CO 9:24 Know you not that the ones running in the stadium, all indeed run, but one receives the victory prize? Thus you run that you should overtake!
1CO 9:25 But every athlete struggling, in all things controls himself; that indeed then that a corruptible crown they should receive; but we an incorruptible crown.
1CO 9:26 I therefore so run, as not uncertainly; so I box, as not flaying the air.
1CO 9:27 But I bruise my body, and bring it into slavery; lest to others having proclaimed, myself I should be debased.
1CO 10:1 But I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, but know that our fathers all were under the cloud, and all went through the sea;
