1CO 10:2 and all unto Moses were immersed in the cloud and in the sea;
1CO 10:3 and all ate the same spiritual food;
1CO 10:4 and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from a spiritual rock following. And the rock was the Christ.
1CO 10:5 But not with the most of them did God think well of; for they were prostrated in the wilderness.
1CO 10:6 But these things became models for us, for us not to be cravers of evils, as those also were cravers.
1CO 10:7 Neither become idolaters, as some of them; as it has been written, The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
1CO 10:8 Neither should we commit harlotry, as some of them committed harlotry, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
1CO 10:9 Neither should we put to test the Christ, as also some of them tested, and by the serpents perished.
1CO 10:10 Neither grumble, as also some of them grumbled, and perished by the annihilator!
1CO 10:11 And these things all came to pass to them as models. And they were written for our admonition, unto whom the ends of the eons are arrived.
1CO 10:12 So that the one thinking to stand take heed lest he should fall!
1CO 10:13 A test has not taken you except what belongs to a human. But God is trustworthy, who will not allow you to be tested above what you are able; but will make with the test also the result for you to be able to endure.
1CO 10:14 Therefore, my beloved, flee from the idolatry!
1CO 10:15 As practical I speak; you judge what I say!
1CO 10:16 The cup of the blessing which we bless, is it not fellowship of the blood of the Christ? The bread which we break, is it not fellowship of the body of the Christ?
1CO 10:17 For as one bread, we the many are one body; for we all partake of the one bread.
1CO 10:18 Look at Israel according to the flesh! Are not the ones eating the sacrifices partners of the altar?
1CO 10:19 What then say I? that an idol is anything, or that what is sacrificed to an idol is anything?
1CO 10:20 But that which the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons, and not to God. But I do not want you to become partners of the demons.
1CO 10:21 You are not able to drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of demons. You are not able to partake of the table of the Lord, and the table of demons.
1CO 10:22 Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
1CO 10:23 All things to me are allowed, but not all things are advantageous. All things to me are allowed, but not all things build up.
1CO 10:24 Let no one seek of himself, but each the thing of the other.
1CO 10:25 Everything in the market place being sold eat of! questioning nothing on account of conscience.
1CO 10:26 For of the Lord is the earth, and the fullness of it.
1CO 10:27 And if anyone invite you of the unbelieving ones, and you want to go; all being placed near you eat of, questioning nothing on account of conscience!
1CO 10:28 But if anyone should say to you, This is sacrificed to idols, do not eat on account of that one indicating, and conscience sake! For of the Lord is the earth, and the fullness of it.
1CO 10:29 But conscience, I say, is not the one of yourself, but the one of the other. For why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?
1CO 10:30 If I partake in favor, why am I blasphemed for what I give thanks?
1CO 10:31 Whether then you eat, or whether you drink, or whether anything you do, do all unto the glory of God!
1CO 10:32 Become not a cause for stumbling - even to Jews, even to Greeks, even to the assembly of God!
1CO 10:33 as even I please all men in all things, not seeking for myself advantage, but the advantage for the many, that they should be delivered.
1CO 11:1 Become mimics of me, as even I of Christ!
1CO 11:2 But I praise you, brothers, that in all things you have remembrance of me, and hold the traditions as I delivered to you.
1CO 11:3 But I want you to know, that the Christ is the head of every man; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.
1CO 11:4 Every man praying or prophesying, having anything on his head, disgraces his own head.
1CO 11:5 And every woman praying or prophesying with uncovered head, disgraces her own head; for it is one and the same as having been shaven.
1CO 11:6 For if a woman be not covered up, also let her be shorn! But if it be shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered up!
1CO 11:7 For indeed a man ought not to be covered of the head, being an image and glory of God. But a woman is glory of man.
1CO 11:8 For not is man of the woman, but the woman of man.
1CO 11:9 For man was not created on account of the woman, but the woman on account of the man.
1CO 11:10 Because of this the woman ought to have the authority upon her head on account of the angels.
1CO 11:11 Furthermore neither is man separate from woman, nor woman separate from man in the Lord.
1CO 11:12 For as the woman is from out of the man, so also the man is through the woman; but all things are from out of God.
1CO 11:13 Among you yourselves judge! Is it becoming for an uncovered woman to pray to God?
1CO 11:14 Or does not even nature itself teach you that a man indeed if he should have long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
1CO 11:15 But a woman, if she should have long hair is it a glory to her; for the hair of the head instead of a wrap is given to her.
1CO 11:16 But if anyone thinks to be contentious, we do not have such a custom, nor the assemblies of God.
1CO 11:17 But in this exhorting I do not praise you, for you do not come together for the better but for the worse.
1CO 11:18 For indeed first in your coming together in assembly, I hear of splits existing among you, and partly I believe it.
1CO 11:19 For must sects even be among you, that the ones approved should become apparent among you?
1CO 11:20 In your coming together then in the same place, is it not to eat the Lord's supper?
1CO 11:21 But each first takes his own supper in the eating, and one hungers, and another is intoxicated.
1CO 11:22 For do you not have houses for the eating and drinking? Or do you disdain the assembly of God, and disgrace the ones not having? What should I say to you? Shall I praise you in this? I do not praise.
1CO 11:23 For I received from the Lord what also I delivered up to you, that the Lord Jesus, in the night in which he was delivered up took bread.
1CO 11:24 And having given thanks, he broke it, and said, Take, eat! This is my body, being broken for you. This do in my remembrance!
1CO 11:25 Likewise also the cup, after having supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood. This do as often as you should drink in my remembrance!
1CO 11:26 For as often as you should eat this bread, and should drink this cup, the death of the Lord you announce until of which ever time he should come.
1CO 11:27 So that who ever should eat this bread or should drink the cup of the Lord unworthily will be liable of the body and blood of the Lord.
1CO 11:28 But let a man prove himself, and thus let him eat of the bread, and drink of the cup!
1CO 11:29 For the one eating and drinking unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discriminating the body of the Lord.
1CO 11:30 Because of this many among you are weak and ill, and a fit amount gone to sleep.
1CO 11:31 For if we examine ourselves we should not be judged.
1CO 11:32 But being judged by the Lord we are corrected, that we should not be condemned with the world.
1CO 11:33 So that, my brothers, coming together for the eating, let us look out for one another!
1CO 11:34 But if anyone hungers, let him eat in his house, that you should not come together for judgment! And the rest whenever I should come I shall set in order.
1CO 12:1 But concerning the spirituals, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.
1CO 12:2 You know that when you were nations, being led away to the voiceless idols even as you were led.
1CO 12:3 Therefore I make known to you, that no one speaking in spirit of God says, Jesus is anathema; and no one is able to say, Lord Jesus, except by holy spirit.
1CO 12:4 But there are divisions of favors, but the same spirit.
1CO 12:5 And there are divisions of services, and the same Lord.
1CO 12:6 And there are divisions of operations, but it is the same God operating all things in all.
1CO 12:7 And to each is given the open display of the spirit for advantage.
1CO 12:8 For indeed one through the spirit is given word of wisdom; and to another word of knowledge, according to the same spirit;
1CO 12:9 and to another belief, in the same spirit; and to another favors of cures, in the same spirit;
1CO 12:10 and to another operations of powers; and to another prophecy; and to another distinction of spirits; and to another types of languages; and to another translation of languages.
1CO 12:11 But all these operate by the one and the same spirit, dividing privately to each as he wills.
1CO 12:12 For just as the body is one, and has many members, but all the members of the one body, being many, are one body; so also the Christ.
1CO 12:13 For also in one spirit we all in one body were immersed, whether Jews, whether Greeks, whether slaves, whether free; and all into one spirit given to drink.
1CO 12:14 For also the body is not one member, but many.
1CO 12:15 If the foot should say that, I am not a hand, I am not of the body; it is not because of this it is not of the body?
1CO 12:16 And if the ear should say that, I am not an eye, I am not of the body; it is not because of this it is not of the body?
1CO 12:17 If all the body was an eye, where would be the hearing? If all was hearing, where would be the smelling?
1CO 12:18 But now God made the members, each one of them in the body, as he wanted.
1CO 12:19 But if it was all one member, where the body?
1CO 12:20 But now there are many members indeed, but one body.
1CO 12:21 And the eye is not able to say to the hand, I have not a need of you; or again the head to the feet, I have not a need of you.
1CO 12:22 But more rather, the members of the body which seem to be weaker are important;
1CO 12:23 and the ones which seem to be exceedingly without honor of the body, these we invest more extra honor; and our indecent parts have more extra decency;
1CO 12:24 but our decent parts have not a need. But God mixed together the body to the part lacking, having given it more extra honor,
1CO 12:25 that there might not be a split in the body; but that the members should have the same concern for one another.
1CO 12:26 And whether one member suffers, all the members suffer along; whether one member be glorified, all the members rejoice along.
1CO 12:27 But you are the body of Christ, and members in turn.
1CO 12:28 And whom indeed God appointed in the assembly, first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, thereupon works of power, then favors of cures, assistance, guidance, types of languages.
1CO 12:29 Not all are apostles. Not all are prophets. Not all are teachers. Not all are works of power.
1CO 12:30 Not all have favors of cures. Not all speak languages. Not all interpret.
1CO 12:31 But be zealous for the better favors. And yet I will show to you a way that exceeds.
1CO 13:1 If I speak the languages of men and of the angels, but I have not love, I have become brass resounding, or a cymbal sounding loudly.
1CO 13:2 And if I have prophecy, and I know the mysteries - all, and all knowledge; and if I have all belief, so as to remove mountains, but I have not love, I am nothing.
1CO 13:3 And if I should distribute all my possessions, and if I should deliver up my body that it should be burned, but I have not love, not one benefit do I derive.
1CO 13:4 Love is lenient, is kind; love is not jealous, love is not rash, not inflated,
1CO 13:5 not indecent, does not seek the things for itself, is not provoked, does not consider the bad;
1CO 13:6 does not rejoice at injustice, but rejoices with the truth;
1CO 13:7 all things it sustains, all things it trusts, all things it hopes, all things it endures.
1CO 13:8 Love at no time falls off. But whether prophecies, they shall cease work; whether languages, they shall cease; whether knowledge, it shall cease work.
1CO 13:9 But in part we know, and in part we prophesy.
1CO 13:10 But whenever the perfect should come, then the thing in part shall cease work.
1CO 13:11 When I was an infant, I spoke as an infant, I thought as an infant, I considered as an infant. But when I became a man, I ceased in the things of the infant.
1CO 13:12 For we see now by a mirror in an enigma; but then face to face. Now I know in part; but then I shall recognize as also I was recognized.
1CO 13:13 But now abide belief, hope, love, these three; but greater of these is love.
1CO 14:1 Pursue love, and be zealous for the spirituals! but more that you should prophesy.
1CO 14:2 For the one speaking a language speaks not to men, but to God. For no one hears him, but in spirit he speaks mysteries.
1CO 14:3 But the one prophesying speaks to men for edifying, and comfort, and consolation.
1CO 14:4 The one speaking a language edifies himself; but the one prophesying edifies the assembly.
1CO 14:5 But I want you all to speak languages, but more that you prophesy. For greater is the one prophesying than the one speaking languages, outside of unless he interprets, that the assembly should receive edification.
1CO 14:6 And now, brothers, if I should come to you speaking languages, what shall I benefit you, unless I shall speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in teaching?
1CO 14:7 Even the lifeless things giving a sound, whether pipe, whether harp, if they should not give a distinction to the tones, how shall the thing piped be known, or the thing being harped?
1CO 14:8 For also if a trumpet should give a concealed sound, who shall make preparations for battle?
1CO 14:9 So also you through the tongue, if you should not give a well-marked word, how shall the thing being spoken be known? for you will be speaking into air.
1CO 14:10 Since there are so many kinds of sounds by chance in the world, and none of them voiceless;
1CO 14:11 if then I do not know the ability of the sound, I will be to the one speaking a barbarian, and the one speaking with me a barbarian.
1CO 14:12 So also you, when you are zealous of spirits, seek that you should abound for the edification of the assembly!
1CO 14:13 Therefore let the one speaking a language pray that he should interpret!
1CO 14:14 For if I should pray in a language, my spirit prays, but my intellect is unfruitful.
1CO 14:15 What then is it? I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray also with the intellect. I will strum praise with the spirit, but I will strum praise also with the intellect.
1CO 14:16 Since if you should bless with the spirit, the one filling the place of the common person, how shall he say the Amen at your thanksgiving, since what you say he knows not?
1CO 14:17 For you indeed well give thanks, but the other is not edified.
1CO 14:18 I give thanks to my God, speaking languages more than all of you.
1CO 14:19 But in the assembly I want to speak five words through my intellect, that also others I should instruct, rather than ten thousand words in a language.
1CO 14:20 Brothers, be not children in the senses; but in evil act like infants, but in the senses become complete!
1CO 14:21 In the law it has been written that, In other languages, and by other lips I shall speak to this people; and neither thus shall they listen to me, says the Lord.
1CO 14:22 So that the languages are for a sign, not to the ones believing, but to the unbelievers. And prophecy is not to the unbelievers, but to the ones believing.
1CO 14:23 If then the entire assembly should come together in one place, and all speak languages, and there should enter common people or unbelievers, shall they not say that you are maniacal?
1CO 14:24 And if all prophesy, and there should enter some unbeliever, or common person, he is reproved by all, he is examined by all.
1CO 14:25 And thus the hidden things of his heart become open; and thus falling upon his face he does obeisance to God, reporting that God really is among you.
1CO 14:26 What then is it, brothers? Whenever you should come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a language, has a revelation, has a translation. Let all things be for edification!
1CO 14:27 Whether anyone speaks a language, let it be two, or the most three, and by turn; and let one interpret!
1CO 14:28 And if there should not be an interpreter, let him be quiet in the assembly; and let him speak to himself, and to God!
1CO 14:29 And prophets - let two or three speak, and the others scrutinize!
1CO 14:30 But if it should be revealed to another sitting by, let the first be quiet!
1CO 14:31 For you are able one by one all to prophesy, that all should learn, and all should be comforted.
1CO 14:32 For spirits of prophets submit to prophets.
1CO 14:33 For he is not the God of commotion, but peace, as in all the assemblies of the holy ones.
1CO 14:34 Let your wives in the assemblies be quiet, for not is it committed to their care to speak! But let them be submitted! as also the law says.
1CO 14:35 But if any shall want to learn, let them ask their own husbands in the house. For it is shameful for wives to speak in assembly.
1CO 14:36 Or, came forth from you the word of God? or to you alone it arrived?
1CO 14:37 If any thinks to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize what I write to you! that they are commandments of the Lord.
1CO 14:38 But if any be ignorant, let him be ignorant!
1CO 14:39 So that, brothers, be jealous to prophesy! and to speak languages be not restrained!
1CO 14:40 All things decently and according to order let be!
1CO 15:1 But I make known to you, brothers, the good news which I announced as good news to you, which also you received, in which also you stand;
1CO 15:2 through which also you are being delivered, if you take control what word I announced as good news to you - outside of unless in vain you believed.
1CO 15:3 For I delivered up to you at first that which also I received, that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
1CO 15:4 and that he was entombed, and that he was raised in the third day according to the scriptures;
1CO 15:5 and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
1CO 15:6 Thereupon, he appeared to above five hundred brothers at once; of whom the most remain until now, but some also are fallen asleep.
1CO 15:7 Thereupon he appeared to James; then to all the apostles.
1CO 15:8 And last of all, just as if to a miscarriage, he appeared also to me.
1CO 15:9 For I am the least of the apostles, whom I am not fit to be called an apostle, for I persecuted the assembly of God.
1CO 15:10 But by favor of God I am what I am. And his favor which was towards me has not become empty; but more extra than them all I tire in labor. But not I, but the favor of God with me.
1CO 15:11 Whether then I, or whether they, so we proclaim, and so you believed.
1CO 15:12 And if Christ is proclaimed that he has been raised from the dead, how say some among you that there is not a resurrection of the dead?
1CO 15:13 And if there is not a resurrection of the dead, not even Christ has been raised.
1CO 15:14 And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and empty also is the belief of yours.
1CO 15:15 And we are found even as false witnesses of God; for we witnessed concerning God that he raised the Christ. Whom he raised not, if indeed it is so the dead are not raised.
1CO 15:16 For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised.
1CO 15:17 And if Christ has not been raised, the belief of yours is in vain; you are still in your sins.
1CO 15:18 And then the ones having been fallen asleep in Christ perished.
1CO 15:19 If in this life only we are hoping in Christ, more pitiable than all men are we.
1CO 15:20 But now Christ has been raised from the dead - he became first-fruit of the ones sleeping.
1CO 15:21 For since through man death came, then through man came the resurrection of the dead.
1CO 15:22 For as all shall die in Adam, so also in the Christ all shall be restored to life.
1CO 15:23 But each in his own order. The first-fruit is Christ; thereupon the ones of the Christ at his arrival.
1CO 15:24 Then the end, whenever he should have delivered up the kingdom to the God and father; whenever he should clear away all rule and all authority and power.
1CO 15:25 For it is necessary for him to reign until of which ever he should have put all the enemies under his feet.
1CO 15:26 The last enemy cleared away is death.
1CO 15:27 For all things he subjected under his feet. But whenever it should say that all things have been subjected, it is manifest that it is outside of the one subjecting to him all things.
1CO 15:28 And whenever all the things should be subjected to him, then also he himself, the son, shall be subjected to the one having subjected to him all the things, that God should be the all in all.
1CO 15:29 Since what shall the ones being immersed for the dead do if wholly the dead are not raised? why also are they immersed for the dead?
1CO 15:30 Why also are we exposed to danger every hour?
1CO 15:31 Daily I die by your boasting, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
1CO 15:32 If according to man I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus, what benefit is it to me if the dead are not raised? We should eat and drink; for tomorrow we die?
1CO 15:33 Be not misled - evil companionships corrupt gracious morals.
1CO 15:34 Sober up righteously, and do not sin! for some have an ignorance of God - to your shame I speak.
1CO 15:35 But someone will say, How are the dead raised? and with what kind of body do they come?
1CO 15:36 Foolish one, what you sow is not restored to life unless it should die.
1CO 15:37 And what you sowed is not the body coming to pass which you sowed, but is a bare kernel - if by chance grain or some of the rest.
1CO 15:38 And God gives to it a body as he wants, and to each of the seeds its own body.
1CO 15:39 Not every flesh is the same flesh. But indeed other flesh is of men, and another flesh of cattle, and another of fishes, and another of birds,
1CO 15:40 and heavenly bodies, and earthly bodies. But another indeed is the glory of the heavenlies, and another is the ones of the earthly.
1CO 15:41 Another glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for star from star differs in glory.
1CO 15:42 So also the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruptibility.
1CO 15:43 It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
1CO 15:44 It is sown a physical body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a physical body, and there is a spiritual body.
1CO 15:45 So also it has been written, The first man Adam became a living soul; the last Adam into a spirit being restored to life.
1CO 15:46 But the spiritual was not first, but the physical; thereupon the spiritual.
1CO 15:47 The first man was from out of the earth, of dust; the second man, the Lord of heaven.
1CO 15:48 Such as the one of dust, such also the ones of dust. And such as the heavenly one, such also the heavenly ones.
1CO 15:49 And as we wore the image of dust, we shall wear also the image of the heavenly.
1CO 15:50 But this I say, brothers, that flesh and blood is not able to inherit the kingdom of God, nor can corruption inherit incorruptibility.
1CO 15:51 Behold, I speak a mystery to you; we shall not all indeed sleep, but all shall be changed,
1CO 15:52 in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For it shall trump, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
1CO 15:53 For it is necessary this corruption to put on incorruptibility, and this mortal to put on immortality.
1CO 15:54 But whenever this corruptible should have put on incorruptibility, and this mortal should have put on immortality, then shall come to pass the word having been written, Death was swallowed down in victory.
1CO 15:55 Where is your sting O death? Where is your victory O Hades?
1CO 15:56 And the sting of death is sin; and the power of sin is the law.
1CO 15:57 But to God be favor, to the one giving to us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO 15:58 So that, my beloved brothers, be settled, immovable, abounding in the work of the Lord at all times, knowing that your toil is not in vain in the Lord!
1CO 16:1 But concerning the collection for the holy ones, as I set in order to the assemblies of Galatia, so also you do!
1CO 16:2 According to one of the sabbaths each of you by yourself put in! treasuring up what ever way he should be prospered in; that not whenever I come then the collections should take place.
1CO 16:3 And whenever I should come, whom ever you should approve through letters, these I will send forth to carry away your favor unto Jerusalem.
1CO 16:4 And if it should be worth for me also to go, they shall go with me.
1CO 16:5 And I will come to you whenever I shall have gone through Macedonia; for Macedonia I do go through.
1CO 16:6 And with you by chance I shall remain, or even pass the winter, that you should send me forward of which ever place I should go.
1CO 16:7 For I do not want just now to see you in passing; but I hope for some time to remain with you, if the Lord commits it to my care.
1CO 16:8 But I shall remain in Ephesus until Pentecost.
1CO 16:9 For a door opens to me great and active, and the ones acting as adversaries are many.
1CO 16:10 And if Timothy should come, see that fearlessly he should be with you! for the work of the Lord he works, as also I.
1CO 16:11 Not anyone then should treat him with contempt, but forward him in peace, that he should come to me - for I look out for him with the brothers!
1CO 16:12 And concerning Apollos the brother, much I appealed to him, that he should come to you with the brothers; and assuredly it was not his will that now he should come; but he will come whenever he should have an opportune time.
1CO 16:13 Be vigilant! Stand firmly in the belief! Be manly! Be fortified!
1CO 16:14 Let all of you be in love!
1CO 16:15 But I appeal to you, brothers, (you know the house of Stephanas, that it is first-fruit of Achaia, and they arranged themselves for service to the holy ones,)
1CO 16:16 that also you should submit to such, and to all working together and tiring in labor.
1CO 16:17 And I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for the deficiency of yours these supplied.
1CO 16:18 For they rested my spirit and the one of yours. Recognize then such!
1CO 16:19 The assemblies of Asia greet you! Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, with the assembly in their house.
1CO 16:20 All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss!
1CO 16:21 The greeting by my hand, Paul.
1CO 16:22 If anyone is not fond of the Lord Jesus Christ, be anathema! Maranatha.
1CO 16:23 The favor of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
1CO 16:24 My love is with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
2CO 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the assembly of God being in Corinth, with all the holy ones being in all Achaia.
2CO 1:2 Favor to you and peace from God our father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2CO 1:3 Blessed be the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the father of compassions, and God of all comfort;
2CO 1:4 the one comforting us in all our affliction, for the enabling us to comfort the ones in every affliction, through the consolation of which we are comforted in ourselves by God.
2CO 1:5 For as the sufferings of the Christ abound in us, so through Christ our comfort also abounds.
2CO 1:6 But whether we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and deliverance, being energized in the endurance of the same sufferings which also we suffer,
2CO 1:7 (and our hope is firm for you;) or whether we are comforted, it is for your comfort and deliverance; knowing that as you are partners of the sufferings, so also of the comfort.
2CO 1:8 For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, over our affliction happening to us in Asia, that we were weighed down in excess, beyond power, so as for us to be destitute even of living.
2CO 1:9 But we have had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not be relying upon ourselves, but upon God, the one raising the dead.
2CO 1:10 Who from out of such a death rescued us, and does rescue; in whom we have hope that also still he shall rescue;
2CO 1:11 working along with you also for us by supplication, that by many persons the favor to us should be for giving thanks through many for you.
2CO 1:12 For this is our boasting - the testimony of our conscience, that in singleness and honesty of God, (not in fleshy wisdom, but by favor of God,) we behaved in the world, and more exceedingly to you.
2CO 1:13 For not another thing do we write to you, other than what you read or also recognize; and I hope that even until the end you will recognize;
2CO 1:14 as also you recognized us in part, that we are your boasting, just as also you are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
2CO 1:15 And in this reliance I was wanting to come to you prior, that a second favor you should have;
2CO 1:16 and by you to go through into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and by you to be sent forward into Judea.
2CO 1:17 This then planning, lest anything did I treat it in lightness? or what I planned, did I plan according to the flesh, that there might be by me the yes, Yes, and the no, No?
2CO 1:18 But trustworthy is God, that our word to you became not, Yes and No.
2CO 1:19 For the son of God, Jesus Christ, the one among you being proclaimed by us, (by me and Silvanus and Timothy,) was not Yes and No, but, Yes became in him.
2CO 1:20 For as many promises of God there are, in him is the yes, and in him the Amen, to God for glory by us.
2CO 1:21 But the one firming us with you unto Christ, and having anointed us, is God;
2CO 1:22 even the one setting a seal upon us, and having given the deposit of the spirit in our hearts.
2CO 1:23 And I call upon God as witness upon my soul, that sparing you no longer came I to Corinth.
2CO 1:24 Not that we dominate the belief of yours, but are fellow-workers of your joy - for in the belief you stand.
2CO 2:1 But I decided in myself this, not again to come in distress to you.
2CO 2:2 For if I grieve you, then who is the one gladdening me, unless it be the one being grieved by me?
2CO 2:3 And I wrote to you this same thing, lest, having come I should have distress from whom it behooved me to rejoice over; relying upon you all, that my joy is all of you.
2CO 2:4 For out of much affliction and conflict of heart I wrote to you through many tears; not that you should be grieved, but that you should know the love which I have more exceedingly towards you.
2CO 2:5 But if any has grieved, he has not grieved me, but in part; that I should not overburden you all.
2CO 2:6 This reproach by the many is enough to such a one.
2CO 2:7 So that on the other hand rather you are to grant favor and to comfort him, lest the more extra distress should swallow down such a one.
2CO 2:8 Therefore I appeal to you to validate love unto him.
2CO 2:9 For unto this also I wrote, that I should know your proof, if in everything you are subjects.
2CO 2:10 But to whom you grant favor in anything, so also I. For also I, if anything have granted favor, to whom I have granted favor, it is for your sake in the person of Christ;
2CO 2:11 that we should not be taken advantage of by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his thoughts.
2CO 2:12 Now, having come unto Troas for the good news of the Christ, even a door was opened to me in the Lord.
2CO 2:13 I did not have relaxation in my spirit at my not finding Titus my brother. But being sent off by them, I went forth into Macedonia.
2CO 2:14 But to God be favor at all times, causing us to triumph in the Christ, and making manifest the scent of the knowledge of him through us in every place.
2CO 2:15 For of Christ we are a pleasant aroma offering to God, among the ones being delivered, and among the ones perishing.
2CO 2:16 To some, a scent of death to death; but to some a scent of life to life. And for these things who is fit?
2CO 2:17 For not are we as the rest, peddling the word of God. But as from honesty, but as of God, before God in Christ we speak.
2CO 3:1 Do we begin again to commend ourselves? unless we need, as some, of introductory letters to you, or introductory letters from you?
2CO 3:2 You are our letter being written in our hearts, being known and being read by all men;
2CO 3:3 being manifested that you are Christ's letter served by us, having been written not with ink, but by spirit of the living God; not on tablets of stones, but on fleshly tablets of the heart.
2CO 3:4 And such reliance we have through the Christ towards God.
2CO 3:5 Not that we are fit of ourselves to consider anything as from out of ourselves; but our fitness is of God;
2CO 3:6 who also made us fit servants of a new covenant; not of contract, but of spirit. For the contract kills, but the spirit restores to life.
2CO 3:7 And if the service of death in contracts having been impressed in stones, happened for glory, so as for the sons of Israel to not be able to gaze into the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, the glory being cleared away;
2CO 3:8 how not more the service of the spirit will be in glory?
2CO 3:9 For if the service of condemnation be glory, much rather abounds the service of righteousness in glory.
2CO 3:10 For also not even the thing having been glorified has been glorified in this part, on account of the exceeding glory.
2CO 3:11 For if the thing being cleared away was through glory, much rather the thing which remains is in glory.
2CO 3:12 Having then such hope, we deal in much confidence.
2CO 3:13 And not as Moses put a covering upon the face of himself, for the thing of the sons of Israel to not gaze unto the end of the thing being cleared away.
2CO 3:14 But their thoughts were calloused. For as far as today the same covering remains upon the reading of the old covenant, not uncovered, which in Christ is being cleared away.
2CO 3:15 But unto today, when Moses is read, a covering lies upon their heart.
2CO 3:16 But when ever it should turn towards the Lord, the covering is being removed.
2CO 3:17 And the Lord is the spirit. But where the spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
2CO 3:18 But we all with uncovered face are reflecting the glory of the Lord, the same image being transformed from glory unto glory, just as from the Lord of spirit.
2CO 4:1 Therefore, having this service, as we were shown mercy, we tire not.
2CO 4:2 But we forbade the hidden things of shame, not walking in cleverness, nor acting treacherously in the word of God; but by open display of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience of men before God.
2CO 4:3 But if even our good news is being covered, it is covered among the ones perishing.
2CO 4:4 In whom the god of this eon blinded the thoughts of the unbelieving, so as to not shine forth to them the illumination of the good news of the glory of the Christ, who is the image of the unseen of God.
2CO 4:5 For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus - Lord; and ourselves your bondmen for the sake of Jesus.
2CO 4:6 For God is the one having told light to radiate from darkness, who radiated in our hearts, for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God in the person of Jesus Christ.
2CO 4:7 But we have this treasure in earthenware vessels, that the excess of the power might be of God, and not of us.
2CO 4:8 We are in every way afflicted, but not having been restricted; perplexed, but not left destitute;
2CO 4:9 persecuted, but not abandoned; thrown down, but not destroyed;
2CO 4:10 at all times the slaying of the Lord Jesus in the body carrying round about, that also the life of Jesus in our body should be manifested.
2CO 4:11 For continually, we the living, are delivered up unto death on account of Jesus, that also the life of Jesus should be manifested in our mortal flesh.
2CO 4:12 So that indeed, death operates in us, but life in you.
2CO 4:13 And having the same spirit of the belief, according to the thing having been written, I believed, therefore I spoke; we also believe, therefore we also speak.
2CO 4:14 Knowing that the one having raised the Lord Jesus, also shall raise us through Jesus, and shall stand beside with you.
2CO 4:15 For all things are on account of you, that the favor superabounding through the many should cause thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
2CO 4:16 Therefore we tire not; but even if our outer man be corrupted, yet the inner man is restored day by day.
2CO 4:17 For the immediate lightness of our affliction, manufactures according to excess to excess an eternal load of glory to us;
2CO 4:18 of our not watching the things being seen, but the things not being seen; for the things being seen are temporary; but the things not being seen are eternal.
2CO 5:1 For we know that if our earthly house of the tent be rested up, we have a construction from God, a house not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.
2CO 5:2 For also in this we moan, longing to put on our dwelling-place of heaven;
2CO 5:3 if indeed also being clothed, we shall not be found naked.
2CO 5:4 For also we the ones being in the tent moan, being weighed down; since we do not want to be stripped, but to put on, that the mortal should be swallowed down by the life.
2CO 5:5 And the one manufacturing us for this same thing is God, the one also having given to us the deposit of the spirit.
2CO 5:6 Taking courage then at all times, and knowing that, while dwelling at home in the body, we are abroad from the Lord.
2CO 5:7 For we walk by belief, not by sight.
2CO 5:8 And we take courage, and take pleasure rather to be abroad from the body, and to dwell at home with the Lord.
2CO 5:9 Therefore also we strive earnestly, whether dwelling at home or whether being abroad, to be well-pleasing to him.
2CO 5:10 For all the ones of us must be manifested before the rostrum of the Christ; that each should receive the things of the body, as to what he practiced, whether good or whether bad.
2CO 5:11 Knowing then the fear of the Lord, we persuade men; but to God we have been made apparent; and I hope also in your consciences we have been made apparent.
2CO 5:12 For we do not commend ourselves again to you, but are giving you opportunity for boasting over us, that you should have something against the ones boasting in appearance, and not in heart.
2CO 5:13 For whether we were startled, it was to God. Or whether we were of a sound mind, it is for you.
2CO 5:14 For the love of the Christ constrains us; having adjudged this, that if one died for all, then all died;
2CO 5:15 and that he died for all, that the ones living no longer should live to themselves, but to the one having died for them and arising.
2CO 5:16 So that we from the present know nothing according to the flesh. And if also we have known Christ according to the flesh, but now no longer do we know him thus.
2CO 5:17 So that if anyone be in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things passed away; behold, all things have become new.
2CO 5:18 And all things are of God, of the reconciling us to himself through Jesus Christ, and having given to us the service of the reconciliation;
2CO 5:19 how that, God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself, not imputing to them their transgressions; and having put in us the word of the reconciliation.
2CO 5:20 For of Christ then we are ambassadors, as of God appealing through us; we beseech for Christ - be reconciled to God!
2CO 5:21 For the one not knowing sin, he made a sin offering for us; that we should be righteousness of God in him.
2CO 6:1 And working together also we appeal for you to not receive the favor of God in vain,
2CO 6:2 (for he says, In an accepted time I heeded you, and in the day of deliverance I helped you. Behold, now is a well-received time; behold, now is the day of deliverance;)
2CO 6:3 in no way giving a cause for stumbling in anything, that the service should not be scoffed at.
2CO 6:4 But in everything commending ourselves as God's servants, in much endurance, in afflictions, in necessities, in straits,
2CO 6:5 in strokes, in imprisonments, in commotions, in toils, in sleeplessnesses, in fastings,
2CO 6:6 in purity, in knowledge, in leniency, in graciousness, in holy spirit, in unpretentious love,
2CO 6:7 in the word of truth, in power of God, through the weapons of righteousness of the right and left,
2CO 6:8 through glory and dishonor, through evil report and good report; as deluded, and yet true;
2CO 6:9 as being not known, and yet being recognized; as dying, and behold, we live; as ones being corrected, and not being put to death;
2CO 6:10 as grieving, but continually rejoicing; as poor, but enriching many; as having nothing, and holding all things.
2CO 6:11 Our mouth has been opened to you, O Corinthians; our heart widened.
2CO 6:12 You have not been restricted by us, but in your feelings of compassion you have been restricted.
2CO 6:13 But the same compensation, (as to children I speak,) you be widened also.
2CO 6:14 Do not become yoked with a different kind - unbelievers. For what sharing is righteousness and lawlessness? And what fellowship light with darkness?
2CO 6:15 And what harmony Christ with Belial? Or what portion believing with unbelieving?
2CO 6:16 And what accord a temple of God with idols? for you are a temple of the living God; as God said that, I will dwell among them, and I will walk about; and I will be their God, and they will be to me a people.
2CO 6:17 Therefore come forth from out of the midst of them, and be separated, says the Lord, and touch not the unclean! and I will take you in.
2CO 6:18 And I will be to you for father, and you shall be to me for sons and daughters, says the Lord almighty.
2CO 7:1 Having then these promises, beloved, we should cleanse ourselves from all contamination of the flesh and spirit, completing holiness in fear of God.
2CO 7:2 Have space for us; no one we wronged, no one we corrupted, no one we took advantage of.
2CO 7:3 I speak not for condemnation. For I have described beforehand that you are in our hearts for the dying together and living together.
2CO 7:4 It is much to me to be in an open manner with you; it is much to me in boasting over you. I have been filled with comfort; I superabound in the joy over all our affliction.
2CO 7:5 For even our coming into Macedonia, our flesh had no relaxation, but in every way being afflicted; from outside - battles; from inside - fears.
2CO 7:6 But the one comforting the humble, comforts us - God, by the arrival of Titus.
2CO 7:7 But not only in his arrival, but also in the comfort in which he was comforted by you, announcing to us your longing, your grieving, your zeal for me; so as for me more to rejoice.
2CO 7:8 For if even I grieved you in the letter, I repent not, if even I repented. For I see that that letter, (if even for an hour,) grieved you.
2CO 7:9 Now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved into repentance. For you were grieved according to God, that in nothing you should suffer loss by us.
2CO 7:10 For distress manufactures an irrevocable repentance towards God unto deliverance; but the distress of the world manufactures death.
2CO 7:11 For behold, for this same thing you fretted towards God - how much it manufactured in you - even diligence, even defense, even indignation, even fear, even longing, even zeal, even punishment. In every way you commended yourselves to be pure in the matter.
2CO 7:12 Then if even I wrote to you, it was not because of the one doing wrong, nor because of the one being wronged, but because of the manifesting our diligence over you, for you before God.
2CO 7:13 On account of this we have been comforted over your comfort. But more exceedingly rather we rejoiced at the joy of Titus, that his spirit has been put at rest by all of you.
2CO 7:14 For if in anything I have boasted to him about you, I was not disgraced; but as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting unto Titus became truth.
2CO 7:15 And his feelings of compassion are more exceedingly towards you, calling to mind the obedience of all of you, as you received him with fear and trembling.
2CO 7:16 I rejoice that in everything I take courage in you.
2CO 8:1 But we make known to you, brothers, the favor of God having been given in the assemblies of Macedonia;
2CO 8:2 that in much proof of affliction, the abundance of their joy, and the depth according to their poorness, abounded to the riches of their simplicity.
2CO 8:3 For according to their power, I witness, and above their power their enthusiasiam,
2CO 8:4 with much consolation beseeching of us the favor and the fellowship of the service for the holy ones, for us to receive it.
2CO 8:5 And not only as we hoped, but of themselves they gave first to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.
2CO 8:6 So that we appealed to Titus, that as he began before, so also he should complete with you also this favor.
2CO 8:7 But as in every way you abound, in belief, and word, and knowledge, and all diligence, and in the love from you to us, that also in this favor you should abound.
2CO 8:8 Not according to command I speak, but through the diligence of others, and the proving of the genuineness of your love.
2CO 8:9 For you know the favor of our Lord Jesus Christ, that for you he became poor - being rich; that you by that ones poorness should be enriched.
2CO 8:10 And an opinion in this I give; for this is advantageous to you, who not only the doing, but also the wanting, began before a year ago.
2CO 8:11 But now also the doing - complete it! So that just as the eagerness of the thing wanted, so also the completing of the having it.
2CO 8:12 For if the eagerness is situated, according to that which ever anyone should have - has., it is well-received, it is not according to that which he does not have.
2CO 8:13 For it is not that others have liberty, but to you affliction;
2CO 8:14 but from out of equality in the present time, that your abundance be for their deficiency, that also their abundance should be for your deficiency, so that equality should take place.
2CO 8:15 As it has been written, The one gathering much was not superabundant; and the one gathering few did not have less.
2CO 8:16 But gratitude be to God, to the one giving the same diligence for you in the heart of Titus.
2CO 8:17 For the comfort indeed he received; but more diligent, being enthusiastic, he came forth to you.
2CO 8:18 And we sent with him the brother, of whom the high praise is in the good news through all the assemblies;
2CO 8:19 and not only so, but also handpicked by the assemblies for our traveling companion with this favor, which is being served by us to the glory of the Lord himself and of your eagerness;
2CO 8:20 getting in readiness for this, lest anyone should scoff at us in the vigor by which this is being served by us;
2CO 8:21 thinking beforehand good things, not only before the Lord, but also before men.
2CO 8:22 And we sent together with them our brother, whom we approved being diligent often in many things, but now much more diligent, in much reliance towards you;
2CO 8:23 whether for Titus, my partner, and for you a fellow-worker; or whether of our brothers, apostles of assemblies, the glory of Christ.
2CO 8:24 The demonstration then of your love, and our boasting for you, demonstrate to them, and in front of the assemblies!
2CO 9:1 For indeed concerning the service for the holy ones, it is more extra for me to write to you.
2CO 9:2 For I know your eagerness, which I boast over you to Macedonia, that Achaia made preparations over a year ago; and the result of your zeal excited the many.
2CO 9:3 And I sent forth the brothers, lest our boasting over you should be nullified in this portion; that, as I said, you should be making preparations;
2CO 9:4 lest perhaps if Macedonians should come with me, and should find you unprepared, we should be disgraced, (so that we should not say - You) in this support of boasting.
2CO 9:5 I esteemed it important then to appeal to the brothers, that they should go forth unto you, and complete beforehand this your preannounced blessing, being prepared, thus as a blessing, and not as if a desire for wealth.
2CO 9:6 But this I say, The one sowing sparingly, also harvests sparingly; and the one sowing for blessings, for blessings also he shall harvest.
2CO 9:7 Let each do as he resolves in the heart, not from distress or from necessity; for God loves a happy giver.
2CO 9:8 And God is able to abound every favor unto you; that in every way, at all times you should abound having all sufficiency for every good work,
2CO 9:9 (As it has been written, He dispersed; he gave to the needy; his righteousness abides into the eon.
2CO 9:10 And the one supplying seed to the one sowing, even may he supply bread for food, and multiply your sowing, and may he increase the offspring of your righteousness;)
2CO 9:11 in every way being enriched in all simplicity, which manufactures through us thankfulness to God.
2CO 9:12 For the service of this ministration not only is filling up in addition the deficiencies of the holy ones, but also abounding through many thanksgivings to God;
2CO 9:13 through the proof of this service glorifying God by the submission of your acknowledgment offering to the good news of the Christ, and simplicity of the fellowship to them and unto all,
2CO 9:14 and their supplication for you, longing after you through the exceeding favor of God unto you.
2CO 9:15 And gratitude be to God over his inexpressible gift.
2CO 10:1 But I myself, Paul appeal to you through the gentleness and clemency of the Christ, who in person indeed am humble among you, and absent I take courage in you.
2CO 10:2 But I beseech you, the one not at hand, to take courage with the reliance which I consider to dare against some of the ones considering us as walking according to the flesh,
2CO 10:3 for walking in the flesh we soldier not according to the flesh.
2CO 10:4 For the weapons of our army are not fleshly, but mighty with God to the demolition of fortresses;
2CO 10:5 demolishing devices, and every height being lifted up against the knowledge of God, and captivating every thought into the obedience of the Christ;
2CO 10:6 and having in readiness to punish all disobedience, whenever your obedience should be fulfilled.
2CO 10:7 The things according to appearance do you take heed only? If anyone is persuaded in himself to be of Christ, let him consider this again of himself, that, as he is of Christ, so also we are of Christ.
2CO 10:8 For if also even more extra somewhat I should boast concerning our authority, (of which the Lord gave to us for construction, and not for your demolition,) I shall not be ashamed - disgraced.;
2CO 10:9 that I should not seem as if to frighten you through letters.
2CO 10:10 For the letters indeed, one says, are heavy and strong; but the arrival of his person weak, and the word being with contempt.
2CO 10:11 Let such consider this, that as we are in word through letters being absent, such are we at work when at hand.
2CO 10:12 For not do we dare to approve or compare ourselves to some of the ones commending themselves. But they notice not that they are measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves to themselves.
2CO 10:13 But we shall not boast to the things immeasurable, but according to the measure of the rule of which God portioned to us, a measure reaching as far as even of you.
2CO 10:14 For not as one not reaching do we overstretch ourselves to you, for unto you even we arrive with the good news of the Christ;
2CO 10:15 not boasting in things immeasurable in another's toils; but having hope, increasing of the belief of yours, to be magnified among you according to our rule in abundance,
2CO 10:16 to announce good news to the ones farther from you, and not to boast in another's rule already prepared.
2CO 10:17 But the one boasting, let him boast in the Lord.
2CO 10:18 For it is not the one commending himself that is approved, but whom the Lord commends.
2CO 11:1 I would you endure me a little folly; but even endure me!
2CO 11:2 For I am zealous for you with zeal of God. For I suited you to one husband, as a pure virgin to present to the Christ.
2CO 11:3 But I fear, perhaps as the serpent cheated Eve in his cleverness, so your thoughts should be corrupted from the simplicity of the one in the Christ.
2CO 11:4 For if indeed the one coming to proclaim another Jesus, whom we proclaimed not, or you received another spirit, which you received not from us; or another good news, which you received not from us - well you withhold from it.
2CO 11:5 For I consider in nothing to be lacking of the more exceeding apostles.
2CO 11:6 And if even I be a common person in the communication, but I am not in the knowledge; but I am in every way making manifest in all things to you.
2CO 11:7 Or did I commit sin humbling myself that you should be exalted, that without charge I announced good news the good news of God to you?
2CO 11:8 Other assemblies I robbed, taking a ration for your service.
2CO 11:9 And being at hand with you, and being lacking, I was not lax of anyone. For my deficiency the brothers filled up in addition, having come from Macedonia; and in everything I kept myself easy to you, and I will keep it so.
2CO 11:10 It is the truth of Christ in me, that this boasting shall not be shut up in me in the regions of Achaia.
2CO 11:11 Why? because I do not love you? God knows.
2CO 11:12 But what I do, also I shall do, that I should cut off the opportunity of the ones wanting an opportunity; that in what they boast, they should be found as also we.
2CO 11:13 For such ones are false apostles, deceitful workers, changing appearance into apostles of Christ.
2CO 11:14 For it is not surprising for Satan himself to change appearance into an angel of light.
2CO 11:15 It is not a great thing then if even his servants change appearance as servants of righteousness; whom the end will be according to their works.
2CO 11:16 Again I say, no one should assume me to be foolish; but if not, indeed, if as foolish receive me, that I also should boast some a little!
2CO 11:17 What I now say, I say not according to the Lord, but as in folly, in this essence of boasting.
2CO 11:18 Since many boast according to the flesh, also I shall boast.
2CO 11:19 For with pleasure you endure the foolish ones, being practical.
2CO 11:20 For you endure if anyone reduce you to slavery, if anyone devours, if anyone takes, if anyone lifts up himself, if anyone flays you in the face.
2CO 11:21 According to dishonor I speak, as that we were weak. But in which ever anyone should be daring, (in folly I speak,) I also am daring.
2CO 11:22 They are Hebrews? I also. They are Israelites? I also. They are seed of Abraham? I also.
2CO 11:23 They are servants of Christ? (ranting I speak over,) I also in toils - more exceedingly; in beatings - above measure; in imprisonments - more exceedingly; in deaths - often.
2CO 11:24 By the Jews five times I received forty strokes save one.
2CO 11:25 Three times I was beaten with a rod, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, night and day in the deep I have spent,
2CO 11:26 in journeys often, in dangers of rivers, in dangers of robbers, in dangers from my race, in dangers from nations, in dangers in the city, in dangers in desolate places, in dangers in the sea, in dangers among false brothers,
2CO 11:27 in toil and trouble, in sleeplessnesses often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in chilliness and nakedness.
2CO 11:28 Separate from the things outwardly, there is the conspiring against me in the daily anxiety concerning all the assemblies.
2CO 11:29 Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is stumbled, and I am not on fire?
2CO 11:30 If I must boast, I will boast in the things of my weakness.
2CO 11:31 The God and father of the Lord Jesus Christ knows, (the one being blessed into the eons,) that I do not lie.
2CO 11:32 In Damascus the ethnarch of Aretas the king guarded the city of the Damascenes, wanting to lay hold of me.
2CO 11:33 And through a window in a cord basket I was let down through the wall, and fled from his hands.
2CO 12:1 To boast indeed is not an advantage to me. For I will come unto apparitions and revelations of the Lord.
2CO 12:2 I know a man in Christ fourteen years ago, (whether in body, I know not; or whether outside the body, I know not - God knows;) being seized by force was such a one unto the third heaven.
2CO 12:3 And I know such a man, (whether in the body, or whether outside the body, I know not - God knows;)
2CO 12:4 that he was seized by force into paradise, and heard sayings not made known, which is not allowed for a man to speak.
2CO 12:5 Concerning such a one I will boast; but concerning myself I shall not boast, unless in my weaknesses.
2CO 12:6 For if I should want to boast, I will not be a foolish one; for I shall speak the truth. But I spare, lest anyone should consider me above what he sees me to be, or hears anything of me.
2CO 12:7 And so that I should not be elevated over the excess of the revelations, there was given to me a barb in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, that he should buffet me, that I should not be elevated.
2CO 12:8 For this three times I appealed to the Lord, that it should abstain from me.
2CO 12:9 And he has said to me, Sufficient to you is my favor. For my power is perfected in weakness. Most gladly then rather I will boast in my weaknesses, that the power of the Christ should set up tent over me.
2CO 12:10 Therefore I think well in weaknesses, in insults, in necessities, in persecutions, in straits for Christ. For whenever I should be weak, then I am mighty.
2CO 12:11 I have become a foolish one boasting - you compelled me. For I ought to be commended by you; for in nothing was I lacking of the more exceeding apostles, if even I am nothing.
2CO 12:12 Indeed the signs of the apostle were worked among you in all endurance, in signs, and miracles, and works of power.
2CO 12:13 For in what is it that you were inferior beyond the rest of the assemblies, unless that I myself was not lax of you? Grant me this injustice!
2CO 12:14 Behold, a third time readily I have come to you; and I will not be lax of you. For I seek not the things of yours, but you. For the children ought not to treasure up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
2CO 12:15 And I most gladly will spend and expend for your souls; if even more exceedingly loving you, I be loved less.
2CO 12:16 But let it be! I did not burden you. But being clever, in cunning I took you.
2CO 12:17 Did by any whom I sent to you, through him take advantage of you?
2CO 12:18 I appealed to Titus, and sent along with him the brother. Did Titus take advantage of you in anything? Do we not walk by the same spirit? not in the same tracks?
2CO 12:19 Again, do you think that to you we make a defense? before God in Christ we speak. But all things, beloved, is for your edification.
2CO 12:20 For I fear perhaps having come I should find you not as I want, and I should be found by you such as you want not; lest perhaps there be strife, jealousies, rages, contentions, evil speakings, whisperings, inflation of minds, commotions;
2CO 12:21 and lest again having come, my God should humble me as to you, and I should mourn much of the ones previously sinning, and not having repented over the uncleanness and harlotry and lewdness which they practiced.
2CO 13:1 This third time I come to you. By the mouth of two witnesses and three every saying is established.
2CO 13:2 I have described beforehand, and say beforehand, as being at hand the second time; and being absent now I write to the ones who previously sinned, and to all the rest, that if I should come, for the again, I shall not spare;
2CO 13:3 since you seek a proof of the Christ speaking in me, which among you is not weak, but is mighty in you.
2CO 13:4 For even if he was crucified from out of weakness, yet he lives through power of God. For even we are weak in him, but we shall live with him by God's power among you.
2CO 13:5 Test yourselves, if you are in the belief! Try yourselves! Or do you not recognize yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you - except you are rejected.
2CO 13:6 But I hope that you know that we are not rejected.
2CO 13:7 But I make a vow to God for you to not do anything evil; not that we should appear approved, but that you should do good, and we might be as rejected.
2CO 13:8 For not are we able to do anything against the truth, but for the truth.
2CO 13:9 For we rejoice whenever we should be weak, but you should be mighty. But this also we make a vow - your readying.
2CO 13:10 On account of these things I write being absent, that being at hand I should not treat you severely, according to the authority which the Lord gave to me for edification, and not for demolition.
2CO 13:11 The rest, brothers, rejoice! Be readied! Be comforted! The same thing think! Make peace! And the God of love and peace will be with you.
2CO 13:12 Greet one another with a holy kiss!
2CO 13:13 All the holy ones greet you.
2CO 13:14 The favor of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the holy spirit, be with you all. Amen.
GAL 1:1 Paul, an apostle, (not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the father, the one raising him from the dead;)
GAL 1:2 and all the brothers with me, to the assemblies of Galatia.
GAL 1:3 5484 c\'ariVFavor to you and peace from God the father, and our Lord Jesus Christ,
GAL 1:4 the one giving himself for our sins, so as to rescue us from out of the present wicked age, according to the will of our God and father;
GAL 1:5 to whom be the glory into the eons of the eons. Amen.
GAL 1:6 I marvel that so quickly you are transferred from your calling in favor of Christ to another good news;
GAL 1:7 which is not another; except there are some disturbing you, and wanting to convert the good news of the Christ.
GAL 1:8 But even if we or an angel out of heaven should announce good news to you beyond which good news we announced to you, let him be anathema!
GAL 1:9 As we described beforehand, and just now again I say, If anyone announces good news to you beyond what you took to yourselves, let him be anathema!
GAL 1:10 For now, do I comply with men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if still I please men, I was not then Christ's bondman.
GAL 1:11 But I make known to you, brothers, the good news, the good news announced by me, that it is not according to man.
GAL 1:12 For I not even received it from man, nor was taught it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
GAL 1:13 For you heard my behavior at some time or other in Judaism, that according to excess I persecuted the assembly of God, and ravaged it.
GAL 1:14 And I progressed in Judaism beyond many contemporaries among my race, being exceedingly more zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
GAL 1:15 But when God thought well to separate me from out of the belly of my mother, and called me by his favor,
GAL 1:16 to reveal his son in me, that I should announce him good news among the nations; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood.
GAL 1:17 Nor went I up to Jerusalem to the apostles before me; but I went forth to Arabia, and again returned to Damascus.
GAL 1:18 Thereupon after three years I went up to Jerusalem to inquire of Peter, and I remained with him fifteen days.
GAL 1:19 But other apostles I saw not, except James the brother of the Lord.
GAL 1:20 And what things I write to you, behold, before God, that I do not lie.
GAL 1:21 Thereupon I came to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
GAL 1:22 And I was not known by face to the assemblies of Judea in Christ.
GAL 1:23 Only they were hearing that, The one persecuting us at one time, now announces good news - the belief, which at one time he ravaged.
GAL 1:24 And they glorified God in me.
GAL 2:1 Then after fourteen years again I ascended to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking along also Titus.
GAL 2:2 And I ascended according to revelation, and presented to them the good news which I proclaim among the nations, and in private to the ones assuming leadership, lest perhaps in vain I run, or ran.
GAL 2:3 But not even Titus, the one with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
GAL 2:4 And that on account of the intrusions of false brothers, who entered privately to spy out our freedom which we have in Christ Jesus, that they shall reduce us to slavery.
GAL 2:5 To whom not even for an hour we yielded way in the submission; that the truth of the good news should abide with you.
GAL 2:6 But from the ones seeming to be something, as to like whatever they were differs nothing to me. God does not take the person of a man; for the ones seeming important conferred nothing to me.
GAL 2:7 But on the other hand, having seen that I have been trusted with the good news of the uncircumcised, as Peter of the circumcision,
GAL 2:8 (for the one operating in Peter for commission of the circumcision, operated also to me among the nations.)
GAL 2:9 And knowing the favor being given to me, James, and Cephas, and John, assuming to be columns of strength, gave to me and Barnabas their right hands of fellowship, that we should go unto the nations, but they to the circumcision.
GAL 2:10 Only that we should remember the poor; which even I was hurried to do this same thing.
GAL 2:11 But when Peter came to Antioch in person, I opposed him, for he was for being condemned.
GAL 2:12 For before the coming of some from James, he was eating with the Gentiles. But when they came, he kept back and separated himself, fearing the ones of the circumcision.
GAL 2:13 And also the rest of the Jews acted the hypocrite with him; so that even Barnabas was led away by them in the hypocrisy.
GAL 2:14 But when I saw that he walked not uprightly to the truth of the good news, I said to Peter in front of all, If you, being Jewish-like, live like the nations and not like a Jew, why do you compel the nations to Judaize?
GAL 2:15 We are by nature Jews, and not sinners of the nations;
GAL 2:16 and knowing that man is not justified from works of law, but through belief of Jesus Christ, and we trusted in Christ Jesus, that we should be justified of belief of Christ, and not by works of law; For not shall any flesh be justified by works of law.
GAL 2:17 And if seeking to be justified in Christ, we have been found also ourselves sinners, is then Christ a servant of sin? May it not be.
GAL 2:18 For if what I deposed, these things again I build back up, I stand a violator myself.
GAL 2:19 For I through law died to law, that to God I should live.
GAL 2:20 5547 crist\'wI have been crucified with Christ. But I live; no longer I, but Christ lives in me. But that flesh which I now live in, I live in belief - in the one of the son of God loving me, and delivering himself up for me.
GAL 2:21 I do not annul the favor of God. For if righteousness is through law, then Christ died for nothing.
GAL 3:1 O unthinking Galatians, who charmed you to not yield to the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was written about beforehand, being crucified among you?
GAL 3:2 This only I want to learn from you, Was it from works of law you received the spirit, or by report of belief?
GAL 3:3 Are you so unthinking? commencing in spirit, you are now completed in flesh?
GAL 3:4 Did you suffer so many things in vain? if indeed even it be vain.
GAL 3:5 The one then supplying to you the spirit, and operates power in you - is it from works of law, or is it from report of belief?
GAL 3:6 As how Abraham trusted in God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness.
GAL 3:7 Know then that the ones of belief, these are sons of Abraham.
GAL 3:8 And the scripture saw at a distance that of belief God justifies the nations, advancing good news to Abraham, saying that, All the nations shall be blessed by you.
GAL 3:9 So that the ones of belief are blessed with the believing Abraham.
GAL 3:10 For as many as are of works of law, are under a curse. For it has been written, Accursed be all who do not adhere in all the things having been written in the scroll of the law to do them.
GAL 3:11 But that by law no one is being justified with God is manifest; for it says, The just one shall live of belief.
GAL 3:12 But the law is not of belief. But the man observing them shall live by them.
GAL 3:13 Christ bought us back from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us. For it has been written, Accursed is every one hanging upon a tree.
GAL 3:14 That to the nations the blessing of Abraham should take place in Christ Jesus; that the promise of the spirit we should receive through the belief.
GAL 3:15 Brothers, according to manman's system. I speak. Even a covenant of a man having been validated, no one annuls or adds further.
GAL 3:16 And to Abraham the promises were spoken, and to his seed. And he says not, to the seeds, as unto many; but as unto one, saying, And to your seed - which is Christ.
GAL 3:17 And this I say, that the covenant being validated before by God in Christ - the law taking place after four hundred and thirty years voids not so as to render the promise useless.
GAL 3:18 For if the inheritance is of law, no longer is it of promise; but to Abraham through promise God granted it.
GAL 3:19 Why then the law? It was added for favor of the violations, until of which time the seed should come to whom it has been promised; it was set in order by messengers in the hand of a mediator.
GAL 3:20 But the mediator is not one; but God is one.
GAL 3:21 Then is the law against the promises of God? May it not be. For if a law was given being able to restore life, then really the righteousness was then of law.
GAL 3:22 But the scripture consigned the whole under sin, that the promise of belief of Jesus Christ should be given to the ones trusting.
GAL 3:23 But before the belief coming, we were guarded by law, having been consigned to the about to be uncovering of belief.
GAL 3:24 So that the law has become our instructor up to Christ, that we should be justified of belief.
GAL 3:25 But of the belief having come, no longer are we under an instructor;
GAL 3:26 for you are all sons of God through the belief in Christ Jesus.
GAL 3:27 For as many as were immersed put on Christ.
GAL 3:28 There is not Jew nor Greek, there is not bondman nor free, there is not male and female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus.
GAL 3:29 And if you are of Christ, then you are of the seed of Abraham, and heirs according to promise.
GAL 4:1 And I say, for as long a time the heir is an infant, in no way does he differ from a bondman, though being master of all things.
GAL 4:2 But he is under caretakers and managers until the fixed day of the father.
GAL 4:3 So also us, when we were infants under the elements of the world, we were being enslaved.
GAL 4:4 But when came the fullness of the time, God sent forth his son, being born of a woman, being born under law,
GAL 4:5 that the ones under law he should buy back, that the adoption we should accept.
GAL 4:6 But because you are sons, God sent out the spirit of his son in your hearts, crying out, Abba father.
GAL 4:7 So that no longer are you a bondman, but a son; and if a son, also an heir of God through Christ.
GAL 4:8 But then indeed not knowing God, you were a slave to the ones not by nature being gods.
GAL 4:9 But now, having known God, but rather having been known by God, how do you return again unto the weak and poor elements, in which again as at the beginning you want to serve?
GAL 4:10 You closely watch days, and months, and times, and years.
GAL 4:11 I fear for you, lest perhaps in vain I have tired in labor for you.
GAL 4:12 I beseech you brothers become as I am for also I am as you! In nothing you wronged me.
GAL 4:13 But you know that through weakness of the flesh I announced good news to you formerly.
GAL 4:14 And my test in my flesh you treated not with contempt, nor rejected with contempt; but as a messenger of God you received me, even as Christ Jesus.
GAL 4:15 What then was your blessing? For I witness to you that if able, having gouged out your eyes you would have given them to me.
GAL 4:16 So then have I become your enemy, being truthful with you?
GAL 4:17 They are zealous for you, but not for well; but they want to exclude you, that you should be zealous for them.
GAL 4:18 But it is good to be zealous in good at all times, and not only in my being at hand with you.
GAL 4:19 My sons, whom again I travail as far as of which time Christ should have been formed in you,
GAL 4:20 and I wanted to be at hand with you just now, and to change my voice; for I am perplexed as to you.
GAL 4:21 Tell me, O ones wanting to be under law - Do you not hearken to the law?
GAL 4:22 For it has been written, that Abraham had two sons, one of the maidservant, and one of the free woman.
GAL 4:23 But the one indeed of the maidservant has been born according to flesh; but the one of the free woman was through the promise.
GAL 4:24 Which things are allegorized. For these are the two covenants; one indeed from mount Sinai, born in slavery, which is Hagar.
GAL 4:25 For Hagar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponding with the present Jerusalem, and she slaved with her children.
GAL 4:26 But the upward Jerusalem is free, which is mother of all of us.
GAL 4:27 For it has been written, Be glad, O sterile one not giving birth! Break asunder and yell, O one not travailing! For many are the children of the barren rather than of the one having the husband.
GAL 4:28 And we, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.
GAL 4:29 But as then the one born according to flesh persecuted the one born according to spirit, so also now.
GAL 4:30 But what says the scripture? Cast out the maidservant and her son! For not in any way shall the son of the maidservant inherit with the son of the free one.
GAL 4:31 So then, brothers, we are not children of the maidservant, but of the free one.
GAL 5:1 In the freedom then in which Christ freed us, stand firmly, and do not again be pressed upon with the yoke of slavery!
GAL 5:2 Behold! I Paul say to you, that if you should be circumcised, Christ shall derive you no benefit.
GAL 5:3 And I testify again to every man being circumcised, that he is a debtor to observe the entire law.
GAL 5:4 You were rendered useless from the Christ, O ones whoever are being justified by the law; you fell from favor.
GAL 5:5 For we in spirit of belief await the hope of righteousness.
GAL 5:6 For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision prevails any, nor uncircumcision; but belief operating through love.
GAL 5:7 You were running well; who hindered you to not comply with the truth?
GAL 5:8 The persuasion is not from out of him calling you.
GAL 5:9 A little yeast leavens the entire batch.
GAL 5:10 I am persuaded as to you in the Lord, that you shall not think any other way; and the one disturbing you shall bear the judgment, whoever he should be.
GAL 5:11 But I, brothers, if circumcision I still proclaim, why yet am I persecuted? Then the obstacle of the cross is cleared away.
GAL 5:12 Ought that they shall cut off the ones overthrowing you.
GAL 5:13 For you were called unto freedom, brothers; only not the freedom in opportunity in the flesh; but through the love serve one another!
GAL 5:14 For the whole law in one account is fulfilled, in the saying; You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
GAL 5:15 But if you bite one another and devour, take heed! lest by one another you should be consumed.
GAL 5:16 And I say, Walk in spirit! and in no way should you fulfill the desire of the flesh.
GAL 5:17 For the flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh. And these are an adversary to one another. That not what ever you should want to do these things you should do.
GAL 5:18 But if in spirit you be led, you are not under law.
GAL 5:19 And the works of the flesh are apparent, which are; adultery, harlotry, uncleanness, lewdness,
GAL 5:20 idolatry, sorcery, hatreds, strifes, jealousies, rages, contentions, discords, sects,
GAL 5:21 envies, murders, intoxications, debaucheries, and the things likened to these. Which I say beforehand to you, as also I foretold, that the ones practicing such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.
GAL 5:22 But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, leniency, graciousness, goodness, belief,
GAL 5:23 gentleness, self-control; against such things there is not a law.
GAL 5:24 But the ones of the Christ crucified the flesh with the passions and the lusts.
GAL 5:25 If we live in spirit, in spirit also we should be conformed to.
GAL 5:26 We should not become ones self-seeking of glory, challenging one another, bearing a grudge against one another.
GAL 6:1 Brothers, if even a man should be taken first in some transgression, you the spiritual ones ready such in spirit of gentleness! watching yourself lest also you should be tested.
GAL 6:2 Bear one another's loads! and so you shall fulfill the law of the Christ.
GAL 6:3 For if anyone thinks to be anything, being nothing, he deceives his own mind.
GAL 6:4 And let each try his own work, and then in himself only shall he have cause for boasting, and not as to another.
GAL 6:5 For each shall bear his own load.
GAL 6:6 And let the one being instructed in the word participate with the one instructing in all good things!
GAL 6:7 Be not misled! God is not to be sneered at. For whatever a man should sow, this also he shall reap.
GAL 6:8 For the one sowing to his own flesh, of the flesh shall harvest corruption; but the one sowing for the spirit, of the spirit shall reap life eternal.
GAL 6:9 And in doing good we should not tire; for in its own time we shall harvest, not fainting.
GAL 6:10 So then as we have occasion, we should work good to all, and especially to the members of the family of the belief.
GAL 6:11 Behold how great letters I wrote to you by my hand!
GAL 6:12 As many as want to have the right appearance in the flesh, these compel you to be circumcised; only that they should not be persecuted for the cross of the Christ.
GAL 6:13 For neither the ones being circumcised themselves guard the law; but they want you to be circumcised, that they should boast in your flesh.
GAL 6:14 But for me may it not be to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom to me the world has been crucified, and I to the world.
GAL 6:15 For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision prevails in anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
GAL 6:16 And as many as shall conform to this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
GAL 6:17 For the rest, let no one make troubles for me. For I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body.
GAL 6:18 The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
EPH 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, to the holy ones being in Ephesus, and believers in Christ Jesus.
EPH 1:2 Favor to you, and peace from God our father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
EPH 1:3 Blessed be the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the one having blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenlies in Christ.
EPH 1:4 As he chose us in him before the founding of the world, for us to be holy and unblemished before him in love.
EPH 1:5 Having predefined us for adoption through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good-pleasure of his will,
EPH 1:6 in high praise of the glory of his favor, in which he showed favor on us by the one being loved.
