EPH 1:7 By whom we have the release by ransom through his blood, the release of transgressions, according to the riches of his favor;
EPH 1:8 which he abounded in us in all wisdom and intelligence;
EPH 1:9 having made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good-pleasure which he purposed in himself,
EPH 1:10 for administration of the fullness of the times, recapitulating all things in the Christ - the things in the heavens, and the things on the earth, in him.
EPH 1:11 In whom also we were chosen by lot, being predefined according to the intention of the one operating all things according to the counsel of his will.
EPH 1:12 For us to be in high praise of his glory - of the ones hoping earlier in the Christ.
EPH 1:13 In whom you also, having heard the word of the truth - the good news of your deliverance; in whom also having trusted, you were sealed in the spirit of the promise in the holy,
EPH 1:14 which is the deposit of our inheritance, in a release by ransom of the procurement, in high praise of his glory.
EPH 1:15 Because of this, I also having heard the belief among you in the Lord Jesus, and the love towards all the holy ones,
EPH 1:16 cease not giving thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
EPH 1:17 that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the father of glory, should give spirit of wisdom to you and revelation in full knowledge of him;
EPH 1:18 giving light of the eyes of your thought, for you to know what is the hope of his calling, and what is the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the holy ones,
EPH 1:19 and what is the exceeding greatness of his power in us the ones believing, according to the energy of the might of his strength,
EPH 1:20 which he operated in the Christ, having raised him from the dead, and seated him at his right hand in the heavenlies,
EPH 1:21 above every sovereignty, and authority, and power, and lordship, and every name named, not only in this eon, but also in the one about to be.
EPH 1:22 And all things he submitted under his feet, and gave him to be head over all things to the assembly,
EPH 1:23 which is his body, the fullness of the one fulfilling all things in all.
EPH 2:1 And you being dead in transgressions and sins;
EPH 2:2 in which at one time you walked according to the eon of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit now operating in the sons of disobedience;
EPH 2:3 among whom also we all behaved at some time or other in the desires of our flesh, doing the wants of the flesh and the thoughts; and were children by nature of wrath, as even the rest.
EPH 2:4 But the God being rich in mercy, through the great love of his which he loved us,
EPH 2:5 and we being dead in the transgressions, are made alive together in the Christ, (by favor you are being delivered;)
EPH 2:6 and raised up together, and seated together in the heavenlies in Christ Jesus.
EPH 2:7 That he should demonstrate in the eons coming, the exceeding riches of his favor in graciousness upon us in Christ Jesus.
EPH 2:8 For by favor you are being preserved through the belief; and this gift of God is not of you -
EPH 2:9 not of works, lest any should boast.
EPH 2:10 For we are a thing made by him, being created in Christ Jesus for good works, the ones whom God prepared beforehand, that in them we should walk.
EPH 2:11 Therefore remember (that you at some time or other, the nations in the flesh, the ones being called the uncircumcision by the one being called the circumcision in the flesh made by hand,)
EPH 2:12 that you were in that time separate from Christ, being separate of the citizenship of Israel, and strangers of the covenants of the promise, not having hope, and atheists in the world!
EPH 2:13 But now in Christ Jesus, you, the ones at some time or other being far off, became near by the blood of the Christ.
EPH 2:14 For he is our peace, the one having made both one, and having loosed the partition of the barrier;
EPH 2:15 the enmity of the law of commandments in decrees he cleared away by his flesh, that the two he should create in himself into one new man, making peace;
EPH 2:16 and should reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the enmity by it.
EPH 2:17 And having come to announce good news of peace to you, to the ones far and to the ones near;
EPH 2:18 that through him we both have the access by one spirit to the father.
EPH 2:19 So then, no longer are you strangers and sojourners, but fellow-citizens of the holy ones, and members of the family of God;
EPH 2:20 being built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets - Jesus Christ himself being the one cornering;
EPH 2:21 in whom every construction fits together to grow into a holy temple in the Lord;
EPH 2:22 in whom also you are being built up together for a home of God in spirit.
EPH 3:1 For this favor, I Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus, for you of the nations,
EPH 3:2 if indeed you heard the administration of the favor of God having been given to me towards you;
EPH 3:3 that by revelation he made known to me the mystery; (as I wrote beforehand a little,
EPH 3:4 to which you are able reading to comprehend my understanding in the mystery of the Christ)
EPH 3:5 which unto other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as now it was revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in spirit;
EPH 3:6 for the nations to be joint-heirs, and joint-bodies, and joint-partners, of his promise in the Christ through the good news,
EPH 3:7 of which I became servant according to the gift of the favor of God given to me according to the energy of his power.
EPH 3:8 To me, the less than the least of all of the holy ones, was given this favor among the nations, to announce good news - the untraceable riches of the Christ;
EPH 3:9 and to enlighten all as to what is the fellowship of the mystery of the thing being concealed from the eons by God, to the one having created all things through Jesus Christ,
EPH 3:10 that the multifarious wisdom of God should be made known now to the sovereignties and to the authorities among the heavenlies through the assembly,
EPH 3:11 according to the intention of the eons, which he made in Christ Jesus our Lord;
EPH 3:12 in whom we have an open manner and access in reliance through the belief of his.
EPH 3:13 Therefore I ask not to tire in my afflictions for you, which is your glory.
EPH 3:14 For this favor I bend my knees to the father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
EPH 3:15 of whom every family in the heavens and upon earth is named,
EPH 3:16 that he should give to you, (according to the riches of his glory,) power to be fortified through his spirit, in the inside man;
EPH 3:17 for the Christ to dwell through the belief in your hearts, in love being rooted and founded;
EPH 3:18 that you should be competent to perceive with all the holy ones what is the width, and length, and depth, and height;
EPH 3:19 and to know the love of the Christ which exceeds knowledge, that you should be filled in all the fullness of God.
EPH 3:20 And to the one being able above all to do superabundantly what we ask or comprehend, according to the power operating in us,
EPH 3:21 to him be the glory in the assembly in Christ Jesus, to all the generations of the eon of the eons. Amen.
EPH 4:1 I appeal then to you, I the prisoner in the Lord, to walk worthily of the calling of which you were called,
EPH 4:2 with all humility and gentleness, with leniency, enduring one another in love;
EPH 4:3 hurrying to keep the unity of the spirit in the bonding together of peace.
EPH 4:4 One body, and one spirit, as also you were called in one hope of your calling;
EPH 4:5 one Lord, one belief, one immersion,
EPH 4:6 one God and father of all, the one over all, and through all, and in you all.
EPH 4:7 And in each one of us was given the favor according to the measure of the gift of the Christ.
EPH 4:8 Therefore he says, Having ascended into the height he captured the captivity, and he gave gifts to men.
EPH 4:9 (And the one that ascended, what is it unless that also he came down first unto the lower parts of the earth?
EPH 4:10 The one having come down, he is also the one having ascended up above all the heavens, that he should fulfill all things.)
EPH 4:11 And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; but some, shepherds and teachers;
EPH 4:12 for the readying of the holy ones for a work of service, for edification of the body of the Christ.
EPH 4:13 Until we should all arrive in the unity of the belief, and of the full knowledge of the son of God, in a perfect man, in the measure of the stature of the fullness of the Christ.
EPH 4:14 That no longer should we be infants, being swelled and carried round about by every wind of the instruction, in the cunning of men, in cleverness to the craft of the delusion;
EPH 4:15 but being truthful in love, we should grow into him in all things, which is the head - the Christ.
EPH 4:16 From whom all the body being fitted together and instructed by every ligament of the supply, according to energy in measure of each one part, be for the growth of the body to produce for itself to the construction of itself in love.
EPH 4:17 This then I say, and testify in the Lord, for you no longer to walk as also the rest of the nations walk, in the folly of their mind,
EPH 4:18 being darkened in the mind, being separated from the life of God, through the ignorance being in them, through the callousness of their heart;
EPH 4:19 who being numbed, delivered themselves up to lewdness, for a work of all uncleanness in a desire for wealth.
EPH 4:20 But you learned not thus the Christ;
EPH 4:21 if indeed you heard him, and were taught by him - as truth is in Jesus;
EPH 4:22 for you to put aside, according to the former behavior, the old man being corrupt according to the desires of the deception;
EPH 4:23 and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind;
EPH 4:24 and to put on the new man, the one according to God being created in righteousness and sacredness of the truth.
EPH 4:25 Therefore having put aside the lie, let each speak truth with his neighbor! For we are members of one another.
EPH 4:26 Be you angry? then do not sin! Do not let the sun set upon the provocation of your anger!
EPH 4:27 Nor give place to the devil!
EPH 4:28 The one stealing no longer let him steal! But rather let him tire working the good thing with the hands, that he should have something to share with the one having need!
EPH 4:29 Every rotten word from out of your mouth let not go forth! but if anything good for edification of the need - that it should give favor to the ones hearing.
EPH 4:30 And do not fret the holy spirit of God, in which you were sealed for the day of release by ransom!
EPH 4:31 All bitterness, and rage, and anger, and roaring, and blasphemy, take away from you with all evil!
EPH 4:32 And be to one another gracious, compassionate; granting to each other, as also God granted to us in Christ!
EPH 5:1 Become then mimics of God as beloved children!
EPH 5:2 And walk in love, as also the Christ loved us, and delivered himself up for us as an offering and sacrifice to God for a scent of pleasant aroma!
EPH 5:3 And harlotry, and all uncleanness, or desire for wealth, let it not be named among you, as is becoming to holy ones;
EPH 5:4 and indecency, and moronish talking, or obscene jokes not relating - but rather thankfulness!
EPH 5:5 For this you are knowing, that every fornicator, or unclean, or hoarder of wealth, who is an idolater, does not have an inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and of God.
EPH 5:6 Let not one of you be deceived with empty words! For on account of these things comes the wrath of God upon the sons of disobedience.
EPH 5:7 Do not then become joint-partners with them!
EPH 5:8 For you were at some time or other darkness, but now light in the Lord - walk as children of light,
EPH 5:9 (for the fruit of the spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth;)
EPH 5:10 distinguishing what is well-pleasing to the Lord!
EPH 5:11 And do not partake together with the unfruitful works of darkness - but rather even reprove!
EPH 5:12 For the things secretly taking place by them, it is shameful even to speak.
EPH 5:13 But all being reproved are made manifest by the light. For the thing manifesting all things is light.
EPH 5:14 Therefore he says, Arise, O sleeping one, and rise up from the dead, and the Christ shall shine upon you!
EPH 5:15 Take heed then how exactly you walk! not as unwise ones, but as wise ones,
EPH 5:16 buying back the time; for the days are wicked.
EPH 5:17 On account of this do not become foolish ones, but be perceiving what the will of the Lord is!
EPH 5:18 And be not intoxicated with wine, in which is carnality! But be filled in spirit!
EPH 5:19 speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual odes, singing and strumming in your heart to the Lord;
EPH 5:20 giving thanks at all times for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the God and father;
EPH 5:21 being submitted to one another in a fear of God.
EPH 5:22 Let the wives submit to their own husbands, as to the Lord!
EPH 5:23 For the husband is head of the wife, as also the Christ is head of the assembly; and he is deliverer of the body.
EPH 5:24 But as the assembly submits to the Christ, so also the wives to their own husbands in all things.
EPH 5:25 Let the husbands love their own wives, as also the Christ loved the assembly, and delivered himself up for it;
EPH 5:26 that he should sanctify it, having cleansed it in the bath of water by the word,
EPH 5:27 that he should present it to himself the honorable assembly, not having stain, or wrinkle, or any such things; but that it should be holy and unblemished.
EPH 5:28 So ought the husbands to love their own wives as their own bodies. The one loving his own wife loves himself.
EPH 5:29 For no one at some time or other detests his own flesh; but nourishes and comforts it, as also the Lord for the assembly.
EPH 5:30 For we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones.
EPH 5:31 For of this a man leaves behind his father and mother, and cleaves to his wife, and the two will be for one flesh.
EPH 5:32 This mystery is great - and I speak as to Christ, and as to the assembly.
EPH 5:33 Only also you, everyone, so let each love his own wife as himself; and the wife - that she should fear the husband!
EPH 6:1 The children - obey your parents in the Lord, for this is just!
EPH 6:2 Esteem your father and mother; (which is the first commandment in promise;)
EPH 6:3 that it should be good to you, and you will be a long time upon the earth!
EPH 6:4 And the fathers - do not provoke to anger your children, but nourish them in instruction and admonition of the Lord!
EPH 6:5 The bondmen - obey the masters according to flesh, with fear and trembling, in simplicity of your heart, as to the Christ!
EPH 6:6 not according to eyeservice, as ones who try to please men, but as bondmen of the Christ, doing the will of God from the soul,
EPH 6:7 with good-will serving as to the Lord, and not to men.
EPH 6:8 Knowing that what ever any good each should do, this he shall carry from the Lord, whether bondman or whether free.
EPH 6:9 And the masters - do the same things to them, sparing intimidation! knowing that also your own master is in heavens; and there is not discrimination with him.
EPH 6:10 For the rest, my brothers, be empowered in the Lord, and in the might of his strength!
EPH 6:11 Put on the full armor of God, for you to be able to stand against the craft of the devil!
EPH 6:12 For the wrestling is not to us against blood and flesh, but against the sovereignties, against the authorities, against the world rulers of the darkness of this eon, against the spirituals of the wickedness in the heavenlies.
EPH 6:13 On account of this take up the full armor of God, that you should be able to oppose in the wicked day, and all things being worked out, to stand!
EPH 6:14 Stand then, girding your loin in truth, and putting on the chest plate of righteousness;
EPH 6:15 and having sandals tied on the feet in preparation of the good news of peace;
EPH 6:16 upon all having taken up the shield of belief, in which you shall be able to extinguish all the arrows of the wicked one being setting on fire!
EPH 6:17 And receive the helmet of deliverance, and the sword of the spirit, which is God's word!
EPH 6:18 Through all prayer and supplication praying at every time in spirit, and in this same thing being sleepless with all attention, and supplication for all the holy ones;
EPH 6:19 and for me, that to me should be given a word in opening my mouth in an open manner, to make known the mystery of the good news,
EPH 6:20 for which I am an ambassador in a chain; that in it I should speak openly as necessary for me to speak.
EPH 6:21 But that you also should know the things concerning me, what I am doing - all things will be made known to you by Tychicus the beloved brother and trustworthy servant in the Lord.
EPH 6:22 Whom I sent forth to you for this very same thing, that you should know the things concerning us, and he should comfort your hearts.
EPH 6:23 Peace to the brothers, and love with belief, from God the father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
EPH 6:24 Favor be with all the ones loving our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility. Amen.
PHI 1:1 Paul and Timothy, bondmen of Jesus Christ, to all the holy ones in Christ Jesus being in Philippi, with the overseers and servants.
PHI 1:2 Favor to you, and peace from God our father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
PHI 1:3 I give thanks to my God for the memory of you all,
PHI 1:4 at all times in every supplication of mine for all of you, making supplication with joy,
PHI 1:5 for your fellowship in the good news from the first day until the present;
PHI 1:6 being persuaded in this same thing, that the one commencing in you a good work will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
PHI 1:7 as is just for me to think this as to you all, because of you having me in your heart; both in my bonds, and in the defense and security of the good news, you all being fellow-partakers of my favor.
PHI 1:8 For God is my witness, how I long after you all in feelings of compassion of Jesus Christ.
PHI 1:9 And this I pray, that the love of yours still more and more should abound in full knowledge and in all perception;
PHI 1:10 for you to approve the things differing; that you might be honest and without cause to stumble in the day of Christ;
PHI 1:11 being filled with fruits of righteousness by Jesus Christ, to glory and high praise of God.
PHI 1:12 But I want you to know, brothers, that the things concerning me rather in progression of the good news have come,
PHI 1:13 so as my bonds to become apparent in Christ in the whole praetorium, and to all the rest;
PHI 1:14 and the more of the brothers relying in the Lord, dare more exceedingly in my bonds to speak the word fearlessly.
PHI 1:15 Some indeed also through envy and strife; but some also through good-pleasure proclaim the Christ.
PHI 1:16 The ones indeed from out of contention announce the Christ, not purely, imagining to add affliction to my bonds.
PHI 1:17 But the ones from out of love, knowing that for a defense of the good news I am situated.
PHI 1:18 For what? Only in every manner, whether an excuse, whether truth, Christ is announced; and in this I rejoice, but, also I will rejoice.
PHI 1:19 For I know that this to me shall result in deliverance through your supplication, and the supplying of the spirit of Jesus Christ,
PHI 1:20 according to my earnest expectation and hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but in every open manner, as at all times, and now Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether through life, whether through death.
PHI 1:21 For to me to live is Christ, and to die gain.
PHI 1:22 But if to live in flesh, this to me is fruit of work. And what I shall take up I know not.
PHI 1:23 But I am constrained by the two, having the desire for disengaging, and to be with Christ is rather much better;
PHI 1:24 but to remain in the flesh is more important for you.
PHI 1:25 And this being persuaded of, I know that I shall abide and continue with you all in your progression and joy of the belief;
PHI 1:26 that your boasting should abound in Christ Jesus in me through my arrival again with you.
PHI 1:27 Only conduct yourselves in public worthily of the good news of the Christ; that whether having come and having seen you, or whether being absent, I should hear the things concerning you, that you stand firmly in one spirit, one soul, fighting together in the belief of the good news;
PHI 1:28 and not being terrified in anything by the ones being an adversary; which to them indeed is a demonstration of destruction, but to you deliverance - and this from God!
PHI 1:29 For to you it was granted concerning Christ, not only the trusting in him, but also the suffering for him;
PHI 1:30 having the same struggle as you saw in me, and now hear of by me.
PHI 2:1 If then there be any comfort in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of spirit, if any feelings of compassion and pities,
PHI 2:2 fulfill my joy, that you should be thinking the same, having the same love, unanimous, thinking one thing;
PHI 2:3 nothing according to contention or self seeking-glory; but in humility, esteeming one another superior than themselves!
PHI 2:4 Let not each watch out for the things of themselves, but each also the things of others!
PHI 2:5 For let this thinking be in you, which also is in Christ Jesus!
PHI 2:6 Who existing in the appearance of God, esteemed it not a seizure to be equal with God;
PHI 2:7 but emptied himself, having taken on the appearance of a bondman, having become in the likeness of men.
PHI 2:8 And in condition having been found as a man, he humbled himself, having become subject unto death, even death of the cross.
PHI 2:9 Therefore also God greatly exalted him, and granted to him the name above every name.
PHI 2:10 That at the name of Jesus every knee should bend - heavenly, and earthly, and underground;
PHI 2:11 and every tongue should acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the father.
PHI 2:12 So that, my beloved, as at all times you obeyed, (not as at my arrival only, but now much rather in my absence,) work out your own deliverance with fear and trembling!
PHI 2:13 For God is the one operating in you both to want and to operate for the good-pleasure.
PHI 2:14 Do all things without grumblings and arguings!
PHI 2:15 that you should become blameless and unmixed, children of God, without blemish, in the midst of a generation crooked and perverted, among whom you appear as luminaries in the world;
PHI 2:16 giving heed to the word of life; for a boasting to me in the day of Christ, that I ran not in vain, nor in vain I tired.
PHI 2:17 But even if I am offered as a libation upon the sacrifice and ministration of the belief of yours, I rejoice, and I rejoice along with all you.
PHI 2:18 And likewise also you rejoice, even rejoice along with me!
PHI 2:19 But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send forth Timothy quickly to you, that I also should be full of confidence, having known the things concerning you.
PHI 2:20 For I have no one like-minded, who genuinely shall have concern for the things concerning you.
PHI 2:21 For all seek the things of themselves, not the things of Christ Jesus.
PHI 2:22 But the proof of him you know, that as to a father he served as a child with me in the good news.
PHI 2:23 This one indeed then I hope to send forth (as whenever I look over the things concerning me) immediately.
PHI 2:24 And I am persuaded in the Lord that also I myself shall come quickly.
PHI 2:25 But I esteemed it important that Epaphroditus the brother and fellow-worker and my fellow-soldier, but your apostle, and minister of my need, to send to you,
PHI 2:26 since he was longing after you all, and was anxious for you heard that he was sick.
PHI 2:27 For even he was sick - close to death. But God showed mercy on him; and not him only, but also me, that I should not have distress upon distress.
PHI 2:28 More diligently then I sent him, that, seeing him again, you should rejoice, and I should be free from sorrow.
PHI 2:29 Favorably receive him then in the Lord with all joy; and have such ones in esteem!
PHI 2:30 For because of the work of the Christ he approached unto death, risking his life, that he should supply your deficiency of the ministration towards me.
PHI 3:1 To the rest, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord! The same things to write to you, to me indeed is not laziness, but for you safe.
PHI 3:2 Take heed of the dogs! Take heed of the evil workers! Take heed to the circumcisers!
PHI 3:3 For we are the circumcision, the ones serving in spirit of God, and boasting in Christ Jesus, and not relying in flesh;
PHI 3:4 though I have reliance even in flesh. If any other thinks to rely in flesh, I more.
PHI 3:5 As to circumcision - on the eight day; of the race - of Israel; as to tribe - Benjamin; a Hebrew - of Hebrews; according to law - a Pharisee;
PHI 3:6 according to zeal - persecuting the assembly; according to righteousness in the law - having become blameless.
PHI 3:7 But what was to me gain, these I esteemed loss through the Christ.
PHI 3:8 But certainly, also I esteem all things to be loss on account of the superiority of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord; through whom all things I suffered loss, and esteem them to be dung, that I should gain Christ,
PHI 3:9 and should be found in him not having my righteousness, the one of the law, but the one through belief of Christ, the righteousness of God unto belief;
PHI 3:10 to know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being conformable to his death;
PHI 3:11 if by any means I should arrive at the resurrection of the dead.
PHI 3:12 Not that already I received, or already I have been perfected; but I pursue, if even I should overtake upon which also I was overtaken by the Christ - Jesus.
PHI 3:13 Brothers, I myself consider not to have overtaken; but in forgetting indeed the things behind, but the things in front stretching out farther,
PHI 3:14 towards the aim I pursue unto the victory prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.
PHI 3:15 As many as then are complete, should think this. And if any think differently, also this God will reveal to you.
PHI 3:16 Besides, in what we attained, by the same rule we are to conform to think the same.
PHI 3:17 Become imitators together of me, brothers, and watch the ones thus walking, as you have us for a model!
PHI 3:18 (For many walk, of whom often I told you, and now even weeping I tell - of the ones enemies of the cross of the of Christ;
PHI 3:19 whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and the glory is in their shame, the ones thinking earthly things.)
PHI 3:20 For of us the citizenship in the heavens exists, of which also we await a deliverer - the Lord Jesus Christ.
PHI 3:21 Who will change the body appearance of our humiliation, for its becoming conformable to the body of his glory, according to the energy of his being able, and to subject to himself the whole.
PHI 4:1 So that, my beloved and longed for brothers, my joy and crown, so stand firm in the Lord, beloved!
PHI 4:2 Euodia I appeal, and Syntyche I appeal, to think the same in the Lord.
PHI 4:3 Yes, I ask also you genuine fellow-companion, aid these women who in the good news fought together with me, also with Clement, and the rest of my fellow-workers, whose names are in the book of life!
PHI 4:4 Rejoice in the Lord at all times! Again, I say, Rejoice!
PHI 4:5 Let your leniency be known to all men! The Lord is near.
PHI 4:6 Let no one be anxious. But in all - in the prayer and in the supplication with thankfulness let your requests be made known to God!
PHI 4:7 And the peace of God, surpassing every mind, shall guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
PHI 4:8 For the rest, brothers, as much as is true, as much as is serious, as much as is just, as much as is pure, as much as is friendly, as much as is of good report; if any virtue, and if any high praise, these things consider!
PHI 4:9 What also you learned, and received, and heard, and saw in me - these things practice, and the God of peace will be with you!
PHI 4:10 And I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that already at some time you flourished again to think about me; upon which also you thought, but lacked means.
PHI 4:11 Not that I speak as to deficiency; for I learned in what I am to be self-sufficient.
PHI 4:12 I know also to be humble, I know also to abound. In everything and in all things I am initiated both to be full and to hunger, and to abound and to be lacking.
PHI 4:13 I am strong for all things in the one empowering me - Christ.
PHI 4:14 Besides you did well, partaking together with my affliction.
PHI 4:15 And know also you, O Philippians, that in the beginning of the good news, when I came forth from Macedonia, not one assembly participated with me in the matter of portioning out and receiving, except you alone.
PHI 4:16 For also in Thessalonica even once and twice you sent forth for my need.
PHI 4:17 Not that I anxiously seek the gift; but I anxiously seek the fruit being superabundant for your account.
PHI 4:18 But I receive all things, and I abound. I am full, having received by Epaphroditus the things from you - a scent of pleasant aroma, a sacrifice accepted, well-pleasing to God.
PHI 4:19 And my God will fill all your need, according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
PHI 4:20 But to the God and father of us be the glory into the eons of the eons. Amen.
PHI 4:21 Greet every holy one in Christ Jesus! The brothers with me greet you.
PHI 4:22 All the holy ones greet you, and especially the ones of the house of Caesar.
PHI 4:23 The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
COL 1:1 Paul, apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, and Timothy the brother,
COL 1:2 to the holy ones in Colosse, and trustworthy brothers in Christ. Favor to you, and peace from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
COL 1:3 We give thanks to the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, at all times praying for you,
COL 1:4 having heard the belief of yours in Christ Jesus, and the love towards all the holy ones,
COL 1:5 on account of the hope being reserved for you in the heavens, which you heard before in the word of the truth of the good news
COL 1:6 being at hand in you, as also in all the world; and is bearing fruit, as also among you from which day you heard, and realized the favor of God in truth.
COL 1:7 As also you learned from Epaphras the beloved fellow-servant of ours, who is a trustworthy servant for you of the Christ;
COL 1:8 the one also having manifested to us your love in spirit.
COL 1:9 On account of this also we, from which day heard, cease not praying for you, and asking that you should be filled with the full knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
COL 1:10 for you to walk worthily of the Lord pleasing to all, bearing fruit in every good work, and growing in the full knowledge of God;
COL 1:11 being strengthened in all power, according to the might of his glory, in all patience and long-suffering with joy;
COL 1:12 giving thanks to the God and father making us fit in the portion of the lot of the holy ones in the light.
COL 1:13 Who rescued us from out of the authority of the darkness, and changed us over to the kingdom of the son of his love.
COL 1:14 In whom we have the release by ransom through his blood - the release of sins.
COL 1:15 Who is the image of the unseen God, first-born of all creation.
COL 1:16 For in him were created the whole - the things in the heavens, and the things upon the earth, the visible and the unseen, whether thrones, whether lordships, whether sovereignties, whether authorities; the whole through him and in him have been created.
COL 1:17 And he is before all, and the whole in him combine.
COL 1:18 And he is the head of the body of the assembly; who is the beginning, the first-born from the dead; that he should be preeminent in all things.
COL 1:19 For in him all the fullness thought well to dwell;
COL 1:20 and through him to reconcile the whole to himself; having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him - whether the things upon the earth, whether the things in the heavens.
COL 1:21 And you at some time or other being separated and enemies in thought by wicked works, but now he reconciled
COL 1:22 in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblemished and without reproach before him;
COL 1:23 if indeed you remain in the belief, being founded and settled, and not being moved about from the hope of the good news of which you heard being proclaimed in all the creation under the heaven, of which I Paul became servant.
COL 1:24 Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and filling up again the deficiencies of the afflictions of the Christ in my flesh for his body, which is the assembly;
COL 1:25 of which I became servant according to the management of God given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God -
COL 1:26 the mystery being concealed from the eons and from the generations, but now made manifest to his holy ones;
COL 1:27 ones to whom God wanted to make known what the wealth of the glory of this mystery is among the nations; which is Christ in you, the hope of the glory;
COL 1:28 whom we announce, admonishing every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we should present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.
COL 1:29 In which also I tire in labor, struggling according to his energy operating in me in power.
COL 2:1 For I want you to know how much struggle I have for you, and the ones in Laodicea, and as many as have not seen my face in flesh;
COL 2:2 that their hearts should be comforted, being instructed in love, and in all riches of the full assurance of the understanding, in full knowledge of the mystery of the God and father and of the Christ;
COL 2:3 in whom are all the treasures of the wisdom and of the knowledge concealed.
COL 2:4 And this I say, that not anyone should mislead you in plausible arguments.
COL 2:5 For if even in the flesh I am absent, yet in the spirit I am with you, rejoicing and seeing your order, and the firmness of your belief in Christ.
COL 2:6 As then you took to yourself the Christ - Jesus the Lord, so walk in him!
COL 2:7 being rooted and built up in him, and being firmed up in the belief, as you were taught, abounding in it with thankfulness.
COL 2:8 Take heed lest there shall be anyone robbing you through the fondness of intellectual pursuits and empty deception, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ!
COL 2:9 For in him dwells all the fullness of the deity bodily.
COL 2:10 And you are being fulfilled in him, who is the head of all sovereignty and authority.
COL 2:11 In whom also you were circumcised by a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping of the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of the Christ;
COL 2:12 having been buried together with him in the immersion, in which also you were risen up together through the belief of the energy of God, of the one having raised him from the dead.
COL 2:13 And you, being dead in the transgressions, and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made you alive together with him, granting forgiveness to us for all the transgressions;
COL 2:14 having wiped away the handwriting by the decrees against us, which was contrary to us, and lifted it from out of the midst, having fastened it with a nail to the cross;
COL 2:15 having divested the sovereignties and the authorities, he made an example in an open manner triumphing over them by it.
COL 2:16 Let not then anyone judge you in food, or in drink, or in the rank of a holiday feast, or new moon, or sabbaths!
COL 2:17 which are a shadow of the things about to be - but the body is of the Christ.
COL 2:18 Let no one deprive you of due reward! wanting by deprivation, and following a religion of angels, entering into things which he has not seen, vainly being inflated by the mind of his flesh,
COL 2:19 and not holding onto the head, from out of which all the body through the ligaments and sinews being supplied and being instructed, grow by the growth of God.
COL 2:20 If then you died with the Christ from the elements of the world, why, as living in the world, do you subject yourselves to decrees,
COL 2:21 ( that is, You should not touch, nor should you taste, nor should you lightly touch;
COL 2:22 which things are all for corruption in abuse;) according to the precepts and instructions of men?
COL 2:23 Which is communication then having wisdom in man made religion, and deprivation, and austerity of the body; not in any value to fullness of the flesh.
COL 3:1 If then you were raised up together with the Christ, seek the things upward, where the Christ is at the right hand of God sitting down!
COL 3:2 Think the things upward, not the things upon the earth!
COL 3:3 For you died, and your life has been hid with the Christ in God.
COL 3:4 Whenever the Christ should be manifested in our life, then also you shall be manifested with him in glory.
COL 3:5 Deaden then your members upon the earth - harlotry, uncleanness, passion, evil desire, and the desire for wealth, which is idolatry!
COL 3:6 through which comes the wrath of God upon the sons of disobedience.
COL 3:7 Among whom also you walked at some time or other, when you were living in these things.
COL 3:8 But now put aside, even you, all anger, rage, evil, blasphemy, obscene talk from out of your mouth!
COL 3:9 Do not lie to one another! but divesting the old man with his actions;
COL 3:10 and putting on the new man being restored in full knowledge, according to the image of the one creating him;
COL 3:11 where there is not Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, bondman, free; but Christ is the all and in all!
COL 3:12 Put on then as chosen ones of God, holy ones, and beloved - feelings of compassion, pity, graciousness, humility, gentleness, long-suffering,
COL 3:13 enduring one another, and granting forgiveness to each other, if any should have any blame against any! As also the Christ granted forgiveness to you, so also you.
COL 3:14 And upon all these things put on the love which is the bonding together of the perfection!
COL 3:15 And let the peace of God preside in your hearts, in which also you were called in one body! And be gracious!
COL 3:16 Let the word of the Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom! teaching and admonishing yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual odes, with favor singing in your heart to the Lord.
COL 3:17 And everything, what ever you should do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to the God and father by him.
COL 3:18 The wives - submit to your own husbands, as relates in the Lord!
COL 3:19 The husbands - love the wives, and be not bitter against them!
COL 3:20 The children - obey the parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing to the Lord!
COL 3:21 The fathers - do not aggravate your children, that they should not be depressed!
COL 3:22 The bondmen - obey in all things the masters according to the flesh; not in eyeservices as ones who try to please men, but in simplicity of heart, fearing God!
COL 3:23 And all, whatever you should do, work from the soul as to the Lord, and not to men!
COL 3:24 knowing that from the Lord you shall accept the reward of the inheritance - for to the Lord Christ serve!
COL 3:25 And the one wronging shall receive for what he wronged; and there is not a discrimination.
COL 4:1 Let the masters furnish the thing just and equal to the bondmen; knowing that also you have a master in heavens!
COL 4:2 In the prayer - attend constantly, being vigilant in it in thankfulness!
COL 4:3 praying together also for us, that God should open to us a door of the word, to speak the mystery of the Christ, on account of which also I have been bound,
COL 4:4 that I should make it manifest as is necessary for me to speak.
COL 4:5 Walk in wisdom to the ones outside! buying back the time;
COL 4:6 with your word at all times in favor, being seasoned with salt, to know how it is necessary for you to answer each one.
COL 4:7 All the things concerning me Tychicus will make known to you, the beloved brother, and trustworthy servant, and fellow-servant in the Lord;
COL 4:8 whom I sent forth to you for this same purpose, that he should know the things concerning you, and should comfort your hearts;
COL 4:9 with Onesimus the trustworthy and beloved brother, who is of you. All the things here they shall make known to you.
COL 4:10 Aristarchus my fellow-captive greets you, and Mark the cousin of Barnabas, (concerning whom you received commands - if he should come to you, receive him!)
COL 4:11 and Joshua, the one being called Justus, the ones being of the circumcision. These alone are fellow-workers in the kingdom of God who became an encouragement to me.
COL 4:12 Epaphras greets you, the one from you, a bondman of Christ, at all times struggling for you in the prayers, that you should stand perfect and being filled in every will of God.
COL 4:13 For I bear witness to him, that he has much zeal for you, and the ones in Laodicea, and the ones in Hierapolis.
COL 4:14 Luke the beloved physician greets you, and Demas.
COL 4:15 You greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the assembly in his house!
COL 4:16 And whenever the letter should be read by you, do it that also in the assembly of Laodiceans it should be read; and the one from Laodicea, that also you should read it!
COL 4:17 And say to Archippus, Take heed to the service which you took to yourself in the Lord, that you should fulfill it!
COL 4:18 The greeting by my hand, Paul. Remember my bonds! The favor be with you. Amen.
1TH 1:1 Paul, and Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of Thessalonians, in God the father, and in the Lord Jesus Christ. Favor to you, and peace from God our father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1TH 1:2 We give thanks to God at all times concerning all of you, making mention of you in our prayers;
1TH 1:3 continually remembering your work of the belief, and the toil of the love, and the endurance of the hope of our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and father.
1TH 1:4 Knowing brothers, O ones being loved by God, of your selection,
1TH 1:5 that our good news did not take place in you in word only, but also in power, and in holy spirit, and in much full assurance; as you know what we became among you for you.
1TH 1:6 And you became imitators of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of holy spirit,
1TH 1:7 so that you became models to all the ones believing in Macedonia and Achaia.
1TH 1:8 For the word of the Lord has resounded from you, not only in Macedonia and in Achaia, but also in every place the belief of yours towards God has gone forth; so as for us to have no need to say anything.
1TH 1:9 For they themselves report concerning us as to like what introduction we had towards you, and how you turned to God from the idols to serve a living and true God;
1TH 1:10 and to await his son from out of the heavens, whom he raised from the dead - Jesus, the one rescuing us from the coming wrath.
1TH 2:1 For you yourselves know, brothers, our introduction towards you, that it has not been in vain.
1TH 2:2 But also having suffered before, and having been insulted, as you know, in Philippi, we were speaking openly in our God, to speak to you the good news of God with much struggle.
1TH 2:3 For our exhortation was not from out of delusion, nor from out of uncleanness, nor in deceit.
1TH 2:4 But as having been proved by God to be trusted with the good news, so we speak; not as pleasing men, but to God - the one trying our hearts.
1TH 2:5 For neither at any time with word of flattery did we exist, (as you know,) nor with an excuse for a desire for wealth, (God is witness,)
1TH 2:6 nor seeking glory from men, nor from you, nor from others; though being able in weight to be as Christ's apostles.
1TH 2:7 But we became calm in your midst, as even a nurse should comfort her own children.
1TH 2:8 Thus longing over you, we thought well to share with you, not only the good news of God, but also our own lives, for you have become beloved to us.
1TH 2:9 For you remember, brothers, our toil and trouble. For working night and day, so as to not overburden any of you, we proclaimed to you the good news of God.
1TH 2:10 You are witnesses, and God, how sacredly and justly and blamelessly we were to you the ones believing.
1TH 2:11 Just as you know how each one of you we were comforting and consoling and testifying to you as a father his own children,
1TH 2:12 for you to walk worthily of God, the one calling you into his own kingdom and glory.
1TH 2:13 On account of this also we give thanks to God continually, that taking to yourselves the word of report of God by us, you received not the word of men, but as it is truly, the word of God, which also exerts energy in you the ones believing.
1TH 2:14 For you became imitators, brothers, of the assemblies of God being in Judea in Christ Jesus; that the same things you also suffered by your own fellow-tribesmen, as also they by the Jews,
1TH 2:15 the ones both killing the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and driving you out, and are not pleasing to God, and opposing to all men;
1TH 2:16 (ones restraining us to speak to the nations that they should be delivered,) so as to fill up their sins at all times. But came upon them the wrath to the end.
1TH 2:17 But we, brothers, being orphaned from you for an hour time, in person, not in heart, more exceedingly hurried to behold your face with much desire.
1TH 2:18 Therefore we wanted to come to you, even indeed I Paul, even once and twice; and Satan hindered us.
1TH 2:19 For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting? or is it not also you in front of our Lord Jesus Christ at his arrival?
1TH 2:20 For you are our glory and joy.
1TH 3:1 Therefore no longer holding off, we thought well to be left behind in Athens alone;
1TH 3:2 and we sent forth Timothy our brother and servant of God, and our fellow-worker in the good news of the Christ, for the supporting you, and to comfort you concerning the belief of yours;
1TH 3:3 in the no one shrinking in these afflictions. For you yourselves know that in this we are situated.
1TH 3:4 For also, when we were with you, we said beforehand to you that we are about to be afflicted; as also it happened, and you know.
1TH 3:5 Because of this, I also no longer holding off, sent forth for the knowing the belief of yours, lest perhaps the one testing tested you, and our toil became in vain.
1TH 3:6 But now Timothy having come to us from you, and having announced good news to us, the belief and the love of yours, and that you have at all times a good remembrance of us, longing to see us, just as also we you;
1TH 3:7 because of this we were comforted, brothers, over you in all our affliction and necessity, because of the belief of yours.
1TH 3:8 For now we live if you stand firmly in the Lord.
1TH 3:9 For what thankfulness are we able to recompense God concerning you, for all the joy which we rejoice on account of you before our God;
1TH 3:10 night and day superabundantly beseeching for the beholding your face, and to ready the deficiencies of the belief of yours?
1TH 3:11 And may our God and father himself and our Lord Jesus Christ straighten out our way to you.
1TH 3:12 And may the Lord superabound you, and may he abound the love towards one another, and towards all, just as also we towards you;
1TH 3:13 so as to support your hearts blameless in holiness before the God and our father, at the arrival of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his holy ones.
1TH 4:1 The rest then, brothers, we ask you, and appeal in the Lord Jesus, that as you received from us the thing how it was necessary for you to walk and to please God, that you should abound more.
1TH 4:2 For you know what exhortations we gave to you through the Lord Jesus.
1TH 4:3 For this is the will of God - your sanctification; for you to be at a distance from harlotry;
1TH 4:4 for each of you to know his own vessel, to possess it in sanctification and honor,
1TH 4:5 not in passion of desire, as even the nations not knowing God;
1TH 4:6 to not surpass and to overabound in the matter of his brother; for the one punishing is the Lord concerning all these things, as also we foretold to you, and testified.
1TH 4:7 For God called us not unto uncleanness, but in sanctification.
1TH 4:8 Accordingly the one disregarding, disregards not man, but God, the one also having given his holy spirit to us.
1TH 4:9 And concerning brotherly affection you have not a need for me to write to you; for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.
1TH 4:10 For even do this towards all the brothers in all Macedonia! But we appeal to you, brothers, to abound more;
1TH 4:11 and to strive earnestly to be quiet, and to do your own things, and to work with your own hands, as we exhorted to you;
1TH 4:12 that you should walk decently towards the ones outside, and no one should have need.
1TH 4:13 But I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning the ones having gone to sleep, that you do not fret, as even the rest not having hope.
1TH 4:14 For if we believe that Jesus died and rose up, so also God will bring with him the ones having gone to sleep through Jesus.
1TH 4:15 For this to you we say by word of the Lord, that we, the ones living, the ones remaining at the arrival of the Lord, in no way should anticipate the ones having gone to sleep.
1TH 4:16 For the Lord himself in a word of command by the voice of an archangel, and with a trumpet of God, shall descend from heaven, and the dead in Christ shall rise up first.
1TH 4:17 Thereupon we the living, the ones remaining, together with them shall be seized in clouds for meeting the Lord in the air. And thus at all times with the Lord we shall be.
1TH 4:18 So then comfort one another by these words!
1TH 5:1 But concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, You have not a need to be written to you,
1TH 5:2 for you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord so comes as a thief in the night.
1TH 5:3 For whenever they should say, Peace and safety; then sudden ruin sets upon them, as if the pangs to the one having one in the womb; and in no way should they flee from it.
1TH 5:4 But you, brothers, are not in darkness, that the day should overtake you as a thief.
1TH 5:5 You are all sons of light, and sons of day; we are not of night nor of darkness.
1TH 5:6 So then we should not be sleeping as also the rest; but we should be vigilant and be sober.
1TH 5:7 For the ones sleeping sleep at night; and the ones being intoxicated, are intoxicated at night.
1TH 5:8 But we, being of day, should be sober, putting on the chest plate of belief and love; and helmet - the hope of deliverance.
1TH 5:9 For God set us not for wrath, but for the procurement of deliverence through our Lord Jesus Christ,
1TH 5:10 the one having died for us, that whether we be vigilant, or whether we sleep, together with him we shall live.
1TH 5:11 Therefore comfort one another, and let one build up the other one, as even you do!
1TH 5:12 And we ask you, brothers, to know the ones tiring in labor among you, and being set over you in the Lord, and admonishing you;
1TH 5:13 and to esteem them superabundantly in love on account of their work. Make peace among yourselves!
1TH 5:14 And we appeal to you, brothers, admonish the ones in disorder! Console the ones being faint-hearted! Hold to the weak! Be long-suffering to all!
1TH 5:15 See that not anyone should recompense anyone hurt for hurt! But at all times pursue good, both towards one another and towards all!
1TH 5:16 At all times rejoice!
1TH 5:17 Continually pray!
1TH 5:18 In everything give thanks! For this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
1TH 5:19 Do not extinguish the spirit!
1TH 5:20 Do not treat prophecies with contempt!
1TH 5:21 Prove all things! Hold to the good!
1TH 5:22 Be at a distance from every appearance of evil!
1TH 5:23 And he, the God of peace, may he sanctify you perfectly complete; and may your entire spirit and soul and body be kept blamelessly in the arrival of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1TH 5:24 The one calling you is trustworthy, who also will act.
1TH 5:25 Brothers, pray for us!
1TH 5:26 Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss!
1TH 5:27 I adjure you by the Lord, for the letter to be read to all the sanctified brothers.
1TH 5:28 The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
2TH 1:1 Paul, and Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of Thessalonians in God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2TH 1:2 Favor to you, and peace, from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2TH 1:3 We ought to give thanks to God at all times concerning you, brothers, as it is worthy, that your belief is caused to grow exceedingly, and the love of each one of all of you is superabundant to one another;
2TH 1:4 so as for us ourselves to boast in you, among the assemblies of God, over your endurance and belief in all your persecutions and afflictions which you endure -
2TH 1:5 a demonstration of the just judgment of God, in the deeming you worthy of the kingdom of God, for of which also you suffer;
2TH 1:6 if indeed it be just by God to recompense to the ones afflicting you with affliction;
2TH 1:7 and to you, the ones being afflicted, a relaxation with us, in the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with angels of his power,
2TH 1:8 in fire of flame, giving punishment to the ones not knowing God, and to the ones not obeying the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ;
2TH 1:9 who with punishment shall pay eternal ruin from the face of the Lord, and from the glory of his strength;
2TH 1:10 whenever he should come to be glorified among his holy ones, and to be marveled at by all the ones having believed (because our testimony to you was believed ) in that day.
2TH 1:11 For which also we pray at all times for you, that you should be worthy of the calling of our God, and should fulfill every good-pleasure of goodness, and work of belief with power.
2TH 1:12 So that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ should be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the favor of our God and of the Lord Jesus Christ.
2TH 2:1 And we ask you, brothers, concerning the arrival of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our assemblage unto him,
2TH 2:2 for you to not quickly be shaken of the mind, nor to be alarmed, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter, as by us, that the day of the Christ is present.
2TH 2:3 Let not any completely deceive you in not one manner! For unless the defection should come first, and the man of sin should be uncovered, the son of destruction;
2TH 2:4 the one being an adversary and elevating himself above all being called god, or object of worship, so as for him to sit in the temple of God as God, exhibiting himself that he is God.
2TH 2:5 Do you not remember that still being with you, I said these things to you?
2TH 2:6 And now the one constraining you know, for the uncovering him in his own time.
2TH 2:7 For the mystery of lawlessness already operates, only there is the one constraining just now until he should be from out of the midst.
2TH 2:8 And then the lawless one shall be uncovered, whom the Lord shall consume by the breath of his mouth, and shall render the grandeur of his arrival useless;
2TH 2:9 whose arrival is according to the energy of Satan in every power and signs and miracles of a lie,
2TH 2:10 and in every deception of unrighteousness among the ones being destroyed; because of which they received not the love of the truth for them to be delivered.
2TH 2:11 And on account of this God shall send forth to them an energy of delusion, for them to believe in the lie;
2TH 2:12 that all the ones not believing in the truth but taking pleasure in unrighteousness should be judged.
2TH 2:13 But we ought to give thanks to God at all times concerning you, brothers, beloved by the Lord, that God took you up from the beginning for deliverance in sanctification of spirit and belief of truth;
2TH 2:14 in which he called you through our good news, in procurement of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2TH 2:15 So then, brothers, stand firmly, and hold the traditions which you were taught, whether by word, or whether by our letter!
2TH 2:16 But our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and the God and our father, the one having loved us, and gave eternal comfort, and good hope in favor,
2TH 2:17 may he comfort your hearts, and support you in every good word and work.
2TH 3:1 For the rest, pray, brothers, for us, that the word of the Lord should run, and should be glorified, as also to you.
2TH 3:2 And that we should be rescued from the unnatural and wicked men; for the belief is not of all.
2TH 3:3 But trustworthy is the Lord, who will support you, and will guard you from evil.
2TH 3:4 But we rely in the Lord as to you, that in which we exhort unto you both you are doing and will do.
2TH 3:5 And may the Lord straighten out your hearts in the love of God, and in the endurance of the Christ.
2TH 3:6 And we make exhortation to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, for you to be in readiness from every brother walking disorderly, and not according to the tradition which he took to himself from us.
2TH 3:7 For you yourselves know how it is necessary to imitate us. For we have not acted disorderly among you;
2TH 3:8 nor freely did we eat bread from anyone; but in toil and trouble night and day, working so as to not overburden any of you.
2TH 3:9 Not that we do not have authority, but that we should give ourselves as a model to you for the imitating us.
2TH 3:10 For also when we were with you, we exhorted this unto you, that if any does not want to work, neither let him eat!
2TH 3:11 For we hear some are walking among you disorderly, not working, but intermeddling.
2TH 3:12 And to such we exhort and appeal by our Lord Jesus Christ, that working with tranquility, they should eat their own bread.
2TH 3:13 But you, brothers, should not tire doing good.
2TH 3:14 And if anyone does not obey our word by this letter, signify and do not intermingle with him, that he should be ashamed!
2TH 3:15 But not as an enemy esteem him, but admonish him as a brother!
2TH 3:16 And may the Lord of peace himself give to you peace continually in every manner. The Lord be with all of you.
2TH 3:17 The greeting by my hand, Paul, which is a sign in every letter - so I write.
2TH 3:18 The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
1TI 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the command of God the father, and our deliverer Jesus Christ, the one of our hope;
1TI 1:2 to Timothy, genuine child in belief. Favor, mercy, peace, from God our father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
1TI 1:3 As I appealed to you to remain in Ephesus, going to Macedonia, that you should exhort some not to teach a different doctrine,
1TI 1:4 nor take heed to fables and unlimited genealogies, which make for inquiries, rather than the administration of God in belief.
1TI 1:5 But the end of the exhortation is love from out of a clean heart, and a good conscience, and of unpretentious belief;
1TI 1:6 which some having missed their aim, turn aside to useless discussion,
1TI 1:7 wanting to be teachers of the law, not comprehending what they say, nor concerning what they positively assert.
1TI 1:8 But we know that the law is good, if anyone should treat it lawfully;
1TI 1:9 knowing this, that to a just one the law is not situated, but for lawless ones, and unsubmissive ones, impious ones, and sinners, unholy ones, and profane ones, murderers of one's father, and murderers of one's mother, manslayers,
1TI 1:10 fornicators, homosexuals, slave traders, liars, perjurers, and if any other be an adversary to healthy instruction;
1TI 1:11 according to the good news of the glory of the blessed God, which I was entrusted.
1TI 1:12 And I have gratitude to the one empowering me - to our Lord Christ Jesus, that he esteemed me trustworthy, appointing me to service;
1TI 1:13 the one formerly being blasphemous, and a persecutor, and arrogant. But I was shown mercy. For being ignorant I acted in unbelief.
1TI 1:14 But the favor of our Lord more than superabounded with belief and love in Christ Jesus.
1TI 1:15 Trustworthy is the word, and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to deliver sinners, whom I am foremost.
1TI 1:16 And because of this I was shown mercy, that in me Jesus Christ should demonstrate foremost all leniency, for setting a pattern for the ones being about to believe upon him unto life eternal.
1TI 1:17 And to the king of the eons, incorruptible, unseen, only wise God, be honor and glory to the eons of the eons. Amen.
1TI 1:18 This exhortation I place unto you, son Timothy, according to the prophecies going before over you, that you should soldier in them the good warfare;
1TI 1:19 having belief, and good conscience; which some having thrust away concerning the belief made shipwreck;
1TI 1:20 whom are Hymeneus and Alexander; whom I delivered up to Satan, that they may be corrected not to blaspheme.
1TI 2:1 I appeal then, first of all to make supplications, prayers, intercessions, thankfulnesses for all men;
1TI 2:2 for kings, and of all the ones being in superiority; that a calm and unassuming existence should be led in all piety and seriousness.
1TI 2:3 For this is good and worthy of being received before God our deliverer;
1TI 2:4 who wants all men to be delivered, and to come to full knowledge of truth.
1TI 2:5 For there is one God, and one mediator of God and of men - the man Christ Jesus;
1TI 2:6 the one giving himself a ransom for all, the testimony to be rendered in its own times;
1TI 2:7 to which I was established a herald and apostle, (truth I speak in Christ, I do not lie;) a teacher of the nations in belief and truth.
1TI 2:8 I want then the men to pray in every place, lifting up sacred hands, separate from anger and arguing.
1TI 2:9 Likewise also the wives in composed apparel, with respect and discreetness to adorn themselves, not in laces, or gold, or pearls, or very costly clothes,
1TI 2:10 but what is becoming to wives promising godliness through good works.
1TI 2:11 Let a wife learn at rest in all submission!
1TI 2:12 And a wife I commit not to their care to teach, nor to domineer a husband, but to be at rest.
1TI 2:13 For Adam first was shaped, then Eve.
1TI 2:14 And Adam was not deceived, but the wife having been deceived has become in violation.
1TI 2:15 But she shall be preserved through childbearing, if they abide in belief and love and sanctification with discreetness.
1TI 3:1 Trustworthy is the word. If any reaches for overseership, he desires a good work.
1TI 3:2 It is necessary then the overseer to be unassailable, a husband of one wife, sober, discreet, composed, hospitable, qualified for teaching,
1TI 3:3 not intemperate in the use of wine, not a brawler, not profiting through vice; but lenient, not quarrelsome, not loving money,
1TI 3:4 standing over his own house well, having children in submission with all seriousness;
1TI 3:5 (and if any knows not how to stand over his own house, how shall he care for the assembly of God?)
1TI 3:6 not a neophyte, that not being deluded he should fall in judgment of the devil.
1TI 3:7 But it is necessary for him also to have a good witness from the ones outside, that he should not fall into scorning, and the snare of the devil.
1TI 3:8 Servants likewise be serious, not double-talking, not attentive to much wine, not profiting through vice;
1TI 3:9 having the mystery of the belief with a clean conscience.
1TI 3:10 And these also, let them be approved first; then let them serve being without reproach!
1TI 3:11 Wives likewise be serious, not slanderers, sober, trustworthy in all things.
1TI 3:12 Servants be husbands of one wife, standing over children well and their own houses!
1TI 3:13 For the ones having served well procure a good rank for themselves, and much confidence in belief in Christ Jesus.
1TI 3:14 These things to you I write, hoping to come to you more quickly.
1TI 3:15 But if I should be slowed, it is that you should know how it is necessary to behave in the house of God, which is the assembly of the living God, column and base of the truth.
1TI 3:16 And confessedly great is the mystery of the piety - God made manifest in flesh, justified in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among nations, believed in the world, taken up in glory.
1TI 4:1 But the spirit expressly says, that in later times some shall leave the belief, taking heed to spirits of delusion, and instructions of demons;
1TI 4:2 in hypocrisy of speaking lies; their own conscience being seared;
1TI 4:3 restraining to marry, restraining to be at a distance from foods, which God created for participation with thankfulness to the ones trustworthy and recognizing the truth.
1TI 4:4 For every creation of God is good, and nothing to be spurned, with thankfulness being received.
1TI 4:5 For it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.
1TI 4:6 In placing these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Jesus Christ, being trained up in the words of the belief and the good instruction, which you have followed closely.
1TI 4:7 But the profane and old wives fables refuse! But exercise yourself to piety!
1TI 4:8 For the bodily exercise for a little is beneficial; but piety is beneficial for all things, having promise of life - of the present, and of the one being about to be.
1TI 4:9 Trustworthy is the word and worthy of all acceptance.
1TI 4:10 For in this also we tire in labor and are berated, because we have hope upon a living God, who is deliverer of all men, especially ones believing.
1TI 4:11 Exhort these things and teach!
1TI 4:12 Let no one disdain your youth! but become a model for the ones believing - in word, in behavior, in love, in spirit, in belief, in purity.
1TI 4:13 Until I come, take heed to the reading, to the consolation, to the instruction!
1TI 4:14 Do not neglect the favor in you, which was given to you through prophecy, with laying on of the hands of the council of elders!
1TI 4:15 These things meditate upon! Be in these things, that your progression should be apparent to all!
1TI 4:16 Give heed to yourself, and to the instruction! Remain in them! For this doing you shall deliver both yourself, and the ones hearing you.
1TI 5:1 You should not rebuke an elder. But appeal to him as a father! younger men as brothers;
1TI 5:2 elder women as mothers; younger women as sisters - with all purity.
1TI 5:3 Esteem widows really widows!
1TI 5:4 And if any widow has children or progeny, let them learn first to be pious for their own house, and to repay a repayment to their precursors! For this is good and worthy of being received before God.
1TI 5:5 And the one really a widow, and being left alone, has hope in God, and remains in the supplications and in the prayers night and day.
1TI 5:6 But the one living extravagantly, while living, has died.
1TI 5:7 And these things exhort, that they should be unassailable!
1TI 5:8 And if any thinks not beforehand of his own and especially the ones of his family, he has denied the belief, and is worse than unbelieving.
1TI 5:9 Let not a widow be enrolled being less than sixty years old a wife of one husband,
1TI 5:10 with good works being witnessed, if she reared children, if she was hospitable, if she washed holy one's feet, if she assisted ones being afflicted, if she followed after every good work.
1TI 5:11 And younger widows refuse; for whenever they should grow careless towards the Christ, they want to marry,
1TI 5:12 having judgment, because the first belief they disregarded.
1TI 5:13 And together also idly they learn to go around the houses; but not only idle, but also in prating and useless works, speaking the things they must not.
1TI 5:14 I prefer then younger ones to marry, to bear children, to manage the home, not one opportunity to give to the adversary reviling favor.
1TI 5:15 For already some were turned aside after Satan.
1TI 5:16 If any believing man or believing woman have widows, assist them, and do not weigh down the assembly; that it should assist the ones really widows!
1TI 5:17 Let the elders being well in charge be worthy of double honor, especially the ones tiring in the word and instruction!
1TI 5:18 For the scripture says, You shall not muzzle an ox threshing, and, The worker is worthy of his wage.
1TI 5:19 Do not welcome a charge against an elder from outside, unless by two or three witnesses!
1TI 5:20 The ones sinning reprove before all, that also the rest should have fear!
1TI 5:21 I testify before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen angels, that these things you should guard, separate from prejudice, doing nothing by inclination.
1TI 5:22 Place upon no one a hand quickly, nor participate with sins of strangers! Keep yourself pure!
1TI 5:23 No longer drink water, but use a little wine because of your stomach, and your frequent sicknesses!
1TI 5:24 Of some men the sins are exposed to view, leading before to judgment; but some also follow after.
1TI 5:25 Likewise also the good works are exposed to view, and the ones otherwise having taken place are not able to be hid.
1TI 6:1 As many bondmen as are under the yoke, let them esteem their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the instruction should not be blasphemed!
1TI 6:2 And the ones having believing masters, let them not disdain because they are brothers! But rather, let them serve them, for they are believers and beloved ones taking hold of good works! These things teach and appeal towards!
1TI 6:3 If anyone teaches a different doctrine, and does not come forward with healthy words, to the ones of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the instruction according to piety,
1TI 6:4 he is deluded, having knowledge of nothing, but diseased concerning inquiries and arguings over words, of which becomes envy, strife, blasphemies, bad opinions,
1TI 6:5 useless disputations of men corrupting the mind, and depriving of the truth, to think revenue to be piety - separate from such!
1TI 6:6 But there is great revenue - piety with sufficiency.
1TI 6:7 For we have carried nothing into the world, and it is manifest that not even are we able to bring forth anything.
1TI 6:8 But having nourishment and shelters - with these we shall be sufficient.
1TI 6:9 But the ones wanting to be rich fall into a test and a snare, and many unthinking and hurtful desires, which submerge the men into ruin and destruction.
1TI 6:10 For a root of all the evils is the fondness of money; of which some reaching for were led astray from the belief, and pierced themselves on all sides with many griefs.
1TI 6:11 But you, O man of God, flee these things! And pursue righteousness, piety, belief, love, endurance, gentleness!
1TI 6:12 Struggle the good struggle of the belief! Take hold of the eternal life! in which also you were called, and acknowledged the good acknowledgment offering before many witnesses.
1TI 6:13 I exhort to you before God, the one restoring to life all things, and Christ Jesus, the one witnessing unto Pontius Pilate the good acknowledgment offering;
1TI 6:14 for you to keep the commandment spotless, unassailable, until the grandeur of our Lord Jesus Christ;
1TI 6:15 which in its own times the blessed and only mighty one shall show - the king of the ones reigning, and Lord of the ones dominating;
1TI 6:16 the one alone having immortality, living in light not to be equalled, whom not one of man beheld, nor is able to behold; to whom is honor and eternal might. Amen.
1TI 6:17 To the rich in the present eon, exhort to not be high-minded! nor to hope upon the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God furnishing to us all things richly for enjoyment;
1TI 6:18 to do good works, to be rich in good works, ready to share, to be sociable;
1TI 6:19 amassing for themselves a good foundation for the time about to be, that they should take hold of the eternal life.
1TI 6:20 O Timothy, guard the deposit in your care! turning aside from the profane idle talk, and oppositions of the falsely named knowledge.
1TI 6:21 Which some promising concerning the belief missed the aim. The favor be with you. Amen.
2TI 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, through the will of God, according to promise of life in Christ Jesus.
2TI 1:2 To Timothy, my beloved son; Favor, mercy, peace, from God the father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
2TI 1:3 Gratitude I have to God, in whom I serve from my precursors with a clean conscience, how I have the memory concerning you continually in my supplications night and day;
2TI 1:4 longing to see you, remembering your tears, that with joy I should be filled;
2TI 1:5 taking recollection of the unpretentious belief in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois, and in your mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that also is in you.
2TI 1:6 For which reason I remind you to rekindle the favor of God, which is in you by the laying on of my hands.
2TI 1:7 For God did not give to us a spirit of dread; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
2TI 1:8 Therefore you should not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor me his prisoner; But suffer evil along with the good news according to the power of God!
2TI 1:9 of the one preserving us, and having called with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own intention and favor, having been given to us in Christ Jesus before times everlasting;
2TI 1:10 and made manifest now through the grandeur of our deliverer Jesus Christ, the one clearing away indeed death, and having enlightened life and incorruptibility through the good news.
2TI 1:11 In which I was appointed herald, and apostle, and teacher of nations.
2TI 1:12 For which reason also these things I suffer. But I am not ashamed; for I know in whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep my deposit in his care for that day.
2TI 1:13 Have a pattern of healthy words, which you heard by me, in belief and love in Christ Jesus!
2TI 1:14 Guard the good trust through holy spirit dwelling in us!
2TI 1:15 Know this, that they turned away from me- all the ones in Asia; of whom is Phygellus and Hermogenes.
2TI 1:16 May the Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus; for often he refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain.
2TI 1:17 But being in Rome, more diligently he sought me, and found me.
2TI 1:18 May the Lord grant to him to find mercy from the Lord in that day; and for as much as in Ephesus he served - better you know it.
2TI 2:1 You then, my child, be empowered in the favor in Christ Jesus!
2TI 2:2 And the things you heard from me through many witnesses, these things place unto trustworthy men, who will be fit also to teach others!
2TI 2:3 You then suffer hardship as a good soldier of Jesus Christ!
2TI 2:4 No one soldiering entangles himself in the matters of existence; that he should have pleased the one recruiting him.
2TI 2:5 And if also anyone should fight, he is not crowned if he should not fight lawfully.
2TI 2:6 The farmer must tire by labor before first sharing the fruits.
2TI 2:7 Comprehend what I say! For may the Lord give to you understanding in all things.
2TI 2:8 Remember Jesus Christ being raised up from the dead, from the seed of David, according to my good news!
2TI 2:9 In which I suffer hardship unto bonds as an evildoer (but the word of God is not bound.)
2TI 2:10 Because of this I endure all things on account of the chosen, that also they should attain deliverance in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
2TI 2:11 Trustworthy is the word; for if we died together, also we shall live together;
2TI 2:12 if we endure, also we shall reign together; if we deny, that one also will deny us;
2TI 2:13 if we disbelieve, that one is sure to abide; to deny himself he is not able.
2TI 2:14 These things be reminded! testifying before the Lord not to argue over words for no profit, unto the undoing of the ones hearing.
2TI 2:15 Hurry to present yourself unadulterated to God! a worker unashamed, cutting straight the word of truth.
2TI 2:16 And the profane idle talk stand from! For unto more they will progress in impious deeds,
2TI 2:17 and their word as a gangrenous pasture holds forth; whom is Hymeneus and Philetus.
2TI 2:18 Who concerning the truth miss the aim, saying, The resurrection already has taken place; and are upsetting the belief of some.
2TI 2:19 However the foundation of God stands solid, having this seal, The Lord knows the ones being his. And, Let every one naming the name of Christ abstain from iniquity!
2TI 2:20 But in a great house not only are there utensils of gold and silver, but also wooden and earthenware; and some for honor, but others for dishonor.
2TI 2:21 If then one should have cleared himself from these, he shall be a utensil for honor, having been sanctified, and useful to the master, having been prepared for every good work.
2TI 2:22 But the youthful desires flee from; and pursue righteousness, belief, love, peace, with the ones calling upon the Lord out of a clean heart!
2TI 2:23 But the moronish and uninstructed inquiries ask pardon from, knowing that they engender fights!
2TI 2:24 And a bondman of the Lord must not quarrel; but be calm to all, qualified for teaching, enduring evil,
2TI 2:25 in gentleness correcting the ones being in opposition; lest at any time God should give to them a change of heart to full knowledge of truth;
2TI 2:26 and they should recover from out of the snare of the devil, having been taken alive by him for that ones's will.
2TI 3:1 But this know - that in the last days ill-tempered times will be present.
2TI 3:2 For men will be fond of themselves, fond of money, ostentatious, proud, blasphemous, resisting the persuasion of parents, ungracious, unholy,
2TI 3:3 unaffectionate, hostile, devilish, immoderate, untamed, disliking good,
2TI 3:4 betrayers, precipitous, being deluded, friends of pleasure rather than friends of God;
2TI 3:5 having the appearance of piety, but denying its power! Even these turn away from!
2TI 3:6 For from out of these are the ones entering into the houses, and capturing the vain women heaped with sins, being led by various desires,
2TI 3:7 at all times learning, and not at any time being able to come in full knowledge of the truth.
2TI 3:8 And in which manner Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so also these oppose the truth; men being corrupted in the mind, unproved concerning the belief.
2TI 3:9 But they shall not progress unto more; for their thoughtlessness will be evident to all, as also their's was.
2TI 3:10 But you have closely followed my instruction, in the conduct, in the intention, in the belief, in the long-suffering, in the love, in the endurance,
2TI 3:11 in the persecutions, in the sufferings, such as happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra - of such persecutions I endured. And from out of all the Lord rescued me.
2TI 3:12 But even all the ones wanting to live piously in Christ Jesus shall be persecuted.
2TI 3:13 But wicked men and impostors shall progress unto the worse, misleading, and being misled.
2TI 3:14 But you abide in the things which you learned, and were trustworthy, knowing from whom you learned!
2TI 3:15 And that from a babe you knew the consecrated writings, being able to make you wise unto deliverance through belief, of the one in Christ Jesus.
2TI 3:16 Every scripture is God inspired, and beneficial for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness;
