2TI 3:17 that the man of God should be complete for accomplishing every good work.
2TI 4:1 I testify then in the presence of God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, the one being about to judge the living and the dead, according to his grandeur and his kingdom.
2TI 4:2 Proclaim the word! Attend opportunely and inopportunely! Reprove! Reproach! Comfort in all long-suffering and teaching!
2TI 4:3 For there will be a time when they will not endure healthy teaching, but according to their own desires they will accumulate to themselves teachers tickling the hearing.
2TI 4:4 And from hearing indeed the truth, they shall turn away, and shall be turned aside unto the fables.
2TI 4:5 But you be sober in all things! Suffer hardships! Do the work of an evangelist! Of your service have full assurance!
2TI 4:6 For I already am offered as a libation, and the time of my separation stands by.
2TI 4:7 The good struggle I have struggled; the race I have finished; the belief I have kept.
2TI 4:8 Remaining reserved for me is the crown of righteousness, which the Lord the just judge will recompense to me in that day; and not only to me, but also to all the ones loving his grandeur.
2TI 4:9 Hurry to come to me quickly!
2TI 4:10 For Demas abandoned me, having loved the present eon, and is gone to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
2TI 4:11 Luke is alone with me. Having taken up Mark, bring him with yourself; for he is useful to me in service!
2TI 4:12 And Tychicus I sent to Ephesus.
2TI 4:13 The hooded cloak which I left in Troas with Carpus, when coming bring, and the scrolls, especially the parchments!
2TI 4:14 Alexander the brazier demonstrated many bad things against me. May the Lord render to him according to his works -
2TI 4:15 whom you also watch out for! For exceedingly he has opposed our words.
2TI 4:16 In my first defense no one came together with me, but all abandoned me. May it not be imputed against them.
2TI 4:17 But the Lord stood by me, and empowered me; that through me the proclamation should be fully assured, and all the nations should hear. And I was rescued from out of the mouth of the lion.
2TI 4:18 And the Lord shall rescue me from every evil work, and shall preserve me for his heavenly kingdom; to whom be the glory into the eons of the eons. Amen.
2TI 4:19 Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the house of Onesiphorus!
2TI 4:20 Erastus stayed in Corinth, but Trophimus I left in Miletus sick.
2TI 4:21 Hurry before winter to come! Eubulus greets you, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brothers.
2TI 4:22 The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Favor be with you. Amen.
TIT 1:1 Paul, a bondman of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for belief of the chosen of God, and full knowledge of truth according to piety;
TIT 1:2 unto the hope of life eternal, which the God incapable of falsehood promised before times eternal;
TIT 1:3 but manifested in his own times - his word by proclamation, which I was entrusted with according to command of God our deliverer.
TIT 1:4 To Titus, genuine child according to our common belief; favor, mercy, peace, from God the father and the Lord Jesus Christ our deliverer.
TIT 1:5 For this favor I left you in Crete, that the things missing you should correct, and should place in every city 1elders, as I set in order for you to do.
TIT 1:6 If anyone is without reproach, husband of one wife, having trustworthy children, not with a charge of carnality or unsubmissiveness.
TIT 1:7 For it is necessary the overseer to be without reproach, as God's manager; not self-willed, not prone to anger, not intemperate in the use of wine, not a brawler, not profiting through vice;
TIT 1:8 but hospitable, a friend of good men, discreet, just, sacred, self-controlled;
TIT 1:9 holding to the trustworthy word according to the teaching, that he might be able both to encourage in the sound teaching, and to reprove the ones disputing.
TIT 1:10 For there are many unsubmissive and vain talkers and mind-deceivers, especially the ones of the circumcision.
TIT 1:11 Whom it is necessary to muzzle, who upset entire houses, teaching what they must not, for favor of shameful gain.
TIT 1:12 There said a certain one of them, a prophet of their own, saying, Cretans continually are liars, evil wild beasts, idle bellies.
TIT 1:13 This testimony is true; for which reason reprove them severely! that they should be sound in the belief;
TIT 1:14 not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, turning away from the truth.
TIT 1:15 All things indeed are pure to the pure. But to the ones being defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.
TIT 1:16 They acknowledge to know God; but in the works they deny him, being abominable, and resisting persuasion, and rejected to every good work.
TIT 2:1 But you speak what is becoming for sound instruction!
TIT 2:2 Old men are to be sober, serious, discreet, being sound in the belief, in the love, in the endurance.
TIT 2:3 Old women likewise, with a consecrated character, not slanderers, not being enslaved to much wine, teachers of virtue;
TIT 2:4 that the young women are to be of a sound mind, to be ones loving their husbands, ones fond of children,
TIT 2:5 discreet, pure, housekeepers, good, ones being submitted to their own husbands, that the word of God should not be blasphemed.
TIT 2:6 The younger men likewise enjoin to be of a sound mind!
TIT 2:7 In all things making yourself a model of good works; in the teaching having integrity, seriousness, incorruptibility,
TIT 2:8 sound word, not open to condemnation; that the one at opposite should be ashamed, having nothing heedless to say concerning us.
TIT 2:9 Bondmen are to be submitted to their own masters! in everything to be well-pleasing, not disputing,
TIT 2:10 not pilfering, but demonstrating all good belief; that the teaching of God our deliverer should be adorned in all things.
TIT 2:11 For the favor of God appeared - the deliverance to all men;
TIT 2:12 and correcting us, that denying impiety and the worldly desires, that sanely, and righteously, and piously, we should live in the present eon;
TIT 2:13 awaiting the blessed hope, and grandeur of the glory of the great God and our deliverer Jesus Christ;
TIT 2:14 who gave himself for us, that he should ransom us from all lawlessness, and should cleanse to himself a prized people, zealous of good works.
TIT 2:15 These things speak, and encourage, and reprove with all command! Let no one speculate about you!
TIT 3:1 Remind them to submit to sovereignties and authorities, to yield obedience, to be prepared for every good work,
TIT 3:2 to blaspheme no one, to not be quarrelsome, but lenient, demonstrating all gentleness to all men!
TIT 3:3 For we were at some time or other also ourselves unthinking, resisting persuasion, erring, being a slave to desires and various satisfactions, leading in evil and envy, odious, detesting one another.
TIT 3:4 And when the graciousness and the humane treatment appeared of God our deliverer,
TIT 3:5 not from works in righteousness which we did, but according to his mercy he delivered us, through the bath of regeneration, and renewal of holy spirit;
TIT 3:6 which he poured out upon us richly through Jesus Christ our deliverer;
TIT 3:7 that having been justified by that favor, we should be heirs according to a hope of life eternal.
TIT 3:8 Trustworthy is the word; and concerning these things I want you to positively assert, that the ones trusting in God should be thoughtful to be set over good works. These are the good and beneficial things to men.
TIT 3:9 But moronish inquiries, and genealogies, and strifes, and legal battles, stand off from! for they are unprofitable and vain.
TIT 3:10 A heretical man, after one and a second admonition, refuse!
TIT 3:11 knowing that such a one is distorted, and sins, being self-condemned.
TIT 3:12 Whenever I should send forth Artemas to you, or Tychicus, hurry to come to me in Nicopolis! for there I have decided to pass the winter.
TIT 3:13 Zenas the legal expert and Apollos diligently send forward, that nothing should be missing to them!
TIT 3:14 But let also the ones of ours learn to be set over good works for the important needs, that they should not be unfruitful!
TIT 3:15 All the ones with me greet you. You greet the ones being fond of us in belief! Favor be with you all. Amen.
PHM 1:1 Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon the beloved, and our fellow-worker,
PHM 1:2 and to Apphia the beloved, and Archippus our fellow-soldier, and to the assembly at your house.
PHM 1:3 Favor to you, and peace from God our father and of the Lord Jesus Christ.
PHM 1:4 I give thanks to my God at all times making mention of you at my prayers,
PHM 1:5 hearing of your love, and the belief which you have towards the Lord Jesus, and to all the sanctified ones;
PHM 1:6 that the fellowship of your belief should become active in full knowledge of every good work in you in Christ Jesus.
PHM 1:7 For we have much gratitude and comfort over your love, because the feelings of compassion of the sanctified ones has been rested through you, O brother.
PHM 1:8 Therefore, having a great openness in Christ, to give orders to you about the related thing,
PHM 1:9 I appeal rather through the love, being such a one as Paul an old man, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
PHM 1:10 I appeal to you concerning my child, whom I engendered in my bonds - Onesimus;
PHM 1:11 the one at some time or other useless to you, but now useful to you and to me, whom I sent back to you.
PHM 1:12 But you, ( that is for him, ) receive the things concerning my feelings of compassion;
PHM 1:13 whom I wanted to keep for myself, that for you he should be serving to me in the bonds of the good news!
PHM 1:14 But without the help of your opinion I wanted to do nothing; that your good should not be as according to necessity, but as voluntary.
PHM 1:15 For perhaps on account of this he was separated for an hour, that you should receive him eternal;
PHM 1:16 no longer as a bondman, but above a bondman, a beloved brother, especially to me; and how much more to you, both in flesh, and in the Lord.
PHM 1:17 If then you have me for a partner, receive him as me!
PHM 1:18 And if in anything he wronged you, or owes, charge this to me!
PHM 1:19 I Paul write in my hand. I will pay (for I should not say to you that even you yourself owes me besides.)
PHM 1:20 Yes, O brother, may I oblige you in the Lord; rest my feelings of compassion in the Lord!
PHM 1:21 Relying upon your obedience, I wrote to you, knowing that even above what I say you will do.
PHM 1:22 But at the same time also prepare for me a guest room! For I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you.
PHM 1:23 They greet you - Epaphras, my fellow-captive in Christ Jesus;
PHM 1:24 Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers.
PHM 1:25 The favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
HEB 1:1 In various parts and in various ways earlier, God, having spoken to the fathers by the prophets,
HEB 1:2 in these last days spoke to us by the son, whom he established heir of all things, through whom also he made the eons;
HEB 1:3 who being the radiance of the glory, and impression of his essence, and bearing the whole by the word of his power, by himself making a cleansing of our sins, sat at the right of the greatness in heights;
HEB 1:4 having become so much better than the angels, he has inherited a name as much more diverse from them.
HEB 1:5 For to whom said he at some time or other of the angels, You are my son, I today engendered you? And again, I will be to him for father, and he will be to me for son.
HEB 1:6 and again whenever he should bring in the first-born into the inhabitable world, he says, And let all angels of God do obeisance to him!
HEB 1:7 And indeed to the angels he says, The one making his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
HEB 1:8 But to the son, saying Your throne, O God, into the eon of the eon. A rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingdom.
HEB 1:9 You loved righteousness, and detested lawlessness; on account of this God your God anointed you with oil of exultation above your partakers.
HEB 1:10 And, saying, You according to beginnings, O Lord, laid the foundation of the earth; and the works of your hands are the heavens.
HEB 1:11 They shall perish; but you abide; and all as a garment shall grow old;
HEB 1:12 and as a wrap-around garment, you shall coil them, and they shall be changed. But you are the same, and your years shall not fail.
HEB 1:13 And to which of the angels said he at some time or other? Sit down at my right, until whenever I should put your enemies as a footstool of your feet!
HEB 1:14 Are they not all ministering spirits, being sent in service on account of the ones being about to inherit deliverance?
HEB 2:1 On account of this it is necessary more exceedingly for us to heed to the things heard, lest at any time we flow away.
HEB 2:2 For if the word being spoken through angels became firm, and every violation and disobedience received just payment;
HEB 2:3 how shall we flee neglecting such a deliverance; which in the beginning receiving, being spoken by the Lord, was firmed up in us by the ones hearing him;
HEB 2:4 God bearing witness with both signs and miracles, and various works of power, and distributions of holy spirit, according to his volition?
HEB 2:5 For not to angels he submitted the inhabitable world about to be, concerning of which we speak.
HEB 2:6 But one testified somewhere saying, What is man, that you remember him? or a son of man that you visit him?
HEB 2:7 You lessened him some a little than the angels; with glory and honor you crowned him, and established him over the works of your hands.
HEB 2:8 All things you submitted underneath his feet. For in the submitting to him all things, he left nothing unsubmissive to him. But now not yet do we see all things being submitted to him.
HEB 2:9 But we see Jesus being lessened a little than the angels, on account of the suffering of death, being crowned with glory and honor; that by favor of God he should taste death for all.
HEB 2:10 For it was becoming to him, (through whom is the whole, and of whom is the whole,) for leading many sons in glory, to perfect the head of their deliverance through sufferings.
HEB 2:11 For both the one sanctifying and the ones being sanctified are all of one. For which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
HEB 2:12 saying, I will report your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing praise to you.
HEB 2:13 And again, I will be yielding upon him. And again, Behold I and the children which God gave to me.
HEB 2:14 Since then the children have participated of flesh and blood, also he closely partook of the same; that through death he should cease the work having the might of death, that is to say - the devil;
HEB 2:15 and should dismiss those, as many as by fear of death on account of all of the living, were liable of servitude.
HEB 2:16 For not in any way does he take hold of angels; but the seed of Abraham he takes hold of.
HEB 2:17 Whereupon he owed in all things to be likened to the brothers, that he should become a merciful and trustworthy chief priest in the things towards God, so as to atone the sins of the people.
HEB 2:18 For in that he suffered himself, having been tested, he is able to help the ones being tested.
HEB 3:1 Whereupon, holy brothers, partakers of the heavenly calling, contemplate the apostle and chief priest of our acknowledgment offering - Christ Jesus!
HEB 3:2 being trustworthy to the one appointing him, as also Moses in all his house.
HEB 3:3 For this one has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, on account of as much as the one carefully preparing the house has more honor than the house.
HEB 3:4 For every house is carefully prepared by someone; but the one carefully preparing the whole is God.
HEB 3:5 And Moses indeed was trustworthy in all his house, as an attendant, for a testimony of the things going to be spoken;
HEB 3:6 but Christ as a son over his house, whose house are we, if indeed the confidence and the boasting of the hope we should hold firm until the end.
HEB 3:7 Therefore, (as the holy spirit says, Today, if you should hearken to his voice,
HEB 3:8 you should not harden your hearts as in the embittering, in the day of the test in the wilderness;
HEB 3:9 of which place your fathers tested me, tried me, and beheld my works forty years.
HEB 3:10 Therefore I loathed that generation, and said, Continually they err in the heart; and they knew not my ways.
HEB 3:11 As I swore by an oath in my wrath, Shall they enter into my rest?)
HEB 3:12 take heed, brothers, lest at any time there shall be in some of you a wicked unbelief in heart, in the separating from the living God.
HEB 3:13 But encourage yourselves according to each day, as long as of which it is called today; that you should not be hardened, any of you, by any deception of sin.
HEB 3:14 For we have become partakers of the Christ, if indeed the beginning of the support we should hold firm until the end,
HEB 3:15 as in the saying, Today if you should hearken to his voice, you should not harden your hearts, as in the embittering.
HEB 3:16 For some having heard, rebelled - even not all the ones coming forth out of Egypt with Moses.
HEB 3:17 And to whom did he loathe forty years? Was it not to the ones having sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?
HEB 3:18 And to whom did he swear by an oath to not to enter into his rest, unless to the ones resisting persuasion?
HEB 3:19 And we see that they were not able to enter because of unbelief.
HEB 4:1 We should fear then, lest at any time, being left behind of the promise to enter into his rest, any of you should seem to fail.
HEB 4:2 For even we are being announced good news, just as those also. But the word of the report did not benefit those, not being mixed together in the belief to the ones having heard.
HEB 4:3 For we entering into the rest, the ones having believed, as he has said, As I swore by an oath in my wrath, shall they enter into my rest? And yet the works from the founding of the world were taking place.
HEB 4:4 For he has said somewhere concerning the seventh day, thus, And God rested in the seventh day from all his works.
HEB 4:5 And in this place again, Shall they enter into my rest?
HEB 4:6 Since then it leaves some to enter into it, and the ones prior having been announced did not enter because of disobedience;
HEB 4:7 again a certain day he confirms, Today, saying in David, after so great a time; as it has been said, Today if you should hearken to his voice, you should not harden your hearts.
HEB 4:8 For if Joshua gave them rest, then he would not speak concerning another day after these things.
HEB 4:9 Then there is left a sabbath rest to the people of God.
HEB 4:10 For the one entering into his rest, himself also rested from his works, as God from his own.
HEB 4:11 We should hurry then to enter into that rest, lest anyone should fall in the same example of disobedience.
HEB 4:12 For the word of God is living, and active, and sharper than any double-edged sword, and penetrating as far as the distribution of both soul and spirit, also of joints and marrows, and is a discerner of the thinking and reflections of the heart.
HEB 4:13 And there is not a creation unapparent before him; but all are naked and laid bare to his eyes to whom the reckoning is to us.
HEB 4:14 Having then a great chief priest, having gone through the heavens, (Jesus the son of God,) let us keep the acknowledgment offering.
HEB 4:15 For not do we have a chief priest not being able to sympathize in our weaknesses; but one having been tested in all things according to our likeness, separate from sin.
HEB 4:16 Let us come forward then with confidence to the throne of favor, that we should receive mercy, and should find favor for opportune help.
HEB 5:1 For every chief priest being taken from among men, is established for men in the things for God, that he should offer both gift offerings and sacrifices for sin offerings;
HEB 5:2 being able to moderate emotions with the ones being ignorant and erring, since also he is encompassed with weakness.
HEB 5:3 And on account of this he ought, as concerning the people, so also concerning himself to offer for sins.
HEB 5:4 And not to himself does anyone take the honor, but the one being called by God, just as Aaron.
HEB 5:5 Thus also the Christ did not glorify himself to become chief priest; but the one saying to him, You are my son, I today have engendered you.
HEB 5:6 As also in another place he says, You are a priest into the eon according to the order of Melchisedek.
HEB 5:7 Who in the days of his flesh offered both supplications and earnest entreaties to the one being able to deliver him from death, with a strong cry and having offered tears, and was listened to because of his veneration;
HEB 5:8 though being a son, he learned obedience from what he suffered.
HEB 5:9 And having been perfected, he became to all the ones obeying him the reason of eternal deliverance;
HEB 5:10 having been addressed by God as chief priest according to the order of Melchisedek.
HEB 5:11 Concerning of whom our word is much and difficult in interpretation to speak, since you have become dull in the hearings.
HEB 5:12 For though you ought to be teachers because of the time, again you have need of one to teach you what are the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God; and you have become having need of milk, and not of solid nourishment.
HEB 5:13 For every one partaking of milk is inexperienced of the word of righteousness; for he is an infant.
HEB 5:14 But solid nourishment is for full grown, even of the ones through the manner of having the senses exercised for the distinction of both good and evil.
HEB 6:1 Therefore having left the matter of the beginning of the Christ, we should bear on unto the perfection, (not casting down again a foundation) of repentance from dead works, and of belief upon God,
HEB 6:2 of the teaching of immersions, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
HEB 6:3 And this we shall do, if indeed God should permit.
HEB 6:4 For it is impossible of the ones once enlightened, having tasted also of the heavenly gift, and becoming partakers of holy spirit,
HEB 6:5 and having tasted the good word of God, and of powers of the eon about to be,
HEB 6:6 and having fallen, again to renew to repentance; crucifying again to themselves the son of God, and making an example of him.
HEB 6:7 For the earth having drunk the rain coming often upon it, and giving birth to fit pasturage for those through whom also it is cultivated, shares of the blessing from God.
HEB 6:8 But that bringing forth thorn-bushes and thistles is rejected, and near to a curse, whose end is for burning.
HEB 6:9 But we are persuaded concerning you, beloved, of better things, and having deliverance, if even thus we speak.
HEB 6:10 For God is not unjust to forget your work and the toil of the love, which you demonstrated in his name, having served to the sanctified ones, and still serving.
HEB 6:11 But we desire each of you to demonstrate the same diligence to the full assurance of the hope as far as until the end.
HEB 6:12 That you should not become dull, but imitators of the ones through belief and long-suffering are inheriting the promises.
HEB 6:13 For to Abraham God having promised, since according to no one had he greater to swear an oath by, swore an oath according to himself,
HEB 6:14 saying, Assuredly blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.
HEB 6:15 And thus, having been long-suffering, he succeeded in the promise.
HEB 6:16 For men indeed swear an oath by the greater, and the oath is an end for security in all disputes to them.
HEB 6:17 In which God more extra wanting to display to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, mediated by an oath.
HEB 6:18 That through two immutable things, (in which it was impossible for God to lie,) we should have strong consolation taking refuge to hold to the hope situated before us.
HEB 6:19 Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both safe and firm, and entering into the inner veil;
HEB 6:20 where as forerunner for us, Jesus entered according to the order of Melchisedek, becoming chief priest into the eon.
HEB 7:1 For this Melchisedek, king of Salem, priest of God the highest, (the one having met with Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and having blessed him,
HEB 7:2 to whom also Abraham portioned a tenth of all;) first indeed being translated king of righteousness, and thereupon also king of Salem, which is king of peace;
HEB 7:3 fatherless, motherless, of unknown genealogy, neither beginning of days, nor having an end of life, and taking an exact image to the son of God; abides a priest for perpetuity.
HEB 7:4 And view how great this one was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave even a tenth of the choice parts.
HEB 7:5 And indeed the ones of the sons of Levi, receiving the priesthood, have a commandment to tithe the people according to the law, that is to say, the ones of their brothers, though they are ones having come forth from out of the loin of Abraham.
HEB 7:6 But the one not tracing descent from them received a tenth from Abraham, and has blessed the one having the promises.
HEB 7:7 But separate from all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the better.
HEB 7:8 And here indeed men die who receive tenths; but there receives one witnessed of that he lives.
HEB 7:9 And, as literally to speak, through Abraham even Levi the one receiving tenths pays a tenth.
HEB 7:10 For he was still in the loin of the father when Melchisedek met with him.
HEB 7:11 If indeed then perfection were through the Levitical priesthood ( for the people established law upon it, ) what still need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchisedek, and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?
HEB 7:12 For the priesthood being transposed, from necessity also a transposition of law takes place.
HEB 7:13 For of whom are said these things, partakes of another tribe, from which no one has given attention to the altar.
HEB 7:14 For it is exposed to view that our Lord has risen from out of Judah, for which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
HEB 7:15 And more extra still it is quite evident, since according to the likeness of Melchisedek another priest arises,
HEB 7:16 who not according to the law of fleshly commandment exists, but according to the power of an indissoluble life.
HEB 7:17 For he testifies, that, You are a priest into the eon according to the order of Melchisedek.
HEB 7:18 For indeed an annulment of the commandment before takes place because of its weak and unprofitable state;
HEB 7:19 for the law perfected nothing, but there is the further introduction of a better hope through which we approach to God.
HEB 7:20 And according to as much as not separate from the swearing of an oath he was made priest
HEB 7:21 (for indeed the ones separate from swearing of an oath are become priests, but the one with swearing of an oath through the saying as to him, The Lord swore by an oath, and will not change his mind; you are a priest into the eon according to the order of Melchisedek.)
HEB 7:22 Jesus has become surety by so much of a better covenant.
HEB 7:23 And indeed, there are more priests being restrained from remaining on account of death;
HEB 7:24 but he, because of his abiding into the eon, has the inviolable priesthood.
HEB 7:25 From where he is able even to deliver totally the ones coming forward through him to God, at all times living to intercede for them.
HEB 7:26 For such a chief priest becomes us - sacred, guileless, undefiled, being separated from sinners, and becoming higher than the heavens;
HEB 7:27 who has not had a daily necessity, as the chief priests, prior to offer sacrifices for their own sins, and thereupon for the sins of the people. For this he did once for all, having offered himself.
HEB 7:28 For the law ordains men chief priests, ones having weakness; but the word of the swearing of an oath, the one after the law, has perfected a son into the eon.
HEB 8:1 But the total sum upon the things being spoken is - we have such a chief priest, one who sat at the right of the throne of the greatness in the heavens,
HEB 8:2 a minister of the holies, and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
HEB 8:3 For every chief priest is ordained for the act of offering both gifts and sacrifices. Whereupon it is important even this one to have something which he should offer.
HEB 8:4 For if indeed he was upon the earth, not even would he be a priest, there being the priests of the ones offering the gifts according to the law;
HEB 8:5 who serve the example and shadow of the heavenlies, as Moses was divinely instructed being about to complete the tent. For, See, says he, you shall make all things according to the model having been shown to you on the mountain.
HEB 8:6 But now a more diverse ministration he has attained, in as much as also he is mediator of a better covenant, which is established upon better promises.
HEB 8:7 For if that first covenant was blameless, there would not be sought place for a second.
HEB 8:8 For complaining against them, he says, Behold, days come, says the Lord, and I will complete upon the house of Israel and upon the house of Judah a new covenant.
HEB 8:9 Not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers in the day of my taking hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they adhered not to my covenant, and I neglected them, says the Lord.
HEB 8:10 But this is the covenant which I will ordain with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord; imputing my laws into their mind, and I will inscribe them upon their hearts. And I will be to them for God, and they will be to me for a people.
HEB 8:11 And in no way should each teach his neighbor, nor each his brother, saying, Know the Lord! For all shall know me, from their small unto their great.
HEB 8:12 For I will be kind to their unrighteousness, and their sins and of their lawless deeds in no way should I remember any more.
HEB 8:13 In the saying, New, he has made the first old. And the one being old and growing old is near extinction.
HEB 9:1 The first tent had indeed then also ordinances of service, and the worldly holy place.
HEB 9:2 For the first tent was carefully prepared, in which was both lamp-stand and the table, and the place setting of the breads, which is called holy;
HEB 9:3 and after the second veil, a tent, being called holy of holies;
HEB 9:4 having a golden incense pan, and the ark of the covenant having been covered over on all sides with gold, in which was the golden jar having the manna, and the rod of Aaron having burst forth, and the tablets of the covenant;
HEB 9:5 and up above it were the cherubim of glory shading the atonement-seat; concerning which it is not for now to speak in turn.
HEB 9:6 And of these things thus being carefully prepared, the priests always enter indeed into the first tent, completing the services.
HEB 9:7 But into the second part the chief priest went in alone once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself, and the ignorance sacrifices for the people.
HEB 9:8 This manifesting of the holy spirit not yet has been made apparent while still the first tent was having a position of the way of the holies.
HEB 9:9 Which is a parable in the time being present, in which both gifts and sacrifices are offered, not being able as to conscience to perfect the one serving;
HEB 9:10 consisting only in foods and drinks, and diverse immersions, and ordinances of flesh, until a time of straightening rests.
HEB 9:11 But Christ being come is chief priest of the good things about to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hand - that is to say, not of this creation;
HEB 9:12 nor through the blood of he-goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered once for all into the holies, having found an eternal ransoming.
HEB 9:13 For if the blood of bulls and he-goats, and ashes of a heifer sprinkling the ones being unclean, sanctifies for the cleanliness of the flesh,
HEB 9:14 how much more the blood of the Christ, (who through eternal spirit offered himself unblemished to God,) shall cleanse your conscience from dead works for serving the living God.
HEB 9:15 And because of this he is mediator of a new covenant, so that death having taken place, for the release by ransom of the violations unto the first covenant, was so the ones having been called should receive of the promise of the eternal inheritance.
HEB 9:16 For where there is a will covenant., it is a necessity for the death of the one ordaining the will to come to bear.
HEB 9:17 For a will with the dead is firm; since not at any time does it prevail when the one ordaining the will lives.
HEB 9:18 Whereupon neither the first covenant has been dedicated separate from blood.
HEB 9:19 For every commandment having been spoken according to the law by Moses to all the people, having taken the blood of the calves and he-goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, both itself the scroll, and all the people he sprinkled,
HEB 9:20 saying, This is the blood of the covenant which God gave charge to you.
HEB 9:21 But also the tent, and all the utensils of the ministration, with blood in like manner he sprinkled.
HEB 9:22 And nearly all things are cleansed with blood according to the law; and separate from blood-letting there becomes not a release.
HEB 9:23 It was a necessity then for indeed the examples of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
HEB 9:24 For not into hand made holy places the Christ entered, which are antitypes of the true; but into heaven itself, now to be revealed to the face of God for us.
HEB 9:25 Nor that he should often offer himself, as the chief priest enters into the holy places yearly with another's blood;
HEB 9:26 since it would have been necessary for him to often suffer from the founding of the world. But now once at the completion of the eons, for annulment of sin, he has been manifested through his sacrifice.
HEB 9:27 And for as much as it has been reserved to men once to die, but after this the judgment;
HEB 9:28 so also the Christ once having been offered for bearing the sins of many, that of a second time separate from sin he shall appear to the ones awaiting him for deliverance.
HEB 10:1 For the law having a shadow of the good things about to be, is not itself the very image of the things which they offer yearly with the same sacrifices in perpetuity, and at no time is able to perfect the ones coming forward;
HEB 10:2 since they would not have ceased to be offered. On account of the ones serving once being cleansed have nothing any longer of a conscience of sins;
HEB 10:3 but in these there is a remembrance of sins yearly.
HEB 10:4 For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and of he-goats to remove sins.
HEB 10:5 Therefore entering into the world, he says, Sacrifice and offering you wanted not, but a body you readied for me.
HEB 10:6 Whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices for sin you thought not well of.
HEB 10:7 Then I said, Behold, I come (in the roll of the scroll it has been written concerning me,) to do, O God, your will.
HEB 10:8 By earlier saying that, Sacrifice and offering and whole burnt offerings and for sin offerings you wanted not, nor think well of (which are offered according to the law;)
HEB 10:9 then he said, Behold, I come to do, O God, your will. In this he does away with the first, that the second should be established.
HEB 10:10 By which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
HEB 10:11 And indeed every priest stands daily officiating and offering the same sacrifices often, which at no time are able to remove sins.
HEB 10:12 But he, having offered one sacrifice for sins in perpetuity, sat at the right of God;
HEB 10:13 for the remaining time looking out until his enemies be placed as a footstool of his feet.
HEB 10:14 For by one offering he has perfected in perpetuity the ones having been sanctified.
HEB 10:15 And the holy spirit bears witness to us also. For after he describes beforehand,
HEB 10:16 This is the covenant which I will ordain with them after those days, says the Lord, putting my laws upon their hearts; and upon their thoughts I will inscribe them;
HEB 10:17 and their sins and their lawless deeds in no way shall I remember any longer.
HEB 10:18 But where there is a release of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.
HEB 10:19 Having then, brothers, confidence for the entrance into the holies by the blood of Jesus,
HEB 10:20 which he dedicated to us a way newly made and living, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
HEB 10:21 and having a great priest over the house of God;
HEB 10:22 let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of belief, with hearts being sprinkled from a wicked conscience, and the body being bathed with clean water.
HEB 10:23 Let us hold fast the acknowledgment offering of the hope unwavering! For trustworthy is the one promising.
HEB 10:24 And let us mind one another for stimulating love and good works;
HEB 10:25 not abandoning the assemblage of ourselves, as the custom with some; but encouraging one another; and by so much more, as much as you see the day approaching!
HEB 10:26 For where voluntarily we sin after receiving the full knowledge of the truth, no longer is left a sacrifice for sins;
HEB 10:27 but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a zealous fire being about to devour the adversaries.
HEB 10:28 Anyone disregarding the law of Moses dies without the help of compassions upon the testimony of two or three witnesses.
HEB 10:29 Of how much do you think worse shall he be worthy of punishment - the one having trampled the son of God, and esteeming the blood of the covenant as common, in which he was sanctified, and having insulted the spirit of favor?
HEB 10:30 For we know the one having said, Punishment is mine, I will recompense, says the Lord. And again, saying, The Lord will judge his people.
HEB 10:31 It is fearful to fall into the hands of the living God.
HEB 10:32 But call to mind the prior days, in which, having been enlightened, you endured much conflict of sufferings;
HEB 10:33 this indeed, being made a public spectacle both in scornings and afflictions; and this - having become partners of the ones thus behaving in being scorned.
HEB 10:34 For both in my bonds you sympathized, and the seizure of your possessions with joy you accepted, knowing to have in yourselves a better possession in heavens, and abiding.
HEB 10:35 Do not throw off then your confidence, which has great payment.
HEB 10:36 For you have need of endurance, that having done the will of God, you should receive the promise, saying,
HEB 10:37 For yet a little while, the one coming shall come, and will not delay.
HEB 10:38 But the just one shall live from belief; and if he keeps back, my soul takes not pleasure in him.
HEB 10:39 But we are not keeping back to destruction; but of belief for a procurement of life.
HEB 11:1 And belief is the reality of hoping of things, the proof not being seen.
HEB 11:2 For in this the elders were borne witness to.
HEB 11:3 By belief we comprehend the eons to be fashioned by the word of God, so that not of things appearing take place the things seen.
HEB 11:4 By belief Abel offered a greater sacrifice than Cain to God, by which he bore witness to be just, by God testifying over his gifts; and through it having died still speaks.
HEB 11:5 By belief Enoch was transposed to not know death; and was not found, for God transposed him. For before his transposition he bore witness, to have been well-pleasing to God.
HEB 11:6 But apart from belief it is impossible to well-please. For it is necessary for the one coming forward to God to believe that he is; and to the ones seeking after him he becomes a paymaster.
HEB 11:7 By belief Noah having received a divine message concerning the things not as yet being seen, showing reverence, carefully prepared the ark for deliverance of his house; by which he condemned the world, and of the thing according to belief he became heir of righteousness.
HEB 11:8 By belief, Abraham being called, obeyed to go forth unto the place which he was about to receive for an inheritance; and he went forth, not having knowledge of where he went.
HEB 11:9 By belief he sojourned in the land of the promise, as an alien, in tents dwelling with Isaac and Jacob, the joint-heirs of the same promise.
HEB 11:10 For he looked out for the city having foundations, of which the craftsman and engineer is God.
HEB 11:11 By belief also Sarah herself received power for founding seed, and past the time of vigor gave birth, since believing she esteemed the one promising.
HEB 11:12 Therefore also from one they were born, (and these were as deadened,) as the stars of the heaven in multitude, and as the sand by the edge of the sea is innumerable.
HEB 11:13 According to belief these all died, not receiving the promises, but at a distance beholding them, and being persuaded, and greeting, and acknowledging that they are strangers and immigrants upon the earth.
HEB 11:14 For the ones saying such things reveal that they anxiously seek the fatherland.
HEB 11:15 And if indeed, those remembering from where they came forth from, they had even time to return.
HEB 11:16 But now a better thing they reach for, that is to say, a heavenly. Therefore God is not ashamed of them to be called their God. For he prepared for them a city.
HEB 11:17 By belief Abraham offered Isaac, being tested, and the one receiving the promises offered up the only child,
HEB 11:18 towards whom it was said that, In Isaac a seed shall be called to you;
HEB 11:19 considering that God was able to raise even from the dead; from where he received him even in parable.
HEB 11:20 By belief concerning things about to be Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau.
HEB 11:21 By belief Jacob dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and did obeisance upon the tip of his cane.
HEB 11:22 By belief Joseph, coming to an end, made mention concerning the exodus of the sons of Israel; and gave charge concerning his bones.
HEB 11:23 By belief Moses, having been born, was hid three months by his fathers, for they saw the child as fair; and they feared not the edict of the king.
HEB 11:24 By belief Moses, having become great, denied to be called son of Pharoah's daughter,
HEB 11:25 rather it being good to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to have temporary enjoyment in sins;
HEB 11:26 esteeming the scorning of the anointed greater riches than the treasures in Egypt; for he looked away to the payment.
HEB 11:27 By belief he left Egypt, not fearing the rage of the king; for as seeing the unseen he persevered.
HEB 11:28 By belief he observed the passover, and the pouring of the blood, lest the one annihilating the first-born should touch them.
HEB 11:29 By belief they passed over the red sea as through dry land; of which the Egyptians taking the attempt were swallowed down.
HEB 11:30 By belief the walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled for seven days.
HEB 11:31 By belief Rahab the harlot was not destroyed together with the ones having disobeyed, receiving the spies with peace.
HEB 11:32 And what yet say I? For it shall be deficient of me not describing the time concerning Gideon, Barak, and also Samson, and Jephthah; also David and Samuel, and the prophets;
HEB 11:33 who through belief conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, succeeded in the promises, shut up mouths of lions,
HEB 11:34 extinguished the power of fire, fled the mouths of swords, were empowered from out of weakness, became strong in war, leaned the camps of aliens,
HEB 11:35 women received of a resurrection of their dead, and others were pounded, not accepting the release by ransom, that a better resurrection they should attain,
HEB 11:36 and others received a trial of mocking and of whips, and still of bonds and prison;
HEB 11:37 they were stoned, were sawn, were tested, died by murder of the sword, went around in sheepskins, in goat's skins, lacking, being afflicted, being mistreated;
HEB 11:38 (of whom the world was not worthy;) wandering in desolate places, and in mountains, and in caves, and the openings of the earth.
HEB 11:39 And these all testifying on account of the belief, while not receiving the promise,
HEB 11:40 having foreseen something better of God for us, that they should not be perfected separate from us.
HEB 12:1 Accordingly also, we having so great a cloud of witnesses encompassing us, having put aside every swelling and accessible sin, through endurance let us run the struggle being situated before us,
HEB 12:2 looking to Jesus the head and perfection of the belief; who instead of the joy being situated before him endured the cross, disdaining the shame, and at the right of the throne of God has sat.
HEB 12:3 For consider the cost by the one enduring such dispute against him by the sinners, that you should not weary fainting in your souls.
HEB 12:4 Not yet unto blood have you stood firm, struggling against sin.
HEB 12:5 And you have been totally forgotten of the exhortation, which he reasons to you as to sons, saying, O my son, do not have little regard for the instruction of the Lord, nor be enfeebled being reproved by him!
HEB 12:6 For whom the Lord loves he corrects, and whips every son whom he welcomes.
HEB 12:7 If you endure discipline, God brings discipline to you as sons. For who is the son whom a father does not correct?
HEB 12:8 And if you are without the help of instruction, of which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate, and not sons.
HEB 12:9 So then indeed, by the flesh of our fathers we have correctors, and we show respect. Shall we not be much more submitted to the father of the spirits, and shall live?
HEB 12:10 For they indeed for a few days, as it seemed good to them, corrected; but he does so for the advantage, for us to share in his sanctity.
HEB 12:11 But any discipline by indeed the hand does not seem to be joy, but distress. But afterwards it renders peaceable fruit of righteousness to the ones having been exercised by it.
HEB 12:12 Therefore the weakened hands and the disabled knees re-erect!
HEB 12:13 And make straight tracks to your feet, that the lame should not be turned aside; but rather should be healed!
HEB 12:14 Pursue peace with all, and the sanctification, (apart from which no one shall see the Lord;)
HEB 12:15 overseeing, lest any should lack from the favor of God; lest any root of bitterness germinating upward should be trouble, and through this many should be defiled;
HEB 12:16 lest there be any fornicator, or profane person as Esau, who for one portion of food delivered over his rights of the first-born!
HEB 12:17 For you understand that also afterwards, wanting to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. For a place was not found for repentance, (though with tears he sought it.)
HEB 12:18 For you have not come forward to the mountain being handled, and being kindled with fire, and to dimness, and to darkness, and to storm,
HEB 12:19 and to the trumpet's sound, and to the voice of utterances, of which the ones hearing asked pardon for the word to not proceed to them;
HEB 12:20 for they could not bear the giving of orders, saying, And if a beast should touch lightly upon the mountain, it shall be stoned, or shot with an arrow.
HEB 12:21 And so fearful was the visible display, Moses said, I am frightened and trembling.
HEB 12:22 But you have come forward to mount Zion, and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels,
HEB 12:23 to the festival and to the assembly of the first-born, having been registered in the heavens, and to God the judge of all, and to spirits of just ones having been perfected,
HEB 12:24 and Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, speaking better than the one of Abel.
HEB 12:25 Take heed that you should not refuse the one speaking! For if those did not flee escaping, refusing the one receiving a divine message upon earth, how much more we the ones turning away the one from heavens,
HEB 12:26 of whose voice the earth shook then. But now he has promised, saying, Still once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heaven.
HEB 12:27 And the saying, Still once more, manifests the transposition of the things being shaken, as things being made, that the things not being shaken should abide.
HEB 12:28 Therefore receiving a kingdom unshaken, we should have favor by which we should serve God pleasantly with respect and veneration.
HEB 12:29 For even our God is a consuming fire.
HEB 13:1 Let brotherly affection abide!
HEB 13:2 Let not hospitality be forgotten - for by this some were unaware having lodged angels!
HEB 13:3 Remember the prisoners, as ones being tied with them, the ones being mistreated, as also yourselves being in the body!
HEB 13:4 The wedding is esteemed in every way, and the marriage-bed undefiled. But fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
HEB 13:5 Let not loving money be the manner, but let being sufficient with the things at hand. For he himself has said, In no way will I forsake you, nor in any way will I abandon you.
HEB 13:6 So that taking courage we say, The Lord is to me a helper, and I will not be afraid what man shall do to me.
HEB 13:7 Remember the ones leading you, who spoke to you the word of God. Whom, contemplating the result of the behavior, you imitate the belief!
HEB 13:8 Jesus Christ yesterday and today the same, and into the eons.
HEB 13:9 Be not carried about by various and strange teachings! For it is a good thing to be firmed up in the heart with favor; not by foods, in which the ones walking derive not a benefit.
HEB 13:10 We have an altar, of which the ones serving the tent do not have authority to eat.
HEB 13:11 For those creatures whose blood is carried in for a sin offering into the holies by the chief priest, of these the bodies are incinerated outside the camp.
HEB 13:12 Therefore also Jesus, that he should sanctify the people by his own blood suffered outside the gate.
HEB 13:13 Therefore let us go forth to him outside the camp, bearing his scorn.
HEB 13:14 For we do not have here an abiding city, but we anxiously seek the one about to be.
HEB 13:15 By him then we should offer a sacrifice of praise at all times to God, that is to say, fruit of the lips of acknowledging to his name.
HEB 13:16 But of the well-doing and fellowship do not forget! For with such sacrifices God is well-pleased.
HEB 13:17 Comply with the ones leading you, and give precedence! For they are sleepless over your souls, for recompensing a reckoning, that with joy they should do this, and not moaning; for this would be unserviceable to you.
HEB 13:18 Pray for us! For we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, in all things wanting to behave well.
HEB 13:19 And more exceedingly I encourage you to do this, that more quickly I should be restored to you.
HEB 13:20 And the God of peace (leading the shepherd of the sheep from the dead, the great shepherd in the blood of the eternal covenant of our Lord Jesus Christ,)
HEB 13:21 ready you in every good work, for the doing the will of his; doing in you the thing well-pleasing before him, through Jesus Christ; to whom is the glory in the eons of the eons. Amen.
HEB 13:22 But I exhort you, brothers, endure the word of the exhortation! For also in short I wrote to you.
HEB 13:23 Know the brother Timothy having been released; with whom if he should come more quickly, I shall see you.
HEB 13:24 Greet all your leaders, and all the holy ones! The ones from Italy greet you.
HEB 13:25 Favor be with you all. Amen.
JAM 1:1 James, bondman of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion, hail!
JAM 1:2 Esteem it all joy, my brothers, whenever you should fall into various tests!
JAM 1:3 Knowing that the proving of the belief of yours manufactures endurance.
JAM 1:4 And let endurance have its perfect work, that you should be perfect and entire, with nothing missing!
JAM 1:5 And if anyone of you miss wisdom, let him ask, (of the giving to all God,) simply and not berating! and it shall be given to him.
JAM 1:6 But let him ask in belief, scrutinizing nothing! For the one scrutinizing is like a swell of the sea driven by wind and being blown about.
JAM 1:7 For let not that man imagine that he shall receive anything from the Lord!
JAM 1:8 For he is a double-minded man confused in all his ways.
JAM 1:9 But let the humble brother boast in his stature,
JAM 1:10 and the rich in his humiliation! For as the flower of grass he will pass away.
JAM 1:11 For the sun rose with the burning wind, and dried the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its countenance perished; so also the rich one in his goings shall wither.
JAM 1:12 Blessed is a man who endures a test; for becoming unadulterated, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to the ones loving him.
JAM 1:13 Let no one being tested say that, From God I am tested! For God is beyond testing by evils, and he himself tests no one.
JAM 1:14 But each is tested by his own desire, being dragged away and being entrapped.
JAM 1:15 So then the desire having conceived, gives birth to sin; but sin, being perpetrated, engenders death.
JAM 1:16 Do not be misled, my beloved brothers!
JAM 1:17 Every good portion and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the father of lights, of whom there is not an alteration or shaded circuit.
JAM 1:18 Willingly he engendered us by word of truth, for us being certain first-fruit of the ones of his creations.
JAM 1:19 So that, my beloved brothers, let every man be quick in the hearing, slow in the speaking, slow in anger!
JAM 1:20 For man's anger does not manufacture righteousness of God.
JAM 1:21 Therefore having put aside all filthiness and abundance of evil, in gentleness receive the implanted word, being able to deliver your souls!
JAM 1:22 But become doers of the word, and not only listeners, misleading yourselves!
JAM 1:23 For if any is a listener of the word, and not a doer, this one is like a man contemplating the face of his creation in a mirror;
JAM 1:24 for he contemplated himself, and went forth, and immediately forgot what he was like.
JAM 1:25 But the one having leaned over into the perfect law, the one of freedom, and remained - this one is not becoming a forgetful listener, but a doer of work, this one shall be blessed in his doing.
JAM 1:26 If anyone seems to be religious among you, and not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, of this one religion is in vain.
JAM 1:27 Religion pure and undefiled before the God and father is this - to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself spotless from the world.
JAM 2:1 My brothers, have no discrimination in the belief of our Lord Jesus Christ, the one of glory!
JAM 2:2 For if a man should enter into your gathering wearing gold rings in bright attire, and there should enter also a poor man in filthy attire;
JAM 2:3 and you should look unto the one wearing the bright attire, and should say to him, You sit down here, well! And to the poor man you should say, You stand there! or, Sit down here under my footstool!
JAM 2:4 Then did you not discriminate among yourselves, and became judges of evil thoughts?
JAM 2:5 Hearken, my beloved brothers! Did not God choose the poor of this world, rich in belief, and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to the ones loving him?
JAM 2:6 But you dishonored the poor. Do not the rich tyrannize over you, and they draw you to judgment seats?
JAM 2:7 Do they not blaspheme the good name you are called by?
JAM 2:8 If however you fulfill the royal law according to the scripture - You shall love your neighbor as yourself; you do well.
JAM 2:9 But if you discriminate because of appearance, you practice sin, being reproved by the law as violators.
JAM 2:10 For whoever shall give heed to the entire law, but shall be at fault in one thing, has become liable of all.
JAM 2:11 For the one having said, You shall not commit adultery, said also, You shall not murder. But if you shall not commit adultery, but shall murder, you have become a violator of the law.
JAM 2:12 So speak, and so do, as by the law of freedom, being about to be judged!
JAM 2:13 For judgment is merciless to the one not having mercy, and mercy glories over judgment.
JAM 2:14 What is the benefit, my brothers, if anyone should say to have belief, but should not have works? Shall the belief be able to deliver him?
JAM 2:15 And if a brother or sister should be naked, and should be forsaken of the daily nourishment,
JAM 2:16 and anyone among you should say to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled! but does not give to them the things needful of the body - what is the benefit?
JAM 2:17 So also belief, if it should not have works it is dead by itself.
JAM 2:18 But one shall say, You have belief, and I have works. Show to me your belief from out of your works, and I will show to you from out of my works my belief!
JAM 2:19 You believe that God is one; you do well; even the demons believe and shudder.
JAM 2:20 But do you want to know, O vain man, that belief separate from works is dead?
JAM 2:21 Was not Abraham our Father justified by works, having offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
JAM 2:22 Do you see that belief was working together with his works, and by the works belief was perfected?
JAM 2:23 And the scripture was fulfilled, saying, And Abraham believed in God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness - and he was called friend of God.
JAM 2:24 See therefore that by works a man is justified, and not by belief only!
JAM 2:25 And in like manner also Rahab the harlot - was she not justified by works, welcoming the messengers, and putting them out by another way?
JAM 2:26 For as the body separate from spirit is dead, so also belief separate from works is dead.
JAM 3:1 Let there not be many teachers, my brothers, knowing that we shall receive greater judgment!
JAM 3:2 For many times we are at fault all together. If any in word is not at fault, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle even his entire body.
JAM 3:3 See! We put the bits into the mouths of the horses, for them to comply to us; and we lead around their entire body.
JAM 3:4 Behold, also the boats, being so great, and are being driven by harsh winds, yet are led around by the least size rudder, where even the thrust of the one straightening wills it to go.
JAM 3:5 So also the tongue is a small member, and brags. Behold, a little fire how much material it lights;
JAM 3:6 And the tongue is a fire - the world of unrighteousness. Thus the tongue is placed among our members, staining the entire body, and blazing the whirlwind of creation; and being set ablaze by Gehenna.
JAM 3:7 For every species of nature, both of wild beasts, and of birds, both of reptiles and marine life, is tamed, and has been tamed by the human nature.
JAM 3:8 But the tongue no one is able of men to tame; it is an unrestrained evil, full of poison causing death.
JAM 3:9 By it we bless God, and father; and by it we curse men, the ones born according to the likeness of God.
JAM 3:10 From out of the same mouth comes forth blessing and curse. It does not behoove us, my brothers, for these things so to be.
JAM 3:11 Does the spring gush from out of the same opening the sweet and the bitter?
JAM 3:12 Is the fig-tree able my brothers to produce olives? or a grapevine, figs? Thus not one spring is able to produce salty and sweet water.
JAM 3:13 Who is wise and intelligent among you? Let him show out of the good behavior his works in gentleness of wisdom!
JAM 3:14 But if you have bitter jealousy and contention in your heart, do not glory over and lie against the truth!
JAM 3:15 This is not the wisdom coming down from above, but earthly, physical, demoniacal.
JAM 3:16 For where there is jealousy and contention, there is commotion and every heedless thing.
JAM 3:17 But the wisdom from above first indeed is pure, thereupon peaceable, lenient, obeys readily, full of mercy and of good fruits, impartial, and unpretentious.
JAM 3:18 And fruit of righteousness in peace is sown to the ones making peace.
JAM 4:1 From where come wars and fights among you? is it not from here, from your pleasures soldiering in your members?
JAM 4:2 You desire, and you do not have. You murder, and are jealous, and are not able to succeed. You do combat and wage war, yet you have not, because you do not ask.
JAM 4:3 You ask, and do not receive, for wickedly you ask, that you should spend for your own pleasures.
JAM 4:4 Adulterers and adulteresses, know you not that the friendship of the world is hatred of God? Who ever therefore should want to be a friend of the world stands as enemy of God.
JAM 4:5 Or do you think that uselessly the scripture says, The spirit which dwells in us longs after with envy?
JAM 4:6 But he gives greater favor. Therefore he says, The LORD resists the proud, but to the humble he gives favor.
JAM 4:7 Be submitted then to God! Oppose the devil, and he will flee from you!
JAM 4:8 Approach to God, and he will approach unto you! Cleanse your hands, O sinners, and purify your hearts, O double-minded!
JAM 4:9 Languish and mourn and weep! Let your laughter be converted into mourning, and your joy into sadness!
JAM 4:10 Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you!
JAM 4:11 Do not speak ill of one another, brothers! The one speaking ill of a brother, and judging his brother, speaks ill of the law, and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of law, but a judge.
JAM 4:12 There is one lawgiver being able to deliver and to destroy. But you, and who are you who judges the other?
JAM 4:13 Come now, O ones saying, Today and tomorrow we should go to thus the city, and we should spend there one year, and should trade, and should make gain;
JAM 4:14 you who know not the thing of tomorrow. For what is your life? For it shall be a vapor, appearing for a little, and thereupon disappearing.
JAM 4:15 Instead your saying should be, If the Lord should will, and we should live, then we should do this or that.
JAM 4:16 But now you boast in your ostentatiousness. All such boasting is wicked.
JAM 4:17 Knowing then to do good and not doing, it is sin to him.
JAM 5:1 Come now, O rich, weep shrieking over your miseries coming upon you!
JAM 5:2 Your riches are rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
JAM 5:3 Your gold and silver is corroded; and their poison shall be for a testimony against you, and shall eat your flesh as fire. You treasured up in your last days.
JAM 5:4 Behold, the wage of the workers reaping your places. The one being deprived by you cries out. And the yells of the ones harvesting have entered into the ears of the Lord of hosts.
JAM 5:5 You indulged upon the earth, and lived extravagantly; you maintained your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.
JAM 5:6 You condemned, you murdered; the just one does not resist against you.
JAM 5:7 Patiently wait then, brothers, until the arrival of the Lord! Behold, the farmer looks out for the precious fruit of the earth, patiently waiting for it, until whenever it should receive the early and late rain.
JAM 5:8 You also patiently wait! Establish your hearts! for the arrival of the Lord approaches.
JAM 5:9 Do not moan against one another, brothers, that you should not be judged! Behold, the judge stands before the doors.
JAM 5:10 Take for an example the evil suffering, my brothers, and the long-suffering of the prophets, who spoke in the name of the Lord!
JAM 5:11 Behold, we declare happy the ones enduring. The endurance of Job you have heard, and the end by the Lord you know; that he is very compassionate and pitying.
JAM 5:12 But before all things, my brothers, do not swear by an oath, neither by the heaven, nor the earth, nor any other oath. But let your yes be, Yes; and the no, No! that you should not fall into hypocrisy.
JAM 5:13 Does anyone suffer hardships among you? let him pray! Is anyone cheerful? let him strum praise!
JAM 5:14 Is anyone sick among you? let him call on the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with olive oil in the name of the Lord!
JAM 5:15 And the vow of belief will deliver the weary one, and the Lord will raise him; and if he should be committing sins, it shall be forgiven him.
JAM 5:16 Acknowledge to one another the transgressions, and make a vow for one another, so that you should be healed! Much prevails by the supplication being energized by a just one.
JAM 5:17 Elijah was a man having the same passions as us, and with prayer he prayed for it not to rain. And it rained not upon the earth for three years and six months.
JAM 5:18 And again he prayed, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth burst forth its fruit.
JAM 5:19 Brothers, if any among you should be misled from the truth, and anyone should return him;
JAM 5:20 know that the one turning a sinner from the delusion of his way, shall deliver a soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins!
1PE 1:1 Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen immigrants of the dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
1PE 1:2 according to the foreknowledge of God the father, in sanctification of spirit, in obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. Favor to you, and peace be multiplied.
1PE 1:3 Blessed is the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the one according to his great mercy regenerated us unto a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
1PE 1:4 unto an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and unfading, being kept in the heavens for us,
1PE 1:5 the ones by power of God being guarded through belief unto deliverance prepared to be uncovered in the last time.
1PE 1:6 In which you exult a little just now, if it is necessary, being fretted by various tests;
1PE 1:7 that the proving of the belief of yours, (much more esteemed than gold that perishes,) even being tried through fire, should be found in high praise and glory and honor in revelation of Jesus Christ.
1PE 1:8 Whom not having seen, you love; in whom now not looking on, but believing, you exult with joy unspeakable, and glorifying;
1PE 1:9 carrying on the end of the your belief - a deliverance of your souls.
1PE 1:10 Concerning which deliverance the prophets sought after and searched out, the ones prophesying concerning the favor towards you;
1PE 1:11 searching in what, or of what kind of time spirit of Christ was manifest in them, testifying beforehand the sufferings in Christ, and the glories after these things;
1PE 1:12 to whom it was revealed, that it was not to themselves, but to us they were serving up those things, which now were announced to you by the ones announcing good news to you in holy spirit sent from heaven; in which angels desire to lean over to see.
1PE 1:13 Therefore having girded the loins of your mind, being sober, perfectly hope upon the favor being brought to you in the revelation of Jesus Christ;
1PE 1:14 as children of obedience, not conforming to the former things in the ignorance of your desires!
1PE 1:15 But as the one calling you is holy, even you yourselves become holy in all your behavior!
1PE 1:16 For it has been written, Become holy! for I am holy.
1PE 1:17 And if you call upon the father, the one impartially judging according to the work of each, behave the sojourn of your time in fear!
1PE 1:18 And be knowing that you were not ransomed by corruptible silver or gold from out of your vain behavior handed down from your fathers;
1PE 1:19 but by the esteemed blood, (as of a lamb unblemished and spotless,) of Christ;
1PE 1:20 having been foreknown indeed before the founding of the world, but being manifested at the last of the times for us,
1PE 1:21 the ones through him believing in God raising him from the dead, and having given glory to him; so as for your belief and hope to be in God;
1PE 1:22 your souls being purified in the obedience of the truth through spirit in unpretentious brotherly affection. From out of a pure heart love one another fervently;
1PE 1:23 being regenerated, not from out of a corruptible sowing, but of incorruptible, by the word of God living and abiding in the eon!
1PE 1:24 For all flesh is as grass, and all glory of man is as the flower of grass; the grass withered, and its flower fell away.
1PE 1:25 But the word of the Lord abides into the eon. And this is the word - the good news being announced to you.
1PE 2:1 Having put aside then all evil, and all treachery, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,
1PE 2:2 as newborn babes, long after the rational sincere milk, that by it you should grow!
1PE 2:3 if indeed you tasted that the Lord is gracious.
1PE 2:4 To whom coming forward as a living stone, indeed being rejected by men, but by God chosen, valued;
1PE 2:5 also yourselves, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices, well-received to God through Jesus Christ.
1PE 2:6 For it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I place in Zion a chosen valued cornering stone; and the one believing upon him in no way shall be disgraced.
1PE 2:7 To you then a stone of value - to the ones believing. But to the ones disobeying, a stone which the ones building rejected, this one became for the head of the corner,
1PE 2:8 and a stone of stumbling, and a rock causing offence, which being disobedient they stumble against the word,; to which also they were appointed.
1PE 2:9 But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for procurement; so that you should publish the virtues of the one calling you from out of darkness into his wonderful light.
1PE 2:10 The ones at some time or other not a people, but now are a people of God. The ones not being shown mercy, but now are shown mercy.
1PE 2:11 Beloved, I appeal to you as sojourners and immigrants, to be at a distance from the fleshy desires, which soldier against the soul;
1PE 2:12 having your behavior good among the nations; that in what they speak ill of you as ones doing evil, that from having scrutinized the good works, they should glorify God in the day of visitation.
1PE 2:13 Submit then to every human institution on account of the Lord; whether to king as being superior,
1PE 2:14 or whether to governors as being sent by him for punishment indeed on ones doing evil, and high praise on ones beneficial!
1PE 2:15 For so is the will of God, by doing good to halt the ignorance of foolish men;
1PE 2:16 as free, and not having freedom as a covering of evil, but as bondmen of God.
1PE 2:17 Honor all! Love the brotherhood! Fear God! Honor the king!
1PE 2:18 Domestic servants - being submitted with all fear to the masters, not only to the good and lenient, but also to the crooked.
1PE 2:19 For this is favor, if through conscience of God anyone endures distress, suffering unjustly.
1PE 2:20 For what fame if sinning, and you endure being buffeted? But if doing good, and you endure suffering, this is favorable with God.
1PE 2:21 For this you were called; for also Christ suffered for us, leaving behind to us a pattern, that you should follow after his tracks;
1PE 2:22 who did not sin, nor was there treachery found in his mouth;
1PE 2:23 who being reviled returned not verbal abuse; when suffering threatened not; but delivered himself up to the one judging justly;
1PE 2:24 who himself bore our sins in his body upon the timber, that becoming dead to sins, we should live to righteousness; of which by his stripe you were healed.
1PE 2:25 For you were as sheep wandering; but are returned now unto the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
1PE 3:1 In like manner the wives, being submitted to their own husbands; that even if any resist persuasion to the word, by the behavior of the wives they shall be gained without a word;
1PE 3:2 having scrutinized your pure behavior in fear.
1PE 3:3 Whom let there not be the outward braiding of hair, and adornment of gold or clothing of garments of ornamentation!
1PE 3:4 But let it be the hidden mankind of the heart, in the incorruptible ornament of the gentle and unassuming spirit, which is lavish in the presence of of God.
1PE 3:5 For thus at some time or other also the holy women hoping upon God, adorned themselves, being submitted to their own husbands;
1PE 3:6 as Sarah obeyed to Abraham, calling him lord; of whom you became children, doing good and not fearing with any terror.
1PE 3:7 The husbands, in like manner, living with them according to knowledge, as being a weaker utensil in the feminine way, bestowing honor as also joint-heirs of favor of life; so as to not hinder your prayers.
1PE 3:8 But the conclusion - all be agreeing, sympathizing, affectionate, compassionate, obliging,
1PE 3:9 not rendering evil for evil, or reviling for reviling. But on the other hand, blessing; knowing that in this you were called, that you should inherit a blessing.
1PE 3:10 For the one wanting to love life, and to behold good days, let him cease his tongue from evil, and his lips to not speak deceit!
1PE 3:11 Let him turn aside from evil, and let him do good! Let him seek peace, and pursue it!
1PE 3:12 For the eyes of the Lord are upon just ones, and his ears towards their supplication. But the face of the Lord is against the ones doing evil to utterly destroy them from the earth\dagger\cvnote3:10-12 See Ps. 34:12-16..
1PE 3:13 And who is the one afflicting you, if you should become mimics of the good?
1PE 3:14 But if also you may suffer because of righteousness, blessed are you; but the fear of them you should not fear, nor should you be disturbed.
1PE 3:15 But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts, and be ready continually for a defense to all - to the one asking you a word concerning the hope in you, with gentleness and fear;
1PE 3:16 having a good conscience, that in what they should speak ill of you as ones doing evil, the ones threatening your good behavior in Christ should be put to shame!
1PE 3:17 For it is better if the will of God wants you to suffer for doing good, than doing evil.
1PE 3:18 For Christ also suffered once for sins - the just one for the unjust ones, that he should lead us forward to God, having put to death indeed the flesh, but being restored to life to the spirit;
1PE 3:19 in which also having gone he proclaimed to the spirits in prison,
1PE 3:20 to the ones who disobeyed at some time or other, when once the long-suffering of God was accepted in the days of Noah, carefully preparing an ark, in which few, that is to say, eight souls were preserved through water.
1PE 3:21 Which antitype also now delivers us - immersion; not flesh getting rid of filth, but the response of a good conscience towards God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
1PE 3:22 who is at the right of God, being gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers being submitted to him.
1PE 4:1 Christ then having suffered for us in flesh, you also be armed by the same reflection! For the one suffering in flesh, has ceased sin;
1PE 4:2 to no longer spend the remaining time in the flesh of men's desires but God's will.
1PE 4:3 For sufficient to us was the having passed time of the existence to have worked the will of the nations, going in lewdnesses, desires, drunkennesses with wine, debaucheries, drinking banquets, and unlawful idolatries;
1PE 4:4 in which they think it strange your not running together in the same pouring out of carnality, being blasphemous;
1PE 4:5 ones who shall render an account to the one readily sufficing to judge the living and dead.
1PE 4:6 For in this also to the dead was announced good news, that they should be judged indeed according to men in flesh, but should live according to God in spirit.
1PE 4:7 But of all things the end approaches. Be of sound mind then, and be sober in the prayers!
1PE 4:8 But before all things having the intense love among yourselves; for love covers a multitude of sins;
1PE 4:9 being hospitable to one another without grumblings -
1PE 4:10 each as he received favor, to each other a same serving, as good managers of the variegated favor of God.
1PE 4:11 If any speaks, let it be as oracles of God; if any serves, let it be as from out of strength which God supplies; that in all things God should be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom is the glory and the might into the eons of the eons. Amen.
1PE 4:12 Beloved, do not take it as strange the burning fire taking place among you to test you, as a strange thing happening to you.
1PE 4:13 But according to that which you participate with the sufferings of the Christ rejoice, that also in the revelation of his glory you should rejoice exulting!
1PE 4:14 If you are berated in the name of Christ, blessed are you; for the fact of the glory and the fact of the spirit of God gives rest unto you. Indeed according to them he is blasphemed, but according to you he is glorified.
1PE 4:15 For let not any of you suffer as a murderer, or thief, or one doing evil, or as a busybody!
1PE 4:16 But if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God in this part!
1PE 4:17 For it is the time to begin the judgment from the house of God. And if first from us, what is the end of the ones disobeying to the thing of the good news of God?
1PE 4:18 And if the just one hardly is delivered, the impious one and sinner, where shall they appear?
1PE 4:19 So then, even the ones suffering according to the will of God, as to a trustworthy creator, let them place their souls in doing good.
1PE 5:1 Elders, the ones among you, I exhort, I the fellow-elder and witness of the sufferings of the Christ, the one also partner of the about to be revealed glory -
1PE 5:2 tend the flock of God among you, overseeing, not by compelling, but voluntarily; nor sordidly, but eagerly;
1PE 5:3 nor as one dominating the lots, but becoming models for the flock!
1PE 5:4 And at the manifesting of the chief shepherd, you shall carry the unfading crown of glory.
1PE 5:5 In like manner, let the younger ones submit to older ones! And all adorn humility being submitted one to another! For God resists the proud, but gives favor to the humble.
1PE 5:6 Be humbled then under the fortified hand of God, that he should exalt you in time!
1PE 5:7 while casting all your anxiety upon him, for with him there is a care concerning you.
1PE 5:8 Be sober! Be vigilant! Your opponent the devil walks as a roaring lion seeking whom he should swallow down.
1PE 5:9 To whom oppose solid in the belief, knowing the same sufferings to the one in the world are being completed by your brotherhood!
1PE 5:10 But the God of all favor, having called us into his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, having suffered a little, may he ready you, support you, strengthen you, found you.
1PE 5:11 To him be the glory and the might into the eons of the eons. Amen.
1PE 5:12 Through Silvanus, the trustworthy brother to you, as I consider, a little I wrote, appealing and attesting this to be the true favor of God in which you stand.
1PE 5:13 She chosen with you in Babylon greets you; and Mark my son.
1PE 5:14 Greet one another with a kiss of love! Peace to you, to all the ones in Christ Jesus. Amen.
2PE 1:1 Simon Peter, a bondman and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the ones equally honored with us having obtained belief in righteousness of our God and deliverer Jesus Christ.
